verdicts.death: put to death, whether by court, by God directly, or by the sword
verdicts.plague: plague, disease, or fire from God, usually on a group
verdicts.captivity: carried captive, bound, or handed to enemies
verdicts.curse: a pronounced curse or standing sentence without immediate death
verdicts.restitution: the wrong was made good under the law of restitution
verdicts.spared: guilty, but spared on repentance, intercession, or by the withdrawal of witnesses

verdicts.unrecorded: the offense and the statute are recorded; scripture does not record the sentence
verdicts.blessed: kept the law, and the blessing scripture records for it

cases.name: Adam and Eve
cases.charge: Eating from the tree God forbade
cases.summary: Adam received the command not to eat of the forbidden tree. The serpent contradicted its warning of death, the woman took and ate and gave to her husband, and he ate also. They covered themselves and hid, then answered God's inquiry by shifting blame. Judgment brought sorrow, toil, mortality, and expulsion; God clothed them before driving them out.
cases.offense: The command and the contradiction stand against each other. God told Adam that eating of the forbidden tree would bring death; the serpent told the woman that they would not surely die (Genesis 2:16-17; Genesis 3:4-5). The temptation offered wisdom while denying the consequence of disobedience. Its doctrine was that the commandment could be broken without the judgment God had spoken. The fruit of lies is the spiritual danger: a word received becomes a deed performed (Hosea 10:13). Eve saw what was desirable, took, ate, and gave to her husband, and he ate also (Genesis 3:6). Paul warns of minds corrupted as the serpent beguiled Eve, and of Satan appearing as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:3,14). The promise of enlightenment did not make the teaching true. Adam's charge was that he hearkened to his wife against the command given to him (Genesis 3:17); another person's persuasion did not remove his responsibility.
cases.judgment: Their covering and hiding could not answer God's inquiry. Job speaks of covering transgressions as Adam, and Lamentations joins exposed nakedness to grievous sin (Job 31:33; Lamentations 1:8). The call, Where art thou, brought the man to account. Adam pointed to the woman God had given him, and she pointed to the serpent, but each still had to answer for the deed (Genesis 3:9-13). The serpent was cursed and brought low, and enmity was appointed between his seed and the woman's seed (Genesis 3:14-15). The promise reaches to Christ's destruction of the devil's works and the bruising of Satan under the saints' feet (1 John 3:8; Romans 16:20). To the woman came multiplied sorrow; to Adam, toil upon cursed ground until his return to dust (Genesis 3:16-19). The lie had promised escape from death, but the sentence established the opposite. God clothed them with coats of skins before driving them out (Genesis 3:21-24). The covering points toward the need for an atonement they could not supply by hiding; the Lamb is the provision named in Revelation 13:8. Mercy in their clothing did not cancel their expulsion. The guarded way to the tree of life left them unable to take for themselves what disobedience had forfeited.

verses.text: And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:
But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.

And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;
Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;
In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
And the Lord God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:
Therefore the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.
So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.
For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.
Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law (also) in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still.

entries.commentary: This is the first Sabbath that you read about in the scriptures. The Most High blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.
Chapter 2 is the manner of creation. It goes back through what you read in chapter 1 and gives you more detail on certain things.

Here is the detail on how man was formed: the Most High formed him of the dust of the ground. The breath of life is talking about the commandments. This is Adam, the chosen. Out of all the people the Most High created on the earth, He had a favorite from the beginning.
The Most High planted the garden eastward in Eden and put the chosen man there. The river Gihon is the Blue Nile; it compasses the whole land of Ethiopia.
Some of these trees are literal trees, and some of these trees represent men.
The Most High looked at the women on the earth and there was no help meet right for Adam. This again shows there were more people on the earth than Adam alone.
The Most High created Eve from Adam because there was no woman on the earth right for him at that time.

Chapter 3 deals with the craftiness of your enemy. This is not a literal snake. Another word for serpent is deceiver; the serpent is Satan. You know it is not a literal serpent because serpents do not speak.

Satan taught Eve doctrine. She had been taught that if she broke the commandments of the Most High she would die; the serpent now taught her that she would not die. The same doctrine is taught today: that your eyes will be opened and you do not have to keep the commandments and you will not die. If you leave the commandments you are going to die.

Any time scripture speaks of good for food like this, it is talking about good to learn. The fruit she ate was the lies. She was enticed to break the commandments of the Most High, then she went and taught her husband the same thing the serpent taught her, and he broke the commandments as well.
They were not literally naked; nakedness represents sin. They were in sin. Remember this is an illustrated story. The fig leaves and aprons represent them trying to cover their transgressions.
The trees of the garden here are people. Adam and his wife tried to hide their sins among the other people that were in the garden with them.

The Most High was not looking for Adam as though He could not find him; He was calling Adam to examine himself. Adam had started to separate himself from the Most High by covering and hiding his sins, and the Most High already knew what he had done.
Adam blamed Eve for his sin, and in saying the woman whom thou gavest he blamed the Most High also. Then Eve blamed the serpent; they played the blame game.

The cattle and the beasts of the field here are the nations. Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

This is a prophecy. It is not talking about the serpent and Eve; the woman is the nation of Israel. The woman does not plant seed; the man plants seed. The Most High is saying He will put enmity between Satan's seed and Israel's seed, and that enmity remains. Christ was to come from the woman. [Revelation 12](/bible/revelation/12) explains this verse. Bruising the heel is making Israel stumble. When a serpent strikes at your heel you stumble; Satan makes Israel stumble through evil communication and corrupting good manners. It shall bruise thy head is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan.

Your desire, your learning, your desire of anything was to be to your husband, and he shall rule over thee. This is one of the first commandments given, alongside be fruitful and multiply, the Sabbath, and the commandment not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Sisters, if you do not allow your husband to rule over you, it does not matter what else you keep; you are not entering the kingdom without fulfilling this.
Because Adam hearkened to his wife and broke the commandment, the ground was cursed for his sake; in sorrow and sweat he would eat of it all his days.

This is animal sacrifice to cover the sins. This is where the Most High ordained the sacrificial law; this is when they started to sacrifice. The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins.
The man was driven out of the garden to till the ground from whence he was taken, and the way of the tree of life was kept.

In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city I was in Babylon, and lay troubled upon my bed, and my thoughts came up over my heart. I saw the desolation of Sion, and the wealth of them that dwelt at Babylon; and my spirit was sore moved, so that I began to speak words full of fear to the most High. Thou gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. Unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way, which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations. In process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them; nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.

When they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, they began again to be more ungodly than the first. Thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham: him thou lovedst, and made an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed. Unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac thou gavest Jacob and Esau: as for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau. When thou leddest his seed out of Egypt, thou broughtest them up to the mount Sinai, and bowing the heavens thou didst set fast the earth, and madest the depths to tremble. Thy glory went through four gates, of fire, and of earthquake, and of wind, and of cold; that thou mightest give the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel.

Yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart, that thy law might bring forth fruit in them. For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him. Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law also in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still. Thou raisedst up a servant, called David, whom thou commandedst to build a city unto thy name, and to offer incense and oblations unto thee therein. When this was done many years, then they that inhabited the city forsook thee, and in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done; and so thou gavest the city over into the hands of thine enemies.

Are their deeds any better that inhabit Babylon, that they should therefore have the dominion over Sion? When I came thither, and had seen impieties without number, then my soul saw many evildoers in this thirtieth year, so that my heart failed me. I have seen how thou sufferest them sinning, and hast spared the wicked doers, and hast destroyed thy people, and hast preserved thine enemies. Are they then of Babylon better than they of Sion? or is there any other people that knoweth thee beside Israel? or what generation hath so believed thy covenants as Jacob? For I have gone here and there through the heathen, and I see that they flow in wealth, and think not upon thy commandments. Weigh thou therefore our wickedness now in the balance, and theirs also that dwell in the world; and so shall thy name no where be found but in Israel. Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

cases.name: Abel
cases.charge: Bringing the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof
cases.summary: Abel brought the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof, and the Lord had respect unto him and his offering. Hebrews witnesses to his faith, and Christ names him righteous Abel. His brother slew him, but his blood cried from the ground and his faith remained a testimony.
cases.offense: Abel brought the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof, and the Lord had respect unto Abel and his offering (Genesis 4:4). His gift was not described merely by its presence at the altar: the firstlings and the fat are specifically named. The later commands concerning the firstborn and the Lord's portion of the fat give precepts for the honour shown in that offering (Exodus 13:12; Leviticus 3:16). Hebrews supplies the decisive testimony: by faith Abel offered a more excellent sacrifice than Cain and obtained witness that he was righteous (Hebrews 11:4). His obedience cannot be reduced to the material of the gift while forgetting the man who brought it. John likewise distinguishes the brothers by their works: Cain's were evil and Abel's righteous (1 John 3:12). Worship and conduct belonged to the same account before God.
cases.judgment: God testified of Abel's gifts, and Christ named him righteous Abel (Hebrews 11:4; Matthew 23:35). His brother's violence did not reverse that judgment. The man rejected by Cain was accepted by God, and the blood shed in the field was not beyond God's hearing (Genesis 4:8-10). Being dead, he yet speaks. Hebrews preserves his faith as a witness after his life was taken; Genesis preserves the cry of his blood. The blessing was a righteous standing before God, not immunity from the wickedness of another. His case condemns envy without making the victim's death evidence against his obedience. Christ places Abel at the beginning of the blood of the prophets shed from the foundation of the world (Luke 11:49-51). His witness therefore reaches beyond the offering itself: righteous works drew his brother's hatred, and the murder of the righteous became a pattern repeated against God's messengers (1 John 3:12). Cain silenced his brother's voice in the field, but could not silence the testimony God gave of him.

verses.text: And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
That thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the Lord’s.
And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour: all the fat is the Lord’s.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

entries.commentary: Here is the birth of trade and of religion with Cain and Abel: Abel a keeper of sheep, Cain a tiller of the ground.

The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth. Remember the earth was cursed in chapter 3, so it was hard to get fruit out of the ground; that is part of why Cain was angry.

The Most High is calling Cain to repent. Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained at [Genesis 3:21](/bible/genesis/3#v21). If Cain would not repent, sin lay at the door; he would become subject to Satan and Satan would rule over him.
When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet.
Cain was cursed from the earth and made a fugitive and a vagabond, the same low estate spoken of the serpent in chapter 3.

Every one that findeth me shall slay me is proof in the pudding, like we brought out in [Genesis 1](/bible/genesis/1), that there were more people on the earth than Adam's household. The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning Cain looked like everybody else, and the Most High marked him so that any finding him would not kill him.

Cain found his wife in the land of Nod; there were already people on the earth during the time of Adam. Cain built a city, and you do not build a city for three people; this is more proof that the earth was peopled. The lands in those days were named after men, which is why the land was called Nod. Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names.

This is the first time you read about a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it. In the beginning it was one wife. When you read about the sons of God in [Genesis 5](/bible/genesis/5) you do not read about them taking multiple wives; only the sons of the wicked.
An instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: these men started making weapons. This is the first you read about weapons being created.

Lamech was murdering men; Satan was working with the sons of the wicked. Lamech knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain's sevenfold, saying seventy and sevenfold. They knew the commandments during that time.

Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works, for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and lay them on men's shoulders, but will not move them with one of their fingers.

All their works they do for to be seen of men. They love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the markets. He that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Woe unto you: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. They devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer, and shall receive the greater damnation. There is a lesson in what they would not do. Where leadership provokes a man to works and he finds himself falling behind, he should take it to heart, because telling people who they are without putting in the labour yields no fruit.

They compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Their rules about swearing by the gold rather than the temple, and by the gift rather than the altar, are called out as blindness: the temple sanctifies the gold and the altar sanctifies the gift.

They pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin and have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

They make clean the outside of the cup and platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Cleanse first that which is within. They are likened unto whited sepulchres, beautiful outward but within full of dead men's bones. Outwardly they appear righteous unto men, but within are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

They build the tombs of the prophets and say they would not have shed their blood, and by saying it they witness against themselves that they are the children of them which killed the prophets. Upon them comes all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias. This is the plainest speaking in the gospel. Christ was no soft man with these teachers of the law who did not believe it.
O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine. The firstborn belong to the Most High.

Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place, and no leavened bread is eaten. This day came ye out in the month Abib: the first month of the year, falling at the first new moon of the spring.

When the Lord brings Israel into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey, this service is kept in this month: seven days of unleavened bread, and in the seventh day a feast to the Lord, with no leaven seen in all thy quarters. Thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt. It is a sign upon thine hand and a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord's law may be in thy mouth. Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year: the Passover is kept every year.

All that openeth the matrix is set apart unto the Lord; the matrix is the womb. Every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast, the males are the Lord's. Every firstling of an ass is redeemed with a lamb, and if not redeemed its neck is broken; and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.

When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? thou shalt say, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage: when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, the Lord slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, therefore the firstborn are sacrificed or redeemed. The children must be taught the righteousness of why the feast is kept. Ask the children of this land why they keep Christmas and they answer that Santa Claus is coming down the chimney; Israel's children are to be taught the works of the Most High instead. It is for a token upon thine hand and for frontlets between thine eyes, for by strength of hand the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt.

When Pharaoh let the people go, God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near, lest peradventure the people repent when they see war and return to Egypt. Israel would have been fearful at the sight of the Philistine army and turned back. The people felt a false security in Egypt: in the wilderness they murmured for the fish, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick of Egypt and loathed the light bread; and when the Assyrians came, Israel again ran down to Egypt for help. The same spirit holds the people in America today: a little job, government assistance, a car, food from the store, and they never want this kingdom to come down. But the Most High has something much greater in store: the world, the earth, and many mansions. So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.
Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

They took their journey from Succoth and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness. The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, to go by day and night. The peace offering of the herd, whether male or female, must be offered without blemish before the Lord: no bruise, no cut, no stain, nothing superfluous like an extra member. Whatever the sacrifice is for the Lord, it has to be the best of the best, a flawless sacrifice. The Passover lamb shows how that was carried out. The lamb was without blemish, a male of the first year, taken out from the sheep and kept from the goats, because if it got in a fight it would take a blemish, a bruise, a cut. It was kept up to the fourteenth day, isolated and given nothing but water, so that it purified itself; and it was eaten roast with fire, not raw and not sodden with water, with the purtenance thereof, for after those days there was nothing left within it.

The peace offering could be of the herd or of the flock, a lamb or a goat, male or female without blemish, unlike the burnt offering of chapter 1, which was a male. The offerer laid his hand upon the head of his offering and killed it at the door of the tabernacle, and Aaron's sons sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about. The blood, the fat that covers the inwards, the two kidneys with the fat upon them by the flanks, and the caul above the liver were the Lord's, burned upon the altar, the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour; the breast and the right shoulder were for the priest. All the fat is the Lord's.

It shall be a perpetual statute that ye eat neither fat nor blood. This is a controversial scripture: brothers and sisters ask whether we are cut off for eating fat. Having that question is a good thing; it means you are reading to understand, not reading just to say you read four chapters. [Leviticus 7](/bible/leviticus/7) answers it in context: whosoever eateth the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord shall be cut off. This is the law of sacrifice, which we are no longer under; Christ is the end of the law for righteousness. The sacrifices stopped after 70 AD at the fall of Jerusalem, when there was no longer a temple. And there is no way to take off all the fat of the meat you eat; we are not koshering our meat.

cases.name: Cain
cases.charge: Murder of his brother Abel
cases.summary: Cain brought of the fruit of the ground and Abel brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. The Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering, and not unto Cain's, and Cain was very wroth. He was called to repent, and warned that if he did not, sin lay at the door. He talked with Abel in the field and slew him, then answered God with a lie and a taunt.
cases.offense: When God did not regard Cain's offering, Cain became very wroth and his countenance fell. Before the murder, God addressed him: if he did well, he would be accepted; if not, sin lay at the door (Genesis 4:3-7). The warning made room for repentance. Rejection of the offering did not require him to become a murderer. Cain answered his brother's righteousness with violence. In the field he rose against Abel and slew him, then denied knowledge of him and asked whether he was his brother's keeper (Genesis 4:8-9). John names the motive plainly: Cain was of that wicked one, and slew his brother because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous (1 John 3:12). He would destroy the man whose conduct exposed his own instead of doing the good set before him. The warning of sin at the door and Peter's warning of the devouring adversary belong together (Genesis 4:7; 1 Peter 5:8). Anger nourished rather than corrected becomes an opening for further evil. The offering, the fallen countenance, the killing, and the lie show a course of refusal, not an unavoidable act forced upon him by God's rebuke.
cases.judgment: Abel's blood cried from the ground. The earth that received it would no longer yield its strength to Cain, and he was made a fugitive and a vagabond (Genesis 4:10-12). His work as a tiller was struck by the sentence. He could not bury the deed and continue as though the ground held no witness against him.
offenseFull: When God did not regard Cain's offering, Cain became very wroth and his countenance fell. Before the murder, God addressed him: if he did well, he would be accepted; if not, sin lay at the door (Genesis 4:3-7). The warning made room for repentance. He would destroy the man whose conduct exposed his own instead of doing the good set before him.

The warning of sin at the door and Peter's warning of the devouring adversary belong together (Genesis 4:7; 1 Peter 5:8). Anger nourished rather than corrected becomes an opening for further evil. entries.commentary: Here is the birth of trade and of religion with Cain and Abel: Abel a keeper of sheep, Cain a tiller of the ground.

The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth. Remember the earth was cursed in chapter 3, so it was hard to get fruit out of the ground; that is part of why Cain was angry.

The Most High is calling Cain to repent. Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained at [Genesis 3:21](/bible/genesis/3#v21). If Cain would not repent, sin lay at the door; he would become subject to Satan and Satan would rule over him.
When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet.
Cain was cursed from the earth and made a fugitive and a vagabond, the same low estate spoken of the serpent in chapter 3.

Every one that findeth me shall slay me is proof in the pudding, like we brought out in [Genesis 1](/bible/genesis/1), that there were more people on the earth than Adam's household. The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning Cain looked like everybody else, and the Most High marked him so that any finding him would not kill him.

Cain found his wife in the land of Nod; there were already people on the earth during the time of Adam. Cain built a city, and you do not build a city for three people; this is more proof that the earth was peopled. The lands in those days were named after men, which is why the land was called Nod. Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names.

This is the first time you read about a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it. In the beginning it was one wife. When you read about the sons of God in [Genesis 5](/bible/genesis/5) you do not read about them taking multiple wives; only the sons of the wicked.
An instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: these men started making weapons. This is the first you read about weapons being created.

Lamech was murdering men; Satan was working with the sons of the wicked. Lamech knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain's sevenfold, saying seventy and sevenfold. They knew the commandments during that time.

Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

verses.text: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:

And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.

cases.name: Lamech
cases.charge: Killing a man and boasting of it; claiming seventy-sevenfold vengeance
cases.summary: Lamech of Cain's line told his wives Adah and Zillah of a killing and claimed seventy-sevenfold vengeance for himself against Cain's sevenfold. His declaration is preserved without a separate sentence executed upon him. Protection pronounced by God over Cain had become a man's boast about his own vengeance.
cases.offense: Lamech of Cain's line took two wives, Adah and Zillah, and addressed them concerning a man he had slain to his wounding and a young man to his hurt (Genesis 4:19,23). His speech culminated in a claim of vengeance: if Cain were avenged sevenfold, Lamech would be seventy and sevenfold (Genesis 4:24). The protection God had pronounced over Cain became the measure of his own boast. God had restrained others from killing Cain; Lamech spoke as though that restraint authorized an even greater claim for himself. He made no recorded appeal for repentance or forgiveness. Vengeance was being treated as a man's possession to enlarge, although the Lord declares that vengeance belongs to him (Deuteronomy 32:35). A divine limit upon retaliation cannot rightly be turned into permission to threaten more of it.
cases.judgment: Genesis gives no separate sentence executed upon this Lamech. His speech is preserved as testimony to the violence and self-exaltation within Cain's genealogy, before the account turns to Seth and those who called upon the Lord (Genesis 4:23-26). The absence of a narrated punishment does not make his claim God's promise. Romans 12:19 commands the hearer not to avenge himself but to leave recompense to the Lord. Lamech's seventy-sevenfold is his own declaration; it is not the Lord extending Cain's protection by a new command.

And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

lawDetails.text: Avenge not yourselves, for vengeance is in God's hands.
All boasting and bragging is wicked.
The restitution and punishment should be according to the crime--Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth. The song opens by calling heaven and earth to witness, just as Moses said in chapter 31. Notice how the verses run together: my doctrine shall drop as the rain, and then, because I will publish the name of the Lord. Doctrine and the name go together, and greatness is ascribed unto our God.

He is the Rock, his work is perfect, all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he. The song gives the Most High his praise first, then turns to what happens when Israel corrupts themselves. They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: the Most High planted us a noble vine, and we became a degenerate plant. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us; we are a perverse and crooked generation.

Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? This is how you repay the magnificent Lord that delivered you, that destroyed whole nations just so you could inherit their land. Is not he thy father that hath bought thee? Hath he not made thee, and established thee? Isaiah recounts the lovingkindness of the Most High toward the house of Israel: he said, surely they are my people, children that will not lie, so he was their Savior. In all our affliction he was afflicted; whenever he saw us going through atrocities he suffered with us, and in his love and in his pity he redeemed us and carried us all the days of old. How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee. Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Did you know the many generations of your forefathers? Somebody had to show you. The men teaching on the corners and bringing out these prophecies and breakdowns are the ones Moses said would teach you these things: ask thy father, and he will shew thee. Inquire of the former age and prepare thyself to the search of thy fathers: study who we were, see where our fathers went wrong, and do not do the same thing. When we suffer persecution and trials we can go to the scriptures and see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers; that is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves. Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. You thought God wants everybody to just come together and hold hands? The God of this Bible has been a God of division from day one; he separated the sons of Adam according to where he had to place the children of Israel, meaning this world revolves around Israel. For the Lord's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. In the division of the nations he set a ruler over every people, but Israel he kept for himself: that is my inheritance, that is my portion.

He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye. The same people the world counted as three fifths of a man are the apple of the Most High's eye. Zechariah shows who that people is: deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Who was held captive in the land of the north, in North America, but the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans? We are Zion, and we must deliver ourselves from the ways we were taught there. He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye: the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns.

As an eagle stirreth up her nest and beareth her young on her wings, so the Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him. The Most High used no idol of wood or stone to lead us through the wilderness and protect us from the nations; he did that alone. He made him ride on the high places of the earth, to eat the increase of the fields, honey out of the rock, butter of kine and milk of sheep, the fat of lambs and rams, and the pure blood of the grape. This is the journey through the wilderness, how Israel came through all those nations and acquired wealth and provision from the Most High's own hand.

But Jeshurun, meaning Israel, waxed fat, and kicked; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. Waxing fat is not about being overweight; [Deuteronomy 8](/bible/deuteronomy/8) explains it. When thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and thy herds and thy silver and thy gold are multiplied, then thine heart is lifted up and thou forgettest the Lord thy God which brought thee out of the house of bondage. With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God; we get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High.

They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods; they sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not. What are examples of new gods? Islam came about in 622 AD, some six hundred years after Christ. The familiar image of Christ painted in the Renaissance era is a new thing under the sun. Even Buddha, whom people think is ancient, came on the scene between the sixth and fourth centuries BC; our kingdom had already been split and carried captive into Babylon before anybody heard of a Buddha. These are new gods that our people go crazy over today, and the Most High said we would come to that estate.

Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee. When it comes to the Rock that created us, we are unmindful. Who is that Rock? Paul says our fathers drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. Christ did not begin two thousand years after Moses; he was with Israel in the wilderness. David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

When the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons and of his daughters; he said, I will hide my face from them, for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. This goes especially into Judah, the southern kingdom: when Christ was on the scene, the scribes and Pharisees rejected him; they were very froward and had no faith that he was the Son of God, and Christ called them a generation of vipers. They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God, and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people. Some close the book right there and say the Most High welcomed all the other nations in place of Israel; no, the ones which are not a people are also Israel. Isaiah says within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people; and Hosea says of the northern kingdom, ye are not my people, yet in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

For a fire is kindled in mine anger; I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them: burning hunger, bitter destruction, and the teeth of beasts sent upon them. You have seen the clips from the civil rights movement, the canines sent at our people to rip at them with their teeth. That was a fulfillment of prophecy: the Most High said he would send the teeth of beasts against us. The sword without, and terror within, destroying young man and virgin, the suckling with the man of gray hairs: the sword of the other nations, and famine and drought as well. This prophecy had to happen against us because we served other gods.

I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. What corners? Isaiah shows the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah gathered from the four corners of the earth: the scattering was worldwide. What nation of people has been scattered throughout the four corners of the earth by slave trades, the transatlantic, the sub-Saharan, the silk road? The so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. This never happened to the people claiming our heritage; it is further proof of who the children of Israel are. The nations we were scattered to took counsel together: come, let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. Divide them, teach them they are not who they really are: if I get them to take pride in being called anything but Israel, they will never remember. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, but the remembrance has not completely ceased.

Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this. The Most High would not let the enemy think they accomplished the complete destruction of the Israelites by their own hand; that is why, after a certain amount of time, he begins waking us up, and why we are starting to remember who we are this day. For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them. O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end. If you knew exactly what disaster was coming and when, you would set every alarm; our forefathers were told all these atrocities ahead of time and still did not consider it. How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had shut them up? How could we be conquered the way we were, thousands rounded up by a few, unless the Most High allowed it? It had to be the Lord.

For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges. For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: that is why the sins of Sodom show up among our people today, even paraded as pride. The Most High said our vine became the vine of Sodom; their grapes are grapes of gall, their wine is the poison of dragons. Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures? These prophecies were sealed up with the Most High until their time.

To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand. After he let these nations deceive and oppress us for so long, the Most High will show who God really is; but he had to let us humble ourselves first for serving all those false gods. For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants: he will change his mind, and instead of inflicting wrath upon us he will save us. When he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left: when he sees that we have fallen to our lowest estate possible, then he moves.

And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted? Now that you are being shot down in the street, locked in cages, where are the idols and the saints you prayed to? Let them rise up and help you. The Most High had to let it play out over a span of time, allowing enemies to afflict us, so we would see that the gods we went off to worship were not real gods, because they could not help when the Lord sent the enemy against us. Jeremiah says our people say to a stock, Thou art my father, and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth; but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us. Where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? Let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods. That is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities; that is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day.

See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand. A statue you made with your hands cannot kill a thing and cannot make alive; the true God does both. That is the terrible God we serve, the God of our people, and once his people get back on his good side, the nations that touched the apple of his eye have judgment coming.

For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever. The Most High will eventually turn back to save us; he will stop hiding his face and come to our defense. If I whet my glittering sword, and mine hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me. I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh; and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy. The Most High takes revenge for the captives, because he is the God of the people that have been in captivity over and over again. In the churches they never read this; they never knew that God is this way, and it shows what they really think about him.

Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people. Read through the Bible: Christ put to death, James put to death, Peter put to death, and since the Bible was written more prophets have lost their lives for the truth, and it will continue. The innocent and righteous blood crieth unto the Most High, and the souls of the just complain continually, asking when he will act; and he answers, I will surely avenge them. This is fulfilled in the destruction of Babylon: rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets, for God hath avenged you on her. Babylon the great in this teaching is the United States of America; that is where the Lord makes his arrows drunk with blood, the vengeance promised for all the wrong these nations have done unto us.

Moses and Joshua spake all the words of this song in the ears of the people, and Moses said, Set your hearts unto all the words which I testify among you this day, which ye shall command your children to observe to do. For it is not a vain thing for you; because it is your life. The words of this law are not something to sit on your dashboard or in your cabinet; this book is your life, and if you are not reading it, you are not living. Through this thing ye shall prolong your days in the land: not just eating right or exercising, but doing this law is how you prolong your days.

That selfsame day the Most High tells Moses: get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, over against Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan; and die in the mount, as Aaron died in mount Hor, because ye trespassed against me at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh, because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel. The account is in Numbers 20: the people angered Moses at the waters of strife, complaining and provoking him after all they had already seen, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes. They provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips: Hear now, ye rebels; and he smote the rock twice instead of speaking to it, the Rock we read about earlier in this chapter. Thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither.

cases.name: Enoch
cases.charge: Walking with God three hundred years
cases.summary: Enoch walked with God, begat sons and daughters, and was not, for God took him. Hebrews says he was translated that he should not see death and had testimony that he pleased God. Jude preserves his warning of judgment upon ungodly deeds and speeches.
cases.offense: Enoch walked with God after the birth of Methuselah for three hundred years and begat sons and daughters (Genesis 5:21-24). The testimony describes a sustained course amid the responsibilities of a household. Walking with God was not confined to a single occasion of danger or a single offering. Jude names him as the seventh from Adam and preserves his prophecy of the Lord coming with ten thousands of his saints to execute judgment upon ungodly deeds and hard speeches (Jude 1:14-15). His walk included testimony against the evil around him. The standard was not the approval of his generation, but the judgment of the Lord he proclaimed.
cases.judgment: Genesis says that he was not, for God took him. Hebrews explains that by faith he was translated that he should not see death, and that before his translation he had testimony that he pleased God (Genesis 5:24; Hebrews 11:5). His disappearance was not presented as failure or abandonment, but as God's taking of the faithful man. The next verse makes the principle available to the hearer: without faith it is impossible to please God, and those who come to him must believe that he rewards those who diligently seek him (Hebrews 11:6). Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) calls Enoch an example of repentance to all generations (Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 44:16). His particular deliverance remains God's act, while the call to seek and please God continues beyond his generation.

verses.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:
And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years:

cases.name: The sons of God and the giants
cases.charge: Leaving their proper estate; taking wives of the daughters of men
cases.summary: The sons of God took wives of all whom they chose, seeing that the daughters of men were fair. The account follows Adam's genealogy and proceeds to the earth's corruption and violence. Mighty men of renown did not preserve that world from judgment. The Lord declared that his spirit would not always strive with man.
cases.offense: After the genealogy of Adam through Seth, Genesis records the sons of God taking wives of all whom they chose because the daughters of men were fair (Genesis 5:1-3; Genesis 6:1-2). The sequence sets the lineage entrusted with godly responsibility beside choices governed by outward attraction. The distinction of a holy calling was not to be surrendered to whatever the eye desired.
cases.judgment: The angels are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. The giants and the world they filled with violence went under the Flood; Noah alone was carried through.

entries.commentary: The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter 5; that is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men. The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis. It was already known, and Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan.
Here the Most High shortened the lifespan of man to a hundred and twenty years. In chapter 5 the forefathers lived seven, eight, and nine hundred years.

The giants in the earth came from the sons of God intermingling with the other nations, and the children born to them became mighty men of renown. The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men of [Genesis 6:4](/bible/genesis/6#v4); they came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God. Another word for angel is messenger.

Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord; he was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood.
The ark was a literal boat, made of gopher wood.

At this time the animals were vegetarian; that is why the Most High explained to Noah to gather food for himself, for his family, and for the animals, and why the animals did not eat one another on the ark.

Noah did all that the Most High commanded him by faith. Up to that time rain had never been seen; it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened. While the ark was preparing, Noah was a preacher of righteousness, telling his people to repent, and the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them to repent. Eight souls were saved by water; the ones that were actually in the water died, so this is not talking about getting baptized. As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

cases.name: Noah
cases.charge: Doing according to all that God commanded him
cases.summary: In a world where every imagination of man's heart was only evil continually, one man was just and perfect in his generations and walked with God. He was told to build an ark and did it exactly, and he and his house were the only ones saved through the flood.
cases.offense: Noah found grace in the Lord's eyes, was just and perfect in his generations, and walked with God while the earth was corrupt and filled with violence (Genesis 6:8-13). He was given a work whose form was specified: the ark's material, rooms, covering, dimensions, door, and stories (Genesis 6:14-16). His faith took the shape of carrying out what he had been told. He also had to gather food and bring living creatures into the ark. Genesis 7 distinguishes the clean beasts taken by sevens from the unclean taken by two (Genesis 6:19-22; Genesis 7:2-5). The distinctions were part of the command, not details he was free to discard. Twice the account records that he did according to all the Lord commanded him. Hebrews says he was warned of things not seen as yet and moved with fear to prepare for the saving of his house (Hebrews 11:7). Peter calls him a preacher of righteousness (2 Peter 2:5). Preparation and testimony belonged together: he acted upon the warning instead of waiting for the destruction to prove it true.
cases.judgment: The Lord called Noah's household into the ark and shut him in; Noah and those with him were preserved when the judgment overtook the earth (Genesis 7:1,16,23). His household benefited from a faith expressed in sustained work. Hebrews calls him an heir of the righteousness which is by faith, not merely a survivor of danger. Afterward he built an altar and offered of the clean beasts and fowls. God established the covenant with Noah, his seed, and every living creature, promising that a flood would not again destroy all flesh and setting the bow in the cloud as its token (Genesis 8:20-22; Genesis 9:8-17). The renewed earth also carried commands: replenish it, abstain from blood, and reckon with God's requirement of human life (Genesis 9:1-6). Deliverance opened a continuing duty, not freedom from God's rule.

verses.text: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
A window shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.
And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; and every thing that is in the earth shall die.
But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons’ wives with thee.
And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee; they shall be male and female.
Of fowls after their kind, and of cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the earth after his kind, two of every sort shall come unto thee, to keep them alive.
And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt gather it to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
And the Lord said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
And Noah builded an altar unto the Lord; and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

And the Lord smelled a sweet savour; and the Lord said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.
While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moveth upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.
Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.
But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.
And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.
Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.
And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.
And God spake unto Noah, and to his sons with him, saying,
And I, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you;
And with every living creature that is with you, of the fowl, of the cattle, and of every beast of the earth with you; from all that go out of the ark, to every beast of the earth.
And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud:
And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.
And God said unto Noah, This is the token of the covenant, which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.

By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord God.

entries.commentary: The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter 5; that is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men. The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis. It was already known, and Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan.
Here the Most High shortened the lifespan of man to a hundred and twenty years. In chapter 5 the forefathers lived seven, eight, and nine hundred years.

The giants in the earth came from the sons of God intermingling with the other nations, and the children born to them became mighty men of renown. The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men of [Genesis 6:4](/bible/genesis/6#v4); they came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God. Another word for angel is messenger.

Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord; he was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood.
The ark was a literal boat, made of gopher wood.

At this time the animals were vegetarian; that is why the Most High explained to Noah to gather food for himself, for his family, and for the animals, and why the animals did not eat one another on the ark.

Noah did all that the Most High commanded him by faith. Up to that time rain had never been seen; it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened. While the ark was preparing, Noah was a preacher of righteousness, telling his people to repent, and the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them to repent. Eight souls were saved by water; the ones that were actually in the water died, so this is not talking about getting baptized. As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

The dietary law was not yet instituted, but the Most High had already defined what was a clean beast and what was an unclean beast, all the way back in Genesis; Moses reiterated that law to the children of Israel. Today this gets confused with the doctrine that says I can eat all things through Christ who strengthens me, and that is not true; the laws were instituted for us to discern between the unclean and the clean. The beasts went in male and female to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth, so that they could repopulate once the earth dried up; nature itself tells you what we should and should not be doing.

Up until this point it had never rained on the earth; a mist went up from the earth and watered the ground. Understand the faith Noah had to have, being told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened.

The great deep is the seas, the rivers, and the oceans. The windows of heaven are the sky, the firmament, and their opening is the rain. This is the first time it ever rained on the earth, and when the rain came it came with destruction.

This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done. The flood came because they despised the commandments; destruction came because of sin. Of them that dwelt in the world only Noah and his household were left, of whom came all righteous men: through Shem's seed to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and through their line the Israelites. The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.
The windows of heaven being stopped and the rain from heaven being restrained shows you that the windows of heaven refer to the rain.

Noah built an altar and offered burnt offerings of every clean beast and every clean fowl, and the Most High smelled a sweet savour and said He would not again curse the ground any more for man's sake. An everlasting covenant was made with Noah that all flesh should perish no more by a flood. Before it was water; the next time it is going to be fire, so let us get our minds right. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)
Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.
The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.
The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3).

Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses. The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31).

The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.
The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18) opens those laws.

Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

Certain of the elders of Israel came and sat before Ezekiel, and the word of the Lord said these men have set up their idols in their hearts, setting up something above God, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. The Most High asks whether He should be inquired of at all by them. Every man of the house of Israel that sets up his idols in his heart and comes to the prophet, the Lord will answer according to the multitude of his idols, that He may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from Him through their idols and spiritual idolatry.

The Most High tells the house of Israel to repent, come back to His laws, and turn themselves from their idols and away from all their abominations. Every one of the house of Israel, or the stranger that sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from Him and sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet to inquire, the Lord will answer by Himself and set His face against that man. He will make him a sign and a proverb, meaning a curse, and cut him off from the midst of His people as an example, that they may know He is the Lord.

If a prophet is deceived when he has spoken a thing, the Lord Himself has deceived that prophet; do not try to deceive yourself in this truth, and when we get counsel we should take it and keep it moving. He will stretch out His hand upon that prophet and destroy him from the midst of His people Israel, and both shall bear the punishment of their iniquity. This is so the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God. -

The word of the Lord came saying that when a land sins by trespassing grievously, He will stretch out His hand upon it, break the staff of its bread, and send famine to cut off man and beast. Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness. No one can save anyone else; it does not matter who you are or what your status is in Israel, you have to save yourself by your own righteousness.

If He causes noisome beasts to pass through the land and spoil it so that it is desolate and no man may pass through, this is one of His judgments. Though these three men were in it, as the Lord lives they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered by their righteousness, but the land shall be desolate.

If He brings a sword upon that land to cut off man and beast, though these three men were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters. They only shall deliver themselves by their righteousness.

If He sends a pestilence into the land and pours out His fury upon it in blood to cut off man and beast, though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter. They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness; everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling, delivering their own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments. -

How much more when the Most High sends His four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, the famine, the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off man and beast; and these are not just for back then but for today. Behold, a remnant shall be left, both sons and daughters, that shall be brought forth unto you, and you shall see their ways and their doings. You shall be comforted concerning the evil the Most High brought upon Jerusalem when you see their ways, and you shall know He has not done without cause all that He has done in it. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)
