cases.name: The generation of the Flood
cases.charge: Corruption and violence filling the earth
cases.summary: A whole world under judgment. The earth was filled with violence and every imagination of the heart was continually evil, so God resolved to blot out what he had made, sparing only Noah's household.
cases.offense: God saw that the wickedness of man was great and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. The earth was corrupt before him and filled with violence (Genesis 6:5-13). The judgment addressed both inward intention and outward harm: corrupt thoughts had become a corrupt way of life. Christ later recalled people eating, drinking, and marrying until the day Noah entered the ark (Matthew 24:37-39). Ordinary activity continued around an extraordinary warning. The danger was not that a meal or marriage was itself the offense named in Genesis, but that people continued without heeding the judgment coming upon their wickedness. God's longsuffering while the ark was preparing did not mean that the warning had been withdrawn (1 Peter 3:20).
cases.judgment: All in whose nostrils was the breath of life upon the dry land died, and Noah only remained alive with those who were in the ark (Genesis 7:21-23). Peter identifies the preserved household as eight souls (1 Peter 3:20). The waters that bore up the ark overtook the world outside it; provision had to be received before the destruction came.

The earth was corrupt before him and filled with violence (Genesis 6:5-13). The judgment addressed both inward intention and outward harm: corrupt thoughts had become a corrupt way of life.

Of the buildings of the temple he says there shall not be left here one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down, and on the mount of Olives the disciples ask when, and what shall be the sign.

Take heed that no man deceive you. Many shall come in my name saying I am Christ, and shall deceive many. Wars and rumours of wars, nation against nation, famines, pestilences and earthquakes are all the beginning of sorrows, not the end.

Ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake, many shall be offended and betray one another, and because iniquity shall abound the love of many shall wax cold. He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. That verse alone answers any man who says he is already saved and has nothing left to endure.
This gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations, and then shall the end come.
The abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place. That has a fulfilment already in history, when swine's flesh was offered in the temple.

Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains, and pray that the flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day. Then shall be great tribulation such as was not since the beginning of the world, and except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved; but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened.

False Christs and false prophets shall shew great signs and wonders, insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Go not forth after them. As the lightning cometh out of the east and shineth even unto the west, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven. He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds. That gathering is itself proof of a people scattered to the four winds.

Learn a parable of the fig tree: when his branch is yet tender and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh. So likewise when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

Of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. As the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be: eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, and they knew not until the flood came and took them all away.

Blessed is that servant whom his lord when he cometh shall find giving the household meat in due season, and he shall be made ruler over all his goods. The evil servant says in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming, and begins to smite his fellowservants; his lord comes in a day he looks not for him and appoints him his portion with the hypocrites. Watching is not only watching the prophecy come to pass. It is keeping a watchful eye on your own spirit, because what is not repented of is what a man will be judged for.

In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city I was in Babylon, and lay troubled upon my bed, and my thoughts came up over my heart. I saw the desolation of Sion, and the wealth of them that dwelt at Babylon; and my spirit was sore moved, so that I began to speak words full of fear to the most High. Thou gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. Unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way, which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations. In process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them; nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.

When they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, they began again to be more ungodly than the first. Thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham: him thou lovedst, and made an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed. Unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac thou gavest Jacob and Esau: as for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau. When thou leddest his seed out of Egypt, thou broughtest them up to the mount Sinai, and bowing the heavens thou didst set fast the earth, and madest the depths to tremble. Thy glory went through four gates, of fire, and of earthquake, and of wind, and of cold; that thou mightest give the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel.

Yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart, that thy law might bring forth fruit in them. For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him. Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law also in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still. Thou raisedst up a servant, called David, whom thou commandedst to build a city unto thy name, and to offer incense and oblations unto thee therein. When this was done many years, then they that inhabited the city forsook thee, and in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done; and so thou gavest the city over into the hands of thine enemies.

Are their deeds any better that inhabit Babylon, that they should therefore have the dominion over Sion? When I came thither, and had seen impieties without number, then my soul saw many evildoers in this thirtieth year, so that my heart failed me. I have seen how thou sufferest them sinning, and hast spared the wicked doers, and hast destroyed thy people, and hast preserved thine enemies. Are they then of Babylon better than they of Sion? or is there any other people that knoweth thee beside Israel? or what generation hath so believed thy covenants as Jacob? For I have gone here and there through the heathen, and I see that they flow in wealth, and think not upon thy commandments. Weigh thou therefore our wickedness now in the balance, and theirs also that dwell in the world; and so shall thy name no where be found but in Israel. Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

cases.name: Ham and the curse on Canaan
cases.charge: Seeing his father's nakedness and telling his brothers
cases.summary: Noah planted a vineyard, drank of the wine, was drunken, and was uncovered within his tent. Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brethren without. Shem and Japheth took a garment on both their shoulders, went backward, and covered their father, and their faces were backward so that they saw not his nakedness. When Noah awoke he cursed Canaan.
cases.offense: Noah drank wine, became drunken, and lay uncovered within his tent. Ham saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers outside. Shem and Japheth took a garment upon their shoulders, went backward, and covered him without looking upon his nakedness (Genesis 9:20-23). Their conduct supplies the contrast: they met the exposure with a covering rather than making it an occasion to look and tell. The duty to honour father and mother remains when a parent's weakness is visible (Exodus 20:12). Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) warns that a man's glory comes from the honour of his father and that parental dishonour is a reproach to the children (Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 3:10-11). Noah's recorded righteousness did not require concealing the account of his drunkenness, and his drunkenness did not give his son permission to treat his exposure without honour. The brothers showed what respectful action required in that moment.
cases.judgment: Awaking from his wine and knowing what his younger son had done, Noah pronounced the curse upon Canaan: a servant of servants would he be unto his brethren (Genesis 9:24-25). The text names Canaan, not all of Ham's descendants, as the object of this sentence. Neither a curse upon every African people nor a statement about skin colour is written here. Noah blessed the Lord God of Shem and spoke of Japheth's enlargement and dwelling in Shem's tents, repeating Canaan's servitude (Genesis 9:26-27). The different parties must remain distinct. The account gives the conduct, the contrasting honour of the brothers, and Noah's words, without explaining every reason why the curse fell upon Canaan. What is withheld cannot be supplied by expanding the sentence beyond the person it names.

verses.text: And Noah began to be an husbandman, and he planted a vineyard:
And he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.

And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father’s nakedness.
And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done unto him.
And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.
And he said, Blessed be the Lord God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.
God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.
The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover: she is thy mother; thou shalt not uncover her nakedness.
Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen.
Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.
For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father; and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.

lawDetails.text: Honor your father and your mother.

entries.commentary: Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.
The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.
The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3).

Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses. The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31).

The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.
The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18) opens those laws.

Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians, and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt. The same word stands for us: when the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom. The land of Canaan was full of idols. If Israel obeyed His voice the Most High would be an enemy to their enemies, bless their bread and water, and take sickness away; the charge in Canaan was not to bow to their gods nor do after their works, but to utterly overthrow them and break down their images. Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

Keep the statutes and judgments of the Most High, which if a man do, he shall live in them. The Ten Commandments are not the whole of the law but a summary. Under the Sabbath commandment sit sub-statutes such as no buying, no selling, no working; likewise under the law of adultery sit all the laws of this chapter, the ordinances of marriage and the forbidden beds. None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to uncover their nakedness; these laws name who a man may not lay down with.

The nakedness of thy father's wife is thy father's nakedness; that is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked. This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did.

The sister, whether born at home or born abroad, and the son's daughter and the daughter's daughter are all forbidden; the grandchildren's nakedness is thine own nakedness. There are sick spirits out there, and some of them are grandfathers, uncles, and fathers. Be careful and mindful who you leave your children around; do not hand your children to just anybody for the sake of your own pleasure.

The father's sister, the mother's sister, and the wife of the father's brother, thine aunt, are all near kinswomen and off limits. Incest is still practiced among the nations of this land, and children born of incestuous unions often carry defects and disabilities; the law guards the seed.

The daughter in law, the brother's wife, and a woman with her daughter or her granddaughter are all forbidden; it is wickedness. Neither take a wife to her sister to vex her, to uncover her nakedness beside the other in her lifetime; that also shuts down what the world today calls threesomes.

A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15) details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class.
To lie carnally with thy neighbour's wife is adultery. This world even sings songs celebrating adultery; the law forbids defiling thyself with her.

Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them, as Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem slaying the children of the Most High. The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

Abomination means a thing that causes disgust or hatred. When a man lies with mankind as with womankind, the Most High calls it disgusting and hateful. What a man hates and finds disgusting he removes far from himself; so we must teach our people to repent and come out of the things the Most High hates.
Lying with any beast is confusion, for man and for woman alike. The nations have set up places where these strange lusts are fulfilled, and the sin is found among every people; it is all wickedness.

In all these things the nations were defiled which the Most High cast out; the Egyptians and the Canaanites were doing these very abominations, and the land itself was defiled by them. The land spews out the defiled. That is why Israel was put out of Jerusalem: we could not abide in the land with our sins, sacrificing to idol gods and working all manner of evil, so the Most High raised up an enemy to carry us into bondage and remove us out of the land. Whosoever commits any of these abominations, the souls that commit them shall be cut off from among their people, meaning put to death.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

cases.name: The builders of Babel
cases.charge: Building a tower to make themselves a name and resist being scattered
cases.summary: The whole earth was of one language and one speech, and journeying from the east they found a plain in the land of Shinar and dwelt there. They said, let us build us a city and a tower whose top may reach unto heaven, and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth. The Lord came down, confounded their language, and scattered them.
cases.offense: The builders at Shinar shared one language and proposed a city and a tower, naming their purpose themselves: make us a name, lest we be scattered over the earth (Genesis 11:1-4). Their unity was directed toward securing their own name and resisting dispersion. This stands against the charge to Noah's sons to be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth (Genesis 9:1). The Lord saw the people as one, with one language, and declared that nothing would be restrained from what they imagined to do (Genesis 11:6). Agreement alone was no proof of righteousness. The people could combine skill and labour while pursuing an end contrary to God's ordering. Nimrod's kingdom began in Babel and the same land of Shinar (Genesis 10:8-10); the name and place belong to the growth of human power, not an authority above God's judgment.
cases.judgment: The Lord confounded their language so that they could not understand one another's speech, scattered them upon the earth, and they left off building the city (Genesis 11:7-9). The sentence brought about the very dispersion they had resolved to prevent. The tower could not secure its builders against the will of God.

The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31).

The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.
The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18) opens those laws.

Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

And it came to pass, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there.
And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter.

So the Lord scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.
Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the Lord did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the Lord scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.
Moreover, the nations in their wicked conspiracy being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserved him blameless unto God, and kept him strong against his tender compassion toward his son.
Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?

cases.name: Abraham
cases.charge: Obeying the Lord's voice; keeping his charge, his commandments, his statutes, and his laws
cases.summary: Told to leave country, kindred and father's house for a land he would be shewed, he went. Told to offer his only son, he rose early in the morning. The Lord's own account of him, given to Isaac, is the law kept: Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
cases.offense: Three great tests display a faith that acts upon the command. He left country, kindred and father's house for a destination he was not told (Genesis 12:1). He circumcised every male of his house on the day he was commanded (Genesis 17:23), at ninety-nine years old, receiving in his flesh the token of the covenant God had explained to him (Genesis 17:10-14; Genesis 17:24). And when the son through whom the whole promise ran was demanded, he rose early in the morning (Genesis 22:3), which is the detail the record chooses to report. Genesis 18 adds that he was expected to command his household after him to keep the way of the Lord (Genesis 18:19) and to do justice and judgment, and the Lord's own summary in Genesis 26 states the standard he met (Genesis 26:5): he kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws. He believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness (Genesis 15:6). That faith did not end in agreement with a promise. Hebrews explains that, when Isaac was required, Abraham accounted God able to raise him even from the dead (Hebrews 11:17-19). The angel stopped his hand, and he offered the ram provided in his son's stead (Genesis 22:11-13). James joins the offering to the earlier faith: faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect (James 2:21-23).
cases.judgment: The promise was enlarged at each stage and finally sworn. After Moriah God swore by himself, having no greater to swear by, that the seed would be multiplied and that in it all the nations of the earth would be blessed (Genesis 22:15-18), and the ground given is explicit: because thou hast obeyed my voice (Genesis 22:18). He was called the friend of God, and the land covenant was made with his seed (Genesis 15:18; Isaiah 41:8). The promise continued through Isaac and Jacob, and the inheritance was divided among the twelve tribes (Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 44:19-22).

verses.text: Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee:
And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
So Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.
And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house; and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.
And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
In the selfsame day was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his son.
And all the men of his house, born in the house, and bought with money of the stranger, were circumcised with him.
And the Lord said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do;
Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.
And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.

And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.
And the angel of the Lord called unto Abraham out of heaven the second time,
And said, By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son:

That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;
And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.

Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;
And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;
Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,
Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.
Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?
And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

entries.commentary: The Most High called Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred, and from his father's house. He called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. Some hold back from repenting because of what family or friends may say. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out, you have to go. Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.
Abram departed at seventy and five years old, with Sarai and Lot, into the land of Canaan; Canaan is northeast Africa.
Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties.

The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had. The Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Abram asked what the Lord would give him, seeing he went childless and the steward of his house, Eliezer of Damascus, stood to inherit everything. The word came: This shall not be thine heir; he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. The Most High prophesied children to Abram out of his own seed.

Look now toward heaven and tell the stars: so shall thy seed be. Abram believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness. Righteousness is immortal, and righteousness is defined by the law: it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments. Abram's faith showed itself in his works.

Abram divided the heifer, the goat, and the ram, and drove the fowls from the carcases; he was offering sacrifice. When the sun went down a deep sleep and a horror of great darkness fell on Abram: he was about to receive a vision of future prophecy. The Most High speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret to His servants the prophets.

Know of a surety: thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, shall serve them, and be afflicted four hundred years. This prophecy was fulfilled in Egypt; the sojourning of the children of Israel in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and the four hundred was an approximation of that time. This verse is not the doctrine about America and 1619. The northern kingdom's captivity on this side began in 1492, and by that counting the years pass four hundred and Israel is still in captivity and still scattered this day; the prophecy of [Genesis 15:13](/bible/genesis/15#v13) was fulfilled at the Exodus. They came out with great substance: the children of Israel required jewels of silver and gold and raiment of the Egyptians, and they spoiled Egypt as they left. The twelve tribes scattered among the nations today, the people called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, are the seed this covenant history belongs to. Abram himself would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age; and the seed would return in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full.

At ninety and nine years old Abram was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse; Christ said nothing new in [Matthew 5:48](/bible/matthew/5#v48), for the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before. Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself.

When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him. Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The same promise was passed down the seed line: Jacob's name was changed to Israel and told a nation and a company of nations and kings would come out of his loins. The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.
The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him.

Circumcision is the token of the covenant: every man child circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised soul cut off from his people. Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had yet being uncircumcised. He believed and obeyed first, and circumcision sealed it; likewise a brother can come into the truth, get built up in the faith, and then go through with the process. It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac. Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart: shall a child be born to a hundred year old man, and Sarah bear at ninety? The Most High read his thought and named the child from it: Isaac means he will laugh.

Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac. Not all who are of Abraham's seed are the children; in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai's plan, with no word from God ordaining it; the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

The selfsame day Abraham circumcised every male of his house, himself at ninety and nine and Ishmael at thirteen. That is the righteous example: he received the commandment and performed it the same day.

The three men who stood by Abraham were angels of the Lord, and they had bodies: their feet were washed with water, they rested under the tree, and they did eat. Be careful how you deal with people, for some have entertained angels unawares. Abraham hastened to serve them. He commanded his household; he told Sarah, Make ready quickly. That is the level of his hospitality and his leadership.

Sarah was barren from the beginning and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women; she laughed within herself at the promise of a son. The Lord answered the thought she never spoke: Wherefore did Sarah laugh? She denied it out of fear, and He said, Nay, but thou didst laugh. The Most High sees what is within the mind. Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

The Lord said, I know Abraham, that he will command his children and his household after him. The man is the leader who makes the rules and keeps his house in the way of the Lord. What makes a great husband and father is commanding the household in the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. Where men walk away from justice and judgment, they cannot properly command their household.

The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah was great and their sin very grievous. The iniquity of Sodom was pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness; she strengthened not the hand of the poor and needy, was haughty, and committed abomination. The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law.

Abraham drew near and negotiated with the Most High because his nephew Lot dwelt in Sodom; that is why he pleaded for the city. Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? Abraham reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten, and the Lord said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake. Below ten there was no more negotiating, and the Lord went His way.

God did tempt Abraham: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Ishmael was alive, but the Most High counted Isaac the only son, because Ishmael was born of the flesh, of a plan the Lord never spoke, while Isaac was the child of the promise. Abraham rose up early in the morning and went. No hesitation, no debating with the word; that is obedience.
Isaac asked, Where is the lamb for a burnt offering? Abraham answered, My son, God will provide himself a lamb. He trusted the Most High with what was missing.

Abraham bound Isaac, laid him on the altar, and stretched forth his hand with the knife; the angel called out of heaven in the midst of it: Lay not thine hand upon the lad. Now I know that thou fearest God. The fear of God is proved in obedience; they that fear the Lord will not disobey His word. Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.

Once the obedience was fulfilled, God provided the sacrifice: a ram caught in a thicket by his horns, offered in the stead of his son, just as Abraham had told Isaac. Abraham called the place Jehovahjireh: in the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.

By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord: in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven and as the sand upon the sea shore, and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies. The seed possessing the gate of his enemies is part of the covenant: the seed of Jacob shall possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen, and Edom shall be a possession. That is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant; the covenant has Israel possessing their enemies. In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

In the famine Isaac was told, Go not down into Egypt; the oath sworn to Abraham was performed unto Isaac: seed as the stars, all these countries, and in thy seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed. In thy seed shall all nations be blessed does not put everybody in the covenant. The seed is Christ, and the children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, scattered into every nation; through Christ scattered Israel in all kindreds of the earth receives repentance and comes back to the Father. The reason the oath stood: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

Isaac said of Rebekah, She is my sister, fearing the men of the place, and Abimelech saw Isaac sporting with Rebekah his wife and knew. Take the lesson from the sporting: love your wife, play with your wife, keep the flirting and the freshness in the marriage. Give her love, attention, and affection all the days.

Isaac sowed and received in the same year an hundredfold, and the man waxed great until he became very great; and the Philistines envied him and stopped the wells with earth. The nations envy the prosperity of Israel. It is not for anything done to them; the blessing itself is what is hated.
Isaac digged again the wells of his father and the herdmen strove for Esek and Sitnah; he removed and digged Rehoboth, and they strove not: for now the Lord hath made room for us.

Abimelech came saying, We have done unto thee nothing but good, though his people had stopped the wells and sent Isaac away. Isaac answered plainly: Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me? Isaac was not simple; he separated from the people that hated him rather than assimilating among them, and he dealt with their covenant with open eyes. The words can be like butter while war is in the heart.

Esau at forty took wives of the Hittites, and they were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. He went straight against the fathers' law of marrying within the kindred; that is the nature of the vessel.

cases.name: Pharaoh and Abimelech, who took Sarah
cases.charge: Taking another man's wife into the king's house
cases.summary: Twice Abraham called Sarah his sister, and twice a king took her. Pharaoh's household was plagued; Abimelech was warned in a dream and required to restore her. God expressly testified that he had kept Abimelech from touching her. The marriage stood despite the account given of it.
cases.offense: In Egypt, Pharaoh's princes commended Sarai and she was taken into Pharaoh's house (Genesis 12:15). In Gerar, Abimelech sent and took Sarah (Genesis 20:2). Both acted on Abraham's word that she was his sister, and Abimelech pleaded the integrity of his heart (Genesis 20:5); the Lord acknowledged his integrity and said that he had withheld him from sinning (Genesis 20:6). Yet Sarah remained another man's wife. Once that was revealed, Abimelech was required to restore her; ignorance was not permission to keep her.
cases.judgment: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai. To Abimelech he came in a dream: thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. The Lord had closed up every womb of the house of Abimelech, and opened them only when Sarah was restored and Abraham, the prophet, prayed for him.

The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.
Abram departed at seventy and five years old, with Sarai and Lot, into the land of Canaan; Canaan is northeast Africa.
Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties.

The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had. The Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
Abraham said again, She is my sister, as he had done entering Egypt, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife's sake; Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety.

God came to Abimelech in a dream: Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. Adultery was sin in Genesis, way before [Exodus 20:14](/bible/exodus/20#v14); the Most High said, I withheld thee from sinning against me. Abimelech had acted in the integrity of his heart, and the Most High withheld him from touching her. Restore the man his wife, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee.

Abimelech called it what it is: a great sin. Adultery is one of the weightier matters; there is no animal sacrifice that atones for it. Abraham thought, Surely the fear of God is not in this place. And technically she was his sister: the daughter of his father but not of his mother, who became his wife; the sister saying was their agreement in every strange land.

Behind the scenes the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah; when Abraham prayed, God healed them. The same happened with Pharaoh before. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet's wife; He does not play about that.

Give thanks unto the Most High, call upon His name, and make known His deeds among the people. Sing unto Him, glory in His holy name, and let the heart of them that seek Him rejoice; seek His face forevermore. Remember His marvelous works, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth. The Bible tells us to remember our past. -

O seed of Abraham and children of Jacob His chosen: the Most High is our God and His judgments are in all the earth. He has remembered His covenant forever, the word commanded to a thousand generations, made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, confirmed to Jacob for a law and to Israel for an everlasting covenant. If Israel was to have an everlasting covenant, then the new covenant cannot suddenly involve all people. You must ask these questions of anyone who does not use the scriptures.

When they were few and strangers in the land, He suffered no man to wrong them and reproved kings for their sake: touch not mine anointed. He called a famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant and bound with fetters until his word came to pass. The king loosed him and made him lord of his house and ruler of his substance, to bind his princes and teach his senators wisdom. Our forefather Joseph taught the Egyptians; those who boast in Egyptology forget our forefathers taught them. -

Israel came into Egypt and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham; He increased His people and made them stronger than their enemies, then turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate them. He sent Moses and Aaron who showed His signs and wonders in the land of Ham; He recounts the plagues of darkness, blood, frogs, flies, lice, hail, fire, and locusts. The locusts and caterpillars devoured all the herbs and fruit of the ground; this is the devourer, and the Most High promises to rebuke the devourer for the sake of a righteous nation. He smote all the firstborn, the chief of all their strength. The firstborn is the chief of one's strength, as Reuben was Jacob's strength before he lost it. -

He brought Israel out with silver and gold, and there was not one feeble person among the tribes; look at the sicknesses we suffer now under the curses. He spread a cloud for a covering and fire for light, brought quails and the bread of heaven, and opened the rock so the waters gushed out in the dry place. He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labor of the people, that they might keep His statutes and laws. But we were not thankful, we went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America. -

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

verses.text: And it came to pass, that, when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair.
The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
And he entreated Abram well for her sake: and he had sheep, and oxen, and he asses, and menservants, and maidservants, and she asses, and camels.
And the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram’s wife.
And Pharaoh called Abram, and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?
Why saidst thou, She is my sister? so I might have taken her to me to wife: now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.
And Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him: and they sent him away, and his wife, and all that he had.
And Abraham journeyed from thence toward the south country, and dwelled between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman which thou hast taken; for she is a man’s wife.
But Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, Lord, wilt thou slay also a righteous nation?
Said he not unto me, She is my sister? and she, even she herself said, He is my brother: in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands have I done this.
And God said unto him in a dream, Yea, I know that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also withheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.

Now therefore restore the man his wife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou restore her not, know thou that thou shalt surely die, thou, and all that are thine.
And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and womenservants, and gave them unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his wife.
And Abimelech said, Behold, my land is before thee: dwell where it pleaseth thee.

And unto Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, he is to thee a covering of the eyes, unto all that are with thee, and with all other: thus she was reproved.
So Abraham prayed unto God: and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants; and they bare children.
For the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah Abraham’s wife.
When they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people;
He suffered no man to do them wrong: yea, he reproved kings for their sakes;
Saying, Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm.
Thou shalt not commit adultery.
Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.

cases.name: Hagar, and the God who seeth
cases.charge: Returning and submitting when the angel sent her back; and calling him Thou God seest me
cases.summary: An Egyptian bondwoman given to Abram by her mistress, despised her when she conceived and was dealt with hardly until she fled. The angel of the Lord found her by a fountain in the wilderness, called her by name and by her station, told her to return and submit, and gave her a promise for her son. She named the Lord that spake unto her and called the well Beer-lahai-roi. Sent away years later with bread and a bottle of water, she was met again when the water was spent.
cases.offense: She was told to go back to a house she had run from and to a mistress who had dealt hardly with her (Genesis 16:6), and she went. The angel gave her both a command to return and a promise that her seed would be multiplied beyond numbering (Genesis 16:9-10). Her son would be called Ishmael because the Lord had heard her affliction; his life and relations with his brethren were foretold before his birth (Genesis 16:11-12). The record does not conceal her fault either, that when she saw she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes, so the case is of a woman corrected and restored rather than of one wronged only.
cases.judgment: The angel found her by a fountain in the wilderness and addressed the servant whom the household dispute had driven away (Genesis 16:7-8). She answered the encounter with the name, Thou God seest me (Genesis 16:13). The well was called after it (Genesis 16:14) and was still known by that name when the account was written. When the bread and the water were gone and she had set the child down and lifted up her voice and wept, God heard the voice of the lad, renewed the promise that he would become a great nation, and opened her eyes to a well of water (Genesis 21:17-19). She filled the bottle and gave him drink, and God was with him as he grew (Genesis 21:20-21). The covenant inheritance was appointed through Isaac, but Ishmael was not forgotten: God had also promised Abraham a nation from this son (Genesis 21:12-13).

cases.name: Sodom and Gomorrah
cases.charge: Grievous sin; inhospitality and violence against strangers
cases.summary: Cities whose sin was grave enough that its cry reached heaven. When two visitors lodged with Lot, the men of the city surrounded the house demanding them. Judgment fell the next morning.
cases.offense: The prophets later name the fuller charge: pride, fullness of bread, careless ease, and no help for the poor and needy (Ezekiel 16:49-50), a hardness that showed itself in the mob at Lot's door. The cry against the cities was great before the messengers reached Lot's house (Genesis 18:20-21). The men then surrounded it, demanded the guests, threatened Lot when he resisted, and pressed upon the door. Even after the angels struck them with blindness, they wearied themselves seeking the entrance (Genesis 19:4-11). Abundance had not produced mercy, and correction did not turn the mob from its purpose. Abraham had pleaded that the righteous not be destroyed with the wicked; the Judge of all the earth distinguished the household brought out from the city overthrown (Genesis 18:23-25; Genesis 19:29).
cases.judgment: Fire and brimstone from the Lord out of heaven (Genesis 19:24), overthrowing the cities and the plain (Genesis 19:25). Lot's wife, looking back, became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). Jude records the cities as an example of judgment upon fornication and strange flesh (Jude 1:7), and Peter sets their overthrow beside the deliverance of just Lot (2 Peter 2:6-9).

verses.text: And the Lord said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;
I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come unto me; and if not, I will know.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.
Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven;
And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.
But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good.

Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.
When the ungodly perished, she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.

Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.

For regarding not wisdom, they gat not only this hurt, that they knew not the things which were good; but also left behind them to the world a memorial of their foolishness: so that in the things wherein they offended they could not so much as be hid.
Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
