entries.commentary: Before going up to Bethel, Jacob told his household, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean. The strange gods were there because Rachel had stolen her father's images and hidden them, sitting on them when Laban searched. Idolatry hidden in the household must be put away before you can stand at Bethel. Rachel finally gave up the images, and Jacob hid them under the oak by Shechem. From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household; of the woman came the beginning of sin. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled.

The terror of God was upon the cities round about, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob. What Jacob feared after Shechem never came, because the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear Him and delivers them.

God appeared to Jacob again and confirmed it: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name. Be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins. The nation and company of nations of Abraham's covenant is Israel, plain and clear, and kings come out of Israel's loins. Christ washed us from our sins and made us kings and priests unto God; the men of Israel are kings in the sight of the Most High. Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion.
The land given to Abraham and Isaac was promised to Jacob and his seed: the land of Canaan, which is northeast Africa, the land the Most High named when He brought Israel out of Egypt.

Rachel travailed in hard labour and died bearing her second son; she called him Benoni, but his father called him Benjamin, the son of the right hand. He was the twelfth son, and Jacob set a pillar upon Rachel's grave in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.

Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard it. That is fornication such as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The judgment followed him: forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it.

Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came the chief ruler, though the birthright was Joseph's, much as Esau came out first but did not keep the place of the heir. The sons and dwellings of Reuben are named down to Beerah, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria carried away captive.

The sons of Gad are set down by the house of their fathers, dwelling in Gilead and Bashan and their towns. The record was reckoned by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel, keeping the account by name.

Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh had valiant men able to bear buckler and sword and skillful in war, four and forty thousand seven hundred and threescore that went to war. They made war with the Hagarites and were helped against them because they cried unto the Most High in the battle and put their trust in Him, and He was entreated of them. They took away much cattle and a hundred thousand captives, for the war was of the Most High; this is the curse of [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) falling on the enemy instead of on us. -
The half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land from Bashan unto Baal-hermon and mount Hermon, and they increased. The heads of the house of their fathers are named, mighty men of valour and famous men.

These tribes transgressed against the God of their fathers and went a-whoring after the gods of the people of the land whom the Most High had destroyed before them. The fringes commanded in Numbers were given so that we would look upon them and remember the commandments and not go a-whoring after our own eyes, which these tribes failed to do. Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, who carried Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity unto this day. -

In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians, and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt. The same word stands for us: when the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom. The land of Canaan was full of idols. If Israel obeyed His voice the Most High would be an enemy to their enemies, bless their bread and water, and take sickness away; the charge in Canaan was not to bow to their gods nor do after their works, but to utterly overthrow them and break down their images. Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

Keep the statutes and judgments of the Most High, which if a man do, he shall live in them. The Ten Commandments are not the whole of the law but a summary. Under the Sabbath commandment sit sub-statutes such as no buying, no selling, no working; likewise under the law of adultery sit all the laws of this chapter, the ordinances of marriage and the forbidden beds. None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to uncover their nakedness; these laws name who a man may not lay down with.

The nakedness of thy father's wife is thy father's nakedness; that is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked. This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did.

The sister, whether born at home or born abroad, and the son's daughter and the daughter's daughter are all forbidden; the grandchildren's nakedness is thine own nakedness. There are sick spirits out there, and some of them are grandfathers, uncles, and fathers. Be careful and mindful who you leave your children around; do not hand your children to just anybody for the sake of your own pleasure.

The father's sister, the mother's sister, and the wife of the father's brother, thine aunt, are all near kinswomen and off limits. Incest is still practiced among the nations of this land, and children born of incestuous unions often carry defects and disabilities; the law guards the seed.

The daughter in law, the brother's wife, and a woman with her daughter or her granddaughter are all forbidden; it is wickedness. Neither take a wife to her sister to vex her, to uncover her nakedness beside the other in her lifetime; that also shuts down what the world today calls threesomes.

A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15) details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class.
To lie carnally with thy neighbour's wife is adultery. This world even sings songs celebrating adultery; the law forbids defiling thyself with her.

Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them, as Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem slaying the children of the Most High. The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

Abomination means a thing that causes disgust or hatred. When a man lies with mankind as with womankind, the Most High calls it disgusting and hateful. What a man hates and finds disgusting he removes far from himself; so we must teach our people to repent and come out of the things the Most High hates.
Lying with any beast is confusion, for man and for woman alike. The nations have set up places where these strange lusts are fulfilled, and the sin is found among every people; it is all wickedness.

In all these things the nations were defiled which the Most High cast out; the Egyptians and the Canaanites were doing these very abominations, and the land itself was defiled by them. The land spews out the defiled. That is why Israel was put out of Jerusalem: we could not abide in the land with our sins, sacrificing to idol gods and working all manner of evil, so the Most High raised up an enemy to carry us into bondage and remove us out of the land. Whosoever commits any of these abominations, the souls that commit them shall be cut off from among their people, meaning put to death.

Whosoever of Israel or of the strangers in the land gave of his seed unto Molech was surely put to death; the people of the land stoned him with stones. This is the child sacrifice shown in [Ezekiel 16](/bible/ezekiel/16), slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to pass through the fire. If the people of the land hid their eyes from the man and killed him not, the Most High set His face against that man and against his family. When you see wickedness you must utter it and expose it; a witness that holds his peace bears iniquity. Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

The soul that turns after such as have familiar spirits and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, is cut off from among his people. Sanctify yourselves and be ye holy; keep the statutes of the Most High, for He is the Lord which sanctifieth you. Every one that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; his blood shall be upon him. Disrespecting your mother and your father carried the death penalty.

The man that committeth adultery with another man's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress, shall surely be put to death. This world openly defends adultery and men even boast of committing it with another man's wife; the scriptures call for death upon both.

The man that lies with his father's wife, and the man that lies with his daughter in law, shall surely be put to death; they have wrought confusion. If a man lie with mankind as he lieth with a woman, both have committed an abomination and shall surely be put to death; abomination means hateful and disgusting unto the Most High. The man that takes a wife and her mother is burnt with fire, both he and they, that there be no wickedness among you. The man or woman that lies with a beast is put to death, and the beast is slain also. All of these judgments fall under the laws of adultery, the sub-statutes of that commandment.

The man that takes his sister and sees her nakedness, it is a wicked thing; they are cut off in the sight of their people, and he bears his iniquity. The man that lies with a woman having her sickness, her menstrual cycle, has discovered her fountain, and both are cut off from among their people; this goes with the laws of [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15). The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless.

Keep all my statutes and all my judgments, that the land whither I bring you spew you not out. Walk not in the manners of the nation cast out before you, for they committed all these things and therefore the Most High abhorred them. I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people. The Most High separated Israel from the other people, so Israel is to walk differently; these laws are the separation.

Put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean; this goes back to [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11), the dietary laws. No shrimp, crab, lobster, pork, catfish, and the like; everything is not clean, whatever the church teaches. If you eat whatever you please, you are not separating yourself from the other nations. Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.

A man or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, was surely put to death by stoning. The tarot card readings, the fortune telling, and the horoscopes of today are that same dealing with familiar spirits; do not touch any of it.

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:
Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power:

cases.name: Joseph's brothers
cases.charge: Conspiracy to murder; selling a brother; deceiving their father with a bloodied coat
cases.summary: Joseph's brothers envied him, conspired against him, sold him for twenty pieces of silver, and used his bloodied coat to deceive their father. Years later famine brought them before Joseph in Egypt. They confessed their guilt, Judah offered himself for Benjamin, and Joseph preserved the household instead of taking vengeance.
cases.offense: At seventeen Joseph brought his father the evil report of his brethren (Genesis 37:2). The law distinguishes bearing necessary witness from concealing known iniquity  (Leviticus 5:1), but Genesis does not reproduce the report or describe a formal demand for testimony. It records the brothers' hatred, their father's favour, and the dreams that increased their envy. The record then names the root twice, and it is not the coat: his brethren envied him (Genesis 37:11), and the envious man hath a wicked eye (Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 14:8). Envy grew into conspiracy, they said one to another, behold, this dreamer cometh, come now therefore, and let us slay him (Genesis 37:19-20), and conspiracy into man-stealing, which the law makes capital: he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, shall surely be put to death (Exodus 21:16). Twenty pieces of silver is what they took for him (Genesis 37:28). The cover-up endured for years through a lie told with a garment and the blood of a kid (Genesis 37:31-33), recalling the garment and the kids used to deceive Isaac, and it brought Jacob to say he would go down into the grave unto his son mourning (Genesis 37:35). Their own verdict on themselves, spoken in Egypt before they knew who was listening, is the one the case records: we are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear (Genesis 42:21). The brothers did not all act alike. Reuben sought to deliver Joseph back to his father, while Judah proposed selling him instead of shedding his blood (Genesis 37:21-27). The sale spared Joseph from their intended murder but still handed their brother into bondage. Years later Judah's willingness to remain a bondman for Benjamin reversed his earlier willingness to send a brother away.
cases.judgment: They were spared, and the sparing is the case. The famine was called and the man was sent ahead of it: he sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant, whose feet they hurt with fetters, he was laid in iron, until the time that his word came, the word of the Lord tried him (Psalms 105:17-19). Then the king sent and loosed him, and made him lord of his house and ruler of all his substance, to bind his princes at his pleasure, and teach his senators wisdom (Psalms 105:20-22). The dreams they hated him for were fulfilled exactly, and they bowed themselves before him with their faces to the earth (Genesis 42:6). Judah, who had proposed the sale, offered himself as a bondman in Benjamin's place rather than see the evil come on his father (Genesis 44:30-34), which is the repentance the case turns on. Joseph's own reading is given twice and it distinguishes mercy from a denial of their guilt: be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither, for God did send me before you to preserve life (Genesis 45:5), and again after Jacob died, ye thought evil against me, but God meant it unto good, to save much people alive (Genesis 50:20). His mercy anticipates the measure of forgiveness Christ taught, not until seven times, but until seventy times seven (Matthew 18:22), and he comforted them and nourished them and their little ones.

entries.commentary: Joseph brought unto his father the evil report of his brethren. That was law, not tale bearing: if a soul hear swearing and be a witness and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity. The law was already around, and Joseph kept it.

Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, the son of his old age, and made him a coat of many colours; and his brethren hated him and could not speak peaceably unto him. That is real hatred among brothers, and the same spirit is on Israel today, where a brother cannot even receive a shalom in peace.

Joseph dreamed, and the sheaves of his brethren made obeisance to his sheaf. The Lord speaks by the prophets in visions and similitudes; the vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, as the likeness of a face to a face. His brethren understood the dream, that he should reign over them, and hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words.

In the second dream the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars made obeisance to Joseph. Jacob interpreted it at once: shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee? The same figures mark Israel: the woman clothed with the sun with a crown of twelve stars is the daughter of Zion, the nation of Israel, and the twelve stars are the tribes. The dream came true. In the famine the whole house of Jacob came down to Joseph in Egypt, and he placed them in the best of the land and nourished them with bread; they bowed to the one the Most High had set over them.
His brethren envied him, but his father observed the saying. Envy consumes a man, and such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom; when envy takes over, wisdom leaves.

When they saw him afar off, they conspired against him to slay him: Behold, this dreamer cometh. That is the same spirit Cain had, and the same spirit Esau had. Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Inner hatred, given room, plots death; that is why the law says thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart.

Reuben delivered him out of their hands: cast him into this pit, but lay no hand upon him; he meant to return him to his father. Judah said, What profit is it if we slay our brother and conceal his blood? They sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites, the people known today as the Arab man, for twenty pieces of silver, and they brought him into Egypt.

The brothers dipped the coat in the blood of a kid and let their father believe an evil beast had devoured Joseph. They dealt falsely and lied, against the law: ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another. Jacob could not see the lie because the thing was of the Lord. As Joseph told them later, ye thought evil against me, but God meant it unto good, to save much people alive; had Joseph never gone down to Egypt, the whole house of Israel would have died in the famine. The Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.

Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt and said unto his sons, why do ye look one upon another? Get you down thither, and buy for us from thence, that we may live, and not die. This is a repeating thing in our history: when famine came, the fathers moved toward Egypt for sustenance and nourishment. There was a famine in Abram's days and he went down into Egypt, and another famine in Isaac's days, when the Lord told him not to go down.

Jacob sent not Benjamin with his brethren; lest peradventure means perhaps mischief befall him. Benjamin was the youngest boy, and he was Rachel's son: Rachel died in hard labour bearing him, calling him Benoni as her soul was departing, but his father called him Benjamin. Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and Rachel was barren for years; she brought forth only Joseph and Benjamin. With Joseph presumed dead, Benjamin was the last son Jacob had of his beloved wife, so he would not let him go down.

Joseph knew his brethren, but made himself strange unto them and spake roughly unto them; and they knew him not. Time had passed, and they supposed he was dead or a slave; they never expected their brother to be set as second in command and ruler over Egypt. They also knew him not because he blended in among the Egyptians: Israel is black as night, just like the ancient Egyptians. When Jacob died, the Canaanites saw the mourning company and took them all for Egyptians; all twelve tribes looked like the people of Egypt. And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them. The sheaves that made obeisance to his sheaf were now his brethren bowing down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.

Hereby ye shall be proved: ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither. Joseph pressed for Benjamin because that was his own mother's son, his baby brother, whom he wanted to see.

We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul when he besought us, and we would not hear. Their conscience was activated; they knew this distress had come upon them for what they did to their brother Joseph, not knowing Joseph stood before them. Reuben answered them, spake I not unto you, saying, do not sin against the child? Reuben was the one who would not have Joseph slain, but said to sell him not and lay no hand on him. They knew not that Joseph understood them, for he spake unto them by an interpreter. He spoke to them in the tongue of the Egyptians and heard every word they said in their own tongue; we have the capacity to understand many languages. He turned himself about from them and wept, for he heard everything they said; then he returned, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.

Every man's bundle of money was in his sack, and they were afraid; and Jacob their father said, me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away. My son shall not go down with you; his brother is dead, and he is left alone. If mischief befell Benjamin by the way, Jacob's gray hairs would go down with sorrow to the grave: he would die of a broken heart, for Benjamin was the last son he had of Rachel.

Joseph made himself known, and his brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled at his presence. They could not recognize their own brother: he was sold as a teenager, and he stood before them now a grown man in his years. He was also clothed in the customs of Egypt: shaved, in Egyptian raiment, decked out as the second in command, and he had made himself strange to them and spoken by an interpreter though he understood their tongue. This does not prove the Israelites looked like the Egyptians; the peoples were all dark people. The change was his age, his dress, and the customs of the land he ruled in.

Be not grieved nor angry with yourselves: it was not you that sent me hither, but God. The Most High sent Joseph before them to preserve life and to save the whole house of Israel by a great deliverance; had he not been in Egypt, they would have died in the famine. Joseph kept the law of forgiveness: forgive thy brother not until seven times, but until seventy times seven. His own brothers sold him into slavery, and he forgave them; that is the law Israel must keep with one another today. The famine itself was called by the Most High, and the man was sent before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant, whose feet they hurt with fetters. The fetters and the iron are the prison where the king's prisoners were bound.

Joseph is yet alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. Everything Egypt was at that point in time came through the influence of Joseph; the prosperity of that land was the favor the Lord had with Israel. The word of the Lord tried Joseph. Until the time that his word came he sat in the prison; then the king sent and loosed him, made him lord of his house and ruler of all his substance, and Joseph taught his senators wisdom. He was the teacher in Egypt, second in command, a king in all but title. To go from prison to governor is favor: the Lord causes the enemy to entreat his remnant well in the time of evil. Keep the commandments, for rulers are not a terror to good works. These are the characteristics of Joseph: my son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation; set thy heart aright and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble. Do not be quick to leave the truth or find excuses in the time of trouble. Gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: he began sold into slavery and put in prison under false pretenses, and the end of the thing was governor of Egypt, a father to Pharaoh. In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider the days that were good, and be patient in spirit: read the Bible more, study more, pray more, apply more. If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small. When trials come, read the afflictions of the forefathers and the attributes they had in those times, and apply them: forgiveness, favor, righteousness, mercy. There is no other way into the kingdom but through tribulation. Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

Joseph fell upon his father's face, and wept upon him, and kissed him, and commanded the physicians to embalm his father; forty days were fulfilled for the embalming, and the Egyptians mourned for Israel threescore and ten days.

Joseph asked leave of Pharaoh according to the oath his father made him swear, to bury him in the grave he had digged in the land of Canaan; and Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.

All the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt went up with Joseph and his brethren and his father's house, with chariots and horsemen, a very great company. The Canaanites saw the mourning in the floor of Atad and said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians; wherefore the place was called Abelmizraim, which means the mourning of the Egyptians, beyond Jordan. The Israelites and the Egyptians were compared as looking like one people, because the Egyptians are black and the Israelites are black. The Bible dictionary defines Ham as the progenitor of the dark races, and Egypt was of Ham; the people sitting in that land today are not the true ancient Egyptians of the scriptures.

His sons did unto him according as he commanded them, and carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre; and Joseph returned into Egypt, he and his brethren, and all that went up with him.

When Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him; for they had sold him as a slave into Egypt. They sent a messenger pleading forgiveness and fell down before his face: Behold, we be thy servants. Joseph wept and answered, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. And he comforted them and spake kindly unto them, and nourished them and their little ones. Joseph had a real forgiving spirit. The lesson is to always be forgiving: sometimes people do evil against you, but the Most High means it unto good for you, so keep that spirit of forgiveness when people do certain things.

Joseph dwelt in Egypt and lived an hundred and ten years, and saw the children of Ephraim of the third generation; the children of Machir the son of Manasseh were brought up upon Joseph's knees. Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel: God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence. So Joseph died, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt. That is why no Egyptologist can show you the mummy of Joseph, the tomb of so famous a man: when Israel fled out of the land of Egypt they took the bones of Joseph with them, according to that oath.

If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he came in by himself he goes out by himself; if he were married when he came in, his wife goes out with him. Deuteronomy repeats the same judgment for a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman sold unto thee. [Nehemiah 5](/bible/nehemiah/5) shows how brethren came into servitude: in the dearth some mortgaged lands, vineyards, and houses to buy corn, some borrowed money for the king's tribute, and some brought their sons and daughters into bondage. The brother that waxes poor is not to be compelled to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant, and not ruled over harshly. If the master gave him a wife and she bare him sons or daughters, the wife and her children are the master's, and he goes out by himself; he did not bring them in. His two choices are to go out alone, or to plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children, have his ear bored through with an aul at the door post, and serve his master for ever. Zedekiah's covenant in Jeremiah confirms the law in the prophets: every man was to let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release.

If a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do. The reason is that her master betrothed her to himself, or unto his son; she is a wife, not a six-year servant, so the release of the menservants does not apply to her. If she please not her master who hath betrothed her to himself, he must let her be redeemed; he has no power to sell her unto a strange nation, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her. The deceit is that he betrothed her to himself and then would not deal with her, keeping her to himself when she could have been another man's wife. If he take him another wife, her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage shall he not diminish; the duty of marriage is the marriage bed. If he lay with her, she belongs to him and he cannot send her away; and if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money. He must take care of her.

If a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand, a place was appointed whither he shall flee. That is the case of the slayer that kills his neighbour ignorantly, as when a man hews wood with his neighbour and the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon him that he die: he flees to the appointed city and lives, lest the avenger of blood overtake him while his heart is hot, for he was not worthy of death, having hated him not in time past. But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die. Men would run and grab the horns of the altar, but wilful murder found no refuge there.

If men strive and one smite another so that he keep his bed, he that smote him shall pay for the loss of his time and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed. That is restitution: paying for the time the man was down and could not work and provide for his family. That is what the court system calls a civil suit today.

If a man smite his servant with a rod and he die under his hand, he shall surely be punished; but if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished, for he is his money. The wisdom writings teach not to be ashamed of much correction of children, nor of making the side of an evil servant to bleed. An evil servant that will not get right could be corrected physically, so long as he was not killed.

If men strive and hurt a woman with child so that her fruit depart from her, this judgment covers the miscarriage: if no mischief follow, he is punished as the woman's husband lays upon him and the judges determine; and if any mischief follow, then life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound.

If an ox gore a man or a woman that they die, the ox is stoned and his flesh not eaten, and the owner is quit. But if the ox were wont to push with his horns in time past, and it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, and it kill a man or a woman, the ox is stoned and his owner also put to death. Most do not have oxen today, but the same judgment reaches the yard dogs, the pit bulls, German shepherds, and rottweilers. If the dog has bitten before and it was reported to you, and it gets out again through a snapped chain or a breach in the fence and mauls or kills somebody, the scripture holds the owner responsible unto death; that is why animal control writes the ticket and warns you to keep your dogs in. The law is slack right now, as Habakkuk says, so many punishments worthy of death in the scriptures, like rape or this judgment, come out today as a fine or a slap on the hand.

When a man hath taken a wife and she find no favour in his eyes because he hath found some uncleanness in her, then let him write her a bill of divorcement, give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. Christ magnified this law: when the Pharisees asked why Moses then commanded to give a writing of divorcement, he said, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery; and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

If the latter husband hate her and write her a bill of divorcement, or if the latter husband die, her former husband which sent her away may not take her again to be his wife after that she is defiled, for that is abomination before the Lord. The question is whether a woman who leaves her husband and becomes another man's wife can be joined to the first again; the prophet asks the same thing: shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?

When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business; he shall be free at home one year and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken. Make it plain: the first year, stay at home and make a baby. Husband and wife render due benevolence to one another; benevolence means good, it is a good thing. The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge, for he taketh a man's life to pledge. The millstone is a tool for grinding meal: the manna was gathered and ground in mills or beaten in a mortar and baked into cakes. Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money.

Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married, and Miriam was not supposed to be speaking against Moses. The anger of the Lord was kindled against them, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow. The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding.

When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge; stand abroad, and let the man bring the pledge out unto thee. If the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge; deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment and bless thee, and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God. The law was already given: if thou at all take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, deliver it by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only, and when he crieth unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious. The history shows how wicked we were to each other: Israel laid themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, stacking up people's raiment like pallets and drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their god, instead of returning the pledge before the sun went down as righteousness. That is why the Lord was judging us.

The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin. The example: as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in Amaziah's hand, he slew his servants which had slain the king his father, but the children of the murderers he slew not, according unto that which is written in the book of the law of Moses. The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.

This is Stephen at the council, addressing the audience just before he is put to death. He answers the high priest by going all the way back to the beginning: the God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran. Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, dwelt in Charran, and after his father died the Most High removed him into this land wherein they now dwell, and gave him no inheritance in it, not so much as to set his foot on, yet promised to give it to him and his seed after him when as yet he had no child. Notice how Stephen recites this history off the top of his head. Our forefathers read more than their four chapters a day. When you read, you put these things to memory, so you can recite it. A lot of us cannot recite our own history, but we can recite LeBron James and the NBA stats, football stats. These men were studious; they constantly gave attendance to studying. They called Paul mad for reading so many letters. Our forefathers were addicted to this gospel.

The Most High spoke that Abraham's seed should sojourn in a strange land and be brought into bondage and treated evil four hundred years, and the nation to whom they were in bondage he would judge, and after that they would come forth and serve him in this place. Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt, but the Most High was with him and delivered him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, who made him governor over Egypt and all his house. When the famine came over Egypt and Canaan, Jacob heard there was corn in Egypt and sent out our fathers first; the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren, and Joseph's kindred was made known to Pharaoh. Jacob went down into Egypt with threescore and fifteen souls, and he and our fathers died and were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money.

As the time of the promise drew near which the Most High had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who knew not Joseph. The same dealt subtly with our kindred and evil-treated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children to the end they might not live.

In that time Moses was born, exceeding fair, nourished up in his father's house three months, and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son. Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was mighty in words and in deeds. That corrects the doctrine that certain Christian pastors preach, that Moses stuttered and could not speak. You cannot be a stupid man and be a prince over Egypt. He was raised under Pharaoh, so he had to learn everything of Egypt, their gods, their laws, the language. He was not a stupid man, and he did not stutter.

When Moses was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel. Contrary to the movie The Ten Commandments, Moses always knew who he was; his own mother raised and nursed him, so he knew his brothers, he was only raised under the household of the Egyptians. Seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him and smote the Egyptian, supposing his brethren would understand that the Most High by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not. The next day, striving to make peace, he was thrust away with, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? Only the Most High could set a man to judge. This is the crabs in a barrel spirit: even after you help somebody, they say, Who are you to be over us? Everybody wants to be the head, the chief, a leader, but nobody wants to be a follower, and nobody wants to give credit when credit is due. The Most High was using the status Moses had in Egypt to help his brother, and they used it against him: Wilt thou kill me as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday? Certain of us will be put in different positions in this society, in politics, in education, and the Most High will use those accolades to your advantage, the same way he used Moses to go to Pharaoh and not be put to death right off the bat. Then Moses fled and was a stranger in the land of Midian, understanding that if he stayed among his own people they would get him killed, and there he begat two sons. People use the excuse that Moses married an Ethiopian to justify interracial marriage, saying maybe the Lord would forgive them the same way. But the Most High says, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy. You are not Moses. Ask Aaron and Miriam, whom the Most High plagued in the skin and put out of the camp seven days for speaking against a matter that did not concern them. Do not point fingers and compare yourself to the person next to you, wondering why one brother is judged for a matter and another is treated differently. Different judgments belong to the Most High. You are not David; do not weigh Saul's sins against David's and assume you know how the Most High will judge, the way men questioned why Uzza was struck for touching the ark. Work out your own soul salvation with fear and trembling, study to be quiet, and mind your own business.

Forty years later, Moses now eighty years old, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush at Mount Sinai. Brothers and sisters say they are too old to repent; you are never too old. The Most High used Moses at eighty to deliver the whole nation, and retained his strength. The voice of the Lord said, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses trembled and durst not behold. He was told to put off his shoes, for the place was holy ground, and the Most High said, I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, I have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them; now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

This Moses, whom they refused saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge, the same did the Most High send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared in the bush. Be careful with one another; the same person you reject is the same person the Most High raises up over you. This is the spirit of preeminence, not wanting another brother to rule over you because you believe you should be in that position. The Most High sees the heart and knows the spirits he is setting up. Moses was the meekest, most humble man. For a prince to go down to people counted as slaves and servants, defend them, and risk himself for a stiffnecked and rebellious people, shows he loved his people even in his position of authority. This is that Moses who said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren like unto me; him shall ye hear. Stephen rehearsed all the history to bring them up to Christ, because the whole ministry throughout Acts is Christ's name preached in the place of animal sacrifice. Even as Pharisees, they knew this prophecy, so he made it plain: the prophet Moses spoke about is that Christ.

This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him in Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received the lively oracles to give unto us. The one in the church in the wilderness is that Christ, the prophet of verse 37. Our fathers would not obey him but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt, telling Aaron, Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses we know not what is become of him. They did not obey Christ in the wilderness, just as they did not obey Christ in his day. They made a calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands, so the Most High gave them up to worship the host of heaven; they took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Remphan, figures they made to worship, and he carried them away beyond Babylon.

Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, made according to the fashion Moses had seen, which our fathers brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom the Most High drove out before their face. That Jesus is Joshua, and the Most High drove out the nations before the fathers. This continued unto the days of David, who found favor before the Most High and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, but Solomon built him a house. Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool; what house will ye build me, saith the Lord, or what is the place of my rest? Hath not my hand made all these things?

Stephen turns it on them: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost; as your fathers did, so do ye. The Holy Ghost the fathers resisted in the wilderness is the same Holy Ghost resisted in Christ's day, and that Holy Ghost is first and foremost the laws. There are three forms of the Holy Ghost taught in this series: first the laws, when you keep the laws of the Most High; then wisdom and understanding, which comes after you keep the laws; and then power, as the apostles received power to speak in tongues and perform miracles. Which of the prophets did their fathers not persecute? They slew them that showed before of the coming of the Just One, of whom they had now been the betrayers and murderers, who received the law by the disposition of angels and kept it not.

When they heard these things they were cut to the heart and gnashed on him with their teeth. But Stephen, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of the Most High and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city, and stoned him; the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen, calling on the Most High, said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, and kneeling down he cried, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge, and fell asleep. This is the same spirit Christ had when he said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

verses.text: And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him.
And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.
Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.
And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him.
And Reuben said unto them, Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might rid him out of their hands, to deliver him to his father again.
And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him;
And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.
And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?
Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.
Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
And they took Joseph’s coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood;
And they sent the coat of many colours, and they brought it to their father; and said, This have we found: know now whether it be thy son’s coat or no.
And he knew it, and said, It is my son’s coat; an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces.
And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.
And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.
And Reuben answered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear? therefore, behold, also his blood is required.
And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.
Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
For these two years hath the famine been in the land: and yet there are five years, in the which there shall neither be earing nor harvest.
And God sent me before you to preserve you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
And when Joseph’s brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him.
And they sent a messenger unto Joseph, saying, Thy father did command before he died, saying,

So shall ye say unto Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the trespass of thy brethren, and their sin; for they did unto thee evil: and now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.
And his brethren also went and fell down before his face; and they said, Behold, we be thy servants.
And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God?
But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.
Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.
And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh merchandise of him, or selleth him; then that thief shall die; and thou shalt put evil away from among you.
And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but God was with him,
And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.

cases.name: Er and Onan
cases.charge: Wickedness before the Lord; refusing to raise up seed to a dead brother
cases.summary: Judah took a Canaanite wife, the daughter of Shuah, and had Er, Onan and Shelah. He took Tamar for Er his firstborn, and Er was wicked in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord slew him. Judah told Onan to go in unto his brother's wife and raise up seed to his brother. Onan knew the seed should not be his, and spilled it on the ground, and the thing which he did displeased the Lord, and he slew him also.
cases.offense: Er's particular wickedness is not named: the record says only that he was wicked in the sight of the Lord (Genesis 38:7). Onan's act is described together with its purpose: he deliberately prevented seed from being raised to his dead brother. The act cannot be separated from the duty he was evading. The text states his motive before it states his method: Onan knew that the seed should not be his, and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother (Genesis 38:9). He took the wife and kept the use of her, and withheld the one thing the arrangement existed for. What he refused was later written into the law: her husband's brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband's brother unto her, that the firstborn she beareth may succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel (Deuteronomy 25:5-6).
cases.judgment: Both died at the Lord's hand, not by any court. The duty Onan refused was later written into the law of the kinsman: the firstborn she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother that is dead.

entries.commentary: Judah took the daughter of Shuah and had Er, Onan, and Shelah; and Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord slew him.

Onan was told to go in unto his brother's wife and raise up seed to his brother, and he refused, spilling it on the ground, and the Lord slew him also. The sin was refusing to raise up seed to his brother, not the act itself; do not build a doctrine on the wrong point. What happened here later became law: the husband's brother raises up the name of the dead, and he that refuses has his shoe loosed and his face spat in, and his house carries the reproach.

Judah promised Tamar to Shelah and did not perform it. When she saw Shelah was grown and she was not given to him, she put off her widow's garments, covered herself with a vail, and sat where Judah would pass. Judah thought her to be an harlot because of the attire; the scriptures show a harlot was always known by her dress, as the woman with the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. She took his signet, bracelets, and staff as a pledge, and conceived by him.

When Judah heard Tamar was with child by whoredom he said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt. A woman promised in the covenant that plays the harlot and brings an heir by another disobeys the law of the Most High, and her reproach is not blotted out; that is why the judgment was so heavy. Then she produced the signet, bracelets, and staff, and Judah acknowledged them: She hath been more righteous than I, because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.

Twins were in her womb: the midwife bound a scarlet thread on the hand of the first, but his brother broke forth first and was called Pharez, and after him came Zarah with the scarlet thread. Judah's line went down into Egypt in the end, and Judah died there with his brethren; and Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God. Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day.

Boaz went up to the gate, called the kinsman of whom he had spoken to turn aside and sit down, and took ten men of the elders of the city to sit with them. What he is doing is calling witnesses. He is about to make a purchase, so he calls witnesses, that it can be put in the books for the future that this is what was done.

Boaz laid the matter before the kinsman: Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land which was our brother Elimelech's. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it; but if not, tell me, for there is none to redeem it beside thee, and I am after thee. And the kinsman said, I will redeem it. What is this going back to? The law of the land, the law of inheritance when it comes to land, read back in the book of Numbers. The husband died and the two sons died, and the only person left is the wife with the land; so she instinctively went to Boaz, and Boaz is now conducting the laws of the land of who it should be passed down to, going down the list of inheritance.

What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive. What law is that going back to? That law goes back to [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25), the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at [Ruth 1:6-9](/bible/ruth/1#v6) in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.

The kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself, for I cannot redeem it. In other words, I already have kids in the way; I cannot do it, I am not doing it.

Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing: for to confirm all things, a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour, and this was a testimony in Israel. So the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thee, and he drew off his shoe. You can read about that shoe back in [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25).

Boaz said unto the elders and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi; moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place. What law is Boaz exercising in this? Love thy neighbour as thyself. That is what Boaz was putting into place and applying, and that is why he is mentioned in the scriptures.

All the people that were in the gate and the elders said, We are witnesses. They blessed the marriage: the Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel; and let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman. In that blessing they are prophesying about David to come.

So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son. The women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel; he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.

Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it; and the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David. Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive in Israel, and although she was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel.

Now these are the generations of Pharez: Pharez is of Judah, so this is the lineage of Judah, how they came about right down to the king. Pharez begat Hezron, and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon, and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David. We read that lineage in Matthew chapter 1: how David came about, how Solomon came about, ultimately down to Christ.

The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a king which made a marriage for his son and sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden, and they would not come. The servants in this parable are not any man who says he loves God. The scripture names who the servants are.
The king sends his armies and destroys those murderers and burns up their city, then sends into the highways, and the wedding is furnished with guests, both bad and good.

The man without a wedding garment is speechless, and is bound hand and foot and cast into outer darkness. Many are called, but few are chosen. The garment is not cloth. It is righteousness, which is the keeping of the laws of the Most High.

The Pharisees take counsel how to entangle him in his talk and send their disciples with the Herodians to ask about tribute to Caesar. He perceives their wickedness, calls them hypocrites, and answers by the image on the coin: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.

The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, bring the case of seven brethren and one wife to make the resurrection look absurd. Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. In the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven. This is not saying there is no marriage in the kingdom. It answers the law they built the question on, which will not need to be kept when there is no more dying.
I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. The multitude was astonished at his doctrine.

Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart is the first and great commandment, and the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets. That is not a reduction of the law to two rules; these two are the ones the rest hang upon.

He asks them whose son Christ is, and they answer, the son of David. Then how does David in spirit call him Lord? No man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions. He perceived what they came for and answered what they needed rather than what they asked. That is how to deal with men who come only to scoff.

cases.name: Judah and Tamar
cases.charge: Withholding Shelah from his brother's widow; going in to a woman he took for a harlot
cases.summary: Judah promised Tamar his third son and never gave him, then lay with her himself on the road to Timnath. When her pregnancy came to light he ordered her burned, until she produced his signet, bracelets and staff. He judged himself: she hath been more righteous than I.
cases.offense: After Er and Onan died, Judah sent Tamar to her father's house to wait for Shelah (Genesis 38:11), and let her wait. Tamar covered her face and sat in an open place (Genesis 38:14), and Judah, taking her for a harlot, went in to her for the price of a kid, leaving his signet, bracelets, and staff as a pledge (Genesis 38:18). Three months later he was told his daughter in law was with child by whoredom (Genesis 38:24), and said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt. Tamar had seen that Shelah was grown and that she was still not given to him (Genesis 38:14). Judah had feared losing another son but left her bound to an expectation he did not fulfil. When the pregnancy was reported, he condemned her before confronting his own part in it. The pledge supplied the identification his accusation lacked.
cases.judgment: No sentence fell on Tamar; Judah stopped it himself when the pledge was laid before him (Genesis 38:25-26), confessed that the fault was his for withholding Shelah, and knew her again no more. She bore Pharez and Zarah, and Pharez stands in the line of David and of Christ. The confession names the withheld duty: she hath been more righteous than I, because that I gave her not to Shelah my son (Genesis 38:26). Judah's comparative judgment does not need to be enlarged into a declaration that every act was faultless. It exposes his own failure and halts the destruction he had ordered. The house did not end with the deaths of Er and Onan. Tamar bore Pharez and Zarah, and the line through Pharez is preserved in the genealogy of David and Christ (Ruth 4:18-22; Matthew 1:3). The record preserves the fault and its acknowledgment alongside the continuation of the family.

verses.text: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
And Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the Lord; and the Lord slew him.
And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother’s wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother’s wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.
And the thing which he did displeased the Lord: wherefore he slew him also.

Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter in law, Remain a widow at thy father’s house, till Shelah my son be grown: for he said, Lest peradventure he die also, as his brethren did. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house.
And in process of time the daughter of Shuah Judah’s wife died; and Judah was comforted, and went up unto his sheepshearers to Timnath, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
And it was told Tamar, saying, Behold thy father in law goeth up to Timnath to shear his sheep.

And she put her widow’s garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife.
When Judah saw her, he thought her to be an harlot; because she had covered her face.

And he turned unto her by the way, and said, Go to, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee; (for he knew not that she was his daughter in law.) And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayest come in unto me?
And he said, I will send thee a kid from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it?
And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that is in thine hand. And he gave it her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.
And she arose, and went away, and laid by her vail from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.

And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she is with child by whoredom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.

When she was brought forth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff.
And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.

If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.
And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.

Then the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him: and if he stand to it, and say, I like not to take her;

Then shall his brother’s wife come unto him in the presence of the elders, and loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face, and shall answer and say, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.
And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.
And let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman.
