verses.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.
And all the people brake off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.

And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To morrow is a feast to the Lord.
And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.
Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
And the Lord plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.
And I looked, and, behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God, and had made you a molten calf: ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the Lord had commanded you.
And I took the two tables, and cast them out of my two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

And I fell down before the Lord, as at the first, forty days and forty nights: I did neither eat bread, nor drink water, because of all your sins which ye sinned, in doing wickedly in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.
For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure, wherewith the Lord was wroth against you to destroy you. But the Lord hearkened unto me at that time also.
And the Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him: and I prayed for Aaron also the same time.

And I took your sin, the calf which ye had made, and burnt it with fire, and stamped it, and ground it very small, even until it was as small as dust: and I cast the dust thereof into the brook that descended out of the mount.
They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image.
Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.
They forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt;
Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.
Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.
To whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt,
Saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us: for as for this Moses, which brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.
Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

cases.name: The sons of Levi at the golden calf
cases.charge: Answering, Who is on the Lord's side? and executing the sentence on their own brethren
cases.summary: When Moses stood in the gate of the camp and asked who was on the Lord's side, all the sons of Levi gathered to him, took their swords, and went through the camp. Three thousand fell. For that day the priesthood and the service of the sanctuary were given to the tribe, and Moses' last blessing names it.
cases.offense: Moses stood in the gate of the camp with the calf ground to powder (Exodus 32:20) and put a question rather than an order: who is on the Lord's side? The whole tribe came to him (Exodus 32:26). What they were then commanded was the hardest thing in the law, to execute the sentence on apostates without regard to kinship, slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour (Exodus 32:27). Deuteronomy 13 states the statute they were applying, that a brother or a son or the wife of thy bosom who entices to other gods is not to be spared or concealed (Deuteronomy 33:8-11). Three thousand fell, and the account is careful that the sword did not fall on strangers.
cases.judgment: Moses read the day as a consecration: consecrate yourselves today to the Lord, even every man upon his son and upon his brother (Exodus 32:29), that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day. The priesthood and the whole service of the sanctuary were given to the tribe (Numbers 3:31), and the Levites were taken instead of the firstborn of Israel (Numbers 3:12). Moses' final blessing on Levi names the cause exactly (Numbers 3:17), that they observed God's word and kept his covenant (Deuteronomy 33:9), and did not acknowledge their own brethren nor know their own children. Malachi holds the covenant with Levi up centuries later as what a priesthood is supposed to be (Malachi 2:4-7).

entries.commentary: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day. Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin. Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means. Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God. Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word. From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables. Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses. As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount. He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day.

Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness. Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried. The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3), the shame of sin uncovered. Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually. Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

This is the blessing wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death. This chapter is prophetic concerning who the tribes would be in the last days: the blessings point to where you can examine history and identify each tribe. The Lord came from Sinai and shined forth from mount Paran, and came with ten thousands of saints; from his right hand went a fiery law for them. Moses commanded us a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob: the laws of the Most High are our inheritance. And he was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people and the tribes of Israel were gathered together.

Let Reuben live, and not die; and let not his men be few. Reuben is the Seminole Indians: under Andrew Jackson the Indian removal campaign set out to exterminate them, and many were slaughtered, but they were not able to kill them all. They tried it, but they were not fully successful; that is why the blessing says let Reuben live, and not die.

Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies. The Most High said we would be scattered into the four corners and the nations would conspire that we not remember who we are; but he wakes Judah first. Judah, the so-called blacks in America, are the first to remember that they are the Israelites, and once Judah learns who they are, they go and teach the other tribes scattered throughout the four corners; that is bring him unto his people. That is why Judah is at the forefront of this work. The gates of hell will try to prevail against the quest to wake up the twelve tribes, but the Most High is a help to Judah from his enemies to fulfill that mission.

And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one. The Urim and the Thummim were worn in the garment of the high priest, as [Exodus 28](/bible/exodus/28) lays out; that pertains to the Levites, the lineage of Aaron, whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah, in [Exodus 17](/bible/exodus/17). Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant. This is the zeal Levi had for the Most High. At the golden calf, when Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me, only the sons of Levi gathered themselves unto him. They took every man his sword and did according to the word of Moses without hesitating, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. That is why the blessing says they saw not father or mother nor acknowledged their brethren: that is the devotion they had for the covenant.

They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar. This is the office the Most High gave Levi, and in particular the high priest. Aaron was chosen out of all men living to offer sacrifices, incense, and a sweet savour, to make reconciliation for the people, and that office pertained to his lineage: to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in his laws. That is why Levi had no land of their own but dwelt among all the tribes of Israel: they were responsible for making the sacrifices and teaching the laws to the people.

Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. His substance goes into the tithes that Levi would receive, and the work of his hands goes into the freewill offerings brought forth to the Lord. Smite through the loins of them that rise against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again. In history you see it in the Haitian revolution under Toussaint Louverture: they smote through the loins of them that hated them. Levi was about that action to a magnitude the other tribes never matched. That they rise not again is ultimately fulfilled when Christ returns.

And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him. Dwelling in safety means Benjamin would not be killed off in slavery. The Lord shall cover him all the day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders: between the shoulders of the Lord represents the skies and the earth, going into the good climate and the good land they would have.

And of Joseph he said, Blessed of the Lord be his land. Joseph is Ephraim and Manasseh: Joseph was one of the twelve sons of Jacob, but Jacob put his name on Joseph's two sons, so his grandsons make up two tribes of Israel; when we read of Joseph we are reading of Ephraim and Manasseh. The precious things of heaven refer to the good weather on their land, and the dew and the deep that coucheth beneath go into the seas whose benefits they reap. The precious fruits brought forth by the sun are the crops their land grows: mango, papaya, avocado, pineapple, coconut, banana, sugar cane, fruits you cannot grow in north Florida. The precious things put forth by the moon go into the coqui, a frog species that exists only in Puerto Rico and comes out at night with its distinct call. The chief things of the ancient mountains are the diamonds, gold, and silver in their land, and the precious things of the lasting hills include the coffee beans that come out of their hills. Let the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, him that was separated from his brethren. Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich: hence the very name Puerto Rico, the port of riches. But like we read earlier, they waxed fat and became prideful as well.

His glory is like the firstling of his bullock: as in the law that sanctified the firstborn unto the Most High, that is the glory of the birthright given to Joseph. His horns are like the horns of unicorns: two horns, Ephraim and Manasseh. With them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: the Most High used Ephraim and Manasseh as the heads to push the ten tribes over to this side of the world, as the account of the tribes taking counsel to go forth into a further country shows. And they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh: the blessing on Jacob's grandsons was to grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. The Most High gets geographic with it: they went from the east to the west and multiplied in the midst of the hemisphere, in Central America.

And of Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents. Notice the grouping: Zebulun and Issachar are blessed together because they would dwell very close, with linked cities at their borders. They shall call the people unto the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness. In the promised land they linked up to make sacrifices of righteousness; but when they linked up on this side of the world as the Aztecs and the Mayans, they erected pyramids and eventually went off and sacrificed to other gods, even human sacrifice, as Hosea testifies of their sacrificing. For they shall suck of the abundance of the seas, and of treasures hid in the sand: the gold and silver discovered in their land, which is why the conquistadors were so glad to stumble upon it.

And of Gad he said, Blessed be he that enlargeth Gad. Gad alone holds over three hundred Indian tribes within itself; it is a very large tribe. He dwelleth as a lion, and teareth the arm with the crown of the head: Gad was a warlike, predator people, and the tearing of the arm goes into the blood brother pact they were known for making, the chief with the crown of feathers having a man tear his arm to be accepted into the tribe. And he provided the first part for himself: that is North America, the mainland, the largest and best portion. Because there, in a portion of the lawgiver, was he seated: the tribe of Gad served as the lawgivers for the northern kingdom. And he came with the heads of the people: the travel to this side of the earth was made with Ephraim and Manasseh, the horns, at the head, dealing with the so-called Hispanics and Indians together. He executed the justice of the Lord, and his judgments with Israel, before they went off.

And of Dan he said, Dan is a lion's whelp: he shall leap from Bashan. Dan is a warlike people; the Carib Indians did not play. He shall leap from Bashan says a lot in a short verse: Bashan was in the most northern part of Israel, so leaping from Bashan lands Dan in the middle of all Israel. That is why Dan today is not their own tribe but is absorbed into all the other tribes, primarily Benjamin, dwelling in the Caribbean. Amos says they shall fall, and never rise up again: Dan fell and never rose again as a tribe, which is why Dan is not mentioned among the tribes of the 144,000 in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7). And as [Genesis 49](/bible/genesis/49) says, Dan is an adder in the path: look how the islands are shaped geographically, like a serpent.

And of Naphtali he said, O Naphtali, satisfied with favour: Naphtali is Argentina and Chile today. Satisfied with favour goes into the grapes they are able to produce in their land for wine, and coffee as well. And full with the blessing of the Lord: to this day their land is rich with agriculture and cattle. Possess thou the west and the south: the Most High gets geographic again. Look at a map of the world: what land sits in the southwestern region of the earth? Argentina and Chile. Stop playing with the prophets; we know who we are.

And of Asher he said, Let Asher be blessed with children. Asher is also a large tribe: the countries that make up Asher today include Brazil, Peru, Colombia, and Uruguay, and Brazil has the largest population of children in the world. Let him be acceptable to his brethren: for a period of time they became so wild in their ways that they were not acceptable in the sight of their brethren. And let him dip his foot in oil: one of the largest outputs of crude oil resources is Colombia. Thy shoes shall be iron and brass: the Hebrew word for iron is barzel; say it fast and you hear Brazil. It goes into the mineral resources in that land, iron, copper, zinc. And as thy days, so shall thy strength be.

There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help. The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee. Notice how the song and blessing have evolved: from Israel provoking the Most High and being punished, the teeth of beasts sent upon us, now it goes into our salvation, how the Most High will be our refuge. Israel then shall dwell in safety alone. Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord! And thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee: after all these years of the crafty counsel, being told you are anything but Israel and that everybody else holds your heritage, the Most High said your enemies shall be found liars, and thou shalt tread upon their high places. Never trust your enemy: your enemy will do everything in his power to keep you oppressed and subject to him, including lying to you about your history. As in the days of the Maccabees, the leaders show the people the falsehood of the heathen and the breach of their oaths, the covenants and treaties they broke with our people; after so long you learn that your enemies have been liars this whole time.

Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

The Most High took the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix. The matrix is the womb; that is what the Lord calls it. All the firstborn are his from the day he smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Verse 13 proves the Most High does not love everybody; he killed all the firstborn of Egypt.

The children of Levi were numbered after the houses of their fathers, by their families. Your lineage is determined by your father, not your mother. The claim that identity passes through the mother is nowhere in the Bible; number the children of Levi after the house of their fathers is the standard of scripture.

Of Gershon were the families of the Libnites and the Shimites, numbered 7,500 males from a month old and upward, and they pitched behind the tabernacle westward. Depending on your family lineage you had a specific side of the tabernacle that you and all your descendants had to be on. The charge of the sons of Gershon was the tabernacle and the tent, the covering thereof, the hanging for the door, the hangings of the court, and the cords of it; that was their responsibility.

The ending "ites" denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath. They numbered 8,600 and pitched on the side of the tabernacle southward. Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot.
Eleazar the son of Aaron was chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary. He was the manager of the tabernacle.

Of Merari were the families of the Mahlites and the Mushites, numbered 6,200, and they pitched on the side of the tabernacle northward. Their custody and charge was the boards of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the sockets, the vessels, and the pillars of the court round about with their sockets, pins, and cords.

Moses and Aaron and his sons encamped before the tabernacle toward the east, keeping the charge of the sanctuary; and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi that approached unto the tabernacle was considered a stranger.

All the Levites numbered from a month old and upward were 22,000; the Most High was separating the tribe of Levi unto himself instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel. The firstborn males of the children of Israel were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen. A score is twenty, so threescore and thirteen is 73; the count is 22,273.

The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. Moses took the redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it unto Aaron and to his sons. The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

verses.text: And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)
Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves to day to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.
And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one, whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah;
Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant.
They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.
Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands: smite through the loins of them that rise against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine;

Because all the firstborn are mine; for on the day that I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I hallowed unto me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast: mine shall they be: I am the Lord.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Number all the firstborn of the males of the children of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

And thou shalt take the Levites for me (I am the Lord) instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel; and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstlings among the cattle of the children of Israel.
And Moses numbered, as the Lord commanded him, all the firstborn among the children of Israel.
And all the firstborn males by the number of names, from a month old and upward, of those that were numbered of them, were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle; and the Levites shall be mine: I am the Lord.
And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.
My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name.
The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.
For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.

If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:
But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you.

cases.name: Nadab and Abihu
cases.charge: Offering strange fire not commanded
cases.summary: Two priests, sons of Aaron, offered fire before the Lord that he had not commanded. Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them on the spot.
cases.offense: The instructions for the incense had already been given, and given to their own father: Aaron was to burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout the generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon (Exodus 30:7-9). So the fault is not an error of enthusiasm but the offering of a thing expressly excluded. They took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not (Leviticus 10:1). The office itself was guarded to this degree: Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death (Numbers 3:10), so nearness to the altar was the most closely regulated standing in Israel and these two held it.
cases.judgment: There went out fire from the Lord and devoured them, and they died before the Lord (Leviticus 10:2). The record notes what fire it was: the same that had come out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar in the chapter before, while the people shouted and fell on their faces (Leviticus 9:24). The fire that had accepted the lawful offering consumed the unlawful one. Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar were then forbidden to uncover their heads or rend their clothes lest they die and wrath come upon all the people, and the mourning was given to the whole house of Israel instead (Leviticus 10:6). The father was not permitted to mourn his own sons, because they died in the midst of the sin, and the sentence pronounced over it is the standing rule of the sanctuary: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified (Leviticus 10:3).

verses.text: And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not.
And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord.
Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.
And the Lord spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the Lord, and died;

And Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord, when they offered strange fire before the Lord, in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children: and Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the sight of Aaron their father.
And Nadab and Abihu died, when they offered strange fire before the Lord.

entries.commentary: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them. The instructions for the incense were already given: Aaron shall burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon. There were instructions on what could be burned and what could not; the strange fire is that Nadab and Abihu put strange incense before the Lord. When the Most High gave instructions through Moses on what to sacrifice and how, it was with specificity; you were to do it exactly the way he told you. They were also not the ones authorized to burn the incense; in the tabernacle service you had to be appointed to certain services and could not take a service upon yourself. Zacharias shows the pattern throughout the generations: he executed the priest's office in the order of his course, and his lot, his appointed job, was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord. The fire that went out from the Lord was the same fire that came out from before the Lord in [Leviticus 9](/bible/leviticus/9) and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar.
Then Moses said unto Aaron, this is what the Lord spake: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and they came near and carried them in their coats out of the camp, as Moses had said.

Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar were told, uncover not your heads, neither rend your clothes, lest ye die and wrath come upon all the people; basically they were told not to mourn for them, because Nadab and Abihu died in the midst of sin and what they did was abominable to the Most High. The whole house of Israel would bewail the burning which the Lord kindled. Ezekiel is the example of that word: the Most High took away the desire of his eyes, his wife, with a stroke, and told him make no mourning for the dead, neither weep, and Ezekiel went and taught the people that morning, and at even his wife died. The same standard fell on Jehoiakim the son of Josiah: they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother, or, Ah lord.
They were not to go out from the door of the tabernacle, for the anointing oil of the Lord was upon them. The anointing oil had already been put on them, so they could not leave the sanctuary.

Some read this and think Aaron and his sons could never drink, but going precept upon precept, this speaks of when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation: they were at work doing the Lord's work, and there was no drinking on the job. Ezekiel lays out the priests' work rules. The priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, kept the charge of the sanctuary; when they entered the gates of the inner court they were clocking in, clothed in linen garments and linen bonnets, girded with nothing that causeth sweat; and going out to the people in the utter court they put off the garments wherein they ministered and put on other garments, like taking off a work uniform. Neither shall any priest drink wine when they enter into the inner court; that is exactly what verse 9 speaks of. They had to be sober minded because they taught the people the difference between the holy and profane and caused them to discern between the unclean and the clean, and in controversy they stood in judgment, judging according to the judgments of the Most High. On the priests' hair: they were not to shave their heads nor suffer their locks to grow long, but only poll their heads. Polling the head means keeping the hair trimmed and maintained; you can grow it, but keep it up.

Moses told Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar to take the meat offering that remained of the offerings made by fire and eat it without leaven beside the altar, in the holy place, for it was their due; and the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten in a clean place, the due of Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever. The wave offering is explained in chapter 7: his own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire, the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.

Moses diligently sought the goat of the sin offering, and behold, it was burnt; and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, because the Most High had given it to them to bear the iniquity of the congregation, and seeing the blood of it was not brought in within the holy place, they should indeed have eaten it in the holy place, as he commanded. Those were the instructions of the law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place, and all the males among the priests shall eat thereof; but no sin offering whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle to reconcile withal shall be eaten, it shall be burnt in the fire.

Aaron answered Moses: this day have they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering, and such things have befallen me; and if I had eaten the sin offering today, should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord? And when Moses heard that, he was content.

*1 And the LORD spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the LORD, and died; 2 And the LORD said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat. 3 Thus shall Aaron come into the holy place: with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering. 4 He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on. 5 And he shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel two kids of the goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering. 6 And Aaron shall offer his bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make an atonement for himself, and for his house. 7 And he shall take the two goats, and present them before the LORD at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. 8 And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the scapegoat. 9 And Aaron shall bring the goat upon which the LORD’s lot fell, and offer him for a sin offering. 10 But the goat, on which the lot fell to be the scapegoat, shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make an atonement with him, and to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness. 11 And Aaron shall bring the bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and shall make an atonement for himself, and for his house, and shall kill the bullock of the sin offering which is for himself: 12 And he shall take a censer full of burning coals of fire from off the altar before the LORD, and his hands full of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the vail: 13 And he shall put the incense upon the fire before the LORD, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy seat that is upon the testimony, that he die not: 14 And he shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the mercy seat eastward; and before the mercy seat shall he sprinkle of the blood with his finger seven times. 15 Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the vail, and do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat: 16 And he shall make an atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions in all their sins: and so shall he do for the tabernacle of the congregation, that remaineth among them in the midst of their uncleanness. 17 And there shall be no man in the tabernacle of the congregation when he goeth in to make an atonement in the holy place, until he come out, and have made an atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel. 18 And he shall go out unto the altar that is before the LORD, and make an atonement for it; and shall take of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about. 19 And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallow it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel. 20 And when he hath made an end of reconciling the holy place, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat: 21 And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness: 22 And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness. 23 And Aaron shall come into the tabernacle of the congregation, and shall put off the linen garments, which he put on when he went into the holy place, and shall leave them there: 24 And he shall wash his flesh with water in the holy place, and put on his garments, and come forth, and offer his burnt offering, and the burnt offering of the people, and make an atonement for himself, and for the people. 25 And the fat of the sin offering shall he burn upon the altar. 26 And he that let go the goat for the scapegoat shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward come into the camp. 27 And the bullock for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall one carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung. 28 And he that burneth them shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp. 29 And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you: 30 For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD. 31 It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever. 32 And the priest, whom he shall anoint, and whom he shall consecrate to minister in the priest’s office in his father’s stead, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen clothes, even the holy garments: 33 And he shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make an atonement for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar, and he shall make an atonement for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation. 34 And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year. And he did as the LORD commanded Moses.*

Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

The Most High took the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix. The matrix is the womb; that is what the Lord calls it. All the firstborn are his from the day he smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Verse 13 proves the Most High does not love everybody; he killed all the firstborn of Egypt.

The children of Levi were numbered after the houses of their fathers, by their families. Your lineage is determined by your father, not your mother. The claim that identity passes through the mother is nowhere in the Bible; number the children of Levi after the house of their fathers is the standard of scripture.

Of Gershon were the families of the Libnites and the Shimites, numbered 7,500 males from a month old and upward, and they pitched behind the tabernacle westward. Depending on your family lineage you had a specific side of the tabernacle that you and all your descendants had to be on. The charge of the sons of Gershon was the tabernacle and the tent, the covering thereof, the hanging for the door, the hangings of the court, and the cords of it; that was their responsibility.

The ending "ites" denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath. They numbered 8,600 and pitched on the side of the tabernacle southward. Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot.
Eleazar the son of Aaron was chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary. He was the manager of the tabernacle.

Of Merari were the families of the Mahlites and the Mushites, numbered 6,200, and they pitched on the side of the tabernacle northward. Their custody and charge was the boards of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the sockets, the vessels, and the pillars of the court round about with their sockets, pins, and cords.

Moses and Aaron and his sons encamped before the tabernacle toward the east, keeping the charge of the sanctuary; and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi that approached unto the tabernacle was considered a stranger.

All the Levites numbered from a month old and upward were 22,000; the Most High was separating the tribe of Levi unto himself instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel. The firstborn males of the children of Israel were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen. A score is twenty, so threescore and thirteen is 73; the count is 22,273.

The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. Moses took the redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it unto Aaron and to his sons. The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

After the plague the Lord commanded a new numbering of the congregation, from twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go to war in Israel. Twenty is the biblical age of a man: Israel sent men to war, not children, so the numbering of them able for war fixes the age of manhood at twenty years old.

Of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites. The ending ites means the descendants of, the people you belong to: Israelites are the descendants of Israel, Edomites the descendants of Edom, and so it goes all down the line through the scriptures. Reading these family names aloud loosens the tongue to say the names of the scriptures fluently and without hesitation. [1 Chronicles 1](/bible/1-chronicles/1) serves the same practice, and it carries the names of Israel's families together with Edom and Ishmael, the nations that come out of Abraham's line.

Dathan and Abiram were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the Lord; the account is back in [Numbers 16](/bible/numbers/16). The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign. Notwithstanding, the children of Korah died not.

Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan, and the families of Judah continued through Shelah, Pharez, and Zerah, threescore and sixteen thousand and five hundred numbered. Do not hear Pharez and think the Pharisees came from the Pharzites; the Pharisees did not come out of that family. The rise of those sects is read of in the books of the Maccabees.

The numbered of the children of Israel were six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty. Unto these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names: to many the more inheritance, to few the less, and the land divided by lot according to the tribes of their fathers. Land is how wealth is built, and Esau knows how important land is; that is why the land is kept in his generations and why Gad, the Native Indian, was never given one square inch of his land back, only the casinos and the little plots called reservations. Israel is getting the most fertile land back; as for this land here, let it burn.

Jochebed the daughter of Levi bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister; and unto Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord; go back and read that account.

Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land. My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land; he let nobody keep him from serving the Most High. Christ said the same thing: he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. If the Lord finds you lukewarm, choosing your kids, your parents, or your spouse over following God and Christ and keeping the commandments wholly, you will not enter into the land; you must follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas. Let that be a lesson learned, for whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

cases.name: The blasphemer in the camp
cases.charge: Blaspheming the Name in a quarrel
cases.summary: In a fight within the camp, a man blasphemed the Name and cursed. He was held until the Lord's mind was made known, and his case set the statute for all Israel.
cases.offense: He is identified by his lineage before his act, and the lineage is the first thing the case teaches. The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and this son of the Israelitish woman and a man of Israel strove together in the camp (Leviticus 24:10). His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan (Leviticus 24:11), so the mother was named and the tribe was named, and he was conceived in Egypt while Israel dwelt among the Egyptians; there is no half Israel, and he was counted with his mother's people. In the strife the Israelitish woman's son blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed (Leviticus 24:11). The offence was against God directly, in the camp, spoken aloud and heard.
cases.judgment: The Lord commanded that the whole congregation stone him outside the camp, the witnesses laying their hands on his head. From his case came the law: whoever blasphemes the Name shall be put to death.

entries.commentary: The children of Israel were commanded to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Aaron ordered it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually, upon the pure candlestick, a statute for ever in your generations.

Twelve cakes of fine flour were set in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord, with pure frankincense upon each row, every sabbath, taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in the holy place, for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the Lord made by fire.

The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and strove in the camp with a man of Israel, and blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. They put him in ward, that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them; and the Lord commanded that he that had cursed be brought forth without the camp, that all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and that all the congregation stone him. The strife in the camp likely arose from a man of Israel correcting him concerning the law. His father being an Egyptian shows he was conceived while Israel was in captivity in the land of Egypt, dwelling among the Egyptians; in the same way Moses, outside of Egypt with Jethro the priest of Midian, took a wife there. And there is no such thing as being half Israelite or a fourth Israelite: if your parent is Israel, you are Israel. Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin, and he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, he shall surely be put to death, as well the stranger as he that is born in the land.

He that killeth any man shall surely be put to death, and he that killeth a beast shall make it good, beast for beast. If a man cause a blemish in his neighbour, as he hath done, so shall it be done to him: breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. One manner of law stood for the stranger as for one of your own country. When Christ came he taught the proper understanding of eye for eye for dealing inside the nation: ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth, but I say unto you that ye resist not evil. As the Son of God he had authority to magnify the law: whosoever smites thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also; if any man sue thee and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also; whosoever compels thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience, and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. cases.name: The complainers at Taberah and the lusters at Kibroth-hattaavah
cases.charge: Murmuring against the Lord; lusting after flesh and despising the manna
cases.summary: The people complained and the fire of the Lord burned in the outskirts of the camp. Days later the mixed multitude fell to lusting and Israel wept for the meat of Egypt. Quail came, and with the quail a plague.
cases.offense: The first sentence names the whole offence: when the people complained, it displeased the Lord, and the Lord heard it, and his anger was kindled (Numbers 11:1). Egypt had been destroyed for them, its firstborn, its army, its land, and at the first trial on the far side of the sea they murmured. Nothing spoken is hidden, and the wise man's warning is the  precept the case sits on: beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable, and refrain your tongue from backbiting, for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought, and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul (Wisdom of Solomon 1:11). The second stage came from outside the nation before it came from inside it: the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting, and the children of Israel also wept again (Numbers 11:4). The nations sprinkled in among Israel lusted first, and Israel followed them, as it always has, and wept for the fish they did eat in Egypt freely, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick (Numbers 11:5), the diet of the house of bondage, weeks after the bondage ended. They had just watched the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp and went back and did the same thing, and the psalm names it: they tempted God in their heart by asking meat for their lust, and they spake against God (Psalms 78:18-19).
cases.judgment: Fire consumed the complainers at Taberah until Moses prayed. At Kibroth-hattaavah, while the flesh was yet between their teeth, the Lord smote the people with a very great plague; the place is named for the graves of the lusters. Paul: these things were our examples.

entries.commentary: The Most High hates it when His people complain. He had just destroyed Egypt for Israel, its land, its infrastructure, its firstborn, and drowned its army in the sea, all to save the people out; then on the other side of the wilderness, at the first trial or tribulation, the people jumped off His bandwagon, and the same is still being done to this day. The Lord heard the complaining, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them. Vengeance, when it punisheth, does not pass by him that speaketh unrighteous things; the murmurer receives the vengeance of the Lord. Nothing spoken behind closed doors is hidden. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, by the Lord and His angels, the same council seen when the Lord asked who shall persuade Ahab that he may fall at Ramothgilead; the sound of a man's words comes unto the Lord, for the ear of jealousy heareth all things. Beware of murmuring and refrain the tongue from backbiting, for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought, and the mouth that belieth, that slandereth a brother, a sister, the leadership, or the Lord, slayeth the soul. Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.

The people cried unto Moses, and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched; the Most High quenched the fire because Moses prayed on behalf of the children of Israel. The place was called Taberah, because the fire of the Lord burnt among them.

The mixed multitude that fell a lusting were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel, the mixed multitude that went up with the people out of Egypt; the law in Leviticus tells what they were for, to be the bondmen and bondmaids of Israel. It was not Israel complaining at first; it was the nations lusting after the food of Egypt, and the children of Israel, gullible and assimilated as always, followed right after them and murmured against their God. The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it. They wept for the fish they ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. It is the same today with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out. They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.

The manna was as coriander seed, the colour of bdellium; the people gathered it, ground it, baked it in pans, and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil. Read precept upon precept to understand what they despised: manna is angels' food, the food the Lord feeds the angels, sent from heaven prepared without their labour; they only had to pick it up. The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.
Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent; the anger of the Lord was kindled greatly, and Moses also was displeased.

Moses asked the Most High why He had afflicted His servant and laid the burden of all this people on him: have I conceived all this people, that thou shouldest say, Carry them in thy bosom as a nursing father? He was carrying grown people who acted like children. The people Moses bore are the same people today; this teaching identifies the children of Israel with the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native American Indians, and the sheer rebellion and complaining in these chapters is one of the marks of the people. Moses said, If thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand; he would rather die than bear so rebellious a people alone and look upon his own wretchedness.

The Lord told Moses to gather seventy men of the elders of Israel to the tabernacle, and He would take of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon them, that they bear the burden of the people with him. Leadership works the same way today. The spirit on the head, the willingness to put in work, the humility, the patience, is meant to trickle down to the men below him, and the spirit the lead sisters roll in sets the spirit of the sisters in the congregation. That is why the leaders must be right according to the scriptures, because the Most High takes their spirit and lets it come upon the others.

The Lord said, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, It was well with us in Egypt, therefore the Lord will give you flesh. Not one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty days, but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils and it be loathsome unto you. He fed them so much of the flesh they begged for that they would grow sick of it and hate it. The reason for the judgment is stated plainly: because ye have despised the Lord which is among you. They spoke evil of His manna and wept to go back among the oppressors He had just destroyed.

Moses inquired how it could be done: the people are six hundred thousand footmen, and that count is not including women and children; there were millions in the wilderness. Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, or all the fish of the sea gathered together for them, to suffice them? The Lord answered, Is the LORD'S hand waxed short? The One who destroyed Egypt asks whether His hand is short; thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not. Be patient and watch the word come to pass.

Moses gathered the seventy elders round about the tabernacle, and the Lord came down in a cloud and took of the spirit that was upon Moses and gave it unto the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease. The same thing happened with Elijah and Elisha. Elisha, Elijah's right hand and disciple, asked for a double portion of his master's spirit before Elijah was taken up, and when the sons of the prophets saw Elisha smite Jordan with the mantle, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.

Two of the men, Eldad and Medad, remained in the camp, and the spirit rested upon them, and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua the son of Nun said, My lord Moses, forbid them. Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD'S people were prophets. Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it; the Most High wants all His people to be prophets. The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

A wind from the Lord brought quails from the sea and let them fall by the camp, a day's journey on this side and on the other, two cubits high upon the face of the earth, and the people gathered them. While the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled and He smote the people with a very great plague, exactly as He had warned. The place was called Kibrothhattaavah, the graves of lust, because there they buried the people that lusted. The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, but the lesson also stands in nature: excess of meat brings sickness. Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched.

And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?
We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:
But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes.

And he called the name of that place Kibroth–hattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.
He caused an east wind to blow in the heaven: and by his power he brought in the south wind.
He rained flesh also upon them as dust, and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea:
And he let it fall in the midst of their camp, round about their habitations.
So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire;
They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths,
The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel.
But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert.
And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul.

cases.name: Eldad and Medad
cases.charge: Prophesying in the camp when the spirit rested on them, and being defended by Moses
cases.summary: Seventy elders were gathered to the tabernacle to be given of the spirit that was on Moses. Two of the written men stayed in the camp, and the spirit rested on them there, and they prophesied. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua said, My lord Moses, forbid them. Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord's people were prophets.
cases.offense: They were of the written number but they were not at the tent. Nothing in the account says they refused to go, and the record does not accuse them; what it records is that the spirit rested on them where they were (Numbers 11:25), and that they did not conceal it or wait for permission before speaking. The complaint against them came from the camp and from Moses' own servant (Numbers 11:27), and the two men are not shown answering it.
cases.judgment: Moses refused to silence them and turned the rebuke on the man who wanted it done: enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord's people were prophets (Numbers 11:29), and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them. The case is entered because the blessing was defended by the one person whose standing it might have threatened, and because the wish Moses expressed is the thing Joel later prophesies and Peter cites at Pentecost as fulfilled. Two men who were not in the room are the volume's earliest evidence that the gift is not confined to the appointed place.

And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.
And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the Lord, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle.

And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.

But there remained two of the men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.
And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.
And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.
And Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!

Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence.
