verses.text: Because all those men which have seen my glory, and my miracles, which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice;
Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it:
Say unto them, As truly as I live, saith the Lord, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you:
Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me,
Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.
But as for you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness.
And your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your whoredoms, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.
After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years, and ye shall know my breach of promise.
I the Lord have said, I will surely do it unto all this evil congregation, that are gathered together against me: in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.
And they rose up early in the morning, and gat them up into the top of the mountain, saying, Lo, we be here, and will go up unto the place which the Lord hath promised: for we have sinned.
And Moses said, Wherefore now do ye transgress the commandment of the Lord? but it shall not prosper.
Go not up, for the Lord is not among you; that ye be not smitten before your enemies.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and ye shall fall by the sword: because ye are turned away from the Lord, therefore the Lord will not be with you.
But they presumed to go up unto the hill top: nevertheless the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and Moses, departed not out of the camp.
Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites which dwelt in that hill, and smote them, and discomfited them, even unto Hormah.
And the Lord heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and sware, saying,
Surely there shall not one of these men of this evil generation see that good land, which I sware to give unto your fathers,
Save Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and to him will I give the land that he hath trodden upon, and to his children, because he hath wholly followed the Lord.
Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness:
When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my work.
Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways:
Unto whom I sware in my wrath that they should not enter into my rest.
For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?
And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.
I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.
Nor the six hundred thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.

cases.name: The man gathering sticks on the Sabbath
cases.charge: Working on the Sabbath
cases.summary: A man was found gathering sticks on the Sabbath day and was held because it had not been declared what should be done to him. The Lord then gave Moses the instruction for this case.
cases.offense: The sabbath had already been given as the sign and its breach already carried death: ye shall keep the sabbath therefore, for it is holy unto you, every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death (Exodus 31:14), and, whosoever doeth any work in the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death (Exodus 31:15). It is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the Lord that doth sanctify you (Exodus 31:13), and keeping it is what marks Israel as his; the nations do not have it. The work in question is not obscure. Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day (Exodus 35:3), and gathering sticks is gathering fuel to kindle it. Bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe (Exodus 16:23) is the rule of the day before: the cooking is done on the sixth day, the sabbath meal is what was laid up. While the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man that gathered sticks upon the sabbath day (Numbers 15:32), and they that found him brought him unto Moses and Aaron, and unto all the congregation (Numbers 15:33). The case is entered as a warning against every man excusing his own trade on that day.
cases.judgment: The Lord instructed Moses that the man must be put to death by stoning outside the camp, and the congregation carried out that command. Numbers 15:34 describes uncertainty about what should be done to this man; it should not be read as saying that no Sabbath death penalty had previously been stated.

entries.commentary: When Israel came into the land of their habitations, they were to make an offering by fire unto the Lord: a burnt offering, a sacrifice in performing a vow, a freewill offering, or an offering in the solemn feasts, for a sweet savour unto the Lord. These are all the accounts on which you would sacrifice to the Lord, taken of the herd or of the flock.

Every sacrifice came with its measured meat offering of flour mingled with oil and its drink offering of wine, and the measures scaled up with the animal: a lamb, a ram, and then a bullock. An hin is roughly a gallon to a gallon and a half, so the bullock, the greatest offering, carried half an hin of oil and half an hin of wine.

Thus it was done for one bullock, one ram, one lamb, or a kid; the kid is the goat. Everyone did according to the number they prepared. All that are born of the country did these things after this manner when offering an offering made by fire of a sweet savour unto the Lord.

The scripture separates the two: the children of Israel and the stranger that sojourns with them. If a stranger joined himself to Israel, he had to keep the law to journey with them in the land. One ordinance and one law stood both for the congregation and for the stranger that was joined with them, an ordinance for ever in their generations: as ye are, so shall the stranger be before the Lord.

When Israel ate of the bread of the land, they offered up a cake of the first of their dough as an heave offering unto the Lord, as they did the heave offering of the threshingfloor. The heave offering was a particular motion in presenting it: the offering was held up to the Most High and brought back down; that is why it was called the heave offering.

If the whole congregation sinned through ignorance, without the knowledge of what they were doing, and the priest came behind them and corrected them on it, then all the congregation offered a young bullock for a burnt offering and a kid of the goats for a sin offering. The priest made an atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it was forgiven them, for it was ignorance; the stranger among them was included in that forgiveness.

If any single soul sinned through ignorance, he brought a she goat of the first year for a sin offering, and the priest made an atonement for him, and it was forgiven him. One law covered him that sinned through ignorance, both for him born among the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourned among them.

But the soul that doeth ought presumptuously sinned willfully; he thought about what he was doing before he did it. Whether born in the land or a stranger, that soul reproached the Lord and was cut off from among his people. Because he despised the word of the Lord and broke his commandment, that soul was utterly cut off, meaning put to death, and his iniquity was upon him.

The man found gathering sticks on the sabbath day is the example of the presumptuous sin just described: someone who thought about the sin before he did it. He was not picking up sticks just to pick up sticks; he was gathering them to kindle a fire and cook on the sabbath. They put him in ward, meaning they locked him up, because it was not declared what should be done to him; then the Lord commanded Moses that the man be surely put to death, and all the congregation stoned him with stones without the camp. He did not even get to the act itself; he had the intention, and for that willful intent he was put to death.

Because of that act, the Most High gave Israel the commandment to make fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and to put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue. The fringe is to look upon and remember all the commandments of the Lord and do them, and not to seek after your own heart and your own eyes; so that when we think of sin, we look at the fringes and remember the laws of the Most High instead of going and picking up sticks. I am the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God.

The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship, to devise cunning works, to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of timber. With him the Lord gave Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted, that they might make all that he had commanded. The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

The wise hearted made all that was commanded: the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is thereupon, all the furniture of the tabernacle, the table and his furniture, the pure candlestick with all his furniture, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot. They made the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons to minister in the priest's office, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense for the holy place, according to all that the Lord commanded. That spirit of workmanship on Israel is why the tabernacle, and later the house Solomon built for the Lord, outshined anything the world had seen; and though strangers shall build up our walls in the kingdom, it will be Israel directing how the Lord wants it done.

Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God; the nations do not have this sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel. Every one that defileth the sabbath shall surely be put to death. The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown; the Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people. Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God.

The children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant; it is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed. Christians use [Mark 2:27](/bible/mark/2#v27) to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude.

When he had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai, he gave him two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God. God literally wrote the testimony with his finger, and we know that was Christ.

Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel: six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord; whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death. Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: kindling fire goes to cooking. Bake that which ye will bake today, and seethe that ye will seethe, and lay up what remains to be kept unto the morning; you could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day, and what you prepare that day is what you eat.

Whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring the Lord's offering: gold, silver, and brass; blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and goats' hair; rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins; shittim wood; oil for the light and spices for the anointing oil and the sweet incense; and onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and the breastplate. These are the offerings the people would bring unto the Lord.

Every wise hearted among you shall come and make all that the Lord hath commanded: those who had skill, the crafty ones. The list runs through the whole work: the tabernacle, his tent, his covering, his taches, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets; the ark of the covenant with the staves and the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering; the table with his staves and vessels and the shewbread; the candlestick, which is the menorah, with his lamps and the oil for the light; the incense altar; the altar of burnt offering, where the burnt offering was burnt, with his brasen grate; the laver; the hangings of the court; and the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office.

The congregation departed from the presence of Moses, and they came, every one whose heart stirred him up and every one whom his spirit made willing, and brought the Lord's offering for the work of the tabernacle; the people brought the gold and silver and all the things listed willingly. Both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold; and every man with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, red skins of rams, badgers' skins, silver, brass, or shittim wood brought it. All the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands; the women knew how to sew, and brought that which they had spun of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats' hair. The rulers brought onyx stones, stones for the ephod and breastplate, spice, and oil.

The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship; the Most High put His spirit on him to be gifted in what he did, to devise curious works in gold, silver, and brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of wood. He hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; the two brothers the Most High was dealing with in workmanship trained and taught their fellow brethren how to do it. It is the same today: the Most High puts His spirit on brothers and sisters with different talents, and they put their talents to use and teach others in the congregation; Israel was putting their talents together and building, showing each other how to do these works.

cases.name: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram
cases.charge: Rebellion against God-appointed authority
cases.summary: Korah led 250 leaders in a challenge to Moses and Aaron, claiming the whole congregation was holy and needed no mediator. The earth answered the claim.
cases.offense: The company is counted exactly: Korah of Levi, with Dathan, Abiram and On of Reuben, and two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown (Numbers 16:1-2). What they claimed was equality, that all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them, wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the Lord (Numbers 16:3). Moses answered by naming what they already held and what they were reaching for: seemeth it but a small thing unto you that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself to do the service of the tabernacle, and ye seek the priesthood also (Numbers 16:9-10). They were Levites, and the service of the tabernacle was theirs and no one else's, and it was not enough. Dathan and Abiram would not even come when called, and charged Moses with bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them in the wilderness and making himself altogether a prince over them (Numbers 16:12-13).
cases.judgment: The test was the censers, since the dispute was over who might come near: take you censers, and put fire therein, and put incense in them before the Lord, and the man whom the Lord doth choose, he shall be holy (Numbers 16:6-7). The ground clave asunder and swallowed Korah's company with their houses and all their goods, and they went down alive into the pit (Numbers 16:31-33). Fire came out from the Lord and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense (Numbers 16:35). The next day the whole congregation murmured, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord, and a plague killed fourteen thousand seven hundred more until Aaron ran with a censer and stood between the dead and the living (Numbers 16:46-48). The censers of the dead were beaten into plates for a covering of the altar, a memorial that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron come near to offer incense (Numbers 16:39-40).

verses.text: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took men:
And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown:

And they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said unto them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the Lord?
And it came to pass, as he had made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground clave asunder that was under them:
And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.
They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.

And there came out a fire from the Lord, and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.
Now they that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah.

Strangers conspired together against him, and maligned him in the wilderness, even the men that were of Dathan’s and Abiron’s side, and the congregation of Core, with fury and wrath.
This the Lord saw, and it displeased him, and in his wrathful indignation were they consumed: he did wonders upon them, to consume them with the fiery flame.
In the congregation of the ungodly shall a fire be kindled; and in a rebellious nation wrath is set on fire.

entries.commentary: Korah was of Levi, and Dathan, Abiram, and On were of Reuben. With them rose up two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown; that is two hundred and fifty three in all against Moses and Aaron. These were known and powerful men among the congregation, and their influence, because of who they were, is how they were able to persuade people. They charged Moses and Aaron with taking too much upon themselves and lifting themselves above the congregation. They thought Moses and Aaron carried themselves as better than the rest, but the Most High is the one who chose them as leaders and was dealing with them; the accusers were jealous of them.

When Moses heard it, he fell upon his face, and told Korah and all his company: even to morrow the Lord will shew who are his, and who is holy; the Most High himself would show whom he chose and whom he was dealing with. The test was censers: take you censers, Korah and all his company, put fire therein and incense before the Lord, and the man whom the Lord doth choose, he shall be holy. Ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.

Moses exhorted Korah: seemeth it but a small thing that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle? Only Levi could do the service of the tabernacle, and that was a heavy job in itself. You already stand before the congregation and minister unto them; the Most High is still dealing with you. But they sought the priesthood also, and for that cause Korah and all his company were gathered together against the Lord: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him?

Dathan and Abiram would not come up when Moses called them. They were being rebellious against Moses because they wanted his spot, accusing him of bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them in the wilderness and of making himself a prince over them. Those same spirits are around today; the same thing that went on in the old time goes on now.

Moses was very wroth and said unto the Lord, respect not thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I hurt one of them. Every man took his censer, two hundred and fifty censers, with Aaron and Korah also, put fire and incense in them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; and Korah gathered all the congregation against Moses and Aaron, and the glory of the Lord appeared unto all the congregation.

The Lord told Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from among the congregation, that he might consume them in a moment: get away from them, because judgment is about to come. Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces and pleaded: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation? They still had that love for their people and pleaded with the Lord not to deal with the whole congregation over one man's sin.

The Lord commanded the congregation to get up from about the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram; Moses warned them to depart from the tents of these wicked men and touch nothing of theirs, lest they be consumed in all their sins and put to death in all that wickedness. The congregation got up from the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood in the door of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little children.

Moses put the proof on the Most High: hereby ye shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works, for I have not done them of mine own mind. If these men die the common death of all men, then the Lord hath not sent me; if the Most High does not do something out of the ordinary to put them to death, then the Lord had not sent him. But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth and swallow them up, and they go down quick into the pit, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.

As he made an end of speaking, the ground clave asunder under them, and the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, their houses, all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods; anybody that had something to do with them went down, with all they owned. The earth just opened and closed upon them, and they perished from among the congregation; all Israel round about fled at the cry of them, for you could hear them crying as they were swallowed up, and they said, lest the earth swallow us up also.
The other two hundred and fifty men that followed them and offered incense did not escape either: there came out a fire from the Lord and consumed them.

The Lord told Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers out of the burning, for they are hallowed, and scatter the fire yonder; the censers of these sinners against their own souls were made broad plates for a covering of the altar, because they were offered before the Lord. The plates were a memorial and a sign unto the children of Israel, that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron come near to offer incense before the Lord, that he be not as Korah and as his company.

On the morrow, the very next day, all the congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord. After they had just seen the earth open up and swallow men, they still would not let it go and gathered against Moses again; that is just how rebellious we are. The Most High saw what was going on, and the cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord appeared; Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle because they knew the Most High was ready to deal with them. The Lord came down ready to put them to death again, saying get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment; and Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces, still pleading for their people because they loved them so much.

Moses told Aaron to take a censer with fire from off the altar and incense, and go quickly unto the congregation and make an atonement for them, for wrath had gone out from the Lord and the plague was begun; the Most High was already putting them to death. Aaron ran into the midst of the congregation, put on incense, made an atonement for the people, and stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.

They that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah; so beside the two hundred and fifty three that died with Korah, fourteen thousand seven hundred more were put to death.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

cases.name: Moses at the waters of Meribah
cases.charge: Failing to honor God as holy before the people
cases.summary: Told to speak to the rock so it would give water, Moses instead struck it twice and spoke rashly to the people. The water came, but so did a sentence: he would not enter the promised land.
cases.offense: The command was exact and it was small: take the rod, gather the assembly, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes, and it shall give forth his water (Numbers 20:8). What Moses did instead is two things, and the first is the graver. He said, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock (Numbers 20:10). That we is how the record shows he was out of the spirit: he put himself and Aaron in the place of the one who was giving the water. Then he lifted up his hand and smote the rock twice with his rod, when he had been told to speak to it (Numbers 20:11). The provocation was real and the  account does not hide it. There was no water, the congregation gathered against him, and they chode with him, which is a loud and angry thing: would God that we had died when our brethren died before the Lord, and wherefore have ye brought up the congregation into this wilderness, that we and our cattle should die there (Numbers 20:3-4). He was carrying twelve tribes at once. The provocation explains the anger and does not excuse the word.
cases.judgment: The water still came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also (Numbers 20:11), so the people lost nothing by it and only the two men did. The sentence is pronounced immediately and the ground given is precise: because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them (Numbers 20:12). Forty years of carrying the nation ended with the leader kept out of the country for one sentence spoken in anger. The place was named Meribah, which is strife, because the children of Israel strove with the Lord, and he was sanctified in them (Numbers 20:13). The psalm reads it the same way, that they angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes, because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips (Psalms 106:32-33).

entries.commentary: The whole congregation came into the desert of Zin in the first month and abode in Kadesh, and Miriam died there and was buried there.

There was no water for the congregation, and the people gathered together against Moses and against Aaron; this is another account of Israel coming against them. When it says the people chode with Moses, they raised their voices; it was loud, angry, a shouting argument: would God that we had died when our brethren died; why have ye brought us into this evil place with no seed, figs, vines, pomegranates, or water to drink. This is us, the blacks and Hispanics. We were taken out of Egypt by the hand of the Most High, headed to the promised land, and we forgot so quickly how we were brought out; anything out of the ordinary, we complained about it. That constant complaining is one of the marks that this book is speaking of this people. Moses had to deal with all twelve tribes at once, twelve personalities and twelve attitudes; give that brother all the honor he deserves.

Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces at the door of the tabernacle, and the glory of the Lord appeared. The command was to take the rod and speak unto the rock before their eyes, and it would give forth his water for the congregation and their beasts. At this point Moses got out of the spirit; a stomach can only take so much of a rebellious people. He said, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? That we is how you know Moses was off: he forgot who was giving the water. It was the Lord giving it, not Moses and not Aaron. Moses lifted up his hand and smote the rock twice with his rod, and the water still came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.

Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel: for this Moses and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land given them. This is the water of Meribah, which means strife, because the children of Israel strove with the Lord, and he was sanctified in them.

Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, Thus saith thy brother Israel. Israel rehearsed the travail: our fathers went down into Egypt, the Egyptians vexed us, we cried unto the Lord and he heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us forth. Edom is identified in this teaching with the people called the white man today, the Caucasians. This is Israel pleading with the brother nation: not sneaking in, not hiding, not touching the fields, the vineyards, or the water of the wells; only the king's highway, turning neither to the right hand nor to the left, until past the borders, to reach the promised land.

Edom answered, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword. Israel stayed humble: we will go by the highway, and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it; I will only go through on my feet. Edom still refused and came out against Israel with much people and with a strong hand, and Israel turned away from him. Why so harsh against a people asking only to pass through? That hatred stands from something: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him, and purposed in his heart to slay his brother. [Genesis 25](/bible/genesis/25) through 27 is the start of the two nations, and Israel was given the birthright and the kingdom while Esau was rejected. The hatred is perpetual, everlasting, never ending. The forefather's hatred showed in [Numbers 20](/bible/numbers/20) and it shows to this day in the nation of Edom still rejecting Israel; it will not stop until Christ stops it, and Israel's part is to repent and come back to the lost statutes and commandments.

At mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, the Lord said Aaron shall be gathered unto his people; he could not enter the land because of the rebellion at the water of Meribah. Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them upon Eleazar his son; the priesthood passed to Eleazar, and Aaron died there in the top of the mount. When all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, all the house of Israel mourned for Aaron thirty days.

Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth. The song opens by calling heaven and earth to witness, just as Moses said in chapter 31. Notice how the verses run together: my doctrine shall drop as the rain, and then, because I will publish the name of the Lord. Doctrine and the name go together, and greatness is ascribed unto our God.

He is the Rock, his work is perfect, all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he. The song gives the Most High his praise first, then turns to what happens when Israel corrupts themselves. They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: the Most High planted us a noble vine, and we became a degenerate plant. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us; we are a perverse and crooked generation.

Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? This is how you repay the magnificent Lord that delivered you, that destroyed whole nations just so you could inherit their land. Is not he thy father that hath bought thee? Hath he not made thee, and established thee? Isaiah recounts the lovingkindness of the Most High toward the house of Israel: he said, surely they are my people, children that will not lie, so he was their Savior. In all our affliction he was afflicted; whenever he saw us going through atrocities he suffered with us, and in his love and in his pity he redeemed us and carried us all the days of old. How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee. Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Did you know the many generations of your forefathers? Somebody had to show you. The men teaching on the corners and bringing out these prophecies and breakdowns are the ones Moses said would teach you these things: ask thy father, and he will shew thee. Inquire of the former age and prepare thyself to the search of thy fathers: study who we were, see where our fathers went wrong, and do not do the same thing. When we suffer persecution and trials we can go to the scriptures and see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers; that is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves. Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. You thought God wants everybody to just come together and hold hands? The God of this Bible has been a God of division from day one; he separated the sons of Adam according to where he had to place the children of Israel, meaning this world revolves around Israel. For the Lord's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. In the division of the nations he set a ruler over every people, but Israel he kept for himself: that is my inheritance, that is my portion.

He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye. The same people the world counted as three fifths of a man are the apple of the Most High's eye. Zechariah shows who that people is: deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Who was held captive in the land of the north, in North America, but the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans? We are Zion, and we must deliver ourselves from the ways we were taught there. He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye: the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns.

As an eagle stirreth up her nest and beareth her young on her wings, so the Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him. The Most High used no idol of wood or stone to lead us through the wilderness and protect us from the nations; he did that alone. He made him ride on the high places of the earth, to eat the increase of the fields, honey out of the rock, butter of kine and milk of sheep, the fat of lambs and rams, and the pure blood of the grape. This is the journey through the wilderness, how Israel came through all those nations and acquired wealth and provision from the Most High's own hand.

But Jeshurun, meaning Israel, waxed fat, and kicked; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. Waxing fat is not about being overweight; [Deuteronomy 8](/bible/deuteronomy/8) explains it. When thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and thy herds and thy silver and thy gold are multiplied, then thine heart is lifted up and thou forgettest the Lord thy God which brought thee out of the house of bondage. With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God; we get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High.

They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods; they sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not. What are examples of new gods? Islam came about in 622 AD, some six hundred years after Christ. The familiar image of Christ painted in the Renaissance era is a new thing under the sun. Even Buddha, whom people think is ancient, came on the scene between the sixth and fourth centuries BC; our kingdom had already been split and carried captive into Babylon before anybody heard of a Buddha. These are new gods that our people go crazy over today, and the Most High said we would come to that estate.

Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee. When it comes to the Rock that created us, we are unmindful. Who is that Rock? Paul says our fathers drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. Christ did not begin two thousand years after Moses; he was with Israel in the wilderness. David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

When the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons and of his daughters; he said, I will hide my face from them, for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. This goes especially into Judah, the southern kingdom: when Christ was on the scene, the scribes and Pharisees rejected him; they were very froward and had no faith that he was the Son of God, and Christ called them a generation of vipers. They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God, and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people. Some close the book right there and say the Most High welcomed all the other nations in place of Israel; no, the ones which are not a people are also Israel. Isaiah says within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people; and Hosea says of the northern kingdom, ye are not my people, yet in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

For a fire is kindled in mine anger; I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them: burning hunger, bitter destruction, and the teeth of beasts sent upon them. You have seen the clips from the civil rights movement, the canines sent at our people to rip at them with their teeth. That was a fulfillment of prophecy: the Most High said he would send the teeth of beasts against us. The sword without, and terror within, destroying young man and virgin, the suckling with the man of gray hairs: the sword of the other nations, and famine and drought as well. This prophecy had to happen against us because we served other gods.

I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. What corners? Isaiah shows the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah gathered from the four corners of the earth: the scattering was worldwide. What nation of people has been scattered throughout the four corners of the earth by slave trades, the transatlantic, the sub-Saharan, the silk road? The so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. This never happened to the people claiming our heritage; it is further proof of who the children of Israel are. The nations we were scattered to took counsel together: come, let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. Divide them, teach them they are not who they really are: if I get them to take pride in being called anything but Israel, they will never remember. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, but the remembrance has not completely ceased.

Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this. The Most High would not let the enemy think they accomplished the complete destruction of the Israelites by their own hand; that is why, after a certain amount of time, he begins waking us up, and why we are starting to remember who we are this day. For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them. O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end. If you knew exactly what disaster was coming and when, you would set every alarm; our forefathers were told all these atrocities ahead of time and still did not consider it. How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had shut them up? How could we be conquered the way we were, thousands rounded up by a few, unless the Most High allowed it? It had to be the Lord.

For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges. For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: that is why the sins of Sodom show up among our people today, even paraded as pride. The Most High said our vine became the vine of Sodom; their grapes are grapes of gall, their wine is the poison of dragons. Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures? These prophecies were sealed up with the Most High until their time.

To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand. After he let these nations deceive and oppress us for so long, the Most High will show who God really is; but he had to let us humble ourselves first for serving all those false gods. For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants: he will change his mind, and instead of inflicting wrath upon us he will save us. When he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left: when he sees that we have fallen to our lowest estate possible, then he moves.

And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted? Now that you are being shot down in the street, locked in cages, where are the idols and the saints you prayed to? Let them rise up and help you. The Most High had to let it play out over a span of time, allowing enemies to afflict us, so we would see that the gods we went off to worship were not real gods, because they could not help when the Lord sent the enemy against us. Jeremiah says our people say to a stock, Thou art my father, and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth; but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us. Where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? Let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods. That is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities; that is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day.

See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand. A statue you made with your hands cannot kill a thing and cannot make alive; the true God does both. That is the terrible God we serve, the God of our people, and once his people get back on his good side, the nations that touched the apple of his eye have judgment coming.

For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever. The Most High will eventually turn back to save us; he will stop hiding his face and come to our defense. If I whet my glittering sword, and mine hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me. I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh; and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy. The Most High takes revenge for the captives, because he is the God of the people that have been in captivity over and over again. In the churches they never read this; they never knew that God is this way, and it shows what they really think about him.

Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people. Read through the Bible: Christ put to death, James put to death, Peter put to death, and since the Bible was written more prophets have lost their lives for the truth, and it will continue. The innocent and righteous blood crieth unto the Most High, and the souls of the just complain continually, asking when he will act; and he answers, I will surely avenge them. This is fulfilled in the destruction of Babylon: rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets, for God hath avenged you on her. Babylon the great in this teaching is the United States of America; that is where the Lord makes his arrows drunk with blood, the vengeance promised for all the wrong these nations have done unto us.

Moses and Joshua spake all the words of this song in the ears of the people, and Moses said, Set your hearts unto all the words which I testify among you this day, which ye shall command your children to observe to do. For it is not a vain thing for you; because it is your life. The words of this law are not something to sit on your dashboard or in your cabinet; this book is your life, and if you are not reading it, you are not living. Through this thing ye shall prolong your days in the land: not just eating right or exercising, but doing this law is how you prolong your days.

That selfsame day the Most High tells Moses: get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, over against Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan; and die in the mount, as Aaron died in mount Hor, because ye trespassed against me at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh, because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel. The account is in Numbers 20: the people angered Moses at the waters of strife, complaining and provoking him after all they had already seen, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes. They provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips: Hear now, ye rebels; and he smote the rock twice instead of speaking to it, the Rock we read about earlier in this chapter. Thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

verses.text: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the congregation and their beasts drink.
And Moses took the rod from before the Lord, as he commanded him.
And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?
And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.

And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.
And the Lord spake unto Moses that selfsame day, saying,

Get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is over against Jericho; and behold the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel for a possession:
And die in the mount whither thou goest up, and be gathered unto thy people; as Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people:
Because ye trespassed against me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah–Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin; because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel.
Yet thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither unto the land which I give the children of Israel.
They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes:
Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.

cases.name: Israel and the fiery serpents
cases.charge: Speaking against God and against Moses; loathing the bread from heaven
cases.summary: Discouraged on the way around Edom, the people spoke against God and Moses: there is no bread, no water, and our soul loatheth this light bread. The Lord sent fiery serpents, and much people of Israel died.
cases.offense: Edom had refused them passage and the way round was long, and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way (Numbers 21:4). Then the people spake against God, and against Moses, wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water, and our soul loatheth this light bread (Numbers 21:5). The bread they loathed was angels' food, rained from heaven every morning (Psalms 78:25), and the complaint is aimed at both the provision and the deliverer in a single breath. Paul files it as tempting Christ: neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents (1 Corinthians 10:9). No other people in the record takes its food so seriously or complains of it so readily, and it is one of the marks by which this nation is known.
cases.judgment: The Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, and much people of Israel died (Numbers 21:6). The biting brought them back into the spirit at once: we have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord, and against thee; pray unto the Lord,  that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people (Numbers 21:7). The serpents were not taken away. Moses was told to make a fiery serpent and set it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived (Numbers 21:9). Wisdom says they were troubled for a  small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, and that he that turned toward it was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by thee that art the Saviour of all (Wisdom of Solomon 16:6-7). The brass serpent was for Israel, to heal the Israelites bitten for rebelling against God and Moses, and Christ took it as the figure of his own death when speaking to a ruler of the Jews: as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life (John 3:14-15). The brass serpent itself became an idol centuries later and Hezekiah broke it in pieces, which is entered under his name in this volume.

verses.text: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way.

And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.
And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.

Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord, and against thee; pray unto the Lord, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.
And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.
And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:
That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, thy wrath endured not for ever:
But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.
For he that turned himself toward it was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by thee, that art the Saviour of all.

He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.

entries.commentary: King Arad the Canaanite, which dwelt in the south, fought against Israel and took some of them prisoners. Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord, and the Lord hearkened and delivered up the Canaanites, and Israel utterly destroyed them and their cities. The Canaanites are identified in this teaching with the people called Africans today. The place was called Hormah, which means utter destruction, because that is exactly what Israel did to them there.

They journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea to compass the land of Edom, and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way: since Edom refused passage, Israel had to go around, and the way was longer than they wanted it to be. The people spake against God and against Moses: no bread, no water, and our soul loatheth this light bread. The bread they were loathing was angels' bread, and they complained about it anyway. No other nation on this earth takes food as seriously as Israel; even the complaints over bread and water are a familiar mark of this people to this day. You cannot put another nation in these scriptures.

The Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, and much people of Israel died. Read it with the nation in view: the people being bitten, the people dying, all of it is Israel. Once the serpents started biting and much people died, the people came back into the spirit: we have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord and against thee; pray unto the Lord that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people. Moses made a serpent of brass and set it upon a pole, and it came to pass that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived. The symbol on ambulances today, a snake wrapped around a pole, comes from this scripture. That brass serpent on the pole was for the Israelites, to heal the Israelites, because it was the Israelites being bitten for rebelling against God and against Moses. Christ brought this same passage to Nicodemus. Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, and he came to Christ, who is also a Jew: two Israelites speaking together about the history of Israel. As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel.

The children of Israel set forward and pitched in Oboth, then in Ijeabarim, in the wilderness before Moab toward the sunrising, then in the valley of Zared, then on the other side of Arnon, which is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites. Now Israel comes among the Moabites and the Ammonites, identified in this teaching with the nations called the Chinese and the Japanese today. It is said in the book of the wars of the Lord what he did in the Red Sea and in the brooks of Arnon.

From thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the Lord spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water. Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, O well. The princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver. The recording ends here, during this passage. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, comes by night. Those men were the teachers of the synagogues, and it would have cost him standing to come openly. Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over.

Nicodemus takes it literally and asks whether a man can enter the second time into his mother's womb. Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. Both are named plainly elsewhere as the word.
That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles.

Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? He was a chief teacher, and men depended on him for the understanding of the law. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?

As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up. The history behind that is plain, and so is who it was for. It was Israel in the wilderness that spake against the Most High and against Moses, and Israel that was bitten, and Israel that looked and lived. The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son. This follows straight on from the serpent, and it is the same people in view. John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. A man can be comfortable and even do well in the darkness he was raised in. Coming into the light requires change, and refusing that change is what condemns him. The Pharisees and the rulers were not condemned by Christ; they condemned themselves by not humbling down to repent. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.

John's disciples notice that all men are coming to Jesus, and John answers, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven. I am not the Christ, but that I am sent before him. He must increase, but I must decrease.

He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true. Not to receive it is to call the record God gave of his son a lie. He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.

Hezekiah son of Ahaz begins to reign over Judah in the third year of Hoshea, the last king of Israel before the captivity. He does that which is right according to all that David his father did, removing the high places, breaking the images, and cutting down the groves. He breaks in pieces the brazen serpent Moses made in the wilderness, which had stood from that time and was now being burned incense to, and he calls it Nehushtan.

Hezekiah trusts in the Most High so that none among the kings of Judah, before or after, was like him. He clave to the Most High, kept the commandments, and the Most High was with him so that he prospered. Prospering here does not mean a mansion or luxury, but the blessing that comes from keeping and doing the commandments. He rebels against the king of Assyria and smites the Philistines even unto Gaza. -

In Hezekiah's fourth year Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, and after three years, in Hezekiah's sixth year, Samaria is taken. Israel was not removed all at once but carried away in stages into Assyria. The reason given again is that they obeyed not the voice of the Most High but transgressed His covenant and all Moses commanded. -

Sennacherib king of Assyria comes up against the fenced cities of Judah and takes them. Hezekiah sends to Lakish acknowledging offense and agrees to bear whatever tribute is laid on him. Assyria appoints three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold, so Hezekiah gives all the silver of the house of the Most High and even cuts the gold from the temple doors.

The king of Assyria sends Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh with a great host to Jerusalem, and they stand by the conduit of the upper pool. Rabshakeh challenges Hezekiah's confidence, mocking his trust and calling Egypt a bruised reed that pierces the hand of any who lean on it. He argues that because Hezekiah removed the high places, even Judah's own worship is now confined to one altar, twisting the reform into a weakness. He boasts that Assyria came up against the land by the word of the Most High Himself, claiming divine backing to destroy it.

Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall will not understand, but he refuses. Rabshakeh cries aloud in the Jews' language, warning the people not to let Hezekiah deceive them or make them trust in the Most High. He promises the people their own vines, fig trees, and waters if they surrender, then a land like their own, seeking to turn them from their king. He asks whether the gods of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah delivered their lands, claiming no god can deliver Jerusalem out of his hand. The people hold their peace and answer not a word, for Hezekiah had commanded silence. Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and tell him the words of Rabshakeh. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)
