cases.name: Sihon and Og
cases.charge: Refusing Israel passage and coming out to battle against them
cases.summary: Israel asked only to pass through on the king's highway, turning neither to the right nor to the left. Sihon gathered his people and came out to fight, and Og after him. Both kingdoms were given into Israel's hand, and the land east of Jordan became the first inheritance.
cases.offense: Moses sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites with words of peace (Deuteronomy 2:26): let me pass through thy land (Numbers 21:22); we will not turn into the fields or the vineyards. Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass, but gathered all his people and fought at Jahaz (Numbers 21:23). Og king of Bashan came out against them at Edrei (Deuteronomy 3:1), the last of the remnant of giants (Deuteronomy 3:11).
cases.judgment: Israel smote Sihon with the edge of the sword (Numbers 21:24) and possessed his land from Arnon to Jabbok. Of Og the Lord said, Fear him not, for I have delivered him into thy hand (Numbers 21:34); they smote him and his sons and all his people until none was left him alive (Numbers 21:35). The psalms remember it as mercy that endureth for ever (Psalms 136:17): who smote great kings, and gave their land for an heritage (Psalms 136:21).

entries.commentary: King Arad the Canaanite, which dwelt in the south, fought against Israel and took some of them prisoners. Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord, and the Lord hearkened and delivered up the Canaanites, and Israel utterly destroyed them and their cities. The Canaanites are identified in this teaching with the people called Africans today. The place was called Hormah, which means utter destruction, because that is exactly what Israel did to them there.

They journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea to compass the land of Edom, and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way: since Edom refused passage, Israel had to go around, and the way was longer than they wanted it to be. The people spake against God and against Moses: no bread, no water, and our soul loatheth this light bread. The bread they were loathing was angels' bread, and they complained about it anyway. No other nation on this earth takes food as seriously as Israel; even the complaints over bread and water are a familiar mark of this people to this day. You cannot put another nation in these scriptures.

The Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, and much people of Israel died. Read it with the nation in view: the people being bitten, the people dying, all of it is Israel. Once the serpents started biting and much people died, the people came back into the spirit: we have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord and against thee; pray unto the Lord that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people. Moses made a serpent of brass and set it upon a pole, and it came to pass that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived. The symbol on ambulances today, a snake wrapped around a pole, comes from this scripture. That brass serpent on the pole was for the Israelites, to heal the Israelites, because it was the Israelites being bitten for rebelling against God and against Moses. Christ brought this same passage to Nicodemus. Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, and he came to Christ, who is also a Jew: two Israelites speaking together about the history of Israel. As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel.

The children of Israel set forward and pitched in Oboth, then in Ijeabarim, in the wilderness before Moab toward the sunrising, then in the valley of Zared, then on the other side of Arnon, which is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites. Now Israel comes among the Moabites and the Ammonites, identified in this teaching with the nations called the Chinese and the Japanese today. It is said in the book of the wars of the Lord what he did in the Red Sea and in the brooks of Arnon.

From thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the Lord spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water. Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, O well. The princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver. The recording ends here, during this passage. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Israel compassed mount Seir many days, and the Lord said, ye have compassed this mountain long enough; turn you northward and pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir, the people called the white man today. They shall be afraid of you: the Most High put fear upon Esau so they would not trouble Israel, because he did not want a war; take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore, and meddle not with them. Mount Seir was given unto Esau for a possession, not so much as a foot breadth of it for Israel; the promise to Israel was the land of Canaan. Israel could buy meat and water of them for money, but take nothing. The Lord thy God hath blessed thee; these forty years he hath been with thee, and thou hast lacked nothing.

Passing from the children of Esau, the same order came concerning Moab: distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle, for Ar was given unto the children of Lot for a possession. For Lot's sake the Most High secured that land to his children; it was not Israel's to conquer.

The Emims dwelt in that land in times past, a people great and many and tall as the Anakims, accounted giants; and the Horims dwelt in Seir beforetime, and the children of Esau succeeded them and dwelt in their stead. That is heavy: the Moabites are not the chosen people, yet they went into a land of giants and took it. Israel had the Most High on their side, the pillar, the power, the angels, and still found a way to be scared of giants.

From Kadesh-barnea to the crossing of the brook Zered was thirty and eight years, until all the generation of the men of war were wasted out from among the host, as the Lord sware unto them. The hand of the Lord was against them to destroy them from among the host until they were consumed; only when all the men of war were dead did the word come to pass over.

Coming over against the children of Ammon, the same charge stood: distress them not, nor meddle with them, for that land was given unto the children of Lot for a possession. Esau, Moab, and Ammon were all off limits; the Most High appointed their possessions, and Israel was to pick no fight with them.

Ammon's land was also accounted a land of giants: the Zamzummims, a people great and many and tall as the Anakims; and the Lord destroyed them, and the Ammonites succeeded them and dwelt in their stead. The giants were famous from the beginning, of great stature and expert in war, yet the Lord chose them not and gave them no knowledge; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom and perished through their own foolishness. There are no giants today; stature and skill in war saved none of them.

As he did to the children of Esau when he destroyed the Horims from before them, so these nations succeeded the giants and dwelt in their stead even unto this day. The Avims which dwelt in Hazerim, even unto Azzah, the Caphtorims destroyed them and dwelt in their stead; the Most High moves nations in and out of lands as he wills.

Rise up, pass over the river Arnon: behold, I have given into thine hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle. This recaps [Numbers 21](/bible/numbers/21), when it was time to destroy the king of the Amorites. This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations under the whole heaven. The Most High never gave Israel the spirit of fear, but when it was time to conquer he put the fear of Israel on the nations, so they trembled and were in anguish.

Moses sent messengers unto Sihon with words of peace: let me pass through thy land by the highway, buying meat and water of thee for money, only passing through on my feet, as was done passing Esau in Seir and Moab in Ar. But Sihon would not let Israel pass, for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand. It is the same dealing as with Pharaoh: the Lord hardened his heart so the judgment could land, for the iniquity of the Amorites was full and their land was appointed to Israel.

Sihon came out against Israel to fight at Jahaz, and the Lord delivered him: they smote him and his sons and all his people, took all his cities, and utterly destroyed the men, women, and little ones of every city; none was left to remain. That is how thorough the judgment of the Most High was for Israel's sake; that is how specially privileged Israel was, and still they struggled to believe and obey him. Only the cattle and the spoil of the cities were taken for a prey. From Aroer by the brink of the river of Arnon even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong: the Lord our God delivered all unto us. Only the land of the children of Ammon they came not unto, nor unto whatsoever the Lord our God forbad: Israel possessed every place the Lord led them and touched nothing he withheld. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Bashan is about to be conquered, and Og the king of Bashan came out with all his people to battle at Edrei. The Most High said fear him not, for I will deliver him and all his people and his land into thy hand, as was done to Sihon king of the Amorites at Heshbon. Always remember, the battle is the Lord's; this fight is spiritual. Israel does not need weapons of mass destruction: the Bible is the weapon, and when Israel keeps the commandments the Most High fights for his people. The Lord our God delivered into our hands also the king of Bashan: they were out there doing physical war, but they gave the praise, the glory, and the victory to the Most High. They did not boast in their own swords; that is how you sanctify the Most High. The same order stands today: when you wake up you thank the Most High, and you thank him for the food even though you cooked it, because he is the one who allowed you to have it. You always put the Most High first.

Threescore cities were taken, all fenced with high walls, gates, and bars, beside unwalled towns a great many, and not one city was left untaken. They utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city, as they did unto Sihon king of Heshbon. That command came from the Most High himself; this is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of the Bible, not the invented gospel that says he loves everybody no matter what. Only the cattle and the spoil of the cities were taken for a prey; those were needed and were spared.

Israel took the land from the two kings of the Amorites on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon. Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His bedstead was a bedstead of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds, showing how tall and big this man was. Og was an Amorite, and the Amorites descend from Ham; [Genesis 10](/bible/genesis/10) proves the lineage. The Hamitic nations were known for great stature, as Goliath the Philistine stood nine feet nine inches, and to this day the tallest peoples on earth, the Watusi, the Dinka, and the Nilotic tribes of Sudan, Ethiopia, and Kenya, are Hamites. Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

The conquered land was divided: from Aroer by the river Arnon and half mount Gilead to the Reubenites and the Gadites, and the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half tribe of Manasseh. All the region of Argob with all Bashan was called the land of giants, because the giants there were of Og's kin, of his family. Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob and called it after his own name, Bashan-havoth-jair, unto this day.

All that were meet for the war were to pass over armed before their brethren, while the wives, the little ones, and the much cattle abode in the cities already given, until the Most High gave rest to their brethren and they also possessed their land beyond Jordan. When you read these wars, put yourself in the position of the brothers going out. Being promised victory over the land did not mean every man would survive it; Israel still had casualties, and there were brothers that gave their lives for their people. Read to understand, not just to say you read your four chapters: bring the scripture to life and visualize what was really going on.

Joshua was commanded at that time: thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings; so shall he do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest. Ye shall not fear them, for the Lord your God he shall fight for you; the victories over Sihon and Og were the proof set before Joshua's own eyes.

Moses besought the Most High: thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness and thy mighty hand, for what God is there in heaven or in earth that can do according to thy works and according to thy might? That greatness shown to Moses was more than the exodus. On Sinai he received the ten commandments and the six hundred plus commandments, ceremonial, civil, moral, dietary, and sacrificial, that the Most High ordained Israel to keep. He was also told many wondrous things: the prophecies such as [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), that the people would go into slave ships under yokes of iron, lose their nationality, become a byword and an astonishment, and that a small remnant would wake up in the end days and come back. He was shown the secrets of the times, the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and the end itself; all of that stands behind this thanksgiving in Deuteronomy.

Moses begged: I pray thee, let me go over and see the good land that is beyond Jordan. The Most High had already told him he would not see the promised land, and Moses was trying to get him to repent of the word he had given. The sentence came from the water of Meribah: Moses said hear now, ye rebels, must we fetch you water out of this rock, and smote the rock twice. He took the credit and became high minded instead of sanctifying the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, so he was told he would not bring the congregation into the land. The contrast is [Deuteronomy 3:3](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v3): after the war with Og the people said the Lord our God delivered them into our hands. That is sanctifying the Most High; Moses at the rock did the opposite. The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel. And the answer was final, let it suffice thee, speak no more unto me of this matter, as a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again.

Get thee up into the top of Pisgah and behold the land with thine eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, for thou shalt not go over this Jordan; seeing it from the mountain was all that was granted. But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people and cause them to inherit the land. The Most High said plainly whom he would deal with for the crossing. Promotion comes from the Most High: he was dealing with Moses and declared who he wanted in charge, and Moses was to strengthen the man chosen to replace him.

When thou goest out to battle and seest horses and chariots and a people more than thou, be not afraid, for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. That goes for us now, because we are still in a battle. We are not physically out battling the nations as our forefathers were when they took the land; we are in a spiritual battle, for the nations are confederate against Israel being a nation any more and against our remembrance of Israel and our laws. This whole world is set up for our people to go into sin and iniquity. Fear makes people trim their ways: afraid of family at the pagan holiday table, tucking their fringes in certain places, scared to be seen in the truth. Stand boldly; the Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, for that spirit came from Satan himself.

When Israel came nigh unto the battle, the priest approached and spoke: let not your hearts faint, fear not, do not tremble, neither be ye terrified, for the Lord your God is he that goeth with you to fight for you against your enemies to save you. A lot of times you do not see that the Lord is fighting for you in the spirit; that is where faith comes in, for the Bible is a faith-based book. You have to have faith that the Most High is fighting for you, with angels encamped round about the righteous, as David told us.

The officers sent home the man that had built a new house and not dedicated it, the man that had planted a vineyard and not eaten of it, and the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her, lest he die in the battle and another man take his portion. You could very well die fighting for your people, so go enjoy these things first: dedicate your new house unto the Lord, eat the fruits of your labour from your vineyard, take your wife, then come to war for your people.

The fearful and fainthearted man was also sent home, lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart. The spirit of fear spreads: one man's fear makes the next man wonder what he knows, and soon the whole company questions the battle.

When the officers finished speaking, they made captains of the armies to lead the people, because you cannot have order without a ranking structure. Everybody cannot be calling the shots; there is one shot caller and the people follow, and that same order set in Moses' time is why a body under rank is proficient in everything it does.

When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, first proclaim peace unto it. If it answered peace and opened, all the people found in it became tributaries unto Israel and served them. In this time Israel had the power to make nations tributaries. Right now we are not even a nation, just a people with Bibles and nothing established; but wait until Christ comes, for Israel will be established as a nation again and rule the earth, and the nations will be tributaries.

Israel came to a land with terms: agree, pay the tribute, and there is peace. If the city would make no peace but made war, Israel besieged it, and when the Lord delivered it into their hands, every male was smitten with the edge of the sword. The women, the little ones, the cattle, and all the spoil of the city Israel took unto themselves and ate the spoil of their enemies which the Lord their God had given them.

That was the rule for the cities very far off. But of the cities of the nations given Israel for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth; everything had to die, from humans to animals. The Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites were to be utterly destroyed for a stated purpose: that they teach you not to do after all their abominations which they have done unto their gods, their whoredoms, their idolatry, and their wicked ways of living, so that Israel sin not against the Lord.

In a long siege the trees for meat were not to be destroyed by forcing an axe against them, for thou mayest eat of them; the tree of the field is man's life. Only the trees known not to be trees for meat could be cut down to build bulwarks against the city that maketh war with thee, until it be subdued.

verses.text: And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn into the fields, or into the vineyards; we will not drink of the waters of the well: but we will go along by the king’s high way, until we be past thy borders.

And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the villages thereof.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even unto Arnon.
And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he, and all his people, to the battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him alive: and they possessed his land.
And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
Let me pass through thy land: I will go along by the high way, I will neither turn unto the right hand nor to the left.
Thou shalt sell me meat for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink: only I will pass through on my feet;
(As the children of Esau which dwell in Seir, and the Moabites which dwell in Ar, did unto me;) until I shall pass over Jordan into the land which the Lord our God giveth us.
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day.
And the Lord said unto me, Behold, I have begun to give Sihon and his land before thee: begin to possess, that thou mayest inherit his land.
Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Jahaz.
And the Lord our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city, we left none to remain:
Only the cattle we took for a prey unto ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we took.
From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the Lord our God delivered all unto us:
Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto me, Fear him not: for I will deliver him, and all his people, and his land, into thy hand; and thou shalt do unto him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
So the Lord our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.
And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many.
And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city.
But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey to ourselves.
And we took at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites the land that was on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon;
(Which Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion; and the Amorites call it Shenir;)
All the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salchah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.
To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And slew famous kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And gave their land for an heritage: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Even an heritage unto Israel his servant: for his mercy endureth for ever.
When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it.
And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.
And if it will make no peace with thee, but will make war against thee, then thou shalt besiege it:

cases.name: Balaam
cases.charge: Divination for hire; counseling Moab to seduce Israel into idolatry
cases.summary: Hired by Balak to curse Israel, Balaam could only bless. So he taught Balak a surer way: draw Israel into fornication and the feasts of Baal-peor and let their own God judge them. It worked, and it killed him.
cases.offense: Balak sent for him to curse Israel and the answer was given him at the first asking: thou shalt not go with them, thou shalt not curse the people, for they are blessed (Numbers 22:12). He asked again when the princes came back with more honour, and the going was permitted in anger, and the angel of the Lord stood in the way for an adversary against him with a drawn sword, and his ass saw what the prophet could not (Numbers 22:22-23). Peter names the spirit: Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness, but was rebuked for his iniquity, the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet (2 Peter 2:15-16). He could not curse them, and blessed them four times against his will, so he found another way to bring the curse. Moses names it after the war: these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor (Numbers 31:16), and Christ  names it in the churches: the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication (Revelation 2:14). The offence was not the failed curse. It was teaching the enemy how to make Israel curse itself.
cases.judgment: He was killed in the war his own counsel caused. Israel slew the kings of Midian, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian, and Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword (Numbers 31:8), so the man who would not go home when the angel stood in the road died among the kings he had advised. Joshua sets him among the slain and calls him the soothsayer (Joshua 13:22). Jude gives the sentence on everyone who follows him: they ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core (Jude 1:11), and his own words are left standing in the record as the verdict on his life, let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his (Numbers 23:10), which was the one thing he did not get.

verses.text: He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me:

Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: peradventure I shall prevail, that we may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land: for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.
And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand; and they came unto Balaam, and spake unto him the words of Balak.
And God said unto Balaam, Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed.
And God came unto Balaam at night, and said unto him, If the men come to call thee, rise up, and go with them; but yet the word which I shall say unto thee, that shalt thou do.
And Balaam rose up in the morning, and saddled his ass, and went with the princes of Moab.
And God’s anger was kindled because he went: and the angel of the Lord stood in the way for an adversary against him. Now he was riding upon his ass, and his two servants were with him.

And they slew the kings of Midian, beside the rest of them that were slain; namely, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.
Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.
Because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.
Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam; but the Lord thy God turned the curse into a blessing unto thee, because the Lord thy God loved thee.
Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.
Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness;
But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man’s voice forbad the madness of the prophet.
Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication.
O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the Lord.

entries.commentary: The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25); go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.

A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25).

They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them.

Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25). Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to [Numbers 5:2](/bible/numbers/5#v2), putting the defiled outside the camp. Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in [Numbers 19](/bible/numbers/19). Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.

Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other. A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle.

Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

Joshua is old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed. The Most High had already said he was not going to drive out these nations in one year, but little and little as Israel increased, so much land still remained. The nations were also left among Israel to prove them, whether they would keep the commandments of the Most High, and so that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might be taught war. We all know what ended up happening with that proving, and it comes later on as we read.

This is the land that yet remains: all the borders of the Philistines with their five lords, the Gazathites, the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites, along with the Avites, the Canaanites, the Sidonians, the Amorites, the Giblites, and all Lebanon toward the sunrising. These are the different peoples that still had to be driven out of these lands.

The Most High himself will drive out the inhabitants of the hill country of Lebanon and all the Sidonians from before the children of Israel; Joshua's part is only to divide the land by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as he was commanded. The land is to be divided only unto the Israelites: unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh, for the other two and a half tribes had already received theirs. It had already been told that these lands must be divided among our people.

The Reubenites and the Gadites had already received their inheritance with the half tribe of Manasseh, which Moses gave them beyond Jordan eastward: all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites and all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who remained of the remnant of the giants, for these did Moses smite and cast out. Nevertheless the children of Israel expelled not the Geshurites nor the Maachathites, but they dwelt among the Israelites until this day. Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance. The Most High had already said the same thing way back to Aaron, that Levi would have no inheritance in the land but would live among the people, and what was stated back then is being carried out in what we are reading now.

Moses gave the tribe of the children of Reuben their inheritance according to their families: from Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon, all the plain by Medeba, Heshbon and all her cities, unto Jordan and his border, the cities and the villages thereof. With the princes of Midian, Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword. This is the same Balaam from [Numbers 22](/bible/numbers/22), the one whose ass saw the angel standing there to kill him when he could not see it himself. He was the one going after the lust of greed, and he ended up getting put to death.

Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of the children of Gad according to their families: Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, half the land of the children of Ammon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, unto the edge of the sea of Chinnereth on the other side Jordan eastward, the cities and their villages.

Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh by their families: from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og, and all the towns of Jair, threescore cities, pertaining unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh. These are the countries which Moses distributed for inheritance in the plains of Moab, on the other side Jordan by Jericho eastward. But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: the Lord God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them. It is the same thing that is said in verse 14.

Hear ye now what the Lord saith; Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice. For the Lord hath a controversy with his people, and he will plead with Israel. O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me. I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of servants; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, that ye may know the righteousness of the Lord.

Wherewith shall I come before the Lord, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old? Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

Are there yet the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the scant measure that is abominable? Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights? The rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth. Therefore also will I make thee sick in smiting thee, in making thee desolate because of thy sins. Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil. For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; therefore ye shall bear the reproach of my people.

cases.name: Israel at Baal-peor
cases.charge: Fornication with the daughters of Moab; sacrificing to their gods
cases.summary: In Shittim the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, who called them to the sacrifices of their gods. Israel ate, bowed down, and joined himself unto Baal-peor. The plague took twenty-four thousand.
cases.offense: It was Balaam's counsel executed. He could not curse a people God had blessed, so he taught Balak the one thing that works: put another god in front of Israel and send the women to bring them to it (Numbers 31:16; Revelation 2:14). Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab (Numbers 25:1), and they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods (Numbers 25:2). The whoredom and the worship were not two sins but one; the rite of Baal-peor was whoredom, and Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor (Numbers 25:3), joined as a man is joined to a wife. Hosea gives the verdict on the whole affair: they went to Baal-peor, and separated themselves unto that shame, and their abominations were according as they loved (Hosea 9:10), and the psalm adds what they ate: they joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead (Psalms 106:28). It was the golden calf again, for the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play, and that play was the same play (1 Corinthians 10:7-8).
cases.judgment: The Lord's sentence began with the leadership: take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel (Numbers 25:4), and Moses said unto the judges of Israel, slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal-peor (Numbers 25:5), every judge by his rank  taking the men under him. A plague ran through the camp while the sentence was being carried out, and it was stayed by the javelin of Phinehas, which is entered separately as a blessing, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand (Numbers 25:9). Paul, counting the day itself, says three and twenty thousand fell in one day (1 Corinthians 10:8). Moses set the outcome before the next generation as a thing their own eyes had seen: all the men that followed Baal-peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them from among you, but ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day (Deuteronomy 4:3-4). Then the judgment turned outward against the nation that had supplied the women, which is entered under the Midianites.

verses.text: And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.
And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.
And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.
And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.
And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.
Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.
Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal–peor: for all the men that followed Baal–peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them from among you.
They joined themselves also unto Baal–peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
Thus they provoked him to anger with their inventions: and the plague brake in upon them.

I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: but they went to Baal–peor, and separated themselves unto that shame; and their abominations were according as they loved.
Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

lawDetails.text: Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.

entries.commentary: Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.

The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25); go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.

A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25).

They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them.

Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25). Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to [Numbers 5:2](/bible/numbers/5#v2), putting the defiled outside the camp. Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in [Numbers 19](/bible/numbers/19). Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.

Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other. A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle.

Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

Hearken, O Israel: hearken means listen, pay attention, and there is a difference between hearing and listening. The statutes and judgments are taught for to do them; knowing you are an Israelite is only half the battle. The main thing is applying the scriptures, doing what the Most High is telling you to do, that ye may live. The promise is to go in and possess the land, and possessing land is true wealth: your milk and honey, your cattle, your agriculture, where you cultivate and take care of your family. It is not the diamonds, the cars, the sneakers, or the newest phone; a big house with no land is not wealth, and that is why the heathen boxes our people into apartments.

Ye shall not add unto the word, neither diminish ought from it. This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book: the prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ, and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes. The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove [Matthew 18:11](/bible/matthew/18#v11) and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.

Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal-peor: all the men that followed Baal-peor were destroyed from among the people, and this recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite. But ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day: those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive. The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.

Keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at. When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group, or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ; but rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

What nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them? The Most High is near unto Israel in all things they call upon him for, and no nation has statutes and judgments so righteous as this law. When Israel keeps the laws, statutes, and commandments, they are the light of the world; in the days when the brothers and sisters were in order, the nations looked on and marveled at what nation this was, so great and so beautiful.

Take heed to thyself and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things thine eyes have seen; and teach them thy sons, and thy sons' sons. These are generational commandments: children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat. Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children. Why learn to fear the Most High? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

The mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, and the Most High spake out of the midst of the fire; ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude. He declared his covenant, even ten commandments: the ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them. And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever.

The Most High commanded Moses at that time to teach the statutes and judgments, and Israel is charged to take good heed, for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day the Lord spake in Horeb. No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches: when the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant. Fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill; it was simple and easy to understand. Lest ye corrupt yourselves and make a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female: Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day. The eagle and the falcon symbols of the powers of this world trace back to the gods and goddesses of Egypt, because this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her. Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt. Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.

The Lord hath taken you and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance. Furthermore the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: again Moses lays his barred crossing on the people. It is how the workers feel when they go out to preach truth and catch anger for it; you are not arguing with the messenger, you are mad at the Bible, so speak the oracles and neither add nor diminish to please anybody. Moses must die in this land and not go over Jordan, but ye shall go over and possess that good land; he kept repeating it, longing for what he would not see.

Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant and make a graven image, for the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When children's children are begotten and the stay in the land grows long, corruption creeps in; make the graven image and do evil to provoke him, and ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land. Heaven and earth are called to witness against Israel this day; the warning was on record before it ever came to pass.

And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen: this is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul; the seeking begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days: the latter days began when Christ came, for God who spake in time past by the prophets hath in these last days spoken by his Son. And shalt be obedient unto his voice: the voice of the Most High tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High. For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

Ask now of the days that are past, since the day that God created man upon the earth: you are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only, but the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it. Did ever people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and live? Hath God assayed to take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand? There is no such history anywhere else; the Most High did this for Israel alone. Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.

Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee; and because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out of Egypt in his sight with his mighty power. To drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou art: they had more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here. Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

Thou shalt keep therefore his statutes and his commandments, that it may go well with thee and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth. This is the solution. The voting, protesting, and marching have never worked and never will; trust in the Most High and keep his laws, and he will take care of his people with long days, families, and the land.

Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising, that the slayer which killed his neighbour unawares, and hated him not in times past, might flee thither and live: Bezer in the wilderness for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. The chapter closes with the summary: this is the law, the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which Moses spake unto the children of Israel after they came forth out of Egypt, in the land of Sihon and of Og, the two kings of the Amorites.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

cases.name: The Midianites, in the matter of Peor
cases.charge: Beguiling Israel with their wiles into fornication and the worship of Baal-peor
cases.summary: Balaam could not curse Israel, so he taught Balak how to make Israel curse itself. The daughters of Midian and Moab drew the people to Peor, and twenty-four thousand died in the plague. The Lord then told Moses to avenge Israel of the Midianites before he was gathered to his people.
cases.offense: On Balaam's counsel the women of Midian invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods (Numbers 25:2); the people ate, and bowed down, and joined themselves to Baal-peor (Numbers 25:3). Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, was brought into the camp itself (Numbers 31:12). They vexed Israel with their wiles, wherewith they beguiled you in the matter of Peor (Numbers 25:18).
cases.judgment: Vex the Midianites, and smite them. Israel warred against Midian as the Lord commanded Moses and slew all the males (Numbers 31:7), the five kings of Midian, and Balaam the son of Beor with the sword (Numbers 31:8). Moses was angry that the women who had caused the trespass were kept alive (Numbers 31:15), and the sentence was carried through on them also.
