verses.text: And Jephthah vowed a vow unto the Lord, and said, If thou shalt without fail deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands,

Then it shall be, that whatsoever cometh forth of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall surely be the Lord’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.
And Jephthah came to Mizpeh unto his house, and, behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances: and she was his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter.

And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he rent his clothes, and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low, and thou art one of them that trouble me: for I have opened my mouth unto the Lord, and I cannot go back.

And she said unto him, My father, if thou hast opened thy mouth unto the Lord, do to me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth; forasmuch as the Lord hath taken vengeance for thee of thine enemies, even of the children of Ammon.
And she said unto her father, Let this thing be done for me: let me alone two months, that I may go up and down upon the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my fellows.
And he said, Go. And he sent her away for two months: and she went with her companions, and bewailed her virginity upon the mountains.
And it came to pass at the end of two months, that she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed: and she knew no man. And it was a custom in Israel,
That the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

Or if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.
And it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these things, that he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing:

And he shall bring his trespass offering unto the Lord for his sin which he hath sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin.
If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.
Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.
And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:

cases.name: Manoah and his wife
cases.charge: Asking how shall we order the child, and doing all that was commanded them
cases.summary: The angel of the Lord appeared to a barren woman of Zorah and told her she would bear a son who was to be a Nazarite from the womb, and gave her a rule for herself as well. She told her husband. He entreated the Lord that the man of God might come again and teach them what they should do unto the child, and the angel came again to the woman in the field, and she ran for her husband. They offered a kid on a rock and the angel ascended in the flame.
cases.offense: Israel had again done evil and had been delivered into the Philistines' hand for forty years when the angel appeared to Manoah's barren wife (Judges 13:1-3). The promise of a son was also the beginning of an answer to the nation's affliction. The child would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines, and his dedication would start in the womb (Judges 13:5). The mother was commanded to drink no wine or strong drink and eat no unclean thing. No razor was to come upon the child's head (Judges 13:4-7). Numbers 6:1-5 gives the separation of the Nazarite: abstinence from the vine and uncut hair during the vow. Nazarite describes consecration, not residence in Nazareth. The instructions were particular, and the promise did not release the household from observing them. Manoah prayed for the messenger to return and teach them how to order the child. When the angel came again, he repeated what had already been commanded to the woman (Judges 13:8-14). Their task was not to invent a manner of upbringing because the child was extraordinary. They were to receive and keep the instruction given. The Lord's purpose for a child lays responsibility upon those raising him. When Manoah offered hospitality, the angel directed any burnt offering to the Lord, not to himself (Judges 13:15-16). Colossians 2:18 warns against worshipping angels, and the angel before John likewise commanded him to worship God (Revelation 22:8-9). Honour toward a heavenly messenger must not become the worship that belongs to the one who sent him.
cases.judgment: Manoah offered the kid and meat offering to the Lord upon a rock. The angel ascended in the flame, and the husband and wife fell upon their faces (Judges 13:19-20). They had received a heavenly visitation, but they had not seen the Most High himself. The messenger's appearance and departure made clear that the promise was no ordinary man's assurance. Manoah feared they would die. His wife answered from what the Lord had done: he had accepted their offering, shown them these things, and announced what was to come (Judges 13:21-23). She weighed the fear against the received promise. The Lord had instructed them concerning a child's life, not prepared them for their own immediate destruction. She bore Samson; he grew, the Lord blessed him, and the Spirit began to move him (Judges 13:24-25). Psalms 113:9 speaks of the barren woman made a joyful mother. Here the blessing reached beyond the household: the promised child would begin the deliverance of an afflicted people. The parents' part was to honour the giver by obeying what he had commanded.
offenseFull: Israel had again done evil and had been delivered into the Philistines' hand for forty years when the angel appeared to Manoah's barren wife (Judges 13:1-3). The promise of a son was also the beginning of an answer to the nation's affliction. The child would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines, and his dedication would start in the womb (Judges 13:5).

The mother was commanded to drink no wine or strong drink and eat no unclean thing. No razor was to come upon the child's head (Judges 13:4-7). Numbers 6:1-5 gives the separation of the Nazarite: abstinence from the vine and uncut hair during the vow. Nazarite describes consecration, not residence in Nazareth. The instructions were particular, and the promise did not release the household from observing them.

Manoah prayed for the messenger to return and teach them how to order the child. When the angel came again, he repeated what had already been commanded to the woman (Judges 13:8-14). Their task was not to invent a manner of upbringing because the child was extraordinary. They were to receive and keep the instruction given. The Lord's purpose for a child lays responsibility upon those raising him.

When Manoah offered hospitality, the angel directed any burnt offering to the Lord, not to himself (Judges 13:15-16). Colossians 2:18 warns against worshipping angels, and the angel before John likewise commanded him to worship God (Revelation 22:8-9). Honour toward a heavenly messenger must not become the worship that belongs to the one who sent him.
judgmentFull: Manoah offered the kid and meat offering to the Lord upon a rock. The angel ascended in the flame, and the husband and wife fell upon their faces (Judges 13:19-20). They had received a heavenly visitation, but they had not seen the Most High himself. The messenger's appearance and departure made clear that the promise was no ordinary man's assurance.

Manoah feared they would die. His wife answered from what the Lord had done: he had accepted their offering, shown them these things, and announced what was to come (Judges 13:21-23). She weighed the fear against the received promise. The Lord had instructed them concerning a child's life, not prepared them for their own immediate destruction.

She bore Samson; he grew, the Lord blessed him, and the Spirit began to move him (Judges 13:24-25). Psalms 113:9 speaks of the barren woman made a joyful mother. Here the blessing reached beyond the household: the promised child would begin the deliverance of an afflicted people. The parents' part was to honour the giver by obeying what he had commanded.

verses.text: And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bare not.
And the angel of the Lord appeared unto the woman, and said unto her, Behold now, thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.
Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing:

For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.
Then Manoah intreated the Lord, and said, O my Lord, let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us, and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born.
And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband was not with her.
And the woman made haste, and ran, and shewed her husband, and said unto him, Behold, the man hath appeared unto me, that came unto me the other day.
And Manoah arose, and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said unto him, Art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? And he said, I am.
And Manoah said, Now let thy words come to pass. How shall we order the child, and how shall we do unto him?
And the angel of the Lord said unto Manoah, Of all that I said unto the woman let her beware.
She may not eat of any thing that cometh of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing: all that I commanded her let her observe.

entries.commentary: The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years. This is the pattern of the book of Judges: after Joshua's death Israel went off, and nation after nation was given power over them before the great captivities ever came.
There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. He was married, but his wife was barren; she was not able to have any children.

The angel of the Lord appeared unto the woman and told her plainly: you are barren now, but you shall conceive and bear a son, a man child. This is one of many examples in the Bible of our foremothers going through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready he enabled them to conceive. Sisters who have tried for years without children should in patience possess their souls, take comfort of the scriptures, meditate on the foremothers, and believe what the Bible says.

The angel commanded the mother herself to drink no wine nor strong drink and to eat no unclean thing, because the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb; even in the womb he was to be kept pure. No razor was to come on his head, for the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb, and he would begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines. This is one of the first examples in scripture of somebody actually living the vow that was laid out in [Numbers 6](/bible/numbers/6). Understand the difference between a Nazarite and a Nazarene. Christ was a Nazarene because he was from the city of Nazareth, not a Nazarite; he drank wine, and Nazarites could not drink the blood of the grape at all. The woman came and told her husband that a man of God came unto her whose countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible. In verse 3 the scripture says it was the angel of the Lord, but he did not tell her, so she was not sure; she only knew his face was terrible like an angel's. The popular pictures of angels as cute babies with smooth cheeks and little white wings do not match the biblical descriptions at all. To see an angel of the Most High was a terrifying sight, not something to jump for joy about. She repeated the message: the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death, and she was to drink no wine nor strong drink nor eat any unclean thing.

Manoah entreated the Lord: let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born. The Most High hearkened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field; she made haste and ran and showed her husband that the man was back.

Manoah arose and went after his wife, came to the man, and asked, art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? He said, I am. Manoah asked how they should order the child and what they should do unto him, and the angel reiterated the instructions he had already given: of all that I said unto the woman let her beware, and all that I commanded her let her observe while she carries this son.

Manoah tried to detain the angel and make ready a kid for him, but the angel refused: though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread, and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord. The angel knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God because we cannot see the Most High, which is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels. Manoah still did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.

Manoah asked the angel his name, so that when his sayings came to pass they might do him honour. The angel answered, why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret? His name was too wonderful to be uttered to him.

Manoah took a kid with a meat offering and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord, and the angel did wondrously: when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame and went out of their sight. Manoah and his wife fell on their faces to the ground at the sight. This is the kind of thing Israel was able to see and witness with their own eyes. The angel appeared no more, and then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord.

Manoah said to his wife, we shall surely die, because we have seen God. This is a passage the contradictors point to, since the Bible says no man hath seen God; but God here is Elohim, which is plural and speaks of heavenly beings. They saw an angel, not the Most High God. No flesh can look upon the Most High God; he is far too fierce and terrible. The furthest anybody got was Moses seeing his back parts. His wife reasoned rightly: if the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things.

The woman bare a son and called his name Samson, and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him. The spirit of the Lord began to move him at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol; the Most High began to deal with him.

cases.name: Samson
cases.charge: Marrying a Philistine; going in to a harlot; betraying his Nazarite vow to Delilah
cases.summary: A Nazarite from the womb who repeatedly went down to the Philistines for women: a wife at Timnath against his parents' counsel, a harlot at Gaza, and Delilah in Sorek, to whom he told all his heart. He woke from her lap shaven, and the Lord had departed from him.
cases.offense: Samson's parents questioned his desire for a Philistine wife, but he insisted upon the woman who pleased him. At the same time, the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines who ruled Israel (Judges 14:1-4). His purpose worked through Samson's weakness without making that weakness a rule of obedience. Isaiah 55:8-9 places the Lord's thoughts above man's, and Proverbs 21:30 declares that no counsel stands against him. At Timnath, the Philistines threatened the woman and her father's house to obtain the answer to Samson's riddle. She pressed him until he told her, then gave the answer to her people (Judges 14:15-18). Samson's strength did not keep him from yielding to pressure. The quarrel spread through the loss of his wife, the burning of the Philistines' crops, and further bloodshed (Judges 14:19-20; 15:1-8). The Lord was bringing an occasion against the oppressor through the very entanglement Samson had pursued. At Gaza he went in to a harlot and escaped an ambush by carrying away the city gates. Afterward he loved Delilah, and the Philistine lords offered her silver to discover how to bind him (Judges 16:1-5). She asked for the means of his affliction, tried what he told her, and repeatedly called the enemy upon him. The warning was not hidden. He remained after the withs, the new ropes, and the weaving of his locks had each been used against him (Judges 16:6-14). Daily pressure overcame his discretion, and he told her all his heart: he had been a Nazarite from his mother's womb, and no razor had come upon his head (Judges 16:15-17). Micah 7:5 commands a guard upon the mouth even toward one who lies in the bosom. Samson treated attachment as security after Delilah had shown what she would do with his words. She called the lords, received their money, and caused his locks to be shaved while he slept (Judges 16:18-19).
cases.judgment: He awoke expecting to escape as before, not knowing that the Lord had departed from him. The Philistines put out his eyes, bound him in brass, and made him grind in prison (Judges 16:20-21). Past escapes had become presumption. The strength that broke cords and carried gates was the Lord's gift, not a possession Samson could command while disregarding his consecration. The Philistines credited Dagon with delivering him into their hands and brought him out for sport (Judges 16:23-25). Yet Dagon had not overcome the Lord. Samson's fall had followed the Lord's departure, and his last strength would come by calling upon the Lord again. At Lehi, the man who slew a thousand had needed God even for water to revive him (Judges 15:14-19). Dependence had always been the truth beneath his great strength. Between the pillars he prayed to be remembered and strengthened once more. He bowed with all his might, the house fell, and he slew more at his death than in his life (Judges 16:26-30). The Lord's occasion against the Philistines reached their lords in the place where they honoured Dagon. Samson died with them and was buried by his father's house (Judges 16:31). His history warns against playing with a known snare, and shows that the oppressor's triumph did not overturn the Most High's purpose.

Samson went down to Timnath and saw a woman of the daughters of the Philistines, and told his father and mother, get her for me to wife. As he grew up this brother had a lust issue with heathen women; that is the infamy the story of Samson is known for. His parents answered him rightly: is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? There were twelve tribes; there was no shortage of women in all the coasts of Israel. Samson insisted, get her for me, for she pleaseth me well. The forefathers always charged their sons not to do this.

His father and his mother knew not that it was of the Lord, that he sought an occasion against the Philistines, for at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel. The Lord was moving Samson's spirit, and the parents did not understand, just as we often question the Most High when we have no idea the depths of his wisdom and what he is really doing. The Most High was using Samson's flaw, his lust after Philistine women, as an occasion against the Philistines, to destroy them for oppressing his people. That is the basis of the whole story: the Lord was behind all of it, pulling the strings. The Most High is in control of everything, good and evil alike. Even affliction that comes on his people is his tactic to make them seek him and repent; nothing anybody does can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning.

As Samson went down to the vineyards of Timnath, a young lion roared against him, challenging him. Here you begin to see the divine power on Samson. The spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him, and he rent the lion as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: no weapon, no sword, nothing. He tore up a young lion, a prince of the jungle, like it was a little goat. This is one of the forms of the spirit of the Lord, spiritual power. He told not his father or his mother what he had done; he did not boast about it.

He went down and talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well. After a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion he had slain, and behold, there was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcase. He took of the honey in his hands and went on eating, and gave to his father and mother and they did eat, but he told them not that he had taken the honey out of the carcase of the lion.

His father went down unto the woman, and Samson made there a feast, as the young men used to do, and when the Philistines saw him they brought thirty companions to be with him. Samson put forth a riddle: if they could declare it within the seven days of the feast, he would give them thirty sheets and thirty change of garments, and if they could not, they would give him the same. The riddle: out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. In three days they could not expound it.

On the seventh day they said unto Samson's wife, entice thy husband that he may declare unto us the riddle, lest we burn thee and thy father's house with fire. They threatened to burn their own countrywoman in her father's house over thirty outfits. She turned to manipulation and wept before him: thou dost but hate me, and lovest me not; thou hast put forth a riddle unto the children of my people and hast not told it me. He answered, I have not told it my father nor my mother, and shall I tell it thee? She wept before him the seven days while their feast lasted, and on the seventh day he told her, because she lay sore upon him. This big strong mighty brother caved in because of the tears of a woman.

She told the riddle to the children of her people, and the men of the city answered him before the sun went down: what is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion? Samson knew exactly what happened: if ye had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle. Never trust your enemy. That was his wife, and her loyalty belonged to him, but when she got the riddle out of him she went and told it to her heathen people, his enemy. That is why it makes no sense to marry the enemy.

The spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and slew thirty men of the Philistines, took their spoil, and gave the change of garments unto them which expounded the riddle; the spirit of the Lord came upon him even for this, against the nation that oppressed Israel. His anger was kindled, and he went up to his father's house, and Samson's wife was given to his companion, whom he had used as his friend; she was his wife to be, for they had not yet consummated the marriage.

Samson went to Gaza, the chief city of the Philistines, and saw there an harlot and went in unto her; once again the whoremongering spirit had hold of this brother. It was told the Gazites that Samson was come, and they compassed him in and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, quiet all the night, saying, in the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him. Samson lay till midnight, arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron. They wanted to wait at the gate for him, so he took the gates.

Afterward he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah; she was seductive and promiscuous, and Samson started leaning on this other heathen woman. The lords of the Philistines came up unto her and said, entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver. They knew what it took to get to Samson, just as the serpent knew what it took to get to Adam. The scheme never changed: when the devil wants to attack a strong Israelite man, he uses the woman.

Delilah asked Samson outright, tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee. She was literally asking him for the formula to get him killed. He told her, if they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak and be as another man. The lords of the Philistines brought them up, she bound him, with liers in wait abiding in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson. He brake the withs as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire, so his strength was not known. A man of war should have recognized right there that this was a setup, and cut her off, but he stayed.

Delilah pressed again: thou hast mocked me and told me lies, now tell me, I pray thee, wherewith thou mightest be bound. Think how backwards that is: she was openly complaining that he would not hand her the way to bind him. His instinct should have been to get away from her, but he stayed. He said, if they bind me fast with new ropes that never were occupied, then shall I be weak; but he was playing with her, for he had already burst through new cords in chapter 15. Delilah took new ropes and bound him, with liers in wait in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he brake them from off his arms like a thread.

She pressed the third time, and he told her, if thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web. She fastened it with the pin and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; he awaked out of his sleep and went away with the pin of the beam and with the web. Three times she had attempted to have his life taken, and he was still dealing with this harlot; it made no sense, but that is the strength of this snare.

She said, how canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me? and she pressed him daily with her words and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death. Day after day she would not let up. He told her all his heart, and that is where he messed up: there hath not come a razor upon mine head, for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb; if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak and be like any other man. This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says.

When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she knew she had him, and sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, and they came up and brought the money in their hand. She made him sleep upon her knees, and she called for a man and caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head, and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him. She said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he awoke out of his sleep and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him. He thought he was going into beast mode like before, but it was over, because he had broken his vow; the hair was shaved from off his head.

The Philistines took him and put out his eyes, brought him down to Gaza, bound him with fetters of brass, and he did grind in the prison house: a blind slave, put on display like an exhibit, the man that had been slaying them now unable even to see. Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven; they did not keep it cut.

The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, an idolatrous ritual, and to rejoice, for they said, our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand. They gave the praise and the glory to their idol, a devil that had not done a thing. Really it was Samson's own transgression that caused the Most High to allow the Philistines to bind and afflict him; that praise to a fake god did not please the Most High. When their hearts were merry, they said, call for Samson, that he may make us sport; and they called for him out of the prison house and set him between the pillars, using the Israelite man for entertainment and mockery while they honoured their idol.

Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them: the two main pillars that bore up the whole building, one at his right hand and one at his left. Now the house was full of men and women, all the lords of the Philistines were there, and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women that beheld while Samson made sport.

Samson called unto the Lord and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes. He took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, of the one with his right hand and of the other with his left, and said, let me die with the Philistines; and he bowed himself with all his might, and the house fell upon the lords and upon all the people that were therein. So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life. Remember [Judges 14:4](/bible/judges/14#v4): the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines, and even with Samson's failings and flaws the Most High used him as a vessel of vengeance on the heathen who oppressed his people and gave the glory of their victory to a fake god. Israel's salvation in scripture is always joined with the destruction of the enemy. The avenging of what has been done to Israel does not come by striving for equality; the righteous justice and judgment is the destruction the Most High brings on the oppressor.

His brethren and all the house of his father came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

When a man or woman vowed the vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the Lord, he separated himself from wine and strong drink, drank no vinegar of wine nor liquor of grapes, and ate nothing made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk. John the Baptist fell under that Nazarite vow: the angel told Zacharias his son shall drink neither wine nor strong drink, and shall be filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb. John was filled with the Holy Spirit before he was born, and Elizabeth did not sleep with an angel; Zacharias was her husband. The same way Christ was filled with the Holy Spirit before birth; the immaculate conception is a Catholic doctrine, not the scriptures.

All the days of the vow no razor came upon his head; he was holy, and let the locks of the hair of his head grow. Samson was a Nazarite also, from the tribe of Dan; he got caught up in wickedness with the daughters of Ham, but he was a Nazarite, and his hair grew in seven locks. That description is not speaking of the people who call themselves Jews today, whatever the movies portray.

All the days of his separation he came at no dead body, and made not himself unclean even for his father, his mother, his brother, or his sister when they died, because the consecration of his God was upon his head. It was a heavy thing to fall under the Nazarite vow; you had to separate yourself from everybody, even family, so you would not be defiled.

If any man died very suddenly by him, the head of his consecration was defiled: he shaved his head on the seventh day of his cleansing, brought two turtles or two young pigeons to the priest on the eighth day, and a lamb of the first year for a trespass offering; the days before were lost. Paul partook in that Nazarite purification. Unto the Jews he became a Jew; he brought himself down to their level of understanding to win them over, not by breaking the law but by walking orderly and keeping it. The elders at Jerusalem told Paul to purify himself with four men which had a vow on them and be at charges with them, that all may know thou thyself walkest orderly and keepest the law. And note it well: the thousands there that believed were Jews, all zealous of the law, and the Gentiles Paul taught among were Jews scattered among the Gentiles.

When the days of his separation were fulfilled, the Nazarite offered a he lamb without blemish for a burnt offering and a ewe lamb without blemish for a sin offering, with unleavened bread and the meat and drink offerings. Without blemish is the same thing going into Christ. He shaved the head of his separation at the door of the tabernacle and put the hair in the fire under the sacrifice of the peace offerings; the priest put the sodden shoulder and the cakes on his hands and waved them for a wave offering, which we covered in Exodus: the priest picks it up and waves it before the Lord. After that the Nazarite may drink wine; before that he could not. In our understanding today you cannot keep the vow of a Nazarite under Christ: you can let your hair grow as long as you want, but when we break bread and take the cup in remembrance of Christ, renewing that covenant, you have to drink that wine to be in covenant with him.

On this wise Aaron and his sons blessed the children of Israel: the Lord bless thee and keep thee, the Lord make his face shine upon thee and be gracious unto thee, the Lord lift up his countenance upon thee and give thee peace; and they shall put my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them. All of that is a stipulation, a contract; it is not unconditional love with the Most High. Keep my commandments and live. When the southern kingdom asked wherefore the Lord pronounced evil against them, the answer was because your fathers forsook me and walked after other gods, and ye have done worse than your fathers. Bring it up to today: Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, every denomination walking after the imagination of its own evil heart, cast out into a land we knew not, serving gods where the Lord shows no favor. That is why our people have no peace and no blessing. The Most High has taken that blessing from us, and we have to work to get it back by repentance and enduring to the end. But it will happen again; the Lord is pulling his spirit back out on us, and the remnant is waking up.

The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read.

Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.
Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted.

For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health.

Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. Those days are coming back when Christ returns.

If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

verses.text: For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.
And Samson went down to Timnath, and saw a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines.
And he came up, and told his father and his mother, and said, I have seen a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines: now therefore get her for me to wife.

Then his father and his mother said unto him, Is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said unto his father, Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well.
Then went Samson to Gaza, and saw there an harlot, and went in unto her.
And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death;

That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother’s womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.

And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, saying, Come up this once, for he hath shewed me all his heart. Then the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and brought money in their hand.
And she made him sleep upon her knees; and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.

And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him.
But the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison house.

And Samson called unto the Lord, and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.
And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, and on which it was borne up, of the one with his right hand, and of the other with his left.

And Samson said, Let me die with the Philistines. And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein. So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life.
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When either man or woman shall separate themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the Lord:
He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink, and shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of strong drink, neither shall he drink any liquor of grapes, nor eat moist grapes, or dried.
All the days of his separation shall he eat nothing that is made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk.

All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
And what shall I more say? for the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.

cases.name: Micah's idols and the tribe of Dan
cases.charge: A house of gods, a hired Levite, and a tribe that stole both
cases.summary: Micah of Ephraim stole silver from his mother, returned it, and she had it made into a graven and molten image. He set up a house of gods, consecrated his own son, then hired a wandering Levite as priest. The Danites, migrating north, took the priest and the idols for themselves.
cases.offense: Micah stole eleven hundred shekels of silver from his mother and restored them after hearing her curse. She answered with a blessing in the Lord's name, then devoted silver to a graven and molten image (Judges 17:1-4). Restitution of the theft was followed by another offense. Calling the gift dedicated to the Lord did not make an image lawful (Exodus 20:4-5). Micah established a house of gods, made an ephod and teraphim, and appointed one of his sons as priest. When a travelling Levite arrived, he offered him ten shekels a year, clothing, and food to become his priest (Judges 17:5-10). The Levite accepted, and Micah concluded that the Lord would do him good because he now had a Levite (Judges 17:11-13). He trusted the man's tribe and title while disregarding what the man had agreed to serve. Religious office cannot sanctify disobedience. Dan's five spies lodged there, obtained the priest's favourable answer concerning their journey, and saw the images. When six hundred armed Danites returned, the spies took the objects. The priest objected until they offered him a whole tribe instead of one household. His heart was glad, and he went with them (Judges 18:14-20). The service purchased by Micah's silver was transferred for a larger place. A change in patron did not change the corruption.
cases.judgment: Micah pursued and cried that they had taken the gods he had made and his priest. He asked what he had left (Judges 18:22-24). The question exposed the emptiness of his confidence: his gods depended on his hands to make them and his strength to recover them. The Danites threatened his household, and he turned back because they were stronger (Judges 18:25-26). Neither his images nor his hired priest delivered him. Dan smote Laish, a quiet and secure people far from Zidon with no deliverer, rebuilt the city, and named it Dan. There they established the image and its priesthood while the house of God was in Shiloh (Judges 18:27-31). A successful conquest did not cleanse what they carried into it. One man's false worship became an institution maintained among a tribe. That course reaches forward to Jeroboam's calf at Dan and to Amos's word against those who swear by its god (1 Kings 12:28-30; Amos 8:14). Judges records the priesthood continuing until the captivity of the land (Judges 18:30). The refrain that every man did right in his own eyes explains the beginning: private invention, a purchased ministry, theft, and public establishment followed one another where the Lord's command should have governed all (Judges 17:6).

entries.commentary: A man of mount Ephraim named Micah stole eleven hundred shekels of silver from his own mother, and when he heard her cursing about the missing silver he confessed, I took it, and restored it to her. Instead of rebuking her son, his mother said blessed be thou of the LORD, and told him she had wholly dedicated the silver for him to make a graven image and a molten image. She refused to keep what he returned, took two hundred shekels to the founder, and had idols made to set up in her son's house. A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel; there were mothers who steered a son down the wrong path.
Micah had a whole house of gods. He made an ephod and teraphim and consecrated one of his own sons to be his priest, a counterfeit priesthood serving counterfeit gods.

This verse is the key to understanding the whole book of Judges. With no king and no government, Israel was sheep without a shepherd, and when you see how the people carry on in these chapters, that is why: every man did that which was right in his own eyes. The same individual spirit is around today in those who say join no camp and let no man teach you. Every time the scripture shows Israel without a leadership structure, all manner of wickedness follows, primarily idolatry.

A young Levite of Bethlehemjudah departed to sojourn wherever he could find a place and came to mount Ephraim to the house of Micah. When Micah learned the man was a Levite, of the tribe known for the priesthood and the knowledge of the sacrifices, he offered him a deal: dwell with me, be unto me a father and a priest, ten shekels of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. He hired himself a personal priest for his idols.

The Levite was content to dwell with him and became as one of his sons. Nothing says the Levite was already in idolatry, but when money was offered he went right along with it; being corrupted for reward was always the Levites' weakness. Then Micah said, now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest. A house full of idols and a hired priest over them, yet he expected the Most High to bless him because a Levite was on the payroll. That is how sick in the mind Israel was without leadership.

Again the scripture reiterates there was no king in Israel. In those days the tribe of the Danites was still seeking an inheritance to dwell in, because unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes; they had conquered in Joshua's day but never attained all their land. The children of Dan sent five men of valour from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out land to conquer, and on their way they came to mount Ephraim and lodged at the house of Micah.

By the house of Micah they knew the voice of the young man the Levite, and they turned in and questioned him: who brought thee hither? what makest thou in this place? A Levite serving in a house of idols raised questions. He told them plainly, Micah hired me and I am his priest. They asked him to ask counsel of God whether their way would be prosperous, and the priest answered, go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein ye go.

The five men came to Laish and saw the people that were therein, how they dwelt careless, quiet and secure, after the manner of the Zidonians, the nearby nation whose lifestyle they copied. They were a chill people with no worries, not even watching for anyone to come in and conquer them. A magistrate is a judge: there was no judicial system in that land to put a man to shame or convict him for a crime. They were also far from the Zidonians, too far for Zidon to interfere, and had no business with any man, no allies. The spies peeped all of it. Their report back at Zorah and Eshtaol: arise, that we may go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good; a place where there is no want of any thing that is in the earth, and God hath given it into your hands. Do not sit still; let us move now.

Six hundred men of the family of the Danites appointed with weapons of war went up from Zorah and Eshtaol, camped at Mahanehdan behind Kirjathjearim, and passed again unto mount Ephraim to the house of Micah. The first time Micah let the five spies lodge in his house, they saw his expensive looking gods and got covetous. Now passing back through they tell their brethren, do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do. On the way to the lick they spotted another lick. The Bible addresses everything: do not bring just anybody into your house, even brethren, because the deceitful man has many tricks and approaches to finesse you out of the goods in your house.

They turned in to the house and saluted the Levite, a friendly greeting at the door; that is one of the deceitful man's many trains. While the six hundred armed men stood by the entering of the gate keeping the priest occupied, the five spies went up inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image. When the priest saw them coming out with the gods and asked, what do ye? they told him hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or unto a tribe and a family in Israel? Do not snitch; roll with us and be the man over a whole tribe. The priest's heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the graven image and went in the midst of the people. His covetous spirit was plain: already sold out to serve idols for Micah's silver, he dropped the man who treated him as a son the moment a bigger position was offered. Disloyal through and through.

When Micah and the men near his house gathered and overtook the children of Dan, Dan asked, what aileth thee, that thou comest with such a company? He answered, ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and ye are gone away: and what have I more? Examine how foolish that sounds: my gods which I made. How can a man make his own god? That is how simple we had become without leadership. Dan's answer: let not thy voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee, and thou lose thy life, with the lives of thy household. In plain terms, hush, because you are going to anger some of these brothers, they will run up on you, and you and your folks will not make it home. Micah saw they were too strong for him and turned back to his house. Dan was a problem.

The Danites took the things which Micah had made and the priest which he had, came unto Laish, unto a people quiet and secure, smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire. There was no deliverer, because Laish was far from Zidon and had no business with any man, exactly what the spies had scoped out; no neighbor and no ally came to save them. They built the city again, dwelt therein, and called the name of it Dan, after Dan their father which was born unto Israel; howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.

The first thing the children of Dan did in the land the Most High allowed them to take was set up the graven image, a god made by the hands of a man they had just robbed. Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land, and they kept Micah's graven image all the time the house of God was in Shiloh. Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going up to sacrifice at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their heart would turn again unto Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him; so he took counsel and made two calves of gold with his own hands, doubling the iniquity of the wilderness, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh that not one of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife. This follows the previous chapter, where the tribes went to war against Benjamin. The people came to the house of God and sat there till evening before God, lifted up their voices and wept sore, asking why it had come to pass that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel. The next day they rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. The children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, for there was one tribe cut off from Israel that day. They had also made a great oath that whoever came not up to the Lord at Mizpeh would surely be put to death.

The question of the chapter: how shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord not to give them our daughters? They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and the law says a sworn oath must be performed; that is why they could not simply turn around and give their daughters.

They searched which tribe came not up to Mizpeh, and behold, none had come from Jabeshgilead to the assembly. So under the great oath the congregation sent twelve thousand of the valiantest men to smite Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, destroying every male and every woman that had lain by man. Among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead they found four hundred young virgins that had not known man by lying with any male, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan. Verse 12 is the precept for what it means in scripture to know somebody: to lie with them, meaning to have sex with them.

The whole congregation sent to speak peaceably to the children of Benjamin at the rock Rimmon, and Benjamin came again. They gave them the wives saved alive of the women of Jabeshgilead, but they sufficed not; there were not enough for all the men that remained. The people repented them for Benjamin because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel, and the elders said there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel. Verse 18 restates why they could not just give their own daughters: the children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin. That is the same oath read in verse 7.

The solution: there was a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, so they commanded the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards, and when the daughters of Shiloh came out to dance in the dances, every man was to catch him a wife of the daughters of Shiloh and go to the land of Benjamin. When the fathers or brethren came to complain, the elders would answer, Be favourable unto them for our sakes; because the fathers did not give their daughters, they would not be guilty of breaking the oath. The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number of them that danced, then returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them.

The children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, to his family, and to his inheritance. In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes. We see that same thing today: most of our people are still in that state, doing what is right in their own eyes. There is nothing new under the sun. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

These are the statutes and judgments which ye shall observe to do in the land: the Lord gave the fathers a land other nations were living in, and Israel went to war with those nations to take it. The whole book of Deuteronomy is the Lord speaking unto his people Israel; he showed his statutes and his judgments to no other nation.

Utterly destroy all the places wherein the nations served their gods, upon the high mountains, upon the hills, and under every green tree. Even after being warned, Israel was still idolatrous: the children of Israel secretly built high places in all their cities, set up images and groves in every high hill and under every green tree, and burnt incense as did the heathen, the very thing the Lord said ye shall not do. Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel; that is how they became the oppressor, and the word says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.
Unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there shall ye seek: out of all the tribes he chose Jerusalem as the place for his name and the temple.

Ye are not as yet come to the rest and to the inheritance: the rest is when the Lord gives rest from all your enemies round about, so that ye dwell in safety. This is why the scripture is pulled out on the street, this is not our rest: Israel today dwells among its enemies and serves them for food, shelter, and clothing, as [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) declares. Arise ye and depart does not mean to leave physically; it means come up out of the ways of this place, because it is polluted. Israel waits for the time when the third part has repented, the hundred forty and four thousand are sealed, and Christ returns to take his people out of this place and set them back in their own land.

Whatsoever thy soul lusteth after is not license to eat anything: it stays within the guidelines of the clean foods, as of the roebuck and as of the hart, the beasts listed in chapter 14, for the law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing. The unclean and the clean that may eat thereof are unclean and clean persons, not unclean meats; Israel had servants then and will have servants again.

Take heed that thou be not snared by inquiring after the gods of the nations after they are destroyed, saying, how did these nations serve their gods, even so will I do likewise; Israel has a history of following what the other nations do. The snare fulfilled is written in the psalm: Israel did not destroy the nations, but was mingled among the heathen, learned their works, served their idols, and sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils, the very abomination the Lord warned of here. The wrath of the Lord was kindled insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance; that snare is why Israel is where it is now, scattered among the heathen and serving them.

Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king. Jeroboam, still in Egypt, heard of it and returned, and the congregation of Israel came to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the grievous yoke and heavy service his father had put on them. The heavy yoke was the labor of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the other nations, but they did have to put in that work. Rehoboam told them to depart three days and return, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer.

Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with. Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders. The young men told him to say his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions, which was disrespectful.

When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions. The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

When all Israel saw the king would not hearken, they said, What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel. So Israel departed and rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only over those in the cities of Judah did Rehoboam reign. Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day. When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself. But the word of the Most High came to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin not to fight against their brethren the children of Israel, for this thing was from the Most High; and they hearkened and returned home.

Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him. Jeroboam took counsel and made two calves of gold, telling Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem, and setting one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made a house of high places and priests of the lowest of the people, not of the sons of Levi. Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

verses.text: And there was a man of mount Ephraim, whose name was Micah.

And he said unto his mother, The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from thee, about which thou cursedst, and spakest of also in mine ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said, Blessed be thou of the Lord, my son.

And when he had restored the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, his mother said, I had wholly dedicated the silver unto the Lord from my hand for my son, to make a graven image and a molten image: now therefore I will restore it unto thee.

Yet he restored the money unto his mother; and his mother took two hundred shekels of silver, and gave them to the founder, who made thereof a graven image and a molten image: and they were in the house of Micah.
And the man Micah had an house of gods, and made an ephod, and teraphim, and consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest.
In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
And Micah said unto him, Dwell with me, and be unto me a father and a priest, and I will give thee ten shekels of silver by the year, and a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. So the Levite went in.
And the Levite was content to dwell with the man; and the young man was unto him as one of his sons.
And Micah consecrated the Levite; and the young man became his priest, and was in the house of Micah.
Then said Micah, Now know I that the Lord will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest.

Then answered the five men that went to spy out the country of Laish, and said unto their brethren, Do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do.
And they turned thitherward, and came to the house of the young man the Levite, even unto the house of Micah, and saluted him.
And the six hundred men appointed with their weapons of war, which were of the children of Dan, stood by the entering of the gate.

And the five men that went to spy out the land went up, and came in thither, and took the graven image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image: and the priest stood in the entering of the gate with the six hundred men that were appointed with weapons of war.
And these went into Micah’s house, and fetched the carved image, the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image. Then said the priest unto them, What do ye?

And they said unto him, Hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or that thou be a priest unto a tribe and a family in Israel?
And the priest’s heart was glad, and he took the ephod, and the teraphim, and the graven image, and went in the midst of the people.

And they took the things which Micah had made, and the priest which he had, and came unto Laish, unto a people that were at quiet and secure: and they smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire.
And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Zidon, and they had no business with any man; and it was in the valley that lieth by Beth–rehob. And they built a city, and dwelt therein.
And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born unto Israel: howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.
And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.
And they set them up Micah’s graven image, which he made, all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.
In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
Ye shall not do after all the things that we do here this day, every man whatsoever is right in his own eyes.
And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan.
And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.

cases.name: The men of Gibeah, and Benjamin
cases.charge: Sodomy, gang rape and murder of a stranger's concubine; a tribe that shielded the guilty
cases.summary: The men of Gibeah surrounded the house where a Levite lodged, demanding him; they were given his concubine and abused her all night until she died on the threshold. He cut her into twelve pieces and sent them through Israel. Benjamin refused to surrender the guilty, and Israel went to war.
cases.offense: The Levite passed by Jebus because he would not lodge in a city of strangers and chose Gibeah, a city of Benjamin. Yet no man there first received him, and an old man from Mount Ephraim brought the travellers into his house (Judges 19:10-21). The guest expected safety among brethren; the city's conduct betrayed that expectation. Men surrounded the house and demanded the male guest, as the men of Sodom had demanded Lot's visitors (Judges 19:22; Genesis 19:4-9). The woman was brought out to them, and they raped and abused her through the night. She fell at the door with her hands upon the threshold and gave no answer when her husband spoke (Judges 19:25-28). This was violence against her, not consent. Deuteronomy 22:25-26 places the guilt of forced intercourse upon the attacker and compares the assault to a man rising against his neighbour to slay him. The Levite sent the evidence throughout Israel, and the congregation assembled as one man. They demanded that Benjamin surrender the perpetrators so that evil could be put away (Judges 19:29-30; 20:1-13). Benjamin refused and gathered to fight its brethren (Judges 20:14). The tribe made itself the defence of the guilty. Loyalty to one's own becomes transgression when it shields the crime instead of submitting the offenders to judgment.
cases.judgment: Israel brought four hundred thousand swordsmen against Benjamin, yet lost twenty-two thousand men on the first day and eighteen thousand on the second (Judges 20:17-25). Numbers and indignation did not secure victory. Israel had enquired of the Lord, but the express promise of deliverance came after the whole congregation wept, fasted, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before him (Judges 20:26-28). They had to humble themselves as well as prosecute the wickedness among their brethren.

Yet no man there first received him, and an old man from Mount Ephraim brought the travellers into his house (Judges 19:10-21). Men surrounded the house and demanded the male guest, as the men of Sodom had demanded Lot's visitors (Judges 19:22; Genesis 19:4-9). The woman was brought out to them, and they raped and abused her through the night. She fell at the door with her hands upon the threshold and gave no answer when her husband spoke (Judges 19:25-28). This was violence against her, not consent. Deuteronomy 22:25-26 places the guilt of forced intercourse upon the attacker and compares the assault to a man rising against his neighbour to slay him.
