They demanded that Benjamin surrender the perpetrators so that evil could be put away (Judges 19:29-30; 20:1-13). Benjamin refused and gathered to fight its brethren (Judges 20:14). The tribe made itself the defence of the guilty. Loyalty to one's own becomes transgression when it shields the crime instead of submitting the offenders to judgment.

entries.commentary: Once more, there was no king in Israel, no leadership structure, still sheep without a shepherd. A certain Levite sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim took to him a concubine out of Bethlehemjudah; a concubine was a woman dealt with on the level of a servant. His concubine played the whore against him, laid with another man, then went away from him unto her father's house to Bethlehemjudah and was there four whole months.

Instead of letting her go, her husband arose and went after her to speak friendly unto her and to bring her again, with his servant and a couple of asses, and the damsel's father rejoiced to meet him. By the law, a woman who is put away and becomes another man's is defiled to her former husband, and taking her back defiles the land. The Most High does not permit it, but with no king in the land and no enforcement of the law, this is what men did.

The damsel's father retained him: eat, drink, lodge, three days, then a fourth, then a fifth. Like an old man who never has anybody to talk to, he kept finding a reason not to let the Levite go, and a one night plan stretched into five days. The father's words on the fifth day cut a popular doctrine. They tarried until afternoon, and he said, behold, the day draweth toward evening, and then, behold, the day groweth to an end. According to the Bible the day ends at evening; and if it ends at evening it begins at evening, so a day runs from evening to evening, including the sabbath. That buries the sunrise to sunrise doctrine, which has no works and no fruits to show it was ever right.

The man would not tarry that night; five days was enough and he had business to tend to. He rose up, departed, and came over against Jebus, which is Jerusalem, with two saddled asses and his concubine. Jerusalem is called Jebus here because the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of Jerusalem, still dwelt in it; this is before David rose up and took it from them. When Israel came out of the wilderness, the promised land was inhabited primarily by Canaanites, and the children of Judah could not drive the Jebusites out.

The sun went down upon them by Gibeah, which belongeth to Benjamin, and when they went in and sat down in a street of the city, no man took them into his house to lodge. The Benjamites were not so friendly. An old man from his work out of the field at even, a man of mount Ephraim sojourning in Gibeah, lifted up his eyes and questioned the wayfaring man: whither goest thou? and whence comest thou? The Levite explained he was passing toward the house of the LORD with straw, provender, bread, and wine of his own, lacking nothing, yet no man would receive him to house. The old man said, peace be with thee; howsoever let all thy wants lie upon me; only lodge not in the street. He knew the manner of the men of that city and what the streets of Gibeah held at night. He brought them into his house, and they washed their feet and did eat and drink.

As they were making their hearts merry, certain sons of Belial, meaning children of the devil, demon seed, beset the house round about and beat at the door in the middle of the night, saying to the master of the house, bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him. To know in this context is sexual intercourse; the men of Gibeah were howling for the man himself. This is a rerun of a very familiar story of old, the men of Sodom at Lot's door, and the scripture names exactly what vile thing they were after.

The men would not hearken, so the man brought his concubine forth unto them; and they knew her, and abused her all the night until the morning. They is plural: this was a gang rape, forced, nothing voluntary about it, done in the anger of men who could not get the man they wanted. When the day began to spring they let her go, and the woman came in the dawning of the day and fell down at the door of the man's house where her lord was, her hands upon the threshold. In the morning he said, up, and let us be going; but none answered. There was no more spirit left in her; she was dead. He laid her upon an ass and got him unto his place. What we witnessed is rape, and the scripture is plain that rape is a sin worthy of death; marriage is the only honorable bed. Men out here calling themselves Israelites and teaching otherwise give Israelites a bad name; we preach the laws of the Most High.

When he was come into his house he took a knife, laid hold on his concubine, and divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel, to make the twelve tribes aware of what was done in Gibeah. All that saw it said, there was no such deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider of it, take advice, and speak your minds. The nation had never seen a matter like this, and it called the whole congregation to counsel.

All the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the LORD in Mizpeh: four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword. Israel got ready for war behind one woman, one victim. There is no hatred of women in this truth; wicked women are rebuked, which is itself love, and here a crime against one sister moved the whole nation to arms.

The children of Benjamin heard that Israel was gone up to Mizpeh. The Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, testified: I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, and the men of Gibeah rose against me and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me; and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead. Forced is the Bible's word for rape. He said they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel. Nowhere in the Bible can rape be called lawful; it is lewdness and folly, and whether the victim lives or dies the matter is counted as murder. Be very mindful of sick, perverted camps that teach otherwise.

All the people arose as one man, saying, we will not any of us go to his tent, neither will we any of us turn into his house; none of us are going home until this is answered. They set an order for war, ten men of an hundred throughout all the tribes to fetch victual for the people, and all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man. Even wicked and without a king, Israel had some morals left; gang rape was intolerable.

The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, what wickedness is this that is done among you? Now deliver us the men, the children of Belial which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and put away evil from Israel; everything those men had going on was worthy of death. But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren; instead they gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah to go out to battle against the children of Israel, riding for their own no matter the crime.

Benjamin numbered twenty and six thousand men that drew sword out of the cities, beside the inhabitants of Gibeah, seven hundred chosen men. Among all this people were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded, every one able to sling stones at an hair breadth and not miss: slinging with the velocity of a firearm and dead accurate. Benjamin was about that action. The men of Israel beside Benjamin were four hundred thousand men of war that drew sword. Four hundred thousand against twenty and six thousand: you would think a landslide victory.

The children of Israel arose, went up to the house of God, and asked counsel of God: which of us shall go up first to the battle against the children of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first. Israel encamped against Gibeah and put themselves in array, and the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground of the Israelites that day twenty and two thousand men. Benjamin opened the battle by giving Judah the business.

The men of Israel encouraged themselves; we cannot go out like that to the men of Gibeah. They set their battle again in array in the same place, went up and wept before the LORD until even, and asked, shall I go up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the LORD said, go up against him. The second day Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground eighteen thousand more, all men that drew the sword. Fresh legs came in against them and Benjamin still had the endurance and stamina to whip them.

Then all the children of Israel and all the people went up unto the house of God, wept, sat there before the LORD, fasted that day until even, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD. This time the whole nation humbled itself. The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it. They asked, shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand: a direct promise of victory on the morrow.

Now Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah. No more going head up against lefthanded slingers you cannot beat straight on; now there was a strategy, an ambush. Part of Israel put themselves in array as at other times, and Benjamin was drawn away from the city, beginning to smite and kill about thirty men and saying, they are smitten down before us as at the first. Little did they know they were falling into the plan; Israel fled on purpose and drew them from the city onto the highways. The liers in wait came forth out of their places, even out of the meadows of Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel: the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men. The victory belonged to the Most High, as he had promised.

There was an appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city. That was the purpose of drawing the Benjamites out: while Benjamin smote about thirty men and thought they were winning as in the first battles, the liers in wait hasted, rushed upon Gibeah, smote all the city with the edge of the sword, and set the sign. When the flame began to arise out of the city with a pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them, and behold, the flame of the city ascended up to heaven; and the men of Benjamin were amazed, for they saw that evil was come upon them. In that moment they knew it was over. They turned their backs before the men of Israel unto the way of the wilderness, toward the rock of Rimmon, but the battle overtook them: eighteen thousand men of valour fell, five thousand were gleaned in the highways, and two thousand slain at Gidom, twenty and five thousand in all, including all those mighty lefthanded men of valour.

Six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon and abode there four months; only that remnant kept the tribe from being utterly destroyed. The men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin and smote them with the edge of the sword, men of every city, and beast, and all that came to hand, and set on fire all the cities they came to. Benjamin was judged big time; the Most High pushed the reset button on the tribe for the sodomite and rape activity that came out of Gibeah. Chapter 21 shows the drastic measures that had to be taken so Benjamin could continue producing as a tribe. That judgment is why Saul, in the days of the first king, calls himself a Benjamite of the smallest of the tribes of Israel; this war is what minimized the tribe. There have been mighty and righteous Benjamites since, Paul chief among them, but it is written, and we learn the history as it is written.

The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh that not one of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife. This follows the previous chapter, where the tribes went to war against Benjamin. The people came to the house of God and sat there till evening before God, lifted up their voices and wept sore, asking why it had come to pass that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel. The next day they rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. The children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, for there was one tribe cut off from Israel that day. They had also made a great oath that whoever came not up to the Lord at Mizpeh would surely be put to death.

The question of the chapter: how shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord not to give them our daughters? They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and the law says a sworn oath must be performed; that is why they could not simply turn around and give their daughters.

They searched which tribe came not up to Mizpeh, and behold, none had come from Jabeshgilead to the assembly. So under the great oath the congregation sent twelve thousand of the valiantest men to smite Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, destroying every male and every woman that had lain by man. Among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead they found four hundred young virgins that had not known man by lying with any male, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan. Verse 12 is the precept for what it means in scripture to know somebody: to lie with them, meaning to have sex with them.

The whole congregation sent to speak peaceably to the children of Benjamin at the rock Rimmon, and Benjamin came again. They gave them the wives saved alive of the women of Jabeshgilead, but they sufficed not; there were not enough for all the men that remained. The people repented them for Benjamin because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel, and the elders said there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel. Verse 18 restates why they could not just give their own daughters: the children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin. That is the same oath read in verse 7.

The solution: there was a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, so they commanded the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards, and when the daughters of Shiloh came out to dance in the dances, every man was to catch him a wife of the daughters of Shiloh and go to the land of Benjamin. When the fathers or brethren came to complain, the elders would answer, Be favourable unto them for our sakes; because the fathers did not give their daughters, they would not be guilty of breaking the oath. The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number of them that danced, then returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them.

The children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, to his family, and to his inheritance. In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes. We see that same thing today: most of our people are still in that state, doing what is right in their own eyes. There is nothing new under the sun. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)
Lot sat in the gate and pressed the two angels into his house, because he knew the men of Sodom. He made them a feast, and they did eat; angels have bodies and functions like men.

The men of Sodom, old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed the house and demanded the men, that we may know them. To know in scripture is to lie with: Rebekah was a virgin, neither had any man known her. The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness.

Lot went out and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. This is Genesis, way before [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18); sodomy was already wickedness and already unlawful before the law was written at Sinai. They pressed on Lot to break the door, and the angels smote them with blindness, small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

Lot's sons in law took him as one that mocked, and they perished. When the warning comes, treating it as a joke is death. While Lot lingered, the angels laid hold on his hand, the Lord being merciful to him. Then the instruction: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee; escape to the mountain.

The angel told Lot, Haste thee, for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. The destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, the same way the angels in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7) hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed. When Lot entered Zoar, the Lord rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. Those cities are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire; what was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands. Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.

Lot's wife looked back, against the instruction, and became a pillar of salt: a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.

Lot's daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and no man was left on the earth to give them seed, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him; he perceived not when they lay down nor when they arose. Do not take any wayward idea from this: uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now. The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.

verses.text: Now as they were making their hearts merry, behold, the men of the city, certain sons of Belial, beset the house round about, and beat at the door, and spake to the master of the house, the old man, saying, Bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him.
And the man, the master of the house, went out unto them, and said unto them, Nay, my brethren, nay, I pray you, do not so wickedly; seeing that this man is come into mine house, do not this folly.
Behold, here is my daughter a maiden, and his concubine; them I will bring out now, and humble ye them, and do with them what seemeth good unto you: but unto this man do not so vile a thing.

But the men would not hearken to him: so the man took his concubine, and brought her forth unto them; and they knew her, and abused her all the night until the morning: and when the day began to spring, they let her go.
Then came the woman in the dawning of the day, and fell down at the door of the man’s house where her lord was, till it was light.

And her lord rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way: and, behold, the woman his concubine was fallen down at the door of the house, and her hands were upon the threshold.
And he said unto her, Up, and let us be going. But none answered. Then the man took her up upon an ass, and the man rose up, and gat him unto his place.
And when he was come into his house, he took a knife, and laid hold on his concubine, and divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel.

And it was so, that all that saw it said, There was no such deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider of it, take advice, and speak your minds.
And the Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, answered and said, I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge.
And the men of Gibeah rose against me, and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me: and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead.
And I took my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the country of the inheritance of Israel: for they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel.
Behold, ye are all children of Israel; give here your advice and counsel.
And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, What wickedness is this that is done among you?

Now therefore deliver us the men, the children of Belial, which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel. But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel:
And the Lord smote Benjamin before Israel: and the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men: all these drew the sword.
So that all which fell that day of Benjamin were twenty and five thousand men that drew the sword; all these were men of valour.
But six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon, and abode in the rock Rimmon four months.

And the men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword, as well the men of every city, as the beast, and all that came to hand: also they set on fire all the cities that they came to.
And the people came to the house of God, and abode there till even before God, and lifted up their voices, and wept sore;
And said, O Lord God of Israel, why is this come to pass in Israel, that there should be to day one tribe lacking in Israel?
They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah: therefore he will remember their iniquity, he will visit their sins.
O Israel, thou hast sinned from the days of Gibeah: there they stood: the battle in Gibeah against the children of iniquity did not overtake them.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.

cases.name: Ruth and Boaz
cases.charge: Ruth: cleaving to Naomi and to Naomi's God. Boaz: the law of gleaning, and the law of the kinsman, done to the letter
cases.summary: A Moabite widow left her people for a mother in law with nothing, and said, thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God. A man of Bethlehem let her glean, ordered handfuls dropped on purpose, and then went to the gate and settled the redemption and marriage before ten elders. Their son was Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David.
cases.offense: Ruth: Intreat me not to leave thee; whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God. Boaz to Ruth: It hath fully been shewed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death of thine husband. Boaz to his reapers: Let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her. At the gate: The day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. And the near kinsman drew off his shoe.
cases.judgment: The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. The Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel. So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son. Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel. They called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

entries.commentary: It came to pass in the days when the judges ruled: the scripture is putting Ruth in a time frame. Ruth takes place in the same time as the book of Judges. There was a famine in the land, and Elimelech of Bethlehemjudah went to sojourn in the country of Moab with his wife Naomi and his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehemjudah.

Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. The sons took them wives of the women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and after they dwelt there about ten years Mahlon and Chilion died also, leaving Naomi without her husband and without her sons. Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab.

Naomi heard in the country of Moab that the Lord had visited his people and given them bread, so she arose with her daughters in law to return unto the land of Judah, and told them, Go, return each to her mother's house; the Lord deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead and with me. The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

The daughters in law said, Surely we will return with thee unto thy people; but Naomi answered, Are there yet any more sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands? Even if she had a husband that night and bore sons, would they tarry until the boys were grown? They were grown women; they were not going to wait. Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. She would not put them under an oath to stay and wait for sons that would likely never come.

They lifted up their voice and wept again; Orpah kissed her mother in law and went back, but Ruth clave unto her. Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served.

Ruth was determined: Intreat me not to leave thee; whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God; where thou diest, will I die. She was saying, do not put me away; Orpah may have gone back, but I am going to cleave unto you. Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same.

When Naomi saw that Ruth was stedfastly minded to go with her, she left speaking unto her, and the two went until they came to Bethlehem, where all the city was moved about them and said, Is this Naomi? She answered, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the Lord hath brought me home again empty. So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter in law with her, and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

Naomi had a kinsman of her husband, a mighty man of wealth of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz. Ruth asked Naomi, Let me now go to the field and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace; and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.

Boaz came from Bethlehem and greeted his reapers, The Lord be with you; and they answered him, The Lord bless thee. When he asked whose damsel this was, the servant set over the reapers answered, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi, and reported how she had asked to glean and had continued from the morning with only a little rest in the house. Boaz told Ruth to glean in no other field but to abide fast by his maidens; he had charged the young men not to touch her, and when she was athirst she could drink of the vessels the young men had drawn.
Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger.

Boaz answered that it had fully been shewed him all she had done for her mother in law since the death of her husband, how she left her father, her mother, and the land of her nativity, and came unto a people she knew not before. The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. Ruth answered, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord, for thou hast comforted me, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.

At mealtime Boaz told her to come and eat of the bread and dip her morsel in the vinegar; he reached her parched corn, and she did eat and was sufficed and left. When she rose to glean, Boaz commanded his young men to let her glean even among the sheaves without reproach, and to let fall handfuls of purpose for her. She gleaned until evening and beat out about an ephah of barley.

Ruth brought what she had gleaned into the city, gave Naomi what she had reserved, and told her, The man's name with whom I wrought to day is Boaz. Naomi blessed him of the Lord, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead, and said, The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen. Naomi told her it was good to go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field; so Ruth kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest, and dwelt with her mother in law.

Naomi said, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee? This is the same rest spoken of in chapter 1, rest in the house of a husband; and Boaz of their kindred was winnowing barley that night in the threshingfloor. Her instructions: wash thyself, anoint thee, put thy raiment upon thee, get thee down to the floor, and make not thyself known unto the man until he has done eating and drinking; mark where he lies, uncover his feet, and lay thee down, and he will tell thee what thou shalt do. Ruth answered, All that thou sayest unto me I will do.

Ruth did according to all her mother in law bade her. When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was merry, he lay down at the end of the heap of corn, and she came softly, uncovered his feet, and laid her down. At midnight the man was afraid, turned himself, and behold, a woman lay at his feet. She answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman. On the skirt: Zondervan's Compact Bible Dictionary, page 137, explains that the basic garments of the men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle, and the cloak, with the headdress and the shoes or sandals; the word skirt in the Bible usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, and carries meanings such as extremity, as in [Ruth 3:9](/bible/ruth/3#v9). Asking Boaz to spread his skirt over her was asking the near kinsman to take her under his covering.

Boaz blessed her: thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich. Ruth could have gone after other men, but even as a Moabitess she was following the customs of Israel, trying to find someone to raise up seed for her dead lord and keep his name in the earth; she was trying to do the right thing and keep the laws of Israel.

Fear not, my daughter; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman. Boaz was honest: it is true that I am thy near kinsman, howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I. Tarry this night, and in the morning, if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; but if not, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the Lord liveth.

She lay at his feet until the morning and rose up before one could know another; that is the same precept of knowing read in [Judges 21](/bible/judges/21), meaning in this case to lie down and have sex with each other. That is also why Boaz said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor. Boaz measured six measures of barley into her vail and she went into the city; she told Naomi, These six measures of barley gave he me; for he said to me, Go not empty unto thy mother in law. Naomi answered, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest until he have finished the thing this day.

Boaz went up to the gate, called the kinsman of whom he had spoken to turn aside and sit down, and took ten men of the elders of the city to sit with them. What he is doing is calling witnesses. He is about to make a purchase, so he calls witnesses, that it can be put in the books for the future that this is what was done.

Boaz laid the matter before the kinsman: Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land which was our brother Elimelech's. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it; but if not, tell me, for there is none to redeem it beside thee, and I am after thee. And the kinsman said, I will redeem it. What is this going back to? The law of the land, the law of inheritance when it comes to land, read back in the book of Numbers. The husband died and the two sons died, and the only person left is the wife with the land; so she instinctively went to Boaz, and Boaz is now conducting the laws of the land of who it should be passed down to, going down the list of inheritance.

What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive. What law is that going back to? That law goes back to [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25), the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at [Ruth 1:6-9](/bible/ruth/1#v6) in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.

The kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself, for I cannot redeem it. In other words, I already have kids in the way; I cannot do it, I am not doing it.

Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing: for to confirm all things, a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour, and this was a testimony in Israel. So the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thee, and he drew off his shoe. You can read about that shoe back in [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25).

Boaz said unto the elders and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi; moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place. What law is Boaz exercising in this? Love thy neighbour as thyself. That is what Boaz was putting into place and applying, and that is why he is mentioned in the scriptures.

All the people that were in the gate and the elders said, We are witnesses. They blessed the marriage: the Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel; and let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman. In that blessing they are prophesying about David to come.

So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son. The women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel; he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.

Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it; and the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David. Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive in Israel, and although she was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel.

Now these are the generations of Pharez: Pharez is of Judah, so this is the lineage of Judah, how they came about right down to the king. Pharez begat Hezron, and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon, and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David. We read that lineage in Matthew chapter 1: how David came about, how Solomon came about, ultimately down to Christ.

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.

If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God. Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day.

verses.text: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:
Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried: the Lord do so to me, and more also, if ought but death part thee and me.
Then said Boaz unto Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, neither go from hence, but abide here fast by my maidens:

Let thine eyes be on the field that they do reap, and go thou after them: have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch thee? and when thou art athirst, go unto the vessels, and drink of that which the young men have drawn.
Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said unto him, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger?

And Boaz answered and said unto her, It hath fully been shewed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death of thine husband: and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and art come unto a people which thou knewest not heretofore.
The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
And when she was risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her not:
And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not.
And he said, Blessed be thou of the Lord, my daughter: for thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich.
And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.
And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I.

Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the Lord liveth: lie down until the morning.

Then went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there: and, behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz spake came by; unto whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.
And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye down here. And they sat down.
And he said unto the kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s:

And I thought to advertise thee, saying, Buy it before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it: but if thou wilt not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know: for there is none to redeem it beside thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem it.
Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.
And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I cannot redeem it.

Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour: and this was a testimony in Israel.
Therefore the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thee. So he drew off his shoe.
And Boaz said unto the elders, and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, of the hand of Naomi.

Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.

And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. The Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel: and do thou worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Beth–lehem:
And let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman.
So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.
And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel.
And he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.
And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it.
And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.
And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger: I am the Lord your God.

If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.
And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.
And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;
And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias;

cases.name: Hannah
cases.charge: Praying in bitterness of soul, vowing a son to the Lord, and giving him when she had him
cases.summary: Barren, provoked yearly by her rival, mistaken for a drunkard by the high priest, she poured out her soul before the Lord and vowed that if he gave her a son she would give him back for all his days. He did, and she did: she brought Samuel to Shiloh as soon as he was weaned. The Lord gave her five more.
cases.offense: Hannah's barrenness was made bitter by repeated provocation. Year by year, when the household went up to worship, her adversary vexed her until she wept and would not eat (1 Samuel 1:4-7). She brought that sorrow before the Lord and vowed that, if he gave her a son, she would give him to the Lord all his days, with no razor upon his head (1 Samuel 1:9-11). The words joined her petition to the separation described in Numbers 6:5. Eli saw her moving lips without hearing her voice and thought her drunk. She answered that she had poured out her soul before the Lord, and he sent her away in peace. She then ate, and her countenance was no more sad (1 Samuel 1:12-18). Her faith was shown before the birth, when she went from prayer able to receive food again. Being misunderstood by the priest did not turn her from the one to whom she had prayed. First John 5:14-15 joins confidence in prayer to asking according to the Lord's will; First John 3:22 joins receiving to keeping his commandments and doing what pleases him. Hannah's answer came in the Lord's time. Prayer did not put the timing of the gift under her control. She entrusted the petition to him and afterward named her son in remembrance of what she had asked (1 Samuel 1:19-20). When Samuel was weaned, she brought him to Shiloh with the offerings and presented him to Eli. The child she had wanted was the child she now gave for lifelong service (1 Samuel 1:24-28). Ecclesiastes 5:4-6 commands the payment of a vow instead of dismissing it as an error. Hannah did not treat answered prayer as the end of her obligation. She performed the promise when its fulfilment required parting with the son she loved.
cases.judgment: Samuel ministered before the Lord, and Hannah brought him a little coat each year. Her dedication did not become forgetfulness; she continued to supply the care she could give (1 Samuel 2:18-19). Eli blessed the household, and the Lord visited her with three sons and two daughters (1 Samuel 2:20-21). The one son was not withheld, and her house received five more. Her song declares that the Lord is a God of knowledge and that actions are weighed by him (1 Samuel 2:3). Her own conduct had joined prayer, promise, and performance. Christ's question—why call him Lord and not do what he says—reaches the same distinction between profession and obedience (Luke 6:46). The words spoken before God are to be followed by the life promised to him. The song passes from her household to the Lord's rule over strength, riches, life, and death. He brings low and lifts up; by strength no man prevails; he gives strength to his king and exalts his anointed (1 Samuel 2:4-10). Hannah's joy therefore ends in the Lord's salvation, not her own victory over the woman who provoked her. The gift was his, the service was his, and the glory remained his.
