That shows us we have to have a level of discipline over our eyes; with these devices today it is very easy to take a two second look at what you know you should not be looking at. Guard your eyes. The people lamented and said, Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? So they sent messengers to Kirjath-jearim to come fetch the ark up. The Bible acknowledges the Most High God as the king of terrors: he was killing thousands at a time, and his judgments are terrifying.

The men of Kirjath-jearim fetched up the ark of the Lord into the house of Abinadab in the hill, and sanctified Eleazar his son to keep it. While the ark abode in Kirjath-jearim the time was long, twenty years, and all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord.

Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel: If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines. Go back to how we lost the battle even with the ark of God among us: we had strange gods among us. Deliverance is not just having the ark, it is applying the commandments that are in the ark, thou shalt have no other gods before me. Who is Ashtoreth? Astaroth in demonology is a chief figure of hell, named after the Near Eastern goddess Astarte, and Astarte is the Hellenized form of Ashtoreth, a form of Ishtar, the goddess called the queen of heaven, associated with love, beauty, sex, and war. Samuel was exhorting the people to depart from these fake gods and goddesses of the nations, and to this day there are Israelites that have not put away Ashtoreth from among them. Easter is at its roots the celebration of Ishtar, the goddess of fertility and sex. When Constantine set out to merge paganism with the faith of the apostles to bring everything under one empire, pagan rituals like Easter and Saturnalia were dressed up as honoring Christ, and that was the birth of Roman Catholicism. Nothing about it mathematically adds up to Christ rising, the apostles never celebrated it or taught it, and a bunny laying eggs has nothing to do with your Lord and Saviour; it is not of Christ. Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only. That is repentance.

Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the Lord. They gathered, drew water and poured it out before the Lord, fasted that day, and said, We have sinned against the Lord; and Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpeh. When the lords of the Philistines heard Israel was gathered at Mizpeh, they came up against Israel again, and Israel was afraid. But this time, instead of running for the ark, the children of Israel charged Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines. They knew the prayer of a righteous man reaches the ears of the Most High.

Samuel took a sucking lamb and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord, and Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him. As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle, but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them, and they were smitten before Israel. That was no regular thunder; it was the Lord entering the battle himself. They had repented, put away the false gods, and the prayer of the righteous man reached his ears, so now the Philistines had to deal with the Most High. The Philistines were so terrified they put up no fight; the men of Israel went out of Mizpeh and pursued them, smiting them until they came under Beth-car. Then Samuel took a stone, set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the Lord helped us. Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul, and by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet. Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High, just as Abraham's faith was tried again and again and he remained faithful.

So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more into the coast of Israel: and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel. As long as Samuel lived, the Lord kept them down. The cities the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored, from Ekron even unto Gath, and Israel delivered the coasts out of the hands of the Philistines; and there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life, and went from year to year in circuit to Bethel, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel in all those places; and his return was to Ramah, for there was his house, and there he built an altar unto the Lord. Ramah was his headquarters. That yearly circuit is leadership making its rounds, establishing the people and coming back to check on them, the same example Paul followed with the churches. These chapters close with the ark lost and regained, and Samuel rising up for the nation: prayer is a superpower, and that is how our mighty forefathers rolled, from Moses to Samuel to Judas Maccabeus all the way to Christ. Keep the commandments and send up that prayer, and the Most High will come down in thunder against your enemies.

The sons of Kohath were numbered from thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, all that enter into the host to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation. You took on that responsibility at thirty years old. Fifty was basically the age of retirement from the service; the law elsewhere shows the elder then sat down to be a judge amongst his brethren.

This is the service of the sons of Kohath about the most holy things. When the camp set forward, Aaron and his sons took down the covering vail and covered the ark of the testimony with it, with the covering of badgers' skins and a cloth wholly of blue. The design of the ark and the tabernacle, the pure gold dishes, spoons, and vessels, was laid out back in [Exodus 35](/bible/exodus/35) and 36; review it there.

The table of shewbread, the candlestick, the golden altar, and all the instruments of ministry were each wrapped in cloths of blue, scarlet, or purple and covered with badgers' skins before they were put on the staves and bars. Badger skin is something we would consider unclean today, yet the Lord had his holy things covered in it. Under the law of sacrifice, defilement came by touching unclean things to eat them; touching them to make something for the tabernacle still left you unclean until sundown, unable to sacrifice, but the skins themselves served the sanctuary.

After Aaron and his sons made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath came to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. The Most High is very particular about the most holy things. The Lord referred to all the tribes together as the camp. If you are not in a camp you are out of order; people avoid camps because a camp carries a certain level of order and subjection, and they want to do their own thing, which is to sit in the midst of sin. All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

To the office of Eleazar pertained the oil for the light, the sweet incense, the daily meat offering, the anointing oil, and the oversight of all the tabernacle. The burning of the sweet incense stayed in that priestly line: Zacharias, of the course of Abia, descended from the line of the Kohathites, and his lot was to burn incense in the temple of the Lord. [Luke 1:6](/bible/luke/1#v6) is the New Testament precept for what it means to be righteous: walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. Highlight that and commit it to memory. The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

The Most High commanded that the families of the Kohathites not be cut off: Aaron and his sons appointed every one to his service and to his burden, but they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die. It was a heavy responsibility; your life was on the line and you could not be out of order. One slip, one curious peek at the shiny gold before it was covered, and God put you to death on the spot. You had to be serious about your job and follow all instructions. That is the God we are dealing with; that is why Christ came, to give us mercy and grace from that thing.

The sons of Gershon were numbered from thirty to fifty years old for their service: bearing the curtains of the tabernacle, the coverings of badgers' skins, the hangings of the court and the doors, the cords, and all the instruments of their service. Their charge was under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. Ithamar had to make sure the priests had covered all the most holy things before the Gershonites came in to bear them; he was responsible for the lives of all the Gershonites that served, and he had to be in order.

The sons of Merari were numbered from thirty to fifty years old, charged with the boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, and cords of the tabernacle and the court, reckoned by name, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron. Only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to oversee, because Nadab and Abihu were killed by the Lord for offering strange fire; there were only two sons of Aaron remaining.

The numbered for service were 2,750 Kohathites, 2,630 Gershonites, and 3,200 Merarites; the total of those from thirty to fifty years old that entered the service of the tabernacle was 8,580, eight thousand and five hundred and fourscore. The Lord constantly repeats himself through these chapters to make sure you stay in order and do not go out of order, because going out of order cost your life. That is why you read the same thing in the Bible over and over again.

cases.name: Samuel
cases.charge: Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth; and an accounting no man could contradict: whose ox have I taken?
cases.summary: Dedicated to the Lord and brought to Shiloh as a child, Samuel received a word of judgment against Eli's house and delivered it without concealment. He judged Israel throughout his life, anointed Saul and David, and stood before the people to give an account of his conduct. They testified that he had neither oppressed them nor taken anything from them.
cases.offense: Samuel's service began before he understood the voice that called him. He ministered before Eli, but the word of the Lord had not yet been revealed to him. When Eli perceived who was calling, he taught Samuel to answer as a servant ready to hear (1 Samuel 3:1-10). Growing up beside holy things was preparation for service; receiving the word required his own response. The first message placed him under a difficult obligation. The Lord pronounced judgment upon the house that had raised him because Eli knew his sons' iniquity and did not restrain them. Samuel feared to tell the vision, yet told Eli everything and hid nothing (1 Samuel 3:11-18). Affection for the hearer could not become permission to alter the judgment. Faithful teaching begins with being faithful to what was given to teach. When Israel demanded a king, Samuel submitted his own administration to examination. Before the Lord and the new king, he asked whose property he had taken, whom he had defrauded or oppressed, and whose bribe had blinded his eyes. The people testified that he had taken nothing (1 Samuel 12:1-5). Exodus 23:8 forbids the gift that blinds judgment. Samuel's authority was supported by an account the people themselves could verify. He then rebuked their demand without abandoning them. He rehearsed the Lord's deliverances, warned both people and king to obey, and declared that he would sin against the Lord if he ceased praying for them (1 Samuel 12:6-25). Correction and intercession belonged together. Their refusal of his counsel did not release him from teaching the good and right way.
cases.judgment: The Lord was with Samuel and let none of his words fall to the ground. Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew him to be an established prophet (1 Samuel 3:19-21). His standing came through the fulfilment of the Lord's word, not through a title taken to himself. At Mizpeh the Lord heard his prayer and thundered against the Philistines; he continued his circuit of judgment through Bethel, Gilgal, Mizpeh, and Ramah (1 Samuel 7:9-17). He anointed Saul, mourned Saul's rejection, and obeyed the command to anoint David (1 Samuel 10:1; 15:35; 16:1-13). The work continued even when its history grieved him. All Israel lamented him at his death (1 Samuel 25:1). Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 46:13-17 remembers his faithfulness in judging by the law and the prayer answered from heaven. His ministry joined an upright hand, an unaltered word, and continuing care for the nation.
offenseFull: Samuel's service began before he understood the voice that called him. He ministered before Eli, but the word of the Lord had not yet been revealed to him. When Eli perceived who was calling, he taught Samuel to answer as a servant ready to hear (1 Samuel 3:1-10). Growing up beside holy things was preparation for service; receiving the word required his own response.

The first message placed him under a difficult obligation. The Lord pronounced judgment upon the house that had raised him because Eli knew his sons' iniquity and did not restrain them. Samuel feared to tell the vision, yet told Eli everything and hid nothing (1 Samuel 3:11-18). Affection for the hearer could not become permission to alter the judgment. Faithful teaching begins with being faithful to what was given to teach.

When Israel demanded a king, Samuel submitted his own administration to examination. Before the Lord and the new king, he asked whose property he had taken, whom he had defrauded or oppressed, and whose bribe had blinded his eyes. The people testified that he had taken nothing (1 Samuel 12:1-5). Exodus 23:8 forbids the gift that blinds judgment. Samuel's authority was supported by an account the people themselves could verify.

He then rebuked their demand without abandoning them. He rehearsed the Lord's deliverances, warned both people and king to obey, and declared that he would sin against the Lord if he ceased praying for them (1 Samuel 12:6-25). Correction and intercession belonged together. Their refusal of his counsel did not release him from teaching the good and right way.
judgmentFull: The Lord was with Samuel and let none of his words fall to the ground. Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew him to be an established prophet (1 Samuel 3:19-21). His standing came through the fulfilment of the Lord's word, not through a title taken to himself. At Mizpeh the Lord heard his prayer and thundered against the Philistines; he continued his circuit of judgment through Bethel, Gilgal, Mizpeh, and Ramah (1 Samuel 7:9-17).

He anointed Saul, mourned Saul's rejection, and obeyed the command to anoint David (1 Samuel 10:1; 15:35; 16:1-13). The work continued even when its history grieved him. All Israel lamented him at his death (1 Samuel 25:1). Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 46:13-17 remembers his faithfulness in judging by the law and the prayer answered from heaven. His ministry joined an upright hand, an unaltered word, and continuing care for the nation.

verses.text: And the Lord called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child.
Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle.
In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end.
For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not.
And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever.

entries.commentary: The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel.

Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

The Lord called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli; and Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The Lord called yet again, and again Samuel went to Eli. Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him. Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel? Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

The Lord called Samuel again the third time, and Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child; therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. The Lord is merciful with us even in these days, in this wickedness: he calls out to us numerous times until we wake up. We do not know who is chosen, so we never know when we are going to wake up; it might be the first time, the second time, or the third time you hear the voice of the Lord calling. Some heard the call the first time because the Most High ordained them to be built up as leaders, to get the spirits of the world off of them so they could be a righteous example and a fit guide for you; you came in at the third call, after they were prepared. Your job is not to try to supersede those that came in before you, but to follow them; God set it up that way for a reason.

And the Lord came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. The Lord did not just call from the heavens: the Lord came down and stood by Samuel and called out to him. That is cold-blooded. Samuel could not see him, but he heard him; that is what happens in the spirit to all of us. Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end. What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not. Therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments; his anger burns unto the lowest hell. Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. But Eli called him and said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee. Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. Eli said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli; that is of the Lord, and we will not know.

Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass. All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord. That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

cases.name: Joel and Abiah, the sons of Samuel
cases.charge: Turning aside after lucre, taking bribes, and perverting judgment in the seat of the judge
cases.summary: Samuel made his sons judges over Israel, and they walked not in his ways. They took bribes and perverted judgment, and the elders of Israel used it as the reason to ask for a king. The sentence recorded falls on the nation that asked, not on the two men who gave them the excuse.
cases.offense: Samuel appointed Joel and Abiah as judges in Beersheba, but they did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after gain, received bribes, and perverted judgment (1 Samuel 8:1-3). Their father's upright administration did not pass to them merely because his office did. The contrast was public: the people could testify that Samuel had taken nothing, while the sons made the seat of judgment serve their own increase (1 Samuel 12:3-5). The law names the corruption precisely. Judges were to judge with just judgment, without respecting persons or taking a gift that blinded the wise and perverted righteous words (Deuteronomy 16:18-20). Exodus 23:8 gives the same warning. A bribe does more than enrich an official. It bends what he is entrusted to see and say, placing those who seek justice at the mercy of those who can buy an answer. The elders brought the sons' conduct before Samuel when they asked for a king (1 Samuel 8:4-5). Corruption in an office that should protect the people gave force to their complaint. A father's reputation could not excuse his sons, and the people's knowledge of their wrongdoing could not be dismissed as a rejection of order. The judges themselves had violated the order established by the Lord.
cases.judgment: The recorded consequence reaches the nation: the elders used the sons' departure as their reason to demand a king like the nations. The Lord identified that demand as a rejection of his reign and instructed Samuel to warn them what the king would take (1 Samuel 8:6-18). Their grievance against corrupt judges was real; the remedy they insisted upon brought obligations and burdens of its own. No personal penalty upon Joel or Abiah is recorded in this chapter. Their offense remains named without an account of their later punishment. Ecclesiastes 5:8 warns the observer of perverted judgment that one higher than the official regards the matter. Silence about the sons' end does not turn their bribery into righteousness. Their place in the history is the damage caused when inherited authority is exercised without the character required to govern.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel.
Now the name of his firstborn was Joel; and the name of his second, Abiah: they were judges in Beer–sheba.
And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.
Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together, and came to Samuel unto Ramah,
And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.
Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.
Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift: for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous.
That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.

Behold, here I am: witness against me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man’s hand.
Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord.

entries.commentary: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel: Joel the firstborn and Abiah his second, judges in Beersheba. But his sons walked not in his ways; they turned aside after lucre, took bribes, and perverted judgment.

All the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel unto Ramah: thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways; now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a king like the other nations have. Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

The thing displeased Samuel when they said, Give us a king to judge us, and Samuel prayed unto the Lord. The Lord said, Hearken unto the voice of the people, for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them; according to all the works they have done since the day I brought them up out of Egypt, forsaking me and serving other gods, so do they also unto thee. Just as they rejected the Most High, they were rejecting Samuel and his counsel. Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

Samuel told all the words of the Lord unto the people that asked of him a king: this will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you. He will take your sons for his chariots and to be his horsemen; he will appoint him captains over thousands and captains over fifties, and set them to ear his ground, to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war. He will take your daughters to be confectionaries, cooks, and bakers; your fields, your vineyards, and your oliveyards, even the best of them, and give them to his servants; the tenth of your seed and of your vineyards for his officers; your menservants, your maidservants, your goodliest young men, and your asses to his work; the tenth of your sheep: and ye shall be his servants. And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you, and the Lord will not hear you in that day. The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay, but we will have a king over us, that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles. Samuel heard all the words of the people and rehearsed them in the ears of the Lord, and the Lord said, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king; and Samuel sent every man unto his city.

Observe the month of Abib and keep the passover unto the Most High, for in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night. Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, even the bread of affliction, because thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste, that thou mayest remember the day all the days of thy life. Nothing of the flesh sacrificed the first day at even, the lamb, may remain all night until the morning. The passover may not be sacrificed within any of thy gates, but only at the place which the Lord thy God shall choose to place his name there, at even, at the going down of the sun. Six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a solemn assembly and no work: the first day of the passover is a sabbath, and the seventh day of the passover is a sabbath.

Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee: begin to number the seven weeks from such time as thou beginnest to put the sickle to the corn, and keep the feast of weeks unto the Most High with a tribute of a freewill offering according as the Lord thy God hath blessed thee. Another name for the feast of weeks is the feast of firstfruits: you count seven weeks and then a day, fifty days, which is Pentecost. Rejoice before the Most High, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow; and remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt.

Thou shalt observe the feast of tabernacles seven days, after that thou hast gathered in thy corn and thy wine. Rejoice in thy feast, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates. Seven days shalt thou keep a solemn feast in the place which the Lord shall choose, because the Most High shall bless thee in all thine increase and in all the works of thine hands; therefore thou shalt surely rejoice.

Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Most High in the place which he shall choose: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. They shall not appear before the Lord empty, meaning they have to come with their sacrifices: every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee.

Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, throughout thy tribes, and they shall judge the people with just judgment. There is nothing new under the sun: when you see judges and officers among us today, know that we are following the things that are written within this book. Thou shalt not wrest judgment, thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift, for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise and pervert the words of the righteous. That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live and inherit the land.

Thou shalt not plant thee a grove of any trees near unto the altar of the Lord thy God; yet these pastors set up Christmas trees inside the church, directly against this law. Neither shalt thou set thee up any image, which the Lord thy God hateth.

Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean. [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.

At the end of chapter 11 Israel crowned Saul at Gilgal. Back in chapter 8 the people had pressured Samuel because they wanted to be like the nations round about them, and the Most High led him to choose Saul the son of Kish. This is the aftermath speech. Samuel is putting it on record: I hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me and made a king over you; whatever happens from here came from what you asked for.

Samuel establishes his blamelessness before he reasons with them. He walked before Israel from his childhood unto this day; whose ox or ass has he taken, whom has he defrauded or oppressed, from whose hand has he taken any bribe? Speak up now and he will restore it. The people answer that he has not defrauded nor oppressed them nor taken anything from any man's hand, and the Lord and his anointed are witness that day. Samuel was never a bad guy to the nation of Israel, and the whole congregation confirms it.

It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now stand still, that Samuel may reason with them before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord which he did to them and to their fathers.

When Jacob was come into Egypt and your fathers cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and made Israel dwell in this place. It is not just about having the ark of the covenant among you; you have to put away the idols and stop serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

When Nahash king of the children of Ammon came against them, Israel said, Nay, but a king shall reign over us, when the Lord their God was their king. That demand exposed their disbelief in the Lord; they wanted a king they could see and touch, because all the nations around them had kings. Now behold the king whom ye have chosen and whom ye have desired. If ye will fear the Lord and serve him and obey his voice and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God. If you and your king do not rebel against the voice of the Lord, the ultimate king, you will be all right. Once the Lord thundered, the people acknowledged their folly: pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not, for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king. Now they confess they were dead wrong for asking for a king.

Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy.

Turn ye not aside, for then should ye go after vain things which cannot profit nor deliver, for they are vain. Something you make with your own hands is not going to make thunder and rain come on your harvest day to show you how wicked you are; idols cannot help you or save you. Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said.

Marinate on this verse. God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you; but I will teach you the good and the right way. Samuel says that as a leader who loved his nation, if he stopped praying for them, that itself would put him in sin. For those who battle with prayer, meditate on that: ceasing to pray for your nation puts you in sin.

Only fear the Lord and serve him in truth with all your heart, and consider how great things he hath done for you. But if ye shall still do wickedly, after the speech, the warning, and the thunder, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king. That is what [Deuteronomy 28:36](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v36) said: you and the king you set over you will be brought into subjection to the other nations. Samuel's exhortation was to get their minds on the right track: you asked for the wrong thing, but now that you have it, keep the commandments and you will be all right.

Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.

Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. What the Lord weighs is actions: if it came out of your mouth, are you going to do it? All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him?
The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.
The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.
The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

He raiseth up the poor out of the dust: out of the dust means out of confusion; he brings the poor out of confusion, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them.

He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail. The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; and he shall give strength unto his king, which is Christ, and exalt the horn of his anointed.

Elkanah went to Ramah to his house, and the child did minister unto the Lord before Eli the priest. Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord. They were the devil. They were Levites, priests in the house of the Lord doing the work of the Lord, and yet it says they knew not the Lord. Why? Because they did not keep the commandments true in their spirit; they kept it on the surface where you can see it. They looked the part: they had on the fringes, they had the beard, they showed up on the sabbath day; but their spirit was not right with the Lord, and they were really the sons of the devil. Do not let that be you, Israel.

The priests' custom with the people was that when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand, and struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. They would dip it in, and what came up was the priest's portion of meat for that day; all the Levites did that, based on the sacrifices Israel brought in. This is how the Lord took care of Levi. He told Levi in the law that Levi would have no inheritance of land among the tribes; the Lord provided for them through the sacrifices that Israel brought, so they had need of nothing.

Also, before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw: I will cook it up my own way, give it to me now, before it is done. And if any man said, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth, he would answer, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force. These were devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord. These priests were disrespecting the offering of the Lord.

But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod; moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bare three sons and two daughters; and the child Samuel grew before the Lord.

Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: the harlots hanging around the temple, and Eli's sons dealing with them. He said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people; ye make the Lord's people to transgress. The Levites were the leaders, so the people followed their actions: what the priests did, the people did also. They saw the sons of Eli sleeping with the harlots and said, it must be all right, look what they have, look how they live in the temple; let us follow their lead. Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them. And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the Lord, and also with men. Eli might have said something to his children, but he did not remove them and put them out of the priesthood for their evil dealings; he said something, but he did not go further than words, he took no action with it. Watch what happened to his children.

That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. The Lord was going to make it hard on the descendants of Eli: he removed them from the priesthood, and it was written down that the descendants of Eli were not to be allowed into the house of the Lord any more. Remember, Levi was given no inheritance of land; so how would they eat, how would they live, how would they survive? Receiving their inheritance and their goods was based on them doing what thus saith the Lord told them to do, teaching the laws. Cut off from the priesthood, Eli's house was left to beg.

cases.name: Israel asking for a king
cases.charge: Rejecting the Lord's rule to be like the nations
cases.summary: The elders came to Samuel and demanded a king to judge them like all the nations. The Lord told Samuel: they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me. Warned what a king would take from them, they said, nay, but we will have a king over us.
cases.offense: Israel's elders named Samuel's age and his sons' corruption, then demanded a king to judge them like the nations (1 Samuel 8:4-5). The law had already provided for a king whom the Lord would choose, a brother who would remain under the commandments (Deuteronomy 17:14-20). The offense was not the existence of every king. It was the rejection of the Lord's reign in favour of the security Israel imagined the nations possessed. Samuel prayed, and the Lord told him that the people had rejected him, not merely his prophet. Their request continued the course of forsaking him and serving other gods since Egypt (1 Samuel 8:6-9). Joshua's congregation had promised to serve the Lord and obey his voice (Joshua 24:21-24). Now the people insisted upon a visible ruler to go before them and fight their battles, though the Lord had repeatedly delivered them through the judges (1 Samuel 8:19-20; 12:6-12).
cases.judgment: The Lord granted the request and sent thunder and rain in wheat harvest as a sign of his displeasure. The people feared and confessed, and Samuel answered, fear not; ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord. They got Saul.

entries.commentary: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel: Joel the firstborn and Abiah his second, judges in Beersheba. But his sons walked not in his ways; they turned aside after lucre, took bribes, and perverted judgment.

All the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel unto Ramah: thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways; now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a king like the other nations have. Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

The thing displeased Samuel when they said, Give us a king to judge us, and Samuel prayed unto the Lord. The Lord said, Hearken unto the voice of the people, for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them; according to all the works they have done since the day I brought them up out of Egypt, forsaking me and serving other gods, so do they also unto thee. Just as they rejected the Most High, they were rejecting Samuel and his counsel. Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

Samuel told all the words of the Lord unto the people that asked of him a king: this will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you. He will take your sons for his chariots and to be his horsemen; he will appoint him captains over thousands and captains over fifties, and set them to ear his ground, to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war. And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you, and the Lord will not hear you in that day. The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

When Saul had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart, and all those signs came to pass that day.

Saul's uncle asked him where they went and what Samuel said unto them. Saul told him plainly that the asses were found, but of the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not.

Remember, we just came out of reading Judges, and we were oppressed by many nations there. Every time one of our judges rose up and delivered us from oppression, we would get right during the life of that judge, and when that judge died we went right back into our falling. And ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you out of all your adversities and your tribulations; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us.

When all the tribes came near, the tribe of Benjamin was taken, then the family of Matri, and Saul the son of Kish was taken; and when they sought him he could not be found, for the Lord answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff. They ran and fetched him thence, and when he stood among the people he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward; he was real tall, taller than everybody. Samuel said unto all the people, See ye him whom the Lord hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people; and all the people shouted, and said, God save the king.
Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the Lord; and Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.

Saul went home to Gibeah, and there went with him a band of men whose hearts God had touched. But the children of Belial said, How shall this man save us? and they despised him, and brought him no presents; but he held his peace. That is just like us today. When a man gets raised up, instead of brothers being happy for him, a brother may feel that should have been me, not knowing he has things to work on in his own spirit, and not realizing that with rank comes responsibility; you should already be doing the work. That is why the scriptures call the ones who despised him the children of Belial, the children of the devil: the haters.

When Ephraim spake trembling, he exalted himself in Israel, but when he offended in Baal, he died.

Now they sin more and more and have made them molten images of their silver, idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen; they say of them, Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time; the craftsman was making idols in the images of men. -
Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.
Yet the Most High is the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no god but him, for there is no saviour beside him.

He knew them in the wilderness, in the land of great drought. According to their pasture they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore they forgot him. That is what happens to us; when we get all the things we need, our food, water, and clothing, and a little excess, we forget the Lord.

Though he be fruitful among his brethren, an east wind shall come, the wind of the Lord coming up from the wilderness, and his spring shall become dry and his fountain dried up; he shall spoil the treasure of all pleasant vessels.

Samaria shall become desolate, for she hath rebelled against her God; they shall fall by the sword, their infants dashed in pieces, and their women with child ripped up. This was a future prophecy at the time Hosea prophesied, about Assyria coming into the land. -

Thou shalt not sacrifice unto the Most High any bullock or sheep wherein is blemish, or any evilfavouredness, for that is an abomination unto the Lord thy God. Back then you could be put to death for sacrificing a bullock or sheep with a blemish, because doing an abominable thing carried death.

If there be found among you man or woman that hath wrought wickedness, transgressed the covenant, and gone and served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, which the Most High commanded not, the matter had to be established first. A lot of people do not know how to apply [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1); the precept for [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is [Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4). Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain that such abomination is wrought in Israel, then judgment proceeds. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death. The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. Wait till we go back to this: the ones who witnessed against you were the first to lay hands on you, so a false witness could not hide behind the crowd. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.

If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, matters of controversy within thy gates, then thou shalt get thee up into the place which the Lord shall choose. Come unto the priests the Levites and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment; thou shalt do according to all that they inform thee, according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. The man that will do presumptuously and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister before the Most High, or unto the judge, even that man shall die; and all the people shall hear, and fear, and do no more presumptuously.

When thou art come unto the land and shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations that are about me, thou shalt in any wise set him king whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. These are the laws for a king that is to rule over Israel. He shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt to multiply horses, for the Lord hath said, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way. Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away. You hear a lot of these dudes today saying king this and king that, and many of the same men pushing for multiple wives; the law of the king says do not multiply wives to thyself. Neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

When he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites. It shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Most High and keep all the words of this law and these statutes to do them. The purpose: that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, that he turn not aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, and that he prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the midst of Israel.
