verses.text: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
And his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why hast thou done so? and he also was a very goodly man; and his mother bare him after Absalom.
And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest: and they following Adonijah helped him.
And Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose, and went, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

And it was told Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah feareth king Solomon: for, lo, he hath caught hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon swear unto me to day that he will not slay his servant with the sword.
And Solomon said, If he will shew himself a worthy man, there shall not an hair of him fall to the earth: but if wickedness shall be found in him, he shall die.
So king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself to king Solomon: and Solomon said unto him, Go to thine house.
And Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bath–sheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Comest thou peaceably? And he said, Peaceably.
He said moreover, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And she said, Say on.

And he said, Thou knowest that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign: howbeit the kingdom is turned about, and is become my brother’s: for it was his from the Lord.
And now I ask one petition of thee, deny me not. And she said unto him, Say on.
And he said, Speak, I pray thee, unto Solomon the king, (for he will not say thee nay,) that he give me Abishag the Shunammite to wife.
And Bath–sheba said, Well; I will speak for thee unto the king.

Bath–sheba therefore went unto king Solomon, to speak unto him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and bowed himself unto her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a seat to be set for the king’s mother; and she sat on his right hand.
Then she said, I desire one small petition of thee; I pray thee, say me not nay. And the king said unto her, Ask on, my mother: for I will not say thee nay.
And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah thy brother to wife.

And king Solomon answered and said unto his mother, And why dost thou ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? ask for him the kingdom also; for he is mine elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.
Then king Solomon sware by the Lord, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah have not spoken this word against his own life.
Now therefore, as the Lord liveth, which hath established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and who hath made me an house, as he promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day.
And king Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him that he died.

Behold, a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.
He shall build an house for my name; and he shall be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.
And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.

And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

cases.name: Solomon at Gibeon
cases.charge: Asking for an understanding heart to judge the people, and not for long life, riches, or the life of his enemies
cases.summary: Offered anything he wanted, the young king asked for wisdom to judge a great people. The speech pleased the Lord, who gave him the wisdom and added the riches and honour he had not asked. The kingdom he built on it was the greatest Israel ever had. What he did with his wives afterward is another case.
cases.offense: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people? And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing. In Wisdom: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me; I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
cases.judgment: Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment; behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee. And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour. All the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

entries.commentary: Solomon makes affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt and takes his daughter, while building his own house, the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem. He loves the Lord and walks in the statutes of David his father, though the people still sacrifice in high places because no house was yet built to the name of the Lord.

At Gibeon the Most High appears to Solomon in a dream and says, ask what I shall give thee. Solomon, calling himself a little child who knows not how to go out or come in, asks for an understanding heart to judge the great people, to discern between good and bad. This is what we still need to pray for. We should pray that the Most High endows our leadership with wisdom, and that we ourselves learn wisdom in these scriptures and how to judge matters among one another. -

Because Solomon asked for understanding to discern judgment and not for long life, riches, or the life of his enemies, the Most High gives him a wise and understanding heart like no other before or after. He also gives what Solomon did not ask, riches and honor, and promises length of days if he walks in his ways.

Two harlots come before the king, each claiming the living child, after one woman's child died in the night and she exchanged it. Solomon calls for a sword and commands the living child divided in two, and gives half to each. The true mother pleads that the child be given alive to the other rather than slain, and by this the king discerns her, for her bowels yearned upon her son. All Israel hears the judgment and fears the king, for they see the wisdom of God is in him to do judgment.

Solomon is king over all Israel, and these are the princes he set: priests, scribes, a recorder, one over the host, one over the officers, one over the household, and one over the tribute. Twelve officers provide victuals for the king and his household, each man his month in the year. This is the establishment of government, showing order. There is the king, then ranking men, each with a position of order, the same pattern of captains and officers set up in the days of Moses.

Judah and Israel are as many as the sand by the sea, eating, drinking, and making merry, and Solomon reigns over all the kingdoms from the river to the border of Egypt, who bring presents and serve him. Every man dwells safely under his vine and fig tree from Dan to Beersheba. Israel dwells safely because of the wars of King David, who put down all the surrounding nations and put them to tribute. That is why Solomon is able to rule in a time of peace.

The Most High gives Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, largeness of heart as the sand on the seashore, so that his wisdom excels all the children of the east country and all the wisdom of Egypt. He is wiser than all men, speaks three thousand proverbs, and his songs are a thousand and five, which is why we have Proverbs and the Song of Songs. He speaks of trees, beasts, fowl, creeping things, and fishes, and people of all nations come to hear his wisdom. Since his wisdom already excelled Egypt's, we have no need to dabble in Egyptology or any doctrine outside the scriptures given to us. -

When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Most High, she came to prove him with hard questions, and came to Jerusalem with a great train, camels bearing spices, much gold, and precious stones. She communed with him of all that was in her heart, and Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hid from the king that he told her not.

When the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, the house he built, the meat of his table, the sitting of his servants, their apparel, his cupbearers, and his ascent to the house of the Most High, there was no more spirit in her. Everything in the kingdom was in order, the servants in uniform, the cupbearers in place; this is why order matters in the body today, so that those who come in are astonished and the worldly spirit of disorder leaves them, seeing the discipline and love for the people.

She told the king the report she heard in her own land was true, that she had not believed it until her eyes had seen it, and behold the half was not told her; his wisdom and prosperity exceeded the fame she heard. She said happy are his men and servants that stand continually before him and hear his wisdom; they were happy to be in order, serving with joyfulness and not complaining, because Solomon ruled wisely and took care of his people. She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

She gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great store, and precious stones; and the navy of Hiram brought from Ophir great plenty of almug trees and precious stones, of which Solomon made pillars for the house of the Most High and harps and psalteries for singers. Solomon knew how to entertain the people, providing for singing and joyfulness in the house of the Most High, for he had vision for the house and wanted Israel to enjoy the feasts and serve with gladness of heart. Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked. People assume this was sexual, but her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order; the word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think, as the law shows the tithe money could be spent on whatever the soul lusted after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food. Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing; she turned and went to her own country with her servants.

The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents, besides that of the merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors. He made two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold, and a great throne of ivory overlaid with the best gold. The throne had six steps, a round top, stays on either side, and two lions by the stays with twelve lions on the six steps, such as was not made in any kingdom. These standing lions were not graven images to bow down to; the law forbids images set up to worship, but these were not worshipped. All Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was nothing accounted of in his days. Once in three years the navy of Tarshish brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and wisdom, and all the earth sought him to hear the wisdom the Most High put in his heart, bringing presents year by year. No king reigned like Solomon or was richer than him. He gathered a thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, placed in the cities and at Jerusalem; these were of his own people, so he provided jobs for them rather than making them slaves. He made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and had horses and linen yarn brought out of Egypt; a chariot came up for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Solomon bought the best of everything, but there comes a point where riches and power can pervert the mind if a man is not grounded, and that is what begins to happen.

Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him exceedingly. The Most High established Solomon before he ever built the house. Solomon spake to all Israel, to the captains of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges and to every governor, the chief of the fathers, and went with all the congregation to the high place at Gibeon, where the tabernacle of the congregation that Moses had made in the wilderness was. The ark of God had already been brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. To read that history, go back to Second Samuel 6, and to First Chronicles 15.

The brasen altar that Bezaleel the son of Uri had made was set before the tabernacle of the Lord, and Solomon and the congregation sought unto it. Solomon went up to that brasen altar before the Lord and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it. In that night the Most High appeared unto Solomon and said, Ask what I shall give thee. This same account is told in First Kings chapter 3, where the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; reading it there gives more detail of what was said. Solomon answered that the Lord had shewed great mercy unto David his father and made him to reign in his stead, and asked that the promise unto David be established, for the Lord had made him king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude. Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.

The Most High said to Solomon that because this was in his heart, and he had not asked riches, wealth, honor, the life of his enemies, nor long life, but wisdom and knowledge to judge the people, wisdom and knowledge were granted unto him. The Lord also gave Solomon riches, wealth, and honor such as no king before him had, and none after him would have the like. When a man seeks the things of the Most High first, the other things are added unto him. Solomon returned from the high place at Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel. He gathered chariots and horsemen, having a thousand and four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem. The king made silver and gold at Jerusalem as plenteous as stones, and cedars as the sycomore trees in the valley for abundance. Horses were brought out of Egypt, and the merchants received the linen yarn at a price and fetched up horses and chariots for all the kings of the Hittites and of Syria.

verses.text: In Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.

And Solomon said, Thou hast shewed unto thy servant David my father great mercy, according as he walked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with thee; and thou hast kept for him this great kindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
And now, O Lord my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.
And thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.
Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.

And God said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;
Behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.
And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour: so that there shall not be any among the kings like unto thee all thy days.
And if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days.
And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore.
And Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.
For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.
And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.
And he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom.
So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.
And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
In that night did God appear unto Solomon, and said unto him, Ask what I shall give thee.
And Solomon said unto God, Thou hast shewed great mercy unto David my father, and hast made me to reign in his stead.
Now, O Lord God, let thy promise unto David my father be established: for thou hast made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude.
Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?

And God said to Solomon, Because this was in thine heart, and thou hast not asked riches, wealth, or honour, nor the life of thine enemies, neither yet hast asked long life; but hast asked wisdom and knowledge for thyself, that thou mayest judge my people, over whom I have made thee king:

Wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee; and I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like.
Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
Neither compared I unto her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.
I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.
All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.
And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them.
I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.
For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.
If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

cases.name: The two women before Solomon
cases.charge: Conflicting claims to a living child
cases.summary: Two women brought competing claims to a living infant before Solomon. One alleged that the other had exchanged their children after her own child died. Solomon tested their responses to a proposed division of the child and identified his mother.
cases.offense: The account first presents the exchange of the children as one woman's testimony. Both women claimed the surviving child. The narrator identifies the mother through her compassion: she preferred to surrender the child rather than see him killed.
cases.judgment: Solomon ordered that the living child be given to his mother and not killed. Israel recognized the wisdom of God in his judgment. The custody decision is explicit; no punishment of the false claimant is recorded. The unrecorded classification refers only to that punishment, not to an absence of a judicial decision.

verses.text: Then came there two women, that were harlots, unto the king, and stood before him.
And the one woman said, O my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house; and I was delivered of a child with her in the house.
And it came to pass the third day after that I was delivered, that this woman was delivered also: and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, save we two in the house.
And this woman’s child died in the night; because she overlaid it.
And she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, while thine handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.
And when I rose in the morning to give my child suck, behold, it was dead: but when I had considered it in the morning, behold, it was not my son, which I did bear.
And the other woman said, Nay; but the living is my son, and the dead is thy son. And this said, No; but the dead is thy son, and the living is my son. Thus they spake before the king.
Then said the king, The one saith, This is my son that liveth, and thy son is the dead: and the other saith, Nay; but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.
And the king said, Bring me a sword. And they brought a sword before the king.
And the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

Then spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her bowels yearned upon her son, and she said, O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it. But the other said, Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it.
Then the king answered and said, Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.
And all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment.

cases.name: King Solomon
cases.charge: Multiplying foreign wives; building high places to their gods
cases.summary: The wisest king loved many strange women, seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, from the very nations the Lord had said, ye shall not go in to them. When he was old they turned his heart, and he built high places for Chemosh and Molech in the hill before Jerusalem.
cases.offense: Solomon received wisdom, riches, honour, and the work of building the Lord's house. Yet he loved many strange women of the nations concerning whom the Lord had warned Israel, and he clave to them in love. In his old age his wives turned his heart after other gods (1 Kings 11:1-4). The warning concerned the very influence he allowed nearest his heart. The law for a king had forbidden multiplying horses, wives, silver, and gold, and required him to read the law all the days of his life so that his heart would not be lifted above his brethren (Deuteronomy 17:16-20). Royal greatness was to remain under instruction. Solomon's abundance did not place him beyond the dangers the command had named in advance. He went after Ashtoreth and Milcom and built high places for Chemosh and Molech. He did likewise for his strange wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods (1 Kings 11:5-8). The man who had built the temple in Jerusalem also established places of forbidden worship. Providing for the practice of those around him made the compromise part of the kingdom's life. The Lord had appeared to him twice and commanded him concerning this very matter (1 Kings 11:9-10). His failure was not a lack of access to wisdom. Nehemiah later remembered that even Solomon, beloved of God and made king over all Israel, was caused to sin by such marriages (Nehemiah 13:26). The greatness of the beginning deepened the warning of the end.
cases.judgment: The Lord was angry, and told him the kingdom would be rent from his son and given to his servant, leaving one tribe for David's sake. Adversaries were raised up in his own lifetime; Jeroboam received the ten tribes at his death. So the kingdom was divided.

Yet he loved many strange women of the nations concerning whom the Lord had warned Israel, and he clave to them in love. In his old age his wives turned his heart after other gods (1 Kings 11:1-4). The warning concerned the very influence he allowed nearest his heart.

The law for a king had forbidden multiplying horses, wives, silver, and gold, and required him to read the law all the days of his life so that his heart would not be lifted above his brethren (Deuteronomy 17:16-20). The man who had built the temple in Jerusalem also established places of forbidden worship. Providing for the practice of those around him made the compromise part of the kingdom's life.

The Lord had appeared to him twice and commanded him concerning this very matter (1 Kings 11:9-10). His failure was not a lack of access to wisdom. Nehemiah later remembered that even Solomon, beloved of God and made king over all Israel, was caused to sin by such marriages (Nehemiah 13:26). The greatness of the beginning deepened the warning of the end.

entries.commentary: Solomon loved many strange women besides the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites, nations the Most High had said Israel should not join with, for surely they would turn their heart after their gods; and Solomon clave to these in love. He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

When Solomon was old his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the Most High as David his father's was; he went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and did evil in the sight of the Most High. David also sinned, but when David sinned he repented and turned back, while Solomon kept going into sin; this is why a righteous man falls seven times and rises again. Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

The Most High was angry with Solomon because his heart was turned from him who had appeared to him twice and commanded him not to go after other gods, but he kept not the commandment. Therefore the Most High said he would surely rend the kingdom from Solomon and give it to his servant, but not in Solomon's days for David's sake; he would rend it out of the hand of his son. This is the pivotal moment in the history of Israel, for this sin divided the kingdom under Jeroboam and Rehoboam. The Most High said he would not rend all the kingdom but would give one tribe to the son of David for David's sake and for Jerusalem's sake.

The Most High stirred up an adversary to Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, of the king's seed in Edom, for when David was in Edom, Joab remained six months until he had cut off every male, and Hadad fled as a child to Egypt where Pharaoh gave him favor, a house, and a wife. Esau was always the first hater and enemy of Israel, comforting himself in the thought of killing us. When Hadad heard David and Joab were dead, he sought to return to his own country. The Most High also stirred up Rezin the son of Eliadah, who gathered men, reigned in Damascus, and was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon. There was peace under Solomon while he kept the commandments, but when he broke them the Most High gave strength to his enemies.

Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant, a mighty man of valor, lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon had made him ruler over the charge of the house of Joseph, which was the two tribes Ephraim and Manasseh. The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam in the way, took his new garment, rent it in twelve pieces, and gave Jeroboam ten, saying the Most High would rend ten tribes from Solomon's hand and give them to him. One tribe would remain for David's servant's sake and for Jerusalem, because Israel had forsaken the Most High and worshipped Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom. The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, so that ten tribes went to Jeroboam. If Jeroboam would walk in the ways of the Most High and keep his statutes, the Most High would build him a sure house as he built for David. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

The rest of the acts of Solomon and his wisdom are written in the book of the acts of Solomon; he reigned in Jerusalem over Israel forty years, then slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.

Thou shalt not sacrifice unto the Most High any bullock or sheep wherein is blemish, or any evilfavouredness, for that is an abomination unto the Lord thy God. Back then you could be put to death for sacrificing a bullock or sheep with a blemish, because doing an abominable thing carried death.

If there be found among you man or woman that hath wrought wickedness, transgressed the covenant, and gone and served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, which the Most High commanded not, the matter had to be established first. A lot of people do not know how to apply [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1); the precept for [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is [Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4). Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain that such abomination is wrought in Israel, then judgment proceeds. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death. The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. Wait till we go back to this: the ones who witnessed against you were the first to lay hands on you, so a false witness could not hide behind the crowd. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.

If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, matters of controversy within thy gates, then thou shalt get thee up into the place which the Lord shall choose. Come unto the priests the Levites and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment; thou shalt do according to all that they inform thee, according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. The man that will do presumptuously and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister before the Most High, or unto the judge, even that man shall die; and all the people shall hear, and fear, and do no more presumptuously.

When thou art come unto the land and shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations that are about me, thou shalt in any wise set him king whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. These are the laws for a king that is to rule over Israel. He shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt to multiply horses, for the Lord hath said, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way. Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away. You hear a lot of these dudes today saying king this and king that, and many of the same men pushing for multiple wives; the law of the king says do not multiply wives to thyself. Neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

When he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites. It shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Most High and keep all the words of this law and these statutes to do them. The purpose: that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, that he turn not aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, and that he prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the midst of Israel.

On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing. When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off. -

Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid. Nehemiah was away in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he returned and understood the evil, he cast all Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber, cleansed the chambers, and brought back the vessels of the house of God with the meat offering and the frankincense.

Nehemiah found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so the Levites and singers had fled every one to his field, and he contended with the rulers and set the Levites back in their place. He made treasurers over the treasuries, faithful men, to distribute unto their brethren, and prayed, Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.

Nehemiah saw men in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, and figs into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath. He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment. -

When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded them shut and set his servants at the gates so no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath, and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. He testified against them and warned that if they came again he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. He then commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women. -

One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah chased him away because he had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites. Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are. -

Solomon makes affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt and takes his daughter, while building his own house, the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem. He loves the Lord and walks in the statutes of David his father, though the people still sacrifice in high places because no house was yet built to the name of the Lord.

At Gibeon the Most High appears to Solomon in a dream and says, ask what I shall give thee. Solomon, calling himself a little child who knows not how to go out or come in, asks for an understanding heart to judge the great people, to discern between good and bad. This is what we still need to pray for. We should pray that the Most High endows our leadership with wisdom, and that we ourselves learn wisdom in these scriptures and how to judge matters among one another. -

Because Solomon asked for understanding to discern judgment and not for long life, riches, or the life of his enemies, the Most High gives him a wise and understanding heart like no other before or after. He also gives what Solomon did not ask, riches and honor, and promises length of days if he walks in his ways.

Two harlots come before the king, each claiming the living child, after one woman's child died in the night and she exchanged it. Solomon calls for a sword and commands the living child divided in two, and gives half to each. The true mother pleads that the child be given alive to the other rather than slain, and by this the king discerns her, for her bowels yearned upon her son. All Israel hears the judgment and fears the king, for they see the wisdom of God is in him to do judgment.

verses.text: But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites;

Of the nations concerning which the Lord said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.
And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.
For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.
For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
And Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and went not fully after the Lord, as did David his father.
Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.
And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.
And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice,
And had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the Lord commanded.

Wherefore the Lord said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.
Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.
Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.
And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:
(But he shall have one tribe for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel:)

Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in mine eyes, and to keep my statutes and my judgments, as did David his father.

But he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt, to the end that he should multiply horses: forasmuch as the Lord hath said unto you, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way.
Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away: neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin.

And Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh’s daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his own house, and the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem round about.
Thou didst bow thy loins unto women, and by thy body thou wast brought into subjection.
Thou didst stain thy honour, and pollute thy seed: so that thou broughtest wrath upon thy children, and wast grieved for thy folly.
So the kingdom was divided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdom.

cases.name: Rehoboam
cases.charge: Forsaking the counsel of the old men; forsaking the law of the Lord
cases.summary: Solomon's son rejected the elders' advice to serve the people and took his young companions' line: my little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. Ten tribes left him that day. Later, when the kingdom was established, he forsook the law of the Lord and all Israel with him.
cases.offense: The people came to Rehoboam at Shechem asking that he lighten the grievous service and heavy yoke laid upon them under Solomon. They offered to serve him if he would hear their burden (1 Kings 12:1-5). The new king asked for three days before answering. Taking time for counsel was sound; the failure came in choosing which counsel would govern him. The elders who had stood before Solomon told him to serve the people that day and answer with good words. His companions told him to announce a heavier yoke and scorpions in place of whips (1 Kings 12:6-11). One answer sought an enduring bond through service. The other treated the people's distress as an opportunity to display superiority. Proverbs 15:1 sets a soft answer against grievous words that stir up anger. Rehoboam chose the rough answer. Possession of the throne had not given him the understanding by which it could be held. Later, after he established and strengthened the kingdom, he forsook the law, and the people followed him (2 Chronicles 12:1). The repeated failure was a heart that had not prepared itself to seek the Lord (2 Chronicles 12:14). Neither inherited position nor strengthened cities supplied that preparation.
cases.judgment: The northern tribes rejected the house of David, stoned Adoram, and made Jeroboam king. Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem (1 Kings 12:16-20). His answer fulfilled the division already declared through Ahijah, yet the prophecy did not make his pride wise. The Lord accomplished his word through a king responsible for the answer he chose. When Rehoboam assembled Judah and Benjamin to recover the kingdom, Shemaiah forbade them to fight their brethren because the division was from the Lord. They obeyed and returned (1 Kings 12:21-24). He could still hearken to correction after refusing sound counsel at Shechem. Shishak afterward took Judah's fortified cities and threatened Jerusalem. Shemaiah named the cause: because they had forsaken the Lord, he had left them in Shishak's hand. The king and princes humbled themselves and confessed that the Lord was righteous (2 Chronicles 12:2-6). The Lord granted some deliverance, but they would serve Shishak and learn the difference between his service and the service of earthly kingdoms (2 Chronicles 12:7-8). Egypt carried away the treasures and Solomon's golden shields; Rehoboam replaced the gold with brass. Humbling preserved him from utter destruction without restoring everything his departure had cost.

verses.text: And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do ye advise that I may answer this people?
And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.
But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, and which stood before him:
And he said unto them, What counsel give ye that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which thy father did put upon us lighter?

And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter unto us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.
And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.
And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel that they gave him;

And spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
Wherefore the king hearkened not unto the people; for the cause was from the Lord, that he might perform his saying, which the Lord spake by Ahijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.
And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
And it came to pass, that in the fifth year of king Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the Lord,

Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the Lord, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The Lord is righteous.

And when the Lord saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the Lord.

And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord did choose out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess.
And Judah did evil in the sight of the Lord, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins which they had committed, above all that their fathers had done.
For they also built them high places, and images, and groves, on every high hill, and under every green tree.
And there were also sodomites in the land: and they did according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.
And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem:
And he took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he even took away all: and he took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made.

Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel. There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin:

entries.commentary: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king. Jeroboam, still in Egypt, heard of it and returned, and the congregation of Israel came to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the grievous yoke and heavy service his father had put on them. The heavy yoke was the labor of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the other nations, but they did have to put in that work. Rehoboam told them to depart three days and return, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer.

Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with. Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders. The young men told him to say his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions, which was disrespectful.

When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions. The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

When all Israel saw the king would not hearken, they said, What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel. So Israel departed and rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only over those in the cities of Judah did Rehoboam reign. Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day. When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself. But the word of the Most High came to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin not to fight against their brethren the children of Israel, for this thing was from the Most High; and they hearkened and returned home.

Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him. Jeroboam took counsel and made two calves of gold, telling Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem, and setting one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made a house of high places and priests of the lowest of the people, not of the sons of Levi. Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

When Rehoboam establishes the kingdom and strengthens himself, he forsakes the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him. One who leads goes astray and carries many others with him; this is why the people must be examples to one another in righteousness, of one mind and one spirit in the rebuilding of the kingdom.

In the fifth year of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem because Rehoboam transgressed against the Lord. Shishak comes with twelve hundred chariots, threescore thousand horsemen, and people without number out of Egypt, the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians. He takes the fenced cities of Judah and comes to Jerusalem; the invasion is the direct result of forsaking the law.

Shemaiah the prophet comes to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah gathered at Jerusalem and declares the word of the Lord: because they have forsaken him, he has left them in the hand of Shishak. The princes and the king humble themselves and say the Lord is righteous. When correction comes, the right response is to confess that the Most High is righteous in what he does, acknowledging the punishment as just.

When the Lord sees that they humble themselves, his word comes to Shemaiah saying he will not destroy them but grant them some deliverance, and his wrath will not be poured on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak. Nevertheless they will be Shishak's servants, that they may know the difference between serving the Most High and serving the kingdoms of the countries. The people today must likewise humble themselves, relearn to obey the commandments, and accept their condition as righteous judgment from the hand of the Most High. -

Shishak takes away the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, carrying off all the shields of gold Solomon had made. Rehoboam makes shields of brass in their place and commits them to the guard that keeps the entrance of the king's house. Whenever the king enters the house of the Lord the guard fetches the shields and returns them to the guard chamber.

Because Rehoboam humbles himself, the wrath of the Lord turns from him so that he is not utterly destroyed, and in Judah things go well. Deliverance and the destruction of enemies come to the people when they humble themselves before the Most High.

Rehoboam strengthens himself in Jerusalem and reigns; he is forty and one years old when he begins to reign and reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord chose to put his name there. His mother's name is Naamah an Ammonitess. He does evil because he prepares not his heart to seek the Lord; the failure is a heart never set on the Most High.

The acts of Rehoboam are written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies, and there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually. Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers, is buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah reigns in his place. The account then turns to Abijah's rule over Judah in the next chapter, continuing this compressed history that is told more fully in 1 and 2 Kings. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

When Jeroboam's son Abijah falls sick, the king tells his wife to disguise herself and go to Ahijah the prophet in Shiloh, carrying loaves, cakes, and honey to inquire about the child. Ahijah is old and blind, but the Most High tells him beforehand that Jeroboam's wife is coming feigning to be another woman. The moment he hears her feet at the door, Ahijah calls her by name and says he is sent to her with heavy tidings.

The message declares that though the Most High exalted Jeroboam from among the people and rent the kingdom from the house of David to give it to him, he did not walk as David who kept the commandments. Instead he made other gods and molten images and cast the Most High behind his back, doing evil above all before him. Therefore the Most High will bring evil on his house, cut off every male, and sweep away the remnant as a man sweeps away dung until it is gone. -

cases.summary: Given ten tribes by the Lord, Jeroboam feared the people would return to Jerusalem to worship, so he set calves in Bethel and Dan, saying, behold thy gods, O Israel, made priests of any who were not Levites, and moved the feast to a month of his own choosing. His sin became a recurring measure of the kings who followed him.

Instead of trusting the promise, he made two golden calves, set them at Bethel and Dan, and told Israel that going to Jerusalem was too much for them (1 Kings 12:26-30). Convenience offered to the people concealed the king's fear for himself. The words announcing their gods repeated the language of the calf in the wilderness (Exodus 32:4). He also made priests who were not sons of Levi and appointed a feast in the eighth month, a month devised from his own heart (1 Kings 12:31-33). He altered the objects, ministers, place, and time of worship to secure his rule. The priests and Levites who would not serve his arrangement left their possessions and came to Judah; others from the tribes followed to seek the Lord at Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 11:13-17). The king asked for his hand to be restored, and it was healed (1 Kings 13:1-6). Yet relief from the immediate judgment did not produce a turning from the system that had occasioned it.

entries.commentary: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king. Jeroboam, still in Egypt, heard of it and returned, and the congregation of Israel came to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the grievous yoke and heavy service his father had put on them. The heavy yoke was the labor of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the other nations, but they did have to put in that work. Rehoboam told them to depart three days and return, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer.

Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with. Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders. The young men told him to say his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions, which was disrespectful.

When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions. The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

When all Israel saw the king would not hearken, they said, What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel. So Israel departed and rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only over those in the cities of Judah did Rehoboam reign. Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day. When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself. But the word of the Most High came to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin not to fight against their brethren the children of Israel, for this thing was from the Most High; and they hearkened and returned home.

Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him. Jeroboam took counsel and made two calves of gold, telling Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem, and setting one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made a house of high places and priests of the lowest of the people, not of the sons of Levi. Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

A man of God comes out of Judah by the word of the Most High and cries against Jeroboam's altar in Bethel while the king stands by it burning incense. He prophesies that a child named Josiah, of the house of David, will one day burn the false priests of the high places on that very altar and burn men's bones upon it. He gives a sign: the altar will be rent and its ashes poured out. When Jeroboam stretches out his hand to have him seized, that hand dries up and cannot be pulled back, and the altar is rent as the sign declared. -

Jeroboam begs the man of God to entreat the Most High so his hand can be restored, and it is healed and becomes as before. The king offers reward and a meal, but the man of God refuses even half the house, because the Most High charged him to eat no bread, drink no water, and return by another way. He obeys and goes home by a different route than he came, honoring the exact terms of his commission out of Judah.

An old prophet in Bethel hears from his sons all that the man of God did, and rides after him, finding him resting under an oak. The old prophet invites him home to eat, and the man of God repeats the charge he received, that he may not eat, drink, or return the same way. The old prophet claims an angel spoke to him by the word of the Most High telling him to bring the man back, but the scripture plainly states he lied. The man of God, giving reverence to the older prophet, goes back and eats. -

As they sit at the table, the word of the Most High comes through the old prophet who lied, declaring that because the man of God disobeyed the mouth of the Most High, his carcass will not come to the sepulchre of his fathers. After he departs, a lion meets him on the way and slays him, and his carcass is cast in the road with the ass and the lion standing by it, neither eaten nor torn. The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man would keep the charge, and disobedience under that dispensation carried the penalty of death. -

The old prophet hears of it, recognizes the man of God who disobeyed, and goes to recover the body, laying it in his own grave and mourning, "Alas, my brother." He charges his sons to bury him beside the man of God's bones, confessing that the word cried against the altar of Bethel and the high places of Samaria will surely come to pass.

After all these signs, Jeroboam does not turn from his evil way but again makes priests of the high places from the lowest of the people. This thing becomes sin to the house of Jeroboam, enough to cut it off and destroy it from the face of the earth.

When Jeroboam's son Abijah falls sick, the king tells his wife to disguise herself and go to Ahijah the prophet in Shiloh, carrying loaves, cakes, and honey to inquire about the child. Ahijah is old and blind, but the Most High tells him beforehand that Jeroboam's wife is coming feigning to be another woman. The moment he hears her feet at the door, Ahijah calls her by name and says he is sent to her with heavy tidings.

The message declares that though the Most High exalted Jeroboam from among the people and rent the kingdom from the house of David to give it to him, he did not walk as David who kept the commandments. Instead he made other gods and molten images and cast the Most High behind his back, doing evil above all before him. Therefore the Most High will bring evil on his house, cut off every male, and sweep away the remnant as a man sweeps away dung until it is gone. -

Ahijah tells the wife that when her feet enter the city, the child will die, and all Israel will mourn and bury him, for in him alone of Jeroboam's house is found some good thing toward the Most High. The Most High will raise up a king to cut off the house of Jeroboam and will scatter Israel beyond the river because they made their groves and provoked Him to anger. As soon as she reaches the threshold of her house, the child dies, exactly as spoken by the hand of Ahijah, and all Israel mourns.

Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years, then slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place. In Judah, Rehoboam, forty-one at his accession, reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, and Judah did evil and provoked the Most High to jealousy above all their fathers. They built high places, images, and groves on every hill, and there were also sodomites in the land, doing according to the abominations of the nations cast out before them. -

In Rehoboam's fifth year, Shishak king of Egypt comes against Jerusalem and takes the treasures of the house of the Most High and the king's house, including the gold shields Solomon made. Rehoboam replaces the gold shields with brass, marking Israel's fall from gold to brass, from the riches of Solomon's day to loss. There is continual war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam, and when Rehoboam dies, Abijam his son reigns in his place.

Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem and walks in all the sins of his father, his heart not perfect with the Most High as David's was. The children did what they saw their fathers do, not merely what was said, which is why the Most High teaches His people to be different. Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented. -

After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did. Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa. Asa takes silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's house and sends it to Benhadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha, and Benhadad smites cities of Israel so Baasha stops building Ramah. Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father. Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite. This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.

Baasha reigns twenty-four years in Tirzah and does evil, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin by which he made Israel to sin. The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.

Hoshea son of Elah reigns nine years over Israel in Samaria and does evil, though not as the kings before him. Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up, and Hoshea becomes his servant and pays tribute. The king of Assyria finds conspiracy in Hoshea because he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped his yearly tribute, so he shuts him up in prison. Assyria besieges Samaria three years, then in the ninth year of Hoshea takes it and carries Israel away to Assyria, placing them in Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes.

This captivity comes because the children of Israel sinned against the Most High who brought them out of Egypt and feared other gods. They walked in the statutes of the heathen, built high places in all their cities, and set up images and groves on every high hill and under every green tree. They wrought wicked things to provoke the Most High and served idols, though He had said plainly, ye shall not do this thing. -

The Most High testified against Israel and Judah by all the prophets and seers, calling them to turn from evil and keep His commandments. They would not hear but hardened their necks like their fathers who did not believe in the Most High. To believe in the Most High is to take heed to the commandments, so those who claim belief while breaking the commandments do not truly believe. They rejected His statutes and covenant, followed vanity, made molten images and two calves, worshipped the host of heaven, and served Baal. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil. -

The Most High is very angry and removes Israel out of His sight, leaving only the tribe of Judah. Judah also fails to keep the commandments and walks in the statutes that Israel made. The Most High rejects all the seed of Israel, afflicts them, and delivers them into the hand of spoilers until He casts them out of His sight. This rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, which resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there. -

The king of Assyria brings men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim to dwell in the cities of Samaria in Israel's place. Because they do not fear the Most High, He sends lions among them that slay some of them. One of the carried-away priests is brought back to Bethel to teach the settlers how they should fear the Most High.

Every nation makes gods of its own and sets them in the houses of the high places the Samaritans had made. The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, Cuth made Nergal, Hamath made Ashima, the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burnt their children to Adrammelech and Anammelech. They feared the Most High and also served their own gods after the manner of the nations they came from. The Most High made His covenant and charged the children of Jacob whom He named Israel, showing the covenant belongs to Israel and not to all nations.

The Most High commanded Israel not to fear, bow to, serve, or sacrifice to other gods, but to fear and worship Him alone who brought them out of Egypt with a stretched out arm. They were to observe His statutes, ordinances, and commandments forevermore, and He would deliver them out of the hand of all their enemies. No nation and no treaty can redeem Israel from their condition, only turning to the Most High can. These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations. -
