verses.text: And Jeroboam said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David:

If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me, and go again to Rehoboam king of Judah.

Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan.
And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.
And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.

And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Beth–el, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Beth–el the priests of the high places which he had made.

So he offered upon the altar which he had made in Beth–el the fifteenth day of the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and ordained a feast unto the children of Israel: and he offered upon the altar, and burnt incense.
And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the Lord unto Beth–el: and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense.

And he cried against the altar in the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the Lord; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.
And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which the Lord hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.

And it came to pass, when king Jeroboam heard the saying of the man of God, which had cried against the altar in Beth–el, that he put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.
The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.

And the king answered and said unto the man of God, Intreat now the face of the Lord thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God besought the Lord, and the king’s hand was restored him again, and became as it was before.

After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places: whosoever would, he consecrated him, and he became one of the priests of the high places.
And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the face of the earth.
Go, tell Jeroboam, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Forasmuch as I exalted thee from among the people, and made thee prince over my people Israel,

And rent the kingdom away from the house of David, and gave it thee: and yet thou hast not been as my servant David, who kept my commandments, and who followed me with all his heart, to do that only which was right in mine eyes;
But hast done evil above all that were before thee: for thou hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back:

Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.
Him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat: for the Lord hath spoken it.
And he shall give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, who did sin, and who made Israel to sin.

And it came to pass, when he reigned, that he smote all the house of Jeroboam; he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him, according unto the saying of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite:
Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.
For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin.
For the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did; they departed not from them;
Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.
And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, that they were driven out of the land.

cases.name: Amaziah the priest of Bethel
cases.charge: Forbidding Amos to prophesy at the king's chapel; accusing him to Jeroboam of conspiracy
cases.summary: A priest of the calf at Bethel sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him, then told the prophet to go earn his bread in Judah. Amos answered that he was no prophet's son but a herdman the Lord had taken from the flock, and gave Amaziah a sentence for his wife, his children, his land and himself.
cases.offense: Amos had pleaded for Jacob when shown judgments of grasshoppers and fire. The Lord then showed him a plumbline set in the midst of Israel and declared the coming desolation of its high places and sanctuaries (Amos 7:1-9). The prophet who announced judgment had first interceded for the people; rebuke was not proof that he wished their destruction. Amaziah sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him and that the land could not bear his words. He then told Amos to flee to Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy no more at Bethel because it was the king's chapel and court (Amos 7:10-13). The priest treated the royal sanctuary as a place where the king's interests could set the limits of the Lord's speech. Amos answered that he had been a herdman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit. The Lord had taken him from following the flock and sent him to prophesy to Israel (Amos 7:14-15). His commission was not employment that Amaziah could transfer to another country. The question was not where he might earn bread, but to whom the Lord had sent him.
cases.judgment: Amos turned Amaziah's prohibition back upon him: because he said not to prophesy against Israel, a word now came concerning his own house. His wife would be a harlot in the city, his sons and daughters would fall by the sword, his land would be divided, and he would die in a polluted land. Israel would surely go into captivity (Amos 7:16-17). The sentence reached the things his royal protection could not secure: household, children, inheritance, and burial land. Silence imposed upon the messenger would not silence the judgment or preserve the place from which he was expelled. The king named here was Jeroboam in the days of Amos, not Jeroboam son of Nebat who first established the calves. Generations had passed, yet Bethel's service still joined royal power to resistance against the Lord's word. The priest defended the sanctuary's standing while refusing the correction that exposed its condition.

Amos answered that he had been a herdman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit. The Lord had taken him from following the flock and sent him to prophesy to Israel (Amos 7:14-15). His commission was not employment that Amaziah could transfer to another country. The question was not where he might earn bread, but to whom the Lord had sent him.
judgmentFull: Amos turned Amaziah's prohibition back upon him: because he said not to prophesy against Israel, a word now came concerning his own house. His wife would be a harlot in the city, his sons and daughters would fall by the sword, his land would be divided, and he would die in a polluted land. Israel would surely go into captivity (Amos 7:16-17).

The sentence reached the things his royal protection could not secure: household, children, inheritance, and burial land. Silence imposed upon the messenger would not silence the judgment or preserve the place from which he was expelled.

The king named here was Jeroboam in the days of Amos, not Jeroboam son of Nebat who first established the calves. Generations had passed, yet Bethel's service still joined royal power to resistance against the Lord's word. The priest defended the sanctuary's standing while refusing the correction that exposed its condition.

verses.text: Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.
Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.
Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit:
And the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.
Now therefore hear thou the word of the Lord: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac.

Therefore thus saith the Lord; Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in a polluted land: and Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his land.
And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.
But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not.
And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.

And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Beth–el, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Beth–el the priests of the high places which he had made.

So he offered upon the altar which he had made in Beth–el the fifteenth day of the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and ordained a feast unto the children of Israel: and he offered upon the altar, and burnt incense.
And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place:
But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.

entries.commentary: The Most High showed Amos grasshoppers formed in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth, after the king's mowings, and they ate the grass of the land. Amos pleaded, asking by whom shall Jacob arise, for he is small, and the Lord repented and said it shall not be.

The Most High showed Amos that he called to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and ate up a part. Amos again beseeched him to cease, asking by whom shall Jacob arise, for he is small, and the Lord repented and said this also shall not be.

The Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline with a plumbline in his hand and asked Amos what he saw, and Amos said a plumbline. The Most High will set a plumbline in the midst of his people Israel and will not again pass by them anymore. The high places of Isaac shall be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel laid waste, and he will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him and that the land could not bear his words. Amaziah told Amos to flee into the land of Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy no more at Bethel, for it was the king's chapel and court.

Amos answered that he was no prophet nor a prophet's son, but a herdman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit whom the Lord took as he followed the flock and sent to prophesy unto his people Israel. Because Amaziah said prophesy not against Israel, the Most High declared his wife would be a harlot in the city, his sons and daughters fall by the sword, his land divided, and he would die in a polluted land while Israel goes into captivity. Amaziah was trying to get the brother to stop prophesying, and judgment came upon him for that. The Most High gives his word to the prophets, and the prophet's job is to carry out the word of the Lord, no more, no less. If you do not like it, too bad.

For three transgressions of Moab and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime. Moab today is the Chinese. He will send a fire upon Moab that shall devour the palaces of Kerioth, and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet, and he will cut off the judge and slay all the princes with him.

For three transgressions of Judah and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they despised the law of the Lord, did not keep his commandments, and their lies caused them to err after which their fathers walked. This is the reason we are in captivity even today. Going back to the Assyrian captivity, our forefathers were rebellious against the Most High's laws, did not want to keep the commandments, and wanted to worship idols. He will send a fire upon Judah that shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.

For three transgressions of Israel and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes. That goes into oppression, and just like in today's time nobody wants to hear the righteous words of the Most High and keep the commandments; when you bring out the commandments you hear "what, I can't wear pants." They pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, turn aside the way of the meek, and a man and his father go in unto the same maid to profane the Most High's holy name. There were men even in that time going in unto their father's wife, and you may find a TV show today promoting that behavior. They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. -

Yet the Most High destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedar and who was strong as the oaks; he destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from beneath. The Amorite is another heathen nation. He brought Israel up from the land of Egypt, led them forty years through the wilderness to possess the land of the Amorite, and raised up their sons for prophets and their young men for Nazirites. You can use this to show that the children of Israel are the prophets of the Most High. But they gave the Nazirites wine to drink and commanded the prophets saying, prophesy not. That goes into lies and deceit, doing anything to stop the word of the Most High.

The Most High is pressed under them as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves; therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, the strong shall not strengthen his force, and the mighty shall not deliver himself, because Israel will be in captivity. He that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day; every possession you had will be stripped from you as you flee, the same way a robber coming to a bank strips everybody down and takes the goods.

Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king. Jeroboam, still in Egypt, heard of it and returned, and the congregation of Israel came to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the grievous yoke and heavy service his father had put on them. The heavy yoke was the labor of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the other nations, but they did have to put in that work. Rehoboam told them to depart three days and return, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer.

Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with. Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders. The young men told him to say his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions, which was disrespectful.

When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions. The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

When all Israel saw the king would not hearken, they said, What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel. So Israel departed and rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only over those in the cities of Judah did Rehoboam reign. Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day. When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself. But the word of the Most High came to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin not to fight against their brethren the children of Israel, for this thing was from the Most High; and they hearkened and returned home.

Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him. Jeroboam took counsel and made two calves of gold, telling Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem, and setting one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made a house of high places and priests of the lowest of the people, not of the sons of Levi. Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months. The king of Egypt puts him down, condemns the land in a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, and makes Eliakim his brother king, turning his name to Jehoiakim, and carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time. -

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord. When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord. The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy. -

The Most High brings upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slays their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and has no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or him that stooped for age. He gives them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes are brought to Babylon. They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of. -

Those who escape the sword are carried away to Babylon, where they are servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia. This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom. Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

cases.name: The man of God from Judah
cases.charge: Turning back to eat and drink at Bethel against the word of the Lord
cases.summary: Sent to cry against Jeroboam's altar, the prophet was charged to eat no bread, drink no water, and not return the way he came. An old prophet of Bethel lied to him, claiming an angel had said otherwise; he went back and ate. A lion met him on the road.
cases.offense: The man of God came to Bethel by the word of the Lord and cried against Jeroboam's altar. He named Josiah and foretold the burning of men's bones upon it. The altar was rent, and the king's outstretched hand dried up (1 Kings 13:1-5). His commission was confirmed before the king and the people. When Jeroboam offered food and reward, he refused even half the king's house. He had been charged to eat no bread, drink no water, and return by another way (1 Kings 13:7-10). He knew the command distinctly and had already kept it under the pressure of royal favour.
cases.judgment: The word of the Lord came through the very man who had deceived him: thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers. The lion killed him and stood by the body without eating it or the ass; the old prophet buried him in his own grave.
offenseFull: The man of God came to Bethel by the word of the Lord and cried against Jeroboam's altar. He named Josiah and foretold the burning of men's bones upon it. The altar was rent, and the king's outstretched hand dried up (1 Kings 13:1-5). His commission was confirmed before the king and the people.

When Jeroboam offered food and reward, he refused even half the king's house. He had been charged to eat no bread, drink no water, and return by another way (1 Kings 13:7-10). He knew the command distinctly and had already kept it under the pressure of royal favour.

entries.commentary: A man of God comes out of Judah by the word of the Most High and cries against Jeroboam's altar in Bethel while the king stands by it burning incense. He prophesies that a child named Josiah, of the house of David, will one day burn the false priests of the high places on that very altar and burn men's bones upon it. He gives a sign: the altar will be rent and its ashes poured out. When Jeroboam stretches out his hand to have him seized, that hand dries up and cannot be pulled back, and the altar is rent as the sign declared. -

Jeroboam begs the man of God to entreat the Most High so his hand can be restored, and it is healed and becomes as before. The king offers reward and a meal, but the man of God refuses even half the house, because the Most High charged him to eat no bread, drink no water, and return by another way. He obeys and goes home by a different route than he came, honoring the exact terms of his commission out of Judah.

An old prophet in Bethel hears from his sons all that the man of God did, and rides after him, finding him resting under an oak. The old prophet invites him home to eat, and the man of God repeats the charge he received, that he may not eat, drink, or return the same way. The old prophet claims an angel spoke to him by the word of the Most High telling him to bring the man back, but the scripture plainly states he lied. The man of God, giving reverence to the older prophet, goes back and eats. -

As they sit at the table, the word of the Most High comes through the old prophet who lied, declaring that because the man of God disobeyed the mouth of the Most High, his carcass will not come to the sepulchre of his fathers. After he departs, a lion meets him on the way and slays him, and his carcass is cast in the road with the ass and the lion standing by it, neither eaten nor torn. The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man would keep the charge, and disobedience under that dispensation carried the penalty of death. -

The old prophet hears of it, recognizes the man of God who disobeyed, and goes to recover the body, laying it in his own grave and mourning, "Alas, my brother." He charges his sons to bury him beside the man of God's bones, confessing that the word cried against the altar of Bethel and the high places of Samaria will surely come to pass.

After all these signs, Jeroboam does not turn from his evil way but again makes priests of the high places from the lowest of the people. This thing becomes sin to the house of Jeroboam, enough to cut it off and destroy it from the face of the earth.

verses.text: And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward.
And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thine house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place:
For so was it charged me by the word of the Lord, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.
So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Beth–el.
And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am.
Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.
And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:
For it was said to me by the word of the Lord, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.

He said unto him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.
So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.
And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the Lord came unto the prophet that brought him back:

And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the Lord, and hast not kept the commandment which the Lord thy God commanded thee,

But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the Lord did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.
And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase.
And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord: therefore the Lord hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake unto him.
And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.
And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, saying, Alas, my brother!
And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones:
For the saying which he cried by the word of the Lord against the altar in Beth–el, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.
But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.
Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.

cases.name: The old prophet of Beth-el
cases.charge: Lying in the name of the Lord, and claiming an angel's word to turn a prophet from his charge
cases.summary: An old prophet in Beth-el heard what the man of God had done, rode after him, and brought him home to eat by claiming an angel had told him to. The text states it flatly: but he lied unto him. The lie killed the man who believed it, and then the same mouth pronounced his sentence over the table.
cases.offense: The old prophet heard from his sons what had happened at Bethel and went after the man of God. He found him beneath an oak and invited him home. The man told him the precise command that prevented his acceptance (1 Kings 13:11-17). The old prophet therefore knew that his invitation stood against an instruction the guest believed he had received from the Lord. He answered by claiming equal prophetic standing and a newer message from an angel. The account states that he lied (1 Kings 13:18). This was not an innocent misunderstanding between two men. He supplied a false divine authorization for the very act the man had been forbidden to perform.
cases.judgment: Against the old prophet, nothing. The word of the Lord came to him as they sat at the table, and he cried the sentence over the guest he had deceived: thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers. A lion met the man of God by the way and slew him. The liar buried him in his own grave, mourned Alas, my brother, and asked to be laid beside his bones, confessing that the word cried against the altar shall surely come to pass. He is the one man in the chapter who deceives, is proved right, and walks away.

As they sit at the table, the word of the Most High comes through the old prophet who lied, declaring that because the man of God disobeyed the mouth of the Most High, his carcass will not come to the sepulchre of his fathers. After he departs, a lion meets him on the way and slays him, and his carcass is cast in the road with the ass and the lion standing by it, neither eaten nor torn. The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man would keep the charge, and disobedience under that dispensation carried the penalty of death. -

The old prophet hears of it, recognizes the man of God who disobeyed, and goes to recover the body, laying it in his own grave and mourning, "Alas, my brother." He charges his sons to bury him beside the man of God's bones, confessing that the word cried against the altar of Bethel and the high places of Samaria will surely come to pass.

After all these signs, Jeroboam does not turn from his evil way but again makes priests of the high places from the lowest of the people. This thing becomes sin to the house of Jeroboam, enough to cut it off and destroy it from the face of the earth.

The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the Lord is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

This shall be the priest's due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw. The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him. For the Most High hath chosen him out of all thy tribes to stand to minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.

If a Levite come from any of thy gates out of all Israel, and come with all the desire of his mind unto the place which the Lord shall choose, then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do which stand there before the Lord. They shall have like portions to eat, beside that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony.

When thou art come into the land, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations: there shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. These things actually existed and they are all real: wizards, necromancers, divination, observers of times, people that consult with familiar spirits. If they were not real, they would not be in the Bible with the Most High telling us not to do them. All that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord, and because of these abominations the Most High driveth those nations out from before thee. Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God, meaning upright; the nations hearken unto observers of times and unto diviners, but as for thee, the Most High hath not suffered thee so to do.

The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken. This is talking about Christ, Yeshua. This answers what Israel desired of the Most High in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not; and the Lord said, They have well spoken that which they have spoken. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him; and whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. If we do not follow Christ and do what Christ says, that judgment falls on us.

The prophet which shall presume to speak a word in the name of the Most High which he hath not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. By this law a lot of these pastors stand condemned: they say things and claim Christ said them, when the Most High never commanded Christ to say it and Christ is not telling them to say it. How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken; the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously, and thou shalt not be afraid of him. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Woe is pronounced on the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of the Most High's pasture and have not visited them, so He will visit upon them the evil of their doings. He will gather the remnant of His flock out of the countries where He drove them, bring them again to their folds, and set up shepherds who will feed them so they fear no more and none are lacking.

The Most High promises to raise unto David a righteous Branch, a King who shall reign, prosper, and execute judgment and justice, in whose days Judah shall be saved and Israel dwell safely. His name is called THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS; this is plainly referring to Christ. The day comes when they will no longer swear by the Most High who brought Israel out of Egypt, but by Him who led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country and all the countries where He had driven them, back to their own land.

Jeremiah's heart is broken and his bones shake like a drunken man because of the prophets and the words of the Most High's holiness, for the land is full of adulterers and mourns under swearing. Both prophet and priest are profane, and the Most High has found their wickedness even in His house, so their way shall be as slippery ways in the darkness where they are driven and fall. The prophets of Samaria prophesied in Baal and caused Israel to err, and the prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery, walk in lies, and strengthen the hands of evildoers so that none return from wickedness, becoming as Sodom and Gomorrah before Him.

The people are told not to hearken to the prophets who make them vain and speak a vision of their own heart, not out of the mouth of the Most High, telling those who despise Him that they shall have peace and no evil shall come. This is like the pastor who says, let me tell you what God told me to tell you, when it is a lie. None of these prophets has stood in the counsel of the Most High; had they stood there and caused the people to hear His words, they would have turned them from their evil way, but instead the whirlwind of His anger will fall grievously upon the head of the wicked in the latter days.

The Most High asks whether He is a God only near and not far off, when He fills heaven and earth and no one can hide in secret places where He cannot see him. He has heard the prophets who prophesy lies in His name saying, I have dreamed, thinking to cause His people to forget His name by their dreams as their fathers forgot it for Baal. Let the prophet with a dream tell a dream, but let him that has His word speak it faithfully, for His word is like a fire and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces; He is against those who steal His words and use their own tongues to lie on the Most High.

When the people, prophet, or priest ask what is the burden of the Most High, Jeremiah is to answer, What burden? for He will forsake them, and every man who claims the burden of the Most High He will punish in his house. Instead of saying the burden of the Most High, they are to ask one another what the Most High has answered and spoken, for they have perverted the words of the living God. Because they keep saying the burden of the Most High after being told not to, He will utterly forget them, forsake them, and cast them out of His presence with an everlasting reproach and perpetual shame that shall not be forgotten. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

verses.text: Now there dwelt an old prophet in Beth–el; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Beth–el: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father.
And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.
And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon,
And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am.
Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.
And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:
For it was said to me by the word of the Lord, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.

He said unto him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.
So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.
And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the Lord came unto the prophet that brought him back:

And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the Lord, and hast not kept the commandment which the Lord thy God commanded thee,

But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the Lord did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.
And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase.
And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord: therefore the Lord hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake unto him.
And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.
And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, saying, Alas, my brother!
And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones:
For the saying which he cried by the word of the Lord against the altar in Beth–el, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.
But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.
I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.
How long shall this be in the heart of the prophets that prophesy lies? yea, they are prophets of the deceit of their own heart;

cases.name: Baasha
cases.charge: Walking in the way of Jeroboam after being raised up to destroy Jeroboam's house
cases.summary: Baasha killed Nadab and every soul of the house of Jeroboam, exactly as Ahijah had prophesied. Then he reigned twenty-four years in the same sins, and the same prophecy was spoken over his own house by Jehu the son of Hanani.
cases.offense: Baasha conspired against Nadab while Israel besieged Gibbethon, killed him, and took his throne. He destroyed the house of Jeroboam according to Ahijah's word (1 Kings 15:25-30). He saw at close hand what became of a royal house that made Israel sin. Nevertheless he walked in Jeroboam's way throughout his own reign (1 Kings 15:33-34). Removing the family did not remove its worship. The man who profited from another king's fall repeated the offense that had brought the fall about. Through Jehu son of Hanani, the Lord reminded Baasha that he had raised him from the dust and made him prince over Israel. The charge was not merely that Baasha had failed to improve the kingdom, but that he had made the people sin and provoked the Lord by the work of his hands (1 Kings 16:1-2, 7). His authority had become another means of perpetuating the corruption he had inherited. The word also charged him concerning the killing of Jeroboam's house (1 Kings 16:7). The fulfilment of a declared judgment did not make every purpose and act of its human instrument obedient. Baasha could not take the outcome as proof that his own conduct stood beyond examination.
cases.judgment: The Lord declared that Baasha's house would become like Jeroboam's. Those dying in the city would be eaten by dogs and those in the field by birds (1 Kings 16:3-4). The comparison made his own history a witness against him: he knew the destruction named because he had carried it out upon another house. Baasha himself died and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah succeeded him (1 Kings 16:6). The destruction of the dynasty followed in Elah's days, when Zimri killed the king and cut off the house, its kinsfolk, and its friends (1 Kings 16:8-13). Baasha's personal burial must be distinguished from the sentence upon his succession.

entries.commentary: Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem and walks in all the sins of his father, his heart not perfect with the Most High as David's was. The children did what they saw their fathers do, not merely what was said, which is why the Most High teaches His people to be different. Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented. -

After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did. Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa. Asa takes silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's house and sends it to Benhadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha, and Benhadad smites cities of Israel so Baasha stops building Ramah. Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father. Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite. This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.

Baasha reigns twenty-four years in Tirzah and does evil, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin by which he made Israel to sin. The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.

The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin. Therefore the Most High will make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and those who die in the city the dogs will eat and those in the field the fowls will eat. The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought.

Elah son of Baasha reigns two years, and his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspires against him while he is drunk in a steward's house and kills him. Zimri, on taking the throne, slays all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, according to the word spoken by Jehu against Baasha. All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities. -

Zimri reigns only seven days in Tirzah. When the people encamped against Gibbethon hear he has slain the king, they make Omri, captain of the host, king over Israel. Omri and Israel go up and besiege Tirzah, and when Zimri sees the city taken, he burns the king's house over himself and dies. His death comes for his sins in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and his treason is recorded, treason being punishable by death in that time.

Israel is divided: half follow Tibni son of Ginath and half follow Omri, but Omri's followers prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns. Omri buys the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, builds the city, and names it after Shemer. Omri does worse than all before him, walking in the way of Jeroboam, then sleeps with his fathers, and Ahab his son reigns in his place.

Ahab son of Omri reigns twenty-two years in Samaria and does evil above all that were before him. As if walking in Jeroboam's sins were a light thing, he takes Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians to wife and serves and worships Baal, rearing an altar and a grove, provoking the Most High more than all the kings before him. This mirrors Solomon, who followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and the marrying outside the people that the law forbids because it turns the heart to other gods. In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua. -

In the six and thirtieth year of Asa, Baasha king of Israel comes up against Judah and builds Ramah to keep any from going out or coming in to Asa. Baasha is trying to stop the northern kingdom from coming down to Judah, because tribes out of Israel had been turning their hearts back to the Most High and joining Asa.

Instead of crying to the Most High as he did against Zerah, Asa takes silver and gold out of the house of the Lord and the king's house and hires Benhadad king of Syria to break his league with Baasha. Benhadad smites the cities of Israel, so Baasha leaves off building Ramah. Asa carries away the stones and timber of Ramah and builds Geba and Mizpah with them.

Hanani the seer comes to Asa and rebukes him for relying on the king of Syria and not on the Most High, so the host of Syria has escaped his hand. Had he relied on the Most High, he would have delivered them as he did the Ethiopians. The eyes of the Most High run to and fro throughout the whole earth to show himself strong for them whose heart is perfect. Asa is wroth, puts the seer in prison, and oppresses some of the people.

In the thirty and ninth year of his reign Asa is diseased in his feet, exceeding great, yet he seeks not to the Most High but to the physicians. The rebuke is not against physicians but against seeking them in place of the Most High, from whom healing cometh. Asa dies in the one and fortieth year of his reign and is buried in his own sepulchre in the city of David, on a bed of sweet odours and spices, with a very great burning. -

cases.name: Zimri
cases.charge: Conspiring against his master Elah as he drank himself drunk; slaying all the house of Baasha
cases.summary: Captain of half the chariots, Zimri killed his king in a steward's house and took the throne. Seven days later the army chose Omri, Tirzah was taken, and Zimri burned the king's house over his own head. His name became a byword: Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
cases.offense: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots. While the king drank himself drunk in the house of his steward Arza, Zimri conspired, struck him, and reigned in his stead (1 Kings 16:8-10). Military office gave him access that he turned against his master. He then destroyed Baasha's house, sparing neither kinsfolk nor friends. The overthrow fulfilled the word spoken through Jehu against Baasha and Elah, but Zimri also walked in Jeroboam's sin (1 Kings 16:11-13, 19). His success in removing the old house did not establish a righteous one. The change was in the man holding the palace, not in the kingdom's obedience. Baasha had repeated Jeroboam's course after destroying his descendants; Zimri repeated it after destroying Baasha's. The accumulated examples of judgment did not persuade the next claimant to forsake the sin beneath them.
cases.judgment: The army encamped against Gibbethon heard that Zimri had conspired and slain the king. It made Omri, captain of the host, king that day. Omri and Israel went up from the camp and besieged Tirzah (1 Kings 16:15-17). Holding the palace did not mean holding the allegiance of the army. When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the palace, burned the king's house over himself, and died. His reign lasted seven days (1 Kings 16:15, 18). The place seized as the seat of his advancement became the place of his death. The account names his sins and treason, not merely Omri's greater force (1 Kings 16:19-20). Years later Jezebel invoked his name against Jehu: had Zimri peace, who slew his master (2 Kings 9:31)? His short reign remained a warning that the killing of a king did not secure the killer's future. The advantage gained through conspiracy was consumed before it could become an enduring house.

verses.text: In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. And the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
And the people that were encamped heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also slain the king: wherefore all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.
And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the palace of the king’s house, and burnt the king’s house over him with fire, and died,
For his sins which he sinned in doing evil in the sight of the Lord, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he did, to make Israel to sin.
Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he wrought, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And as Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.

entries.commentary: The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin. Therefore the Most High will make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and those who die in the city the dogs will eat and those in the field the fowls will eat. The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought.

Elah son of Baasha reigns two years, and his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspires against him while he is drunk in a steward's house and kills him. Zimri, on taking the throne, slays all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, according to the word spoken by Jehu against Baasha. All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities. -

Zimri reigns only seven days in Tirzah. When the people encamped against Gibbethon hear he has slain the king, they make Omri, captain of the host, king over Israel. Omri and Israel go up and besiege Tirzah, and when Zimri sees the city taken, he burns the king's house over himself and dies. His death comes for his sins in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and his treason is recorded, treason being punishable by death in that time.

Israel is divided: half follow Tibni son of Ginath and half follow Omri, but Omri's followers prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns. Omri buys the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, builds the city, and names it after Shemer. Omri does worse than all before him, walking in the way of Jeroboam, then sleeps with his fathers, and Ahab his son reigns in his place.

Ahab son of Omri reigns twenty-two years in Samaria and does evil above all that were before him. As if walking in Jeroboam's sins were a light thing, he takes Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians to wife and serves and worships Baal, rearing an altar and a grove, provoking the Most High more than all the kings before him. This mirrors Solomon, who followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and the marrying outside the people that the law forbids because it turns the heart to other gods. In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua. -

Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

The wicked flee when no man pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion. Peter and John were perceived as unlearned men, yet their boldness made men take knowledge that they had been with Christ, who taught as one having authority. We can be bold this same way by using the words of the Most High, which no one can gainsay. For the transgression of a land many are its princes, but by a man of understanding and knowledge its state shall be prolonged. That understanding and knowledge is the Most High's commandments; David told Solomon that keeping the commandments keeps a man on the throne of Israel. -

A poor man that oppresses the poor is like a sweeping rain that leaves no food. They that forsake the law praise the wicked, but such as keep the law contend with them, as we do daily in these scriptures. Evil men do not understand judgment, but they that seek the Most High understand all things. Better is the poor who walks uprightly than the perverse rich man.

Whoever keeps the law is a wise son, but a companion of riotous men shames his father. He that increases his substance by usury and unjust gain gathers it for one who will pity the poor. He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be an abomination, as [John 9](/bible/john/9) says the Most High does not hear sinners. -

Whoever causes the righteous to go astray in an evil way shall fall into his own pit, but the upright shall have good things. The rich man is wise in his own conceit, but the poor that has understanding searches him out. He that covers his sins shall not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them shall have mercy. The Most High has mercy on those that forsake their sins; that is why we must repent, Israel. Happy is the man that fears always, but he that hardens his heart falls into mischief.

As a roaring lion and a raging bear, so is a wicked ruler over the people. The prince that lacks understanding is a great oppressor, but he that hates covetousness shall prolong his days. A man that does violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him. Whoever walks uprightly shall be saved, but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once. Our people cannot say "I'm saved," for he that endures to the end shall be saved; [Ezekiel 18](/bible/ezekiel/18) shows that if your last act is evil, the Most High will not remember the good you did before.

He that tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he that follows vain persons shall have poverty enough. Tilling the land is hard work, and the Most High says hate not laborious work; chasing vain persons means always being on some get-rich-quick scheme that does not work. A faithful man shall abound with blessings, but he that makes haste to be rich shall not be innocent. To have respect of persons is not good, for a piece of bread that man will transgress. He that hastens to be rich has an evil eye and does not consider that poverty will come; if you chase quick riches you care nothing for your victims.

He that rebukes a man shall afterward find more favor than he that flatters with the tongue. Whoever robs his father or mother and says it is no transgression is a companion of a destroyer. Think of the times, even as grown people, some went into a mother's purse or stole from a father; we must repent from these things, Israel. He that is of a proud heart stirs up strife, but he that puts his trust in the Most High shall be made fat.

He that trusts in his own heart is a fool, but whoever walks wisely shall be delivered. He that gives to the poor shall not lack, but he that hides his eyes shall have many a curse. Ecclesiasticus and the law say the same: do not turn your eye from the needy, and open your hand wide to your poor brother, for if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul his prayer is heard. [Sirach 12](/bible/sirach/12) says if you do good, know to whom you do it, and the law commands us to help our brothers who keep the commandments. When the wicked rise, men hide themselves, but when they perish the righteous increase. -

cases.name: Omri
cases.charge: Doing worse than all that were before him; walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin
cases.summary: After Zimri burned the palace over himself, Israel divided: half followed Tibni and half followed Omri. Omri prevailed, reigned twelve years, bought the hill Samaria, and built the city that became the northern kingdom’s capital. He wrought evil in the eyes of the Lord and did worse than all that were before him.
cases.offense: After Zimri’s death the people of Israel divided into two parts: half followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri. The people that followed Omri prevailed, Tibni died, and Omri reigned (1 Kings 16:21–22). The throne was gained through civil struggle, and the cost of the division left no visible impression on the rule that followed. Omri reigned twelve years over Israel, six of them in Tirzah. He bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, built on it, and named the city after the owner of the hill (1 Kings 16:23–24). Samaria became the seat of the northern kingdom and the symbol of its departure from the Lord.
cases.judgment: Omri wrought evil in the eyes of the Lord and did worse than all that were before him. He walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities (1 Kings 16:25–26). Each king surpassed his predecessor, yet the standard of comparison was always the original departure: the sin of Jeroboam. Omri slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigned in his stead (1 Kings 16:28). His son then exceeded him, as if walking in Jeroboam’s sins were a light thing (1 Kings 16:31). The house Omri built became the house through which Baal worship entered Israel, and the prophet Micah later named the accumulated corruption as the statutes of Omri (Micah 6:16).

verses.text: Then were the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half followed Omri.
But the people that followed Omri prevailed against the people that followed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.

cases.name: Ahab
cases.charge: Marrying Jezebel; serving Baal; sparing Ben-hadad whom the Lord appointed to destruction
cases.summary: Ahab did more to provoke the Lord than all the kings before him: he married a Zidonian, built Baal a house in Samaria, and made a grove. He spared the king of Syria for a trade deal after the Lord gave him the victory, and sold himself to work wickedness in Naboth's vineyard.
cases.offense: Ahab treated walking in Jeroboam's sins as a light thing and added service to Baal. He married Jezebel, built a house and altar for Baal in Samaria, and made a grove, provoking the Lord above the kings before him (1 Kings 16:30-33). The inherited corruption became the foundation for further departure rather than a warning to turn back. During the famine he called Elijah the troubler of Israel. Elijah returned the charge to Ahab and his father's house for forsaking the commandments and following Baalim (1 Kings 18:17-18). The king blamed the bearer of the warning for the distress produced by his own course. Killing the messenger or silencing him could not restore the rain. The Lord afterward delivered the Syrians into his hand, declaring that Israel would know him as the Lord. Ahab received Ben-hadad as a brother and released him under a covenant promising restored cities and trading streets (1 Kings 20:28-34). The prophet answered that Ahab had let go a man appointed to destruction; his life would answer for that life (1 Kings 20:42). A useful agreement did not authorize setting aside the judgment. When Naboth refused his vineyard, Ahab withdrew in displeasure. Jezebel arranged false witnesses and Naboth's death, and Ahab went down to take possession (1 Kings 21:1-16). Elijah met him there and joined the acts in one charge: killing and taking possession. Ahab's benefit from the murder was not separated from its guilt because another person organized it.
cases.judgment: Elijah pronounced the cutting off of Ahab's house and the consuming of its dead by dogs and birds. Ahab rent his clothes, fasted, wore sackcloth, and went softly. The Lord regarded his humbling and deferred the evil upon his house to his son's days (1 Kings 21:20-29). Mercy was shown within the judgment, without declaring his earlier deeds acceptable. At Ramoth-gilead, Micaiah warned that Israel would be scattered as sheep without a shepherd. Ahab imprisoned him and went to battle in disguise (1 Kings 22:17, 26-30). He sought safety through changing his appearance while refusing to change the course against which the word had spoken. An archer drawing at a venture struck him between the joints of his armour. He died that evening, and dogs licked his blood when the chariot was washed at Samaria (1 Kings 22:34-38). Neither a royal army nor a disguise could keep the sentence from finding him. His house continued for a time, but the king himself did not return in the peace he had demanded from his prophets.

verses.text: And Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord above all that were before him.

And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.
And he reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
And Ahab made a grove; and Ahab did more to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel that were before him.
And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.

And his servants said unto him, Behold now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings: let us, I pray thee, put sackcloth on our loins, and ropes upon our heads, and go out to the king of Israel: peradventure he will save thy life.

So they girded sackcloth on their loins, and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel, and said, Thy servant Ben–hadad saith, I pray thee, let me live. And he said, Is he yet alive? he is my brother.

Now the men did diligently observe whether any thing would come from him, and did hastily catch it: and they said, Thy brother Ben–hadad. Then he said, Go ye, bring him. Then Ben–hadad came forth to him; and he caused him to come up into the chariot.

And Ben–hadad said unto him, The cities, which my father took from thy father, I will restore; and thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria. Then said Ahab, I will send thee away with this covenant. So he made a covenant with him, and sent him away.

And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
But there was none like unto Ahab, which did sell himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.
And he did very abominably in following idols, according to all things as did the Amorites, whom the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.
And it came to pass, when Ahab heard those words, that he rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his flesh, and fasted, and lay in sackcloth, and went softly.
And the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Seest thou how Ahab humbleth himself before me? because he humbleth himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days: but in his son’s days will I bring the evil upon his house.

And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
And the battle increased that day: and the king was stayed up in his chariot against the Syrians, and died at even: and the blood ran out of the wound into the midst of the chariot.
And there went a proclamation throughout the host about the going down of the sun, saying, Every man to his city, and every man to his own country.
So the king died, and was brought to Samaria; and they buried the king in Samaria.
And one washed the chariot in the pool of Samaria; and the dogs licked up his blood; and they washed his armour; according unto the word of the Lord which he spake.
And when the Lord thy God shall deliver them before thee; thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them:
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.
