cases.name: The widow of Zarephath
cases.charge: Making the prophet's cake first, out of the last handful of meal
cases.summary: A Gentile widow gathering two sticks to cook a last meal for herself and her son was asked by a stranger to feed him first from it, on a promise from the God of Israel. She did. The barrel of meal did not waste and the cruse of oil did not fail until the rain came, and when her son died the prophet raised him.
cases.offense: As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die. Elijah said, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah. Christ named her against Nazareth: unto none of the widows of Israel was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta.
cases.judgment: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth. And she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. When her son fell sick and there was no breath left in him, Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times and cried unto the Lord, and the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived. The woman said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.

entries.commentary: Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab that as the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom he stands, there shall not be dew nor rain these years but according to his word. Elijah prayed and it was no rain. The teaching opens by framing the whole session on the power of the Most High: he has power over everything, the animals and all creation, and he set that power on display through his prophet.

The word of the Lord sent Elijah eastward to hide by the brook Cherith before Jordan, and there he drank of the brook and the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning and in the evening. This shows the power of the Most High over the animals: he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will, just as he did Elijah.

The brook dried up for want of rain, and the Lord sent Elijah all the way across the land to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon on the coast, where he had commanded a widow woman to sustain him. From the east side by Jordan to the west by Sidon was a hard walk of a Sabbath day's journey or more, with no water anywhere. Coming to the gate, Elijah asked the widow for water and a morsel of bread, and she answered that she had but a handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruise, gathering two sticks to dress a last meal for herself and her son that they might eat it and die. Elijah told her to make him a little cake first and after that for herself and her son, for the Lord God of Israel said the barrel of meal would not waste nor the cruise of oil fail until the day the Lord sent rain. She obeyed, and she and Elijah and her house did eat many days. For trusting in the Lord and obeying, she was sustained. The instruction to feed the man of God first is a precept: the man eats first. Sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

After these things the widow's son fell sick, and his sickness was so sore that there was no breath left in him. She said unto Elijah, Art thou come to call my sin to remembrance and to slay my son? Her thought was that the child was paying for the parent's sins. Elijah took the child up to the loft, laid him on his own bed, and cried unto the Lord, stretching himself upon the child three times and praying that the child's soul come into him again. The Lord heard the voice of Elijah, and the soul of the child came into him again and he revived. Elijah delivered the living child to his mother, and she said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth. All praises that Elijah was there to call upon the Lord, for it was not the young man's time to go. A man's days are determined and appointed, and he cannot pass the bound the Most High has set; because it was not the child's time, the Lord let his soul return.

Being full of the Holy Ghost he is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, forty days tempted of the devil, and in those days he did eat nothing. He answers with the law: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

The devil shows him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. No man can do that, which settles who was standing there. All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever I will I give it. The offer is real, and the price is worship. Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Again the answer is a commandment.

Set on a pinnacle of the temple and answered with scripture, he replies, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God. When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season. The whole battle was fought with the word, and that is the only way it is won.

As his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. He reads from Esaias: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, to preach deliverance to the captives. This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

They wonder at the gracious words, and then ask, Is not this Joseph's son? No prophet is accepted in his own country. He names the widow of Sarepta and Naaman the Syrian, and they are filled with wrath, thrust him out of the city, and lead him to the brow of the hill to cast him down headlong, but he passes through the midst of them.

In the synagogue there was a man which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and it cried out, I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God. That spirit was sitting in the house of worship, and it knew exactly who he was. Knowing who he is and doing what he says are two different things.

He rebukes the fever in Simon's wife's mother and it leaves her, and he lays his hands on every one of the sick brought to him. I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent. He went where the people were, and some received the word and some did not.

Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.

verses.text: And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee.

So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

And she said, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.
For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth.
And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.
And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.
And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.
And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?
And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
And he cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.
And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother: and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.
And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.
But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.
He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.
And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:

cases.name: Obadiah, who hid the prophets
cases.charge: Taking a hundred prophets and hiding them by fifty in a cave, and feeding them with bread and water, while serving in Ahab's house
cases.summary: The governor of Ahab's house feared the Lord greatly. When Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord he took a hundred of them, hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water through a famine. Sent out by the king to look for grass, he met Elijah, and was afraid to carry the message that would summon Ahab, in case the Spirit carried the prophet away and he was killed for it. Elijah swore he would shew himself, and he went.
cases.offense: Obadiah governed Ahab's house and feared the Lord greatly. When Jezebel cut off the Lord's prophets, he hid a hundred of them, fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water (1 Kings 18:3-4). Service within the royal household did not require him to join its persecution. The fear of the Lord governed what he would do with the position he held. The famine made this sustained care costly. Ahab himself went out seeking grass to preserve horses and mules, dividing the search with Obadiah (1 Kings 18:5-6). While the kingdom struggled to find provision, Obadiah maintained people the queen intended to destroy. His service was measured in lives sheltered and food supplied, not merely in a private refusal to approve her deeds. When Elijah met him and sent him to announce his presence to Ahab, Obadiah named his fear. Ahab had searched kingdoms and nations for the prophet. If Obadiah reported that Elijah was there and the Spirit carried him away before Ahab arrived, the king would kill the messenger (1 Kings 18:7-12). His concern was not imaginary, nor did he conceal it beneath a claim of fearlessness. He reminded Elijah that he had feared the Lord from his youth and had hidden the prophets. Elijah swore that he would show himself to Ahab that day. Obadiah then went to meet the king and told him (1 Kings 18:12-16). He received the assurance and performed the errand. Courage was seen in his obedience with the danger understood.
cases.judgment: A hundred prophets had been preserved when Jezebel sought to cut them off. Obadiah's provision kept their hiding places from becoming places of starvation. His fear of God bore fruit in the continuing lives of other servants, even while he occupied a post beneath a king who had forsaken the commandments. His message also brought Ahab to Elijah, preparing the meeting from which the summons to Carmel followed (1 Kings 18:16-19). The hidden work of feeding and sheltering was followed by an errand that served a public confrontation. Different duties required the same fidelity. Hebrews 6:10 declares that God does not forget work and labour of love shown in ministering to the saints. Obadiah's account does not conclude with a new title or an estate bestowed upon him. The good already accomplished was substantial: servants were alive, and the required message was delivered. Elijah would later speak of being left alone, but the Lord's work in Israel had never been limited to what one prophet could see (1 Kings 19:10, 18). Obadiah's caves belonged to that larger history of preservation. A man inside Ahab's house had feared the Lord more than he agreed with the house's evil.

verses.text: And Ahab called Obadiah, which was the governor of his house. (Now Obadiah feared the Lord greatly:
For it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, that Obadiah took an hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)

entries.commentary: After many days the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year: Go show thyself unto Ahab, and I will send rain upon the earth. There was a sore famine in Samaria. Ahab called Obadiah, governor of his house, who feared the Lord greatly; when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took an hundred prophets and hid them by fifty in a cave and fed them with bread and water, putting his own life in danger to save them. The famine was so sore it was hitting the animals, so Ahab and Obadiah divided the land between them, each going his own way to seek fountains and brooks to find grass to save the horses and mules alive. This was the fruit of the drought Elijah had pronounced.

As Obadiah went his way, Elijah met him; Obadiah fell on his face and said, Art thou my lord Elijah? Elijah told him to go tell Ahab that Elijah is here. Obadiah was afraid, for Ahab had searched every nation and kingdom to find and slay Elijah; that is how badly Jezebel wanted him dead, so she got Ahab to do her bidding. This is why Elijah had been on the run, first by Jordan, then years with the widow. Obadiah feared that the spirit of the Lord would carry Elijah away and Ahab would slay him for a false report, so he pleaded his own record: he feared the Lord from his youth and had hidden a hundred of the Lord's prophets by fifty in a cave. Elijah swore by the Lord of hosts that he would surely show himself to Ahab that day, and so Obadiah went to Ahab, and Ahab came to meet Elijah.

When Ahab saw Elijah he said, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? That is the mind of a wicked person: he blamed the trouble on the ordained prophet of God rather than on his own wickedness. When the spirit is gone, wisdom cannot enter a malicious soul, so Ahab had thoughts without understanding. Elijah answered, I have not troubled Israel, but thou and thy father's house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord and thou hast followed Baalim. It was Ahab following the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, worshipping the golden calves, that brought the trouble. Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

Ahab gathered the prophets and all Israel to Mount Carmel, and Elijah said unto the people, How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him, but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word. That is a call for all of us to examine ourselves: cast away every burden and sin and follow the Most High and his son fully, keeping the commandments, and do not keep one foot in and one foot out. Being lukewarm, playing the middle ground, ends with Christ spewing a man out of his mouth, and the next step after that is death. Elijah proposed the test: let each side dress a bullock, lay it on wood, and put no fire under, and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. All the people said, It is well spoken.

The prophets of Baal dressed their bullock first and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us, but there was no voice nor any that answered, and they leaped upon the altar. Picture the scene: eight hundred and fifty men doing this, running wild, while Elijah sat back watching the madness. At noon Elijah mocked them, saying, Cry aloud, for he is a god; either he is talking, or pursuing, or on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth and must be awaked. They cried aloud and cut themselves with knives and lancets till the blood gushed out, for cutting themselves was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal. From midday past the time of the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor any to answer nor any that regarded. No one answered because the Most High will not give his glory to another, and the gods of the nations are idols that are not real; they are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.

Elijah repaired the altar of the Lord with twelve stones according to the twelve tribes of the sons of Jacob, made a trench about it, laid the wood and the bullock in order, and had them drench the sacrifice with four barrels of water three times until the water filled the trench. At the time of the evening sacrifice Elijah prayed, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel and that I am thy servant. As the law appointed a sacrifice in the morning and in the evening, this was the evening sacrifice as the sun went down. Elijah prayed, Hear me, O Lord, that this people may know that thou art the Lord God and that thou hast turned their heart back again. Then the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench. When all the people saw it they fell on their faces and cried, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God. Elijah commanded, Take the prophets of Baal, let not one of them escape, and they were brought down to the brook Kishon and slain there. In the last days it will be the same: when the Most High rains down fire again by the hands of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape, for they that feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee.

Elijah told Ahab to get up and eat and drink, for there was a sound of abundance of rain. Ahab went up to eat while Elijah went to the top of Carmel, cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees to pray. Elijah sent his servant seven times to look toward the sea; at the seventh time he reported a little cloud out of the sea like a man's hand. Elijah sent word to Ahab to prepare his chariot and get down before the rain stopped him, for the hand of the Lord was coming. The heaven grew black with clouds and wind and there was a great rain; Ahab rode to Jezreel, a city in the north in Samaria, and the hand of the Lord was on Elijah so that he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

cases.name: The prophets of Baal at Carmel
cases.charge: Prophesying in the name of other gods
cases.summary: Four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal cried from morning to noon and cut themselves with knives until the blood gushed out, and there was neither voice nor any to answer. Elijah's bullock, drenched three times, was consumed by fire from heaven with the water and the stones.
cases.offense: At Carmel Elijah asked Israel how long they would halt between two opinions. If the Lord was God, they were to follow him; if Baal, then Baal. The people answered nothing (1 Kings 18:21). The contest exposed a divided service that could not be made right by refusing to decide. Four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal stood against Elijah. They chose a bullock, dressed it, and called upon Baal from morning until noon. There was no voice and no answer. They leaped upon the altar and, after Elijah challenged them, cried aloud and cut themselves with knives and lancets until the blood flowed (1 Kings 18:22-28). Increasing noise and injury did not give their god power to answer. The law forbade a prophet to speak in the name of other gods (Deuteronomy 18:20). Deuteronomy 13:1-5 also required Israel to reject a teacher who led them after other gods, even if a sign accompanied his words. Here no answer came at all, yet the servants of Baal continued until the time of the evening sacrifice (1 Kings 18:29). Zeal for the practice could not make the practice obedience. Elijah repaired the Lord's altar, drenched the offering, and prayed that the people know the Lord and turn back to him (1 Kings 18:30-37). The difference was not merely between two methods of conducting worship. It was between calling upon the living God according to his word and persisting in a service he had forbidden.
cases.judgment: The Lord's fire consumed the offering, wood, stones, dust, and water. The people fell upon their faces and confessed that the Lord was God (1 Kings 18:38-39). The answer left the assembly no reason to maintain its earlier silence. What the prophets of Baal could not obtain through hours of crying was accomplished when the Lord answered his servant. Elijah commanded that none of the prophets of Baal escape. They were taken to the brook Kishon and slain (1 Kings 18:40). The sentence belonged to the covenant law against leading Israel into the service of other gods; the crowd's earlier acceptance and the worship's royal standing did not remove that charge. Rain followed after Elijah prayed upon Carmel (1 Kings 18:41-45). The drought had not been ended by Baal's servants, their multitude, their cries, or their wounds. The return of rain confirmed the same distinction as the fire: the Lord who had withheld it was the one who could send it again.

verses.text: Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel’s table.
Then said Elijah unto the people, I, even I only, remain a prophet of the Lord; but Baal’s prophets are four hundred and fifty men.

And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped upon the altar which was made.

And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.
And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them.
And it came to pass, when midday was past, and they prophesied until the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.
Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.
And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God.
And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them: and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slew them there.
If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder,
And the sign or the wonder come to pass, whereof he spake unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known, and let us serve them;

Thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams: for the Lord your God proveth you, to know whether ye love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
Ye shall walk after the Lord your God, and fear him, and keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and ye shall serve him, and cleave unto him.

And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the Lord thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee.
But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.
Ye shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor print any marks upon you: I am the Lord.

Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the Lord is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

This shall be the priest's due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw. The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him. For the Most High hath chosen him out of all thy tribes to stand to minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.

If a Levite come from any of thy gates out of all Israel, and come with all the desire of his mind unto the place which the Lord shall choose, then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do which stand there before the Lord. They shall have like portions to eat, beside that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony.

When thou art come into the land, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations: there shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. These things actually existed and they are all real: wizards, necromancers, divination, observers of times, people that consult with familiar spirits. If they were not real, they would not be in the Bible with the Most High telling us not to do them. All that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord, and because of these abominations the Most High driveth those nations out from before thee. Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God, meaning upright; the nations hearken unto observers of times and unto diviners, but as for thee, the Most High hath not suffered thee so to do.

The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken. This is talking about Christ, Yeshua. This answers what Israel desired of the Most High in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not; and the Lord said, They have well spoken that which they have spoken. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him; and whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. If we do not follow Christ and do what Christ says, that judgment falls on us.

The prophet which shall presume to speak a word in the name of the Most High which he hath not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. By this law a lot of these pastors stand condemned: they say things and claim Christ said them, when the Most High never commanded Christ to say it and Christ is not telling them to say it. How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken; the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously, and thou shalt not be afraid of him. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.

cases.name: Elisha
cases.charge: Asking a double portion of the spirit; leaving the oxen and following, and refusing Naaman's reward
cases.summary: Called from ploughing, Elisha fed the people and followed Elijah. He asked a double portion of his spirit and continued the ministry after his master was taken. He supplied households, restored the Shunammite’s son, refused Naaman’s reward, and fed the Syrians delivered into Samaria. After his death, a man revived upon touching his bones.
cases.offense: Elisha was ploughing when Elijah cast his mantle upon him. He left the oxen, asked to kiss his father and mother, and returned to prepare a farewell meal. He slew a yoke of oxen, boiled the flesh with their instruments, fed the people, and arose to minister to Elijah (1 Kings 19:19-21). The call was answered by a change of service, not merely an expression of admiration for the prophet. When Elijah's departure approached, Elisha would not leave him at Gilgal, Bethel, or Jericho. He crossed Jordan with him and asked for a double portion of his spirit. Elijah called it a hard thing and gave the condition that Elisha see him taken (2 Kings 2:1-10). The request concerned the power required to continue the work, not wealth or a place at the king's table. After Naaman's cleansing, Elisha refused the gift pressed upon him, swearing by the Lord before whom he stood that he would receive none (2 Kings 5:15-16). Gehazi afterward pursued what his master refused. The same opportunity distinguished service from covetousness. The healing was not to be turned into a private bargain by a servant who had not supplied its power. At Dothan, surrounded by the Syrian host, Elisha answered his servant's fear by praying that his eyes be opened. The mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kings 6:15-17). Elisha did not deny the surrounding army; he knew it was not the only host present. He sought that his servant see the protection already there.
cases.judgment: Elisha saw Elijah taken and received the mantle that fell. Returning to Jordan, he struck the water and called upon the Lord God of Elijah. The waters divided, and the sons of the prophets recognised that Elijah's spirit rested upon him (2 Kings 2:11-15). The departed master was not the source exhausted by his departure. The Lord remained with the servant appointed to continue. His ministry supplied households and preserved life: the widow's oil paid her debt, the Shunammite received her son alive, harmful pottage was made safe, and a hundred men ate from twenty barley loaves and left food remaining (2 Kings 4:1-7, 32-44). The wonders were not detached displays. They answered debt, bereavement, hunger, and danger among the people. When the Syrians sent to seize him were led into Samaria, the king asked whether to kill them. Elisha commanded that food and water be set before them and that they return to their master. They ate and departed (2 Kings 6:18-23). Power to deliver an enemy into the city did not require that power to be used for slaughter. The prophet who announced judgments also directed mercy where the Lord had given that charge. Elisha eventually became sick and died, but the Lord's power was not buried with him. A dead man cast into his sepulchre touched his bones, revived, and stood upon his feet (2 Kings 13:20-21). Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 48:12-14 remembers both the wonders of his life and the marvel after his death. His strength had never resided in possessions gathered from those he helped, but in the Lord whose word he served.

He slew a yoke of oxen, boiled the flesh with their instruments, fed the people, and arose to minister to Elijah (1 Kings 19:19-21). The call was answered by a change of service, not merely an expression of admiration for the prophet.

When Elijah's departure approached, Elisha would not leave him at Gilgal, Bethel, or Jericho. He crossed Jordan with him and asked for a double portion of his spirit. Elijah called it a hard thing and gave the condition that Elisha see him taken (2 Kings 2:1-10). The request concerned the power required to continue the work, not wealth or a place at the king's table.

After Naaman's cleansing, Elisha refused the gift pressed upon him, swearing by the Lord before whom he stood that he would receive none (2 Kings 5:15-16). At Dothan, surrounded by the Syrian host, Elisha answered his servant's fear by praying that his eyes be opened. The mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kings 6:15-17). Elisha did not deny the surrounding army; he knew it was not the only host present. He sought that his servant see the protection already there.

The waters divided, and the sons of the prophets recognised that Elijah's spirit rested upon him (2 Kings 2:11-15). The departed master was not the source exhausted by his departure. When the Syrians sent to seize him were led into Samaria, the king asked whether to kill them. Elisha commanded that food and water be set before them and that they return to their master. His strength had never resided in possessions gathered from those he helped, but in the Lord whose word he served.

cases.name: Ben-hadad and the Syrians at Aphek
cases.charge: Saying the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys
cases.summary: Beaten at Samaria, the Syrians told their king the God of Israel was a hill god and would lose on level ground. The Lord heard it. A prophet told Ahab the outcome before the battle: that ye may know that I am the Lord.
cases.offense: After defeat before Samaria, the Syrian servants attributed Israel's strength to the hills. They proposed replacing the kings with captains and fighting on the plain, where they supposed Israel's God could not give the same victory (1 Kings 20:23-25). They changed the ground without changing the presumption beneath the war. Ben-hadad gathered another host at Aphek. Israel appeared like two little flocks while the Syrians filled the country (1 Kings 20:26-27). The visible imbalance encouraged confidence in numbers, but the Lord's answer addressed the claim about his power. He would deliver the multitude so Israel would know that he was the Lord (1 Kings 20:28). Neither terrain nor a larger army marked the limit of his dominion.
cases.judgment: After seven days facing one another, Israel struck a hundred thousand Syrian footmen in one day. The survivors fled into Aphek, where a wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand; Ben-hadad hid in an inner chamber (1 Kings 20:29-30). The place chosen to reverse the first defeat became the place of a greater overthrow. Ahab afterward received Ben-hadad and released him under a covenant. That release was charged against Ahab: he had let go a man appointed to destruction (1 Kings 20:31-42). The Syrian king's escape did not prove his claim about the Lord or make the agreement righteous. Victory given to Israel still required obedience from Israel's king.

verses.text: And the servants of the king of Syria said unto him, Their gods are gods of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we; but let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.
And do this thing, Take the kings away, every man out of his place, and put captains in their rooms:

And number thee an army, like the army that thou hast lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot: and we will fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they. And he hearkened unto their voice, and did so.
And it came to pass at the return of the year, that Ben–hadad numbered the Syrians, and went up to Aphek, to fight against Israel.

And the children of Israel were numbered, and were all present, and went against them: and the children of Israel pitched before them like two little flocks of kids; but the Syrians filled the country.

And there came a man of God, and spake unto the king of Israel, and said, Thus saith the Lord, Because the Syrians have said, The Lord is God of the hills, but he is not God of the valleys, therefore will I deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.

And they pitched one over against the other seven days. And so it was, that in the seventh day the battle was joined: and the children of Israel slew of the Syrians an hundred thousand footmen in one day.
But the rest fled to Aphek, into the city; and there a wall fell upon twenty and seven thousand of the men that were left. And Ben–hadad fled, and came into the city, into an inner chamber.

And, behold, there came a prophet unto Ahab king of Israel, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? behold, I will deliver it into thine hand this day; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.
For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.

entries.commentary: Ben-hadad the king of Syria gathered all his hosts, with thirty-two kings, horses, and chariots, and besieged Samaria. He sent to Ahab demanding his silver, gold, wives, and children, even the goodliest, and Ahab answered, My lord, O king, I am thine, and all that I have. Ben-hadad sent again, saying that his servants would come and search Ahab's house and take away whatsoever was pleasant in his eyes. This siege was Ahab's judgment from the Lord for trying to kill Elijah, for serving Baal, and for letting Jezebel run him and kill the prophets.

Ahab called the elders of the land, who told him not to hearken nor consent to Ben-hadad's demand, so Ahab sent word that he would grant the first demand but not the second. Ben-hadad swore by his gods to reduce Samaria to dust for handfuls among his people. Ahab answered, Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off. When Ben-hadad heard this while drinking with the kings in the pavilions, he commanded his servants to set themselves in array against the city; Ahab's boast had provoked him to prepare for battle.

A prophet came unto Ahab saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? I will deliver it into thine hand this day, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord. Asked by whom, the prophet answered, By the young men of the princes of the provinces, and that Ahab himself should order the battle. Two hundred and thirty-two young men of the princes of the provinces went out first, followed by the children of Israel, being seven thousand; they went out at noon while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk with the thirty-two kings, taking Israel lightly. The young men slew every one his man and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them; Ben-hadad escaped on a horse, and the king of Israel smote the horses and chariots and slew the Syrians with a great slaughter. The Most High gave the victory though Israel's numbers were small.

The prophet warned Ahab to strengthen himself and mark, for at the return of the year the king of Syria would come up against him again. The servants of Ben-hadad counseled that Israel's gods were gods of the hills, so they should fight in the plain, replace the kings with captains, and number a fresh army horse for horse and chariot for chariot; Ben-hadad hearkened and did so. At the return of the year Ben-hadad came up to fight, and the children of Israel pitched before them like two little flocks of kids while the Syrians filled the country; Israel's army was small compared to the great Syrian host. A man of God told Ahab, Because the Syrians have said the Lord is God of the hills but not of the valleys, I will deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I am the Lord. Here the Most High was giving Ahab a chance to repent, redeeming him by showing his power with fewer numbers; yet Ahab still did not repent, did not check Jezebel, and did not destroy the idols of Baal, for his sin had blinded him. Israel and Syria pitched one against the other seven days, and on the seventh day the battle was joined, and the children of Israel slew of the Syrians a hundred thousand footmen in one day. The rest fled to Aphek, where a wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand of the men left. Seven thousand against a hundred thousand, and the numbers did not matter because the Lord was with Israel; but Ahab still did not repent.

Ben-hadad fled into an inner chamber, and his servants, having heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful, put sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads and went to plead for his life. Ahab, hearing that Ben-hadad lived, called him his brother and had him brought up into his chariot. Look at Ahab's wickedness: this was a Syrian who was just trying to kill him last year, and he brought him up into the king's chariot. Ben-hadad offered to restore the cities his father had taken and give Ahab streets in Damascus, and Ahab said, I will send thee away with this covenant, and he made a covenant with the heathen and sent him away.

cases.name: The man who refused the prophetic command
cases.charge: Refusing a command delivered in the word of the Lord
cases.summary: A man of the sons of the prophets asked his neighbour to strike him in the word of the Lord. The neighbour refused. The prophet announced that a lion would kill him, and the stated judgment followed.
cases.offense: A son of the prophets commanded his neighbour, in the word of the Lord, to smite him. The man refused (1 Kings 20:35). The command belonged to the prophetic action by which Ahab would be confronted, and the prophet expressly identified the refusal as not obeying the Lord's voice (1 Kings 20:36). The act must be understood within that commission. The prophet needed to appear wounded before the king and present the case of a prisoner allowed to escape. The neighbour was asked to participate in a particular sign, not to decide whether the message against Ahab should proceed. His refusal did not cancel the work the Lord had appointed.
cases.judgment: After the man departed, a lion found and killed him. Another man then struck and wounded the prophet, who used his disguise in the encounter with Ahab that follows. This event is distinct from the death of the man of God from Judah in 1 Kings 13.

entries.commentary: Ben-hadad the king of Syria gathered all his hosts, with thirty-two kings, horses, and chariots, and besieged Samaria. He sent to Ahab demanding his silver, gold, wives, and children, even the goodliest, and Ahab answered, My lord, O king, I am thine, and all that I have. Ben-hadad sent again, saying that his servants would come and search Ahab's house and take away whatsoever was pleasant in his eyes. This siege was Ahab's judgment from the Lord for trying to kill Elijah, for serving Baal, and for letting Jezebel run him and kill the prophets.

Ahab called the elders of the land, who told him not to hearken nor consent to Ben-hadad's demand, so Ahab sent word that he would grant the first demand but not the second. Ben-hadad swore by his gods to reduce Samaria to dust for handfuls among his people. Ahab answered, Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off. When Ben-hadad heard this while drinking with the kings in the pavilions, he commanded his servants to set themselves in array against the city; Ahab's boast had provoked him to prepare for battle.

A prophet came unto Ahab saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? I will deliver it into thine hand this day, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord. Asked by whom, the prophet answered, By the young men of the princes of the provinces, and that Ahab himself should order the battle. Two hundred and thirty-two young men of the princes of the provinces went out first, followed by the children of Israel, being seven thousand; they went out at noon while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk with the thirty-two kings, taking Israel lightly. The young men slew every one his man and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them; Ben-hadad escaped on a horse, and the king of Israel smote the horses and chariots and slew the Syrians with a great slaughter. The Most High gave the victory though Israel's numbers were small.

The prophet warned Ahab to strengthen himself and mark, for at the return of the year the king of Syria would come up against him again. The servants of Ben-hadad counseled that Israel's gods were gods of the hills, so they should fight in the plain, replace the kings with captains, and number a fresh army horse for horse and chariot for chariot; Ben-hadad hearkened and did so. At the return of the year Ben-hadad came up to fight, and the children of Israel pitched before them like two little flocks of kids while the Syrians filled the country; Israel's army was small compared to the great Syrian host. A man of God told Ahab, Because the Syrians have said the Lord is God of the hills but not of the valleys, I will deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I am the Lord. Here the Most High was giving Ahab a chance to repent, redeeming him by showing his power with fewer numbers; yet Ahab still did not repent, did not check Jezebel, and did not destroy the idols of Baal, for his sin had blinded him. Israel and Syria pitched one against the other seven days, and on the seventh day the battle was joined, and the children of Israel slew of the Syrians a hundred thousand footmen in one day. The rest fled to Aphek, where a wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand of the men left. Seven thousand against a hundred thousand, and the numbers did not matter because the Lord was with Israel; but Ahab still did not repent.

Ben-hadad fled into an inner chamber, and his servants, having heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful, put sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads and went to plead for his life. Ahab, hearing that Ben-hadad lived, called him his brother and had him brought up into his chariot. Look at Ahab's wickedness: this was a Syrian who was just trying to kill him last year, and he brought him up into the king's chariot. Ben-hadad offered to restore the cities his father had taken and give Ahab streets in Damascus, and Ahab said, I will send thee away with this covenant, and he made a covenant with the heathen and sent him away.

verses.text: And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his neighbour in the word of the Lord, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man refused to smite him.

Then said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of the Lord, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he was departed from him, a lion found him, and slew him.
Then he found another man, and said, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man smote him, so that in smiting he wounded him.
So the prophet departed, and waited for the king by the way, and disguised himself with ashes upon his face.

And as the king passed by, he cried unto the king: and he said, Thy servant went out into the midst of the battle; and, behold, a man turned aside, and brought a man unto me, and said, Keep this man: if by any means he be missing, then shall thy life be for his life, or else thou shalt pay a talent of silver.
And as thy servant was busy here and there, he was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.
And he hasted, and took the ashes away from his face; and the king of Israel discerned him that he was of the prophets.

And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
And the king of Israel went to his house heavy and displeased, and came to Samaria.

cases.name: Jezebel and Naboth's vineyard
cases.charge: Judicial murder to seize an inheritance
cases.summary: Ahab coveted Naboth's vineyard; Naboth would not sell his fathers' inheritance. Jezebel arranged false witnesses to accuse him of blaspheming God and the king, had him stoned, and handed the land to Ahab.
cases.offense: Naboth refused to sell or exchange his vineyard because it was the inheritance of his fathers (1 Kings 21:1-3). Ahab's desire for a garden did not extinguish the obligation by which Naboth held the land. The king withdrew in displeasure, and Jezebel promised to obtain what he had been refused. She wrote in Ahab's name, sealed the letters with his seal, and ordered a fast, an accusation by two false witnesses, and Naboth's execution (1 Kings 21:8-14). The elders obeyed. The outward form of judgment was made to serve a conclusion already chosen. Exodus 23:7 forbids slaying the innocent and righteous; the number of witnesses could not cleanse testimony known to be false.
cases.judgment: Ahab went down to take possession, and Elijah met him there with the question joining the crimes: had he killed and also taken possession (1 Kings 21:16-19)? The benefit of the murder stood beside the murder itself. Jezebel's management of the plot did not remove the king's responsibility for receiving its fruit. The Lord pronounced judgment upon Ahab, Jezebel, and their house. Ahab's humbling delayed the destruction of his house, but did not restore Naboth or approve the seizure (1 Kings 21:20-29). Later Joram's body was cast into Naboth's portion, and Jehu recalled the blood of Naboth and his sons (2 Kings 9:25-26). The stolen inheritance remained a witness against the royal house.

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things, that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

And Ahab spake unto Naboth, saying, Give me thy vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near unto my house: and I will give thee for it a better vineyard than it; or, if it seem good to thee, I will give thee the worth of it in money.
And Naboth said to Ahab, The Lord forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.

And Ahab came into his house heavy and displeased because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him: for he had said, I will not give thee the inheritance of my fathers. And he laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and would eat no bread.
So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters unto the elders and to the nobles that were in his city, dwelling with Naboth.
And she wrote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people:
And set two men, sons of Belial, before him, to bear witness against him, saying, Thou didst blaspheme God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him, that he may die.
And the men of his city, even the elders and the nobles who were the inhabitants in his city, did as Jezebel had sent unto them, and as it was written in the letters which she had sent unto them.
They proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people.

And there came in two men, children of Belial, and sat before him: and the men of Belial witnessed against him, even against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, Naboth did blaspheme God and the king. Then they carried him forth out of the city, and stoned him with stones, that he died.
And the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, which is in Samaria: behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, whither he is gone down to possess it.

And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.
And of Jezebel also spake the Lord, saying, The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.
And when Jehu was come to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; and she painted her face, and tired her head, and looked out at a window.
And as Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
And he lifted up his face to the window, and said, Who is on my side? who? And there looked out to him two or three eunuchs.
And he said, Throw her down. So they threw her down: and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses: and he trode her under foot.
And when he was come in, he did eat and drink, and said, Go, see now this cursed woman, and bury her: for she is a king’s daughter.
And they went to bury her: but they found no more of her than the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands.

Wherefore they came again, and told him. And he said, This is the word of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel:
And the carcase of Jezebel shall be as dung upon the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel; so that they shall not say, This is Jezebel.

entries.commentary: Naboth had a vineyard next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel, and Ahab asked to trade or buy it, offering a better vineyard or its worth in money. Naboth refused because the land was the inheritance of his fathers. He could not simply hand off an inheritance that was given to him. -

Ahab went home heavy and displeased, laid down on his bed, turned away his face, and would eat no bread. He threw a fit and sulked because he could not get his way, angry that a subject would not surrender his inheritance.

Jezebel came to Ahab and asked why his spirit was so sad that he would not eat, and he told her Naboth's refusal. Jezebel mocked his weakness, telling him he was king and should let his heart be merry, and she promised to get the vineyard of Naboth for him.

Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, sending them to the elders and nobles of Naboth's city. The seal was a signet, an official mark of the king's authority, so the letters carried royal weight as if Ahab himself had written them. She commanded them to proclaim a fast, set Naboth on high, and set two sons of Belial before him to bear false witness that he blasphemed God and the king, then stone him. This was evil counsel and a murderous plot. -

The elders and nobles obeyed Jezebel's letters, proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people. Two children of Belial, children of the devil, sat before Naboth and falsely witnessed that he had blasphemed God and the king. They carried Naboth out and stoned him to death, then sent word to Jezebel that he was dead.

When Jezebel heard Naboth was dead, she told Ahab to arise and take possession of the vineyard he had been refused. Ahab rose up and went down to take the vineyard. This is extortion, seizing what another has by violence and force. Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward. -

The word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite to go down and meet Ahab in the vineyard of Naboth. Elijah was to declare, Thus saith the Lord, hast thou killed and also taken possession, and in the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs would lick Ahab's own blood.

Ahab called Elijah his enemy, and Elijah answered that he had found him because Ahab had sold himself to work evil in the sight of the Lord. The Most High would bring evil on Ahab, cut off every male of his house, and make his house like the house of Jeroboam and the house of Baasha because of the provocation by which he made Israel to sin. The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely. -

The Most High declared that the dogs would eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Any of Ahab's house dying in the city the dogs would eat, and any dying in the field the fowls of the air would eat, matching the curses spoken in the law. -

There was none like Ahab, who sold himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, stirred up by Jezebel his wife. He did very abominably in following idols, as did the Amorites whom the Most High cast out before the children of Israel.

When Ahab heard these words he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth, fasted, and went softly, humbling himself before the Most High. Because Ahab humbled himself, the Most High told Elijah he would not bring the evil in Ahab's own days but would bring it upon his house in his son's days. The judgment was not cancelled but delayed and transferred to the next generation, showing that genuine humbling before the Most High moves his hand. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

cases.name: Micaiah the son of Imlah
cases.charge: What the Lord saith unto me, that will I speak; against four hundred prophets and two kings
cases.summary: Two kings sat in their robes at the gate of Samaria and four hundred prophets told them to go up and prosper. Jehoshaphat asked whether there was not one more. There was one, whom Ahab hated because he never prophesied good. The messenger who fetched him coached him to agree. He said he would speak what the Lord said, told them the truth, was struck on the face and sent to prison on bread and water until the king came back in peace. The king did not come back.
cases.offense: Four hundred prophets encouraged the expedition to Ramoth-gilead, and the messenger sent for Micaiah urged him to agree. His answer was settled before he entered the court: what the Lord said, he would speak (1 Kings 22:6, 13-14). Agreement with a multitude was not his commission. Before the enthroned kings he declared that Israel would be scattered like sheep without a shepherd. He also disclosed the vision of the lying spirit sent to persuade Ahab through his prophets (1 Kings 22:17-23). The warning reached the king before the battle. Ahab was not left without testimony against the pleasant answer he preferred.

Ahab was not left without testimony against the pleasant answer he preferred.

cases.name: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah, and the four hundred prophets
cases.charge: Prophesying victory at Ramoth-gilead by a lying spirit; smiting Micaiah on the cheek
cases.summary: Four hundred prophets told Ahab to go up and prosper. One, Micaiah, saw the Lord on his throne and a lying spirit sent into the mouths of the rest. Zedekiah struck him for it and asked which way the Spirit had gone. The battle answered for Ahab; scripture leaves Zedekiah hiding in an inner chamber.
cases.offense: Zedekiah made horns of iron and announced, in the Lord's name, that Ahab would push the Syrians until he consumed them. The other prophets agreed (1 Kings 22:11-12). The visible sign and united approval presented certainty without establishing that the Lord had sent the word. When Micaiah exposed the contrary purpose, Zedekiah struck him and demanded how the Spirit had passed from himself to Micaiah (1 Kings 22:24). He treated his own standing as proof against correction. The blow defended a claim of authority; it supplied no answer to the prophecy.
cases.judgment: Micaiah told him he would see when he went into an inner chamber to hide (1 Kings 22:25). The confidence displayed before the kings was set against an approaching need for concealment. Ahab died at Ramoth-gilead rather than consuming the Syrians as promised. Deuteronomy 18:22 identifies the unfulfilled word as one the Lord has not spoken. The failure of Zedekiah's promise exposed his presumption, although no subsequent account of his personal punishment is given. Iron horns, agreement, and violence could not make a false assurance stand against the Lord's judgment.
