verses.text: And Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben–hadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.
And the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and go, meet the man of God, and enquire of the Lord by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?

So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Ben–hadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the Lord hath shewed me that he shall surely die.
And he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept.

And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.
And Hazael said, But what, is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha answered, The Lord hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.
So he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, He told me that thou shouldest surely recover.
And it came to pass on the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
In those days the Lord began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel;
From Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron:
But I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which shall devour the palaces of Ben–hadad.

I will break also the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the plain of Aven, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of Eden: and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir, saith the Lord.
O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation.

I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
Howbeit he meaneth not so, neither doth his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy and cut off nations not a few.
Thou shalt not kill.

entries.commentary: Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him. They submit as his servants, and Jehu's second letter commands them to take the heads of Ahab's seventy sons and bring them to Jezreel by the next day. The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

Jehu meets the brethren of Ahaziah going to salute the king's children and has all forty-two of them slain at the pit of the shearing house, guilty by association with the house of Ahab. He takes up Jehonadab the son of Rechab, whose heart is right with his, into the chariot to see his zeal for the Most High. At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

Jehu gathers all the worshippers of Baal by pretending he will serve Baal much more than Ahab did, doing it in subtilty to destroy them. He fills the house of Baal, brings out vestments for every worshipper, and makes sure no servant of the Most High is among them, only Baal worshippers, as with the clergy garments and idolatry seen in false worship today. After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel. -

Though Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel, he does not depart from the golden calves that Jeroboam set up in Bethel and in Dan; hold Dan in mind for later scriptures. The Most High commends Jehu for executing what is right against the house of Ahab and promises his children to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel. Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin. -

In those days the Most High begins to cut Israel short, and Hazael smites them in all the coasts from Jordan eastward through Gilead and Bashan. The rest of Jehu's acts are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel, and he reigns twenty-eight years in Samaria before Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place. Jehu's life is a warning that the walk is a marathon, not a sprint, and the difference is whether a man gets back up and repents or stays down and departs from the law. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

Woe is pronounced on those who decree unrighteous decrees and write grievous laws to turn aside the needy from judgment and take away the right from the poor. That is us: we are the needy, we are the poor. Back then this was the Assyrians doing it to us because of our disobedience. Today it is your friendly neighborhood white man writing unrighteous laws and prescribing them for us to keep. It is a twofold prophecy. The unrighteous decrees rob the widows and the fatherless. The question is put to the oppressor: what will you do in the day of visitation and desolation, to whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory. Without the Most High they bow down under the prisoners and fall under the slain, for His anger is not turned away and His hand is stretched out still.

The Most High calls the Assyrian the rod of His anger, the staff in their hand His indignation. He used nations to punish us. He sends the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, the people of His wrath, to take the spoil and tread them down like the mire of the streets. The Most High calls us hypocrites because we love to say we love the Most High, but we do not want to do what the Bible says. The Assyrian did not mean it that way; it was in his heart to destroy and cut off nations. He boasted of the kingdoms he conquered and their idols, not realizing the Most High was using him to punish us and the rest of the nations. We had graven images throughout our land, breaking the Most High's laws.

When the Most High has finished His work on Zion and Jerusalem, He will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria and the glory of his high looks. The Assyrian said, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent," boasting that he removed the treasures and inhabitants of the people on his own. The Most High asks whether the axe boasts against the one who hews with it, or the saw magnifies itself against the one who shakes it. The Assyrian was only the axe; the Most High used him to cut us down from rulership to captivity. Therefore the Most High sends leanness among the fat ones and kindles a burning fire that devours the thorns and briers in one day and consumes the glory of the forest, both soul and body, until the trees are so few a child may write them.

In that day the remnant of Israel and those who escaped of the house of Jacob shall no more stay upon him that smote them, but stay upon the Most High, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. This is a future prophecy. "Stay" means to rely upon. Just like back then, we still rely upon the ones who smote us, even today under the nation of Edom, trusting in oppression, relying on the very ones still smiting us in the streets. In that day the remnant, those keeping the Most High's commandments in their right mind, will escape and stop leaning on the oppressor. Though Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall return. The Most High will make a consumption decreed and overflowing with righteousness in the midst of all the land. -

The Most High tells His people who dwell in Zion not to be afraid of the Assyrian who smites with a rod and lifts up his staff after the manner of Egypt, for in a very little while the indignation will cease and His anger will turn to their destruction. The Most High will stir up a scourge for the Assyrian, and his yoke shall be taken off Israel's neck and destroyed because of the anointing. The chapter traces the invader's march through the towns until he shakes his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion. Then the Most High of hosts lops the bough with terror, the high ones are hewn down, and Lebanon falls by a mighty one.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

cases.name: Jehu
cases.charge: Executing the house of Ahab, then keeping the calves of Jeroboam
cases.summary: Anointed to cut off the house of Ahab, Jehu killed Joram, Ahaziah, Jezebel, seventy sons of Ahab, and every worshipper of Baal in Samaria, and destroyed Baal out of Israel. But from the golden calves at Bethel and Dan Jehu departed not.
cases.offense: Jehu executed the judgment against Ahab's house and destroyed Baal's worship in Israel. Yet he did not depart from Jeroboam's calves at Bethel and Dan (2 Kings 10:28-29). His zeal removed one established evil while leaving another standing. He invited Jehonadab to see his zeal, but the final measure was whether he took heed to walk in the law with all his heart (2 Kings 10:16, 31). A public work of judgment was not a substitute for continuing obedience. The destruction of a rival house did not release the new king from the same commandments.
cases.judgment: The Lord acknowledged what Jehu had done rightly against Ahab and promised that his sons would sit upon Israel's throne to the fourth generation (2 Kings 10:30). The record preserves that reward beside the charge against the calves. Approval of one deed was not blanket approval of the reign. In those days Hazael began cutting Israel short. Jehu's line continued as promised, ending with Zechariah, who was murdered after six months (2 Kings 15:8-12). Hosea also pronounced the visiting of Jezreel's blood upon Jehu's house (Hosea 1:4). The dynasty's promised duration and its eventual reckoning stand together: a commission carried out did not make the house permanent or its bloodshed beyond examination.
offenseFull: Jehu executed the judgment against Ahab's house and destroyed Baal's worship in Israel. Yet he did not depart from Jeroboam's calves at Bethel and Dan (2 Kings 10:28-29). His zeal removed one established evil while leaving another standing.

He invited Jehonadab to see his zeal, but the final measure was whether he took heed to walk in the law with all his heart (2 Kings 10:16, 31). A public work of judgment was not a substitute for continuing obedience. The destruction of a rival house did not release the new king from the same commandments.
judgmentFull: The Lord acknowledged what Jehu had done rightly against Ahab and promised that his sons would sit upon Israel's throne to the fourth generation (2 Kings 10:30). The record preserves that reward beside the charge against the calves. Approval of one deed was not blanket approval of the reign.

In those days Hazael began cutting Israel short. Jehu's line continued as promised, ending with Zechariah, who was murdered after six months (2 Kings 15:8-12). Hosea also pronounced the visiting of Jezreel's blood upon Jehu's house (Hosea 1:4). The dynasty's promised duration and its eventual reckoning stand together: a commission carried out did not make the house permanent or its bloodshed beyond examination.

entries.commentary: Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him. They submit as his servants, and Jehu's second letter commands them to take the heads of Ahab's seventy sons and bring them to Jezreel by the next day. The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

Jehu meets the brethren of Ahaziah going to salute the king's children and has all forty-two of them slain at the pit of the shearing house, guilty by association with the house of Ahab. He takes up Jehonadab the son of Rechab, whose heart is right with his, into the chariot to see his zeal for the Most High. At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

Jehu gathers all the worshippers of Baal by pretending he will serve Baal much more than Ahab did, doing it in subtilty to destroy them. He fills the house of Baal, brings out vestments for every worshipper, and makes sure no servant of the Most High is among them, only Baal worshippers, as with the clergy garments and idolatry seen in false worship today. After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel. -

Though Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel, he does not depart from the golden calves that Jeroboam set up in Bethel and in Dan; hold Dan in mind for later scriptures. The Most High commends Jehu for executing what is right against the house of Ahab and promises his children to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel. Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin. -

In those days the Most High begins to cut Israel short, and Hazael smites them in all the coasts from Jordan eastward through Gilead and Bashan. The rest of Jehu's acts are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel, and he reigns twenty-eight years in Samaria before Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place. Jehu's life is a warning that the walk is a marathon, not a sprint, and the difference is whether a man gets back up and repents or stays down and departs from the law. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
The word of the Lord came unto Hosea the son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

The Lord tells Hosea to go take a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms, for the land has committed great whoredom, departing from the Lord. He took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, who conceived and bare him a son. He took a whore because it was symbolic of how the people committed spiritual fornication against the Most High.

The Lord tells him to call his name Jezreel, for in a little while he will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu and cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel. At that day he will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.

She conceives again and bears a daughter, named Loruhamah, meaning no more mercy upon the house of Israel, for he will utterly take them away. But he will have mercy upon the house of Judah and save them by the Lord their God, not by bow, nor sword, nor battle, nor horses, nor horsemen.
When she had weaned Loruhamah she conceived and bare a son, named Loammi, meaning ye are not my people and I will not be your God.

Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered, and in the place where it was said they are not my people, there it shall be said they are the sons of the living God. The blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans are the ones whose number is as the sand of the sea, not the so-called white man that calls himself a Jew. The so-called white people as a whole are the minority; they do not reproduce at the rate that other nations do, especially the children of Israel. Because they cannot keep up with the numbers, they come up with tactics to stop other people from reproducing. That is one sign right there that they are not the people of God, for God's people are as the sand of the sea, not the minority.

Then the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, both the northern and southern kingdoms, and appoint themselves one head, and come up out of the land, for great shall be the day of Jezreel. We come together under God's laws and appoint ourselves one head, which is Christ. We do not need any other nation to put a stamp on it, because we already know we are the children of God.

Azariah, also called Uzziah, begins to reign over Judah and does that which is right in the sight of the Most High as his father Amaziah had done. The high places were not removed, so the people still sacrificed and burned incense there, an incomplete obedience. The Most High smote him so that he was a leper until his death, and he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people. Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to [2 Chronicles 26](/bible/2-chronicles/26) for a more detailed account of his life and acts. -

Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel only six months and does that which is evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Shallum conspires against Zachariah, smites him before the people, slays him, and reigns in his place. The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation. -

Shallum reigns a full month in Samaria before Menahem son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah, smites him, and reigns in his stead. Menahem strikes Tiphsah and its coasts because they would not open to him, and he ripped up the women with child, a mark of his cruelty.

Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand. Menahem raises the tribute by exacting fifty shekels of silver from each mighty man of wealth, so the king of Assyria turns back and does not stay in the land.

Pekahiah son of Menahem reigns two years over Israel and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pekah, a captain of his, conspires against him and smites him in the king's house at Samaria with fifty Gileadites, then reigns in his room. This is a military coup, where a trusted captain kills the king and seizes the throne.

Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years over Israel, the same Pekah spoken of in the book of Isaiah. In his days Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and takes Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, carrying them captive to Assyria. Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, smites and slays him, and reigns in his stead.

Jotham son of Uzziah reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem and does that which is right, according to all his father Uzziah had done. Again the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. Jotham builds the higher gate of the house of the Most High. In those days the Most High begins to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

verses.text: And he arose, and went into the house; and he poured the oil on his head, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed thee king over the people of the Lord, even over Israel.
And thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the Lord, at the hand of Jezebel.
For the whole house of Ahab shall perish: and I will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel:
And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah:
And the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her. And he opened the door, and fled.
So Jehu slew all that remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, and his kinsfolks, and his priests, until he left him none remaining.
Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
Howbeit from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, Jehu departed not from after them, to wit, the golden calves that were in Beth–el, and that were in Dan.

And the Lord said unto Jehu, Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.
But Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart: for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, which made Israel to sin.
In those days the Lord began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel;
From Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
And the Lord said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.

cases.name: Athaliah
cases.charge: Destroying the seed royal of Judah; usurping the throne
cases.summary: Ahab's daughter, married into Judah's line, saw her son Ahaziah dead at Jehu's hand and murdered all the seed royal to reign herself. One infant, Joash, was hidden in the house of the Lord for six years. In the seventh, Jehoiada the priest brought him out.
cases.offense: When Ahaziah died, Athaliah rose against the royal seed and seized the kingdom. Jehosheba rescued Joash and hid him with his nurse, preserving a child from the destruction (2 Kings 11:1-3). Athaliah's possession of the throne rested upon violence against the house she should have protected. Her reign also belonged to the corruption of worship. Her sons had broken up God's house and devoted its things to Baalim (2 Chronicles 24:7). The seizure of the kingdom and misuse of holy possessions joined the same disregard for what had been entrusted to the royal house.
cases.judgment: In the seventh year Jehoiada revealed the king's son, arranged his protection, and crowned him with the testimony. Athaliah heard the rejoicing and cried treason when she saw him standing in his place (2 Kings 11:4-14). The cry came from the ruler whose own position had been obtained by destroying the succession. Jehoiada ordered her taken outside rather than killed within the Lord's house. She was slain by the way leading to the king's house, and the people broke down Baal's house (2 Kings 11:15-18). The covenant was renewed, the people rejoiced, and the city was quiet. The hidden child outlasted the reign that had sought to erase him.
offenseFull: When Ahaziah died, Athaliah rose against the royal seed and seized the kingdom. Jehosheba rescued Joash and hid him with his nurse, preserving a child from the destruction (2 Kings 11:1-3). Athaliah's possession of the throne rested upon violence against the house she should have protected.

Her reign also belonged to the corruption of worship. Her sons had broken up God's house and devoted its things to Baalim (2 Chronicles 24:7). The seizure of the kingdom and misuse of holy possessions joined the same disregard for what had been entrusted to the royal house.
judgmentFull: In the seventh year Jehoiada revealed the king's son, arranged his protection, and crowned him with the testimony. Athaliah heard the rejoicing and cried treason when she saw him standing in his place (2 Kings 11:4-14). The cry came from the ruler whose own position had been obtained by destroying the succession.

Jehoiada ordered her taken outside rather than killed within the Lord's house. She was slain by the way leading to the king's house, and the people broke down Baal's house (2 Kings 11:15-18). The covenant was renewed, the people rejoiced, and the city was quiet. The hidden child outlasted the reign that had sought to erase him.

verses.text: And when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons which were slain; and they hid him, even him and his nurse, in the bedchamber from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
And he was with her hid in the house of the Lord six years. And Athaliah did reign over the land.
And when Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she came to the people into the temple of the Lord.

And when she looked, behold, the king stood by a pillar, as the manner was, and the princes and the trumpeters by the king, and all the people of the land rejoiced, and blew with trumpets: and Athaliah rent her clothes, and cried, Treason, Treason.

But Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of the hundreds, the officers of the host, and said unto them, Have her forth without the ranges: and him that followeth her kill with the sword. For the priest had said, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord.
And they laid hands on her; and she went by the way by the which the horses came into the king’s house: and there was she slain.
But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not.
And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land.
Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people into the house of the Lord:

And she looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason.

Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds that were set over the host, and said unto them, Have her forth of the ranges: and whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the Lord.
So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house, they slew her there.
For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the Lord did they bestow upon Baalim.
Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, as did the house of Ahab: for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.

entries.commentary: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw her son was dead, she moved to destroy all the royal seed so she could seize the throne. Jehosheba, sister of Ahaziah, took the infant Joash and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain, hiding him in the house of the Most High for six years while Athaliah reigned. The rightful king was preserved and concealed the entire time the usurper sat on the throne.

In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest brought the captains together, took an oath of them in the house of the Most High, and showed them the king's son. He commanded them how to guard the king by watches and companies so that the house would not be broken down. The guard was to compass the king round about, every man with his weapon in his hand, and to stay with him as he went out and came in. -
Every man stood armed around the king, and any who came within the ranges was to be slain.

The captains did according to all that Jehoiada commanded, taking their men to the priest. Jehoiada gave the captains King David's spears and shields that were in the temple, and the guard stood every man with his weapons in hand around the king. Then he brought forth the king's son, put the crown upon him, gave him the testimony, anointed him, and the people clapped their hands and said, God save the king. The weapons they carried then were physical; today the weapon of Israel is the scriptures.

Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and the people and came into the temple, and saw the king standing by a pillar as the manner was. She rent her clothes and cried, Treason, treason, but Jehoiada commanded the captains to have her forth outside the ranges. She was not to be slain in the house of the Most High, so they took her out by the way the horses came into the king's house and slew her there.

Jehoiada made a covenant between the Most High, the king, and the people, that they should be the Lord's people. All the people went to the house of Baal, broke down its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. Joash was brought to the throne, the people rejoiced, the city was quiet, and he was seven years old when he began to reign. This same covenant is what happens today: as a person wakes up, repents, keeps the commandments, and comes out of idolatry, they again become the Lord's people.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his stead, for the band of Arabians had slain all the elder sons. Ahaziah was forty and two years old when he began to reign and reigned one year in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, and the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father died, to his destruction. This is a warning against being ruled by the wrong counsel: instead of going to the priests and the judges, he went to his mother, and she counselled him into ruin. A woman with a grudge can rule a kingdom through her son, and that is what Athaliah did.

Ahaziah walked after their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Jehoram was wounded. He went down to see the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel, and the destruction of Ahaziah was of the Most High, for by going he came into the path of Jehu, whom the Most High had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. That same Jehu who killed the seventy sons of Ahab found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brethren and slew them, then sought and caught Ahaziah, who was hid in Samaria. They buried Ahaziah for the sake of Jehoshaphat his forefather who sought the Most High with all his heart; but the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep the kingdom, so the wicked king was cut off by the same hand the Most High anointed to avenge Israel.

When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah, killing the king's sons. But Jehoshabeath the daughter of king Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, hiding him and his nurse in a bedchamber. She hid the child in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned over the land, showing that Athaliah was ruling in the position of the son she had lost. Athaliah did not carry out this slaughter alone; she had weak men helping her run over everything, which is how she seized and held the throne.

In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the captains of hundreds into covenant with him, and they gathered the Levites and the chief of the fathers out of all the cities of Judah to Jerusalem. The congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God, and Jehoiada declared that the king's son should reign, as the Most High had said of the sons of David. He set his plan: a third part of the priests and Levites to keep the doors, a third at the king's house, and a third at the gate of the foundation, with all the people in the courts. None but the priests and ministering Levites were to enter the house of the Most High, and the Levites were to compass the king round about, every man with his weapon, and put to death any who forced their way in.

The Levites and all Judah did according to all Jehoiada commanded, each man keeping his company, for Jehoiada did not dismiss the courses of the Levites but kept them at their work with security added for the king. Jehoiada delivered to the captains the spears and shields that had been king David's, kept in the house of God, and set every man with his weapon from one side of the temple to the other, round about the king. They brought out the king's son, put the crown upon him, gave him the testimony, and made him king, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, God save the king. This was done by the proper custom: a priest anoints the king, as Samuel the priest anointed Saul and then David; so Jehoiada the priest anointed Joash.

When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came into the house of the Most High and saw the king standing at his pillar with the princes, trumpets, and singers rejoicing. She rent her clothes and cried, Treason, treason, but her cry came too late, for the covenant was already made and the true king was crowned. Jehoiada commanded the captains to have her forth from the ranges and to slay any that followed her, but not to slay her in the house of the Most High. They laid hands on her, brought her to the entering of the horse gate by the king's house, and slew her there, ending the reign of the woman who had killed the seed royal.

Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they should be the Most High's people, and the people went to the house of Baal, broke it down, brake its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal. Jehoiada appointed the officers of the house of the Most High by the hand of the priests and Levites whom David had distributed, to offer burnt offerings with rejoicing and singing as ordained by David. He set the porters at the gates so that none unclean in anything should enter, then brought the king down and set him upon the throne of the kingdom, and the people rejoiced and the city was quiet. Before a king is set in his position he is under tutors and governors; young Joash was king in rank, yet he was still a learner under Jehoiada, for even kings had to be taught. Athaliah had no place ruling Israel; being the king's mother did not make her the ruler. -

Joash was seven years old when he began to reign and reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba. Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days of Jehoiada the priest, because that is what he was taught. He had seen the wicked men of Israel try to kill him, so he followed the man who showed him the ropes; Jehoiada taught him how to be a righteous king and keep the commandments. A king had a job to do and could not simply sit back; he had a kingdom to watch over, and he had the priests there to help him do it.

Joash was minded to repair the house of the Most High and gathered the priests and Levites, telling them to go to the cities of Judah and gather money of all Israel to repair the house from year to year, and to hasten the matter. The Levites did not hasten it, so the king called Jehoiada the chief and asked why he had not required of the Levites the collection appointed by Moses for the tabernacle of witness. Money was needed because Israel did not let the workmen labor for nothing; when men did the jobs they were paid, for the workman is worthy of his hire, and we dealt righteously with our people. The sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God and bestowed all its dedicated things upon Baalim, which is why so much repair was needed.

At the king's commandment they made a chest and set it at the gate of the house of the Most High, and made a proclamation to bring in the collection Moses laid upon Israel in the wilderness, and the princes and people rejoiced and cast in until they made an end. Day by day the king's scribe and the high priest's officer emptied the chest and gathered money in abundance, and the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work, hiring masons, carpenters, and workers of iron and brass. Money was a defense here because it paid the skilled brothers who got the temple work done; we must deal righteously with our people today, treating a brother's business as a place to help the family and the body. Not everyone was given the same task; masons, carpenters, and metalworkers each had their charge, and every man had to listen to a manager, for business requires order and submission to authority. The workmen perfected the work and set the house of God in its state, then brought the rest of the money to make vessels of gold and silver to minister and offer with, and they offered burnt offerings continually all the days of Jehoiada. -

Jehoiada waxed old and was full of days and died, being a hundred and thirty years old at his death. They buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel both toward the Most High and toward his house. That a priest was buried among the kings shows how much respect and diligence this man had earned; his faithfulness set him alongside the rulers of the land.

After the death of Jehoiada the princes of Judah came and made obeisance to the king, and the king hearkened to them. They left the house of the Most High and served groves and idols, and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for their trespass. The Most High sent prophets to bring them again unto Him, and they testified against them, but the people would not give ear. As soon as Jehoiada died, Israel went off again, because the king was weak and started listening to those who served other gods; this teaches the lesson that lust drives Israel to idolatry, and that the Most High will always send prophets to warn them.

The spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood above the people and asked why they transgressed the commandments so that they could not prosper, telling them that because they had forsaken the Most High, He had also forsaken them. They conspired against Zechariah and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king, in the court of the house of the Most High. When the prophet came to correct the king, the king had him killed for telling him the truth; this is the same spirit our people show when a laborer brings the medicine and is met with violence. As Zechariah died he said, The Most High look upon it and require it. He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture; it is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people. -

At the end of the year the host of Syria came up against Joash, destroyed the princes of the people, and sent the spoil to the king of Damascus. The Syrians came with a small company, yet the Most High delivered a very great host of Judah into their hand, because Judah had forsaken the Most High God of their fathers; so judgment was executed on Joash for killing Zechariah. They left Joash in great diseases, and his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada and slew him on his bed, and he was buried in the city of David but not in the sepulchres of the kings. Joash began by doing right under Jehoiada's guidance, repairing the house and clearing out the idols, but none of that was remembered in the end because of the wickedness he turned to after being warned. Amaziah his son reigned in his stead; the fuller record of Joash is written in the story of the book of the kings. -

Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

cases.name: Jeroboam the son of Joash
cases.charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord; not departing from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
cases.summary: Jeroboam the son of Joash reigned forty-one years over Israel and restored the coast from Hamath to the sea of the plain, as the Lord had spoken by Jonah the prophet. The Lord saw that Israel’s affliction was bitter and saved them by his hand, yet Jeroboam did evil and departed not from Jeroboam’s sins.
cases.offense: Jeroboam the son of Joash began to reign in the fifteenth year of Amaziah and reigned forty-one years in Samaria. He did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin (2 Kings 14:23–24). The longest reign of any northern king carried no reform with it. He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the Lord spoken by the hand of his servant Jonah the son of Amittai (2 Kings 14:25). The restoration was accomplished through him, yet it was the Lord’s doing, because the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter: there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel (2 Kings 14:26).
cases.judgment: The Lord said not that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven but saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash (2 Kings 14:27). The deliverance was not because of Jeroboam’s righteousness but because of the Lord’s mercy toward His afflicted people. Jeroboam slept with his fathers, and Zechariah his son reigned in his stead (2 Kings 14:29). The prosperity of his reign did not secure his house: Zechariah was slain after six months, fulfilling the word that Jehu’s house would sit on the throne unto the fourth generation (2 Kings 15:12). The kingdom was saved through an evil king and then taken from his descendants according to a limit already spoken.

verses.text: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty and one years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gath–hepher.
For the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter: for there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel.
And the Lord said not that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven: but he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.

Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel; and Zachariah his son reigned in his stead.

entries.commentary: Amaziah the son of Joash began to reign over Judah at twenty-five and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High, yet not like David his father, meaning he did not serve with a perfect heart. When the kingdom was confirmed, he slew the servants who had killed his father, but did not slay their children, according to the law of Moses that every man is put to death for his own sin. -
Amaziah slew ten thousand of Edom in the valley of salt and took Selah by war, calling its name Joktheel unto this day.

Amaziah sent to Jehoash king of Israel to face one another in battle, and Jehoash answered with the parable of the thistle and the cedar, warning him to stay home lest he fall. Amaziah would not hear, so the two faced one another at Bethshemesh, and Judah was put to the worse before Israel and fled. Jehoash broke down the wall of Jerusalem, took the gold, silver, and vessels from the house of the Most High and the king's house, took hostages, and returned to Samaria.

Jehoash slept with his fathers and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place. Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash, and a conspiracy was made against him in Jerusalem so that he fled to Lachish and was slain there. The people took Azariah, sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.

Jeroboam the son of Joash, Jeroboam II, began to reign over Israel and reigned forty-one years, doing evil and not departing from the sins of the first Jeroboam. He restored the coast of Israel according to the word spoken by Jonah the son of Amittai, for the Most High saw the bitter affliction of Israel and would not blot out their name. The Most High saved them by the hand of Jeroboam, who recovered Damascus and Hamath, and when he slept with his fathers Zechariah his son reigned in his place. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

cases.name: Hosea the prophet
cases.charge: Obeying the Lord’s command to take a wife of whoredoms as a sign; prophesying Israel’s scattering and restoration
cases.summary: The word of the Lord came to Hosea in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, and of Jeroboam the son of Joash. He was commanded to marry Gomer, a wife of whoredoms, as a living sign of how Israel committed spiritual fornication against the Lord. Three children bore prophetic names—Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi—yet the promise followed: the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea.
cases.offense: The Lord told Hosea to go take a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms, for the land had committed great whoredom, departing from the Lord. So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim (Hosea 1:2–3). The prophet’s own household became the picture of the nation’s unfaithfulness. Three children were born, each named by the Lord’s word. Jezreel: the Lord would avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu and cause to cease the kingdom of Israel (Hosea 1:4). Lo-ruhamah: the Lord would no more have mercy upon the house of Israel but utterly take them away (Hosea 1:6). Lo-ammi: ye are not my people and I will not be your God (Hosea 1:9). The names declared scattering, the withdrawal of mercy, and the severing of the covenant. Yet the promise followed: the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered, and in the place where it was said, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said, Ye are the sons of the living God (Hosea 1:10). They would be gathered under one head (Hosea 1:11).
cases.judgment: The Lord commanded Hosea again to love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress, according to the love of the Lord toward the children of Israel. He bought her for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a half of barley and told her to abide many days (Hosea 3:1–3). For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, without a prince, without a sacrifice, without an image, without an ephod, and without teraphim. Afterward shall the children of Israel return and seek the Lord their God, and David their king, and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days (Hosea 3:4–5). The long dispersion would end in a return.

cases.name: Menahem king of Israel
cases.charge: Ripping up the women with child at Tiphsah, and buying Assyria with money exacted from Israel
cases.summary: Menahem came up from Tirzah, killed Shallum, and took the throne. When Tiphsah would not open to him he smote it and ripped up all the women therein that were with child. He then paid Pul a thousand talents of silver, exacted from the wealthy of Israel, to confirm the kingdom in his hand — and died in his bed.
cases.offense: Menahem struck Tiphsah because it would not open to him and ripped up its pregnant women (2 Kings 15:16). The refusal of entry became an occasion for cruelty against those least able to resist. His rise did not bring a departure from Jeroboam's sins; he continued in them throughout his reign (2 Kings 15:17-18). When Pul of Assyria came, Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand. He exacted the money from Israel's wealthy men (2 Kings 15:19-20). The people paid for the foreign support by which their ruler sought to secure his own position.
cases.judgment: Assyria withdrew, and Menahem died after a ten-year reign, with Pekahiah succeeding him (2 Kings 15:20-22). No separate personal penalty is recorded against him. The successful payment must not be mistaken for a judgment declaring his cruelty righteous. His son's reign lasted two years before Pekah killed him. Further Assyrian conquest and deportation followed in Pekah's days (2 Kings 15:23-29). The support purchased for Menahem did not establish lasting security for the house or nation. He had obtained time on the throne without addressing the sin that left Israel exposed to further overthrow.

The refusal of entry became an occasion for cruelty against those least able to resist. His rise did not bring a departure from Jeroboam's sins; he continued in them throughout his reign (2 Kings 15:17-18).

When Pul of Assyria came, Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand. He exacted the money from Israel's wealthy men (2 Kings 15:19-20). The people paid for the foreign support by which their ruler sought to secure his own position.

His son's reign lasted two years before Pekah killed him. Further Assyrian conquest and deportation followed in Pekah's days (2 Kings 15:23-29). The support purchased for Menahem did not establish lasting security for the house or nation. He had obtained time on the throne without addressing the sin that left Israel exposed to further overthrow.

verses.text: For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Then Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all that were therein, and the coasts thereof from Tirzah: because they opened not to him, therefore he smote it; and all the women therein that were with child he ripped up.
In the nine and thirtieth year of Azariah king of Judah began Menahem the son of Gadi to reign over Israel, and reigned ten years in Samaria.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
And Pul the king of Assyria came against the land: and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

And Menahem exacted the money of Israel, even of all the mighty men of wealth, of each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and stayed not there in the land.
And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Menahem slept with his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his stead.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,
Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up.

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border:

entries.commentary: Azariah, also called Uzziah, begins to reign over Judah and does that which is right in the sight of the Most High as his father Amaziah had done. The high places were not removed, so the people still sacrificed and burned incense there, an incomplete obedience. The Most High smote him so that he was a leper until his death, and he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people. Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to [2 Chronicles 26](/bible/2-chronicles/26) for a more detailed account of his life and acts. -

Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel only six months and does that which is evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Shallum conspires against Zachariah, smites him before the people, slays him, and reigns in his place. The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation. -

Shallum reigns a full month in Samaria before Menahem son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah, smites him, and reigns in his stead. Menahem strikes Tiphsah and its coasts because they would not open to him, and he ripped up the women with child, a mark of his cruelty.

Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand. Menahem raises the tribute by exacting fifty shekels of silver from each mighty man of wealth, so the king of Assyria turns back and does not stay in the land.

Pekahiah son of Menahem reigns two years over Israel and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam. Pekah, a captain of his, conspires against him and smites him in the king's house at Samaria with fifty Gileadites, then reigns in his room. This is a military coup, where a trusted captain kills the king and seizes the throne.

Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years over Israel, the same Pekah spoken of in the book of Isaiah. In his days Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and takes Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, carrying them captive to Assyria. Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, smites and slays him, and reigns in his stead.

Jotham son of Uzziah reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem and does that which is right, according to all his father Uzziah had done. Again the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. Jotham builds the higher gate of the house of the Most High. In those days the Most High begins to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

Hoshea son of Elah reigns nine years over Israel in Samaria and does evil, though not as the kings before him. Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up, and Hoshea becomes his servant and pays tribute. The king of Assyria finds conspiracy in Hoshea because he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped his yearly tribute, so he shuts him up in prison. Assyria besieges Samaria three years, then in the ninth year of Hoshea takes it and carries Israel away to Assyria, placing them in Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes.

This captivity comes because the children of Israel sinned against the Most High who brought them out of Egypt and feared other gods. They walked in the statutes of the heathen, built high places in all their cities, and set up images and groves on every high hill and under every green tree. They wrought wicked things to provoke the Most High and served idols, though He had said plainly, ye shall not do this thing. -

The Most High testified against Israel and Judah by all the prophets and seers, calling them to turn from evil and keep His commandments. They would not hear but hardened their necks like their fathers who did not believe in the Most High. To believe in the Most High is to take heed to the commandments, so those who claim belief while breaking the commandments do not truly believe. They rejected His statutes and covenant, followed vanity, made molten images and two calves, worshipped the host of heaven, and served Baal. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil. -

The Most High is very angry and removes Israel out of His sight, leaving only the tribe of Judah. Judah also fails to keep the commandments and walks in the statutes that Israel made. The Most High rejects all the seed of Israel, afflicts them, and delivers them into the hand of spoilers until He casts them out of His sight. This rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, which resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there. -

The king of Assyria brings men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim to dwell in the cities of Samaria in Israel's place. Because they do not fear the Most High, He sends lions among them that slay some of them. One of the carried-away priests is brought back to Bethel to teach the settlers how they should fear the Most High.

Every nation makes gods of its own and sets them in the houses of the high places the Samaritans had made. The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, Cuth made Nergal, Hamath made Ashima, the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burnt their children to Adrammelech and Anammelech. They feared the Most High and also served their own gods after the manner of the nations they came from. The Most High made His covenant and charged the children of Jacob whom He named Israel, showing the covenant belongs to Israel and not to all nations.

The Most High commanded Israel not to fear, bow to, serve, or sacrifice to other gods, but to fear and worship Him alone who brought them out of Egypt with a stretched out arm. They were to observe His statutes, ordinances, and commandments forevermore, and He would deliver them out of the hand of all their enemies. No nation and no treaty can redeem Israel from their condition, only turning to the Most High can. These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations. -
When Ephraim spake trembling, he exalted himself in Israel, but when he offended in Baal, he died.

Now they sin more and more and have made them molten images of their silver, idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen; they say of them, Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time; the craftsman was making idols in the images of men. -
Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.
Yet the Most High is the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no god but him, for there is no saviour beside him.

He knew them in the wilderness, in the land of great drought. According to their pasture they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore they forgot him. That is what happens to us; when we get all the things we need, our food, water, and clothing, and a little excess, we forget the Lord.

Therefore he will be unto them as a lion, as a leopard by the way will he observe them; he will meet them as a bear bereaved of her whelps, rend the caul of their heart, and there devour them like a lion; the wild beast shall tear them.
O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself, but in the Most High is thine help.

He will be thy king; where is any other that may save thee in all thy cities, and thy judges of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes? The Lord is telling us there is none that saveth but him. -
He gave thee a king in his anger and took him away in his wrath.

cases.name: Hoshea, last king of Israel
cases.charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord; conspiring with Egypt against Assyria
cases.summary: Hoshea the son of Elah, last king of the northern kingdom, did evil though not as the kings before him. He became tributary to Assyria, then conspired with So king of Egypt and withheld tribute. Shalmaneser shut him in prison, besieged Samaria three years, and carried Israel away to Assyria.
cases.offense: Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign in the twelfth year of Ahaz and reigned nine years in Samaria. He did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him (2 Kings 17:1–2). The qualification does not excuse his reign; it measures how far the standard had fallen when the best that could be said of a king was that he was less evil than his predecessors. Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against him, and Hoshea became his servant and paid tribute. But the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and brought no present as he had done year by year (2 Kings 17:3–4). Instead of turning to the Lord, Hoshea turned to Egypt, the very nation from which the Lord had brought Israel out.
cases.judgment: The king of Assyria shut Hoshea up and bound him in prison. He came up throughout all the land and besieged Samaria three years. In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away, placing them in Halah, in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes (2 Kings 17:4–6). The northern kingdom ceased to exist. The Lord removed Israel out of His sight, as He had said by all His servants the prophets (2 Kings 17:23). Every warning through every prophet sent to the northern kingdom was fulfilled in a single removal. The accumulated sin from Jeroboam through Hoshea was answered in captivity, and the tribes were scattered among the nations.

verses.text: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him.

cases.name: The captivity of Israel (the northern kingdom)
cases.charge: Two centuries of the sins of Jeroboam; secret sins; idols, high places, and children through the fire
cases.summary: Second Kings 17 is the indictment of a nation: they feared other gods, walked in the statutes of the heathen and of the kings of Israel, built high places in every city, served idols the Lord had said they should not, made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil.
cases.offense: Hoshea's conspiracy and withheld tribute occasioned Assyria's siege, but the account gives a deeper cause for Israel's removal: they sinned against the Lord who brought them out of Egypt and feared other gods (2 Kings 17:3-8). Political events carried a judgment rooted in the covenant they had forsaken. The Lord repeatedly sent prophets and seers to call them back to his statutes. They refused, hardened their necks, followed vanity, and continued the calves, Baal worship, divination, and the burning of their children (2 Kings 17:13-17). Repetition of warning was evidence of mercy; repetition of refusal made the guilt no less deliberate.
cases.judgment: Samaria fell after a three-year siege. Israel was carried to Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes (2 Kings 17:5-6). The land from which their fathers had driven other worships no longer protected them while they practised those same departures. Assyria brought other peoples to dwell in the cities. Their mixture of reverence for the Lord and service to their own images did not fulfil the command to serve him alone (2 Kings 17:24-41). The account also warns that Judah had failed to keep the commandments (2 Kings 17:19). The northern kingdom's fall was not permission for the southern kingdom to presume upon its own continued place.
