cases.name: Nineveh under Jonah
cases.charge: Wickedness come up before the Lord
cases.summary: Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least; the king rose from his throne, sat in ashes, and decreed that man and beast cry mightily unto God and turn from the violence in their hands.
cases.offense: Nineveh's wickedness had come up before the Lord. Jonah entered the city and announced that it would be overthrown in forty days. The king's own proclamation identified the needed change: each person was to turn from his evil way and from the violence in his hands. The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth. The king rose from his throne, laid aside his robe, and sat in ashes. His command joined crying mightily to God with abandoning violence. The outward humiliation was to accompany an actual change in conduct.
cases.judgment: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way, and did not bring the announced evil upon them. Their deliverance was not credited to Nineveh's power, wealth, or former standing, but to repentance before the God who had warned them. Christ later declared that the men of Nineveh would rise in judgment against a generation that refused a greater witness than Jonah. Their response exposes the guilt of hearing God's warning without turning. A threatened judgment can be an opportunity for mercy when those who hear it believe and amend their ways.
offenseFull: Nineveh's wickedness had come up before the Lord. Jonah entered the city and announced that it would be overthrown in forty days. The king's own proclamation identified the needed change: each person was to turn from his evil way and from the violence in his hands.

The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth. The king rose from his throne, laid aside his robe, and sat in ashes. His command joined crying mightily to God with abandoning violence. The outward humiliation was to accompany an actual change in conduct.
judgmentFull: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way, and did not bring the announced evil upon them. Their deliverance was not credited to Nineveh's power, wealth, or former standing, but to repentance before the God who had warned them.

Christ later declared that the men of Nineveh would rise in judgment against a generation that refused a greater witness than Jonah. Their response exposes the guilt of hearing God's warning without turning. A threatened judgment can be an opportunity for mercy when those who hear it believe and amend their ways.

verses.text: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
And Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:
But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?
And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.
And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it;
If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.
The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.
The men of Nineve shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

entries.commentary: The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me. But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, went down to Joppa, found a ship going to Tarshish, paid the fare thereof, and went down into it.

The Lord sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest, so that the ship was like to be broken. The mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares into the sea; but Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship, and lay, and was fast asleep. They cast lots to know for whose cause this evil was upon them, and the lot fell upon Jonah. He answered them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land. Then were the men exceedingly afraid, for they knew that he fled from the presence of the Lord.

Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you. The men rowed hard to bring it to the land, but they could not, for the sea wrought and was tempestuous against them. They cried unto the Lord, Lay not upon us innocent blood; then they took up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from her raging, and the men feared the Lord exceedingly. Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time, saying, Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee. Jonah arose and went unto Nineveh according to the word of the Lord; and he cried, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

The people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. The king arose from his throne, laid his robe from him, covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes, and made the decree that neither man nor beast taste anything, but be covered with sackcloth and cry mightily unto God. Let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands. God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil that he had said that he would do unto them, and he did it not.

It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry. He said, Was not this my saying when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil. Take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live. Then said the Lord, Doest thou well to be angry? Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.

The Lord God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, to be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief; so Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd. God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered; and he prepared a vehement east wind, and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted. Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow, which came up in a night, and perished in a night. And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle? --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)
The disciples pluck the ears of corn on the sabbath being an hungred, and the Pharisees accuse them of doing that which is not lawful.
Christ answers with what David did: he entered the house of God and ate the shewbread, which was lawful only for the priests, because he was not of Levi.

The priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless, because the service itself is commanded. If ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. The Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

A man with a withered hand is set before him to see whether he would heal on the sabbath, that they might accuse him. A man will lift his own sheep out of a pit on the sabbath day, and a man is better than a sheep. Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. The distinction is between what falls out and what is planned. A sheep does not fall into a pit by appointment, and spilt milk is cleaned up when it happens. Wilful sin is the thing thought out beforehand.
The hand is restored whole, like as the other.

The Pharisees hold a council how they might destroy him, and he withdraws himself and heals the multitudes, charging them not to make him known. This too was written beforehand: behold my servant, whom I have chosen, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

One possessed with a devil, blind and dumb, is healed, and the people ask, Is not this the son of David? The Pharisees answer that he casts out devils by Beelzebub, saying his power came from the devil.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan cast out Satan, his kingdom cannot stand. By whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they shall be your judges. No man enters a strong man's house and spoils his goods except he first bind the strong man. The binding is the taking away of his understanding; then his house can be spoiled.
He that is not with me is against me, and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.

All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men, but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven. The Holy Ghost is bound to the law, so speaking against it is not only with the mouth. Going back into the world and back into the ways that were left is a man's actions speaking for him.

The tree is known by his fruit, and a man is known by what he brings forth and by those he teaches. Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh, and every idle word that men shall speak they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

The scribes and Pharisees ask for a sign, and no sign is given but the sign of the prophet Jonas: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and the queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. These men had a greater than both standing in front of them and would not hear.

The unclean spirit returns to a house swept and garnished and brings seven others more wicked than himself, and the last state of that man is worse than the first. That is the end of turning back after knowing.

Who is my mother, and who are my brethren? Whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother. This does not unmake a man's natural family. It names a second family, made of those keeping the laws of the Most High.
Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples. He gives them the words: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

The friend at midnight will not rise because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth. Importunity is persistence to the point of annoyance. The man kept knocking, and the man inside gave him enough that he would not come back.

Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. The parable before it is the point: prayer is not said once and left. There is persistence in it, and there is action behind it, because the man in the parable was standing at the door. If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
He casts out a devil, and it was dumb, and when the devil was gone out the dumb spake, and the people wondered. Others said he cast out devils through Beelzebub.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges. But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace; but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, he taketh from him all his armour and divideth his spoils. He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

The unclean spirit returns and finds the house swept and garnished, and takes seven other spirits more wicked than himself. The house was clean and empty. There was no stronger one dwelling in it, and that is why what came back could enter, and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
A woman blesses the womb that bare him, and he answers, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it. He turned honour away from the mother and onto the keeping of the word.

This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet. The queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and a greater than Solomon is here. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and a greater than Jonas is here. Men came a long way for less than what these would not cross the room for.

The light of the body is the eye: when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness. One lamp lights a whole room, and put out, the whole room is dark. An eye fixed on the word fills the man with light; an eye that goes looking in dark places fills the whole man, thoughts and judgments together, with darkness.

Ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness. Ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and ye are as graves which appear not.

One of the lawyers says, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also, and is answered with a woe of his own. Ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers. Ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them, so ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers. The blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, shall be required of this generation. Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
The scribes and Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him. From that point they were done with him.

cases.name: Jeremiah
cases.charge: Speaking the word of the Lord faithfully despite persecution; not holding back when commanded to prophesy
cases.summary: Before Jeremiah was formed in the belly the Lord knew him, sanctified him, and ordained him a prophet unto the nations—set over kingdoms to root out, pull down, destroy, throw down, build, and plant. His own city conspired to kill him. The word burned like fire shut up in his bones. He was threatened with death, saved by Ahikam, and cast into a miry dungeon before Ebed-melech the Ethiopian drew him out.
cases.offense: The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee, and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations (Jeremiah 1:5). When Jeremiah protested he was a child, the Lord told him to go wherever he was sent and speak whatever was commanded. Be not afraid of their faces, for I am with thee to deliver thee (Jeremiah 1:7–8). The Lord put forth His hand, touched Jeremiah’s mouth, and said, I have put my words in thy mouth. See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant (Jeremiah 1:9–10). The commission was both destructive and constructive, and neither part could be refused. When Jeremiah prophesied in the temple court that this house would become like Shiloh, the priests and the prophets and the people took him and said, Thou shalt surely die. He answered that the Lord had sent him and that if they put him to death they would bring innocent blood upon themselves (Jeremiah 26:8–15). The hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with him, and they did not give him to the people (Jeremiah 26:24). Mocked and derided daily, Jeremiah resolved to stop speaking in the Lord’s name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay (Jeremiah 20:9). The word did not allow itself to be contained.

When Jeremiah protested he was a child, the Lord told him to go wherever he was sent and speak whatever was commanded. Be not afraid of their faces, for I am with thee to deliver thee (Jeremiah 1:7–8).

The Lord put forth His hand, touched Jeremiah’s mouth, and said, I have put my words in thy mouth. See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant (Jeremiah 1:9–10). The commission was both destructive and constructive, and neither part could be refused.

When Jeremiah prophesied in the temple court that this house would become like Shiloh, the priests and the prophets and the people took him and said, Thou shalt surely die. He answered that the Lord had sent him and that if they put him to death they would bring innocent blood upon themselves (Jeremiah 26:8–15). The hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with him, and they did not give him to the people (Jeremiah 26:24).

Mocked and derided daily, Jeremiah resolved to stop speaking in the Lord’s name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay (Jeremiah 20:9). The word did not allow itself to be contained.

cases.name: Pashur the son of Immer
cases.charge: Smiting the prophet and putting him in the stocks; prophesying lies
cases.summary: Pashur, chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard Jeremiah prophesy the city's fall, struck him, and put him in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin overnight. In the morning Jeremiah gave him a new name.
cases.offense: Pashur, the priest and chief governor in the Lord's house, heard Jeremiah prophesy and struck him. He put the prophet in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin, using his office to punish the word he should have received. When Pashur released him the next day, Jeremiah did not withdraw the message. The Lord gave Pashur the name Magor-missabib, fear round about. His violence against the messenger could neither disprove the prophecy nor remove the danger it announced.
cases.judgment: The Lord declared that Pashur would become a terror to himself and his friends. Judah's strength and treasures would be given to Babylon. Pashur and his household would go into captivity, and he would die and be buried there with the friends to whom he had prophesied lies. The passage records this sentence against him; it does not give a separate account of its execution. The keeper of the stocks was warned of his own coming confinement. Authority in the sanctuary provided no exemption from answering for violence and false prophecy.

verses.text: Now Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard that Jeremiah prophesied these things.
Then Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet, and put him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the Lord.
And it came to pass on the morrow, that Pashur brought forth Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then said Jeremiah unto him, The Lord hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor–missabib.

For thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will make thee a terror to thyself, and to all thy friends: and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it: and I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall carry them captive into Babylon, and shall slay them with the sword.

Moreover I will deliver all the strength of this city, and all the labours thereof, and all the precious things thereof, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah will I give into the hand of their enemies, which shall spoil them, and take them, and carry them to Babylon.

And thou, Pashur, and all that dwell in thine house shall go into captivity: and thou shalt come to Babylon, and there thou shalt die, and shalt be buried there, thou, and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies.
Then came Jeremiah from Tophet, whither the Lord had sent him to prophesy; and he stood in the court of the Lord’s house; and said to all the people,

Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring upon this city and upon all her towns all the evil that I have pronounced against it, because they have hardened their necks, that they might not hear my words.

Now it came to pass, when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking all that the Lord had commanded him to speak unto all the people, that the priests and the prophets and all the people took him, saying, Thou shalt surely die.

Why hast thou prophesied in the name of the Lord, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate without an inhabitant? And all the people were gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the Lord.
When the princes of Judah heard these things, then they came up from the king’s house unto the house of the Lord, and sat down in the entry of the new gate of the Lord’s house.
Then spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is worthy to die; for he hath prophesied against this city, as ye have heard with your ears.
If there be a controversy between men, and they come unto judgment, that the judges may judge them; then they shall justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked.
And it shall be, if the wicked man be worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his fault, by a certain number.
Forty stripes he may give him, and not exceed: lest, if he should exceed, and beat him above these with many stripes, then thy brother should seem vile unto thee.

entries.commentary: Pashur the priest, chief governor in the house of the Most High, hears Jeremiah prophesy, smites him, and puts him in the stocks in the high gate of Benjamin. When he is let out the next day, Jeremiah tells him the Most High has renamed him Magor-missabib, a terror to himself and all his friends, for they shall fall by the sword of the king of Babylon. All Judah, all the strength and treasures of the city, and Pashur's whole household will be carried captive to Babylon, and Pashur will die there and be buried there with all the friends to whom he prophesied lies.

Jeremiah is going through it so bad, mocked and reproached daily, that he says he will not make mention of the Most High nor speak any more in His name. Just like us when we go out to camp, if somebody does not speak evil of us every time we do something big, there is a hater or somebody trying to demonize us. But the word was in his heart like a burning fire shut up in his bones; he was weary with holding it in and could not stay, he had to blast them, he could not hold it.

Jeremiah hears the defaming of many and his familiar friends watching for his stumbling, hoping to be enticed against him and take their revenge. The Most High is with him as a mighty terrible one, so his persecutors will stumble, not prevail, and be greatly ashamed in an everlasting confusion that will never be forgotten. He commits his cause to the Most High who tries the righteous and sees the reins and the heart, and sings praise because He delivers the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers.

Crushed by the persecution, Jeremiah curses the day he was born and the man who brought his father the news of a man child, wishing that man to be like the cities the Most High overthrew. He asks why he came forth out of the womb only to see labor and sorrow and to have his days consumed with shame.

In the beginning of Jehoiakim's reign the Most High commands Jeremiah to stand in the court of the Lord's house and speak all His words to the cities of Judah, diminishing not a word, that they might hearken and turn from their evil way. If they will not hearken and walk in His law, He will make this house like Shiloh and this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.

When Jeremiah finished speaking all that the Most High commanded, the priests, the prophets, and all the people took him and said, Thou shalt surely die. They were angry that he prophesied the house would be like Shiloh and the city desolate; this is the same thing we go through when we read the Bible to people and tell them thus saith the Lord, and they get mad and want to harm us.

When the princes of Judah heard, they came up from the king's house and sat in the entry of the new gate, and the priests and prophets said this man is worthy to die for prophesying against this city. It was not about Jeremiah speaking the word of the Most High but about their feelings getting hurt; he prophesied only because the Most High told him what to say, the same way people today say you cannot speak against this country when we are only saying what the Bible says.

Jeremiah answers the princes and all the people that the Most High sent him to prophesy against this house and city, and tells them to amend their ways and obey, that the Most High might repent of the evil pronounced against them. He puts himself in their hand to do as they see good, but warns that if they put him to death they bring innocent blood upon themselves and upon the city, for of a truth the Most High sent him to speak these words.

The princes and all the people then say to the priests and prophets that this man is not worthy to die, for he has spoken in the name of the Most High; our people were rebellious but they were not that dumb. The elders rise and recall that Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah that Zion would be plowed like a field, yet Hezekiah did not put him to death but feared the Most High, who then repented of the evil.

The elders also recall Urijah the son of Shemaiah, who prophesied against the city like Jeremiah; when Jehoiakim sought to kill him he fled to Egypt, but the king sent men who fetched him back and slew him with the sword. One king knew the word came from the Most High and spared the prophet, while another king put his prophet to death; nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah so he was not given to the people to be killed.

If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God. Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day.

cases.name: Jehoiakim
cases.charge: Building with unrighteousness; shedding innocent blood; burning the scroll of the Lord's words
cases.summary: Necho's puppet king built a great house with unpaid labor, killed the prophet Urijah for prophesying like Jeremiah, and when Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, cut it with a penknife leaf by leaf and burned it in the hearth. Neither he nor his servants were afraid.
cases.offense: Jehoiakim enlarged his house through unrighteousness, using his neighbor's service without paying his wages. Jeremiah contrasted his display with Josiah's judgment of the poor and needy: that was to know the Lord. Jehoiakim's eyes and heart were set on covetousness, innocent blood, oppression, and violence. He also had Urijah brought back from Egypt and killed for prophesying against the city.
cases.judgment: He shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem. He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat and in the night to the frost. His son reigned three months and went to Babylon; his brother was the last king.

entries.commentary: Jeremiah is sent down to the king of Judah's house to command the king to execute judgment and righteousness, deliver the oppressed, and do no violence to the stranger, the fatherless, or the widow. If they obey, kings will keep entering the gates riding in chariots and on horses, but if they will not hear, the Most High swears by Himself that this house shall become a desolation. Many nations will pass by and ask why He did this to so great a city, and the answer is that they forsook His covenant and worshipped other gods.

The people are told not to weep for the dead but to weep sore for him that goes away, Shallum the son of Josiah who reigned in his father's place. Shallum went forth out of his place and shall not return, but shall die in the land where they led him captive and see his native country no more.

Woe is pronounced on Jehoiakim, who builds his house by unrighteousness and his chambers by wrong, using his neighbor's service without wages and painting his wide house with vermilion. His father ate and drank yet did judgment and justice for the poor and needy, and it was well with him, but Jehoiakim's eyes and heart are set only on covetousness, innocent blood, oppression, and violence. Therefore no one will lament him; he shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

Jerusalem is told to cry from Lebanon and Bashan because all her lovers are destroyed; she would not hear in her prosperity, which has been her manner from her youth. Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, even were he the signet on the Most High's right hand, will be plucked off and given into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and the Chaldeans whose face he fears, cast out with his mother into a country where they were not born to die. The Most High writes this man childless, for no man of his seed shall prosper sitting upon the throne of David or ruling in Judah anymore; Deacon Marathon and the History of a King class break down this curse of Coniah in fuller detail.

In the beginning of Jehoiakim's reign the Most High commands Jeremiah to stand in the court of the Lord's house and speak all His words to the cities of Judah, diminishing not a word, that they might hearken and turn from their evil way. If they will not hearken and walk in His law, He will make this house like Shiloh and this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.

When Jeremiah finished speaking all that the Most High commanded, the priests, the prophets, and all the people took him and said, Thou shalt surely die. They were angry that he prophesied the house would be like Shiloh and the city desolate; this is the same thing we go through when we read the Bible to people and tell them thus saith the Lord, and they get mad and want to harm us.

When the princes of Judah heard, they came up from the king's house and sat in the entry of the new gate, and the priests and prophets said this man is worthy to die for prophesying against this city. It was not about Jeremiah speaking the word of the Most High but about their feelings getting hurt; he prophesied only because the Most High told him what to say, the same way people today say you cannot speak against this country when we are only saying what the Bible says.

Jeremiah answers the princes and all the people that the Most High sent him to prophesy against this house and city, and tells them to amend their ways and obey, that the Most High might repent of the evil pronounced against them. He puts himself in their hand to do as they see good, but warns that if they put him to death they bring innocent blood upon themselves and upon the city, for of a truth the Most High sent him to speak these words.

The princes and all the people then say to the priests and prophets that this man is not worthy to die, for he has spoken in the name of the Most High; our people were rebellious but they were not that dumb. The elders rise and recall that Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah that Zion would be plowed like a field, yet Hezekiah did not put him to death but feared the Most High, who then repented of the evil.

The elders also recall Urijah the son of Shemaiah, who prophesied against the city like Jeremiah; when Jehoiakim sought to kill him he fled to Egypt, but the king sent men who fetched him back and slew him with the sword. One king knew the word came from the Most High and spared the prophet, while another king put his prophet to death; nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah so he was not given to the people to be killed.

In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the Most High tells Jeremiah to take a roll of a book and write in it all the words He has spoken against Israel, against Judah, and against all the nations, from the days of Josiah until that day. The purpose is that the house of Judah, hearing all the evil purposed against them, might return every man from his evil way so that He would forgive their iniquity and their sin.

Jeremiah calls Baruch the son of Neriah, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the Most High upon the roll. Because Jeremiah is shut up and cannot go into the house of the Most High, he sends Baruch to read the roll in the ears of the people on the fasting day, that they might present their supplication and turn from their evil way, for great is the anger and fury pronounced against this people. Baruch does all that the prophet commanded, reading the book of the words of the Most High in the Most High's house.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, a fast is proclaimed before the Most High to all the people in Jerusalem and those who came from the cities of Judah. Baruch reads the words of Jeremiah in the temple in the chamber of Gemariah, in the ears of all the people. Michaiah the son of Gemariah, having heard the words, goes down into the king's house to the scribe's chamber where all the princes are sitting, and declares to them all he had heard when Baruch read.

The princes send Jehudi to bring Baruch with the roll, and they ask him to sit and read it in their ears. When they hear all the words they are afraid, both one and another, and say they will surely tell the king; they ask Baruch how he wrote all these words, and he answers that Jeremiah pronounced them with his mouth while Baruch wrote them with ink in the book. The princes tell Baruch to go hide himself and Jeremiah, and to let no man know where they are.

The princes lay up the roll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe and tell all the words in the ears of the king, who sends Jehudi to fetch it and read it before him and the princes. The king sits in the winter house in the ninth month with a fire burning on the hearth; as Jehudi reads three or four leaves, the king cuts them with a penknife and casts them into the fire until the whole roll is consumed. Neither the king nor his servants are afraid nor rend their garments; though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah make intercession that he not burn the roll, he will not hear, and he commands that Baruch and Jeremiah be seized, but the Most High hides them.

After the king burns the roll, the word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah to take another roll and write all the former words that Jehoiakim had burned. Against Jehoiakim He pronounces that he shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night, and He will punish him, his seed, and his servants for their iniquity. Jeremiah gives a second roll to Baruch, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the burned book, and many like words are added besides.

In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, then turned and rebelled against him. The Lord sent bands of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites against Judah to destroy it according to the word he spake by his prophets. This came upon Judah at the commandment of the Lord to remove them out of his sight for the sins of Manasseh and the innocent blood he shed, which the Lord would not pardon. -

Jehoiakim slept with his fathers and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place. The king of Egypt came no more out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that pertained to Egypt from the river of Egypt to the river Euphrates. Babylon took over as had been prophesied throughout the Bible, in Daniel and in Jeremiah, that Nebuchadnezzar would ransack Jerusalem and the surrounding lands.

Jehoiachin was eighteen years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done. The servants of Nebuchadnezzar came up against Jerusalem and besieged it, and the king himself came against the city while it was besieged. Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, servants, princes, and officers, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

Nebuchadnezzar carried out all the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and cut in pieces the vessels of gold Solomon had made, as the Lord had said. He carried away all Jerusalem, all the princes, all the mighty men of valour, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths, leaving only the poorest of the people of the land. He carried Jehoiachin, the king's mother, wives, and officers to Babylon, along with the men of might and craftsmen and smiths, wanting them to build for him what they had built in their own land, as conquering nations always used Israel's skill and industry. -

The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's father's brother, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah. Zedekiah was twenty one years old and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all Jehoiakim had done. Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out of his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. -

Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, went up to the house of the Most High with the priests, the prophets, and all the people both small and great, and read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found there. Our forefathers had the Bible; the king read it openly, then stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all their heart and soul. All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book. -

The king commanded Hilkiah and the priests to bring out of the temple all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all the host of heaven, and he burned them in the fields of Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel. He put down the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places and around Jerusalem, and those that burnt incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the host of heaven. When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong. -

He brought the grove out of the house of the Lord to the brook Kidron, burned it, stamped it to powder, and cast the powder on the graves of the children of the people. He broke down the houses of the sodomites that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove; there should be no sodomite among the sons of Israel, yet they had grown so bold as to do this wickedness right beside the temple. He brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where they had burnt incense, and though the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar, they still ate of the unleavened bread among their brethren.

Josiah defiled Topheth in the valley of the children of Hinnom so that no man might make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech. Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own. -

He took away the horses the kings of Judah had given to the sun and burnt the chariots of the sun with fire. He beat down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's chamber and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron. He defiled the high places Solomon had built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, the abominations of the Zidonians, Moabites, and Ammonites, and broke in pieces the images, cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men. This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and to fall under punishment. -

Josiah also destroyed the altar and high place at Bethel that Jeroboam had made when he set up the golden calves, burning it and stamping it small to powder. Turning himself, he spied the sepulchres in the mount, took out the bones, and burnt them upon the altar to pollute it, according to the word the man of God had proclaimed. When told which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who prophesied these things, he said to let him alone and let no man move his bones. -

Josiah also took away all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, and did to them as he had done at Bethel. The northern kingdom had already been carried into captivity by Assyria, so most of the people were gone, yet the idolatrous houses remained. He slew all the priests of the high places upon their altars, burnt men's bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

The king commanded all the people to keep the Passover to the Lord their God as it is written in the book of this covenant. Such a Passover had not been held from the days of the judges nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah, but in the eighteenth year of Josiah this Passover was held in Jerusalem. Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today. -

Josiah also put away the workers with familiar spirits, the wizards, the images, the idols, and all the abominations spied in Judah and Jerusalem, that he might perform the words of the law found by Hilkiah. There was no king before or after him that turned to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might according to all the law of Moses; he put things in order like a true leader. Nevertheless the Lord did not turn from the fierceness of his great wrath because of the provocations of Manasseh, and said he would remove Judah out of his sight as he had removed Israel and cast off Jerusalem.

Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates, and Josiah went against him and was slain at Megiddo. Josiah got involved in a matter that did not concern him and lost his life in it, a warning not to enter into quarrels that are not one's own. His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and buried him, and the people took Jehoahaz his son and anointed him king in his father's place.

Jehoahaz was twenty three years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done. Pharaohnechoh bound him at Riblah so he might not reign, put the land to a tribute of silver and gold, and made Eliakim the son of Josiah king, turning his name to Jehoiakim. Jehoiakim taxed the people to pay Pharaoh, exacting the silver and gold of every man of the land, and he also did evil in the sight of the Lord like his forefathers, not like his father Josiah.

Hearken, O Israel: hearken means listen, pay attention, and there is a difference between hearing and listening. The statutes and judgments are taught for to do them; knowing you are an Israelite is only half the battle. The main thing is applying the scriptures, doing what the Most High is telling you to do, that ye may live. The promise is to go in and possess the land, and possessing land is true wealth: your milk and honey, your cattle, your agriculture, where you cultivate and take care of your family. It is not the diamonds, the cars, the sneakers, or the newest phone; a big house with no land is not wealth, and that is why the heathen boxes our people into apartments.

Ye shall not add unto the word, neither diminish ought from it. This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book: the prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ, and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes. The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove [Matthew 18:11](/bible/matthew/18#v11) and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.

Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal-peor: all the men that followed Baal-peor were destroyed from among the people, and this recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite. But ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day: those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive. The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.

Keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at. When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group, or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ; but rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

What nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them? The Most High is near unto Israel in all things they call upon him for, and no nation has statutes and judgments so righteous as this law. When Israel keeps the laws, statutes, and commandments, they are the light of the world; in the days when the brothers and sisters were in order, the nations looked on and marveled at what nation this was, so great and so beautiful.

Take heed to thyself and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things thine eyes have seen; and teach them thy sons, and thy sons' sons. These are generational commandments: children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat. Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children. Why learn to fear the Most High? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

The mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, and the Most High spake out of the midst of the fire; ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude. He declared his covenant, even ten commandments: the ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them. And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever.

The Most High commanded Moses at that time to teach the statutes and judgments, and Israel is charged to take good heed, for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day the Lord spake in Horeb. No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches: when the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant. Fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill; it was simple and easy to understand. Lest ye corrupt yourselves and make a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female: Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day. The eagle and the falcon symbols of the powers of this world trace back to the gods and goddesses of Egypt, because this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her. Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt. Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.

The Lord hath taken you and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance. Furthermore the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: again Moses lays his barred crossing on the people. It is how the workers feel when they go out to preach truth and catch anger for it; you are not arguing with the messenger, you are mad at the Bible, so speak the oracles and neither add nor diminish to please anybody. Moses must die in this land and not go over Jordan, but ye shall go over and possess that good land; he kept repeating it, longing for what he would not see.

Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant and make a graven image, for the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When children's children are begotten and the stay in the land grows long, corruption creeps in; make the graven image and do evil to provoke him, and ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land. Heaven and earth are called to witness against Israel this day; the warning was on record before it ever came to pass.

And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen: this is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul; the seeking begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days: the latter days began when Christ came, for God who spake in time past by the prophets hath in these last days spoken by his Son. And shalt be obedient unto his voice: the voice of the Most High tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High. For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

Ask now of the days that are past, since the day that God created man upon the earth: you are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only, but the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it. Did ever people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and live? Hath God assayed to take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand? There is no such history anywhere else; the Most High did this for Israel alone. Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.

Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee; and because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out of Egypt in his sight with his mighty power. To drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou art: they had more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here. Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

Thou shalt keep therefore his statutes and his commandments, that it may go well with thee and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth. This is the solution. The voting, protesting, and marching have never worked and never will; trust in the Most High and keep his laws, and he will take care of his people with long days, families, and the land.

Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising, that the slayer which killed his neighbour unawares, and hated him not in times past, might flee thither and live: Bezer in the wilderness for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. The chapter closes with the summary: this is the law, the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which Moses spake unto the children of Israel after they came forth out of Egypt, in the land of Sihon and of Og, the two kings of the Amorites.

verses.text: Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong; that useth his neighbour’s service without wages, and giveth him not for his work;
That saith, I will build me a wide house and large chambers, and cutteth him out windows; and it is cieled with cedar, and painted with vermilion.
Shalt thou reign, because thou closest thyself in cedar? did not thy father eat and drink, and do judgment and justice, and then it was well with him?
He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well with him: was not this to know me? saith the Lord.
But thine eyes and thine heart are not but for thy covetousness, and for to shed innocent blood, and for oppression, and for violence, to do it.

Therefore thus saith the Lord concerning Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah; They shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother! or, Ah sister! they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah lord! or, Ah his glory!
He shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

And there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the Lord, Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjath–jearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah:

And when Jehoiakim the king, with all his mighty men, and all the princes, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death: but when Urijah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and went into Egypt;
And Jehoiakim the king sent men into Egypt, namely, Elnathan the son of Achbor, and certain men with him into Egypt.
And they fetched forth Urijah out of Egypt, and brought him unto Jehoiakim the king; who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.

So the king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll: and he took it out of Elishama the scribe’s chamber. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king, and in the ears of all the princes which stood beside the king.
Now the king sat in the winterhouse in the ninth month: and there was a fire on the hearth burning before him.

And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.
Yet they were not afraid, nor rent their garments, neither the king, nor any of his servants that heard all these words.
Nevertheless Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the roll: but he would not hear them.
But the king commanded Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to take Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet: but the Lord hid them.

And thou shalt say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, Thus saith the Lord; Thou hast burned this roll, saying, Why hast thou written therein, saying, The king of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land, and shall cause to cease from thence man and beast?

Therefore thus saith the Lord of Jehoiakim king of Judah; He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David: and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost.

And I will punish him and his seed and his servants for their iniquity; and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them; but they hearkened not.
In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years: then he turned and rebelled against him.

And the Lord sent against him bands of the Chaldees, and bands of the Syrians, and bands of the Moabites, and bands of the children of Ammon, and sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by his servants the prophets.

Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.

cases.name: Hananiah the son of Azur
cases.charge: Prophesying a lie in the name of the Lord
cases.summary: In the temple, before the priests and all the people, Hananiah declared that the Lord would break Babylon's yoke within two years and bring back the vessels and the captives. He broke the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck to prove it.
cases.offense: Hananiah announced in the Lord's name that Babylon's yoke would be broken within two years and that the temple vessels and captives would return. He broke the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck before the priests and people, making a visible sign serve his false promise. Jeremiah desired the people's restoration, but a desirable promise was not thereby a word from God. He reminded them that a prophet of peace would be known when the word came to pass. After Hananiah's display, Jeremiah went his way until the Lord gave him an answer.
cases.judgment: The Lord declared that the broken wooden yokes would be replaced by yokes of iron. Babylon's appointed rule would not end according to Hananiah's timetable. Jeremiah told him plainly that the Lord had not sent him and that he had made the people trust in a lie. Because he had taught rebellion against the Lord, Hananiah would die that year. He died in the seventh month, within the year of the confrontation. The prophet who promised swift release could not escape the swift judgment pronounced upon his own falsehood.

entries.commentary: In the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, in the fifth month, Hananiah the son of Azur, a prophet of Gibeon, spake in the house of the Lord before the priests and all the people. This so-called prophet spoke the things he claimed the Most High was going to do: that He had broken the yoke of the king of Babylon and within two full years would bring back the vessels of the Lord's house and Jeconiah with all the captives of Judah.

Jeremiah answered Amen, the Lord do so, the Lord perform thy words to bring again the vessels and the captives; but he told Hananiah not to hold on to that. The prophets before them prophesied of war, of evil, and of pestilence, nothing of peace; so when a prophet prophesies peace, only when the word comes to pass is that prophet known to be truly sent of the Lord, and if it does not come to pass, the Lord is not working with him.

Hananiah took the yoke from off Jeremiah's neck, the yoke he wore in his captivity, and broke it before all the people. He said thus saith the Lord, even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within two full years; and Jeremiah went his way.

The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah: thou hast broken the yokes of wood, but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron. The Most High had put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who was the superpower at this time, and He gave him the beasts of the field also.

Jeremiah told Hananiah the Lord had not sent him, but he made the people trust in a lie and was leading his people astray. Because he taught rebellion against the Lord, teaching the people to go against the Most High instead of accepting that they had to go through captivity, the Lord would cast him from off the face of the earth and he would die that year; Hananiah died the same year in the seventh month.

The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the Lord is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

This shall be the priest's due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw. The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him. For the Most High hath chosen him out of all thy tribes to stand to minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.

If a Levite come from any of thy gates out of all Israel, and come with all the desire of his mind unto the place which the Lord shall choose, then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do which stand there before the Lord. They shall have like portions to eat, beside that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony.

When thou art come into the land, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations: there shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. These things actually existed and they are all real: wizards, necromancers, divination, observers of times, people that consult with familiar spirits. If they were not real, they would not be in the Bible with the Most High telling us not to do them. All that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord, and because of these abominations the Most High driveth those nations out from before thee. Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God, meaning upright; the nations hearken unto observers of times and unto diviners, but as for thee, the Most High hath not suffered thee so to do.

The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken. This is talking about Christ, Yeshua. This answers what Israel desired of the Most High in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not; and the Lord said, They have well spoken that which they have spoken. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him; and whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. If we do not follow Christ and do what Christ says, that judgment falls on us.

The prophet which shall presume to speak a word in the name of the Most High which he hath not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. By this law a lot of these pastors stand condemned: they say things and claim Christ said them, when the Most High never commanded Christ to say it and Christ is not telling them to say it. How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken; the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously, and thou shalt not be afraid of him. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Woe is pronounced on the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of the Most High's pasture and have not visited them, so He will visit upon them the evil of their doings. He will gather the remnant of His flock out of the countries where He drove them, bring them again to their folds, and set up shepherds who will feed them so they fear no more and none are lacking.

The Most High promises to raise unto David a righteous Branch, a King who shall reign, prosper, and execute judgment and justice, in whose days Judah shall be saved and Israel dwell safely. His name is called THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS; this is plainly referring to Christ. The day comes when they will no longer swear by the Most High who brought Israel out of Egypt, but by Him who led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country and all the countries where He had driven them, back to their own land.

Jeremiah's heart is broken and his bones shake like a drunken man because of the prophets and the words of the Most High's holiness, for the land is full of adulterers and mourns under swearing. Both prophet and priest are profane, and the Most High has found their wickedness even in His house, so their way shall be as slippery ways in the darkness where they are driven and fall. The prophets of Samaria prophesied in Baal and caused Israel to err, and the prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery, walk in lies, and strengthen the hands of evildoers so that none return from wickedness, becoming as Sodom and Gomorrah before Him.

The people are told not to hearken to the prophets who make them vain and speak a vision of their own heart, not out of the mouth of the Most High, telling those who despise Him that they shall have peace and no evil shall come. This is like the pastor who says, let me tell you what God told me to tell you, when it is a lie. None of these prophets has stood in the counsel of the Most High; had they stood there and caused the people to hear His words, they would have turned them from their evil way, but instead the whirlwind of His anger will fall grievously upon the head of the wicked in the latter days.

The Most High asks whether He is a God only near and not far off, when He fills heaven and earth and no one can hide in secret places where He cannot see him. He has heard the prophets who prophesy lies in His name saying, I have dreamed, thinking to cause His people to forget His name by their dreams as their fathers forgot it for Baal. Let the prophet with a dream tell a dream, but let him that has His word speak it faithfully, for His word is like a fire and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces; He is against those who steal His words and use their own tongues to lie on the Most High.

When the people, prophet, or priest ask what is the burden of the Most High, Jeremiah is to answer, What burden? for He will forsake them, and every man who claims the burden of the Most High He will punish in his house. Instead of saying the burden of the Most High, they are to ask one another what the Most High has answered and spoken, for they have perverted the words of the living God. Because they keep saying the burden of the Most High after being told not to, He will utterly forget them, forsake them, and cast them out of His presence with an everlasting reproach and perpetual shame that shall not be forgotten. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

verses.text: And it came to pass the same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, and in the fifth month, that Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon, spake unto me in the house of the Lord, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,
Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of the Lord’s house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away from this place, and carried them to Babylon:

And I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, that went into Babylon, saith the Lord: for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiah’s neck, and brake it.

So Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month.

cases.name: Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah
cases.charge: Prophesying lies in the Lord's name to the captives; committing adultery with their neighbours' wives
cases.summary: Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah prophesied lies among the captives and committed adultery with their neighbors' wives. The Lord named their sins and announced that Nebuchadnezzar would kill them and that their names would become a curse among the exiles.
cases.offense: Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah prophesied lies in the Lord's name among the captives in Babylon. They also committed adultery with their neighbors' wives. God joined their public religious falsehood with the private wickedness they might have thought concealed. These were the two named prophets among the exiles, not the kings who bore the same names. The Lord declared that He knew and was a witness. Neither distance from Jerusalem nor the conditions of captivity put their conduct beyond His sight.
cases.judgment: The Lord announced that He would deliver them into Nebuchadnezzar's hand and that the king would kill them before the captives' eyes. Their names would become a curse among the exiles, recalling the two whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire. Jeremiah's letter records the announced punishment. Their position as speakers to the captive community made the lie no less accountable. God's people were to reject false promises and heed the word He had actually sent concerning their life in exile and His appointed time of return.

Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

The soul that turns after such as have familiar spirits and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, is cut off from among his people. Sanctify yourselves and be ye holy; keep the statutes of the Most High, for He is the Lord which sanctifieth you. Every one that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; his blood shall be upon him. Disrespecting your mother and your father carried the death penalty.

The man that committeth adultery with another man's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress, shall surely be put to death. This world openly defends adultery and men even boast of committing it with another man's wife; the scriptures call for death upon both.

The man that lies with his father's wife, and the man that lies with his daughter in law, shall surely be put to death; they have wrought confusion. If a man lie with mankind as he lieth with a woman, both have committed an abomination and shall surely be put to death; abomination means hateful and disgusting unto the Most High. The man that takes a wife and her mother is burnt with fire, both he and they, that there be no wickedness among you. The man or woman that lies with a beast is put to death, and the beast is slain also. All of these judgments fall under the laws of adultery, the sub-statutes of that commandment.

The man that takes his sister and sees her nakedness, it is a wicked thing; they are cut off in the sight of their people, and he bears his iniquity. The man that lies with a woman having her sickness, her menstrual cycle, has discovered her fountain, and both are cut off from among their people; this goes with the laws of [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15). The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless.

Keep all my statutes and all my judgments, that the land whither I bring you spew you not out. Walk not in the manners of the nation cast out before you, for they committed all these things and therefore the Most High abhorred them. I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people. The Most High separated Israel from the other people, so Israel is to walk differently; these laws are the separation.

Put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean; this goes back to [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11), the dietary laws. No shrimp, crab, lobster, pork, catfish, and the like; everything is not clean, whatever the church teaches. If you eat whatever you please, you are not separating yourself from the other nations. Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.

A man or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, was surely put to death by stoning. The tarot card readings, the fortune telling, and the horoscopes of today are that same dealing with familiar spirits; do not touch any of it.
