cases.name: Johanan and the remnant that went down to Egypt
cases.charge: Asking the word of the Lord, swearing to obey it, and refusing it; burning incense to the queen of heaven in Egypt
cases.summary: The remnant asked Jeremiah to pray for direction and swore to obey whatever the Lord said. Ten days later the answer came: stay in the land and I will build you; go to Egypt and the sword you fear will overtake you there. They called the prophet a liar, took him with them to Egypt, and there openly returned to the queen of heaven.
cases.offense: Ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the Lord your God, saying, Pray for us unto the Lord our God; and according unto all that the Lord our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it. In Egypt the men who knew their wives burned incense to other gods answered Jeremiah: we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, as we did in the cities of Judah; for then had we plenty of victuals.
cases.judgment: Then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die. I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt, and they shall all be consumed, and fall in the land of Egypt; none shall return but such as shall escape. The sign given was Pharaoh-hophra delivered into the hand of his enemies, as Zedekiah had been.

entries.commentary: All the captains, Johanan, Jezaniah, and all the people from the least to the greatest came to Jeremiah the prophet before going into Egypt and begged him to pray to the Most High for them, that they might know the way to walk and what to do. Jeremiah agreed to pray and promised to declare everything the Most High answered, keeping nothing back. They swore the Most High would be a true and faithful witness against them if they did not obey His voice, whether good or evil, so that it might be well with them.

After ten days the word of the Most High came to Jeremiah, and he called Johanan and all the people to hear the answer. The Most High told them that if they would still abide in the land He would build them and not pull them down, plant them and not pluck them up, for He repented of the evil He had done to them; He does not desire evil against His people, He only wants His laws kept. He told them not to be afraid of the king of Babylon of whom they were afraid, for He was with them to save them, deliver them from his hand, and show them mercies so they could return to their own land.

If instead they refused to dwell in the land and said they would go into Egypt to see no war, hear no trumpet, and hunger for no bread, then the sword they feared would overtake them there and the famine would follow close after them, and there they would die. All the men who set their faces to go into Egypt would die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and none would remain or escape the evil He would bring; the Most High set before them life or death and told them to choose life. As His anger was poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so His fury would be poured out on them when they entered Egypt, and they would become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach, and see the land no more.

The Most High plainly told the remnant of Judah to go not into Egypt, and Jeremiah warned them He had admonished them that day. They had dissembled in their hearts when they sent him to pray, giving a false appearance and concealing that they did not truly mean to obey; some people speak words they do not believe. Because they had not obeyed His voice, they would certainly die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence in the very place they desired to go; we are these same people, quick to say we will not do what the Most High commands, though now that we understand who we are in these last days many of us want to keep His laws.

When Jeremiah finished speaking all the words of the Most High, Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men told him he spoke falsely and called him a lying prophet; pride is destruction according to the scriptures. They accused Baruch the son of Neriah of setting Jeremiah against them to deliver them into the hand of the Chaldeans, to be put to death or carried captive to Babylon. Many people ask for counsel while already having their own minds made up; when the counsel is not what they want to hear they go looking for someone who will tell them what they want, and so these men obeyed not the voice of the Most High to dwell in Judah.

Johanan and all the captains took the whole remnant of Judah, the men, women, children, and the king's daughters that Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch. They came into the land of Egypt as far as Tahpanhes because they obeyed not the voice of the Most High.

The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes to take great stones and hide them in the clay of the brick kiln at the entry of Pharaoh's house, in the sight of the men of Judah. The Most High declared He would send for Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, His servant, set his throne upon those hidden stones, spread his royal pavilion over them, and smite the land of Egypt. When Nebuchadnezzar came he would deliver such as were for death to death, such as were for captivity to captivity, and such as were for the sword to the sword; in war each person already has an appointed end that the Most High has set. He would kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, array himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd puts on his garment so that none escape, break the images of Bethshemesh, and burn the houses of the gods of the Egyptians with fire. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt and in the country of Pathros; the Most High reminded them of all the evil He had brought on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, now a desolation where no man dwelt, because of the wickedness they committed provoking Him to anger. They went to burn incense and serve other gods that neither they nor their fathers knew, yet the Most High sent all His servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, pleading with them not to do this abominable thing that He hates. The same work goes on today; we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets He raised up to give warning. -

They hearkened not nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness and burn no incense to other gods, so the Most High's fury and anger was poured forth and kindled in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem until they were wasted and desolate. He asks why they commit this great evil against their own souls, cutting off man and woman, child and suckling out of Judah, leaving none to remain. They provoke Him to wrath with the works of their hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where they had gone to dwell, cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth. -

The Most High asks whether they have forgotten the wickedness of their fathers, the kings of Judah, their wives, and their own wickedness committed in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem; they were not humbled even to that day, nor did they fear or walk in His law and statutes. Therefore He will set His face against them for evil, to cut off all Judah, and take the remnant that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall all be consumed and fall by the sword and the famine, from the least to the greatest. They shall become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach; only a small number escaping the sword shall return, for none shall return to Judah though they have a desire to dwell there. -

All the men who knew their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women, a great multitude in Egypt and Pathros, answered Jeremiah defiantly. These men did not rule their houses well and had no authority over their households; their wives were in the midst of idolatry, the same disorder we see in this place spiritually called Egypt, in Babylon the great today. They said they would not hearken to the word spoken in the name of the Most High but would perform their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings, claiming they had plenty of victuals and saw no evil until they left off, and then wanted all things and were consumed by the sword and famine. The women declared they made their cakes to worship her and poured out drink offerings without their men; the times women gather together without their men, such as baby showers with cakes and drinks and partying, are burning incense to other gods to keep in mind.

Jeremiah answered all the people, men and women, that the incense they burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, they and their fathers, kings, and princes, the Most High remembered and it came into His mind. The Most High could no longer bear the evil of their doings and the abominations they committed, therefore their land became a desolation, an astonishment, and a curse without an inhabitant as at that day. This evil happened to them because they burned incense and sinned against the Most High and did not obey His voice nor walk in His law, statutes, and testimonies.

Jeremiah told all the people and all the women that they and their wives had both spoken with their mouths and fulfilled with their hands their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and would surely accomplish them. Therefore the Most High swore by His great name that His name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all Egypt, saying "The Lord GOD liveth"; He will watch over them for evil and not for good until they are consumed by the sword and famine. Only a small number escaping the sword shall return out of Egypt into Judah, and all the remnant that went to Egypt shall know whose words shall stand, His or theirs.

The Most High gives a sign that He will punish them in that place so they may know His words shall surely stand against them for evil; He will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies as He gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Evil does not come merely by chance; the Most High brings that evil upon us when we turn from Him and follow our own mind, sinning against the one true living God in Christ. -

Woe to the rebellious children who take counsel but not of the Most High, and who go down into Egypt without asking at his mouth. This is the same rebellion named at the start of the book. Leaning to Pharaoh's strength instead of the Most High turns their trust into shame and confusion. There were times kings sought the Most High, and times they sought heathen kings to fight their battles for them. -

The riches carried down to Egypt on asses and camels buy help that profits nothing, for the Egyptians shall help in vain. The same thing happened in the Babylonian captivity, and the same thing is happening to us today. The Most High tells Isaiah to write it in a table and note it in a book for a time to come forever, because these things were written for our learning. -

This is a rebellious, lying people that will not hear the law of the Most High, telling the seers to prophesy smooth things and deceits. Our pastors do the same today, teaching that the laws are done away with. They want the Holy One of Israel to cease from before them because they love their oppression and the ways of their slave masters. That iniquity becomes a breach ready to fall, breaking suddenly like a potter's vessel that cannot be spared.

In returning and rest, in quietness and confidence, is our salvation and strength, but the people would not have it. Instead they say they will flee upon horses. Because they trust their own swiftness, one thousand will flee at the rebuke of one, until they are left as a lonely beacon on a hill.

The Most High waits to be gracious and exalts himself to have mercy, for he is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him. Waiting means holding patience through the trials and tribulations. People will come, even family members, saying no one is coming to save you and you must save yourself with guns. You must stay steadfast and answer the Most High's cry with patience. -

Though the Most High gives the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, our teachers will no longer be removed into a corner; our eyes shall see our teachers. We see this now on these platforms, in the daily bread classes, radio shows, the Sabbath, and the street corners. The ear hears a word behind saying "This is the way, walk ye in it," because the men are out teaching. Then the people defile and cast away their idols of silver and gold as a menstruous cloth, as we have watched brothers cast off crosses and ankhs at camp.

Then the Most High gives rain for the seed, bread of the increase, fat and plenteous pasture, and rivers on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter when the towers fall. The light of the moon shall be as the sun, and the sun sevenfold, in the day he binds up the breach of his people and heals the stroke of their wound.

The name of the Most High comes from far, burning with anger, his tongue a devouring fire, sifting the nations with the sieve of vanity. His people shall have a song and gladness of heart as when one comes to the mountain of the Most High. Like King David dancing before the ark until Michal despised him, we will be joyful in that day when we no longer fear being shot in the street, having our doors kicked in, or losing our homes. Through the voice of the Most High the Assyrian is beaten down, for Tophet is ordained of old and its fire kindled by the breath of the Most High.

verses.text: Then all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest, came near,

And said unto Jeremiah the prophet, Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee, and pray for us unto the Lord thy God, even for all this remnant; (for we are left but a few of many, as thine eyes do behold us:)
That the Lord thy God may shew us the way wherein we may walk, and the thing that we may do.

Then Jeremiah the prophet said unto them, I have heard you; behold, I will pray unto the Lord your God according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatsoever thing the Lord shall answer you, I will declare it unto you; I will keep nothing back from you.
Then they said to Jeremiah, The Lord be a true and faithful witness between us, if we do not even according to all things for the which the Lord thy God shall send thee to us.
Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the Lord our God.
But if ye say, We will not dwell in this land, neither obey the voice of the Lord your God,
Saying, No; but we will go into the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell:
And now therefore hear the word of the Lord, ye remnant of Judah; Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; If ye wholly set your faces to enter into Egypt, and go to sojourn there;

Then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die.

So shall it be with all the men that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: and none of them shall remain or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them.

For thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; As mine anger and my fury hath been poured forth upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem; so shall my fury be poured forth upon you, when ye shall enter into Egypt: and ye shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach; and ye shall see this place no more.
The Lord hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day.

For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the Lord your God, saying, Pray for us unto the Lord our God; and according unto all that the Lord our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it.
And now I have this day declared it to you; but ye have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God, nor any thing for the which he hath sent me unto you.
Now therefore know certainly that ye shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, in the place whither ye desire to go and to sojourn.
And it came to pass, that when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking unto all the people all the words of the Lord their God, for which the Lord their God had sent him to them, even all these words,

Then spake Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men, saying unto Jeremiah, Thou speakest falsely: the Lord our God hath not sent thee to say, Go not into Egypt to sojourn there:
But Baruch the son of Neriah setteth thee on against us, for to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they might put us to death, and carry us away captives into Babylon.
So Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, and all the people, obeyed not the voice of the Lord, to dwell in the land of Judah.
But Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, took all the remnant of Judah, that were returned from all nations, whither they had been driven, to dwell in the land of Judah;

Even men, and women, and children, and the king’s daughters, and every person that Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah.
So they came into the land of Egypt: for they obeyed not the voice of the Lord: thus came they even to Tahpanhes.

Then all the men which knew that their wives had burned incense unto other gods, and all the women that stood by, a great multitude, even all the people that dwelt in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
As for the word that thou hast spoken unto us in the name of the Lord, we will not hearken unto thee.

But we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, as we have done, we, and our fathers, our kings, and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem: for then had we plenty of victuals, and were well, and saw no evil.
But since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.
And when we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured out drink offerings unto her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings unto her, without our men?
Moreover Jeremiah said unto all the people, and to all the women, Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah that are in the land of Egypt:

Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saying; Ye and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hand, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her: ye will surely accomplish your vows, and surely perform your vows.

Therefore hear ye the word of the Lord, all Judah that dwell in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, saith the Lord, that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord God liveth.
Behold, I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them.

Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs.
And this shall be a sign unto you, saith the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, that ye may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil:

Thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will give Pharaoh–hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.
Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin:
That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!
Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.

cases.name: Moab and Ammon
cases.charge: Magnifying themselves against the Lord and against his people; rejoicing over the sanctuary when it was profaned
cases.summary: Lot's two sons, neighbours to Israel from the wilderness on, are judged in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos and Zephaniah for one long habit: pride against the Lord and gladness at Judah's ruin. Ammon ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge its border; Moab said, Aha, against the house of Judah.
cases.offense: We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud: of his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart. He shall be no more praised, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Of Ammon: because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity. Amos: they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.
cases.judgment: Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. Of Ammon: I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and Rabbah shall be a stable for camels; Zephaniah: Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation. Nebuchadnezzar came through both.

entries.commentary: This is the word of the Most High against Moab. Woe unto Nebo, for it is spoiled; Kiriathaim is confounded and taken. There shall be no more praise of Moab. In Heshbon they have devised evil against it: come, let us cut it off from being a nation. These are the Moabites, and God calls the so-called Chinese by that name.

A voice of crying goes up from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction. Moab is destroyed, and her little ones cause a cry to be heard. Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness. There is no standing against the judgment that is coming.

Because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken. Chemosh their god goes into captivity with his priests and princes together. The spoiler comes upon every city, and no city escapes. The valley perishes and the plain is destroyed, as the Most High has spoken.
Cursed be he that doeth the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood. The work of the Most High is not to be done half-heartedly.

Moab has been at ease from his youth and settled on his lees, never emptied from vessel to vessel, never gone into captivity. Therefore his taste remained in him and his scent is not changed. The Most High will send wanderers to empty his vessels and break their bottles, and Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel.

How say ye, we are mighty and strong men for the war? Moab is spoiled, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts. The calamity of Moab is near to come and his affliction hastens fast. All that know his name are to bemoan how the strong staff is broken.

The daughter that inhabits Dibon is told to come down from her glory and sit in thirst, for the spoiler of Moab comes upon her. The inhabitant of Aroer is to stand by the way and ask the one who flees, what is done. Moab is confounded, for it is broken down. Howl and cry, and tell it in Arnon that Moab is spoiled.

Judgment comes on the whole plain country, city by city, from Holon and Jahazah to Dibon, Nebo, Kiriathaim, Kerioth, and Bozrah, upon all the cities of Moab, far or near. The horn of Moab is cut off and her arm is broken. The strength of the nation is taken away by the Most High.

Make Moab drunken, for he magnified himself against the Lord, and he shall wallow in his own vomit and be in derision. The Most High asks, was not Israel a derision unto thee? Did the Lord not punish his own children? Then what makes the heathen think their time is not going to come? He punishes his own, so he will surely punish the wicked.

The pride of Moab is called out: exceedingly proud, his loftiness, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart. For all that pride, these Moabites will go back to their proper place and serve the nation of Israel for what they have done. The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for. -

The Most High declares he will howl and mourn for Moab, for the men of Kir-heres and the vine of Sibmah, because the spoiler is fallen upon the summer fruits and the vintage. Joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field. He will cause to cease in Moab him that offereth in the high places and him that burneth incense to his gods. The idolatry is cut off with the people.

The heart of the Most High sounds like pipes for Moab, because the riches he has gotten are perished. Every head shall be bald and every beard clipped, with cutting upon the hands and sackcloth upon the loins. A good majority of Moab bald their heads and shave their faces rather than keep their beards, the same as the Mongolians right next door to them. There shall be lamenting generally upon the housetops of Moab.

Moab is broken like a vessel wherein is no pleasure. They howl, asking how it is broken down, and Moab becomes a derision and a dismay to all around him. He that judges shall fly as an eagle and spread his wings over Moab. The mighty men's hearts that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pains, and Moab shall be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the Lord.

Fear, the pit, and the snare are upon the inhabitants of Moab. He that flees the fear falls into the pit, and he that climbs out of the pit is taken in the snare; there is no escape from the years of their visitation. A fire comes forth out of Heshbon and devours the corner of Moab. Woe unto Moab, for thy sons and thy daughters are taken captives.

Yet the Most High will bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. This has not happened yet, but it will come to pass, for he has spoken it and his word shall not return. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.

The word of the Most High comes against the Ammonites, the so-called Japanese, because they said Aha against His sanctuary when it was profaned, against the land of Israel when it was desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into captivity. Because they clapped their hands, stamped their feet, and rejoiced in heart with all their despite against Israel, cheering our destruction, He will deliver them to the men of the east for a possession, cut them off from the people, and cause them to perish, that they may know He is the Lord.

Because Moab, the so-called Chinese, and Seir say that the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen, claiming Judah is no longer the Most High's chosen people, judgment is pronounced against them. The Most High will open the side of Moab from his frontier cities, the glory of the country, and deliver them to the men of the east along with the Ammonites so that the Ammonites be not remembered among the nations, and He will execute judgments upon Moab.

Because Edom, the so-called white man, dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance and greatly offended, the Most High will stretch out His hand upon Edom, cut off man and beast, and make it desolate from Teman, and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword. He will lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to His anger and His fury. This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger to perform righteous recompense with our own hands. -

Because the Philistines dealt by revenge and took vengeance with a despiteful heart to destroy for the old hatred, never letting the feud go the way they always warred with us from the days of the judges, Samuel, Saul, and David, judgment comes upon them. The Most High will stretch out His hand upon the Philistines, cut off the Cherethims, destroy the remnant of the sea coast, and execute great vengeance with furious rebukes, that they may know He is the Lord when He lays His vengeance upon them.

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

For three transgressions of Moab and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime. Moab today is the Chinese. He will send a fire upon Moab that shall devour the palaces of Kerioth, and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet, and he will cut off the judge and slay all the princes with him.

For three transgressions of Judah and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they despised the law of the Lord, did not keep his commandments, and their lies caused them to err after which their fathers walked. This is the reason we are in captivity even today. Going back to the Assyrian captivity, our forefathers were rebellious against the Most High's laws, did not want to keep the commandments, and wanted to worship idols. He will send a fire upon Judah that shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.

For three transgressions of Israel and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes. That goes into oppression, and just like in today's time nobody wants to hear the righteous words of the Most High and keep the commandments; when you bring out the commandments you hear "what, I can't wear pants." They pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, turn aside the way of the meek, and a man and his father go in unto the same maid to profane the Most High's holy name. There were men even in that time going in unto their father's wife, and you may find a TV show today promoting that behavior. They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. -

Yet the Most High destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedar and who was strong as the oaks; he destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from beneath. The Amorite is another heathen nation. He brought Israel up from the land of Egypt, led them forty years through the wilderness to possess the land of the Amorite, and raised up their sons for prophets and their young men for Nazirites. You can use this to show that the children of Israel are the prophets of the Most High. But they gave the Nazirites wine to drink and commanded the prophets saying, prophesy not. That goes into lies and deceit, doing anything to stop the word of the Most High.

The Most High is pressed under them as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves; therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, the strong shall not strengthen his force, and the mighty shall not deliver himself, because Israel will be in captivity. He that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day; every possession you had will be stripped from you as you flee, the same way a robber coming to a bank strips everybody down and takes the goods.

Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; before the decree bring forth, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you. Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.

Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up. The word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant. The coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed thereupon: for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.

I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border. Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts. He will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness. This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation!

Send the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion, for the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon as a wandering bird cast out of the nest. Moab is told to take counsel, execute judgment, make her shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday, hide the outcasts, and not betray the one that wanders. She is asked to be a covert to the outcasts from the face of the spoiler. When the extortioner and spoiler are consumed out of the land, the throne shall be established in mercy, and one shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging and seeking judgment and hasting righteousness.

We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud, of his haughtiness and pride and wrath, but his lies shall not be so. Therefore Moab shall howl for Moab, everyone shall howl. For the foundations of Kirhareseth they shall mourn, surely they are stricken. The fields of Heshbon languish and the vine of Sibmah, whose principal plants the lords of the heathen have broken down; her branches are stretched out, gone over the sea.

The prophet bewails the vine of Sibmah with weeping and waters Heshbon and Elealeh with his tears, for the shouting over the summer fruits and harvest is fallen. Gladness and joy are taken away out of the plentiful field; in the vineyards there is no singing nor shouting, and the treaders tread out no wine in their presses, for the Most High has made the vintage shouting to cease. The prophet's inward parts sound like a harp for Moab and for Kirharesh, and when Moab wearies himself upon the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, he shall not prevail.

This is the word the Most High has spoken concerning Moab since that time. But now the Most High speaks, saying that within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be contemned with all that great multitude, and the remnant shall be very small and feeble.

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.
