cases.name: Nineveh under Nahum
cases.charge: A bloody city, full of lies and robbery, mistress of witchcrafts
cases.summary: Nahum charged Nineveh with bloodshed, lies, plunder, and the corruption of nations. The Lord who is slow to anger would not acquit the wicked. The city's defenses, commerce, and commanders would fail, and the peoples it had injured would rejoice at its overthrow.
cases.offense: Nahum charged Nineveh as a bloody city, full of lies and robbery, whose prey did not depart. Its power was pictured as a lions' dwelling filled with torn prey. Violence, deceit, and the entangling of nations had enriched the city and spread its injury abroad.
cases.judgment: The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace dissolved. Nineveh is laid waste; who will bemoan her? There is no healing of thy bruise. Tobit records hearing of its destruction by Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus before he died, and rejoicing over it.

entries.commentary: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite. God is jealous, and the Lord revengeth; the Lord revengeth, and is furious; the Lord will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth wrath for his enemies. The Lord is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the Lord hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet. The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt, and the earth is burned at his presence, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein. Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger? his fury is poured out like fire, and the rocks are thrown down by him.

The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him. With an overrunning flood he will make an utter end of the place thereof, and darkness shall pursue his enemies. What do ye imagine against the Lord? he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time. There is one come out of thee, that imagineth evil against the Lord, a wicked counsellor.

Though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more. For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder. The Lord hath given a commandment concerning thee, that no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the graven image and the molten image. Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace! O Judah, keep thy solemn feasts, perform thy vows: for the wicked shall no more pass through thee; he is utterly cut off. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

He that dasheth in pieces is come up before thy face: keep the munition, watch the way, make thy loins strong, fortify thy power mightily. For the Lord hath turned away the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel: for the emptiers have emptied them out, and marred their vine branches. The chariots shall be with flaming torches in the day of his preparation; they shall rage in the streets, they shall justle one against another in the broad ways: they shall seem like torches, they shall run like the lightnings.

The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be dissolved. Nineveh is of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee away. Stand, stand, shall they cry; but none shall look back. Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold: for there is none end of the store and glory out of all the pleasant furniture. She is empty, and void, and waste: and the heart melteth, and the knees smite together, and much pain is in all loins, and the faces of them all gather blackness.

Where is the dwelling of the lions, and the feedingplace of the young lions, where the lion, even the old lion, walked, and none made them afraid? The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps, and filled his holes with prey, and his dens with ravin. Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions: and I will cut off thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.

Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not. There is a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcases; and there is none end of their corpses; they stumble upon their corpses. Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts. Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts; and I will discover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will shew the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame. All they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?

Art thou better than populous No, that was situate among the rivers, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was from the sea? Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers. Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity: her young children also were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honourable men, and all her great men were bound in chains. Thou also shalt be drunken; all thy strong holds shall be like fig trees with the firstripe figs: if they be shaken, they shall even fall into the mouth of the eater. The gates of thy land shall be set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire shall devour thy bars.

Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds: there shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off. Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away. Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria: thy nobles shall dwell in the dust: thy people is scattered upon the mountains, and no man gathereth them. There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually? ---

Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; before the decree bring forth, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you. Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.

Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up. The word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant. The coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed thereupon: for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.

I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border. Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts. He will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness. This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation!

Woe is pronounced on those who decree unrighteous decrees and write grievous laws to turn aside the needy from judgment and take away the right from the poor. That is us: we are the needy, we are the poor. Back then this was the Assyrians doing it to us because of our disobedience. Today it is your friendly neighborhood white man writing unrighteous laws and prescribing them for us to keep. It is a twofold prophecy. The unrighteous decrees rob the widows and the fatherless. The question is put to the oppressor: what will you do in the day of visitation and desolation, to whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory. Without the Most High they bow down under the prisoners and fall under the slain, for His anger is not turned away and His hand is stretched out still.

The Most High calls the Assyrian the rod of His anger, the staff in their hand His indignation. He used nations to punish us. He sends the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, the people of His wrath, to take the spoil and tread them down like the mire of the streets. The Most High calls us hypocrites because we love to say we love the Most High, but we do not want to do what the Bible says. The Assyrian did not mean it that way; it was in his heart to destroy and cut off nations. He boasted of the kingdoms he conquered and their idols, not realizing the Most High was using him to punish us and the rest of the nations. We had graven images throughout our land, breaking the Most High's laws.

When the Most High has finished His work on Zion and Jerusalem, He will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria and the glory of his high looks. The Assyrian said, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent," boasting that he removed the treasures and inhabitants of the people on his own. The Most High asks whether the axe boasts against the one who hews with it, or the saw magnifies itself against the one who shakes it. The Assyrian was only the axe; the Most High used him to cut us down from rulership to captivity. Therefore the Most High sends leanness among the fat ones and kindles a burning fire that devours the thorns and briers in one day and consumes the glory of the forest, both soul and body, until the trees are so few a child may write them.

In that day the remnant of Israel and those who escaped of the house of Jacob shall no more stay upon him that smote them, but stay upon the Most High, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. This is a future prophecy. "Stay" means to rely upon. Just like back then, we still rely upon the ones who smote us, even today under the nation of Edom, trusting in oppression, relying on the very ones still smiting us in the streets. In that day the remnant, those keeping the Most High's commandments in their right mind, will escape and stop leaning on the oppressor. Though Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall return. The Most High will make a consumption decreed and overflowing with righteousness in the midst of all the land. -

The Most High tells His people who dwell in Zion not to be afraid of the Assyrian who smites with a rod and lifts up his staff after the manner of Egypt, for in a very little while the indignation will cease and His anger will turn to their destruction. The Most High will stir up a scourge for the Assyrian, and his yoke shall be taken off Israel's neck and destroyed because of the anointing. The chapter traces the invader's march through the towns until he shakes his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion. Then the Most High of hosts lops the bough with terror, the high ones are hewn down, and Lebanon falls by a mighty one.

verses.text: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
God is jealous, and the Lord revengeth; the Lord revengeth, and is furious; the Lord will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth wrath for his enemies.
The Lord is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the Lord hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.

And the Lord hath given a commandment concerning thee, that no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the graven image and the molten image: I will make thy grave; for thou art vile.
The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be dissolved.
And Huzzab shall be led away captive, she shall be brought up, and her maids shall lead her as with the voice of doves, tabering upon their breasts.
But Nineveh is of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee away. Stand, stand, shall they cry; but none shall look back.
Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold: for there is none end of the store and glory out of all the pleasant furniture.
She is empty, and void, and waste: and the heart melteth, and the knees smite together, and much pain is in all loins, and the faces of them all gather blackness.
Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not;
The noise of a whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of the pransing horses, and of the jumping chariots.

The horseman lifteth up both the bright sword and the glittering spear: and there is a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcases; and there is none end of their corpses; they stumble upon their corpses:
Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.
Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts; and I will discover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will shew the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.
And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gazingstock.
And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?
There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
And he will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness.

And flocks shall lie down in the midst of her, all the beasts of the nations: both the cormorant and the bittern shall lodge in the upper lintels of it; their voice shall sing in the windows; desolation shall be in the thresholds: for he shall uncover the cedar work.

This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down in! every one that passeth by her shall hiss, and wag his hand.
But before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineve, which was taken by Nabuchodonosor and Assuerus: and before his death he rejoiced over Nineve.
O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation.

I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
Howbeit he meaneth not so, neither doth his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy and cut off nations not a few.
For he saith, Are not my princes altogether kings?
Is not Calno as Carchemish? is not Hamath as Arpad? is not Samaria as Damascus?
As my hand hath found the kingdoms of the idols, and whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem and of Samaria;
Shall I not, as I have done unto Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

Wherefore it shall come to pass, that when the Lord hath performed his whole work upon mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks.

cases.name: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin
cases.charge: Weakening the hands of the people; hiring counsellors against them to frustrate the building of the house of God
cases.summary: The people of the land offered to help build the temple and were refused, and turned to hindrance: hired counsellors, letters to Artaxerxes, and a stop-work order enforced by force and power. The work lay still until the second year of Darius, whose decree turned the tables: whoever altered it would be hanged on timber from his own house.
cases.offense: The adversaries first offered to join the building, claiming to seek the same God. Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the chief fathers refused, declaring that they would build the house of the Lord according to Cyrus's command. The rejected offer was followed by open obstruction: the people of the land discouraged Judah, troubled the builders, and hired counselors to frustrate the work (Ezra 4:1-5). Ezra also records accusations against Jerusalem under later kings. Rehum and Shimshai represented the city as rebellious and warned that rebuilding would cost the king tribute and dominion. They obtained an order and enforced it by force and power (Ezra 4:11-23). Opposition clothed itself in concern for royal interests while working to weaken the returned people.
cases.judgment: When the temple work resumed under Haggai and Zechariah, the elders continued while the inquiry went to Darius. The eye of their God was upon them (Ezra 5:5). A search recovered Cyrus's decree, and Darius ordered the work left alone and its expenses supplied from the royal tribute (Ezra 6:1-10). His decree threatened severe punishment against anyone who altered it. The account does not record that penalty being executed upon the earlier adversaries. It records their obstruction overcome: the elders built, the house was finished, and the children of the captivity dedicated it with joy. The authority invoked to hinder the work now required that it be supplied.

verses.text: Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel;

Then they came to Zerubbabel, and to the chief of the fathers, and said unto them, Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do; and we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.

But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the fathers of Israel, said unto them, Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.
Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building,
And hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
This is the copy of the letter that they sent unto him, even unto Artaxerxes the king; Thy servants the men on this side the river, and at such a time.

Be it known unto the king, that the Jews which came up from thee to us are come unto Jerusalem, building the rebellious and the bad city, and have set up the walls thereof, and joined the foundations.
Be it known now unto the king, that, if this city be builded, and the walls set up again, then will they not pay toll, tribute, and custom, and so thou shalt endamage the revenue of the kings.
Now because we have maintenance from the king’s palace, and it was not meet for us to see the king’s dishonour, therefore have we sent and certified the king;

That search may be made in the book of the records of thy fathers: so shalt thou find in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful unto kings and provinces, and that they have moved sedition within the same of old time: for which cause was this city destroyed.
We certify the king that, if this city be builded again, and the walls thereof set up, by this means thou shalt have no portion on this side the river.

Now when the copy of king Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went up in haste to Jerusalem unto the Jews, and made them to cease by force and power.
Then ceased the work of the house of God which is at Jerusalem. So it ceased unto the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
Now therefore, Tatnai, governor beyond the river, Shethar–boznai, and your companions the Apharsachites, which are beyond the river, be ye far from thence:
Let the work of this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God in his place.

Moreover I make a decree what ye shall do to the elders of these Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the river, forthwith expenses be given unto these men, that they be not hindered.

And that which they have need of, both young bullocks, and rams, and lambs, for the burnt offerings of the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the appointment of the priests which are at Jerusalem, let it be given them day by day without fail:
That they may offer sacrifices of sweet savours unto the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king, and of his sons.
Also I have made a decree, that whosoever shall alter this word, let timber be pulled down from his house, and being set up, let him be hanged thereon; and let his house be made a dunghill for this.

And the God that hath caused his name to dwell there destroy all kings and people, that shall put to their hand to alter and to destroy this house of God which is at Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree; let it be done with speed.
Then Tatnai, governor on this side the river, Shethar–boznai, and their companions, according to that which Darius the king had sent, so they did speedily.

And the elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. And they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
But it came to pass, that when Sanballat heard that we builded the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked the Jews.

And he spake before his brethren and the army of Samaria, and said, What do these feeble Jews? will they fortify themselves? will they sacrifice? will they make an end in a day? will they revive the stones out of the heaps of the rubbish which are burned?
Now Tobiah the Ammonite was by him, and he said, Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall.
Hear, O our God; for we are despised: and turn their reproach upon their own head, and give them for a prey in the land of captivity:
And cover not their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from before thee: for they have provoked thee to anger before the builders.
So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.

entries.commentary: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin hear of the building and come to Zerubbabel asking to build with them, claiming to seek the same God since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assur. These were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, not true worshippers but taught only to appease the God of the land. -

Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the chief of the fathers refuse them: the strangers have nothing to do with building the house of the God of Israel. Israel would build to the Lord alone as Cyrus commanded. The forefathers understood that the work of the Most High is not shared with other nations.

The people of the land weaken the hands of Judah and trouble them in building. They hire counselors to frustrate the purpose all the days of Cyrus, even until the reign of Darius, a hindrance stretching across the kings in between.
In the reign of Ahasuerus and later Artaxerxes, the adversaries write accusations against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. The letter was written and interpreted in the Syrian tongue.

Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe write against Jerusalem, joined by the very nations the Assyrian king had set in the cities of Samaria. These are the same peoples named in [2 Kings 17](/bible/2-kings/17), brought over by the great and noble Asnappar, now bringing the accusation.

The letter warns the king that if Jerusalem is built the Jews will not pay toll, tribute, or custom, damaging the king's revenue. They call it a rebellious and hurtful city and urge the king to search the records to find cause to stop it.

The king answers that the records show Jerusalem made insurrection of old and had mighty kings who ruled beyond the river and received tribute. He commands the men to cease and the city not be built until another commandment is given from him.

When the letter is read, Rehum and Shimshai go up in haste to Jerusalem and make the Jews cease by force and power. The work of the house of God ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia. The same account, with a troop of horsemen halting the work, is told in 1 Esdras. -

Darius made search, and in the palace at Achmetha in the province of the Medes the roll was found recording the decree of Cyrus. The decree ordered the house rebuilt with strong foundations and set dimensions, the expenses given out of the king's house, and the gold and silver vessels restored to their place. Cyrus helped fund the rebuilding of the house of Israel.

Darius commanded Tatnai and his companions to leave the work alone and let the elders of the Jews build. He decreed that the cost be paid from the king's tribute beyond the river so the builders would not be hindered. Once a Persian decree was made it was upheld rather than vetoed. Even in Esther a decree against the Jews was not revoked but answered by a stronger decree in their favor. -

The king ordered daily provision of bullocks, rams, lambs, wheat, salt, wine, and oil so the priests could offer sacrifices without fail, and that they might pray for the life of the king and his sons. Whoever altered the decree was to be hanged on timber pulled from his own house, and his house made a dunghill. The God who caused his name to dwell there was called on to destroy any king or people who tried to destroy this house.

The elders prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah and finished the house by the commandment of the Most High and of the Persian kings. The house was finished, and the children of the captivity kept the dedication with joy, offering a hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve he goats for a sin offering according to the number of the tribes of Israel. This was a great praise, and the Levites' hands were full doing the service. The priests were set in their divisions and the Levites in their courses as it is written in the book of Moses, every man having his ordered task. -

The children of the captivity kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, for the priests and Levites were purified together and killed the passover for all the captivity. The passover can be kept in captivity with joyfulness and gladness of heart. Going back to the past shows how Israel is meant to operate, and these had the kingdom mindset to see the vision and finish the work.

When Sanballat hears that the wall is being built he is wroth, takes great indignation, and mocks the Jews. One of the heathen rulers rises up against the work, treating the rebuilding of Jerusalem as something to be scorned.

Before his brethren and the army of Samaria, Sanballat mocks the feeble Jews, asking if they will fortify themselves, sacrifice, finish in a day, and revive the burned stones out of the heaps of rubbish. He makes his mockery in front of his army, calling the people weak, the same way the heathen today mock the men who go out in one mind to do the work of the Most High.

Tobiah the Ammonite stands by him and says that even what they build, if a fox go up on it, would break down their stone wall. The enemy despises the work as flimsy, but the builders answer by praying that their reproach be turned upon their own head.

The wall is joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work. This is the pattern for Israel United in Christ today, a people with a mind to work who understand the condition of their people and the mission to rebuild their minds. -
Nehemiah answers the mockery with prayer, asking the Most High to turn the enemies' reproach upon their own heads.

When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites hear that the walls are going up and the breaches are being stopped, they are very wroth. The breaches are the weaker places the enemies expected would fail. When they hear those gaps are fortified, their anger rises because their expectation of failure is broken.
They conspire together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to hinder the work. Their whole plan is to cause the work to cease and keep the city from being rebuilt. -
The builders make prayer to the Most High and set a watch against the enemies day and night.

Judah says the strength of the bearers of burdens is decayed, there is much rubbish, and they are not able to build the wall. Even among the workers the burden grows heavy and discouragement sets in as the enemy pressure mounts.

The adversaries say they will not be known or seen until they come into the midst and slay them and cause the work to cease. The enemies plot a surprise attack, aiming to kill the builders and stop the work entirely.

Nehemiah sets the people in the lower and higher places behind the wall after their families with their swords, spears, and bows. He arms the people by family and posts them at the exposed places, ready to defend the work.

Nehemiah tells the nobles, rulers, and people not to be afraid but to remember the Lord, who is great and terrible, and to fight for their brethren, sons, daughters, wives, and houses. The answer to fear is to remember the greatness of the Most High and to fight for the family and the people.

From that time half of the servants work while the other half hold the spears, shields, and bows, and the rulers stand behind all of Judah. The people labor and guard at the same time, knowing the enemies are plotting against the rebuilding.
Those who bear burdens work with one hand and hold a weapon with the other. Every builder keeps a weapon ready even while laying the wall, watchful against attack.

Every builder has his sword girded by his side as he builds, and the one who sounds the trumpet stays by Nehemiah. The trumpet becomes the signal to gather, keeping the scattered workers ready to unite at the point of attack.

Nehemiah tells the people that the work is great and large and they are separated far from one another along the wall. Because the builders are spread out, they need a plan to come together quickly if the enemy strikes.
Wherever they hear the sound of the trumpet, they are to resort there, for the Most High shall fight for them. The confidence of the builders rests on the truth that their God fights for them.
They labor in the work, half of them holding the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appear. The people work from dawn to nightfall, giving the full day to the task.

Neither Nehemiah, his brethren, his servants, nor the men of the guard put off their clothes, saving only for washing. They are so serious about the work and so watchful that they stay dressed and ready at all times, of one mind to finish the wall, the same way the people are to be of one mind and one spirit today in the resurrection of the people.

cases.name: Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest
cases.charge: Obeying the voice of the Lord by Haggai; rising up and working on the house of the Lord
cases.summary: Sixteen years the temple foundation lay bare while the people built themselves ceiled houses and said the time was not come. Haggai spoke, and the governor and the high priest with the remnant of the people obeyed and came and worked, twenty-four days after the word. The Lord said, I am with you, and by Zechariah, not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
cases.offense: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him, and the people did fear before the Lord. And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God. Zechariah: Joshua stood before the angel clothed with filthy garments, and Satan at his right hand to resist him; and the Lord rebuked Satan and clothed him with change of raiment.
cases.judgment: Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. From this day will I bless you. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee. The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it. And the elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah, and finished it in the sixth year of Darius. Sirach names them together: Zorobabel, as a signet on the right hand; Jesus the son of Josedec, who set up the holy temple to the Lord.

entries.commentary: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the governor of Judah, and to Joshua the high priest. This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord's house should be built. Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?

Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes. Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord. Ye looked for much, and lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house. Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit. And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon all the labour of the hands.

Then Zerubbabel, and Joshua the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him; and the people did fear before the Lord. Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. The Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God. --- Topics: [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The word comes to Zerubbabel the governor of Judah, to Joshua the high priest, and to the residue of the people. Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory, and how do ye see it now? Is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing? The question is about the state of the people and the land, not the building alone. The temple was not reconstructed yet. Be strong, and work, for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts.

According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not. Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; and I will shake all nations. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, and in this place will I give peace. That has not come to fruition yet, because there is no peace in Israel now.

Ask now the priests concerning the law. If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy? The priests answered, No. If one that is unclean by a dead body touch any of these, shall it be unclean? The priests answered, It shall be unclean. Holiness does not spread by contact, but uncleanness does. So is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the Lord; and so is every work of their hands, and that which they offer there is unclean. The desire to serve the Most High in sincerity was not there among the remnant of Judah in that time.

Consider from this day and upward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord. When one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were but ten; when one came to the pressfat for to draw out fifty vessels out of the press, there were but twenty. I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands; yet ye turned not to me, saith the Lord. Israel has been afflicted repeatedly, captivity after captivity, and remained rebellious as a people.

Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day that the foundation of the Lord's temple was laid. Is the seed yet in the barn? Yea, as yet the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree, hath not brought forth: from this day will I bless you.

I will shake the heavens and the earth, and I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen. I will overthrow the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother. In that day will I take thee, O Zerubbabel my servant, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord of hosts. The Most High gave Haggai these prophecies to speak to Zerubbabel, showing him the things that are to come to pass. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

He shewed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him. The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan; even the Lord that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?

Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel. Take away the filthy garments from him. Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment. And they set a fair mitre upon his head. The garment is twofold. The change of raiment is Israel becoming righteous: keeping the commandments, putting the Most High first, and dealing rightly with him and with our own people.

If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by. Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at; for behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH. That is the remnant of Israel, Judah and Benjamin and Levi. Behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes: and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The angel came again and waked me, as a man that is wakened out of his sleep, and asked what I saw. A candlestick all of gold, with a bowl upon the top of it, and his seven lamps thereon, and seven pipes to the seven lamps. Two olive trees by it, one upon the right side of the bowl, and the other upon the left side thereof.

This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts. Who art thou, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it. The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it. Who hath despised the day of small things? Those seven are the eyes of the Lord, which run to and fro through the whole earth.

What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof, and these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves? These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.

Darius made search, and in the palace at Achmetha in the province of the Medes the roll was found recording the decree of Cyrus. The decree ordered the house rebuilt with strong foundations and set dimensions, the expenses given out of the king's house, and the gold and silver vessels restored to their place. Cyrus helped fund the rebuilding of the house of Israel.

Darius commanded Tatnai and his companions to leave the work alone and let the elders of the Jews build. He decreed that the cost be paid from the king's tribute beyond the river so the builders would not be hindered. Once a Persian decree was made it was upheld rather than vetoed. Even in Esther a decree against the Jews was not revoked but answered by a stronger decree in their favor. -

The king ordered daily provision of bullocks, rams, lambs, wheat, salt, wine, and oil so the priests could offer sacrifices without fail, and that they might pray for the life of the king and his sons. Whoever altered the decree was to be hanged on timber pulled from his own house, and his house made a dunghill. The God who caused his name to dwell there was called on to destroy any king or people who tried to destroy this house.

The elders prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah and finished the house by the commandment of the Most High and of the Persian kings. The house was finished, and the children of the captivity kept the dedication with joy, offering a hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve he goats for a sin offering according to the number of the tribes of Israel. This was a great praise, and the Levites' hands were full doing the service. The priests were set in their divisions and the Levites in their courses as it is written in the book of Moses, every man having his ordered task. -

The children of the captivity kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, for the priests and Levites were purified together and killed the passover for all the captivity. The passover can be kept in captivity with joyfulness and gladness of heart. Going back to the past shows how Israel is meant to operate, and these had the kingdom mindset to see the vision and finish the work.

verses.text: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying,
Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord’s house should be built.
Then came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet, saying,
Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?
Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.

Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.
Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.
Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord.

Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him, and the people did fear before the Lord.
Then spake Haggai the Lord’s messenger in the Lord’s message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord.

And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God,
In the four and twentieth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.

Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts:
According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not.
For thus saith the Lord of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land;
And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the Lord of hosts.
The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts.
The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the Lord of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the Lord of hosts.
Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day that the foundation of the Lord’s temple was laid, consider it.
Is the seed yet in the barn? yea, as yet the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree, hath not brought forth: from this day will I bless you.
And again the word of the Lord came unto Haggai in the four and twentieth day of the month, saying,
Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth;

And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen; and I will overthrow the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother.

In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the Lord, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord of hosts.
And he shewed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him.
And the Lord said unto Satan, The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan; even the Lord that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?
Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel.

And he answered and spake unto those that stood before him, saying, Take away the filthy garments from him. And unto him he said, Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment.
And I said, Let them set a fair mitre upon his head. So they set a fair mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments. And the angel of the Lord stood by.
And the angel of the Lord protested unto Joshua, saying,

Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by.
Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.
Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.
Moreover the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it; and thou shalt know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto you.

For who hath despised the day of small things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the Lord, which run to and fro through the whole earth.

And the elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. And they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
And the children of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of God with joy,
How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand:
So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to the Lord, which was prepared for everlasting glory.

cases.name: Ezra
cases.charge: Preparing his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments
cases.summary: A ready scribe in the law of Moses came up from Babylon with the king's letter and the king's silver, refused a guard because he had told the king the hand of God is on all that seek him, fasted at the river Ahava, and arrived. He read the law to the people from morning to midday, and they wept, and kept the feast of tabernacles as it had not been kept since Joshua.
cases.offense: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel (Ezra 7:10). The charge of teaching began with the ordering of his own heart and conduct. Royal favor supplied authority and provisions, but his commission remained governed by God's law. At Ahava he gathered the travelers, obtained ministers for the sanctuary, and proclaimed a fast to seek a right way for the people, their little ones, and their substance. Having testified that God's hand was upon those who sought Him, he was ashamed to request soldiers for protection. He also weighed the treasure into appointed hands and required it to be watched and weighed again at Jerusalem (Ezra 8:21-34). Trust in God was joined to careful stewardship.
cases.judgment: And the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him. Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king's heart, to beautify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem. The hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy, and of such as lay in wait by the way. And all the people went their way to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, because they had understood the words that were declared unto them. Since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.
offenseFull: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel (Ezra 7:10). The charge of teaching began with the ordering of his own heart and conduct. Royal favor supplied authority and provisions, but his commission remained governed by God's law.

At Ahava he gathered the travelers, obtained ministers for the sanctuary, and proclaimed a fast to seek a right way for the people, their little ones, and their substance. Having testified that God's hand was upon those who sought Him, he was ashamed to request soldiers for protection. He also weighed the treasure into appointed hands and required it to be watched and weighed again at Jerusalem (Ezra 8:21-34). Trust in God was joined to careful stewardship.
judgmentFull: The Lord delivered the company from enemies along the way. The treasure arrived and was counted and weighed in the house of God. The good hand acknowledged before the journey was acknowledged after it.

At the water gate, Ezra read the law while the Levites gave the sense so the congregation understood. The people wept, received instruction to rejoice and share with those lacking provision, and kept the feast in booths (Nehemiah 8:1-18). The fruit of teaching was understanding followed by obedience, not merely the public reading of words.

entries.commentary: Ezra's genealogy is traced back through Zadok and Phinehas to Eleazar the son of Aaron the chief priest, marking him a priest of the true line. Ezra went up from Babylon a ready scribe in the law of Moses, and the king granted all his requests because the hand of the Most High was upon him.

Some of the children of Israel, priests, Levites, singers, porters, and Nethinims went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes, and Ezra came in the fifth month by the good hand of his God. Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others. -

Artaxerxes' letter names Ezra a scribe of the law of the God of heaven and grants that any of Israel who willingly desire may go up to Jerusalem with him. The king and his counselors freely offered silver and gold for the house of God, for sacrifices, and for whatever else was needful, drawn even from the king's treasure house. This was favor, letting the captivity return with the treasures of Babylon, as the nations will one day bring back all Israel's substance. -

Artaxerxes decreed to the treasurers beyond the river to supply Ezra speedily with silver, wheat, wine, oil, and salt, so that no wrath would come against the king and his sons. The priests, Levites, singers, porters, and Nethinims were freed from toll, tribute, and custom. This is using the favor of those set over you without abusing it, being granted the freedom the world around still had to pay.

Ezra was told, after the wisdom of his God in his hand, to set magistrates and judges to judge the people and to teach those who did not know the laws of the Most High. The king decreed judgment on any who would not do the law of God and the law of the king. Ezra then blessed the Most High who put it in the king's heart to beautify the house, and was strengthened as the hand of his God was upon him. A heathen king supported the work of the prophets even though he was not an Israelite.

The chief of the fathers and their genealogy are recorded, listing the heads of families who went up with Ezra from Babylon and the number of males with each. Every name is set down deliberately. These were actual people who put their work into the building of the house, and names mean something, which is why Israel desires their names written in the book.

Ezra gathered the company at the river Ahava, abode three days, and viewing the people found none of the sons of Levi, so he sent men of understanding to Iddo at Casiphia to bring ministers for the house. By the good hand of the Most High they brought back men of understanding of the sons of Levi and a large number of Nethinims appointed for the service, all expressed by name. Ezra knew which men among him had understanding and called on them.

Ezra proclaimed a fast at the river Ahava that they might afflict their souls before the Most High and seek of him a right way for themselves, their little ones, and their substance. To afflict the soul is to fast, taking neither food nor water, and one may fast and pray for wisdom and a right path. Ezra was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help against the enemy in the way, having testified that the hand of God is upon all who seek him for good. -

--- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

All the people gather as one man into the street before the water gate and ask Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses. He reads before the congregation of men, women, and all that could understand, from morning until midday. The Most High does not favor camps and closed rooms. Ezra stood in the open street to teach, men and women together, and the people were attentive to the words of the law.

Ezra stands upon a pulpit of wood with brothers on his right hand and brothers on his left hand, and opens the book in the sight of all the people, blessing the Most High, to whom the people answer, Amen, Amen. The Levites cause the people to understand the law, reading distinctly and giving the sense so the people understood the reading. Teaching is meant to bring understanding, not merely to be recited.

Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites tell the people the day is holy and they should not mourn or weep, for the people wept when they heard the words of the law. They are told to eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared, for the joy of the Most High is their strength. The people go their way to make great mirth because they understood the words that were declared.

On the second day the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gather to Ezra to understand the words of the law, and they find written that Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month. -

After these things, when Artaxerxes the king of the Persians reigned, came Esdras, of the line of Aaron the chief priest. This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a scribe, being very ready in the law of Moses, that was given by the God of Israel. The king did honour him: for he found grace in his sight in all his requests. Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.

The commission written from Artaxerxes gave order that such of the nation of the Jews, and of the priests and Levites, as were willing should go with Esdras unto Jerusalem. They were to look unto the affairs of Judea and Jerusalem, agreeably to that which is in the law of the Lord, and to carry the gifts unto the Lord of Israel to Jerusalem. Whatsoever Esdras the priest and reader of the law of the most high God should send for, the keepers of the treasuries in Syria and Phenice should give it him with speed. Let all things be performed after the law of God diligently unto the most high God, that wrath come not upon the kingdom of the king and his sons. No tax nor any other imposition was to be required of the priests, Levites, holy singers, porters, ministers of the temple, or any that have doings in this temple. Thou, Esdras, according to the wisdom of God, ordain judges and justices, that they may judge in all Syria and Phenice: all those that know the law of thy God thou shalt teach, and those that know it not.

Blessed be the only Lord God of my fathers, who hath put these things into the heart of the king, to glorify his house that is in Jerusalem. Therefore was I encouraged by the help of the Lord my God, and gathered together men of Israel to go up with me.

These are the chief, according to their families and several dignities, that went up with Esdras from Babylon in the reign of king Artaxerxes, counted family by family with the number of men. They gathered together at the river called Theras, where they pitched their tents three days, and Esdras surveyed them. When he found there none of the priests and Levites, he sent unto the principal men and learned, that they should send such men as might execute the priest's office in the house of the Lord. By the mighty hand of the Lord they brought unto them skilful men of the sons of Moli the son of Levi, the son of Israel, and of the ministers of the temple whom David had ordained.

There Esdras vowed a fast unto the young men before the Lord, to desire of him a prosperous journey both for them and their children and their cattle. I was ashamed to ask the king footmen and horsemen and conduct for safeguard against our adversaries; for we had said unto the king, that the power of the Lord our God should be with them that seek him, to support them in all ways. Then I separated twelve of the chief of the priests, and weighed them the gold, and the silver, and the holy vessels of the house of our Lord, which the king and his council and the princes and all Israel had given. Ye are holy unto the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the gold and the silver is a vow unto the Lord of our fathers: watch ye, and keep them till ye deliver them to the chief of the priests and Levites at Jerusalem.

From the river Theras we departed the twelfth day of the first month, and came to Jerusalem by the mighty hand of our Lord, which was with us. From the beginning of our journey the Lord delivered us from every enemy, and so we came to Jerusalem. When we had been there three days, the gold and silver that was weighed was delivered in the house of our Lord on the fourth day, all by number and weight, and the whole weight of them was written up the same hour. They that were come out of the captivity offered sacrifice unto the Lord God of Israel, even twelve bullocks for all Israel, fourscore and sixteen rams, threescore and twelve lambs, and twelve goats for a peace offering.

The rulers came unto Esdras and said, The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles. For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity. As soon as I had heard these things, I rent my clothes and the holy garment, and pulled off the hair from off my head and beard, and sat me down sad and very heavy. Rising up from the fast with my clothes and the holy garment rent, and bowing my knees, and stretching forth my hands unto the Lord, I said, O Lord, I am confounded and ashamed before thy face. For our sins are multiplied above our heads, and our ignorances have reached up unto heaven, for ever since the time of our fathers we have been and are in great sin, even unto this day.

In some measure hath mercy been shewed unto us from thee, O Lord, that there should be left us a root and a name in the place of thy sanctuary, and to give us food in the time of our servitude. When we were in bondage we were not forsaken of our Lord, but he made us gracious before the kings of Persia, so that they gave us food, and honoured the temple of our Lord, and raised up the desolate Sion. We have transgressed thy commandments, which thou gavest by the hand of thy servants the prophets, saying, The land which ye enter into to possess as an heritage is a land polluted with the pollutions of the strangers of the land. Therefore now shall ye not join your daughters unto their sons, neither shall ye take their daughters unto your sons; and ye shall never seek to have peace with them, that ye may be strong, and eat the good things of the land, and leave the inheritance of the land unto your children for evermore. All that is befallen is done unto us for our wicked works and great sins; but thou, O Lord, didst make our sins light, and didst give unto us such a root: yet we have turned back again to transgress thy law, and to mingle ourselves with the uncleanness of the nations of the land.

As Esdras in his prayer made his confession, weeping, and lying flat upon the ground before the temple, there gathered unto him from Jerusalem a very great multitude of men and women and children, and there was great weeping among the multitude. Then Jechonias the son of Jeelus, one of the sons of Israel, called out and said, O Esdras, we have sinned against the Lord God, we have married strange women of the nations of the land. Let us make an oath to the Lord, that we will put away all our wives, which we have taken of the heathen, with their children, like as thou hast decreed, and as many as do obey the law of the Lord. Arise, and put in execution: for to thee doth this matter appertain, and we will be with thee: do valiantly. So Esdras arose, and took an oath of the chief of the priests and Levites of all Israel to do after these things; and so they sware. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

verses.text: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him.
And there went up some of the children of Israel, and of the priests, and the Levites, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinims, unto Jerusalem, in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
For upon the first day of the first month began he to go up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month came he to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.
Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem:

And hath extended mercy unto me before the king, and his counsellors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. And I was strengthened as the hand of the Lord my God was upon me, and I gathered together out of Israel chief men to go up with me.
Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the river of Ahava, that we might afflict ourselves before our God, to seek of him a right way for us, and for our little ones, and for all our substance.

For I was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy in the way: because we had spoken unto the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him; but his power and his wrath is against all them that forsake him.
So we fasted and besought our God for this: and he was intreated of us.

Then we departed from the river of Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go unto Jerusalem: and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy, and of such as lay in wait by the way.
And we came to Jerusalem, and abode there three days.

And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded to Israel.
And Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation both of men and women, and all that could hear with understanding, upon the first day of the seventh month.

And he read therein before the street that was before the water gate from the morning until midday, before the men and the women, and those that could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.

And Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people; (for he was above all the people;) and when he opened it, all the people stood up:
And Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God. And all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands: and they bowed their heads, and worshipped the Lord with their faces to the ground.

Also Jeshua, and Bani, and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law: and the people stood in their place.
So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.

And Nehemiah, which is the Tirshatha, and Ezra the priest the scribe, and the Levites that taught the people, said unto all the people, This day is holy unto the Lord your God; mourn not, nor weep. For all the people wept, when they heard the words of the law.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
So the Levites stilled all the people, saying, Hold your peace, for the day is holy; neither be ye grieved.
And all the people went their way to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, because they had understood the words that were declared unto them.
And on the second day were gathered together the chief of the fathers of all the people, the priests, and the Levites, unto Ezra the scribe, even to understand the words of the law.
And they found written in the law which the Lord had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month:

And that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, Go forth unto the mount, and fetch olive branches, and pine branches, and myrtle branches, and palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make booths, as it is written.

So the people went forth, and brought them, and made themselves booths, every one upon the roof of his house, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the street of the water gate, and in the street of the gate of Ephraim.

And all the congregation of them that were come again out of the captivity made booths, and sat under the booths: for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.

Also day by day, from the first day unto the last day, he read in the book of the law of God. And they kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day was a solemn assembly, according unto the manner.
And after these things, when Artexerxes the king of the Persians reigned came Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Ezerias, the son of Helchiah, the son of Salum,

The son of Sadduc, the son of Achitob, the son of Amarias, the son of Ezias, the son of Meremoth, the son of Zaraias, the son of Savias, the son of Boccas, the son of Abisum, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest.
This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a scribe, being very ready in the law of Moses, that was given by the God of Israel.
And the king did him honour: for he found grace in his sight in all his requests.
There went up with him also certain of the children of Israel, of the priest of the Levites, of the holy singers, porters, and ministers of the temple, unto Jerusalem,

In the seventh year of the reign of Artexerxes, in the fifth month, this was the king’s seventh year; for they went from Babylon in the first day of the first month, and came to Jerusalem, according to the prosperous journey which the Lord gave them.
For Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.
Now the copy of the commission, which was written from Artexerxes the king, and came to Esdras the priest and reader of the law of the Lord, is this that followeth;

cases.name: The returned exiles who married strange wives
cases.charge: Mingling the holy seed with the peoples of the lands
cases.summary: Ezra was told that the people, priests, and Levites had taken wives of the Canaanites, Hittites, Ammonites, Moabites, and Egyptians, and that the princes and rulers had been chief in the trespass. He rent his garment and sat astonished until the evening sacrifice. A generation later Nehemiah found children who could not speak the Jews' language.
cases.offense: The returned people, including priests and Levites, had joined themselves in marriage to the peoples whose abominations Ezra named. The princes and rulers were chief in the trespass (Ezra 9:1-2). Deuteronomy had warned against the marriages it forbade because they would turn Israel's children from following the Lord to serving other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Ezra's grief measured the offense against the mercy already received. God had punished them less than their iniquities deserved and given a remnant deliverance. To return to the forbidden alliances after that revival was to disregard both the command and the lesson of captivity (Ezra 9:13-15).
cases.judgment: The congregation wept and covenanted to put away the strange wives and the children born of them. The matter was examined at appointed times with the elders and judges, beginning in the tenth month and ending by the first day of the first month. Priests found guilty gave their hands to the separation and offered a ram for their trespass (Ezra 10:2-19). Later Nehemiah confronted renewed offenses and recalled Solomon, whom outlandish women had caused to sin. He drove away the priestly descendant allied by marriage to Sanballat (Nehemiah 13:23-29). The leaders' position did not exempt them from the covenant obligations they were responsible to uphold.
