verses.text: And before this, Eliashib the priest, having the oversight of the chamber of the house of our God, was allied unto Tobiah:

And he had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime they laid the meat offerings, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithes of the corn, the new wine, and the oil, which was commanded to be given to the Levites, and the singers, and the porters; and the offerings of the priests.
But in all this time was not I at Jerusalem: for in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon came I unto the king, and after certain days obtained I leave of the king:
And I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.
And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.
Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, with the meat offering and the frankincense.
And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.
Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.
Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters unto Tobiah, and the letters of Tobiah came unto them.
For there were many in Judah sworn unto him, because he was the son in law of Shechaniah the son of Arah; and his son Johanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah.
Also they reported his good deeds before me, and uttered my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear.

But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?
Then answered I them, and said unto them, The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.
Now Tobiah the Ammonite was by him, and he said, Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall.
An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever:
Because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.
On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever;
Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.
Now it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.

lawDetails.text: No Ammonite or Moabite (those of another race). shall enter the assembly of the LORD; none of their descendants, even to the tenth generation, shall ever enter the assembly of the LORD.

entries.commentary: On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing. When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off. -

Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid. Nehemiah was away in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he returned and understood the evil, he cast all Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber, cleansed the chambers, and brought back the vessels of the house of God with the meat offering and the frankincense.

Nehemiah found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so the Levites and singers had fled every one to his field, and he contended with the rulers and set the Levites back in their place. He made treasurers over the treasuries, faithful men, to distribute unto their brethren, and prayed, Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.

Nehemiah saw men in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, and figs into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath. He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment. -

When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded them shut and set his servants at the gates so no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath, and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. He testified against them and warned that if they came again he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. He then commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women. -

One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah chased him away because he had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites. Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are. -

When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian, and the rest of the enemies hear that the wall is built with no breach left, though the doors are not yet set on the gates, they turn to another plan. With the wall standing, the enemies shift from open threat to schemes against Nehemiah himself.
Sanballat and Geshem send for Nehemiah to meet together in one of the villages in the plain of Ono, but they think to do him mischief. The invitation is a trap to draw Nehemiah away and harm him.

Nehemiah sends messengers saying he is doing a great work and cannot come down, asking why the work should cease while he leaves it to come to them. Nehemiah uses wisdom, refusing to leave the work for a meeting he knows is a plot to put him to death.
They send to him four times after the same manner, and he answers them the same way each time. The enemies keep pressing, and Nehemiah keeps giving the same steady refusal.
The fifth time Sanballat sends his servant with an open letter in his hand. The open letter is meant to be read by others, a public pressure tactic against Nehemiah.

The letter reports among the heathen, and Geshem says it, that Nehemiah and the Jews think to rebel and that this is why he builds the wall, that he may be their king. The enemies invent a charge of rebellion to frighten Nehemiah and give the king cause against him.

The letter claims Nehemiah has appointed prophets to proclaim him king in Judah and threatens to report it to the king, inviting him to take counsel together. The false report is designed to force Nehemiah into their meeting under fear.
Nehemiah answers that there are no such things done as they say, but that they feign them out of their own heart. Nehemiah plainly names the accusation as an invention of their own minds.

They all try to make the builders afraid, saying their hands shall be weakened so the work is not done, and Nehemiah prays for the Most High to strengthen his hands. The whole aim is to weaken the hands and stop the work, so Nehemiah turns to the Most High for strength.

Shemaiah, shut up in his house, tells Nehemiah to meet within the temple and shut the doors because men will come to slay him in the night. A hired man tries to lure Nehemiah into hiding in the temple, framing it as safety.

Nehemiah answers, should such a man as I flee, and who, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life, and says he will not go in. Nehemiah refuses to run or to misuse the temple to save himself, standing firm in his place.

Nehemiah perceives that the Most High had not sent Shemaiah, but that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him to pronounce this prophecy. Nehemiah discerns the false prophecy and sees the hand of the enemies who paid for it.

Shemaiah was hired so that Nehemiah would be afraid, do so, and sin, giving them matter for an evil report to reproach him. The scheme is to trap Nehemiah into a fearful sin they could use to shame him.

Nehemiah asks the Most High to think upon Tobiah, Sanballat, the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets who would have put him in fear according to their works. He commits the hired accusers and false prophets to the judgment of the Most High.
The wall is finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days. Despite all the plots, the whole wall is completed in fifty-two days.

When the enemies and all the heathen about them hear of it, they are much cast down in their own eyes, for they perceive that the work was wrought of the Most High. The completed wall shames the enemies, who recognize that this was the work and pleasure of the Most High.
In those days the nobles of Judah send many letters to Tobiah, and his letters come to them. Even inside Judah some remain tied to Tobiah, keeping a line of communication with the enemy.

Many in Judah are sworn to Tobiah because he is the son-in-law of Shechaniah and his son married the daughter of Meshullam. Marriage alliances bind some of Judah to the enemy, dividing loyalty within the people.

They report Tobiah's good deeds before Nehemiah and carry Nehemiah's words to Tobiah, and Tobiah sends letters to put him in fear. To the end the enemy uses those inside to pressure and frighten Nehemiah, the same way anything that can be done to stop the work of the Most High is still done today, and the people must keep their spiritual eyes open to see it. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

In the month Nisan in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, wine is before him and Nehemiah takes up the wine and gives it to the king. This is Artaxerxes the first, the king that came after Ahasuerus of the book of Esther. Nehemiah had not before been sad in the king's presence, for a cupbearer must be of a cheerful countenance, so the king asks why his countenance is sad seeing he is not sick, saying this is nothing but sorrow of heart, and Nehemiah is very sore afraid.

Nehemiah answers, Let the king live for ever, why should not his countenance be sad when the city, the place of his fathers' sepulchres, lies waste and its gates are consumed with fire. The king asks what request he makes, and Nehemiah prays to the God of heaven before he answers, seeking the Most High even in that moment before the king.

Nehemiah asks that if it please the king and if his servant have found favour, the king would send him to Judah, to the city of his fathers' sepulchres, that he may build it. The king, the queen also sitting by him, asks how long his journey would be and when he would return, so Nehemiah sets him a time, and it pleased the king to send him.

Nehemiah asks for letters to the governors beyond the river to convey him until he comes into Judah, and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king's forest to give him timber for the beams of the gates, the wall, and the house he would enter. The king grants him all this according to the good hand of his God upon him. Nehemiah had already prayed, and the Most High heard him and put it upon the king's heart to allow him to go. -

Nehemiah comes to the governors beyond the river and gives them the king's letters, and the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with him, an armed escort to see him safe. When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, hear of it, it grieves them exceedingly that a man has come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before. -

Nehemiah comes to Jerusalem and is there three days, then arises in the night with a few men, telling no man what his God had put in his heart to do, for saying too much could ruin the plan. He goes out by night through the gate of the valley, past the dragon well to the dung port, and views the walls of Jerusalem broken down and the gates consumed with fire, then goes on to the gate of the fountain and the king's pool. The rulers do not know where he went or what he did, neither had he yet told the Jews, priests, nobles, rulers, or the rest that did the work.

Nehemiah then tells them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lies waste and its gates are burned; come and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem that we be no more a reproach. He tells them of the good hand of his God upon him and the king's words, and they say, Let us rise up and build, and strengthen their hands for this good work. What is admirable in Nehemiah, as in Ezra, is that he never says the work was of his own knowledge or wisdom, but that the Lord's hand was upon him, and he puts that same vision on the men around him so they strengthen their hands to help.

When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian hear it, they laugh them to scorn, despise them, and ask what this thing is, and whether they will rebel against the king. Nehemiah answers that the God of heaven will prosper them, and his servants will arise and build, but the mockers have no portion nor right nor memorial in Jerusalem. There was no shame in what he came to do. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

When Sanballat hears that the wall is being built he is wroth, takes great indignation, and mocks the Jews. One of the heathen rulers rises up against the work, treating the rebuilding of Jerusalem as something to be scorned.

Before his brethren and the army of Samaria, Sanballat mocks the feeble Jews, asking if they will fortify themselves, sacrifice, finish in a day, and revive the burned stones out of the heaps of rubbish. He makes his mockery in front of his army, calling the people weak, the same way the heathen today mock the men who go out in one mind to do the work of the Most High.

Tobiah the Ammonite stands by him and says that even what they build, if a fox go up on it, would break down their stone wall. The enemy despises the work as flimsy, but the builders answer by praying that their reproach be turned upon their own head.

The wall is joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work. This is the pattern for Israel United in Christ today, a people with a mind to work who understand the condition of their people and the mission to rebuild their minds. -
Nehemiah answers the mockery with prayer, asking the Most High to turn the enemies' reproach upon their own heads.

When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites hear that the walls are going up and the breaches are being stopped, they are very wroth. The breaches are the weaker places the enemies expected would fail. When they hear those gaps are fortified, their anger rises because their expectation of failure is broken.
They conspire together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to hinder the work. Their whole plan is to cause the work to cease and keep the city from being rebuilt. -
The builders make prayer to the Most High and set a watch against the enemies day and night.

Judah says the strength of the bearers of burdens is decayed, there is much rubbish, and they are not able to build the wall. Even among the workers the burden grows heavy and discouragement sets in as the enemy pressure mounts.

The adversaries say they will not be known or seen until they come into the midst and slay them and cause the work to cease. The enemies plot a surprise attack, aiming to kill the builders and stop the work entirely.

Nehemiah sets the people in the lower and higher places behind the wall after their families with their swords, spears, and bows. He arms the people by family and posts them at the exposed places, ready to defend the work.

Nehemiah tells the nobles, rulers, and people not to be afraid but to remember the Lord, who is great and terrible, and to fight for their brethren, sons, daughters, wives, and houses. The answer to fear is to remember the greatness of the Most High and to fight for the family and the people.

From that time half of the servants work while the other half hold the spears, shields, and bows, and the rulers stand behind all of Judah. The people labor and guard at the same time, knowing the enemies are plotting against the rebuilding.
Those who bear burdens work with one hand and hold a weapon with the other. Every builder keeps a weapon ready even while laying the wall, watchful against attack.

Every builder has his sword girded by his side as he builds, and the one who sounds the trumpet stays by Nehemiah. The trumpet becomes the signal to gather, keeping the scattered workers ready to unite at the point of attack.

Nehemiah tells the people that the work is great and large and they are separated far from one another along the wall. Because the builders are spread out, they need a plan to come together quickly if the enemy strikes.
Wherever they hear the sound of the trumpet, they are to resort there, for the Most High shall fight for them. The confidence of the builders rests on the truth that their God fights for them.
They labor in the work, half of them holding the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appear. The people work from dawn to nightfall, giving the full day to the task.

Neither Nehemiah, his brethren, his servants, nor the men of the guard put off their clothes, saving only for washing. They are so serious about the work and so watchful that they stay dressed and ready at all times, of one mind to finish the wall, the same way the people are to be of one mind and one spirit today in the resurrection of the people.

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

cases.name: The Sabbath traders of Jerusalem and Tyre
cases.charge: Treading winepresses, bringing in sheaves, and selling fish and wares on the Sabbath
cases.summary: Nehemiah saw men of Judah treading winepresses and loading asses on the Sabbath, and Tyrian merchants selling fish in Jerusalem on the holy day. He testified against the nobles, shut the gates at dusk, set his own servants to guard them, and threatened to lay hands on the merchants who camped outside.
cases.offense: Nehemiah saw men treading winepresses, loading animals, and bringing produce into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. Men of Tyre sold fish and other wares to Judah within the city. He contended with the nobles because this trade profaned the day they were charged to sanctify (Nehemiah 13:15-17). He reminded them that their fathers' conduct had brought evil upon the city. Returning from captivity and rebuilding Jerusalem did not authorize a return to the practices for which it had suffered. Jeremiah had likewise warned against carrying burdens through its gates on the Sabbath (Jeremiah 17:21-27).
cases.judgment: The merchants lodged outside the wall once or twice; Nehemiah warned them, and from that time forth came they no more on the sabbath. He commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also.
offenseFull: Nehemiah saw men treading winepresses, loading animals, and bringing produce into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. Men of Tyre sold fish and other wares to Judah within the city. He contended with the nobles because this trade profaned the day they were charged to sanctify (Nehemiah 13:15-17).

He reminded them that their fathers' conduct had brought evil upon the city. Returning from captivity and rebuilding Jerusalem did not authorize a return to the practices for which it had suffered. Jeremiah had likewise warned against carrying burdens through its gates on the Sabbath (Jeremiah 17:21-27).

entries.commentary: On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing. When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off. -

Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid. Nehemiah was away in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he returned and understood the evil, he cast all Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber, cleansed the chambers, and brought back the vessels of the house of God with the meat offering and the frankincense.

Nehemiah found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so the Levites and singers had fled every one to his field, and he contended with the rulers and set the Levites back in their place. He made treasurers over the treasuries, faithful men, to distribute unto their brethren, and prayed, Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.

Nehemiah saw men in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, and figs into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath. He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment. -

When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded them shut and set his servants at the gates so no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath, and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. He testified against them and warned that if they came again he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. He then commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women. -

One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah chased him away because he had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites. Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are. -

The Most High showed Amos a basket of summer fruit and said the end is come upon his people of Israel, and he will not again pass by them anymore. The songs of the temple shall be howlings in that day, and there shall be many dead bodies in every place, cast forth with silence.

Hear this, you that swallow up the needy and make the poor of the land to fail, longing for the new moon and the sabbath to be gone so you may sell corn and set forth wheat. They make the ephah small and the shekel great, falsify the balances by deceit, and buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of shoes, selling the refuse of the wheat. This shows the wickedness of our people, more willing to pursue business than to follow the commandments of the Lord, and to deal deceitfully with one another rather than keep the commandments.

The Lord has sworn by the excellency of Jacob that he will never forget any of their works, and the land shall tremble and rise up wholly as a flood. He will cause the sun to go down at noon and darken the earth in the clear day. He will turn their feasts into mourning and their songs into lamentations, bring sackcloth upon all loins and baldness upon every head, and make it as the mourning of an only son.

The Most High will send a famine in the land, not of bread nor thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord, and men shall wander from sea to sea and run to and fro to seek the word and not find it. In that day the fair virgins and young men shall faint for thirst, and they that swear by the sin of Samaria and by the god of Dan and the manner of Beersheba shall fall and never rise up again. This last verse shows that the tribe of Dan was going to fall and never rise again. That is why Dan does not have a gate. Dan fell and did not rise up again as a tribe.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

The Most High tells the prophet to cry aloud and spare not, to lift up his voice like a trumpet and show the people their transgression and the house of Jacob their sins. The people seek him daily and delight to know his ways as a nation that did righteousness, and they ask why they have fasted and afflicted their soul and he has taken no knowledge of it.

Their fasting is for strife and debate and to smite with the fist of wickedness, and such a fast will not make their voice to be heard on high. The Most High is not looking for a man to bow his head like a bulrush and spread sackcloth and ashes. The fast he has chosen is to loose the bands of wickedness, undo the heavy burdens, let the oppressed go free, break every yoke, deal thy bread to the hungry, bring the poor that are cast out to thy house, and cover the naked. The reward is that thy light breaks forth as the morning, thy health springs forth speedily, thy righteousness goes before thee, and the glory of the Lord is thy reward; then thou shalt call and the Lord shall answer. "The putting forth of the finger" is when you blame other people. Somebody comes and says a brother did this or that, and instead of taking it, the brother says, "no, but what about her, look what she did." You have to take accountability for your own actions; this is about taking accountability.

If thou draw out thy soul to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, thy light shall rise in obscurity and thy darkness be as the noonday, and the Lord shall guide thee continually and make fat thy bones. Thou shalt be like a watered garden and a spring of water whose waters fail not, and they that come of thee shall build the old waste places and be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy own pleasure on his holy day, and call the sabbath a delight and honor him, then thou shalt delight thyself in the Lord. He will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken it.

verses.text: In those days saw I in Judah some treading wine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals.
There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish, and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?
Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.

And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.
So the merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without Jerusalem once or twice.
Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath.

And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.
Thus saith the Lord; Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem;
Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.
But they obeyed not, neither inclined their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, nor receive instruction.

But if ye will not hearken unto me to hallow the sabbath day, and not to bear a burden, even entering in at the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day; then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.
Hear this, O ye that swallow up the needy, even to make the poor of the land to fail,
Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?
That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes; yea, and sell the refuse of the wheat?
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:

But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:

cases.name: Bigthan and Teresh
cases.charge: Conspiring to lay hands on king Ahasuerus
cases.summary: Two chamberlains who kept the door were wroth and sought to lay hand on the king. Mordecai heard of it and told Esther, who told the king in Mordecai's name. They were hanged, and the thing was written in the chronicles, where a sleepless king found it years later on the night before Haman meant to hang Mordecai.
cases.offense: Bigthan and Teresh were chamberlains entrusted with keeping the door. In their anger they sought to lay hands on Ahasuerus. Access given for the king's protection became an opportunity for a plot against his life (Esther 2:21). Mordecai learned of it and told Esther, who reported it to the king in Mordecai's name. The accusation was investigated and found true. The sequence distinguishes a discovered plot from a sentence resting upon an unexamined report (Esther 2:22-23).
cases.judgment: Both conspirators were hanged on a tree, and the matter was entered in the royal chronicles. Mordecai's service received no immediate reward, but the written record preserved his part in saving the king. Later, during a sleepless night, Ahasuerus heard that record read and asked what honor Mordecai had received. Haman arrived intending to request Mordecai's death and instead was commanded to honor him (Esther 6:1-11). The record of one defeated conspiracy helped overturn another. A service apparently forgotten remained available at the moment its remembrance would matter.
offenseFull: Bigthan and Teresh were chamberlains entrusted with keeping the door. In their anger they sought to lay hands on Ahasuerus. Access given for the king's protection became an opportunity for a plot against his life (Esther 2:21).

Mordecai learned of it and told Esther, who reported it to the king in Mordecai's name. The accusation was investigated and found true. The sequence distinguishes a discovered plot from a sentence resting upon an unexamined report (Esther 2:22-23).

Later, during a sleepless night, Ahasuerus heard that record read and asked what honor Mordecai had received. Haman arrived intending to request Mordecai's death and instead was commanded to honor him (Esther 6:1-11). The record of one defeated conspiracy helped overturn another. A service apparently forgotten remained available at the moment its remembrance would matter.

verses.text: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai’s name.
And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.
On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.
And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s chamberlains, the keepers of the door, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
And the king said, What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this? Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, There is nothing done for him.

Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, and take the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, that sitteth at the king’s gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.

Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour.
Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.
Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.
Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.

entries.commentary: After the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what was decreed against her. His servants counsel that fair young virgins be sought for the king in every province and gathered to Shushan the palace under the custody of the keeper of the women. Fair young virgins here does not mean little girls but women of marital age, and the maiden who pleased the king would be made queen instead of Vashti, and the thing pleased the king. -

There was a certain Jew in Shushan named Mordecai, son of Jair, a Benjamite carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity taken with Jeconiah king of Judah whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away. This gives the lapse of time telling when Mordecai was put into captivity. Mordecai brought up Hadassah, that is Esther, his uncle's daughter, for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful, and when her parents were dead he took her for his own daughter. Esther is a Persian name after Ishtar, which is one reason the old rabbis said little of this book.

When the king's commandment was heard and many maidens were gathered to Shushan under Hegai, Esther was brought also to the king's house, and the maiden pleased him and obtained kindness, and he gave her things for purification and seven maidens and preferred her to the best place of the house of the women. Esther had not shown her people nor her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her not to show it, and Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women's house to know how Esther did. She is racially ambiguous, a daughter of Israel who could not be told at a glance to be black or Hispanic, which is why we go by whether a spirit bears witness with this Bible.

Every maid's turn to go in to the king came after twelve months of purification, six months with oil of myrrh and six months with sweet odours and other things for the purifying of the women. Israel kept such a season of preparing, and our women always smelled good. She went in the evening and returned to the second house of the women under the keeper of the concubines, and came in unto the king no more except he delighted in her and called her by name. The king had houses set aside for his concubines, for he was the king of Persia and not an Israelite.

When Esther's turn came, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai who took her for his daughter, she required nothing but what Hegai the keeper of the women appointed, and Esther obtained favour in the sight of all who looked upon her. The king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour more than all the virgins, so he set the royal crown upon her head and made her queen instead of Vashti, and made a great feast, Esther's feast, and a release to the provinces with gifts. Esther was chosen above all the women, for that is what a daughter of Israel is.

When the virgins were gathered the second time, Mordecai sat in the king's gate, and Esther had not yet showed her kindred nor her people as Mordecai had charged her. Esther did the commandment of Mordecai just as when she was brought up with him, still subject to her uncle and still listening to him even after she was made queen.

In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's chamberlains that kept the door were wroth and sought to lay hands on king Ahasuerus, plotting a coup against him. The thing was known to Mordecai who told it to Esther the queen, and Esther told the king in Mordecai's name, and when it was searched out and found true the two were both hanged on a tree, and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king. Israel wrote down our history and our chronicles, and this deed of Mordecai's would later help our whole nation. -

That night the king could not sleep, and he called for the book of records of the chronicles to be read before him. This is how the Most High works, moving even a king's sleeplessness to set His purpose in motion. It was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two chamberlains who sought to lay hand on the king, and yet nothing had been done to honor him for it. The king asked what honor had been done to Mordecai, and his servants answered that there was nothing done for him.

The king asked who was in the court, and Haman had just come into the outer court to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared. In the previous chapter Haman's wife had told him to make a gallows fifty cubits high and hang Mordecai on it, so Haman was coming to carry out that plan at the very moment the king had learned Mordecai saved his life. The king's servant said Haman stood in the court, and the king called for him to come in.

The king asked Haman what should be done to the man the king delights to honor, and Haman, being so full of himself, assumed the king must mean him, for who in the kingdom was better than he. Haman laid out a full plan of royal apparel the king wears, the horse the king rides, and the crown set upon the head, all delivered by a noble prince to array the man and parade him through the city. Because of his pride Haman designed the highest honor imaginable, thinking he himself would receive it.

The king told Haman to make haste and do exactly as he said to Mordecai the Jew who sat at the king's gate, letting nothing fail of all he had spoken. Haman then took the apparel and the horse, arrayed Mordecai, brought him on horseback through the street, and proclaimed before him. What Haman planned for himself was given to the man he hated. This is how the Most High works, and it should put a smile on your face.

Mordecai returned to the king's gate, but Haman hurried to his house mourning with his head covered, and told his wife Zeresh and his friends all that had happened. His wise men and his wife told him that if Mordecai was of the seed of the Jews, before whom he had begun to fall, he would not prevail but would surely fall before him. While they yet talked, the king's chamberlains came to hasten Haman to the banquet Esther had prepared, the banquet she set up after hearing of the decree against her people.

Dead flies make the apothecary's ointment stink; so a little folly ruins the man who holds a reputation for wisdom and honor. A wise man's heart is at his right hand, but a fool's heart at his left. Even as the fool walks by the way his wisdom fails him, and he shows everyone that he is a fool. If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, leave not your place, for yielding pacifies great offenses.

There is an evil under the sun, an error that proceeds from the ruler: folly is set in high dignity while the rich sit in a low place. He has seen servants riding upon horses and princes walking as servants upon the earth, the natural order turned upside down.

He that digs a pit shall fall into it, and whoever breaks a hedge a serpent shall bite; he that removes stones is hurt by them, and he that cleaves wood is endangered by it. If the iron is blunt and the edge is not whetted, more strength is needed, but wisdom is profitable to direct. The serpent bites without enchantment, and a babbler is no better.

The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious, but the fool is swallowed up by his own lips. His talk begins in foolishness and ends in mischievous madness. A fool is full of words, though no man can tell what shall be after him. The labor of the foolish wearies every one of them because he does not even know how to go to the city.

Woe to the land whose king is a child and whose princes eat in the morning; blessed is the land whose king is the son of nobles and whose princes eat in due season, for strength and not for drunkenness. Slothfulness lets the building decay and idleness makes the house drop through. A feast is made for laughter and wine makes merry, but money answers all things. Curse not the king, not even in your thought, nor the rich in your bedchamber, for a bird of the air shall carry the voice and tell the matter.

cases.name: Haman the Agagite
cases.charge: Plotting the destruction of all the Jews; building a gallows for Mordecai
cases.summary: Because one Jew would not bow to him, Haman sought to destroy all the Jews in the empire, bought the decree with ten thousand talents, cast lots for the day, and built a gallows fifty cubits high for Mordecai. Esther exposed him at her second banquet.
cases.offense: Mordecai's refusal to bow filled Haman with wrath. He scorned the idea of laying hands on one man alone and sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom. He represented their distinct laws as disloyalty and offered a vast sum to obtain their destruction (Esther 3:5-9). The sealed letters appointed a day to kill young and old, women and children, and take their spoil. Haman's personal resentment had become a decree against an entire people. Even his rank, wealth, and invitations to Esther's banquets gave him no satisfaction while Mordecai remained at the gate. He prepared a gallows for the man whose submission he could not obtain (Esther 5:9-14).
cases.judgment: Before Haman could ask for Mordecai's death, the king required him to proclaim Mordecai's honor. At Esther's banquet she exposed him as the enemy seeking her life and her people's. The king ordered Haman hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai (Esther 7:3-10). His estate and authority passed to those he had endangered. A further decree permitted the Jews to stand for their lives. Haman's ten sons were later killed and their bodies hanged. Purim preserved the remembrance of the appointed destruction turned against its deviser (Esther 8:1-11; 9:10-26).

verses.text: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.
And all the king’s servants, that were in the king’s gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.
And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.

And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.

And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.

Then said Zeresh his wife and all his friends unto him, Let a gallows be made of fifty cubits high, and to morrow speak thou unto the king that Mordecai may be hanged thereon: then go thou in merrily with the king unto the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman; and he caused the gallows to be made.
And Esther said, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath went into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther was. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.
So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king’s wrath pacified.
The ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, slew they; but on the spoil laid they not their hand.
Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,
He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.
His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.

Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.
For Aman, a Macedonian, the son of Amadatha, being indeed a stranger from the Persian blood, and far distant from our goodness, and as a stranger received of us,
Had so far forth obtained the favour that we shew toward every nation, as that he was called our father, and was continually honoured of all the next person unto the king.
But he, not bearing his great dignity, went about to deprive us of our kingdom and life:

Having by manifold and cunning deceits sought of us the destruction, as well of Mardocheus, who saved our life, and continually procured our good, as also of blameless Esther, partaker of our kingdom, with their whole nation.
For by these means he thought, finding us destitute of friends to have translated the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.

entries.commentary: After these things the king promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite and set his seat above all the princes, and all the king's servants in the king's gate bowed and reverenced him, for the king had so commanded, but Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence. The servants asked daily why Mordecai transgressed the king's commandment, and he hearkened not, but told them he was a Jew, and they told Haman to see whether Mordecai's matter would stand. We do not bow, the same as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, for we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High. -

When Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence, he was full of wrath, and thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone once they had shown him the people of Mordecai. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai, not one man only. Because Mordecai would not bow, Edom's hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, seeking to erase us out of history.

In the first month, Nisan, in the twelfth year of the king, they cast Pur, that is the lot, before Haman from day to day and month to month, to the twelfth month, Adar. Haman told the king there was a certain people scattered abroad whose laws were diverse from all people and who kept not the king's laws, and it was not for the king's profit to suffer them, offering ten thousand talents of silver to have them destroyed. The king took his ring and gave it to Haman the Jews' enemy, granting him the silver and the people to do as he pleased. This is putting a hit out on the entire nation of Israel.

On the thirteenth day of the first month the king's scribes wrote according to all Haman commanded, to the king's lieutenants, governors and rulers of every province in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring. Letters were sent by posts to destroy, kill and cause to perish all Jews, young and old, little children and women, in one day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, and to take the spoil for prey. The copy was published in every province so they should be ready, and the king and Haman sat down to drink while the city Shushan was perplexed.

On the third day Esther put on her royal apparel and stood in the inner court of the king's house over against the king's house, and the king sat on his royal throne over against the gate. When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favour in his sight, and he held out to her the golden sceptre in his hand, and Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre. She was not called by name, yet as soon as he saw her he received her, for a daughter of Israel finds favour in the eyes of a man.

The king asked what would Esther the queen and what was her request, offering even to the half of the kingdom, and Esther asked that the king and Haman come that day to a banquet she had prepared. The king said cause Haman to make haste that he may do as Esther said, so the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared. When a woman he loves prepares a table for him, the king bends to hear her every request.

At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther's petition and request, to the half of the kingdom, and Esther answered that if she had found favour and it pleased the king, let the king and Haman come again to the banquet she would prepare on the morrow, and she would do as the king had said. The book of Esther shows both sides, the good side of a woman doing what she should and the wicked side of what she should not, so it puts a check on the spirit that rises up in women to rebel.

Haman went forth that day joyful and glad of heart, but when he saw Mordecai in the king's gate who stood not up nor moved for him, he was full of indignation, yet refrained himself and went home and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife. Haman told them of the glory of his riches, his many children, and all the ways the king had advanced him above the princes, and that Esther had let no man come to the banquet with the king but himself, and he was bidden again on the morrow. Yet all this availed him nothing so long as he saw Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate. Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends counselled that a gallows fifty cubits high be made, and on the morrow he should speak to the king that Mordecai be hanged thereon, and then go merrily to the banquet, and the thing pleased Haman and he caused the gallows to be made. It was the wife's idea, for the enemy's women are in cahoots with the work against Israel. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther her petition, promising it would be granted even to the half of the kingdom. Esther pleaded for her life and the life of her people, for they had been sold to be destroyed, slain, and to perish, and had it been only bondage she would have held her tongue. The king demanded to know who he was that dared presume in his heart to do such a thing.

Esther named the adversary and enemy as this wicked Haman, and Haman was afraid before the king and the queen. Sitting at the table, Haman could hardly eat, for he had just arrayed Mordecai and just heard his own household warn him he would fall before the Jews, and now he was exposed at the dinner table.

The king rose in his wrath and went into the palace garden, and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther, seeing that evil was determined against him. When the king returned, Haman had fallen upon the bed where Esther was, and the king took it as an assault on the queen in his own house. As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

Mordecai was great in the king's house and his fame went throughout all the provinces, and this man waxed greater and greater. The other Jews in the king's provinces gathered, stood for their lives, had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, laying not their hands on the prey. This was on the thirteenth day of Adar, and on the fourteenth they rested and made a day of feasting and gladness. These days were called Purim after the name Pur, and the Jews ordained and took upon themselves and their seed to keep these two days every year. The days were to be remembered and kept throughout every generation, family, province, and city. These days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews nor the memorial of them perish from their seed, which shows Israel still celebrates Purim today.

Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim. If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. cases.name: Mordecai and Esther
cases.charge: Mordecai: bowing not to Haman. Esther: going in to the king against the law, after three days' fast: if I perish, I perish
cases.summary: A Jew in the king's gate would not bow to an Agagite, and the Agagite bought a decree to kill every Jew in the empire. His cousin the queen fasted three days with all the Jews of Shushan and went in to the king uncalled. Haman was hanged on his own gallows, the Jews were given the day, and Mordecai was next unto the king. The feast of Purim keeps it.
cases.offense: All the king's servants bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence; for he had told them that he was a Jew. Esther: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish. Mordecai's word to her: who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
cases.judgment: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified. The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour. Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed. The Greek Esther adds Mordecai's dream and the Lord's answer: the Lord hath done wonders for his people.

entries.commentary: After these things the king promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite and set his seat above all the princes, and all the king's servants in the king's gate bowed and reverenced him, for the king had so commanded, but Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence. The servants asked daily why Mordecai transgressed the king's commandment, and he hearkened not, but told them he was a Jew, and they told Haman to see whether Mordecai's matter would stand. We do not bow, the same as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, for we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High. -

When Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence, he was full of wrath, and thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone once they had shown him the people of Mordecai. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai, not one man only. Because Mordecai would not bow, Edom's hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, seeking to erase us out of history.

In the first month, Nisan, in the twelfth year of the king, they cast Pur, that is the lot, before Haman from day to day and month to month, to the twelfth month, Adar. Haman told the king there was a certain people scattered abroad whose laws were diverse from all people and who kept not the king's laws, and it was not for the king's profit to suffer them, offering ten thousand talents of silver to have them destroyed. The king took his ring and gave it to Haman the Jews' enemy, granting him the silver and the people to do as he pleased. This is putting a hit out on the entire nation of Israel.

On the thirteenth day of the first month the king's scribes wrote according to all Haman commanded, to the king's lieutenants, governors and rulers of every province in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring. Letters were sent by posts to destroy, kill and cause to perish all Jews, young and old, little children and women, in one day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, and to take the spoil for prey. The copy was published in every province so they should be ready, and the king and Haman sat down to drink while the city Shushan was perplexed.

When Mordecai perceived all that was done he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, went out into the midst of the city and cried with a loud and bitter cry, and came before the king's gate, for none might enter it clothed with sackcloth. In every province where the king's commandment and decree came there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes. Imagine a decree today to kill every descendant of Israel, and you begin to feel what they went through.

Esther's maids and chamberlain told her, and the queen was exceedingly grieved and sent raiment to clothe Mordecai and take away his sackcloth, but he received it not. She sent Hatach, appointed to attend her, to learn what it was and why. Mordecai told Hatach all that had happened and of the money Haman promised to pay for the Jews to be destroyed, and gave him a copy of the decree published in Shushan to show Esther, charging her to go in to the king and make supplication for her people.

Esther answered by Hatach that all the king's servants and people knew that whosoever came unto the king in the inner court uncalled, man or woman, there was one law, to be put to death, except the king held out the golden sceptre that he may live. She said she had not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days, and they told Mordecai her words. She made an excuse, though she was the queen the king had chosen and loved above all the women.

Mordecai sent answer that Esther should not think she would escape in the king's house more than all the Jews, for if she altogether held her peace at this time, then enlargement and deliverance would arise to the Jews from another place, but she and her father's house would be destroyed. Who knoweth whether Esther was come to the kingdom for such a time as this. She was put in her position to serve this very purpose, and the deliverance of Israel cannot be held back; she would either help it along or be left behind while it came another way.

Esther returned answer that Mordecai should gather all the Jews in Shushan to fast for her, neither eating nor drinking three days, night or day, and she and her maidens would fast likewise, and so she would go in unto the king not according to the law, and if she perished, she perished. So Mordecai went his way and did according to all Esther commanded him. She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people. -

On the third day Esther put on her royal apparel and stood in the inner court of the king's house over against the king's house, and the king sat on his royal throne over against the gate. When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favour in his sight, and he held out to her the golden sceptre in his hand, and Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre. She was not called by name, yet as soon as he saw her he received her, for a daughter of Israel finds favour in the eyes of a man.

The king asked what would Esther the queen and what was her request, offering even to the half of the kingdom, and Esther asked that the king and Haman come that day to a banquet she had prepared. The king said cause Haman to make haste that he may do as Esther said, so the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared. When a woman he loves prepares a table for him, the king bends to hear her every request.

At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther's petition and request, to the half of the kingdom, and Esther answered that if she had found favour and it pleased the king, let the king and Haman come again to the banquet she would prepare on the morrow, and she would do as the king had said. The book of Esther shows both sides, the good side of a woman doing what she should and the wicked side of what she should not, so it puts a check on the spirit that rises up in women to rebel.

Haman went forth that day joyful and glad of heart, but when he saw Mordecai in the king's gate who stood not up nor moved for him, he was full of indignation, yet refrained himself and went home and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife. Haman told them of the glory of his riches, his many children, and all the ways the king had advanced him above the princes, and that Esther had let no man come to the banquet with the king but himself, and he was bidden again on the morrow. Yet all this availed him nothing so long as he saw Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate. Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends counselled that a gallows fifty cubits high be made, and on the morrow he should speak to the king that Mordecai be hanged thereon, and then go merrily to the banquet, and the thing pleased Haman and he caused the gallows to be made. Esther pleaded for her life and the life of her people, for they had been sold to be destroyed, slain, and to perish, and had it been only bondage she would have held her tongue. The king demanded to know who he was that dared presume in his heart to do such a thing.

Esther named the adversary and enemy as this wicked Haman, and Haman was afraid before the king and the queen. Sitting at the table, Haman could hardly eat, for he had just arrayed Mordecai and just heard his own household warn him he would fall before the Jews, and now he was exposed at the dinner table.

The king took off the ring he had taken from Haman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman. Everything Haman had was given to Mordecai.

Esther fell down at the king's feet and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite and the device he had devised against the Jews. The king held out the golden scepter, and Esther rose and asked that letters be written to reverse the letters Haman devised to destroy the Jews in all the provinces. She asked how she could endure to see the evil that would come upon her people and the destruction of her kindred.

The king told Esther and Mordecai that he had given Esther the house of Haman and had hanged Haman for laying hand upon the Jews. He granted them to write for the Jews in the king's name and seal it with the king's ring, for a writing sealed with the king's ring could no man reverse. Esther and Mordecai were given the king's authority, so the reputation and word of the king stood behind whatever they wrote.

The king's scribes were called in the third month, Sivan, on the twenty-third day, and it was written to the Jews, lieutenants, deputies, and rulers of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, a hundred twenty and seven provinces, each in its own writing and language. This is the span of the Persian empire, and Israel was scattered all through it, from India to Ethiopia, not concentrated in one place but spread out during the captivity, which shows we have history in these lands. -

The king granted the Jews in every city to gather, stand for their life, and destroy any power that would assault them, both little ones and women, and to take the spoil. Everyone who had listened to Haman's proclamation to kill the Jews was now subject to the Jews' revenge upon their enemies. The decree was to be ready upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar, the day the Jews would avenge themselves, for nothing pacifies the Most High but vengeance on the enemies of His people. The posts rode out hastened on mules, camels, and dromedaries by the king's commandment.

Mordecai went out from the king in royal apparel of blue and white, a great crown of gold, and a garment of fine linen and purple, and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad. The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor, and in every province and city where the decree came they had a feast and a good day. Many of the people of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews fell upon them, a picture of the future when the fear of Israel will be on all nations and they will serve the Most High.
