cases.name: Nebuchadnezzar
cases.charge: Pride: is not this great Babylon, that I have built?
cases.summary: Warned by Daniel's interpretation of the tree dream to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor, the king walked on his palace roof twelve months later and took the credit for the empire. While the word was in his mouth a voice fell from heaven.
cases.offense: Nebuchadnezzar received a dream warning that his greatness would be cut down until he knew that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men. Daniel interpreted it and counseled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor (Daniel 4:19-27). The warning offered instruction before the sentence fell. Twelve months later the king walked in his palace and boasted of Babylon as the work of his own might for the honor of his majesty. He treated entrusted dominion as an achievement belonging wholly to himself. The words were still in his mouth when the heavenly answer declared that his kingdom had departed (Daniel 4:28-32).
cases.judgment: He was driven from men, ate grass as oxen, and was wet with the dew of heaven until the appointed times passed. His dependence was exposed beneath the grandeur in which he had gloried. At the end he lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed the Most High. His counselors sought him again, his kingdom was restored, and he confessed that the King of heaven can abase those who walk in pride (Daniel 4:33-37). The restored king's testimony gave God the honor his former boast had claimed for himself.
offenseFull: Nebuchadnezzar received a dream warning that his greatness would be cut down until he knew that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men. Daniel interpreted it and counseled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor (Daniel 4:19-27). The warning offered instruction before the sentence fell.

Twelve months later the king walked in his palace and boasted of Babylon as the work of his own might for the honor of his majesty. He treated entrusted dominion as an achievement belonging wholly to himself. The words were still in his mouth when the heavenly answer declared that his kingdom had departed (Daniel 4:28-32).
judgmentFull: He was driven from men, ate grass as oxen, and was wet with the dew of heaven until the appointed times passed. His dependence was exposed beneath the grandeur in which he had gloried.

At the end he lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed the Most High. His counselors sought him again, his kingdom was restored, and he confessed that the King of heaven can abase those who walk in pride (Daniel 4:33-37). The restored king's testimony gave God the honor his former boast had claimed for himself.

verses.text: Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity.
All this came upon the king Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of the kingdom of Babylon.
The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?
While the word was in the king’s mouth, there fell a voice from heaven, saying, O king Nebuchadnezzar, to thee it is spoken; The kingdom is departed from thee.

And they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field: they shall make thee to eat grass as oxen, and seven times shall pass over thee, until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.

The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.

And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:

And all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing: and he doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?

At the same time my reason returned unto me; and for the glory of my kingdom, mine honour and brightness returned unto me; and my counsellors and my lords sought unto me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent majesty was added unto me.
Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.
O thou king, the most high God gave Nebuchadnezzar thy father a kingdom, and majesty, and glory, and honour:

And for the majesty that he gave him, all people, nations, and languages, trembled and feared before him: whom he would he slew; and whom he would he kept alive; and whom he would he set up; and whom he would he put down.
But when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him:

And he was driven from the sons of men; and his heart was made like the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild asses: they fed him with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven; till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men, and that he appointeth over it whomsoever he will.

Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made; well: but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands?
And now have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant; and the beasts of the field have I given him also to serve him.
And all nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son’s son, until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.
The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.
For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

entries.commentary: Nebuchadnezzar proclaimed to all people, nations, and languages the signs and wonders the high God worked toward him, whose kingdom is everlasting, then told how a dream made him afraid and he decreed to bring in all the wise men of Babylon to interpret it. Remember from the day before that he had already brought in all his wise men once and they could not recall or interpret his dream; when the captain went out to slay the wise men he came upon Daniel, who was granted favour, consulted the Most High, and was given the vision.

The magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers could not make known the interpretation, but at last Daniel came in, named Belteshazzar after the king's god, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. Daniel was named after one of the king's gods. It is the same thing as Hadassah, whose name was changed to Esther; this is not new for us.

Nebuchadnezzar saw a great tree reaching to heaven, feeding and sheltering all flesh, then a watcher and a holy one came down and commanded it hewn down, its stump left bound with iron and brass, its heart changed to a beast's, till seven times pass over him. The matter is by the decree of the watchers, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and giveth it to whomsoever he will and setteth over it the basest of men. That is what we see today, the basest of men ruling the earth. -

Daniel, astonished for an hour, told the king the dream was for his enemies: the tree is the king himself, grown strong to the ends of the earth. The decree of the Most High is that he shall be driven from men to dwell with the beasts and eat grass as oxen, wet with the dew of heaven, till seven times pass and he knows the Most High ruleth; the stump left means his kingdom is kept for him once he knows the heavens do rule. Daniel counselled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor, that his tranquillity might be lengthened. You need to walk in righteousness and show mercy to the poor.

Twelve months later, walking in his palace, the king boasted, is not this great Babylon that I have built by my might for the honour of my majesty. He was very proud and boastful. While the word was in his mouth a voice from heaven pronounced the kingdom departed, and the same hour he was driven from men, ate grass as oxen, his hairs grown like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.

At the end of the days Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed and honoured the Most High, whose dominion is everlasting and before whom all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing. None can stay his hand or say unto him, what doest thou. When the Most High declares a thing shall come to pass, it comes to pass. -

His reason and the glory of his kingdom returned, and he praised and extolled the King of heaven, whose works are truth and ways judgment, and who is able to abase those that walk in pride. We already understood that the Most High can bring one up and set another down, but the heathen had to learn it by being jacked up, literally turned to crawl like a bird with the heart of a beast; as soon as his understanding returned he praised the one true living God. -

Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords and, while tasting the wine, commanded the golden and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought so he, his princes, wives, and concubines might drink in them. This is Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, who is Daniel. They drank and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. -

In the same hour fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster of the wall, and the king's countenance changed, his knees smote together, so terrified that the joints of his loins were loosed. Picture him sitting back drinking with his lords, wives, and concubines, having a good time, and then a hand starts writing on the wall; he was terrified out of everything. He cried aloud for the astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers, offering scarlet, a gold chain, and to be third ruler in the kingdom to whoever could read it, but none of his wise men could read the writing or interpret it, and he was greatly troubled.

The queen came into the banquet house and told the king of the man Daniel, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods, whom Nebuchadnezzar his father had made master of the magicians because an excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him. Daniel was brought in, and the king offered him scarlet, a gold chain, and the third rulership if he could read the writing and make known the interpretation.

Daniel told the king to keep his gifts and rewards, then recounted how the Most High gave Nebuchadnezzar his kingdom and greatness, and how, when his heart was lifted up in pride, he was deposed and driven to dwell with the wild asses until he knew the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Belshazzar had not humbled his heart though he knew all this, but lifted himself against the Lord of heaven, drank from the temple vessels, and praised gods of silver, gold, brass, iron, wood, and stone that see not nor hear, while the God in whose hand his breath is he did not glorify. -

Daniel read the writing: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. MENE, God has numbered the kingdom and finished it; TEKEL, the king is weighed in the balances and found wanting; PERES, the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

Belshazzar clothed Daniel with scarlet, put a chain about his neck, and proclaimed him third ruler, but that same night Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old. Immediately after the interpretation the kingdom was translated from Belshazzar to the Medes and Persians.

Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, threescore cubits high and six cubits broad, and set it up in the plain of Dura, then gathered the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, counsellors, sheriffs, and rulers to its dedication. We have seen things like this before. When they build a monument or a new federal building they hold a dedication and a ribbon-cutting ceremony. This is very similar.

A herald cried that when the people heard the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of music they were to fall down and worship the golden image. We see the same thing today when they play the national anthem at ball games and ceremonies. You are supposed to take your hat off and put your hand over your heart. That is a form of worshipping the image of the eagle today.

Whoever did not fall down and worship would the same hour be cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace, so when the music sounded all the people, nations, and languages fell down and worshipped the golden image.

Certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews, telling the king that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom he had set over the affairs of the province, did not regard him, serve his gods, nor worship the golden image. The reason we did not bow was according to the law. -

In his rage Nebuchadnezzar brought the three men and demanded whether they would fall down and worship, threatening the furnace and asking, who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands. He is talking tough, talking big, challenging our God when he asks who is going to deliver you out of his hands.

The three answered that they were not careful to answer him in this matter: their God whom they serve is able to deliver them from the burning fiery furnace and out of the king's hand. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that they would not serve his gods nor worship the golden image. This is exactly what was read in [Exodus 20](/bible/exodus/20).

Full of fury, Nebuchadnezzar commanded the furnace heated seven times more than usual and had his mighty men bind the three in their coats and garments and cast them in. The furnace was so hot that the flame slew the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up to it. For more of this history the Song of the Three Holy Children can be read; for the sake of time it was only referenced here.

The three men fell down bound into the furnace, but Nebuchadnezzar rose up astonished and said he saw four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, unhurt, and the form of the fourth was like the Son of God.

Nebuchadnezzar called them servants of the Most High God to come forth, and the fire had no power on their bodies: not a hair singed, their coats unchanged, nor the smell of fire on them. It was as if they had never fallen into the fire; not even the smell of smoke was on these brothers.

Nebuchadnezzar blessed the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel to deliver the servants that trusted in him and would not serve nor worship any god except their own God. He understood at that time that we had our own God. Why do people not understand that today. He decreed that any people, nation, or language that spake amiss against their God would be cut in pieces, because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort, and he promoted the three in the province of Babylon. When the nations get jacked up they come to know who has the real, true, living God; other heathen rulers came to the same acknowledgement, such as Antiochus and Naaman the Syrian. -

The Most High tells Jeremiah to make bonds and yokes, put them on his neck, and send them to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, and Zidon by their messengers to Zedekiah. The Most High made the earth, man, and beast by His power and outstretched arm and gives it to whom it seems meet to Him; He has now given all these lands and the beasts of the field into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar His servant. All the nations shall serve him, his son, and his son's son until the time of his land comes, when many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him; the Most High uses people, He used Nebuchadnezzar, Cyrus, and Pharaoh alike.

The nation and kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar and will not put its neck under the yoke of Babylon the Most High will punish with the sword, the famine, and the pestilence until they are consumed. Therefore they must not hearken to their prophets, diviners, dreamers, enchanters, and sorcerers who say they shall not serve the king of Babylon, for they prophesy a lie. The nations that bring their neck under the yoke and serve him He will let remain in their own land to till it and dwell there; this is the Most High saying that whatever we are commanded to do, even the other nations are told to serve Babylon or answer to Him.

Jeremiah speaks the same words to Zedekiah, telling him to bring his neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him and live, rather than die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence. He is not to hearken to the prophets who say he shall not serve Babylon, for they prophesy a lie in the Most High's name that will drive the people out to perish along with the prophets themselves.

Jeremiah warns the priests and all the people not to listen to the prophets who claim the vessels of the Lord's house will shortly be brought back from Babylon, for they prophesy a lie; they should serve the king of Babylon and live. If they were true prophets they would make intercession that the remaining vessels not go to Babylon, but instead the pillars, the sea, the bases, and the residue of the vessels shall be carried to Babylon and remain there until the day the Most High visits them and restores them to this place. The whole warning is that Babylon is one the Most High will use to take over everything, and the people had better listen and serve him, because all these prophecies were meant to happen and they did happen. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

cases.name: Belshazzar
cases.charge: Drinking from the temple vessels and praising the gods of gold and silver
cases.summary: At a feast for a thousand lords, Belshazzar called for the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the house of God in Jerusalem, drank wine from them with his wives and concubines, and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. Fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster.
cases.offense: Belshazzar commanded that the vessels taken from Jerusalem's temple be brought to his feast. He and his company drank from them while praising gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone (Daniel 5:1-4). Holy vessels became instruments in a public display of contempt for the God whose house they had served. Daniel reminded him of Nebuchadnezzar's humbling and charged that he had not humbled his own heart though he knew it. The gods praised at the feast could neither see nor hear, while the God holding his breath and all his ways received no glory (Daniel 5:18-23). Knowledge of the earlier judgment increased his accountability.
cases.judgment: The writing on the wall announced that God had numbered and finished his kingdom, weighed him and found him wanting, and given the kingdom to the Medes and Persians. Gifts and advancement offered to the interpreter could not purchase a different interpretation. Belshazzar clothed Daniel in scarlet and proclaimed his rank, but that night the king was slain and Darius the Median received the kingdom (Daniel 5:25-31). The sentence reached the ruler while the honors he could distribute still appeared to be in his hand. His feast could not preserve the breath he had failed to acknowledge as God's gift.
offenseFull: Belshazzar commanded that the vessels taken from Jerusalem's temple be brought to his feast. He and his company drank from them while praising gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone (Daniel 5:1-4). Daniel reminded him of Nebuchadnezzar's humbling and charged that he had not humbled his own heart though he knew it. Belshazzar clothed Daniel in scarlet and proclaimed his rank, but that night the king was slain and Darius the Median received the kingdom (Daniel 5:25-31). The sentence reached the ruler while the honors he could distribute still appeared to be in his hand. His feast could not preserve the breath he had failed to acknowledge as God's gift.

verses.text: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand.

Belshazzar, whiles he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein.
Then they brought the golden vessels that were taken out of the temple of the house of God which was at Jerusalem; and the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, drank in them.
They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.
And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this;

But hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before thee, and thou, and thy lords, thy wives, and thy concubines, have drunk wine in them; and thou hast praised the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which see not, nor hear, nor know: and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified:
Then was the part of the hand sent from him; and this writing was written.
And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it.
TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.
PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.
Then commanded Belshazzar, and they clothed Daniel with scarlet, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made a proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom.
In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain.
And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.
Also Cyrus the king brought forth the vessels of the house of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought forth out of Jerusalem, and had put them in the house of his gods;
Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called, The lady of kingdoms.
I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.
And thou saidst, I shall be a lady for ever: so that thou didst not lay these things to thy heart, neither didst remember the latter end of it.

Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:

But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.
For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.

Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off: and desolation shall come upon thee suddenly, which thou shalt not know.
In their heat I will make their feasts, and I will make them drunken, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the Lord.

entries.commentary: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords and, while tasting the wine, commanded the golden and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought so he, his princes, wives, and concubines might drink in them. This is Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, who is Daniel. They drank and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. -

In the same hour fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster of the wall, and the king's countenance changed, his knees smote together, so terrified that the joints of his loins were loosed. Picture him sitting back drinking with his lords, wives, and concubines, having a good time, and then a hand starts writing on the wall; he was terrified out of everything. He cried aloud for the astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers, offering scarlet, a gold chain, and to be third ruler in the kingdom to whoever could read it, but none of his wise men could read the writing or interpret it, and he was greatly troubled.

The queen came into the banquet house and told the king of the man Daniel, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods, whom Nebuchadnezzar his father had made master of the magicians because an excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him. Daniel was brought in, and the king offered him scarlet, a gold chain, and the third rulership if he could read the writing and make known the interpretation.

Daniel told the king to keep his gifts and rewards, then recounted how the Most High gave Nebuchadnezzar his kingdom and greatness, and how, when his heart was lifted up in pride, he was deposed and driven to dwell with the wild asses until he knew the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Belshazzar had not humbled his heart though he knew all this, but lifted himself against the Lord of heaven, drank from the temple vessels, and praised gods of silver, gold, brass, iron, wood, and stone that see not nor hear, while the God in whose hand his breath is he did not glorify. -

Daniel read the writing: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. MENE, God has numbered the kingdom and finished it; TEKEL, the king is weighed in the balances and found wanting; PERES, the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

Belshazzar clothed Daniel with scarlet, put a chain about his neck, and proclaimed him third ruler, but that same night Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old. Immediately after the interpretation the kingdom was translated from Belshazzar to the Medes and Persians.

In the first year of Cyrus the word of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah is fulfilled. The Lord stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout his kingdom. Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem. His coming was prophesied long before by name. -

Cyrus calls for any of the Most High's people to go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the Lord God of Israel. Those who remained behind were to help the returning ones with silver, gold, goods, and beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God.

The chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, with the priests and the Levites, rose up, all whose spirit the Most High had raised to go build the house of the Lord. Those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver and gold, with goods and beasts and precious things, beside the freewill offerings.

Cyrus brings out the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar had carried from Jerusalem and stored among his own goods. He sends them back by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer and numbers them to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.

The vessels are counted out, gold and silver charges, basins, knives, and other vessels totaling 5,400. All these Sheshbazzar brings up with the captives that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem. The same account is recorded in 1 Esdras.

The Most High raises against Babylon a destroying wind and sends fanners to fan her and empty her land. Spare not her young men; destroy utterly all her host. The slain fall in the land of the Chaldeans, thrust through in her streets, for Israel has not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.

Israel and Judah have not been forsaken of the Most High. Flee out of the midst of Babylon and deliver every man his soul; do not be cut off in her iniquity, for this is the time of the Lord's vengeance. -

Babylon has been a golden cup in the Lord's hand that made all the earth drunken; the nations drank of her wine and are mad. All the nations partook, and even the children of Israel were made to drink of the cup of our own destruction. Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed. We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed; forsake her, and let everyone go into his own country.
Her judgment reaches unto heaven and is lifted up even to the skies. The Most High has brought forth our righteousness; come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.

Make bright the arrows and gather the shields; the Lord has raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his device against Babylon is to destroy it, the vengeance of his temple. Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set the watchmen, and prepare the ambushes. The standard is the Bible, and the men are made ready, for the Most High has both devised and done what he spoke.

Babylon dwells upon many waters, abundant in treasures, but thine end is come. She dwells upon many waters because her embassies reach into every land, from South Africa to Europe to the Philippines; her treasure was built on the backs of the slaves and the stolen Western Hemisphere. The Lord of hosts has sworn to fill her with men as with caterpillars who lift up a shout against her. She is destroyed from within, because being a melting pot, the other nations infiltrate and destroy America from the inside out, the way a caterpillar becomes an infestation that devours a whole land.

He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding; he brings the wind out of his treasures. Every man is brutish in his knowledge, and every founder is confounded by the graven image, for his molten image is falsehood and there is no breath in them. But the portion of Jacob is not like them, for he is the former of all things, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance.

Thou art my battle-ax and weapons of war; with thee the Most High breaks in pieces the nations and destroys kingdoms, the horse and his rider, the chariot and his rider. With thee he breaks in pieces man and woman, old and young, the young man and the maid, the shepherd and his flock, the husbandman and his oxen, and the captains and rulers. The sisters who love feminism had better humble down, because the woman is named right alongside the man. -

The Most High will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all the evil they have done in Zion. Behold, he is against thee, O destroying mountain that destroys all the earth. He will stretch out his hand, roll her down from the rocks, and make her a burnt mountain; they shall take of her no stone for a corner nor foundation, but she shall be desolate forever.

Set up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, and prepare the nations against her; call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz, and appoint a captain against her. Prepare the nations with the king of the Medes, the captains, the rulers, and all the land of his dominion against Babylon.

The land trembles and sorrows, for every purpose of the Lord is performed against Babylon to make it a desolation without inhabitant. The mighty men of Babylon forbear to fight and remain in their holds; their might fails and they become as women. One post runs to meet another to tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken at one end and the passages are stopped. The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor; it is time to thresh her, and the time of her harvest shall come.

Nebuchadnezzar has devoured Israel, crushed her, made her an empty vessel, and swallowed her like a dragon. Let the violence done to Zion be upon Babylon, and her blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea. The Most High will plead Zion's cause, take vengeance for her, and dry up Babylon's sea and springs. Babylon shall become heaps, a dwelling place for dragons, an astonishment and a hissing without inhabitant.

They roar together like lions and yell as lions' whelps. In their heat the Most High makes their feasts and makes them drunken, that they may sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. He brings them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with the he-goats.

How is Sheshach taken, the praise of the whole earth surprised, and Babylon become an astonishment among the nations? The sea is come up upon Babylon, covered with the multitude of its waves. Her cities are a desolation, a dry land and a wilderness, where no man dwells and no son of man passes by.

The Most High will punish Bel in Babylon and bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed, and the wall of Babylon shall fall. My people, go out of the midst of her and deliver every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord. A rumor shall come one year and another rumor the next, with violence in the land and ruler against ruler. Do not let your heart faint at the rumor that is heard.

The days come when the Most High does judgment upon the graven images of Babylon, and her whole land is confounded and her slain fall in her midst. Then heaven and earth and all in them sing for Babylon, for the spoiler comes from the north. As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.

Ye that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still, remember the Lord afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind. We are confounded because strangers have come into the sanctuaries of the Lord's house. Though Babylon should mount up to heaven and fortify the height of her strength, yet from the Most High shall spoilers come unto her.

A cry and great destruction come from Babylon, for the Lord has spoiled her. Her mighty men are taken and their bows broken, and the Lord of recompense shall surely requite. He makes drunk her princes, wise men, captains, rulers, and mighty men, that they sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken and her high gates burned with fire, and the people shall labor in vain.

Jeremiah commanded Seraiah, when he went with Zedekiah to Babylon, to read all the evil written against Babylon and then declare that the Most High has spoken to cut off this place forever. After reading the book, Seraiah was to bind a stone to it and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates, saying, thus shall Babylon sink and not rise from the evil the Most High brings upon her. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah. Rejoice in the destruction of our enemies, which is the salvation of the righteous. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

cases.name: Daniel's accusers
cases.charge: Conspiring by law against an innocent man
cases.summary: Unable to find fault in Daniel's administration, his enemies procured a decree forbidding petition to any god or man except the king for thirty days. They used his continued prayer to obtain his condemnation. God preserved Daniel, and the king turned the punishment upon the accusers.
cases.offense: The presidents and princes searched Daniel's conduct for a charge and found neither error nor fault. They therefore devised a law aimed at his faithfulness: for thirty days, petition to any god or man except Darius would be punished by the lions' den (Daniel 6:4-9). They found Daniel praying as he had before and presented his devotion as disregard for the king. When Darius sought to deliver him, they pressed the rule that his decree could not be altered. Their scheme used the form of law to punish a man whose administration they could not impeach.
cases.judgment: Daniel came out of the den without a mark because he believed in his God. The king commanded those who had accused him, with their children and wives, cast into the den; the lions broke all their bones before they reached the bottom.
offenseFull: The presidents and princes searched Daniel's conduct for a charge and found neither error nor fault. They therefore devised a law aimed at his faithfulness: for thirty days, petition to any god or man except Darius would be punished by the lions' den (Daniel 6:4-9).

They found Daniel praying as he had before and presented his devotion as disregard for the king. When Darius sought to deliver him, they pressed the rule that his decree could not be altered. Their scheme used the form of law to punish a man whose administration they could not impeach.

entries.commentary: It pleased Darius to set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom, with three presidents over them, of whom Daniel was first, so the king should have no damage. Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm. He was set in a very high position in government.

The presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom but could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him. He was blameless. This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in. They concluded they could only find something against him concerning the law of his God. -

The presidents and princes assembled and persuaded Darius to sign a firm decree that whoever asked a petition of any god or man for thirty days, save the king, would be cast into the den of lions, by the unchanging law of the Medes and Persians.

When Daniel knew the writing was signed he went home, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem kneeled and prayed three times a day, giving thanks as he did before. The men assembled, found him praying, and reported to the king that Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, regarded neither the king nor the decree but made his petition three times a day. They really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God.

The king was displeased with himself and laboured till sundown to deliver Daniel, but the men pressed that the law could not be changed, so he commanded Daniel cast into the den, saying, thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee. The king already understood why he was under the realm of Babylon and had seen what was going on. A stone was laid on the den and sealed with the king's signet.

The king went to his palace and passed the night fasting, with no instruments of music brought before him and his sleep gone from him. Why would the king be fasting. He rose very early and went in haste to the den, crying with a lamentable voice, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God able to deliver thee from the lions.

Daniel answered that his God had sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths because innocency was found in him and he had done no hurt. The king was glad and commanded Daniel taken up, and no manner of hurt was found on him because he believed in his God; then the accusers, their children, and wives were cast in and the lions brake their bones before they reached the bottom. -

Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages that in every dominion men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God, stedfast for ever, whose kingdom shall not be destroyed and who delivereth and rescueth and worketh signs and wonders. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian. He had a wise and humble spirit, was beloved by the king, could answer visions and interpret dreams, and was of the king's seed as shown in chapter one. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

When the Most High cut off the nations of the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and Israel succeeded them and dwelt in their cities and houses, Israel was to separate three cities in the midst of the land and prepare the way to them. This law goes into accidental death, what the Bible sometimes calls manslaughter. An Israelite who accidentally killed another could flee to one of these three cities of refuge, where the avenger of blood could not seek him out and kill him there to revenge the blood of his nearest of kin.

Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past, means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident. The example given is two men hewing wood, and the axe head slips from the helve and strikes the neighbour that he die: he shall flee to one of those cities and live. The avenger of blood is the nearest of kin, and while his heart is hot he may pursue and overtake the slayer because the way is long. But the slayer was not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time past; there was no premeditation, no intention to kill. Accidents happen, and the Most High put laws in place for when these things happened. If it was for sure an accident, the man is not worthy of death, as the scripture says.

If the Lord enlarge thy coast as he sware unto the fathers, then three more cities were to be added. As Israel grew and possessed more of the land of Canaan, more cities of refuge were established where a slayer could flee from the avenger of blood. The purpose is stated plainly: that innocent blood be not shed in the land which the Lord giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.

This gives the distinction between an accident and intentional killing; this is describing murder. He hated his neighbour and lay in wait for him: he devised a scheme, waited for the right opportunity and the right time, rose up against him, and smote him mortally that he died. The murderer cannot then run to a city of refuge to lay low. Those cities were not established for him; they were established so retaliation did not come on those who accidentally brought harm to somebody. The elders of his own city shall fetch him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him: putting away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel is what makes it go well with the nation.

What is a landmark? It pays to use tools outside the scriptures, because what good is reading the Bible without understanding of the words written in it. The Zondervan Bible Dictionary defines a landmark as an object, stone, or post used to mark the boundary of a field, and notes that removal of landmarks was prohibited by the Mosaic law. The landmark establishes the boundaries of a man's property, where it begins and where it ends. A man who keeps nudging his neighbour's landmark over little by little until he has taken an acre is stealing land; the dictionary notes it was considered equal to theft.

One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin. One man alone saying he saw a theft is not proof; anybody can come and lie and get people put to death, imprisoned, or beaten. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. It has to be clear-cut; two or three solid witnesses, not one solid witness and a shaky witness. We deal with facts.

When a false witness rises up, both men in the controversy stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges of those days. False accusation is real: people will lie on a man to cover themselves, and false witnesses arise among your own people as well, which is part of why the nation fell into captivity. The judges shall make diligent inquisition: they get to the bottom of the matter and find out exactly who is telling the truth, who is lying, and what the facts are. A judge cannot judge a matter off what one person says; each side tells the story in his own favour, so you must examine the whole matter, question both sides against each other, and decipher the truth. Diligent inquisition is what separates a good judge from a bad judge; a lazy or partial judge makes false judgment. If the witness is found false, then shall ye do unto him as he had thought to have done unto his brother. Accuse a man falsely of stealing, and the judgment for stealing comes on you; accuse him falsely of adultery or another sin punishable by death, and you are put to death, because that is what you intended for your neighbour. So is evil put away from Israel.
The judgment is public and it teaches: those which remain shall hear and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil among you.

Thine eye shall not pity: in this time under Moses it was life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law. Christ spoke on this saying, because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge. Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

As snow in summer and rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool. As the bird wandering and the swallow flying, the causeless curse shall not come. A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back. Ecclesiasticus says the same: correction and work are for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back. -

Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you become like him. Many of us have argued with an idiot and been made to look like an idiot; onlookers wonder why you are even arguing with him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. He that sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks damage.

The legs of the lame are not equal, and so is a parable in the mouth of fools. As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he that gives honor to a fool. As a thorn goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools. Like a splinter driven under the skin, it hurts and can take days to work out.

The great God that formed all things both rewards the fool and rewards transgressors. As a dog returns to his vomit, so a fool returns to his folly. Second Peter calls this a true proverb, showing the apostles quoted Solomon: those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning. -

Do you see a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope for a fool than for him. The slothful man says there is a lion in the way and in the streets. As the door turns on its hinges, so the slothful turns on his bed; he hides his hand in his bosom and it grieves him to bring it back to his mouth. The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

He that passes by and meddles with strife not belonging to him is like one that takes a dog by the ears. Ecclesiasticus warns not to strive in a matter that does not concern you. A young lady who tried to break up a high-school fight was grabbed by police, slammed face-first, and left with brain damage; the Bible is a true book. As a madman who casts firebrands, arrows, and death, so is the man that deceives his neighbor and says, "Am I not in sport?" -

Where there is no wood the fire goes out, and where there is no tale-bearer the strife ceases. As coals to burning coals and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindle strife. The words of a tale-bearer are as wounds that go down into the innermost parts of the belly. Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.

He that hates dissembles with his lips and lays up deceit within, so when he speaks fair, do not believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart. Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the whole congregation, put out on display. Luke says nothing is covered that shall not be revealed. Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit; that thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High. -

Whoever digs a pit shall fall in it, and he that rolls a stone will have it return upon him. A lying tongue hates those that are afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin. That flattery is deceit.

verses.text: Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Then said these men, We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.
Then these presidents and princes assembled together to the king, and said thus unto him, King Darius, live for ever.

All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Then these men assembled, and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.

Then they came near, and spake before the king concerning the king’s decree; Hast thou not signed a decree, that every man that shall ask a petition of any God or man within thirty days, save of thee, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions? The king answered and said, The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.

Then answered they and said before the king, That Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, regardeth not thee, O king, nor the decree that thou hast signed, but maketh his petition three times a day.
Then the king, when he heard these words, was sore displeased with himself, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him: and he laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver him.
Then these men assembled unto the king, and said unto the king, Know, O king, that the law of the Medes and Persians is, That no decree nor statute which the king establisheth may be changed.
Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.

And the king commanded, and they brought those men which had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions had the mastery of them, and brake all their bones in pieces or ever they came at the bottom of the den.
If a false witness rise up against any man to testify against him that which is wrong;
Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother: so shalt thou put the evil away from among you.
He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.
His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.
Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

cases.name: The priests who despised the Name
cases.charge: Offering polluted bread and blemished beasts; being partial in the law
cases.summary: After the return, the priests offered the blind, the lame, and the sick on the altar and said the table of the Lord was contemptible and its service a weariness. Offer it now unto thy governor, Malachi says; will he be pleased with thee? They also departed out of the way and caused many to stumble at the law.
cases.offense: The priests despised the Lord's name by bringing polluted offerings and treating His table as contemptible. They offered the blind, lame, and sick, though such a gift would not please their governor. Their conduct withheld from the great King the honor they understood how to show to earthly authority (Malachi 1:6-14).
cases.judgment: I will curse your blessings; yea, I have cursed them already. I will spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts. Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have been partial in the law.

entries.commentary: The Levitical priesthood was established in Aaron and his sons. Certain things were consecrated that could not be touched by the rest of Israel, and a priest with his uncleanness upon him could not go unto the holy things, lest that soul be cut off from the presence of the Most High. Aaron was consecrated and anointed to minister in the priest's office, and his sons were clothed and anointed as their father, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

A man of the seed of Aaron that was a leper, had a running issue, or touched any unclean thing could not eat of the holy things until he was clean: he washed his flesh with water, and when the sun was down he was clean and could afterward eat. That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith. That same law elsewhere says to give such a thing unto the stranger or sell it to an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: these laws were given to Israel alone, and the other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people. There is no equality in that.

No stranger may eat of the holy thing, neither a sojourner of the priest nor an hired servant. But the soul the priest buys with his money, and he that is born in his house, they eat of his meat, because they are joined to the priest's household. The priest's daughter married unto a stranger may not eat of the offering of the holy things; but if she is a widow or divorced and has no child, and is returned unto her father's house as in her youth, she eats of her father's meat, because she returns to her father's covering. A woman was commonly under her father's covering until she came under a husband's. The independent woman was not birthed from the Bible; she was birthed from Babylon. He that eats of the holy thing unwittingly adds the fifth part unto it and gives it to the priest with the holy thing; the priests must not suffer the children of Israel to bear the iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things.

Whatever offering is brought for a vow or a freewill offering must be a male without blemish, of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goats. Beeves goes to the ox and that family, the oxen and bulls. Blind, broken, maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, shall not be offered unto the Lord. Scurvy is just having scratches; these offerings could have no scratches and no bruises, nothing bruised or crushed or broken or cut. Neither from a stranger's hand shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them and blemishes be in them; they shall not be accepted for you.

When a bullock or a sheep or a goat is brought forth, it shall be seven days under the dam. The dam is that animal's mother; the young must stay under its mother seven days, and from the eighth day it is accepted for an offering. Whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day. And the sacrifice of thanksgiving is eaten the same day; none of it is left until the morrow.

Therefore shall ye keep my commandments and do them: neither shall ye profane my holy name, but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel. I am the Lord which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. The Most High brought Israel out of the land of Egypt to be their God; that is the foundation the commandments stand on.

At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release: every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it, and shall not exact it of his neighbour or of his brother, because it is called the Lord's release. Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again, but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release. The seven year release stands on the sabbath of the land already given in [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25).

If thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Most High to observe all these commandments, thou shalt lend unto many nations but thou shalt not borrow, and thou shalt reign over many nations but they shall not reign over thee. This is the blessing that was to come upon us. Since we broke the commandments of the Most High, the other nations lend to us and we borrow from them; we go to them for loans and everything else.

If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren, thou shalt not harden thine heart nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother. It is a commandment to us to help our brothers: open thine hand wide unto him and lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand, and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother and thou givest him nought; if he cry unto the Lord against thee, it is sin unto thee. Give him surely, and let not thine heart be grieved when thou givest, for because of this thing the Most High shall bless thee in all thy works. Notice that Esau had this Bible, these commandments and these laws, yet worked us to death for over four hundred years, and when they released us we did not go out with anything. They had these laws written before them and did not do them. The poor shall never cease out of the land; Christ said the same, that the poor are always going to be among us. That is why no campaign can fight poverty out of existence: Christ said it will always be among us.

If thy brother, an Hebrew man or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee and serve thee six years, then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free, and thou shalt not let him go away empty. When people say slavery was taking place in Africa among us, it was not slavery like we suffered: it was people among us that fell poor and sold themselves to their brothers, the very case this law and [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) govern. Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress; he must leave blessed, with some of the flock, the corn, and the wine. He cannot go out poor the way he came in; that shows you the Most High is a good God. The reason given is memory: remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee.

If the servant say, I will not go away from thee, because he loveth thee and thine house and is well with thee, then thou shalt take an aul and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever; likewise unto thy maidservant. It shall not seem hard unto thee when thou sendest him away free, for he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee in serving thee six years. A double hired servant: reading this makes you think about slavery and how many years they had us. We were double hired servants unto them, and we still serve them even to this day.

All the firstling males of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto the Most High: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock, nor shear the firstling of thy sheep. The firstlings were to do no work at all; they were to be sacrificed to the Most High, and thou shalt eat it before the Lord thy God year by year in the place which the Lord shall choose. If there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame or blind, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God; thou shalt eat it within thy gates, the unclean and the clean person alike, as the roebuck and as the hart. Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it upon the ground as water.

verses.text: A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear? saith the Lord of hosts unto you, O priests, that despise my name. And ye say, Wherein have we despised thy name?
Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar; and ye say, Wherein have we polluted thee? In that ye say, The table of the Lord is contemptible.

And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil? offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the Lord of hosts.
But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the Lord is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible.

Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it! and ye have snuffed at it, saith the Lord of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering: should I accept this of your hand? saith the Lord.

But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.
And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you.

If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the Lord of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart.
Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it.
For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.
Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law.
But whatsoever hath a blemish, that shall ye not offer: for it shall not be acceptable for you.

And whosoever offereth a sacrifice of peace offerings unto the Lord to accomplish his vow, or a freewill offering in beeves or sheep, it shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish therein.
Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, ye shall not offer these unto the Lord, nor make an offering by fire of them upon the altar unto the Lord.
And if there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame, or blind, or have any ill blemish, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God.

cases.name: Judah robbing God in tithes and offerings
cases.charge: Withholding the tithe from the storehouse
cases.summary: Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me. But ye say, wherein? In tithes and offerings. The returned community had left the Levites unsupported so that they fled to their fields, and the house of God was forsaken while every man ran to his own house.
cases.offense: The Lord called the sons of Jacob to return from their departure out of His ordinances. They answered by asking wherein they should return and wherein they had robbed Him. The charge was direct: in tithes and offerings (Malachi 3:6-9). What they retained was not theirs to withhold merely because it remained in their possession. The neglect had practical consequences for God's house. Nehemiah found the Levites and singers gone to their fields because their portions had not been supplied. He confronted the rulers and restored both the ministers and the storehouses (Nehemiah 13:10-13). Provision for service was part of the people's obedience, not an incidental matter outside it.
cases.judgment: Malachi pronounced a curse upon the nation but joined the rebuke to a way of return. They were to bring the tithes into the storehouse so that there would be provision in God's house. The Lord promised opened windows of heaven, rebuke of the devourer, and preservation of the fruit of their land (Malachi 3:10-12). The promise addressed the covenant people and the provision they had withheld. Repentance required restoring that provision. God's call to return showed that the sentence was not an invitation to despair, but a summons to abandon the neglect and receive the blessing He offered.
