entries.commentary: On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing. When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off. -

Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid. Nehemiah was away in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he returned and understood the evil, he cast all Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber, cleansed the chambers, and brought back the vessels of the house of God with the meat offering and the frankincense.

Nehemiah found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so the Levites and singers had fled every one to his field, and he contended with the rulers and set the Levites back in their place. He made treasurers over the treasuries, faithful men, to distribute unto their brethren, and prayed, Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.

Nehemiah saw men in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, and figs into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath. He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment. -

When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded them shut and set his servants at the gates so no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath, and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. He testified against them and warned that if they came again he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. He then commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women. -

One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah chased him away because he had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites. Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are. -

In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the governor of Judah, and to Joshua the high priest. This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord's house should be built. Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?

Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes. Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord. Ye looked for much, and lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house. Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit. And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon all the labour of the hands.

Then Zerubbabel, and Joshua the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him; and the people did fear before the Lord. Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. The Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God. --- Topics: [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

A singular vow is a man binding himself to the Most High: promising that in exchange for a blessing he will give himself, or what is his, to the service of the Lord. The persons vowed were valued by the estimation of the priest. Hannah is the example: in bitterness of soul she vowed that if the Lord gave her a man child she would give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and that is how the story of Samuel began. Christ taught on this because a vow is dangerous: you must pay your vow. Better not to swear at all, but let your communication be yea, yea; that is why we just say Lord's will, Lord's will I get this done.

The estimation is the value set for redeeming a person out of the vow. A male from twenty to sixty years old, the prime of life, was fifty shekels of silver after the shekel of the sanctuary, and a female thirty shekels. From five years to twenty years old the male was twenty shekels and the female ten; from a month old to five years the male was five shekels and the female three; and from sixty years old and above the male was fifteen shekels and the female ten. If the man was poorer than the estimation and could not pay it, he presented himself before the priest, and the priest valued him according to the ability of him that vowed, his worth and what he was able to bring forth.

If a beast was brought as an offering to the Most High it had to be holy, not blemished; it could not be altered or changed, a good for a bad or a bad for a good, and if it was changed at all, both it and the exchange became holy. An unclean beast, one with a blemish that could not be sacrificed, was presented before the priest and the priest valued it, good or bad; and to redeem it, a fifth part had to be added to the estimation to get that beast back.

A man could sanctify his house to be holy unto the Most High, and the priest estimated it, good or bad, and as the priest estimated it, so it stood. To redeem the house he added the fifth part of the money of the estimation: if the house was worth a hundred thousand, he paid that hundred thousand plus the extra twenty thousand, and it was his again.

A field sanctified to the Most High was estimated according to the seed thereof, an homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver; from the year of jubile the estimation stood full, but after the jubile the priest reckoned the money according to the years that remained, and it was abated from the estimation. The jubile was the year of release, when the land had to rest, so the value was reckoned by how close the jubile was: the fewer years left to reap the field, the lower the estimation. It is like trading in a car; a two year old car with twenty thousand miles brings more value than an old car with a hundred and fifty thousand miles on it. To redeem a sanctified field the fifth part was added to the estimation. A field not redeemed, or sold to another man, could not be redeemed any more, but went out in the jubile holy unto the Lord, a devoted field, the possession of the priest; and in the year of jubile a bought field returned to him of whom it was bought. All the estimations were according to the shekel of the sanctuary, twenty gerahs to the shekel; that was the standard, the set price.

The firstling of the beasts could not be sanctified by any man, because as a firstling it was the Lord's already, whether ox or sheep; an unclean firstling was redeemed by the estimation with the fifth part added, or sold according to the estimation. No devoted thing that a man devoted unto the Most High, of man, beast, or field of his possession, could be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy unto the Lord, and a devoted man was surely put to death.

All the tithe of the land, of the seed of the land or the fruit of the tree, is the Lord's; it is holy unto the Lord. To redeem out of the tithes a man added the fifth part thereto. The tithe of the herd and the flock, the tenth of whatsoever passeth under the rod, was holy unto the Lord; he was not to search whether it was good or bad or change it, and if he changed it at all, both it and the change were holy and could not be redeemed. The quick recap of the chapter: when a brother or sister vowed themselves to the Most High, the redemption from that vow went according to the estimation, by age and by sex, and likewise a house or a field; all these things go into how the priest calculated the estimation of these particular things to release you from the vow. The chapter can be tricky, so read it over and over. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The Lord told Aaron that he and his sons and his father's house would bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and of their priesthood; that was their job. This explains who should minister in the tabernacle after Israel's cry in the last chapter. The tribe of Levi was joined unto Aaron to minister unto him and keep the charge of the tabernacle, their jobs; only they were not to come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, the ark of the covenant and the different vessels, that neither they nor the priests die. The Levites were given to Aaron as a gift for the Lord, to do the service of the tabernacle; Aaron and his sons kept the priest's office for every thing of the altar and within the vail. The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death: an Israelite not of Levi could not come near the tabernacle.

The Lord gave Aaron the charge of the heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel, by reason of the anointing, to him and his sons by an ordinance for ever. Of the most holy things reserved from the fire, every oblation, meat offering, sin offering, and trespass offering was most holy for Aaron and his sons; the priests kept a portion of it and ate it in the most holy place. The heave offering of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Israel, was given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever; every one that is clean in the house could eat of it. This is what the children of Israel gave for the Levites.

All the best of the oil, the best of the wine, and the wheat, the firstfruits which they offered unto the Lord, were given to the priests; whatsoever is first ripe in the land was theirs, and every one that was clean in the house could eat of it. Every thing devoted in Israel was theirs.

Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, whether of men or beasts, was the Lord's; the firstborn was to be offered. Nevertheless the firstborn of man was surely redeemed, because you would not sacrifice the firstborn of our people, and the firstling of unclean beasts was redeemed also. Verse 16 explains how you redeem them: those to be redeemed from a month old were redeemed for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs; twenty gerahs equal one shekel. But the firstling of a cow, a sheep, or a goat was not redeemed, because those you could sacrifice: they are holy; their blood was sprinkled upon the altar and their fat burnt for an offering made by fire, for a sweet savour unto the Lord.

The flesh of them was the priest's, as the wave breast and as the right shoulder; all the heave offerings of the holy things which the children of Israel offered unto the Lord were given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever, to the lineage of the Levites. [Exodus 29](/bible/exodus/29) shows how the wave offering and the heave offering were done. The wave offering was put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved, meaning shaken, before the Lord; then it was received of their hands and burnt upon the altar. Each had a different way it was waved or lifted up to the Most High before it was actually burnt and offered to the Lord, and the breast of the ram of consecration was waved and became the priest's part. It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, unto Aaron and to his seed with him, the children that come after them.

The Lord told Aaron: thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither any part among them; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel. The Levites had no inheritance of land to pass down; the Most High said, I will be taking care of you. The Lord gave the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance. This is the tithe: the tenth part was given to the Levites for their service which they served, the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, their sacrificing and teaching of the laws. That tenth went to the children of Levi, and it was done away with when Christ came and died and took that priesthood; we no longer give that tenth to Levi. The children of Israel were not to come nigh the tabernacle of the congregation, lest they bear sin and die; it was a sin for the other tribes of Israel to come near the tabernacle, on pain of death. All the work to be done in the tabernacle was committed unto the Levites, and they bore their iniquity, a statute for ever.

When the Levites took of the children of Israel the tithes given them for their inheritance, they offered up of it an heave offering for the Lord, even a tenth part of the tithe: after the Levites got their tenth, the Most High wanted his tenth part of that, which they had to offer up. Their heave offering was reckoned unto them as though it were the corn of the threshingfloor and the fulness of the winepress, and the Lord's heave offering out of all their tithes was given to Aaron the priest; out of all their gifts they offered every heave offering of the Lord, of all the best thereof, even the hallowed part. When they had heaved the best thereof from it, they could eat it in every place, they and their households, for it was their reward for their service in the tabernacle of the congregation; and they bore no sin by reason of it when they heaved the best of it, neither polluted the holy things of the children of Israel, lest they die. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Ye are the children of the Lord your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead. These customs came from the other nations, like the young folks today cutting designs into their eyebrows; we are not supposed to be doing that. Cutting the flesh was a form of self-torture in mourning; the Most High requires none of that of us, only to be righteous and keep his commandments.

Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a peculiar people unto himself above all the nations upon the earth. Peter writes to that same peculiar people, a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation: his letter is addressed to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. Who were those strangers? Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, dwelling in the very regions Peter lists, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia; that is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are. Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing: this rules the whole chapter. The whatsoever thy soul lusteth after of chapter 12 sits inside these guidelines of clean foods; you cannot eat anything you want. Some of our people, still unlearned, think that as long as they pray over it they can eat it; that is not true, it is a misunderstanding carried out of the New Testament. The law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing. The chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls; the rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods.

Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed that the field bringeth forth year by year, and eat before the Lord the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, that thou mayest learn to fear the Lord thy God always. The corn, wine, and oil are the same increase promised in chapter 11 for hearkening to the commandments; this all goes together. If Israel did not keep the commandments, he would shut up the heaven, there would be no rain, the land would be chapt, and famine would teach the fear of the Lord. Today Israel is disconnected from that fear because the oppressor nourishes us; the food comes from the grocery store. That understanding must be brought back to our people, and that is why the laws are read four chapters a day, from Genesis all the way to Revelation, to gain the understanding that we are the Israelites.

Ye are cursed with a curse: for ye have robbed me, even this whole nation.

Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the field, saith the Lord of hosts.
And all nations shall call you blessed: for ye shall be a delightsome land, saith the Lord of hosts.
And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them: for the Levites and the singers, that did the work, were fled every one to his field.
Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.
Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.
Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?
Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.

Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.

cases.name: Alcimus
cases.charge: Slandering Judas to the king; slaying sixty Asideans under a sworn peace; pulling down the wall of the inner court
cases.summary: Alcimus, who had defiled himself wilfully in the times of the mingling with the Gentiles, sought the high priesthood from Demetrius by accusing Judas Maccabeus of sedition. Sent with an army, he swore peace to the Asideans and killed sixty of them in one day. Later he commanded the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary pulled down, the work of the prophets.
cases.offense: Perjury, judicial murder, and sacrilege by a priest. The people remembered the psalm over the dead: the flesh of thy saints have they cast out, and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them.
cases.judgment: As he began to pull down the wall, Alcimus was plagued; his mouth was stopped, he was taken with a palsy, and could no more speak or set his house in order. So Alcimus died at that time with great torment.

entries.commentary: The heathen have come into the inheritance of the Most High, defiled His holy temple, and laid Jerusalem on heaps. The dead bodies of His servants have been given as meat to the fowls of heaven and the flesh of His saints to the beasts of the earth, their blood shed like water round about Jerusalem with none to bury them. This is not a one-time thing. It happened before David a few times, when Babylon besieged us first, again during the time of the Greeks who destroyed our land, and again in 70 A.D. when we were pushed out of the land. During the Greeks not all of us were pushed out and taken captive in other nations like with Babylon and 70 A.D. Even during the time of kings, our forefather King Zedekiah was taken into captivity, he and his sons and daughters. A remnant was taken captive in Babylon, which is why Daniel was born there, and they destroyed the temple and the city. We are become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us. The neighbors in this context are the enemies, the other nations, the heathen. You know this because verse one already established that the heathen came in and defiled the temple, so the neighbors reproaching us are those same nations. -

The prayer asks how long the Most High will be angry, and whether His jealousy shall burn like fire forever. It asks Him to pour out His wrath upon the heathen that have not known Him and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon His name, for they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place. The heathen having "not known thee" does not mean there are heathen who do know the Lord. To know God is to keep His commandments, and the commandments were only given to the israelites. The other nations do not truly know God, His ways, or His judgments; we do. -

The plea is that the Most High remember not against us former iniquities, that His tender mercies speedily prevent us, for we are brought very low. It asks Him to help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of His name, to deliver us and purge away our sins for His name's sake. It asks why the heathen should say, Where is their God, and that He be known among the heathen in our sight by avenging the blood of His servants which is shed.

Let the sighing of the prisoner come before Him, and according to the greatness of His power let Him preserve those that are appointed to die. Render unto our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom the reproach wherewith they have reproached the Lord. The neighbors here in verse twelve, like verse four, are the other nations. You know this because verse thirteen turns to the redemption of the people. So we His people and sheep of His pasture will give Him thanks forever and show forth His praise to all generations. This goes into when the Most High redeems us from the hands of our enemies; we will give thanks forever when we get into the kingdom.

verses.text: There came unto him all the wicked and ungodly men of Israel, having Alcimus, who was desirous to be high priest, for their captain:
And they accused the people to the king, saying, Judas and his brethren have slain all thy friends, and driven us out of our own land.
Now therefore send some man whom thou trustest, and let him go and see what havock he hath made among us, and in the king’s land, and let him punish them with all them that aid them.
Then the king chose Bacchides, a friend of the king, who ruled beyond the flood, and was a great man in the kingdom, and faithful to the king,
And him he sent with that wicked Alcimus, whom he made high priest, and commanded that he should take vengeance of the children of Israel.
Then did there assemble unto Alcimus and Bacchides a company of scribes, to require justice.
Now the Assideans were the first among the children of Israel that sought peace of them:
For said they, One that is a priest of the seed of Aaron is come with this army, and he will do us no wrong.
So he spake unto them, peaceably, and sware unto them, saying, we will procure the harm neither of you nor your friends.
Whereupon they believed him: howbeit he took of them threescore men, and slew them in one day, according to the words which he wrote,
The flesh of thy saints have they cast out, and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them.
Wherefore the fear and dread of them fell upon all the people, who said, There is neither truth nor righteousness in them; for they have broken the covenant and oath that they made.
But Alcimus contended for the high priesthood.
And unto him resorted all such as troubled the people, who, after they had gotten the land of Juda into their power, did much hurt in Israel.
Now when Judas saw all the mischief that Alcimus and his company had done among the Israelites, even above the heathen,
He went out into all the coasts of Judea round about, and took vengeance of them that had revolted from him, so that they durst no more go forth into the country.

On the other side, when Alcimus saw that Judas and his company had gotten the upper hand, and knew that he was not able to abide their force, he went again to the king, and said all the worst of them that he could.

Moreover in the hundred fifty and third year, in the second month, Alcimus commanded that the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary should be pulled down; he pulled down also the works of the prophets

And as he began to pull down, even at that time was Alcimus plagued, and his enterprizes hindered: for his mouth was stopped, and he was taken with a palsy, so that he could no more speak any thing, nor give order concerning his house.
So Alcimus died at that time with great torment.

Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles, seeing that by no means he could save himself, nor have any more access to the holy altar,

Came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fiftieth year, presenting unto him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace.
Howbeit having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprize, and being called into counsel by Demetrius, and asked how the Jews stood affected, and what they intended, he answered thereunto:
Those of the Jews that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace.
Therefore I, being deprived of mine ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither:

First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of mine own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforesaid.
Wherefore, O king, seeing knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that thou readily shewest unto all.
For as long as Judas liveth, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.

But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was betwixt them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king’s successor.

Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste unto Antioch.
The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the heaven, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; and there was none to bury them.

cases.name: Aman, who ensnared Achiacharus
cases.charge: Treachery against the man who brought him up
cases.summary: Tobit's dying counsel to his son holds up one case: remember how Aman handled Achiacharus that brought him up, how out of light he brought him into darkness, and how he rewarded him again. Achiacharus, the king's cupbearer and Tobit's kinsman, had once interceded for Tobit himself.
cases.offense: Ingratitude become betrayal, against a benefactor who stood as a father. The story assumed by the text is the tale of Ahikar: the adopted nephew who forged evidence to have his uncle executed.
cases.judgment: Achiacharus was saved, but the other had his reward: for he went down into darkness. Aman fell into the snare and perished. Tobit's moral: consider what alms doeth, and how righteousness doth deliver.

entries.commentary: As snow in summer and rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool. As the bird wandering and the swallow flying, the causeless curse shall not come. A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back. Ecclesiasticus says the same: correction and work are for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back. -

Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you become like him. Many of us have argued with an idiot and been made to look like an idiot; onlookers wonder why you are even arguing with him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. He that sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks damage.

The legs of the lame are not equal, and so is a parable in the mouth of fools. As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he that gives honor to a fool. As a thorn goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools. Like a splinter driven under the skin, it hurts and can take days to work out.

The great God that formed all things both rewards the fool and rewards transgressors. As a dog returns to his vomit, so a fool returns to his folly. Second Peter calls this a true proverb, showing the apostles quoted Solomon: those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning. -

Do you see a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope for a fool than for him. The slothful man says there is a lion in the way and in the streets. As the door turns on its hinges, so the slothful turns on his bed; he hides his hand in his bosom and it grieves him to bring it back to his mouth. The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

He that passes by and meddles with strife not belonging to him is like one that takes a dog by the ears. Ecclesiasticus warns not to strive in a matter that does not concern you. A young lady who tried to break up a high-school fight was grabbed by police, slammed face-first, and left with brain damage; the Bible is a true book. As a madman who casts firebrands, arrows, and death, so is the man that deceives his neighbor and says, "Am I not in sport?" -

Where there is no wood the fire goes out, and where there is no tale-bearer the strife ceases. As coals to burning coals and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindle strife. The words of a tale-bearer are as wounds that go down into the innermost parts of the belly. Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.

He that hates dissembles with his lips and lays up deceit within, so when he speaks fair, do not believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart. Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the whole congregation, put out on display. Luke says nothing is covered that shall not be revealed. Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit; that thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High. -

Whoever digs a pit shall fall in it, and he that rolls a stone will have it return upon him. A lying tongue hates those that are afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin. That flattery is deceit.

This is the prayer that we all have, especially us as Israel. We want the Most High to fight against those who fight against us. That is a righteous prayer that our forefather David had. This is the prayer we have for everybody that comes against us. If you do not feel like that, then you do not believe in the Bible. David is praying that the same destruction his enemies want to bring on him falls on them instead. That is what we have to understand: the Most High is not a god of saving everybody, he is a god of destroying our enemies. He has been that way and it is not going to change.

The salvation David rejoices in is the destruction of his enemies. That is what salvation is. You cannot be saved if you still have to answer to your enemies. You do not save the wolf and the sheep together. They just came out with more footage about Ahmaud Arbery saying the brother was still alive when the police came, and the one who shot him admitted it, and the police still let them go home. These are the things we have to pray for. That is the salvation we are looking for. We do not worship a God that saves our enemies alongside us. No matter what we think, Esau is too strong for us right now. He owns a military. Black people do not own a military. You may be able to fight one and win, but we do not own a military. We are behind enemy lines. They took over this country and we still have not taken it back. The Most High is the only one who is going to save us from that one who is stronger than us. That is what David prophesied about the nation of Israel.

False witnesses rise up and lay to our charge things we knew not. That happens with us right now. You have our own brothers claiming we are with the Rosicrucians, sold out to the Illuminati, that we wear purple because we had to choose a color. The most racist people in the world are not going to recruit us. We have our own money; we gave out gold coins worth a million dollars at the 2015 or 2016 Passover. They rewarded evil for good, but when they were sick, David's clothing was sackcloth and he humbled his soul with fasting. That is praying for your enemies and for those that despitefully use and persecute you. You do not go railing for railing. You defend yourself, but you do not turn around and do something wicked back to them. When they were down, David felt their pain just as they had felt it. That is how we have to move. David bowed down heavily as one that mourns for his mother, but in his adversity they rejoiced and gathered themselves together against him. When our school got hit by a tornado, people on Facebook and all social media were rejoicing, saying all praises to the Lord that a tornado hit our school. But those same people, when they needed help, we were there. A lot of it we did not say anything about, because this is the prayer we had: let the Most High look on it and see how we move and how they move, and let him judge that. Our feast days are full of hypocrites, people who do not have the betterment of their people at heart. They come to the feast days, the new moons, the sabbaths, and sit there wicked, crept in unawares. It always happens. This is what David was talking about when he spoke of hypocritical mockers in feast.

David cries out asking how long the Most High will look on, and asks him to rescue his soul from their destructions. He asks that his enemies not wrongfully rejoice over him nor wink with the eye that hate him without a cause. When we fall or do something, they point and mock, "Aha, aha, I have seen it." No matter what happens, you have to keep the commandments of the Most High and keep your faith in him. When everybody is against you, keep your faith. That is the example David set.

David asks the Most High not to keep silence, to stir up himself and awake to his judgment, and to judge him according to his righteousness. He prays that his enemies not say in their hearts, "We would have had it," or "We have swallowed him up," but that they be brought to confusion. There are people not in the body who see what we go through and pray the best for us. Brothers from a lot of different backgrounds saw what we went through as a body and said they pray the best for us. That is a righteous thing to have. But the ones who do not, the prayer is to let them be brought to confusion, along with all the stuff they talk all the time.

verses.text: And bury me decently, and thy mother with me; but tarry no longer at Nineve. Remember, my son, how Aman handled Achiacharus that brought him up, how out of light he brought him into darkness, and how he rewarded him again: yet Achiacharus was saved, but the other had his reward: for he went down into darkness. Manasses gave alms, and escaped the snares of death which they had set for him: but Aman fell into the snare, and perished.

Wherefore now, my son, consider what alms doeth, and how righteousness doth deliver. When he had said these things, he gave up the ghost in the bed, being an hundred and eight and fifty years old; and he buried him honourably.

And there passed not five and fifty days, before two of his sons killed him, and they fled into the mountains of Ararath; and Sarchedonus his son reigned in his stead; who appointed over his father’s accounts, and over all his affairs, Achiacharus my brother Anael’s son.

And Achiacharus intreating for me, I returned to Nineve. Now Achiacharus was cupbearer, and keeper of the signet, and steward, and overseer of the accounts: and Sarchedonus appointed him next unto him: and he was my brother’s son.

And I knew not that there were sparrows in the wall, and mine eyes being open, the sparrows muted warm dung into mine eyes, and a whiteness came in mine eyes: and I went to the physicians, but they helped me not: moreover Achiacharus did nourish me, until I went into Elymais.
And Achiacharus, and Nasbas his brother’s son, came:
Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
For without cause have they hid for me their net in a pit, which without cause they have digged for my soul.
Let destruction come upon him at unawares; and let his net that he hath hid catch himself: into that very destruction let him fall.

cases.name: Andronicus
cases.charge: Murder of Onias the high priest under a sworn assurance
cases.summary: Onias, having exposed Menelaus' theft of the temple vessels, took sanctuary at Daphne. Menelaus persuaded the king's deputy Andronicus to lure him out; he came to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths, and though suspected, persuaded him to leave the sanctuary, and shut him up immediately without regard of justice.
cases.offense: A murder achieved by a false oath and the violation of asylum. Even the Greeks, the text says, were grieved for the unjust death of a man who had lived soberly and in virtue.
cases.judgment: When Antiochus heard of it he was sorry in his mind, and sent for Andronicus, stripped him of his purple, rent his clothes, led him through the city, and slew him in the same place where he had committed impiety against Onias. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.

entries.commentary: If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he came in by himself he goes out by himself; if he were married when he came in, his wife goes out with him. Deuteronomy repeats the same judgment for a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman sold unto thee. [Nehemiah 5](/bible/nehemiah/5) shows how brethren came into servitude: in the dearth some mortgaged lands, vineyards, and houses to buy corn, some borrowed money for the king's tribute, and some brought their sons and daughters into bondage. The brother that waxes poor is not to be compelled to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant, and not ruled over harshly. If the master gave him a wife and she bare him sons or daughters, the wife and her children are the master's, and he goes out by himself; he did not bring them in. His two choices are to go out alone, or to plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children, have his ear bored through with an aul at the door post, and serve his master for ever. Zedekiah's covenant in Jeremiah confirms the law in the prophets: every man was to let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release.

If a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do. The reason is that her master betrothed her to himself, or unto his son; she is a wife, not a six-year servant, so the release of the menservants does not apply to her. If she please not her master who hath betrothed her to himself, he must let her be redeemed; he has no power to sell her unto a strange nation, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her. The deceit is that he betrothed her to himself and then would not deal with her, keeping her to himself when she could have been another man's wife. If he take him another wife, her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage shall he not diminish; the duty of marriage is the marriage bed. If he lay with her, she belongs to him and he cannot send her away; and if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money. He must take care of her.

If a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand, a place was appointed whither he shall flee. That is the case of the slayer that kills his neighbour ignorantly, as when a man hews wood with his neighbour and the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon him that he die: he flees to the appointed city and lives, lest the avenger of blood overtake him while his heart is hot, for he was not worthy of death, having hated him not in time past. But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die. Men would run and grab the horns of the altar, but wilful murder found no refuge there.

If men strive and one smite another so that he keep his bed, he that smote him shall pay for the loss of his time and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed. That is restitution: paying for the time the man was down and could not work and provide for his family. That is what the court system calls a civil suit today.

If a man smite his servant with a rod and he die under his hand, he shall surely be punished; but if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished, for he is his money. The wisdom writings teach not to be ashamed of much correction of children, nor of making the side of an evil servant to bleed. An evil servant that will not get right could be corrected physically, so long as he was not killed.

If men strive and hurt a woman with child so that her fruit depart from her, this judgment covers the miscarriage: if no mischief follow, he is punished as the woman's husband lays upon him and the judges determine; and if any mischief follow, then life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound.

If an ox gore a man or a woman that they die, the ox is stoned and his flesh not eaten, and the owner is quit. But if the ox were wont to push with his horns in time past, and it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, and it kill a man or a woman, the ox is stoned and his owner also put to death. Most do not have oxen today, but the same judgment reaches the yard dogs, the pit bulls, German shepherds, and rottweilers. If the dog has bitten before and it was reported to you, and it gets out again through a snapped chain or a breach in the fence and mauls or kills somebody, the scripture holds the owner responsible unto death; that is why animal control writes the ticket and warns you to keep your dogs in. The law is slack right now, as Habakkuk says, so many punishments worthy of death in the scriptures, like rape or this judgment, come out today as a fine or a slap on the hand.

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

verses.text: While those things were in doing, they of Tarsus and Mallos made insurrection, because they were given to the king’s concubine, called Antiochus.
Then came the king in all haste to appease matters, leaving Andronicus, a man in authority, for his deputy.

Now Menelaus, supposing that he had gotten a convenient time, stole certain vessels of gold out of the temple, and gave some of them to Andronicus, and some he sold into Tyrus and the cities round about.
Which when Onias knew of a surety, he reproved him, and withdrew himself into a sanctuary at Daphne, that lieth by Antiochia.

Wherefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus apart, prayed, him to get Onias into his hands; who being persuaded thereunto, and coming to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths; and though he were suspected by him, yet persuaded he him to come forth of the sanctuary: whom forthwith he shut up without regard of justice.
For the which cause not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man.

And when the king was come again from the places about Cilicia, the Jews that were in the city, and certain of the Greeks that abhorred the fact also, complained because Onias was slain without cause.
Therefore Antiochus was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead.

And being kindled with anger, forthwith he took away Andronicus his purple, and rent off his clothes, and leading him through the whole city unto that very place, where he had committed impiety against Onias, there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.
But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.
Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen.

cases.name: Antiochus Epiphanes
cases.charge: Defiling the temple; forbidding the law; murdering the faithful
cases.summary: The Seleucid king outlawed the law of Moses, defiled the temple with an idol, and put to death those who kept the covenant. The books of Maccabees record both his persecution and his end.
cases.offense: He forbade circumcision and the sabbaths, set up the abomination on the altar, forced sacrifice to idols, and killed mothers who circumcised their sons and families who kept the law in secret.
cases.judgment: Struck with an incurable disease of the bowels, worms rising from the living body, he died in a strange land in bitter grief, by the account, confessing at the last that it was right to be subject to God.

entries.commentary: In the first year of Darius the Mede, the messenger stood to confirm and to strengthen him.

Three more kings would stand up in Persia: Cyrus, Cambyses, and Darius. The fourth would be far richer than they all. This is Xerxes, who profited from all that the kingdom had already gained, and by his strength through his riches he stirred up all against the realm of Grecia. This is where they gathered all the heathen together and formed the Greeks. They conquered the original Greeks and named themselves the Greeks, and all the nations, even some of my own tribes, came together and were called the Greeks.

The mighty king that stands up and rules with great dominion, doing according to his will, is Alexander the Greek. When a nation is a superpower it does what it will and nobody can stop it, the same as America does today. When he stood up his kingdom was broken, because he eventually died and left no children, so it was not passed to his posterity. His kingdom was divided toward the four winds of heaven, to his four generals, Cassander, Lysimachus, Seleucus, and Ptolemy, not according to his own dominion.
The king of the south that grows strong is Ptolemy, who was over Egypt. One of his princes grows strong above him with a great dominion. Out of Ptolemy came Antiochus.

In the end of years they join themselves together, and the king's daughter of the south comes to the king of the north to make an agreement. She does not retain the power of the arm, neither does he stand nor his arm. The power of the arm is Antiochus' strength.

Out of a branch of her roots one stands up in her estate, comes with an army, enters the fortress of the king of the north, deals against them and prevails. It was actual war over the kingdoms. He carries captives into Egypt, their gods with their princes and their precious vessels of silver and gold, for Ptolemy was over Egypt, and he continues more years than the king of the north.

His sons are stirred up, assemble a multitude of great forces, and one comes and overflows and passes through, even to his fortress. The king of the south is moved with anger, comes forth, and fights the king of the north, who sets forth a great multitude, but the multitude is given into the hand of the south. When he has taken away the multitude his heart is lifted up and he becomes prideful, casting down many ten thousands, but he is not strengthened by it.
The king of the north returns and sets forth a multitude greater than the former, coming after certain years with a great army and much riches.

In those times many stand up against the king of the south, meaning Ptolemy. The robbers of thy people, the heathen, the Greeks who robbed Israel, exalt themselves to establish the vision, but they shall fall.

The king of the north comes up, casts up a mount, and takes the most fenced cities, and the arms of the south cannot withstand, neither his chosen people, meaning Israel, nor any strength to withstand. He that comes against him does according to his own will, and none stands before him, because he is the power at this time, and he stands in the glorious land which is consumed by his hand.

He sets his face to enter with the strength of his whole kingdom, and gives him the daughter of women, corrupting her, but she does not stand on his side. He turns his face unto the isles of the coastline and takes many, but a prince causes the reproach he offered to cease and turns it back upon him. Someone causes him to stop conquering land, so he is conquered and falls, and this goes to Ptolemy. Then he turns his face toward the fort of his own land, but he stumbles and falls and is not found.
In his estate stands up a raiser of taxes in the glory of the kingdom, a ruler taxing and ruling the people, but within few days he is destroyed, neither in anger nor in battle.
In his estate stands up a vile person to whom they do not give the honor of the kingdom, but he comes in peaceably and obtains the kingdom by flatteries. -
With the arms of a flood they are overflown and broken from before him, yea also the prince of the covenant, and after the league made with him he works deceitfully. -

After the league is made he works deceitfully, this being Jason working deceitfully against his own people. He comes up and becomes strong with a small people. He enters peaceably even upon the fattest places of the province, the best places of the land, and does what his fathers and his fathers' fathers had not done, scattering among them the prey and spoil and riches, going against his own people for riches.
He stirs up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south is stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army. -

They that feed of the portion of his meat destroy him, his army overflows, and many fall down slain. Both these kings' hearts are set to do mischief, and they speak lies at one table, but it does not prosper, for the end is yet at the time appointed.
Then he returns into his land with great riches, and his heart is against the holy covenant. -

At the time appointed he returns toward the south, but it is not as the former, for the ships of Chittim come against him, therefore he is grieved and has indignation against the holy covenant. He returns and has intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant, because our people were forsaking the laws at this time. -
An arm stands on his part, they pollute the sanctuary of strength, take away the daily sacrifice, and place the abomination that maketh desolate. -

Such as do wickedly against the covenant he corrupts by flatteries, but the people that do know their God shall be strong and do exploits. They that understand among the people instruct many, yet they fall by the sword, by flame, by captivity, and by spoil many days, and some of understanding fall to try them, to purge, and to make them white, even to the time of the end. -

The king does according to his will, exalts and magnifies himself above every god, and speaks marvelous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the indignation is accomplished. He does not regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor any god, for he magnifies himself above all. In his estate he honors the god of forces, a god whom his fathers knew not, with gold and silver and precious stones, and he causes them to rule over many and divides the land for gain.

At the time of the end the king of the south pushes at him, and the king of the north comes against him like a whirlwind with chariots and horsemen and many ships, and enters into the countries and overflows and passes over. He enters the glorious land, and many countries are overthrown, but Edom and Moab and the chief of the children of Ammon escape out of his hand. He stretches his hand upon the countries, and Egypt does not escape, and he has power over the treasures of gold and silver, with the Libyans and the Ethiopians at his steps. Tidings out of the east and north trouble him, so he goes forth with great fury to destroy, and plants the tabernacles of his palace between the seas in the glorious holy mountain, yet he comes to his end and none shall help him.
