verses.text: Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people,
And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king.
Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.
For the king had sent letters by messengers unto Jerusalem and the cities of Juda that they should follow the strange laws of the land,
And forbid burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and drink offerings, in the temple; and that they should profane the sabbaths and festival days:
And pollute the sanctuary and holy people:
Set up altars, and groves, and chapels of idols, and sacrifice swine’s flesh, and unclean beasts:
That they should also leave their children uncircumcised, and make their souls abominable with all manner of uncleanness and profanation:
To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.
And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.

Now the fifteenth day of the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and fifth year, they set up the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and builded idol altars throughout the cities of Juda on every side;
And burnt incense at the doors of their houses, and in the streets.
And when they had rent in pieces the books of the law which they found, they burnt them with fire.
And whosoever was found with any the book of the testament, or if any committed to the law, the king’s commandment was, that they should put him to death.
Thus did they by their authority unto the Israelites every month, to as many as were found in the cities.
Now the five and twentieth day of the month they did sacrifice upon the idol altar, which was upon the altar of God.
At which time according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised.
And they hanged the infants about their necks, and rifled their houses, and slew them that had circumcised them.
Howbeit many in Israel were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat any unclean thing.
Wherefore the rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.
And there was very great wrath upon Israel.
Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God:
And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.

But the Lord Almighty, the God of Isreal, smote him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;
And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.

Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews, and commanding to haste the journey: but it came to pass that he fell down from his chariot, carried violently; so that having a sore fall, all the members of his body were much pained.

And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground, and carried in an horselitter, shewing forth unto all the manifest power of God.
So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.
And the man, that thought a little afore he could reach to the stars of heaven, no man could endure to carry for his intolerable stink.
And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.
Now when the king heard these words, he was astonished and sore moved: whereupon he laid him down upon his bed, and fell sick for grief, because it had not befallen him as he looked for.
And there he continued many days: for his grief was ever more and more, and he made account that he should die.
Wherefore he called for all his friends, and said unto them, The sleep is gone from mine eyes, and my heart faileth for very care.
And I thought with myself, Into what tribulation am I come, and how great a flood of misery is it, wherein now I am! for I was bountiful and beloved in my power.
But now I remember the evils that I did at Jerusalem, and that I took all the vessels of gold and silver that were therein, and sent to destroy the inhabitants of Judea without a cause.
I perceive therefore that for this cause these troubles are come upon me, and, behold, I perish through great grief in a strange land.

cases.name: Apollonius
cases.charge: Falling upon Jerusalem on the Sabbath under a pretence of peace; slaying a great multitude; taking women and children captive
cases.summary: Sent by Antiochus with twenty-two thousand men, Apollonius spoke peaceable words to Jerusalem, waited for the Sabbath when the people would not fight, and slew them going out to see the show. Judas Maccabeus met him in the field, killed him, and carried his sword for the rest of his life.
cases.offense: He came to Jerusalem, and speaking peaceable words unto them, but all was deceit: for when they had given him credence, he fell suddenly upon the city, and smote it very sore, and destroyed much people of Israel. He took the spoils of the city, set it on fire, and pulled down the houses and walls round about. He commanded his men to arm themselves, and to slay all those that went out to see the holy Sabbath, and there were slain great multitudes.
cases.judgment: Judas gathered those that were willing, and Apollonius gathered the Gentiles together, and a great host out of Samaria, to fight against Israel. Judas perceived it, and went forth to meet him, and so he smote him, and slew him: many also fell down slain, but the rest fled. Wherefore Judas took their spoils, and Apollonius' sword also, and therewith he fought all his life long.

entries.commentary: The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship, to devise cunning works, to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of timber. With him the Lord gave Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted, that they might make all that he had commanded. The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

The wise hearted made all that was commanded: the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is thereupon, all the furniture of the tabernacle, the table and his furniture, the pure candlestick with all his furniture, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot. They made the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons to minister in the priest's office, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense for the holy place, according to all that the Lord commanded. That spirit of workmanship on Israel is why the tabernacle, and later the house Solomon built for the Lord, outshined anything the world had seen; and though strangers shall build up our walls in the kingdom, it will be Israel directing how the Lord wants it done.

Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God; the nations do not have this sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel. Every one that defileth the sabbath shall surely be put to death. The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown; the Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people. Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God.

The children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant; it is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed. Christians use [Mark 2:27](/bible/mark/2#v27) to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude.

When he had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai, he gave him two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God. God literally wrote the testimony with his finger, and we know that was Christ.

David asks the Most High to give ear to his prayer and not hide from his supplication. You have to put yourself in the Bible and see yourself in these scriptures, the way Elder Kena, Bishop, and the leadership men teach. He mourns and makes a noise because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked, who cast iniquity upon him and hate him in wrath. The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil. -

His heart is sore pained within him and the terrors of death are fallen upon him. Think about the condition we are in today; even keeping the commandments, we still suffer the same oppression, though the Most High covers those that keep them. When you drive, police will still jump behind you and run your plates, so make sure your tags are legal and not expired. The fearfulness and trembling and horror are written in the curses, the curses we did not learn in the Christian church. Many of the scriptures come back to these curses. -

He wishes for wings like a dove to fly away and be at rest, to wander far off and remain in the wilderness, hastening his escape from the windy storm and tempest. When these things come upon us many times you would think, if I could just get away, just leave this place. But the scriptures say we must serve out this punishment and endure much tribulation to enter the kingdom. Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield. -

He asks the Most High to destroy and divide their tongues, for he has seen violence and strife in the city. This is us being cursed in the city. You want to hasten your escape because you open the doors and go out into the world to work, shop, or school, and there is all this strife among our people. Moses dealt with the same thing when he left Pharaoh's house and found two men fighting. Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets. -

It was not an enemy that reproached him, which he could have borne, but a man his equal, his guide and his acquaintance, with whom he took sweet counsel and walked to the house of God. This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth. -

He asks that death seize the wicked and they go down quick into hell, for wickedness is in their dwellings, while he calls upon the Most High evening, morning, and at noon, and is heard and delivered. The Most High hears and afflicts them because they have no changes; there was no change in us, no repentance. Even when He pitied us and provided everything, bearing us on His wings, we rebelled and vexed His Holy Spirit, so He turned to be our enemy. -

The betrayer put forth his hands against those at peace with him and broke his covenant; his words were smoother than butter and softer than oil, yet were drawn swords, war in his heart. Cast thy burden upon the Most High and He shall sustain thee; He will never suffer the righteous to be moved, but bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days.

verses.text: And after two years fully expired the king sent his chief collector of tribute unto the cities of Juda, who came unto Jerusalem with a great multitude,
And spake peaceable words unto them, but all was deceit: for when they had given him credence, he fell suddenly upon the city, and smote it very sore, and destroyed much people of Israel.
And when he had taken the spoils of the city, he set it on fire, and pulled down the houses and walls thereof on every side.
But the women and children took they captive, and possessed the cattle.
Then builded they the city of David with a great and strong wall, and with mighty towers, and made it a strong hold for them.
And they put therein a sinful nation, wicked men, and fortified themselves therein.
They stored it also with armour and victuals, and when they had gathered together the spoils of Jerusalem, they laid them up there, and so they became a sore snare:
For it was a place to lie in wait against the sanctuary, and an evil adversary to Israel.
Thus they shed innocent blood on every side of the sanctuary, and defiled it:

Insomuch that the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them: whereupon the city was made an habitation of strangers, and became strange to those that were born in her; and her own children left her.
Her sanctuary was laid waste like a wilderness, her feasts were turned into mourning, her sabbaths into reproach her honour into contempt.
As had been her glory, so was her dishonour increased, and her excellency was turned into mourning.
He sent also that detestable ringleader Apollonius with an army of two and twenty thousand, commanding him to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort:
Who coming to Jerusalem, and pretending peace, did forbear till the holy day of the sabbath, when taking the Jews keeping holy day, he commanded his men to arm themselves.
And so he slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the sabbath, and running through the city with weapons slew great multitudes.
Then Apollonius gathered the Gentiles together, and a great host out of Samaria, to fight against Israel.
Which thing when Judas perceived, he went forth to meet him, and so he smote him, and slew him: many also fell down slain, but the rest fled.
Wherefore Judas took their spoils, and Apollonius’ sword also, and therewith he fought all his life long.

Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death: for whosoever doeth any work therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.

cases.name: Heliodorus
cases.charge: Attempting to plunder the temple treasury
cases.summary: Sent by King Seleucus on the information of Simon the temple governor, Heliodorus came to seize the money laid up in the treasury, though the high priest Onias told him it was the relief of widows and fatherless children and deposits held in trust. The whole city lay in sackcloth. He went in anyway.
cases.offense: Sacrilege against the place, and theft from the poor the place protected. The law that forbids afflicting widows and the fatherless, and the law that makes God's house holy, were both in front of him. He proceeded as he had resolved.
cases.judgment: A horse with a terrible rider in golden armor struck him with its forefeet, and two young men scourged him without ceasing; he fell to the ground in darkness and was carried out on a litter. Onias offered sacrifice for his life, and he lived. He returned to the king and testified: if thou hast any enemy or traitor, send him thither, and thou shalt receive him well scourged.

entries.commentary: If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

The Most High reigneth, clothed with majesty and girded with strength. The world is established that it cannot be moved, and His throne is established of old; He is from everlasting. The floods have lifted up their voice and their waves, but the Most High on high is mightier than the noise of many waters.

His testimonies are very sure; holiness becometh His house forever. If each of us took a strong look at ourselves, we are more wise than before we came into the knowledge of the truth, because we should be growing in understanding as we continue to apply the commandments. The scriptures are spiritual; the law is spiritual. -

verses.text: But one Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was made governor of the temple, fell out with the high priest about disorder in the city.
And when he could not overcome Onias, he gat him to Apollonius the son of Thraseas, who then was governor of Celosyria and Phenice,

And told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money, so that the multitude of their riches, which did not pertain to the account of the sacrifices, was innumerable, and that it was possible to bring all into the king’s hand.

Now when Apollonius came to the king, and had shewed him of the money whereof he was told, the king chose out Heliodorus his treasurer, and sent him with a commandment to bring him the foresaid money.
So forthwith Heliodorus took his journey; under a colour of visiting the cities of Celosyria and Phenice, but indeed to fulfil the king’s purpose.

And when he was come to Jerusalem, and had been courteously received of the high priest of the city, he told him what intelligence was given of the money, and declared wherefore he came, and asked if these things were so indeed.
Then the high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children:

And that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: the sum whereof in all was four hundred talents of silver, and two hundred of gold:

And that it was altogether impossible that such wrongs should be done unto them, that had committed it to the holiness of the place, and to the majesty and inviolable sanctity of the temple, honoured over all the world.
But Heliodorus, because of the king’s commandment given him, said, That in any wise it must be brought into the king’s treasury.
So at the day which he appointed he entered in to order this matter: wherefore there was no small agony throughout the whole city.

But the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests’ vestments, called unto heaven upon him that made a law concerning things given to he kept, that they should safely be preserved for such as had committed them to be kept.
Then whoso had looked the high priest in the face, it would have wounded his heart: for his countenance and the changing of his colour declared the inward agony of his mind.
For the man was so compassed with fear and horror of the body, that it was manifest to them that looked upon him, what sorrow he had now in his heart.
Others ran flocking out of their houses to the general supplication, because the place was like to come into contempt.
And the women, girt with sackcloth under their breasts, abounded in the streets, and the virgins that were kept in ran, some to the gates, and some to the walls, and others looked out of the windows.
And all, holding their hands toward heaven, made supplication.
Then it would have pitied a man to see the falling down of the multitude of all sorts, and the fear of the high priest being in such an agony.
They then called upon the Almighty Lord to keep the things committed of trust safe and sure for those that had committed them.
Nevertheless Heliodorus executed that which was decreed.

Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, the Lord of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of God, and fainted, and were sore afraid.

For there appeared unto them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and smote at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.

Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.
And Heliodorus fell suddenly unto the ground, and was compassed with great darkness: but they that were with him took him up, and put him into a litter.

Thus him, that lately came with a great train and with all his guard into the said treasury, they carried out, being unable to help himself with his weapons: and manifestly they acknowledged the power of God.
For he by the hand of God was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.

But they praised the Lord, that had miraculously honoured his own place: for the temple; which a little afore was full of fear and trouble, when the Almighty Lord appeared, was filled with joy and gladness.
Then straightways certain of Heliodorus’ friends prayed Onias, that he would call upon the most High to grant him his life, who lay ready to give up the ghost.
So the high priest, suspecting lest the king should misconceive that some treachery had been done to Heliodorus by the Jews, offered a sacrifice for the health of the man.

Now as the high priest was making an atonement, the same young men in the same clothing appeared and stood beside Heliodorus, saying, Give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake the Lord hath granted thee life:
And seeing that thou hast been scourged from heaven, declare unto all men the mighty power of God. And when they had spoken these words, they appeared no more.
So Heliodorus, after he had offered sacrifice unto the Lord, and made great vows unto him that had saved his life, and saluted Onias, returned with his host to the king.
Then testified he to all men the works of the great God, which he had seen with his eyes.
And when the king Heliodorus, who might be a fit man to be sent yet once again to Jerusalem, he said,
If thou hast any enemy or traitor, send him thither, and thou shalt receive him well scourged, if he escape with his life: for in that place, no doubt; there is an especial power of God.
For he that dwelleth in heaven hath his eye on that place, and defendeth it; and he beateth and destroyeth them that come to hurt it.
And the things concerning Heliodorus, and the keeping of the treasury, fell out on this sort.
Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.
If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry;
And my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
Thy testimonies are very sure: holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever.

cases.name: Holofernes
cases.charge: Making Nebuchadnezzar a god; blasphemy against the God of Israel; lust and drunkenness
cases.summary: Nebuchadnezzar's captain, sent to make all the earth worship the king alone as god, cut down the groves and gods of every nation and besieged Bethulia. Who is God but Nebuchadnezzar, he asked, and told Achior that the God of Israel would not save his people. Judith came to his camp.
cases.offense: Idolatry enforced by the sword, and contempt for the Lord spoken to his face through Achior. On the fourth night his heart was ravished with Judith and he was filled with wine, more than he had drunk at any time in one day since he was born.
cases.judgment: Judith took his own fauchion, smote twice upon his neck with all her might, and took away his head; his army, finding him headless in his tent, fled and was cut down. Judith's song: the Lord Almighty hath disappointed them by the hand of a woman.

verses.text: And when he had ended his counsel, Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians called Holofernes the chief captain of his army, which was next unto him, and said unto him.

Thus saith the great king, the lord of the whole earth, Behold, thou shalt go forth from my presence, and take with thee men that trust in their own strength, of footmen an hundred and twenty thousand; and the number of horses with their riders twelve thousand.
And thou shalt go against all the west country, because they disobeyed my commandment.

And thou shalt declare unto that they prepare for me earth and water: for I will go forth in my wrath against them and will cover the whole face of the earth with the feet of mine army, and I will give them for a spoil unto them:
So that their slain shall fill their valleys and brooks and the river shall be filled with their dead, till it overflow:
And I will lead them captives to the utmost parts of all the earth.
Thou therefore shalt go forth. and take beforehand for me all their coasts: and if they will yield themselves unto thee, thou shalt reserve them for me till the day of their punishment.
But concerning them that rebel, let not thine eye spare them; but put them to the slaughter, and spoil them wheresoever thou goest.
For as I live, and by the power of my kingdom, whatsoever I have spoken, that will I do by mine hand.
And take thou heed that thou transgress none of the commandments of thy lord, but accomplish them fully, as I have commanded thee, and defer not to do them.

Yet he did cast down their frontiers, and cut down their groves: for he had decreed to destroy all the gods of the land, that all nations should worship Nabuchodonosor only, and that all tongues and tribes should call upon him as god.

And who art thou, Achior, and the hirelings of Ephraim, that thou hast prophesied against us as to day, and hast said, that we should not make war with the people of Israel, because their God will defend them? and who is God but Nabuchodonosor?

He will send his power, and will destroy them from the face of the earth, and their God shall not deliver them: but we his servants will destroy them as one man; for they are not able to sustain the power of our horses.

For with them we will tread them under foot, and their mountains shall be drunken with their blood, and their fields shall be filled with their dead bodies, and their footsteps shall not be able to stand before us, for they shall utterly perish, saith king Nabuchodonosor, lord of all the earth: for he said, None of my words shall be in vain.

Now when Judith came in and sat down, Holofernes his heart was ravished with her, and his mind was moved, and he desired greatly her company; for he waited a time to deceive her, from the day that he had seen her.
Then said Holofernes unto her, Drink now, and be merry with us.
So Judith said, I will drink now, my lord, because my life is magnified in me this day more than all the days since I was born.
Then she took and ate and drank before him what her maid had prepared.
And Holofernes took great delight in her, and drank more wine than he had drunk at any time in one day since he was born.
And Judith was left along in the tent, and Holofernes lying along upon his bed: for he was filled with wine.
Then she came to the pillar of the bed, which was at Holofernes’ head, and took down his fauchion from thence,
And approached to his bed, and took hold of the hair of his head, and said, Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, this day.
And she smote twice upon his neck with all her might, and she took away his head from him.
And tumbled his body down from the bed, and pulled down the canopy from the pillars; and anon after she went forth, and gave Holofernes his head to her maid;

And she put it in her bag of meat: so they twain went together according to their custom unto prayer: and when they passed the camp, they compassed the valley, and went up the mountain of Bethulia, and came to the gates thereof.
These slaves have dealt treacherously; one woman of the Hebrews hath brought shame upon the house of king Nabuchodonosor: for, behold, Holofernes lieth upon the ground without a head.
When the captains of the Assyrians’ army heard these words, they rent their coats and their minds were wonderfully troubled, and there was a cry and a very great noise throughout the camp.
He bragged that he would burn up my borders, and kill my young men with the sword, and dash the sucking children against the ground, and make mine infants as a prey, and my virgins as a spoil.
But the Almighty Lord hath disappointed them by the hand of a woman.

For, behold, the Assyrians are multiplied in their power; they are exalted with horse and man; they glory in the strength of their footmen; they trust in shield, and spear, and bow, and sling; and know not that thou art the Lord that breakest the battles: the Lord is thy name.

Throw down their strength in thy power, and bring down their force in thy wrath: for they have purposed to defile thy sanctuary, and to pollute the tabernacle where thy glorious name resteth and to cast down with sword the horn of thy altar.
Behold their pride, and send thy wrath upon their heads: give into mine hand, which am a widow, the power that I have conceived.
Smite by the deceit of my lips the servant with the prince, and the prince with the servant: break down their stateliness by the hand of a woman.

cases.name: Jason the high priest
cases.charge: Buying the priesthood; setting up a Greek gymnasium; drawing his countrymen to heathen customs
cases.summary: Onias' brother Jason obtained the high priesthood from Antiochus for three hundred and sixty talents and a promise of more, then built a place of exercise under the tower itself, brought the young men under the Greek hat, and had the priests neglect the sacrifices to hasten to the games. He sent silver for the sacrifice of Hercules.
cases.offense: The narrator's summary: such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest. A bought office, a foreign religion imported into the sanctuary's shadow, and the law despised for the sake of the games. Then Menelaus outbid him.
cases.judgment: Driven out, he attacked Jerusalem with a thousand men, slew his own citizens without mercy, and was driven out again. He fled from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws; he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, and perished in a strange land.

verses.text: But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest,
Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents:

Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.
Which when the king had granted, and he had gotten into his hand the rule he forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.

And the royal privileges granted of special favour to the Jews by the means of John the father of Eupolemus, who went ambassador to Rome for amity and aid, he took away; and putting down the governments which were according to the law, he brought up new customs against the law:
For he built gladly a place of exercise under the tower itself, and brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat.
Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest;

That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;
Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.
By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly, and unto whom they desired to be like in all things.
For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God: but the time following shall declare these things.
Now when the game that was used every faith year was kept at Tyrus, the king being present,

This ungracious Jason sent special messengers from Jerusalem, who were Antiochians, to carry three hundred drachms of silver to the sacrifice of Hercules, which even the bearers thereof thought fit not to bestow upon the sacrifice, because it was not convenient, but to be reserved for other charges.
This money then, in regard of the sender, was appointed to Hercules’ sacrifice; but because of the bearers thereof, it was employed to the making of gallies.
Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon’s brother, to bear the money unto the king, and to put him in mind of certain necessary matters.

But he being brought to the presence of the king, when he had magnified him for the glorious appearance of his power, got the priesthood to himself, offering more than Jason by three hundred talents of silver.
So he came with the king’s mandate, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast.
Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites.

Now when there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men, and suddenly made an assault upon the city; and they that were upon the walls being put back, and the city at length taken, Menelaus fled into the castle:

But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.
Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason, and fled again into the country of the Ammonites.

In the end therefore he had an unhappy return, being accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt.
Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians, and thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred:
And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.

In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.
So this device pleased them well.
Then certain of the people were so forward herein, that they went to the king, who gave them licence to do after the ordinances of the heathen:
Whereupon they built a place of exercise at Jerusalem according to the customs of the heathen:
And made themselves uncircumcised, and forsook the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the heathen, and were sold to do mischief.

cases.name: Judas' soldiers with idol tokens under their coats
cases.charge: Carrying things consecrated to idols into battle
cases.summary: After the battle near Adullam, Judas and his company came to bury their dead and found under the coat of every slain man things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy: thou shalt not bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Joshua's men had died at Ai for Achan's hidden spoil; these had died in a battle they otherwise won.
cases.judgment: The survivors praised the Lord, the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid, and prayed that the sin might be wholly put out of remembrance. Judas took a collection and sent it to Jerusalem for a sin offering for the dead.

entries.commentary: The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read.

Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.
Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted.

For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health.

Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. Those days are coming back when Christ returns.

If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

Who committed the trespass? Many will answer Achan, but read the first sentence: the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing. Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel. Your individual sins can hurt the rest of the nation. You can be the hindrance to why your camp is not growing, why your family, your marriage, or your children have issues, when you have a spirit on you that you know about and keep secret, not praying, not fasting, not seeking counsel. That is the spirit of Achan, and the children of Israel pay for it; we are supposed to be one mind, one body, one spirit.

The men who viewed Ai came back confident: let not all the people go up, but about two or three thousand men, for they are but few. The way Israel had been winning, they thought they could not lose; but what happened in verse 1 was about to play its part. About three thousand went up, and they fled before the men of Ai, who smote about thirty and six men and chased them from before the gate; the hearts of the people melted and became as water. The Lord is the one who wins the battles and gets the victory, not us. Pick out the weakest nation on earth: no matter how strong Israel is physically, if we are not spiritually right with the Lord, he will make us lose, for this fight is not carnal. Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

Joshua rent his clothes and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads, grieving over the war just lost and the men that died. Israel turning their backs means they were fleeing, retreating, defeated. Joshua understood what the nations do when they see Israel take a loss: the Canaanites would hear of it, environ us round, surround us, capitalize while we are down, and cut off our name from the earth. And what wilt thou do unto thy great name? If Israel is cut off, who will be there to praise the Most High?

The Lord said, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou upon thy face? Israel hath sinned. It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. This walk is not selfish or individual: when you are in sin you hurt your wife, your husband, your children, the congregation, and the leadership, for we are all our brother's keeper and responsible for one another. They have taken of the accursed thing, and stolen, and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff: the Lord says they. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with his children as one house; we pay for one another's sins. Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies: the Lord was not going to let them win, and he put a mightier warring spirit on the men of Ai. However well you train with your sword and shield, the Most High controls the outcome. His power cannot be comprehended: great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend; touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out. Stop trying to figure the Creator out and questioning why he created what he created; you are the creation, so keep the commandments and play your role. Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it.

Up, sanctify the people against tomorrow: there is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel; thou canst not stand before thine enemies until ye take away the accursed thing from among you. The search would narrow by the Lord's own taking: tribe, then family, then household, then man by man; and he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath. The folly was wrought against a plain commandment: Joshua had already charged them in [Joshua 6:18-19](/bible/joshua/6#v18) to keep from the accursed thing lest they trouble the camp, and adjured them in [Joshua 6:26](/bible/joshua/6#v26); the transgressor troubled the camp, the army and congregation of Israel.

Joshua rose up early and brought Israel by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken; then the family of the Zarhites, then the household of Zabdi man by man, and Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me. Joshua said hide it not from me because it was already not hidden from One mightier than he: we cannot hide what we do from the Lord. The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good; he sees everything we do. If you are in this walk as a manpleaser, the Lord sees what you do away from the brotherhood and the sisterhood. The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

Achan confessed: indeed I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel. He saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight; he coveted them, took them, and hid them in the earth in the midst of his tent. Joshua had said all the silver and gold and vessels were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so Achan was not stealing from men; he was literally stealing from the Most High. I coveted them: covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, and as a father saves the weightiest warning for last but not least, the Lord ends the ten with thou shalt not covet. To covet is to carry the spirit of jealousy and envy, and there is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: he sets his own soul to sale, selling out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes.

Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent, and behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it; they laid it all out before the Lord with the whole congregation present. The Lord revealed it, and the scripture cannot be broken: as Jericho was made a curse, so the one who took of it. Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the garment, the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all that he had, unto the valley of Achor. His sons and daughters did not steal it, yet because he lacked knowledge and understanding they paid for the covetous spirit he carried. Why hast thou troubled us? the Lord shall trouble thee this day. Achan was the reason men died in that battle and the nation was nearly overtaken; his selfish, individual spirit never weighed what his family would pay. All Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones: them, because his household went with him. My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: reject knowledge and the Lord will reject thee, and the end of [Hosea 4:6](/bible/hosea/4#v6) that we seldom quote says, I will also forget thy children. The Lord hits where it hurts, and your sin reaches your children, your wife, your husband, your brothers and sisters. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God, and that is where Achan fell, and unfortunately his sons and daughters and all he had with him. Some of our people in the islands and elsewhere still ignorantly carry out such public executions to this day; we do not condone it, for we are not under the law of sacrifice now but under grace, and the judgment is of the Lord. Consider the contrast that closes these chapters: Achan, an Israelite of Judah, lacked faith and was put to death, while Rahab the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for her faith. When Israel will not obey his voice, the Lord likens the house of Judah unto all the heathen; so we must have the fear of the Lord in our hearts. They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out and none came in. Jericho had a military, and a garrison, a military base, was built there, with the walls shut so nobody could enter or leave. The Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour: the battle was already decided.

The battle plan came from the Lord: compass the city with all the men of war once a day for six days, seven priests bearing seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark; on the seventh day compass the city seven times, and at the long blast all the people shout with a great shout, and the wall shall fall down flat. The blowing of the trumpets activates the armies of the Lord, the angels, to help in battle. Remember Elisha's servant: when his eyes were opened he saw the host of angels that were there warring and protecting Israel. This is the spirit behind the men of Israel rehearsing the righteous acts with trumpets and shofars today, at the camps and at the new moons; it is spiritual and an act of faith.

Joshua called the priests and gave the order: seven priests bear seven trumpets before the ark, the armed men pass on before the ark, and the rereward, the guards in the rear, came after the ark. Joshua commanded the people, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout. The ark of the Lord compassed the city once, and they came into the camp and lodged there.

They repeated the act six days back to back, rising early, the priests bearing the ark and blowing the trumpets, the armed men before and the rereward after, one compass of the city each day. Every army in the world stole this from the Israelites: the pass and review of the militaries, with their battalions and units, their guidons with the eagle on the tip of the spear, marching round the field sounding off with cadences and trumpets, is patterned after what Israel did here.

On the seventh day they rose about the dawning of the day and compassed the city seven times. There is something about the number seven that the Lord loves; you read about it in Revelation. At the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city. The men apply [Joshua 6](/bible/joshua/6) to this day: when a scoffer will not hear the word and thinks to outcry the truth, the brothers say the scripture together with one mind, one body, one spirit. That unity is spiritual, a rehearsal of the righteous acts. Unity and order are what the enemies fear: not gangs and drug dealing, but the so-called Black man, Hispanic man, and Native American man unified in the order of a military, with structure and organization. That is what puts fear in the nations.

The city shall be accursed, even it and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers. She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell. Rahab was a Canaanite, a heathen, yet the heathen can be blessed when they do it to benefit Israel; blessed is he that blesseth thee. Rahab is the scripture's own example that a man is justified by works and not by faith only: faith and works go hand in hand, for your actions prove whether you believe. Works by the Bible's own dictionary is keeping his commandments: set your hope in God, forget not his works, but keep his commandments. Words say a lot, but actions always speak louder, and by him actions are weighed. Keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it: your individual sins affect the whole nation of Israel, your brothers, your sisters, and the children. That is why we must examine ourselves whether we be in the faith. All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

The people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets, and the wall fell down flat. That shout is [Isaiah 58:1](/bible/isaiah/58#v1) in action, cry aloud and spare not: the sound coming out of their mouths with the trumpets broke everything down, like thousands of lions roaring at once. The people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city and utterly destroyed all that was in it, both man and woman, young and old, ox, sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.

Joshua sent the two spies into the harlot's house to bring out Rahab and all that she had, as they sware unto her; they brought out her father, mother, brethren, and all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel. They burnt the city with fire and all that was therein; only the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron went into the treasury of the house of the Lord. Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers. She helped the nation of Israel toward rulership, and that is the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not food stamps, welfare, or reparations, but tell our people who they are, the Israelites the Bible speaks of, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and that we must keep the commandments of the Most High. Whoever does that will receive mercy just as Rahab did.

Joshua adjured them at that time: cursed be the man before the Lord that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho; he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it. The city was not to be rebuilt. So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame was noised throughout all the country.

verses.text: So Judas gathered his host, and came into the city of Odollam, And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place.
And upon the day following, as the use had been, Judas and his company came to take up the bodies of them that were slain, and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves.

Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.
All men therefore praising the Lord, the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid,

Betook themselves unto prayer, and besought him that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance. Besides, that noble Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin, forsomuch as they saw before their eyes the things that came to pass for the sins of those that were slain.

And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing therein very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection:

And also in that he perceived that there was great favour laid up for those that died godly, it was an holy and good thought. Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.

Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.

Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.

cases.name: Lysimachus
cases.charge: Sacrilege: robbing the temple with Menelaus' consent
cases.summary: Menelaus' brother committed many sacrileges in the city by his brother's consent and carried away much gold. The multitude gathered against him; he armed three thousand men under a captain of years and madness and attacked the crowd.
cases.offense: Plunder of the sanctuary treated as family business, then armed force against the people who objected. The narrator calls him the church-robber.
cases.judgment: The people took up stones and clubs and ashes, wounded many, killed some, put the rest to flight, and slew Lysimachus himself beside the treasury. Judgment executed by the congregation at the scene of the crime.

entries.commentary: If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

Thou shalt not sacrifice unto the Most High any bullock or sheep wherein is blemish, or any evilfavouredness, for that is an abomination unto the Lord thy God. Back then you could be put to death for sacrificing a bullock or sheep with a blemish, because doing an abominable thing carried death.

If there be found among you man or woman that hath wrought wickedness, transgressed the covenant, and gone and served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, which the Most High commanded not, the matter had to be established first. A lot of people do not know how to apply [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1); the precept for [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is [Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4). Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain that such abomination is wrought in Israel, then judgment proceeds. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death. The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. Wait till we go back to this: the ones who witnessed against you were the first to lay hands on you, so a false witness could not hide behind the crowd. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.

If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, matters of controversy within thy gates, then thou shalt get thee up into the place which the Lord shall choose. Come unto the priests the Levites and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment; thou shalt do according to all that they inform thee, according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. The man that will do presumptuously and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister before the Most High, or unto the judge, even that man shall die; and all the people shall hear, and fear, and do no more presumptuously.

When thou art come unto the land and shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations that are about me, thou shalt in any wise set him king whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. These are the laws for a king that is to rule over Israel. He shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt to multiply horses, for the Lord hath said, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way. Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away. You hear a lot of these dudes today saying king this and king that, and many of the same men pushing for multiple wives; the law of the king says do not multiply wives to thyself. Neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

When he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites. It shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Most High and keep all the words of this law and these statutes to do them. The purpose: that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, that he turn not aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, and that he prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the midst of Israel.
