cases.name: Menelaus
cases.charge: Buying the priesthood over Jason; stealing the temple vessels; procuring the murder of Onias; bribing his way past the king's judgment
cases.summary: Sent by Jason to carry the king's money, Menelaus outbid him by three hundred talents and came back high priest, though he was not of Aaron's line by the account. He stole gold vessels from the temple to pay his debt, had the righteous Onias murdered for exposing him, and bought off the king when the Jews accused him.
cases.offense: Second Maccabees lists him as the cause of all the mischief: a great traitor to the laws and to his own country, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant and the rage of a savage beast. The bribe that acquitted him sent his three accusers to death instead.
cases.judgment: At last the King of kings moved Antiochus Eupator against him. In Beroea he was thrust into a tower of ashes fifty cubits high, the death for sacrilege, not having so much as burial in the earth: for inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.

verses.text: Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon’s brother, to bear the money unto the king, and to put him in mind of certain necessary matters.

But he being brought to the presence of the king, when he had magnified him for the glorious appearance of his power, got the priesthood to himself, offering more than Jason by three hundred talents of silver.
So he came with the king’s mandate, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast.
Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites.
So Menelaus got the principality: but as for the money that he had promised unto the king, he took no good order for it, albeit Sostratis the ruler of the castle required it:

Now Menelaus, supposing that he had gotten a convenient time, stole certain vessels of gold out of the temple, and gave some of them to Andronicus, and some he sold into Tyrus and the cities round about.
Which when Onias knew of a surety, he reproved him, and withdrew himself into a sanctuary at Daphne, that lieth by Antiochia.

Wherefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus apart, prayed, him to get Onias into his hands; who being persuaded thereunto, and coming to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths; and though he were suspected by him, yet persuaded he him to come forth of the sanctuary: whom forthwith he shut up without regard of justice.
For the which cause not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man.

Now when many sacrileges had been committed in the city by Lysimachus with the consent of Menelaus, and the fruit thereof was spread abroad, the multitude gathered themselves together against Lysimachus, many vessels of gold being already carried away.
Of these matters therefore there was an accusation laid against Menelaus.
Now when the king came to Tyrus, three men that were sent from the senate pleaded the cause before him:
But Menelaus, being now convicted, promised Ptolemee the son of Dorymenes to give him much money, if he would pacify the king toward him.
Whereupon Ptolemee taking the king aside into a certain gallery, as it were to take the air, brought him to be of another mind:

Insomuch that he discharged Menelaus from the accusations, who notwithstanding was cause of all the mischief: and those poor men, who, if they had told their cause, yea, before the Scythians, should have been judged innocent, them he condemned to death.
Thus they that followed the matter for the city, and for the people, and for the holy vessels, did soon suffer unjust punishment.
Wherefore even they of Tyrus, moved with hatred of that wicked deed, caused them to be honourably buried.
And so through the covetousness of them that were of power Menelaus remained still in authority, increasing in malice, and being a great traitor to the citizens.
Yet was he not content with this, but presumed to go into the most holy temple of all the world; Menelaus, that traitor to the laws, and to his own country, being his guide:
Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made governor.

But the King of kings moved Antiochus’ mind against this wicked wretch, and Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so that the king commanded to bring him unto Berea, and to put him to death, as the manner is in that place.
Now there was in that place a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, and it had a round instrument which on every side hanged down into the ashes.
And whosoever was condemned of sacrilege, or had committed any other grievous crime, there did all men thrust him unto death.
Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly:
For inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.

cases.name: Nicanor
cases.charge: Blasphemy against the temple; breaking covenant with Judas; resolving to attack on the Sabbath
cases.summary: Demetrius' general, having sworn friendship to Judas and broken it at Alcimus' instigation, stretched out his hand toward the temple and swore that if Judas were not delivered to him he would burn the house and build a temple to Bacchus. He resolved to attack on the Sabbath; asked if there were a Mighty one in heaven who commanded the day, he answered that he was mighty on earth.
cases.offense: Contempt for the sanctuary, for the Sabbath, and for the God of both, spoken aloud as policy. The priests prayed at the altar for vengeance on the blasphemer; Judas' army prayed the prayer of Hezekiah against Sennacherib.
cases.judgment: Nicanor fell first in the battle at Adasa, and his army fled. They cut off his head and the right hand which he stretched out so proudly, cut out the tongue of the blasphemer, hung the head from the tower over against the temple, and ordained the day a yearly feast, the day before Mordecai's day.

entries.commentary: The psalmist asks why the Most High has cast us off forever and why His anger smokes against the sheep of His pasture, which is Israel. He asks the Most High to remember the congregation He purchased of old, the rod of His inheritance He redeemed, this Mount Zion where He dwelt. The Most High purchased us when He instituted animal sacrifice, when Moses sprinkled the blood over the people. -

The enemies roar in the midst of the congregations and set up their ensigns for signs; a man was famous as he lifted up axes upon the thick trees. The ensigns set up for signs are the other nations setting up their images, histories, and laws for us to follow. In school you get American history, French history, all the histories of their people, never ours. They break down the carved work with axes and hammers and cast fire into the sanctuary, defiling the dwelling place of the Most High's name to the ground. They said in their hearts, let us destroy them together, and burned up all the synagogues of God in the land. -

There is no more any sign, no prophet, and none who knows how long. In slavery there was a time when our image of Christ was replaced with a white image and no one could teach us who we were or how long, because the Most High cast us off. Even today the other nations fight to keep this alive: the Christian church ideologies, their politics, their government, everything they set up. He asks how long the adversary shall reproach and whether the enemy shall blaspheme the Most High's name forever, and why He withdraws His hand. He asks the Most High to pluck His right hand out of His bosom, meaning show forth His righteousness and strength against the other nations.

God is his King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth; He divided the sea by His strength and broke the heads of the dragons in the waters. He broke the heads of leviathan and gave him as meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness, and He cleaved the fountain and the flood and dried up mighty rivers. The day is His and the night also; He prepared the light and the sun, referring back to Genesis chapter one when He created all things on the earth. He set all the borders of the earth and made summer and winter.

Remember that the enemy has reproached and the foolish people have blasphemed His name; do not deliver the soul of His turtledove unto the multitude of the wicked, and forget not the congregation of the poor forever. The congregation of the poor is the Israelites; have respect unto the covenant, for the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of cruelty. The covenant is that His people would inherit the Kingdom of Heaven, established from Adam and Shem onward. Let not the oppressed return ashamed; let the poor and needy praise His name. Our people will not return to the Lord ashamed; the prophecies show Israel will be redeemed with a mighty salvation. Arise, O God, plead thine own cause, and remember how the foolish man reproaches daily; the enemy's tumult increases continually, thinking evil upon their beds every day on how to oppress and crush Israel. We must keep in mind it is because of our own doing; He put us in captivity for our disobedience. As long as we come with a clean heart and fix what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting. -

verses.text: Then the king sent Nicanor, one of his honourable princes, a man that bare deadly hate unto Israel, with commandment to destroy the people.
So Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great force; and sent unto Judas and his brethren deceitfully with friendly words, saying,
Let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men, that I may see you in peace.
He came therefore to Judas, and they saluted one another peaceably. Howbeit the enemies were prepared to take away Judas by violence.
Which thing after it was known to Judas, to wit, that he came unto him with deceit, he was sore afraid of him, and would see his face no more.
Nicanor also, when he saw that his counsel was discovered, went out to fight against Judas beside Capharsalama:
Where there were slain of Nicanor’s side about five thousand men, and the rest fled into the city of David.

After this went Nicanor up to mount Sion, and there came out of the sanctuary certain of the priests and certain of the elders of the people, to salute him peaceably, and to shew him the burnt sacrifice that was offered for the king.
But he mocked them, and laughed at them, and abused them shamefully, and spake proudly,
And sware in his wrath, saying, Unless Judas and his host be now delivered into my hands, if ever I come again in safety, I will burn up this house: and with that he went out in a great rage.
So Nicanor went out of Jerusalem, and pitched his tents in Bethhoron, where an host out of Syria met him.
But Judas pitched in Adasa with three thousand men, and there he prayed, saying,
O Lord, when they that were sent from the king of the Assyrians blasphemed, thine angel went out, and smote an hundred fourscore and five thousand of them.
Even so destroy thou this host before us this day, that the rest may know that he hath spoken blasphemously against thy sanctuary, and judge thou him according to his wickedness.
So the thirteenth day of the month Adar the hosts joined battle: but Nicanor’s host was discomfited, and he himself was first slain in the battle.
Now when Nicanor’s host saw that he was slain, they cast away their weapons, and fled.
Then they pursued after them a day’s journey, from Adasa unto Gazera, sounding an alarm after them with their trumpets.

Whereupon they came forth out of all the towns of Judea round about, and closed them in; so that they, turning back upon them that pursued them, were all slain with the sword, and not one of them was left.
Afterwards they took the spoils, and the prey, and smote off Nicanors head, and his right hand, which he stretched out so proudly, and brought them away, and hanged them up toward Jerusalem.
For this cause the people rejoiced greatly, and they kept that day a day of great gladness.
Moreover they ordained to keep yearly this day, being the thirteenth of Adar.

But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was betwixt them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king’s successor.

Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste unto Antioch.
When this came to Nicanor’s hearing, he was much confounded in himself, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles which were agreed upon, the man being in no fault.
But because there was no dealing against the king, he watched his time to accomplish this thing by policy.

Notwithstanding, when Maccabeus saw that Nicanor began to be churlish unto him, and that he entreated him more roughly than he was wont, perceiving that such sour behaviour came not of good, he gathered together not a few of his men, and withdrew himself from Nicanor.

But the other, knowing that he was notably prevented by Judas’ policy, came into the great and holy temple, and commanded the priests, that were offering their usual sacrifices, to deliver him the man.
And when they sware that they could not tell where the man was whom he sought,

He stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath in this manner: If ye will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of God even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple unto Bacchus.
After these words he departed. Then the priests lifted up their hands toward heaven, and besought him that was ever a defender of their nation, saying in this manner;
Thou, O Lord of all things, who hast need of nothing, wast pleased that the temple of thine habitation should be among us:
Therefore now, O holy Lord of all holiness, keep this house ever undefiled, which lately was cleansed, and stop every unrighteous mouth.
But Nicanor, hearing that Judas and his company were in the strong places about Samaria, resolved without any danger to set upon them on the sabbath day.

Nevertheless the Jews that were compelled to go with him said, O destroy not so cruelly and barbarously, but give honour to that day, which he, that seeth all things, hath honoured with holiness above all other days.
Then the most ungracious wretch demanded, if there were a Mighty one in heaven, that had commanded the sabbath day to be kept.
And when they said, There is in heaven a living Lord, and mighty, who commanded the seventh day to be kept:
Then said the other, And I also am mighty upon earth, and I command to take arms, and to do the king’s business. Yet he obtained not to have his wicked will done.
Now when the battle was done, returning again with joy, they knew that Nicanor lay dead in his harness.
Then they made a great shout and a noise, praising the Almighty in their own language.

And Judas, who was ever the chief defender of the citizens both in body and mind, and who continued his love toward his countrymen all his life, commanded to strike off Nicanor’s head, and his hand with his shoulder, and bring them to Jerusalem.
So when he was there, and called them of his nation together, and set the priests before the altar, he sent for them that were of the tower,
And shewed them vile Nicanor’s head, and the hand of that blasphemer, which with proud brags he had stretched out against the holy temple of the Almighty.
And when he had cut out the tongue of that ungodly Nicanor, he commanded that they should give it by pieces unto the fowls, and hang up the reward of his madness before the temple.
So every man praised toward the heaven the glorious Lord, saying, Blessed be he that hath kept his own place undefiled.
He hanged also Nicanor’s head upon the tower, an evident and manifest sign unto all of the help of the Lord.

And they ordained all with a common decree in no case to let that day pass without solemnity, but to celebrate the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, which in the Syrian tongue is called Adar, the day before Mardocheus’ day.
Arise, O God, plead thine own cause: remember how the foolish man reproacheth thee daily.
Forget not the voice of thine enemies: the tumult of those that rise up against thee increaseth continually.

cases.name: Ptolemy the son of Abubus
cases.charge: Murdering Simon the high priest and two of his sons at a banquet in his own castle
cases.summary: Simon's son in law, captain of the plain of Jericho, wanted the country and the crown. He received Simon and his sons Mattathias and Judas in the castle of Docus, made them a great banquet, and killed them when they had drunk well. He sent men to kill John Hircanus too; John was told first and killed the messengers.
cases.offense: Ptolemeus the son of Abubus, being made captain in the plain of Jericho, had abundance of silver and gold, for he was the high priest's son in law. Wherefore his heart being lifted up, he thought to get the country to himself, and thereupon consulted deceitfully against Simon and his sons to destroy them. When Simon and his sons had drunk largely, Ptolemee and his men rose up, and took their weapons, and came upon Simon into the banqueting place, and slew him and his two sons.
cases.judgment: In which doing he committed a great treachery, and recompensed evil for good. He wrote to the king to send him an host and deliver him the country, and sent others to take Jerusalem. One ran before to Gazara and told John that his father and brethren were slain, and he laid hands on them that came to destroy him, and slew them. The first book of the Maccabees ends there; the murderer's sentence is not in it. Deuteronomy's is.

entries.commentary: On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

The fining pot and furnace remove impurities from silver and gold; likewise the Most High tries our hearts through trials to rid us of our impurities. We must go through trials and tribulations to gain the kingdom. This is why Christianity is false when it teaches you only have to accept Jesus in your heart to be saved forever. That is not what the scriptures say. Whoso mocks the poor reproaches his Maker, and gladness at another man's calamity does not go unpunished. Children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers. Many of us grew up in fatherless homes, but we must not glory in a father's dishonor. Sisters should not speak evil of the man they chose to lie down with and bring in seed by, no matter how bad he is; children raised to despise their fathers must repent of it in this truth. Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness. -

A gift is as a precious stone to him that has it; a well-instructed wife is one of these gifts, silent and loving, priceless and far above rubies. A silent and loving woman does not mean one who never talks; it means a shamefaced sister who is not a chest bumper, whose continent mind cannot be valued. He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned. -

A reproof enters more into a wise man than a hundred stripes into a fool; the wise receive correction while the fool must be beaten. Whoso rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house. That is everything right there. The beginning of strife is like letting out water, so leave off contention before it is meddled with; where envying and strife are, there is confusion and every evil work. Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, so the strife the fool starts flows from an evil heart. -

He that justifies the wicked and he that condemns the just are both an abomination to the Most High. To justify the wicked is to wrest judgment and take a bribe. A bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous, and this perverting of judgment is something we suffer with as a people. Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who justify the wicked for reward; the reward usually comes as a financial gift or a place of importance. There is no point in a fool holding a price to buy wisdom when he has no heart for it. -

A friend loves at all times and a brother is born for adversity; a man void of understanding strikes hands and becomes surety before his friend. He that loves transgression loves strife, and he that exalts his gate seeks destruction; a froward heart finds no good and a perverse tongue falls into mischief.

A foolish son is grief to his father; Solomon understood the reasonings of men, which is why a wicked man takes a gift from the bosom to pervert judgment appears again and again in this one chapter. A merry heart does good like a medicine, but a broken spirit dries the bones. Wisdom is before him that has understanding, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth. Understanding comes only through keeping the commandments. This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man. -

A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to his mother; to punish the just and strike princes for equity is not good. He that has knowledge spares his words, and even a fool who holds his peace is counted wise. Talking too much, especially without the words of the Most High, marks a fool. Let thy speech be short, comprehending much in few words; speak only when there is need of thee and hold thy tongue among great men. -

verses.text: Moreover in the plain of Jericho was Ptolemeus the son of Abubus made captain, and he had abundance of silver and gold:
For he was the high priest’s son in law.
Wherefore his heart being lifted up, he thought to get the country to himself, and thereupon consulted deceitfully against Simon and his sons to destroy them.

Now Simon was visiting the cities that were in the country, and taking care for the good ordering of them; at which time he came down himself to Jericho with his sons, Mattathias and Judas, in the hundred threescore and seventeenth year, in the eleventh month, called Sabat:
Where the son of Abubus receiving them deceitfully into a little hold, called Docus, which he had built, made them a great banquet: howbeit he had hid men there.

So when Simon and his sons had drunk largely, Ptolemee and his men rose up, and took their weapons, and came upon Simon into the banqueting place, and slew him, and his two sons, and certain of his servants.
In which doing he committed a great treachery, and recompensed evil for good.
Then Ptolemee wrote these things, and sent to the king, that he should send him an host to aid him, and he would deliver him the country and cities.
He sent others also to Gazera to kill John: and unto the tribunes he sent letters to come unto him, that he might give them silver, and gold, and rewards.
And others he sent to take Jerusalem, and the mountain of the temple.
Now one had run afore to Gazera and told John that his father and brethren were slain, and, quoth he, Ptolemee hath sent to slay thee also.
Hereof when he heard, he was sore astonished: so he laid hands on them that were come to destroy him, and slew them; for he knew that they sought to make him away.
Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.
Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.

cases.name: Simon the governor of the temple
cases.charge: Betraying the temple treasury to the king out of a private quarrel; slandering Onias the high priest
cases.summary: Falling out with Onias over the market of the city, Simon of the tribe of Benjamin told the governor of Coelosyria that the treasury at Jerusalem was full of infinite sums and could be brought under the king's power. That report sent Heliodorus. When it failed, Simon slandered Onias as the author of the mischief and had a man of his party commit murders.
cases.offense: Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was made governor of the temple, fell out with the high priest about disorder in the city. When he could not overcome Onias, he went to Apollonius the son of Thraseas and told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money. Afterward he slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus and been the worker of these evils, and so proceeded in his malice that murders were committed by one Apollonius, a furious man.
cases.judgment: Onias went to the king, not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all. Scripture does not record Simon's end; it records that his brother Menelaus bought the priesthood with the same appetite, and how that ended. The law's word on the man who takes a bribe against the innocent, and on the false accuser, stands over him unrecorded.

entries.commentary: Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean. [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

verses.text: But one Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was made governor of the temple, fell out with the high priest about disorder in the city.
And when he could not overcome Onias, he gat him to Apollonius the son of Thraseas, who then was governor of Celosyria and Phenice,

And told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money, so that the multitude of their riches, which did not pertain to the account of the sacrifices, was innumerable, and that it was possible to bring all into the king’s hand.

Now when Apollonius came to the king, and had shewed him of the money whereof he was told, the king chose out Heliodorus his treasurer, and sent him with a commandment to bring him the foresaid money.
So forthwith Heliodorus took his journey; under a colour of visiting the cities of Celosyria and Phenice, but indeed to fulfil the king’s purpose.
This Simon now, of whom we spake afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus, and been the worker of these evils.
Thus was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws.
But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed,
Onias seeing the danger of this contention, and that Apollonius, as being the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, did rage, and increase Simon’s malice,
He went to the king, not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private:
For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto.
Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon’s brother, to bear the money unto the king, and to put him in mind of certain necessary matters.
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.

cases.name: The Hellenizers who forsook the holy covenant
cases.charge: Covenanting with the heathen; removing circumcision; profaning the Sabbath; sacrificing to idols
cases.summary: In the days of Antiochus, wicked men went out of Israel persuading many to make a covenant with the heathen round about. They built a place of exercise at Jerusalem, made themselves uncircumcised, forsook the holy covenant, and were sold to do mischief. When the king's decree came, many Israelites consented to his religion.
cases.offense: First Maccabees calls them sinners and wicked men; Second Maccabees traces the profaneness to Jason. Every mark of the covenant was surrendered by choice: circumcision, Sabbath, sacrifice, food, and the company of the nations.
cases.judgment: Mattathias and his friends smote sinful men in their anger and wicked men in their wrath; the rest fled to the heathen for succour. Judas burnt up those that vexed his people, and the wicked shrunk for fear of him. After Antiochus, the ungodly out of Israel who sought Alcimus' priesthood found Judas had taken vengeance on their sort.

entries.commentary: At ninety and nine years old Abram was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse; Christ said nothing new in [Matthew 5:48](/bible/matthew/5#v48), for the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before. Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself.

When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him. Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The same promise was passed down the seed line: Jacob's name was changed to Israel and told a nation and a company of nations and kings would come out of his loins. The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.
The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him.

Circumcision is the token of the covenant: every man child circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised soul cut off from his people. Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had yet being uncircumcised. He believed and obeyed first, and circumcision sealed it; likewise a brother can come into the truth, get built up in the faith, and then go through with the process. It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac. Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart: shall a child be born to a hundred year old man, and Sarah bear at ninety? The Most High read his thought and named the child from it: Isaac means he will laugh.

Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac. Not all who are of Abraham's seed are the children; in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai's plan, with no word from God ordaining it; the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

The selfsame day Abraham circumcised every male of his house, himself at ninety and nine and Ishmael at thirteen. That is the righteous example: he received the commandment and performed it the same day.

The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship, to devise cunning works, to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of timber. With him the Lord gave Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted, that they might make all that he had commanded. The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

The wise hearted made all that was commanded: the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is thereupon, all the furniture of the tabernacle, the table and his furniture, the pure candlestick with all his furniture, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot. They made the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons to minister in the priest's office, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense for the holy place, according to all that the Lord commanded. That spirit of workmanship on Israel is why the tabernacle, and later the house Solomon built for the Lord, outshined anything the world had seen; and though strangers shall build up our walls in the kingdom, it will be Israel directing how the Lord wants it done.

Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God; the nations do not have this sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel. Every one that defileth the sabbath shall surely be put to death. The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown; the Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people. Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God.

The children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant; it is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed. Christians use [Mark 2:27](/bible/mark/2#v27) to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude.

When he had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai, he gave him two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God. God literally wrote the testimony with his finger, and we know that was Christ.

verses.text: In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.
So this device pleased them well.
Then certain of the people were so forward herein, that they went to the king, who gave them licence to do after the ordinances of the heathen:
Whereupon they built a place of exercise at Jerusalem according to the customs of the heathen:
And made themselves uncircumcised, and forsook the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the heathen, and were sold to do mischief.
Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.
Then many of the people were gathered unto them, to wit every one that forsook the law; and so they committed evils in the land;
So they joined their forces, and smote sinful men in their anger, and wicked men in their wrath: but the rest fled to the heathen for succour.
Then Mattathias and his friends went round about, and pulled down the altars:
And what children soever they found within the coast of Israel uncircumcised, those they circumcised valiantly.
They pursued also after the proud men, and the work prospered in their hand.
So they recovered the law out of the hand of the Gentiles, and out of the hand of kings, neither suffered they the sinner to triumph.
For He pursued the wicked, and sought them out, and burnt up those that vexed his people.
Wherefore the wicked shrunk for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were troubled, because salvation prospered in his hand.
He grieved also many kings, and made Jacob glad with his acts, and his memorial is blessed for ever.
Moreover he went through the cities of Juda, destroying the ungodly out of them, and turning away wrath from Israel:
Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest;

That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;
Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.
And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.

Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death: for whosoever doeth any work therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.

cases.name: The Jew who sacrificed at Modin
cases.charge: Sacrificing on the heathen altar at the king's command
cases.summary: The king's officers came to Modin to compel sacrifice and offered Mattathias silver, gold, and the title of king's friend to go first. He refused for himself and his sons. A Jew stepped forward in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar according to the king's commandment.
cases.offense: Deuteronomy 13 and 17: the man who serves other gods, or entices to it, in Israel shall be put to death, and the hand of the witnesses first upon him. He did it publicly, for reward, to lead the rest.
cases.judgment: Mattathias was inflamed with zeal, ran upon him, and slew him at the altar, and the king's commissioner with him, and pulled down the altar. Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God, like as Phinees did unto Zambri. The revolt began there.

entries.commentary: The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

Thou shalt not sacrifice unto the Most High any bullock or sheep wherein is blemish, or any evilfavouredness, for that is an abomination unto the Lord thy God. Back then you could be put to death for sacrificing a bullock or sheep with a blemish, because doing an abominable thing carried death.

If there be found among you man or woman that hath wrought wickedness, transgressed the covenant, and gone and served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, which the Most High commanded not, the matter had to be established first. A lot of people do not know how to apply [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1); the precept for [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is [Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4). Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain that such abomination is wrought in Israel, then judgment proceeds. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death. The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. Wait till we go back to this: the ones who witnessed against you were the first to lay hands on you, so a false witness could not hide behind the crowd. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.

If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, matters of controversy within thy gates, then thou shalt get thee up into the place which the Lord shall choose. Come unto the priests the Levites and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment; thou shalt do according to all that they inform thee, according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. The man that will do presumptuously and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister before the Most High, or unto the judge, even that man shall die; and all the people shall hear, and fear, and do no more presumptuously.

When thou art come unto the land and shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations that are about me, thou shalt in any wise set him king whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. These are the laws for a king that is to rule over Israel. He shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt to multiply horses, for the Lord hath said, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way. Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away. You hear a lot of these dudes today saying king this and king that, and many of the same men pushing for multiple wives; the law of the king says do not multiply wives to thyself. Neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

When he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites. It shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Most High and keep all the words of this law and these statutes to do them. The purpose: that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, that he turn not aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, and that he prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the midst of Israel.

Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.
