verses.text: In the mean while the king’s officers, such as compelled the people to revolt, came into the city Modin, to make them sacrifice.
And when many of Israel came unto them, Mattathias also and his sons came together.
Then answered the king’s officers, and said to Mattathias on this wise, Thou art a ruler, and an honourable and great man in this city, and strengthened with sons and brethren:

Now therefore come thou first, and fulfil the king’s commandment, like as all the heathen have done, yea, and the men of Juda also, and such as remain at Jerusalem: so shalt thou and thy house be in the number of the king’s friends, and thou and thy children shall be honoured with silver and gold, and many rewards.

Then Mattathias answered and spake with a loud voice, Though all the nations that are under the king’s dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, and give consent to his commandments:
Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers.
God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances.
We will not hearken to the king’s words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.
Now when he had left speaking these words, there came one of the Jews in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar which was at Modin, according to the king’s commandment.
Which thing when Mattathias saw, he was inflamed with zeal, and his reins trembled, neither could he forbear to shew his anger according to judgment: wherefore he ran, and slew him upon the altar.
Also the king’s commissioner, who compelled men to sacrifice, he killed at that time, and the altar he pulled down.
Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God like as Phinees did unto Zambri the son of Salom.
And Mattathias cried throughout the city with a loud voice, saying, Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.
So he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that ever they had in the city.

If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:
But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
If there be found among you, within any of thy gates which the Lord thy God giveth thee, man or woman, that hath wrought wickedness in the sight of the Lord thy God, in transgressing his covenant,
And hath gone and served other gods, and worshipped them, either the sun, or moon, or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded;
And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel:
Then shalt thou bring forth that man or that woman, which have committed that wicked thing, unto thy gates, even that man or that woman, and shalt stone them with stones, till they die.
At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.
The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.
And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand;
And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.

Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy.

cases.name: The men of Joppa
cases.charge: Drowning two hundred of the Jews that dwelt among them, under a pretence of peace
cases.summary: The men of Joppa invited the Jews living in their city, with their wives and children, into boats they had prepared, as though they meant them no hurt. The Jews accepted by common decree of the city, suspecting nothing. When they were out in the deep, the Joppites drowned no less than two hundred of them.
cases.offense: They prayed the Jews that dwelt among them to go with their wives and children into the boats which they had prepared, as though they had meant them no hurt. Who accepted of it according to the common decree of the city, as being desirous to live in peace, and suspecting nothing: but when they were gone forth into the deep, they drowned no less than two hundred of them. The invitation itself was the weapon; the men of Jamnia were minded to do in like manner.
cases.judgment: When Judas heard of this cruelty done unto his countrymen, he commanded those that were with him to make them ready, and calling upon God the righteous Judge, he came against those murderers of his brethren, and burnt the haven by night, and set the boats on fire, and those that fled thither he slew. He came upon the Jamnites also by night and set fire on their haven and navy, so that the light of the fire was seen at Jerusalem two hundred and forty furlongs off.

entries.commentary: An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel. Solomon is giving understanding in this proverb, and from the very top he is basically talking about the fear of the Most High and understanding. These verses lay out why the proverbs are given: to know wisdom and instruction, to perceive the words of understanding, to receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, judgment, and equity, to give subtlety to the simple, and to the young man knowledge and discretion. A wise man will hear and increase learning, and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels, to understand the proverb and the interpretation, the words of the wise and their dark sayings.

The fear of the Most High is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction. This is the key that runs through all four chapters. My son, hear the instruction of thy father and forsake not the law of thy mother, for they shall be an ornament of grace unto thy head and chains about thy neck.

A key point is verse 10: my son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not. If somebody who is committing sin entices you or tries to get you to go with them, do not go with them. To bring some life to it, look at something like a robbery. If they say come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause, that means you are doing evil to the innocent for no reason. Let us swallow them up alive as the grave, and we shall find all precious substance and fill our houses with spoil. Whatever you take from this person, you are going to fill your own pockets with their goods. Cast in thy lot among us, let us all have one purse. The sinner is enticing you, saying that if you consent, then they will share the spoils of what they get. My son, walk not thou in the way with them, refrain thy foot from their path. Solomon is giving wisdom: do not fall into the hands of sinners, do not be enticed by the things they want to do, and do not be enticed by their greediness. So are the ways of everyone that is greedy of gain, which taketh away the life of the owners thereof. If you are greedy of gain, you will be going with them, you will be enticed, and you will consent to them.

Wisdom cries without and utters her voice in the streets, in the chief place of concourse and in the openings of the gates, calling out to the simple ones who love simplicity, the scorners who delight in their scorning, and the fools who hate knowledge. Turn ye at my reproof, behold I will pour out my spirit unto you and make known my words unto you. The reproof is the correction of the Most High, that is, His commandments. Because I have called and you refused, I have stretched out my hand and no man regarded, but ye have set at nought all my counsel and would none of my reproof, I also will laugh at your calamity and mock when your fear cometh.

Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me, because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Most High. They were none of my counsel and despised all my reproof, all His commandments. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own devices. The Most High is going to give you up to whatever you are choosing to do; whatever you put over Him is what He will allow you to do. For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them, but whoso hearkeneth unto the Most High shall dwell safely and be quiet from fear of evil.

David asks the Most High to give ear to his prayer and not hide from his supplication. You have to put yourself in the Bible and see yourself in these scriptures, the way Elder Kena, Bishop, and the leadership men teach. He mourns and makes a noise because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked, who cast iniquity upon him and hate him in wrath. The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil. -

His heart is sore pained within him and the terrors of death are fallen upon him. Think about the condition we are in today; even keeping the commandments, we still suffer the same oppression, though the Most High covers those that keep them. When you drive, police will still jump behind you and run your plates, so make sure your tags are legal and not expired. The fearfulness and trembling and horror are written in the curses, the curses we did not learn in the Christian church. Many of the scriptures come back to these curses. -

He wishes for wings like a dove to fly away and be at rest, to wander far off and remain in the wilderness, hastening his escape from the windy storm and tempest. When these things come upon us many times you would think, if I could just get away, just leave this place. But the scriptures say we must serve out this punishment and endure much tribulation to enter the kingdom. Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield. -

He asks the Most High to destroy and divide their tongues, for he has seen violence and strife in the city. This is us being cursed in the city. You want to hasten your escape because you open the doors and go out into the world to work, shop, or school, and there is all this strife among our people. Moses dealt with the same thing when he left Pharaoh's house and found two men fighting. Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets. -

It was not an enemy that reproached him, which he could have borne, but a man his equal, his guide and his acquaintance, with whom he took sweet counsel and walked to the house of God. This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth. -

He asks that death seize the wicked and they go down quick into hell, for wickedness is in their dwellings, while he calls upon the Most High evening, morning, and at noon, and is heard and delivered. The Most High hears and afflicts them because they have no changes; there was no change in us, no repentance. Even when He pitied us and provided everything, bearing us on His wings, we rebelled and vexed His Holy Spirit, so He turned to be our enemy. -

The betrayer put forth his hands against those at peace with him and broke his covenant; his words were smoother than butter and softer than oil, yet were drawn swords, war in his heart. Cast thy burden upon the Most High and He shall sustain thee; He will never suffer the righteous to be moved, but bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days.

cases.name: The priests of Bel
cases.charge: Deceiving the king and the people with an idol that seemed to eat
cases.summary: The Babylonians spent twelve measures of fine flour, forty sheep, and six vessels of wine daily on Bel, and the king asked Daniel why he would not worship a living god who ate so much. Daniel laughed. Ashes strewn on the temple floor showed the footprints of the seventy priests, their wives and children, who came in by a secret door under the table every night.
cases.offense: Priests feeding themselves on offerings made to a lump of clay and brass, and threatening Daniel with death to protect the trade. The Epistle of Jeremiah describes the same racket: as for the things sacrificed unto them, their priests sell and abuse.
cases.judgment: Therefore the king slew them, and delivered Bel into Daniel's power, who destroyed him and his temple. When Daniel then destroyed the dragon, the Babylonians forced the king to throw him to the lions; he came out unharmed, and those that were the cause of his destruction were cast into the den and devoured in a moment.

entries.commentary: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen; thus saith the Lord that made thee and formed thee from the womb and will help thee. Fear not, for I will pour water upon him that is thirsty and floods upon the dry ground, and pour my spirit upon thy seed and my blessing upon thine offspring. They shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the watercourses. One shall say I am the Lord's, another shall call himself by the name of Jacob, and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord and surname himself by the name of Israel. This is prophecy of our name being changed back: on the sabbath classes a member is announced no longer a Corinthian or an Ephesian, because they take a pen and legalize their name change, subscribing with the hand as the scripture said. -

Thus saith the Lord the King of Israel and his redeemer the Lord of hosts: I am the first and I am the last, and beside me there is no God. Who as I shall call and declare it and set it in order, since I appointed the ancient people? Fear ye not, neither be afraid; have not I told thee from that time and declared it? Ye are even my witnesses. Is there a God beside me? Yea, there is no God, I know not any. Our God stays bragging through the bible that he knows no other God. -

They that make a graven image are all of them vanity, their delectable things shall not profit, and they are their own witnesses; they see not nor know, that they may be ashamed. Who has formed a god or molten a graven image profitable for nothing? The smith works it in the coals and fashions it with hammers, working with the strength of his arms until he is hungry and his strength fails; the carpenter stretches out his rule, marks it with a compass, and makes it after the figure of a man. Same as Jeremiah said, they fasten idols with nails so they move not and must be carried, so how can it have power? He heweth down cedars, cypress, and oak, which grow among the trees of the forest; part of the same tree he burns to warm himself and bake bread, and the residue he maketh a god and worshippeth it, falling down and praying deliver me, for thou art my god. He uses the same wood to warm himself yet thinks the rest is a god.

They have not known nor understood, for he hath shut their eyes that they cannot see and their hearts that they cannot understand. None considereth in his heart to say I have burned part in the fire and roasted flesh, so shall I make the residue an abomination and fall down to the stock of a tree? This is the strong delusion: our people are convinced color does not matter, so it is easy for a white jesus to sit in the temple and show himself to be god, when Christ is shown black from the scripture. He feedeth on ashes, a deceived heart hath turned him aside, and he cannot deliver his soul nor say, is there not a lie in my right hand? -

Remember these, O Jacob and Israel, for thou art my servant; I have formed thee, thou shalt not be forgotten of me. I have blotted out as a thick cloud thy transgressions and as a cloud thy sins; return unto me, for I have redeemed thee. Repentance is for Israel; when he blots out the sins he is speaking of Jacob, the servants that sinned whom God is calling back. Sing O ye heavens, shout ye lower parts of the earth, break forth into singing, for the Lord hath redeemed Jacob and glorified himself in Israel. -

Thus saith the Lord thy redeemer that formed thee from the womb: I am the Lord that maketh all things, that stretcheth forth the heavens alone and spreadeth abroad the earth by myself. There is no God beside our God. He frustrateth the tokens of the liars and maketh diviners mad, turning wise men backward and making their knowledge foolish, for the wisdom of the world is foolishness to God. He confirmeth the word of his servant and performeth the counsel of his messengers. That saith to Jerusalem, thou shalt be inhabited, and to the cities of Judah, ye shall be built, raising up the decayed places. That saith of Cyrus, he is my shepherd and shall perform all my pleasure, saying to Jerusalem thou shalt be built and to the temple thy foundation shall be laid. Jerusalem will be the place where Christ's feet touch down and Israel rules the world, not the gentiles trodding it down now.

The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

verses.text: Now the Babylons had an idol, called Bel, and there were spent upon him every day twelve great measures of fine flour, and forty sheep, and six vessels of wine.
And the king worshipped it and went daily to adore it: but Daniel worshipped his own God. And the king said unto him, Why dost not thou worship Bel?
Who answered and said, Because I may not worship idols made with hands, but the living God, who hath created the heaven and the earth, and hath sovereignty over all flesh.
Then said the king unto him, Thinkest thou not that Bel is a living God? seest thou not how much he eateth and drinketh every day?
Then Daniel smiled, and said, O king, be not deceived: for this is but clay within, and brass without, and did never eat or drink any thing.
So the king was wroth, and called for his priests, and said unto them, If ye tell me not who this is that devoureth these expences, ye shall die.
But if ye can certify me that Bel devoureth them, then Daniel shall die: for he hath spoken blasphemy against Bel. And Daniel said unto the king, Let it be according to thy word.
Now the priests of Bel were threescore and ten, beside their wives and children. And the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.
So Bel’s priests said, Lo, we go out: but thou, O king, set on the meat, and make ready the wine, and shut the door fast and seal it with thine own signet;
And to morrow when thou comest in, if thou findest not that Bel hath eaten up all, we will suffer death: or else Daniel, that speaketh falsely against us.
And they little regarded it: for under the table they had made a privy entrance, whereby they entered in continually, and consumed those things.

So when they were gone forth, the king set meats before Bel. Now Daniel had commanded his servants to bring ashes, and those they strewed throughout all the temple in the presence of the king alone: then went they out, and shut the door, and sealed it with the king’s signet, and so departed.
Now in the night came the priests with their wives and children, as they were wont to do, and did eat and drink up all.
And as soon as he had opened the dour, the king looked upon the table, and cried with a loud voice, Great art thou, O Bel, and with thee is no deceit at all.
Then laughed Daniel, and held the king that he should not go in, and said, Behold now the pavement, and mark well whose footsteps are these.
And the king said, I see the footsteps of men, women, and children. And then the king was angry,
And took the priests with their wives and children, who shewed him the privy doors, where they came in, and consumed such things as were upon the table.
Therefore the king slew them, and delivered Bel into Daniel’s power, who destroyed him and his temple.

When they of Babylon heard that, they took great indignation, and conspired against the king, saying, The king is become a Jew, and he hath destroyed Bel, he hath slain the dragon, and put the priests to death.
So they came to the king, and said, Deliver us Daniel, or else we will destroy thee and thine house.
Now when the king saw that they pressed him sore, being constrained, he delivered Daniel unto them:
Who cast him into the lions’ den: where he was six days.
And in the den there were seven lions, and they had given them every day two carcases, and two sheep: which then were not given to them, to the intent they might devour Daniel.
Upon the seventh day the king went to bewail Daniel: and when he came to the den, he looked in, and behold, Daniel was sitting.
Then cried the king with a loud voice, saying, Great art Lord God of Daniel, and there is none other beside thee.
And he drew him out, and cast those that were the cause of his destruction into the den: and they were devoured in a moment before his face.
They are borne upon shoulders, having no feet whereby they declare unto men that they be nothing worth.

They also that serve them are ashamed: for if they fall to the ground at any time, they cannot rise up again of themselves: neither, if one set them upright, can they move of themselves: neither, if they be bowed down, can they make themselves straight: but they set gifts before them as unto dead men.
As for the things that are sacrificed unto them, their priests sell and abuse; in like manner their wives lay up part thereof in salt; but unto the poor and impotent they give nothing of it.
They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.
Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?
Behold, all his fellows shall be ashamed: and the workmen, they are of men: let them all be gathered together, let them stand up; yet they shall fear, and they shall be ashamed together.

And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the Lord thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee.

cases.name: The two elders who accused Susanna
cases.charge: Attempted adultery by extortion; false witness against an innocent woman
cases.summary: Two elders of Babylon's Jews, appointed judges, hid in Joacim's garden, tried to force his wife Susanna, and when she cried out, accused her of adultery with a young man. The assembly believed them, as elders and judges, and condemned her to death. Daniel stopped the execution and examined them apart.
cases.offense: Lust turned to extortion and then to perjury: they perverted their own hearts and turned away their eyes that they might not look unto heaven nor remember just judgments. Examined separately, one said the pair were under a mastick tree and the other under a holm tree. Their own mouths convicted them of false witness.
cases.judgment: According to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day. Deuteronomy 19 is the statute; this is its clearest case.

entries.commentary: When the Most High cut off the nations of the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and Israel succeeded them and dwelt in their cities and houses, Israel was to separate three cities in the midst of the land and prepare the way to them. This law goes into accidental death, what the Bible sometimes calls manslaughter. An Israelite who accidentally killed another could flee to one of these three cities of refuge, where the avenger of blood could not seek him out and kill him there to revenge the blood of his nearest of kin.

Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past, means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident. The example given is two men hewing wood, and the axe head slips from the helve and strikes the neighbour that he die: he shall flee to one of those cities and live. The avenger of blood is the nearest of kin, and while his heart is hot he may pursue and overtake the slayer because the way is long. But the slayer was not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time past; there was no premeditation, no intention to kill. Accidents happen, and the Most High put laws in place for when these things happened. If it was for sure an accident, the man is not worthy of death, as the scripture says.

If the Lord enlarge thy coast as he sware unto the fathers, then three more cities were to be added. As Israel grew and possessed more of the land of Canaan, more cities of refuge were established where a slayer could flee from the avenger of blood. The purpose is stated plainly: that innocent blood be not shed in the land which the Lord giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.

This gives the distinction between an accident and intentional killing; this is describing murder. He hated his neighbour and lay in wait for him: he devised a scheme, waited for the right opportunity and the right time, rose up against him, and smote him mortally that he died. The murderer cannot then run to a city of refuge to lay low. Those cities were not established for him; they were established so retaliation did not come on those who accidentally brought harm to somebody. The elders of his own city shall fetch him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him: putting away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel is what makes it go well with the nation.

What is a landmark? It pays to use tools outside the scriptures, because what good is reading the Bible without understanding of the words written in it. The Zondervan Bible Dictionary defines a landmark as an object, stone, or post used to mark the boundary of a field, and notes that removal of landmarks was prohibited by the Mosaic law. The landmark establishes the boundaries of a man's property, where it begins and where it ends. A man who keeps nudging his neighbour's landmark over little by little until he has taken an acre is stealing land; the dictionary notes it was considered equal to theft.

One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin. One man alone saying he saw a theft is not proof; anybody can come and lie and get people put to death, imprisoned, or beaten. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. It has to be clear-cut; two or three solid witnesses, not one solid witness and a shaky witness. We deal with facts.

When a false witness rises up, both men in the controversy stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges of those days. False accusation is real: people will lie on a man to cover themselves, and false witnesses arise among your own people as well, which is part of why the nation fell into captivity. The judges shall make diligent inquisition: they get to the bottom of the matter and find out exactly who is telling the truth, who is lying, and what the facts are. A judge cannot judge a matter off what one person says; each side tells the story in his own favour, so you must examine the whole matter, question both sides against each other, and decipher the truth. Diligent inquisition is what separates a good judge from a bad judge; a lazy or partial judge makes false judgment. If the witness is found false, then shall ye do unto him as he had thought to have done unto his brother. Accuse a man falsely of stealing, and the judgment for stealing comes on you; accuse him falsely of adultery or another sin punishable by death, and you are put to death, because that is what you intended for your neighbour. So is evil put away from Israel.
The judgment is public and it teaches: those which remain shall hear and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil among you.

Thine eye shall not pity: in this time under Moses it was life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law. Christ spoke on this saying, because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge. Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean. [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.

verses.text: The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people.
These kept much at Joacim’s house: and all that had any suits in law came unto them.
Now when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went into her husband’s garden to walk.
And the two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was inflamed toward her.
And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments.
Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders rose up, and ran unto her, saying,
Behold, the garden doors are shut, that no man can see us, and we are in love with thee; therefore consent unto us, and lie with us.
If thou wilt not, we will bear witness against thee, that a young man was with thee: and therefore thou didst send away thy maids from thee.
Then Susanna sighed, and said, I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death unto me: and if I do it not I cannot escape your hands.
It is better for me to fall into your hands, and not do it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord.
With that Susanna cried with a loud voice: and the two elders cried out against her.
Then ran the one, and opened the garden door.
So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the garden, they rushed in at the privy door, to see what was done unto her.
But when the elders had declared their matter, the servants were greatly ashamed: for there was never such a report made of Susanna.
Then the two elders stood up in the midst of the people, and laid their hands upon her head.
And she weeping looked up toward heaven: for her heart trusted in the Lord.
And the elders said, As we walked in the garden alone, this woman came in with two maids, and shut the garden doors, and sent the maids away.
Then a young man, who there was hid, came unto her, and lay with her.
Then we that stood in a corner of the garden, seeing this wickedness, ran unto them.
And when we saw them together, the man we could not hold: for he was stronger than we, and opened the door, and leaped out.
But having taken this woman, we asked who the young man was, but she would not tell us: these things do we testify.
Then the assembly believed them as those that were the elders and judges of the people: so they condemned her to death.
Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth whose name was Daniel:
Who cried with a loud voice, I am clear from the blood of this woman.
Then all the people turned them toward him, and said, What mean these words that thou hast spoken?
So he standing in the midst of them said, Are ye such fools, ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel?
Return again to the place of judgment: for they have borne false witness against her.
So when they were put asunder one from another, he called one of them, and said unto him, O thou that art waxen old in wickedness, now thy sins which thou hast committed aforetime are come to light.
For thou hast pronounced false judgment and hast condemned the innocent and hast let the guilty go free; albeit the Lord saith, The innocent and righteous shalt thou not slay.
Now then, if thou hast seen her, tell me, Under what tree sawest thou them companying together? Who answered, Under a mastick tree.
And Daniel said, Very well; thou hast lied against thine own head; for even now the angel of God hath received the sentence of God to cut thee in two.
So he put him aside, and commanded to bring the other, and said unto him, O thou seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty hath deceived thee, and lust hath perverted thine heart.
Thus have ye dealt with the daughters of Israel, and they for fear companied with you: but the daughter of Juda would not abide your wickedness.
Now therefore tell me, Under what tree didst thou take them companying together? Who answered, Under an holm tree.
Then said Daniel unto him, Well; thou hast also lied against thine own head: for the angel of God waiteth with the sword to cut thee in two, that he may destroy you.
With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and praised God, who saveth them that trust in him.
And they arose against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth:
And according to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day.
If a false witness rise up against any man to testify against him that which is wrong;
Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother: so shalt thou put the evil away from among you.
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.

cases.name: Timotheus
cases.charge: Gathering the heathen to root out the Jews; a second campaign after being once spared
cases.summary: Timotheus raised the Ammonites and Arabians against the returned Jews, was beaten at the river and shut up in Gazara, and was let go alive when he pleaded his hostages. He came again with a hundred and twenty thousand, and Judas's men found him hid in a pit and slew him.
cases.offense: Timotheus, whom the Jews had overcome before, when he had gathered a great multitude of foreign forces, and horses out of Asia not a few, came as though he would take Jewry by force of arms. He had boasted over the Jews and blasphemed, and the Jews would not spare his men who had provoked them.
cases.judgment: Judas and his company, calling upon the Lord, came to the Jews' ease: Timotheus and his host were overthrown at Raphon and thirty thousand slain. Timotheus fell into the hands of Dositheus and Sosipater, whom he besought with much craft to let him go with his life, and they let him go for the saving of their brethren. At last, in the second campaign, he fled to Gazara, and Judas's men, finding Timotheus hid in a certain pit, killed him and his brother Chereas, and Apollophanes.

verses.text: Now Timotheus, whom the Jews had overcome before, when he had gathered a great multitude of foreign forces, and horses out of Asia not a few, came as though he would take Jewry by force of arms.
But when he drew near, they that were with Maccabeus turned themselves to pray unto God, and sprinkled earth upon their heads, and girded their loins with sackcloth,
And fell down at the foot of the altar, and besought him to be merciful to them, and to be an enemy to their enemies, and an adversary to their adversaries, as the law declareth.
So after the prayer they took their weapons, and went on further from the city: and when they drew near to their enemies, they kept by themselves.

Now the sun being newly risen, they joined both together; the one part having together with their virtue their refuge also unto the Lord for a pledge of their success and victory: the other side making their rage leader of their battle
But when the battle waxed strong, there appeared unto the enemies from heaven five comely men upon horses, with bridles of gold, and two of them led the Jews,

And took Maccabeus betwixt them, and covered him on every side weapons, and kept him safe, but shot arrows and lightnings against the enemies: so that being confounded with blindness, and full of trouble, they were killed.
And there were slain of footmen twenty thousand and five hundred, and six hundred horsemen.
As for Timotheus himself, he fled into a very strong hold, called Gawra, where Chereas was governor.
But they that were with Maccabeus laid siege against the fortress courageously four days.
And they that were within, trusting to the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly, and uttered wicked words.

Nevertheless upon the fifth day early twenty young men of Maccabeus’ company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall manly, and with a fierce courage killed all that they met withal.

Others likewise ascending after them, whiles they were busied with them that were within, burnt the towers, and kindling fires burnt the blasphemers alive; and others broke open the gates, and, having received in the rest of the army, took the city,
And killed Timotheus, that was hid in a certain pit, and Chereas his brother, with Apollophanes.
When this was done, they praised the Lord with psalms and thanksgiving, who had done so great things for Israel, and given them the victory.

But of the governours of several places, Timotheus, and Apollonius the son of Genneus, also Hieronymus, and Demophon, and beside them Nicanor the governor of Cyprus, would not suffer them to be quiet and live in peace.

And Maccabeus ranged his army by bands, and set them over the bands, and went against Timotheus, who had about him an hundred and twenty thousand men of foot, and two thousand and five hundred horsemen.

Now when Timotheus had knowledge of Judas’ coming, he sent the women and children and the other baggage unto a fortress called Carnion: for the town was hard to besiege, and uneasy to come unto, by reason of the straitness of all the places.

But when Judas his first band came in sight, the enemies, being smitten with fear and terror through the appearing of him who seeth all things, fled amain, one running into this way, another that way, so as that they were often hurt of their own men, and wounded with the points of their own swords.
Judas also was very earnest in pursuing them, killing those wicked wretches, of whom he slew about thirty thousand men.

Moreover Timotheus himself fell into the hands of Dositheus and Sosipater, whom he besought with much craft to let him go with his life, because he had many of the Jews’ parents, and the brethren of some of them, who, if they put him to death, should not be regarded.
So when he had assured them with many words that he would restore them without hurt, according to the agreement, they let him go for the saving of their brethren.
After these things gathered Timotheus another host and encamped against Raphon beyond the brook.
So Judas sent men to espy the host, who brought him word, saying, All the heathen that be round about us are assembled unto them, even a very great host.
He hath also hired the Arabians to help them and they have pitched their tents beyond the brook, ready to come and fight against thee. Upon this Judas went to meet them.

Then Timotheus said unto the captains of his host, When Judas and his host come near the brook, if he pass over first unto us, we shall not be able to withstand him; for he will mightily prevail against us:
But if he be afraid, and camp beyond the river, we shall go over unto him, and prevail against him.

Now when Judas came near the brook, he caused the scribes of the people to remain by the brook: unto whom he gave commandment, saying, Suffer no man to remain in the camp, but let all come to the battle.
So he went first over unto them, and all the people after him: then all the heathen, being discomfited before him, cast away their weapons, and fled unto the temple that was at Carnaim.
But they took the city, and burned the temple with all that were therein. Thus was Carnaim subdued, neither could they stand any longer before Judas.
The heathen are sunk down in the pit that they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.
The Lord is known by the judgment which he executeth: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.

cases.name: Tryphon
cases.charge: Taking Jonathan the high priest by treachery under a covenant of friendship; slaying him and the young king Antiochus
cases.summary: Tryphon set up a boy king to reach the crown himself, feared Jonathan would not suffer it, and took him at Ptolemais with fair words and a thousand men, killing the rest. He took Jonathan's sons as hostages, took a hundred talents for his release, kept both, and killed Jonathan on the way home. Then he killed the boy.
cases.offense: Tryphon went forth to deceive Jonathan: he said, Why hast thou brought all this people to so much trouble? Send them home, and choose a few men to wait on thee, and come thou with me to Ptolemais. When Jonathan entered, they of Ptolemais shut the gates and took him, and all them that came with him they slew with the sword. Afterward he sought to slay Simon's men as well, and having deceived Simon of the hundred talents and the children, went and slew Jonathan at Bascama.
cases.judgment: Tryphon dealt deceitfully with the young king Antiochus and slew him, and reigned in his stead, and brought a great calamity upon the land. Scripture records his crown, not his sentence: Antiochus the son of Demetrius came against him, the men of war forsook him, he fled by ship to Orthosias, and the book leaves him running. The law's sentence on the murderer and on the man who breaks a covenant of peace is written elsewhere and does not run out.

entries.commentary: David asks the Most High to give ear to his prayer and not hide from his supplication. You have to put yourself in the Bible and see yourself in these scriptures, the way Elder Kena, Bishop, and the leadership men teach. He mourns and makes a noise because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked, who cast iniquity upon him and hate him in wrath. The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil. -

His heart is sore pained within him and the terrors of death are fallen upon him. Think about the condition we are in today; even keeping the commandments, we still suffer the same oppression, though the Most High covers those that keep them. When you drive, police will still jump behind you and run your plates, so make sure your tags are legal and not expired. The fearfulness and trembling and horror are written in the curses, the curses we did not learn in the Christian church. Many of the scriptures come back to these curses. -

He wishes for wings like a dove to fly away and be at rest, to wander far off and remain in the wilderness, hastening his escape from the windy storm and tempest. When these things come upon us many times you would think, if I could just get away, just leave this place. But the scriptures say we must serve out this punishment and endure much tribulation to enter the kingdom. Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield. -

He asks the Most High to destroy and divide their tongues, for he has seen violence and strife in the city. This is us being cursed in the city. You want to hasten your escape because you open the doors and go out into the world to work, shop, or school, and there is all this strife among our people. Moses dealt with the same thing when he left Pharaoh's house and found two men fighting. Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets. -

It was not an enemy that reproached him, which he could have borne, but a man his equal, his guide and his acquaintance, with whom he took sweet counsel and walked to the house of God. This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth. -

He asks that death seize the wicked and they go down quick into hell, for wickedness is in their dwellings, while he calls upon the Most High evening, morning, and at noon, and is heard and delivered. The Most High hears and afflicts them because they have no changes; there was no change in us, no repentance. Even when He pitied us and provided everything, bearing us on His wings, we rebelled and vexed His Holy Spirit, so He turned to be our enemy. -

The betrayer put forth his hands against those at peace with him and broke his covenant; his words were smoother than butter and softer than oil, yet were drawn swords, war in his heart. Cast thy burden upon the Most High and He shall sustain thee; He will never suffer the righteous to be moved, but bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days.

verses.text: Now Tryphon went about to get the kingdom of Asia, and to kill Antiochus the king, that he might set the crown upon his own head.

Howbeit he was afraid that Jonathan would not suffer him, and that he would fight against him; wherefore he sought a way how to take Jonathan, that he might kill him. So he removed, and came to Bethsan.
Then Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand men chosen for the battle, and came to Bethsan.
Now when Tryphon saw Jonathan came with so great a force, he durst not stretch his hand against him;
But received him honourably, and commended him unto all his friends, and gave him gifts, and commanded his men of war to be as obedient unto him, as to himself.
Unto Jonathan also he said, Why hast thou brought all this people to so great trouble, seeing there is no war betwixt us?

Therefore send them now home again, and choose a few men to wait on thee, and come thou with me to Ptolemais, for I will give it thee, and the rest of the strong holds and forces, and all that have any charge: as for me, I will return and depart: for this is the cause of my coming.
So Jonathan believing him did as he bade him, and sent away his host, who went into the land of Judea.
And with himself he retained but three thousand men, of whom he sent two thousand into Galilee, and one thousand went with him.
Now as soon as Jonathan entered into Ptolemais, they of Ptolemais shut the gates and took him, and all them that came with him they slew with the sword.
So Tryphon removed from Ptolemaus with a great power to invade the land of Judea, and Jonathan was with him in ward.
But Simon pitched his tents at Adida, over against the plain.
Now when Tryphon knew that Simon was risen up instead of his brother Jonathan, and meant to join battle with him, he sent messengers unto him, saying,
Whereas we have Jonathan thy brother in hold, it is for money that he is owing unto the king’s treasure, concerning the business that was committed unto him.
Wherefore now send an hundred talents of silver, and two of his sons for hostages, that when he is at liberty he may not revolt from us, and we will let him go.
Hereupon Simon, albeit he perceived that they spake deceitfully unto him yet sent he the money and the children, lest peradventure he should procure to himself great hatred of the people:
Who might have said, Because I sent him not the money and the children, therefore is Jonathan dead.
So he sent them the children and the hundred talents: howbeit Tryphon dissembled neither would he let Jonathan go.
And after this came Tryphon to invade the land, and destroy it, going round about by the way that leadeth unto Adora: but Simon and his host marched against him in every place, wheresoever he went.
Now they that were in the tower sent messengers unto Tryphon, to the end that he should hasten his coming unto them by the wilderness, and send them victuals.
Wherefore Tryphon made ready all his horsemen to come that night: but there fell a very great snow, by reason whereof he came not. So he departed, and came into the country of Galaad.
And when he came near to Bascama he slew Jonathan, who was buried there.
Afterward Tryphon returned and went into his own land.
Now Tryphon dealt deceitfully with the young king Antiochus, and slew him.
And he reigned in his stead, and crowned himself king of Asia, and brought a great calamity upon the land.
In the hundred threescore and fourteenth year went Antiochus into the land of his fathers: at which time all the forces came together unto him, so that few were left with Tryphon.
Wherefore being pursued by king Antiochus, he fled unto Dora, which lieth by the sea side:
For he saw that troubles came upon him all at once, and that his forces had forsaken him.
Then camped Antiochus against Dora, having with him an hundred and twenty thousand men of war, and eight thousand horsemen.
And when he had compassed the city round about, and joined ships close to the town on the sea side, he vexed the city by land and by sea, neither suffered he any to go out or in.
In the mean time fled Tryphon by ship unto Orthosias.
He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.
The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
But thou, O God, shalt bring them down into the pit of destruction: bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; but I will trust in thee.

cases.name: Eleazar the scribe
cases.charge: Choosing to die gloriously rather than eat swine's flesh, or pretend to, at ninety years old
cases.summary: One of the principal scribes, an aged man and of a well favoured countenance, was compelled to open his mouth and eat swine's flesh. He spat it out. Old friends offered to let him bring his own meat and only pretend. He refused, so that the young would not be deceived by Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, into thinking he had gone over to a strange religion. He went to the torment and died leaving his death for an example.
cases.offense: But he choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment. Being fourscore years old and ten: it becometh not our age in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar was now gone to a strange religion. For though for the present time I should be delivered from the punishment of men: yet should I not escape the hand of the Almighty, neither alive, nor dead. Wherefore now, manfully changing this life, I will shew myself such an one as mine age requireth, and leave a notable example to such as be young to die willingly and courageously for the honourable and holy laws.
cases.judgment: And thus this man died, leaving his death for an example of a noble courage, and a memorial of virtue, not only unto young men, but unto all his nation. When he was ready to die with stripes, he groaned, and said, It is manifest unto the Lord, that hath the holy knowledge, that whereas I might have been delivered from death, I now endure sore pains in body by being beaten: but in soul am well content to suffer these things, because I fear him. The blessing recorded is the memorial: his name and his refusal, kept by his nation for ever, and the resurrection the next chapter's martyrs claim aloud.

entries.commentary: [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11) tells you what you can and cannot eat. Among all the beasts of the earth, ye shall eat whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud. A cloven hoof is a hoof split into two toes; mammals with this hoof include cattle, deer, antelopes, gazelles, goats, and sheep. Chewing the cud means the animal has more than one stomach: it chews its food, brings it back up into its mouth to be chewed again, and then digests it through another stomach.

Both marks must be present. There are animals that chew the cud and animals that divide the hoof but do not have both; those are unclean. The camel cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof: you cannot eat camel. The coney is the pika, a small mountain dwelling mammal that resembles its close relative the rabbit, found at heights among the highest of any mammal. The scriptures already had it right: the rocks are a refuge for the conies, and the conies, a feeble folk, make their houses in the rocks. You cannot eat coney, and the hare likewise is unclean. The swine has only the one mark: he divideth the hoof and is clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean unto you. You cannot eat pork; leave it alone. Their carcase shall ye not touch sits inside the dietary law: it goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with the mouth. It does not mean a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with the hands; the tabernacle itself had to be built by hand with badgers' skins.

Of all that are in the waters, ye shall eat whatsoever hath fins and scales; whatever has not fins and scales is an abomination. No shrimp, no crab, no lobster, no bottom dwellers. The Most High gave an excellent dietary law: high blood pressure and the like come from eating shellfish. He made these animals and knows what they do; if you eat what he allowed you will be fine. It is simple: if it does not have both fins and scales, leave it alone. A fish must have both scales and fins. Tilapia has scales and fins, so it may be eaten if you want it; sardines do not show both, so it looks like sardines are a no.

These are the fowls in abomination that shall not be eaten: the eagle, the ossifrage, the osprey, the vulture and the kite after his kind, every raven after his kind, the owl, the nighthawk, the cuckow, the hawk, the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl, the swan, the pelican, the gier eagle, the stork, the heron after her kind, the lapwing, and the bat. Look these up. The ossifrage, the bone breaker, is an older name for the bearded vulture, a scavenger famous for dropping bones on rocks to crack them open. The osprey is the seahawk or fishhawk, a fish eating bird of prey. The kite is a bird of prey in the family of the eagle. What is interesting is that all of these are scavengers and hunters; even in the waters the Most High did not want you to have the scavengers, and no shark, a hunter. He gave you this diet because he made these animals and knows what they do. After his kind: when the Most High made one, he made many of them, so the rule covers the whole family. On duck: the swan's closest relatives include the geese and ducks. The swan is unclean, and duck falls in the family of the swan, so you cannot eat duck; they are related, and it is the same thing.

All fowls that creep, going upon all four, are an abomination, yet those which have legs above their feet to leap withal upon the earth may be eaten: the locust, the bald locust, the beetle, and the grasshopper after his kind. You can eat locusts; John the Baptist ate locusts.

The carcases of every beast which divideth the hoof and is not clovenfooted nor cheweth the cud are unclean; whoever touches them is unclean until the even, and whoever bears the carcase washes his clothes. Whatsoever goeth upon his paws, among all manner of beasts that go on all four, is unclean: you cannot eat mountain lion, tiger, cougar, gorilla, dog, or cat; they have paws and walk on all fours.

These creeping things are unclean: the weasel, the mouse, the tortoise after his kind, the ferret, the chameleon, the lizard, the snail, and the mole. You cannot eat tortoise. If you find a dead mouse in your house, do not touch it: sweep it into a bag and throw it out. Whatever vessel one of them falls into when dead is unclean until the even and must be put into water; if it falls into one of your pots, clean that pot out and cook nothing in it until the even. An earthen vessel it falls into is broken and thrown out, and ovens and ranges for pots are broken down. If any part of their carcase falls on sowing seed which is to be sown, the seed is clean; but if water be put upon the seed and the carcase fall thereon, it is unclean and no good.

Even of a beast which ye may eat, if it die of itself, he that toucheth, eateth of, or beareth the carcase is unclean until the even and washes his clothes. Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth is an abomination: whatsoever goeth upon the belly, whatsoever goeth upon all four, and whatsoever hath more feet. You cannot eat centipedes and millipedes.

Sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy, for I am holy: for I am the Lord that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. This is the law of the beast and of the fowl and of every living creature that moveth in the waters and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth; the Most High explained everything and then summed it all up, to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. Do not confuse yourself with [1 Timothy 4:4](/bible/1-timothy/4#v4), that you can eat whatever you want. Every creature is good and nothing to be refused if it be received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the word of God; so find what the word of God sanctified, and that is the law of the beast in [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11). What is sanctified is what he already made clean. The law perisheth not, but remaineth in his force; that law did not change at all. Do not let anybody confuse you, especially if you are new in the truth: eat what the Most High instructed you to eat.

Ye are the children of the Lord your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead. These customs came from the other nations, like the young folks today cutting designs into their eyebrows; we are not supposed to be doing that. Cutting the flesh was a form of self-torture in mourning; the Most High requires none of that of us, only to be righteous and keep his commandments.

Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a peculiar people unto himself above all the nations upon the earth. Peter writes to that same peculiar people, a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation: his letter is addressed to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. Who were those strangers? Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, dwelling in the very regions Peter lists, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia; that is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are. Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing: this rules the whole chapter. The whatsoever thy soul lusteth after of chapter 12 sits inside these guidelines of clean foods; you cannot eat anything you want. Some of our people, still unlearned, think that as long as they pray over it they can eat it; that is not true, it is a misunderstanding carried out of the New Testament. The law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing. The chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls; the rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods.

Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed that the field bringeth forth year by year, and eat before the Lord the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, that thou mayest learn to fear the Lord thy God always. The corn, wine, and oil are the same increase promised in chapter 11 for hearkening to the commandments; this all goes together. If Israel did not keep the commandments, he would shut up the heaven, there would be no rain, the land would be chapt, and famine would teach the fear of the Lord. Today Israel is disconnected from that fear because the oppressor nourishes us; the food comes from the grocery store. That understanding must be brought back to our people, and that is why the laws are read four chapters a day, from Genesis all the way to Revelation, to gain the understanding that we are the Israelites.
