verses.text: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:
Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.

And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.
But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.
He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.
And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim:
That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,
The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles;
The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.
From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin.
He that hateth me hateth my Father also.
If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.
Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward;
How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;

cases.name: Herod Antipas and Herodias
cases.charge: Taking his brother's wife; beheading John for saying so
cases.summary: Herod the tetrarch married Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and John told him it was not lawful. Herodias wanted John dead; Herod feared him and heard him gladly, but at his birthday feast swore to give her dancing daughter whatever she asked. She asked for John's head on a charger.
cases.offense: Leviticus twice: thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother's wife. Then a rash oath kept at the cost of a prophet's life, for the sake of them which sat with him. Christ called him that fox and would not answer him at his trial.
cases.judgment: Scripture records no sentence on Herod or Herodias; the gospels leave them at Christ's trial, mocking him. History records Antipas exiled by Caligula at his wife's ambition. The record here is the crime and the statute.

entries.commentary: In his own country they are astonished at his wisdom and his mighty works, and then are offended at him because they know his family. A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. What was done to him is done to those teaching today: men who knew you before you repented ask who you think you are.

He could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk and healed them, and he marvelled because of their unbelief. Consider what that means. The unbelief of his own people was such that it made the son of the Most High marvel.

He sends them forth by two and two with power over unclean spirits, taking nothing for the journey but a staff. Whosoever will not receive you nor hear you, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. The word goes out whether they hear or whether they forbear, and that shaking of the dust seals the judgment.

Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead. John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

Herodias had a quarrel against John and would have killed him, but could not, for Herod feared him, knowing that he was a just man and an holy. When the oath is made, the daughter asks her mother what to ask, and is told, The head of John the Baptist. The king was exceeding sorry, but for his oath's sake he sent the executioner.

He was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things. Five loaves and two fishes feed five thousand men, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up. He made them sit down by companies, in ranks by hundreds and by fifties. No man argued about where he was placed. The Most High is a God of order, and the eating came after the order.

He comes to them walking upon the sea, and they suppose it had been a spirit and cry out. These were fishermen; they knew what water does. They were sore amazed, for they considered not the miracle of the loaves, for their heart was hardened. Men can watch a thing done in front of them and still not take it to heart.
Wherever he entered, they laid the sick in the streets and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment, and as many as touched him were made whole.
The rulers of that hour are named, and Annas and Caiaphas are both called high priests. There was to be one, and the naming of two shows how far out of order that priesthood had come.
John preaches the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, as it is written in the book of the words of Esaias: the voice of one crying in the wilderness.

O generation of vipers, bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father. Being dipped in water without works that go with it is not what is written here. The fruits worthy of repentance are the works.

He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none. The publicans are told to exact no more than that which is appointed them, and the soldiers to do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely, and be content with their wages.

I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire, and he will gather the wheat into his garner, but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.
Herod, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which he had done, added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.

Jesus being baptized and praying, the heaven was opened, and the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

Jesus began to be about thirty years of age, being, as was supposed, the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli. Heli was the father of Mary, so this line is reckoned through the son-in-law. The generations run back through Nathan and David, through Judah, Jacob, Isaac and Abraham, through Sem and Noe, and to Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.

Of the Galilaeans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices, and of the eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, he says they were not sinners above all others. I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish. It is said twice, in the same words.

Three years he came seeking fruit on the fig tree and found none, and the dresser asks for one more year to dig about it and dung it. If it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down. Three years is the length of his own ministry among the people, and Jerusalem was cut down after it.

A woman bowed together eighteen years and unable to lift herself up is loosed from her infirmity, and immediately made straight. The ruler of the synagogue answers with indignation that there are six days in which men ought to work. Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering? Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day? All his adversaries were ashamed, and all the people rejoiced.
The kingdom of God is like a grain of mustard seed which grew and waxed a great tree, and like leaven hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened.

Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many will seek to enter in, and shall not be able. The strait way is a narrow one, walked by discipline: correction, falling, getting back up, and correcting yourself. Many hear this word and turn back to the world rather than walk it. We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. And he shall say, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity. They shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. They come from the four corners because they were scattered to the four corners.

The Pharisees tell him to depart, for Herod will kill him, and he answers, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow. I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem. He knew his work and would not be moved off it by a threat.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

They accuse him of perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and Pilate says, I find no fault in this man. Matthew's account gives the reason he could see it: he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing. He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

Pilate says a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him. He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Barabbas, cast into prison for sedition and murder, is released, and Jesus is delivered to their will.

Simon a Cyrenian is laid hold upon and made to bear the cross after him. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. If they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Two malefactors, criminals, are led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.

One malefactor railed on him; the other rebuked him, took the blame of his own deeds, and said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. That man repented at the last hour, and was answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

There was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour, and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.
The centurion glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that came together to that sight smote their breasts and returned.

Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man and a just, had not consented to their counsel and deed, and begged the body and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone. He was buried the same day, which is the custom written in the law. There is no waiting days over a body. The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians, and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt. The same word stands for us: when the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom. The land of Canaan was full of idols. If Israel obeyed His voice the Most High would be an enemy to their enemies, bless their bread and water, and take sickness away; the charge in Canaan was not to bow to their gods nor do after their works, but to utterly overthrow them and break down their images. Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

Keep the statutes and judgments of the Most High, which if a man do, he shall live in them. The Ten Commandments are not the whole of the law but a summary. Under the Sabbath commandment sit sub-statutes such as no buying, no selling, no working; likewise under the law of adultery sit all the laws of this chapter, the ordinances of marriage and the forbidden beds. None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to uncover their nakedness; these laws name who a man may not lay down with.

The nakedness of thy father's wife is thy father's nakedness; that is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked. This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did.

The sister, whether born at home or born abroad, and the son's daughter and the daughter's daughter are all forbidden; the grandchildren's nakedness is thine own nakedness. There are sick spirits out there, and some of them are grandfathers, uncles, and fathers. Be careful and mindful who you leave your children around; do not hand your children to just anybody for the sake of your own pleasure.

The father's sister, the mother's sister, and the wife of the father's brother, thine aunt, are all near kinswomen and off limits. Incest is still practiced among the nations of this land, and children born of incestuous unions often carry defects and disabilities; the law guards the seed.

The daughter in law, the brother's wife, and a woman with her daughter or her granddaughter are all forbidden; it is wickedness. Neither take a wife to her sister to vex her, to uncover her nakedness beside the other in her lifetime; that also shuts down what the world today calls threesomes.

A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15) details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class.
To lie carnally with thy neighbour's wife is adultery. This world even sings songs celebrating adultery; the law forbids defiling thyself with her.

Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them, as Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem slaying the children of the Most High. The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

Abomination means a thing that causes disgust or hatred. When a man lies with mankind as with womankind, the Most High calls it disgusting and hateful. What a man hates and finds disgusting he removes far from himself; so we must teach our people to repent and come out of the things the Most High hates.
Lying with any beast is confusion, for man and for woman alike. The nations have set up places where these strange lusts are fulfilled, and the sin is found among every people; it is all wickedness.

In all these things the nations were defiled which the Most High cast out; the Egyptians and the Canaanites were doing these very abominations, and the land itself was defiled by them. The land spews out the defiled. That is why Israel was put out of Jerusalem: we could not abide in the land with our sins, sacrificing to idol gods and working all manner of evil, so the Most High raised up an enemy to carry us into bondage and remove us out of the land. Whosoever commits any of these abominations, the souls that commit them shall be cut off from among their people, meaning put to death.

Whosoever of Israel or of the strangers in the land gave of his seed unto Molech was surely put to death; the people of the land stoned him with stones. This is the child sacrifice shown in [Ezekiel 16](/bible/ezekiel/16), slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to pass through the fire. If the people of the land hid their eyes from the man and killed him not, the Most High set His face against that man and against his family. When you see wickedness you must utter it and expose it; a witness that holds his peace bears iniquity. Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

The soul that turns after such as have familiar spirits and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, is cut off from among his people. Sanctify yourselves and be ye holy; keep the statutes of the Most High, for He is the Lord which sanctifieth you. Every one that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; his blood shall be upon him. Disrespecting your mother and your father carried the death penalty.

The man that committeth adultery with another man's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress, shall surely be put to death. This world openly defends adultery and men even boast of committing it with another man's wife; the scriptures call for death upon both.

The man that lies with his father's wife, and the man that lies with his daughter in law, shall surely be put to death; they have wrought confusion. If a man lie with mankind as he lieth with a woman, both have committed an abomination and shall surely be put to death; abomination means hateful and disgusting unto the Most High. The man that takes a wife and her mother is burnt with fire, both he and they, that there be no wickedness among you. The man or woman that lies with a beast is put to death, and the beast is slain also. All of these judgments fall under the laws of adultery, the sub-statutes of that commandment.

The man that takes his sister and sees her nakedness, it is a wicked thing; they are cut off in the sight of their people, and he bears his iniquity. The man that lies with a woman having her sickness, her menstrual cycle, has discovered her fountain, and both are cut off from among their people; this goes with the laws of [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15). The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless.

Keep all my statutes and all my judgments, that the land whither I bring you spew you not out. Walk not in the manners of the nation cast out before you, for they committed all these things and therefore the Most High abhorred them. I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people. The Most High separated Israel from the other people, so Israel is to walk differently; these laws are the separation.

Put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean; this goes back to [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11), the dietary laws. No shrimp, crab, lobster, pork, catfish, and the like; everything is not clean, whatever the church teaches. If you eat whatever you please, you are not separating yourself from the other nations. Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.

A man or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, was surely put to death by stoning. The tarot card readings, the fortune telling, and the horoscopes of today are that same dealing with familiar spirits; do not touch any of it.

verses.text: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife: for he had married her.
For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.
Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;
And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.
And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath’s sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.
And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.
For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.
And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
But when Herod’s birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.
Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask.
And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist’s head in a charger.
And the king was sorry: nevertheless for the oath’s sake, and them which sat with him at meat, he commanded it to be given her.
And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.
And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.
But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip’s wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done,
Added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.
The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.
And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.
And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was desirous to see him of a long season, because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him.
Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.
And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him.
And Herod with his men of war set him at nought, and mocked him, and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate.
And the same day Pilate and Herod were made friends together: for before they were at enmity between themselves.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother’s wife: it is thy brother’s nakedness.
And if a man shall take his brother’s wife, it is an unclean thing: he hath uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they shall be childless.

cases.name: Herod the Great and the children of Bethlehem
cases.charge: Slaying all the male children of Bethlehem from two years old and under
cases.summary: Mocked by the wise men who did not return to report the child, Herod was exceeding wroth and sent and slew all the children in Bethlehem and its coasts from two years old and under, according to the time he had inquired of them. Matthew hears Rachel weeping in Ramah.
cases.offense: Innocent blood on a scale of a town, from a king's fear for his throne. The children's only crime was their age and their address.
cases.judgment: Matthew records only that Herod died and Joseph brought the child back from Egypt. Scripture pronounces no sentence on him; secular history records a hideous death. The law's word on innocent blood stands over the case regardless.

entries.commentary: Wise men come from the east to Jerusalem to worship him. This is prophetic; it was written that kings from far off would come and bow before him.

Herod was set up as king over Judea by Rome, and he was an Edomite, not of Israel. When the messiah is born he is troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. If the messiah were coming to save all nations, there would be nothing in his birth to trouble a ruler of the nations. Herod is troubled because the coming of the messiah to Israel means judgment upon those who hold Israel down.

The chief priests and the scribes answer at once: Bethlehem of Judea, for so it is written by the prophet. They knew the scriptures concerning the messiah. The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.
Herod calls the wise men privily and tells them to bring him word that he may come and worship also. He had no worship in mind; the next verses show what he intended.

The star goes before them and stands over the place where the young child was, and they fall down and worship him and open their treasures. Gold, frankincense and myrrh are the presents and gifts David prophesied of in the psalm. What was written was fulfilled exactly.
Warned of the Most High in a dream, they go home another way and do not report back to Herod.

The angel tells Joseph to take the young child and his mother and flee into Egypt, because Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. They hid in Egypt among the Egyptians. A family that did not look like the people of that land would have been no more hidden there than anywhere else.
They remain in Egypt until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, Out of Egypt have I called my son.
Herod slays all the children in Bethlehem from two years old and under. This is the same pattern as Egypt, where the ruler killed the young children to stop a deliverer from rising.
The mourning in Ramah was written of beforehand by Jeremiah.

After Herod dies the family returns, but Archelaus reigns in Judea, so being warned of the Most High Joseph turns aside into Galilee and dwells in Nazareth. Nazareth had no reputation. That the messiah was raised there was itself a fulfilment of what the prophets spoke.

At the same time the Most High will be the God of all the families of Israel and they shall be His people; the people left of the sword found grace in the wilderness when He went to give Israel rest. He appeared of old saying He loved them with an everlasting love and with lovingkindness drew them; again He will build the virgin of Israel, adorned with her tabrets and going forth in the dances, planting vines on the mountains of Samaria until the watchmen on Mount Ephraim cry, Arise, let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God. -

Sing with gladness for Jacob and shout among the chief of the nations, saying, O Lord, save thy people the remnant of Israel; He will bring them from the north country and gather them from the coasts of the earth, the blind and the lame, the woman with child, a great company returning. They shall come with weeping and supplications, and He will lead them and cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way wherein they shall not stumble, for He is a father to Israel and Ephraim is His firstborn; the straight way is keeping God's laws. Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel. -

Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off: He that scattered Israel will gather him and keep him as a shepherd doth his flock, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he. They shall come and sing in the height of Zion and flow together to the goodness of the Lord, for the wheat, the wine, the oil, and the young of the flock and herd, and their soul shall be as a watered garden and sorrow no more. Both young men and old shall rejoice in the dance, for He will turn their mourning into joy, comfort them, and satiate the soul of the priest with fatness, and His people shall be satisfied with His goodness. -

A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted because they were not; but the Most High tells her to refrain her voice from weeping, for her work shall be rewarded and her children shall come again from the land of the enemy to their own border. He heard Ephraim bemoaning himself, saying thou hast chastised me and I was chastised as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke; turn thou me and I shall be turned, for after he was turned he repented and was ashamed, bearing the reproach of his youth. Is Ephraim His dear son, a pleasant child? Since He spake against him He earnestly remembers him still, His bowels are troubled for him, and He will surely have mercy; Jeremiah speaks these words of the Lord to His people.

Set up waymarks and high heaps, set thine heart toward the highway, and turn again O virgin of Israel to these thy cities; how long wilt thou go about, O backsliding daughter? The Lord has created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall compass a man; it is a new thing that women would be out front of the man and the man pretty much serving the woman, and we can see the fruition of that today. When He brings again the captivity, the Lord bless thee O habitation of justice and mountain of holiness; there shall dwell together in Judah the husbandmen, who are the prophets bringing the word of the Lord, and they that go forth with flocks, for He has satiated the weary soul and replenished the sorrowful soul.

The days come that the Most High will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast, so they shall have plenty. As He watched over them to pluck up, break down, and destroy, so will He watch over them to build and to plant. In those days they shall say no more that the fathers have eaten a sour grape and the children's teeth are set on edge, but every man shall die for his own iniquity; you die for your own sin, not for the sin of the next man, for that dreaded judgment comes behind iniquity.

The Most High will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, the northern and southern kingdom, not other nations, not according to the covenant He made with their fathers when He took them out of Egypt, which they brake although He was a husband unto them. Just as a husband and wife have a covenant for their marriage, the Most High uses that analogy for the covenant we have with Him. He will put His law in their inward parts and write it in their hearts, and be their God and they His people; they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, for they shall all know Him and keep His laws from the least to the greatest, and He will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.

The Lord gives the sun for a light by day and the ordinances of the moon and the stars for a light by night, and divides the sea when the waves roar; the Lord of hosts is His name. For the Most High to cast away His people, those ordinances would have to depart, the sun would have to stop shining, the moon and stars stop giving light; that is not going to happen, so He is not casting away the seed of Israel. Only a small percentage of the earth has been discovered and the heavens above cannot be measured, so He will not cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done; you can even see where the seas are divided from the coast, the Pacific and the Atlantic, one seed of water divided from another.

The days come that the city shall be built to the Lord from the tower of Hananeel unto the gate of the corner, and the measuring line shall go forth over the hill Gareb and compass about to Goath. The whole valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields unto the brook of Kidron, unto the corner of the horse gate toward the east, shall be holy unto the Lord and shall not be plucked up nor thrown down anymore forever; this goes into the Kingdom. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

If you are surety for your friend or have struck your hand with a stranger, you are snared by the words of your mouth. Deliver yourself, go humble yourself, and make sure your friend. A surety in today's terms is like co-signing for someone, vouching that they are good and guaranteeing they will be taken care of. -

Give no sleep to your eyes; deliver yourself as a roe from the hand of the hunter. Go to the ant, consider her ways and be wise; having no guide, overseer, or ruler, she provides her meat in the summer and gathers her food in the harvest. A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands, and poverty comes as one that travels and want as an armed man. This is why in the proving stage the sisters and leadership ask a brother whether he works, has his own place, and can provide for a woman and offspring. Leadership keeps a report on these men so there are no back-door marriages. -

A naughty, wicked man walks with a froward mouth, winks with his eyes, speaks with his feet, teaches with his fingers, and devises mischief continually, sowing discord. Therefore his calamity comes suddenly and he is broken without remedy.

Six things the Most High hates, seven are an abomination to Him. He cannot be all love if He hates certain things. A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood. Because He hates hands that shed innocent blood, the murderers among Esau and the nations that took us captive and shed our blood have no place ruling over us in the kingdom, yet our people keep trying to get them in. A heart that devises wicked imaginations such as sex changes, homosexuality and lesbianism; feet swift running to mischief such as gangs and gang initiation; a false witness that speaks lies; and he that sows discord among brethren through gossip and heresies. -

Keep your father's commandment and forsake not the law of your mother; bind them upon your heart and tie them about your neck. When you go it leads you, when you sleep it keeps you, and when you wake it talks with you. The commandment is a lamp and the law is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life, to keep you from the evil woman and the flattery of the strange woman already described.

Do not lust after her beauty in your heart, which is your mind, nor let her take you with her eyelids. By means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread, and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life. A man cannot take fire in his bosom and not be burned, nor go on hot coals and not be burned; so he that goes in to his neighbour's wife and touches her shall not be innocent. -

Men do not despise a thief who steals to satisfy his hunger, yet he must restore sevenfold. But whoever commits adultery destroys his own soul; a wound and dishonour he gets, and his reproach is not wiped away. Jealousy is the rage of a man; in the day of vengeance he will spare nothing and regard no ransom. Let a husband find out his wife has been cheating and inquire the matter, and he may well put that brother to death once he catches up to him. -

cases.name: Jerusalem, that killeth the prophets
cases.charge: Killing the prophets and stoning them that are sent; not knowing the time of her visitation
cases.summary: Christ wept over the city and told it what was coming: thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee, because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation. He said not one stone of the temple would be left on another, and that this generation would see it.
cases.offense: The blood of all the prophets shed from the foundation of the world, from Abel to Zacharias, required of this generation; and the rejection of the one who would have gathered her children as a hen her chickens. Daniel had said the people of the prince that shall come would destroy the city and the sanctuary.
cases.judgment: There shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people. And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. Deuteronomy 28 had described the siege in detail.

entries.commentary: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works, for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and lay them on men's shoulders, but will not move them with one of their fingers.

All their works they do for to be seen of men. They love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the markets. He that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Woe unto you: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. They devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer, and shall receive the greater damnation. There is a lesson in what they would not do. Where leadership provokes a man to works and he finds himself falling behind, he should take it to heart, because telling people who they are without putting in the labour yields no fruit.

They compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Their rules about swearing by the gold rather than the temple, and by the gift rather than the altar, are called out as blindness: the temple sanctifies the gold and the altar sanctifies the gift.

They pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin and have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

They make clean the outside of the cup and platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Cleanse first that which is within. They are likened unto whited sepulchres, beautiful outward but within full of dead men's bones. Outwardly they appear righteous unto men, but within are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

They build the tombs of the prophets and say they would not have shed their blood, and by saying it they witness against themselves that they are the children of them which killed the prophets. Upon them comes all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias. This is the plainest speaking in the gospel. Christ was no soft man with these teachers of the law who did not believe it.
O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.

Of the buildings of the temple he says there shall not be left here one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down, and on the mount of Olives the disciples ask when, and what shall be the sign.

Take heed that no man deceive you. Many shall come in my name saying I am Christ, and shall deceive many. Wars and rumours of wars, nation against nation, famines, pestilences and earthquakes are all the beginning of sorrows, not the end.

Ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake, many shall be offended and betray one another, and because iniquity shall abound the love of many shall wax cold. He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. That verse alone answers any man who says he is already saved and has nothing left to endure.
This gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations, and then shall the end come.
The abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place. That has a fulfilment already in history, when swine's flesh was offered in the temple.

Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains, and pray that the flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day. Then shall be great tribulation such as was not since the beginning of the world, and except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved; but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened.

False Christs and false prophets shall shew great signs and wonders, insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Go not forth after them. As the lightning cometh out of the east and shineth even unto the west, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven. He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds. That gathering is itself proof of a people scattered to the four winds.

Learn a parable of the fig tree: when his branch is yet tender and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh. So likewise when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

Of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. As the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be: eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, and they knew not until the flood came and took them all away.

Blessed is that servant whom his lord when he cometh shall find giving the household meat in due season, and he shall be made ruler over all his goods. The evil servant says in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming, and begins to smite his fellowservants; his lord comes in a day he looks not for him and appoints him his portion with the hypocrites. Watching is not only watching the prophecy come to pass. It is keeping a watchful eye on your own spirit, because what is not repented of is what a man will be judged for.

Of the Galilaeans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices, and of the eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, he says they were not sinners above all others. I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish. It is said twice, in the same words.

Three years he came seeking fruit on the fig tree and found none, and the dresser asks for one more year to dig about it and dung it. If it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down. Three years is the length of his own ministry among the people, and Jerusalem was cut down after it.

A woman bowed together eighteen years and unable to lift herself up is loosed from her infirmity, and immediately made straight. The ruler of the synagogue answers with indignation that there are six days in which men ought to work. Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering? Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day? All his adversaries were ashamed, and all the people rejoiced.
The kingdom of God is like a grain of mustard seed which grew and waxed a great tree, and like leaven hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened.

Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many will seek to enter in, and shall not be able. The strait way is a narrow one, walked by discipline: correction, falling, getting back up, and correcting yourself. Many hear this word and turn back to the world rather than walk it. We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. And he shall say, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity. They shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. They come from the four corners because they were scattered to the four corners.

The Pharisees tell him to depart, for Herod will kill him, and he answers, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow. I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem. He knew his work and would not be moved off it by a threat.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

They accuse him of perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and Pilate says, I find no fault in this man. Matthew's account gives the reason he could see it: he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing. He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

Pilate says a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him. He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Barabbas, cast into prison for sedition and murder, is released, and Jesus is delivered to their will.

Simon a Cyrenian is laid hold upon and made to bear the cross after him. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. If they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Two malefactors, criminals, are led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.

One malefactor railed on him; the other rebuked him, took the blame of his own deeds, and said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. That man repented at the last hour, and was answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

There was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour, and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.
The centurion glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that came together to that sight smote their breasts and returned.

Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man and a just, had not consented to their counsel and deed, and begged the body and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone. He was buried the same day, which is the custom written in the law. There is no waiting days over a body. The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, made king over the realm of the Chaldeans, Daniel understood by the books the seventy years of the desolations of Jerusalem spoken to Jeremiah. This is the same Darius dealt with when the Persians and Medes were shown in chapters 7 and 8.

Daniel set his face unto the Most High to seek him by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes, confessing that the people had sinned, committed iniquity, done wickedly, and rebelled, departing from his precepts and judgments. They had not hearkened unto the prophets who spake in his name to their kings, princes, fathers, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to the Most High, but confusion of faces to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, near and far off, driven through all the countries because of their trespasses. Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned. -

All Israel transgressed the law by departing, so the curse was poured upon them and the oath written in the law of Moses, because they had sinned against him. The oath that was written is [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), verses 1 through 68. -

Daniel appealed to the Most High who brought his people out of Egypt with a mighty hand, confessing they had sinned and done wickedly, and asking that his anger and fury be turned away from his city Jerusalem, his holy mountain. He pleaded for the Most High to hear, forgive, hearken, and do, not for their righteousness but for his great mercies, since the city and the people are called by his name.

While Daniel was speaking, praying, and confessing his sin and the sin of his people Israel, the man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision, was caused to fly swiftly and touched him about the time of the evening oblation. Gabriel came to give him skill and understanding, for at the beginning of his supplications the commandment came forth, and Daniel was greatly beloved.

Seventy weeks are determined upon the people and the holy city to finish the transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up the vision, and anoint the most Holy. From the going forth of the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem unto Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks and threescore and two weeks, the street built again even in troublous times. After threescore and two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for himself, and the people of the prince that shall come destroy the city and the sanctuary. He confirms the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week causes the sacrifice and oblation to cease. Daniel was given the four beasts first, then this further vision of the seventy weeks by Gabriel in the midst of his prayer and supplications. The bishop's class on the seventy weeks opens this up in full.

If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe and to do all his commandments, the Most High will set thee on high above all nations of the earth. Diligent means characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort. You have to be on fire for the laws of the Most High, standing fast. You cannot be one foot in and one foot out, lukewarm, yawning through the classes. You cannot be tired of the word of the Lord; be excited to hear it.
All these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God. Hearken means to listen.

Blessed in the city and blessed in the field; blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, which is your children, and the fruit of thy ground and cattle. Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store: that is going into your surplus. Blessed when thou comest in and blessed when thou goest out: it is twofold, but it is going into coming in and out of Jerusalem.

The enemies that rise up against thee shall flee before thee seven ways; the blessing is commanded on thy storehouses and on all thou settest thine hand unto. The Most High shall establish thee an holy people unto himself, and all the people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord and be afraid of thee. Thou shalt lend unto many nations and not borrow; the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail, above only and not beneath, if thou hearken to the commandments and turn not aside after other gods. Isaiah sums up [Deuteronomy 28:1-14](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v1): we possessed it but a little while. Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships, and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings.

But if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee. Now we do some precepting, word by word. The voice of the Lord is his commandments; to hearken unto his voice means to keep his commandments. Observe to DO all his commandments: do is the action word. The Most High is a God of doing, and by him actions are weighed. Do not talk proudly and arrogantly, saying God loves me no matter what and God knows my heart; he had a personal relationship with a few men like Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, and David, and talking like you are one of them is arrogancy coming out of your mouth. Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

Cursed shalt thou be in the city: as when police fired on a car of siblings as young as nine years old in Georgia after the children panicked when a cruiser followed their vehicle. That is cursed in the city. Cursed shalt thou be in the field: we came off the slave ship and went right to the field, picking cotton from sunup to sundown. We know that one.

Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store: that goes into your businesses and your holdings. It is hard enough for a black man or woman to start a business; we are left with side hustles while the major trades, the ships, the metals, and the timber belong to Esau. These curses are on us as a nation. It is not about us individually; keep that in mind.

Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body: your children. The same children panicking in front of police, and the dozens of children killed by youth gun violence in Chicago in a matter of months. Cursed shall be the fruit of thy land, thy kine, and thy sheep: the food we eat is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us. Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as [Deuteronomy 14](/bible/deuteronomy/14) says.

Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in and cursed when thou goest out. He is talking about Jerusalem, but it is twofold: it is coming in and going out of life itself. Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: we are born under the curses and we die still living under them.

The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke in all that thou settest thine hand unto, until thou be destroyed. Rebuke means sharp disapproval or criticism because of your behavior: no matter what you do, nobody will see the silver lining in it; even what you mean for good turns out bad. Vexation means the state of being annoyed or a thing that causes annoyance: among these nations they do not love you, they tolerate you. Your marching for equal rights annoys them; they ask why you will not just accept what you were given.

The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee: diseases. He shall smite thee with a consumption, a fever, an inflammation, an extreme burning, the sword, blasting, and mildew. Amos shows what the blasting and mildew go into: famine, pestilence after the manner of Egypt, young men slain with the sword, death and destruction.

Thy heaven over thy head shall be brass, and the earth under thee iron. It is twofold: rain not coming down and crops not coming up. It also goes into the chains above your head and the shackles of iron on your feet. Look up the images of slavery and you see whose neck the chains were on. The rain of thy land shall be powder and dust from heaven until thou be destroyed.

Thou shalt go out one way against thine enemies and flee seven ways before them, and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth: 1492 and 1619. Thy carcase shall be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away. Look up Wounded Knee, where the United States cavalry killed the Native Americans, who are Gad in the Bible, and left their bodies in the snow.

The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, the emerods, the scab, and the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed. The itch that cannot be healed: look up who has the highest rates of sexually transmitted diseases right now. It is us.

The Lord shall smite thee with madness, blindness, and astonishment of heart, and thou shalt grope at noonday as the blind gropeth in darkness. Thou shalt not prosper in thy ways, and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee: going back into bondage. Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

Thou shalt betroth a wife and another man shall lie with her: our wives were taken away, raped, robbed, and murdered in the captivity. Thou shalt build an house and not dwell therein: we built the master's house, we built the White House, and to this day our people frame the roofs of suburban houses they will never live in. Thou shalt plant a vineyard and not gather the grapes: down south our people and the Haitians, who are Levi, are still in the fields picking beans and oranges, and none of it comes back to them; it is packaged and shipped somewhere else. Thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face and shall not be restored to thee: no reparations. They just pulled the okey-doke in North Carolina, promising reparations and then saying it would not be paid in money but in infrastructure. The Most High said it would not be restored.

Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look and fail with longing for them all the day long, and there shall be no might in thine hand. The slave narratives collected in When I Was a Slave back it up: slaves were treated like cattle, a speculator went about the country buying them up, and it was pitiful to see children taken from the mother's breast, mothers sold from children, husbands sold from wives. Another narrative: slavery days were hell; babies were snatched from their mother's breast and sold to speculators, children separated from sisters and brothers and never saw each other again. The Bible is a true book, and our ancestors backed it up.

The fruit of thy land and all thy labours shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up, and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway. The record of the conquistadors says one Spaniard ate enough for seven of the Indians, the northern kingdom. They literally ate up the fruit of the land. Thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.

The Lord shall bring thee and thy king unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone. Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations: Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, African American, gentile. We lost our name and left it for a curse, like it says in Isaiah, while others wear the name and cry anti-Semitic.

Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field and gather but little in; thou shalt plant vineyards but neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes; olive trees through all thy coasts, but no oil to anoint thyself. Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity: the same story the slave narratives tell. It happened before the ships too. When we ruled in Spain, in what they call the Dark Ages, a shipload of our people cast out on the African coast had the men and youths sold into slavery, the defenseless women ravished, and the aged, the sick, and the infants tortured and murdered by the thousands. That is recorded in The Jews and Moors in Spain; get that book if you do not have it.

All thy trees and the fruit of thy land shall the locust consume. The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high, and thou shalt come down very low; he shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him; he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail. Basically, you will always be oppressed. Their own book, New World Jewry, says the Jewish converts were so disseminated through all the trading parts of the world that they became the pegs and nails that keep the whole frame of commerce together, back in the 1600s. But the curse says Israel comes down very low and borrows from the stranger. The lender at the top of world trade and the cursed borrower cannot be the same people; somebody is lying, and now we caught it.

All these curses shall pursue thee and overtake thee till thou be destroyed, because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God. They shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. There is no time limit on this thing; that is how we know we are the real Israelites, because these curses are still hitting us all over the earth in some shape, form, or fashion to this day. The Most High said you would be the bottom, and he meant it until the kingdom comes. That is why they do not want to go to [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28).

Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart for the abundance of all things: we have to be happy keeping these commandments. That means joyful at the new moon, joyful on the sabbath, joyful in the classes. The lack of joy in keeping the commandments is the very reason the captivity came. Sisters, that includes the commandment to be obedient and in subjection to your husband. Do not act like it is bondage; your husband cannot save you on the day of judgment, and you must work out your own salvation and stand before Christ with a joyful spirit in the commandments.

Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in want of all things, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck until he have destroyed thee. Here is one way we stay destroyed: Juneteenth. The slave narrative records the master telling his slaves, this is military law, but I am forced to tell you this law says you are now free; I cannot make you stay unless you want to. That June 19th announcement of the master's law is what is still celebrated in Texas. Our people celebrate Juneteenth like it is something to be proud of, but it is the slave master's holiday, and we are still slaves under the curses.

The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth: the eagle is the symbol of Esau's nation. A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand: we did not speak English, and our brothers in the islands and South America did not speak Spanish when the ships came. New World Jewry itself records that many slaves were called ladino, which in that context means a negro slave who could speak Spanish. So the northern kingdom brother who says he is not black is simply a negro that speaks Spanish; welcome home, you are our brother. A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old nor shew favour to the young: they worked the old to death in the cotton fields, and today an old man dies with a knee held on his neck for over eight minutes, and children get fired on by police. Neither old nor young is spared.

He shall eat the fruit of thy cattle and the fruit of thy land until thou be destroyed, leaving thee neither corn, wine, nor oil. The Native Americans lived off the land, following the buffalo and the deer and making coats of skins. Now Reuben stays by the casino and Gad lives on reservation lands like barren wasteland where nothing grows, with outdoor plumbing, and it has never been restored. Reparations is not a casino, and it is not being called sovereign while occupied by another nation.

He shall besiege thee in all thy gates until thy high and fenced walls come down. Verse 52 onward is going into the siege of Jerusalem by Babylon and by Rome, and Assyria did this also. This is NOT talking about black-on-black violence; do not use it for that. Thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and daughters, in the siege and in the straitness wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee. The Most High starved our people out in the siege until they boiled and ate their own children. The proof it is not street violence is in the text itself: the tender man's eye shall be evil toward the wife of his bosom and toward the remnant of his children, because he has nothing left in the siege. It describes a good, caring, delicate man broken by famine, not violence in the neighborhood. The tender and delicate woman, which would not set the sole of her foot upon the ground for delicateness: our sisters have fallen a long way from that standard of tenderness and delicateness, and they need to return to it.

If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law written in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD THY GOD, then he will make thy plagues wonderful, plagues of thy seed, of long continuance, and sore sicknesses. Verse 59 is saying the Most High will make up diseases to keep punishing you; he will even have Esau create them in a laboratory and make them affect you more than anybody else. He will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt which thou wast afraid of, and also every sickness and every plague which is NOT written in the book of this law, until thou be destroyed.

Ye shall be left few in number, whereas ye were as the stars of heaven for multitude, because thou wouldest not obey the voice of the Lord thy God. As the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you. We have to understand who we are dealing with: he is happy to bless you and happy to destroy you for breaking the commandments. That is the God this Christianity needs to be teaching, to put some fear back in our people.

The Lord shall scatter thee among all people from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone: that is talking about Christianity and Islam. The Handbook of Denominations records that as early as 1700 white slaveholders in the south provided religious teaching for their slaves, and the slaves identified with the faith of their owners: if your slave master was Baptist you were Baptist; if he was Catholic you were Catholic. The same book says black Baptist doctrine runs quite parallel to that of white Baptist churches: it is the same exact thing, the slave master's religion with a black face on it. The Most High is saying: wherever I scatter you, you will not know me; you will be caught up thinking you serve me, but you do not know me. The only time you will know him is when he puts his spirit back on the earth and reveals it in the last days. That is why there is so much turmoil in our life, because we were not serving God right.

Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest, but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind. No ease: the northern kingdom is catching it right now, with migrant children taken from their families and detained in hotels not even registered with the government before deportation, and thousands of those children cannot be found.

Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee, and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life. That is why those children panicked when the police car pulled up behind them: no assurance of thy life. In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even, and at even, Would God it were morning, for the fear of thine heart and the sight of thine eyes.

Here is the nail in the coffin: the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships. Egypt means bondage; the scripture defines it right in [Deuteronomy 5](/bible/deuteronomy/5), the land of Egypt, the house of bondage. He is saying: I will bring you into slavery again, with ships. It is not the literal land of Egypt, because you can walk to Egypt; Isaiah shows Israel walked down to Egypt. The false pastors who say we were shipped back across the Red Sea are wrong; the ships went to a spiritual Egypt. Revelation names it: the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt. The greatest country on the face of the earth, America, Babylon the great, is the Egypt we were carried into with ships. Even their own scholarship confirms who was there the first time: a treatise on physical geography admits that negroes existed in Egypt in the days of Rameses with the same national features they have now. The Bible says the negroes go INTO Egypt, bondage, AGAIN. There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.
Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee; the quick precept for no man shall buy you.
