verses.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?

Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:
That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
And Jesus went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him for to shew him the buildings of the temple.
And Jesus said unto them, See ye not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!
Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,
Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.
For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,
And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.
Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.
For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.
And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.
For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.
Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.
For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.
The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand;
A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young:

And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed: which also shall not leave thee either corn, wine, or oil, or the increase of thy kine, or flocks of thy sheep, until he have destroyed thee.

And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land: and he shall besiege thee in all thy gates throughout all thy land, which the Lord thy God hath given thee.

And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee:

And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.

cases.name: Judas Iscariot
cases.charge: Theft from the common purse; betraying innocent blood for thirty pieces of silver
cases.summary: One of the twelve, keeper of the bag, and a thief who took what was put in it. He went to the chief priests and asked what they would give him; they weighed thirty pieces of silver. He delivered Christ with a kiss. In the morning he brought the silver back: I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood.
cases.offense: Covetousness ripened into treachery. Zechariah had priced the shepherd at thirty pieces of silver, the price of a gored slave. His own confession names the statute: cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. Christ: good were it for that man if he had never been born.
cases.judgment: The priests would not take the money back; he cast it down in the temple, went and hanged himself, and the silver bought the potter's field. Acts adds that he fell headlong and burst asunder. Peter, citing the Psalms, says he went to his own place, and his bishoprick passed to another.

entries.commentary: The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. The feast of unleavened bread and the passover are spoken of here as one and the same season.

Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve. The chief priests and captains were glad, and covenanted to give him money. Men are not in their right mind when they can be glad over a thing like that.
Peter and John are sent to prepare the passover. Christ kept the passover, and a follower of Christ keeps what he kept.

With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer. This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.
Behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table. He told the rest, while sitting with them, that one of them would do it.

The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors: men who take a benefit for ruling over others. But ye shall not be so. He that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve. As a man is raised in knowledge and understanding he is made more of a servant, not less. I am among you as he that serveth, and he was the greatest of them.
Ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The apostles are set to judge the twelve tribes, which is who this word is for.

Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat; but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not; and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren. Peter walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm, and what he strengthens his brethren with is the same thing.
Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death. He is told the cock shall not crow this day, before he shall thrice deny that he knows him.
This that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors. He is quoting the prophets, because the new testament was not yet written when he walked the earth.

Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done. Being in an agony he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground. He found them sleeping for sorrow. Grief drains a man and puts him to sleep, and that is what was on them knowing what was coming.

Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss? The servant's ear is cut off and he touches it and heals him. A miracle was done in front of those men in that moment, and they carried him away regardless. This is your hour, and the power of darkness.

Peter denies him three times, and the third time he is known by his speech, for he is a Galilaean. He sounded like the man he was denying. The Lord turned, and looked upon Peter; and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, and went out, and wept bitterly.

The men that held him mocked him and smote him, and blindfolded him. Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God. Art thou then the Son of God? And he said, Ye say that I am.

Luke wrote both the Gospel of Luke and the book of Acts. The "former treatise" is the Gospel of Luke, which was also addressed to Theophilus, so the two books are two letters from the same hand. The scriptures we have are a collection of the apostles' teaching passed down to the young men under them, the seventy, and the other disciples. Luke was not one of the twelve, though it is speculated he was of the seventy, and he was there from the beginning. Just as the bishops and elders pass down history to us today so that we can speak on it though we were not there, that knowledge was passed down to Luke. Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke addresses him as "most excellent," a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed "most noble Festus." -

Luke gave a full historical account of everything Christ did, from his birth to the day he was taken up, and records that Christ, through the Holy Ghost, gave commandments to the apostles he had chosen. The end of Luke segues straight into Acts. The commandment was that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. "All nations" does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria (which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled), then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece, and Rome, then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history. -

After his passion Christ showed himself alive by many infallible proofs, being seen forty days and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of the Most High. He did not appear for only a day or two; he stayed forty days to open the understanding further. Within that time he was seen by many. Cephas is another name for Peter and means stone. -

The commandment was to not depart from Jerusalem but to wait for the promise of the Father, which is the Holy Ghost, given only after Christ was glorified. Christ could teach only so much in three years because a man can bear only so much. The Comforter would open their understanding in increments after his death, guiding them into all truth and bringing his words back to their remembrance. The Holy Ghost comes in an order that begins with the law: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and opens the understanding. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth. -

John truly baptized with water, but they would be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence. There is a distinction between what John taught and what Christ brought. Baptism comes from the word baptizo, out of the purification laws. John was of the tribe of Levi, his father Zacharias a priest and his mother Elizabeth of the daughters of Aaron, so his water baptism was always symbolic, a preparation leading up to Christ. John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments. Two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him, which is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water even though Christ himself baptized not with water but with the Holy Ghost. When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly, meaning wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind that consumes and filters information; but that Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified. -

Even after all of this they asked whether he would at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel, which shows the Holy Ghost was not yet fully given. It is given in measures, and every man is dealt a measure of faith that he has to grow in; in Christ there was no measure, but the disciples knew only so much at that time. They asked because they thought Rome was the last captivity, and John the Baptist thought the same when he sent to ask whether Christ was the one or they should look for another. They knew Daniel's beasts up to Rome because their fathers had lived through them, but they did not yet understand the little horn, Babylon the great and America, or the seven seals that only the Lion of the tribe of Judah could open. That fuller understanding was given later to John, to Peter, and now in these last days. The falling away had to come first and the man of sin be revealed; he could not be openly named under Rome, where you were jailed for sedition, so Paul wrote in allegory. He would be revealed in a land like America, where the freedom to speak allows the man of sin to be identified plainly. "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die. -

Christ said it is not for them to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power. Even after his resurrection Christ did not know the time, which disproves the trinity and the idea that Christ is the Father, showing the Son is separate from the Father. You come to understand the times and seasons as you live through the prophecies and see prophecy become history.

They would receive power after the Holy Ghost came upon them, and be witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judaea, in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth. Christians misunderstand this power as merely speaking in tongues, but the Bible defines the power of the Holy Ghost by the signs that follow: casting out devils, speaking with new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. Peter was sought to heal by his shadow and Paul by his handkerchief. -

While they beheld, Christ was taken up and a cloud received him out of their sight. He was taken up in the middle of his speaking after forty days; that was the exit. The Most High maketh the clouds his chariot, so this was not merely a cloud but a chariot, an instrument of the angels, the same as the moon being an instrument of the armies above. Christ was received up by a chariot, not carried by little white angels in the clouds as the Christian movies depict. The kind of chariot that masks itself in a cloud was seen in 2011 over the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, a glowing orb that descended and then shot off at about four thousand miles an hour over one of the most secure no-fly zones in the world, witnessed by thousands and reported internationally. -

Two men stood by them in white apparel and asked the men of Galilee why they stood gazing up into heaven, saying this same Jesus shall so come in like manner as they had seen him go. The same way Christ ascended into what men call outer space is the same way he will descend.

They returned from the mount called Olivet, a sabbath day's journey from Jerusalem, and went up into an upper room where the eleven abode; their names are listed. The lists differ across the gospels. Simon is also called Peter and Cephas. Simon the Canaanite is the same as Simon Zelotes. Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus, is the same as Judas the brother of James, who is also called Jude. Judas the brother of James is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude or Thaddaeus so as not to be associated with the traitor. -
Simeon hath declared how the Most High first visited the gentiles; that Simeon is Simon Peter.

They all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brethren. This was not only the men; the women also had to learn. The men always understood that the women learn alongside them, so a camp that keeps the women out of the congregation is wrong. Our people came into slavery together and will come out of captivity together. "His brethren" are Christ's own brothers. During his ministry they did not believe in him and told him to go show himself openly in Judaea, but after his death and the miracles they came to believe. James the Just, the Lord's brother, became an apostle and was later killed. -

Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars. Howl, fir tree; for the cedar is fallen; because the mighty are spoiled. There is a voice of the howling of the shepherds; for their glory is spoiled: a voice of the roaring of young lions; for the pride of Jordan is spoiled.

Feed the flock of the slaughter, whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty; and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not. The verse names a people who were possessed, sold, and slain by those who held themselves not guilty, and whose own shepherds do not pity them. That is Israel, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans.

I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith the Lord: but lo, I will deliver the men every one into his neighbour's hand, and into the hand of his king: and they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them. I will feed the flock of slaughter, even you, O poor of the flock. And I took unto me two staves; the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Bands; and I fed the flock. Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me. I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another. The scripture says plainly what the end of this land is, and it is why keeping the law matters now.

I took my staff, even Beauty, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people. I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. The Lord said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the Lord. Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel. That breaking is the split of the southern and northern kingdoms. He broke it, and he also says he will put it back together.

Take unto thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd. For lo, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, which shall not visit those that be cut off, neither shall seek the young one, nor heal that that is broken, nor feed that that standeth still: but he shall eat the flesh of the fat, and tear their claws in pieces. Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! The sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise, for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are open against me, and they have spoken against me with a lying tongue. The people speaking against us are the nations. They compassed me about also with words of hatred and fought against me without a cause. For my love they are my adversaries, but I give myself unto prayer. We have to give ourselves unto prayer and let God fight our battles, for it is not by our might. -

Set thou a wicked man over him and let Satan stand at his right hand; when he shall be judged let him be condemned, and let his prayer become sin. Let his days be few and let another take his office, his rulership. Let his children be fatherless and his wife a widow; let his children be continually vagabonds, meaning bums, and beg, seeking their bread out of their desolate places, walking around like bums begging for crumbs. Let the extortioner catch all that he hath and let the strangers spoil his labor; let there be none to extend mercy unto him nor to favor his fatherless children. Let his posterity, his future generations, be cut off and their name blotted out. Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered with the Lord and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out; let them be before the Lord continually, that He may cut off the memory of them from the earth, that they may be destroyed.

Because he remembered not to show mercy but persecuted the poor and needy man, that he might even slay the broken in heart. The enemies showed us no mercy in captivity and continued to destroy us even when our iniquity came to an end. As he loved cursing, so let it come unto him; as he delighted not in blessing, so let it be far from him. This is the nations doing their own will against the Israelites, afflicting the poor. Let this be the reward of my adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul. The adversaries are the nations, and the Lord fights for us against our enemies to save us. -

But do thou for me, O God the Lord, for thy name's sake; because thy mercy is good, deliver thou me. For I am poor and needy and my heart is wounded within me; I am gone like the shadow when it declineth and am tossed up and down as the locust. My knees are weak through fasting and my flesh faileth of fatness, meaning I am skinny now. I have become also a reproach unto the adversaries; when they look upon me they shake their heads.

Help me, O Lord my God; O save me according to thy mercy, that they, the adversaries, may know that this is thy hand, that thou, Lord, hast done it. The destruction of the nations will be by the Lord's Spirit. Let them curse, but bless thou; when they arise let them be ashamed, but let thy servant rejoice. Let the adversaries be clothed with shame and cover themselves with their own confusion. The nations meant evil against us, but God means it for good. I will greatly praise the Lord with my mouth and praise Him among the multitude, for He shall stand at the right hand of the poor, the Israelites, to save him from those that condemn his soul. He saves the poor by His commandments; keeping God's commandments and enduring in this truth is how we will be saved. -

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

verses.text: Then saith one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, which should betray him,
Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor?
This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.
And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him;
Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.
And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them.
And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.
And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,
And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.
And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
And while he yet spake, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast.
And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.
And Jesus said unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.
Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.
And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.
And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.
And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in.
Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.
Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;
And gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.
Men and brethren, this scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost by the mouth of David spake before concerning Judas, which was guide to them that took Jesus.
For he was numbered with us, and had obtained part of this ministry.
Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.
And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.
For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.
That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.
And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.
And the Lord said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the Lord.
Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.
Let his days be few; and let another take his office.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.

cases.name: Nazareth, his own country
cases.charge: Being offended at him; seeking to cast him down the hill
cases.summary: In the synagogue where he had been brought up he read Isaiah and said the scripture was fulfilled that day. They marvelled, then asked if this was not the carpenter's son, then were filled with wrath and led him to the brow of the hill. He did no mighty work there, and passed through the midst of them.
cases.offense: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? And they were offended at him. When he reminded them that Elijah was sent to a widow of Sidon and Elisha cleansed a Syrian, all they in the synagogue were filled with wrath, and rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
cases.judgment: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house. And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief; he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them; and he marvelled because of their unbelief. He passing through the midst of them went his way, and Nazareth kept what it had chosen: a carpenter's son and no miracles.

entries.commentary: Being full of the Holy Ghost he is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, forty days tempted of the devil, and in those days he did eat nothing. He answers with the law: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

The devil shows him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. No man can do that, which settles who was standing there. All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever I will I give it. The offer is real, and the price is worship. Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Again the answer is a commandment.

Set on a pinnacle of the temple and answered with scripture, he replies, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God. When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season. The whole battle was fought with the word, and that is the only way it is won.

As his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. He reads from Esaias: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, to preach deliverance to the captives. This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

They wonder at the gracious words, and then ask, Is not this Joseph's son? No prophet is accepted in his own country. He names the widow of Sarepta and Naaman the Syrian, and they are filled with wrath, thrust him out of the city, and lead him to the brow of the hill to cast him down headlong, but he passes through the midst of them.

In the synagogue there was a man which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and it cried out, I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God. That spirit was sitting in the house of worship, and it knew exactly who he was. Knowing who he is and doing what he says are two different things.

He rebukes the fever in Simon's wife's mother and it leaves her, and he lays his hands on every one of the sick brought to him. I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent. He went where the people were, and some received the word and some did not.

In his own country they are astonished at his wisdom and his mighty works, and then are offended at him because they know his family. A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. What was done to him is done to those teaching today: men who knew you before you repented ask who you think you are.

He could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk and healed them, and he marvelled because of their unbelief. Consider what that means. The unbelief of his own people was such that it made the son of the Most High marvel.

He sends them forth by two and two with power over unclean spirits, taking nothing for the journey but a staff. Whosoever will not receive you nor hear you, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. The word goes out whether they hear or whether they forbear, and that shaking of the dust seals the judgment.

Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead. John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

Herodias had a quarrel against John and would have killed him, but could not, for Herod feared him, knowing that he was a just man and an holy. When the oath is made, the daughter asks her mother what to ask, and is told, The head of John the Baptist. The king was exceeding sorry, but for his oath's sake he sent the executioner.

He was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things. Five loaves and two fishes feed five thousand men, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up. He made them sit down by companies, in ranks by hundreds and by fifties. No man argued about where he was placed. The Most High is a God of order, and the eating came after the order.

He comes to them walking upon the sea, and they suppose it had been a spirit and cry out. These were fishermen; they knew what water does. They were sore amazed, for they considered not the miracle of the loaves, for their heart was hardened. Men can watch a thing done in front of them and still not take it to heart.
Wherever he entered, they laid the sick in the streets and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment, and as many as touched him were made whole.

A sower goes forth to sow. Seed falls by the way side, on stony places, among thorns, and into good ground, and only the good ground brings forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.

It is given unto the disciples to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but not unto them. Whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance; but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.

In them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias: by hearing ye shall hear and shall not understand, and seeing ye shall see and shall not perceive. They saw the works and did not perceive. The heart was made fat and the ears heavy so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come.
Blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear. Many prophets and righteous men desired to see these things and did not see them.

The seed by the way side is the one who hears and understands not, and the wicked one catches away what was sown in his heart. The stony ground is the one who receives it with joy and has no root, and is offended when tribulation or persecution arises. That can come through family or through a job. The thorns are the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, which choke the word. The good ground hears and understands, and brings others in behind him.

An enemy sows tares among the wheat while men slept, and the householder will not have them gathered up before the harvest lest the wheat be rooted up with them. The separating is not ours to do. Both grow together until the harvest.
The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, the least of all seeds, which becomes the greatest among herbs. This work starts small and ends covering the earth.

The leaven hid in three measures of meal leavens the whole, and all these things were spoken in parables, that it might be fulfilled, I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.

Christ gives the meaning himself: the sower is the Son of man, the field is the world, the good seed are the children of the kingdom, the tares are the children of the wicked one, the enemy is the devil, the harvest is the end of the world, and the reapers are the angels. The tares are gathered and burned, and the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hid in a field, which a man finds and for joy thereof sells all that he hath and buys that field. Finding out who you are is that joy.
The merchant man, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had and bought it.

The net gathers of every kind, and the good are put into vessels and the bad cast away. The angels sever the wicked from among the just. This is not only about the other nations. Israel must keep these laws, and there will be those in these last days who are not keeping them.
Every scribe instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like a householder which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

In his own country they are astonished and ask, Is not this the carpenter's son? They name his mother, his brethren James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and his sisters, all of them living among them. A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country and in his own house, and he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power, which is why the same sentence can say both.
All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not. What gives life is the word itself. The flesh profits nothing; the words are spirit and they are life.

There was a man sent from God, whose name was John, sent to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe. He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of it. He prepared the way. The blessing that came down on all men is traced in the scripture to one head, and rested on Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes.

He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not. He came unto his own, and his own received him not. His own are named all through the scriptures: the people the law was appointed to, and sin is the breaking of that law.
But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.
And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

The law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ. Grace and mercy are said in the scriptures to be with his saints, and the truth is named in the psalm as the law itself. Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

John confessed, and denied not, but confessed, I am not the Christ, nor Elias, nor that prophet. I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias. I baptize with water: but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not. Men came to that baptism confessing their sins, and a man has to be taught the law to know what he is confessing.

Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water. John says himself who this was made known to. Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizeth with the Holy Ghost.

Two of John's disciples follow him and ask where he dwelt. He said, Come and see, and they abode with him that day. He had a place to stay. Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, and brought him to Jesus, who said, Thou shalt be called Cephas.

We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write. What was written of him was written in the law and the prophets before ever he came. Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile. Nathanael answered, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel. That is the title given him here, and it names one people. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

verses.text: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.
And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,
To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.
And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him.
And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?
And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.
And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.
But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.
And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.
And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
But he passing through the midst of them went his way,
And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?
Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.
And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.
And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.
And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?
Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?
And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?
And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.
And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
For neither did his brethren believe in him.

cases.name: Peter's denial
cases.charge: Denying Christ three times with cursing and swearing
cases.summary: Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Before the cock crew twice he had denied him three times, the last with oaths and curses, to a maid and to bystanders in the high priest's courtyard. The Lord turned and looked upon Peter, and he went out and wept bitterly.
cases.offense: Whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father. Peter did it three times and sealed it with a false oath. The sin was foretold, and so was the mercy: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
cases.judgment: No sentence but the look and the tears. After the resurrection Christ asked him three times, lovest thou me? and three times restored him: feed my sheep. Peter's godly sorrow worked repentance; Judas' sorrow worked death.

entries.commentary: The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. The feast of unleavened bread and the passover are spoken of here as one and the same season.

Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve. The chief priests and captains were glad, and covenanted to give him money. Men are not in their right mind when they can be glad over a thing like that.
Peter and John are sent to prepare the passover. Christ kept the passover, and a follower of Christ keeps what he kept.

With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer. This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.
Behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table. He told the rest, while sitting with them, that one of them would do it.

The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors: men who take a benefit for ruling over others. But ye shall not be so. He that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve. As a man is raised in knowledge and understanding he is made more of a servant, not less. I am among you as he that serveth, and he was the greatest of them.
Ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The apostles are set to judge the twelve tribes, which is who this word is for.

Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat; but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not; and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren. Peter walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm, and what he strengthens his brethren with is the same thing.
Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death. He is told the cock shall not crow this day, before he shall thrice deny that he knows him.
This that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors. He is quoting the prophets, because the new testament was not yet written when he walked the earth.

Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done. Being in an agony he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground. He found them sleeping for sorrow. Grief drains a man and puts him to sleep, and that is what was on them knowing what was coming.

Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss? The servant's ear is cut off and he touches it and heals him. A miracle was done in front of those men in that moment, and they carried him away regardless. This is your hour, and the power of darkness.

Peter denies him three times, and the third time he is known by his speech, for he is a Galilaean. He sounded like the man he was denying. The Lord turned, and looked upon Peter; and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, and went out, and wept bitterly.

The men that held him mocked him and smote him, and blindfolded him. Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God. Art thou then the Son of God? And he said, Ye say that I am.

Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.
