cases.name: The Samaritan village, and the sons of thunder
cases.charge: Refusing to receive him because his face was toward Jerusalem; James and John asking for fire from heaven
cases.summary: A village of Samaria would not take him in, and James and John asked leave to call down fire as Elias did. He rebuked them, not the village: ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of; the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. They went to another village.
cases.offense: They did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem. And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
cases.judgment: He turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. And they went to another village. The village was spared a sentence, and the disciples were taught the difference between Elijah's day and theirs; one of those two sons of thunder later went down to Samaria with Peter to lay hands on believers there.

entries.commentary: He gave the twelve power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases, and sent them to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick. Take nothing for your journey. Where they are not received, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
Herod is perplexed, hearing that John was risen from the dead, or that Elias had appeared, and says, John have I beheaded: but who is this?
Five loaves and two fishes feed about five thousand men, sat down by fifties in a company, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up.

Whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God. The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day. That word stood alongside all the power they had just seen, and they still could not hold the two together.

If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. What is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away? Whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed.

As he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias, who spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem. Out of the cloud came a voice, This is my beloved Son: hear him. And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone.

A father brings his only child, whom the disciples could not deliver, and Christ answers, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? He rebukes the unclean spirit, heals the child, and delivers him again to his father, and they were all amazed at the mighty power of God.

Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men. The saying comes straight after a devil the disciples could not cast out. He had power to give power, and would still be delivered into the hands of men. They understood it not, and feared to ask him.
There arose a reasoning among them which of them should be greatest, and he set a child by him and said, He that is least among you all, the same shall be great.

John reports one casting out devils in his name whom they forbade, because he followed not with them. Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us. Men who are not speaking against Christ and are teaching the same identity of the people are not to be forbidden merely because they do not stand with us.

The Samaritan village would not receive him, and James and John ask to command fire to come down from heaven. Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them.

Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head. Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God. This is not a bar on burying your own father. It is leaving the affairs of those who are not keeping the commandments to be handled by them, while the work goes on. No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High. -

Ahaziah falls down through a lattice in his upper chamber and is sick, and sends messengers to inquire of Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, the lord of the flies, whether he shall recover. He turns to an idol rather than to the Most High for his answer. The angel of the Lord sends Elijah the Tishbite to meet the messengers and ask whether it is because there is no God in Israel that they go to inquire of Beelzebub. The word of the Lord is that Ahaziah shall not come down from his bed but shall surely die. When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron. -

The king sends a captain of fifty with his fifty to Elijah, who sits on the top of a hill, and the captain commands the man of God to come down. Elijah answers that if he is a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume him and his fifty, and it does. A second captain of fifty is sent and speaks the same way, and fire from heaven consumes him and his fifty as well. The third captain goes up, falls on his knees, and pleads that his life and the lives of his fifty be precious in Elijah's sight. The angel of the Lord tells Elijah to go down with the third captain and not to fear him. Elijah delivers to the king the same word, that because he sent to inquire of Beelzebub as though there were no God in Israel, he shall surely die.

Ahaziah dies according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram reigns in his stead because Ahaziah had no son. The rest of the acts of Ahaziah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, comes by night. Those men were the teachers of the synagogues, and it would have cost him standing to come openly. Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over.

Nicodemus takes it literally and asks whether a man can enter the second time into his mother's womb. Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. Both are named plainly elsewhere as the word.
That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles.

Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? He was a chief teacher, and men depended on him for the understanding of the law. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?

As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up. The history behind that is plain, and so is who it was for. It was Israel in the wilderness that spake against the Most High and against Moses, and Israel that was bitten, and Israel that looked and lived. The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son. This follows straight on from the serpent, and it is the same people in view. John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. A man can be comfortable and even do well in the darkness he was raised in. Coming into the light requires change, and refusing that change is what condemns him. The Pharisees and the rulers were not condemned by Christ; they condemned themselves by not humbling down to repent. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.

John's disciples notice that all men are coming to Jesus, and John answers, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven. I am not the Christ, but that I am sent before him. He must increase, but I must decrease.

He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true. Not to receive it is to call the record God gave of his son a lie. He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.

Saul was consenting unto Stephen's death. This is Saul who becomes Paul, part of the same people persecuting the church, killing disciples and women, thinking he was doing it for the right reasons. That is why the scripture says judge no one before their time; a man as evil as Saul was doing back there became Paul the apostle. At that time there was a great persecution against the church at Jerusalem, and they were all scattered abroad throughout Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Notice that unlike the other epistles, the book of Acts never closes with Amen, showing there is a continuation: the apostles come back on the scene and redo the Acts all over again, so the things that happened back then are the things that happen today. There will be a great persecution today. This gospel is a witness against the whole world. When you pray thy kingdom come, thy will be done, you are saying the Most High's will overpowers America's will, Russia's, China's, every nation racing for world domination. To preach a black Christ in the streets is to speak against the system that was designed to keep our people debased, a Christ with many crowns upon his head who takes the crowns of all the nations. They are not going to let a people they despise rise up and preach a gospel that overthrows the world superpowers and do nothing; it is going to be a great persecution. Gird your mind, study, pray, and apply, because wisdom and knowledge will be the stability of our time.
Devout men carried Stephen to his burial and made great lamentation over him. A devout man is a man according to the laws of the Most High who has a good report.

As for Saul, he made havoc of the church, entering into every house, haling men and women and committing them to prison. This is the same spirit that will rise up in the religious leaders again; they will seek after us and put us through hell, thinking they do the Most High a service. Because of this you have to be as a pilgrim, one that is ready to get up at any moment and abandon everything. They may come to your house to arrest you, and you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence, and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime, the way our fathers were fugitives. Christ warned the disciples this would happen from city to city, and it came to pass, and it is coming again.

Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ unto them. Philip was preaching to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles; the Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

The people with one accord gave heed to the things Philip spoke, hearing and seeing the miracles he did. Unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, came out of many that were possessed, and many taken with palsies and that were lame were healed, and there was great joy in that city.

Before this there was a certain man called Simon who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, and they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. History outside the Bible says Simon Magus followed Peter performing tricks, became known as the father of heretics, taught salvation by grace alone without works, and finally fell to his death when Peter commanded the demons carrying him to release him; the validity of that account is uncertain, but it shows Simon was a sorcerer deceiving the people. Christianity works the same way, a binding spell over our people that covers the eyes from seeing the truth. You can read the plain scripture that Christ is black and that he came first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and they walk away not believing, or say they do not want to hear the Bible, only your opinion, and then reject that too. It is an enchantment to the highest level, where a man can read something in front of them and they see something else.

But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of the Most High and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Then Simon himself believed also, and was baptized, and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs. Some of our brothers recover themselves, though the outside history says Simon never truly recovered and went back to what he was doing.

When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands he may receive the Holy Ghost. Simon had the spirits of covetousness, envy, preeminence, and vainglory; he had held status as the great power of God, and when he lost it those spirits rose up in him and he wanted to buy back what he had, thinking, I have the money, I will pay you for what you have.

Peter said, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of the Most High may be purchased with money; thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter, for thy heart is not right. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness and pray, for I perceive thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. The gall of bitterness is resentment and bitterness of spirit. Simon became jealous because the signs the Most High worked through the apostles overshadowed what the people had known him for. That thing did not come overnight; he fed envy, preeminence, vainglory, and covetousness day by day until the roots of bitterness took hold and bound him, and he became a prisoner of his own mind, trapped and sinning. This is why, when people come into the truth, some who had status, fame, or money as celebrities, pastors, or deacons have to come up as a member and clean themselves. Some get jealous, hold on to the envy, and try to bring different doctrines to sway members away, the same spirit of bitterness that moved the Pharisees to kill Christ because the disciples came from nowhere, spoke more eloquently, and went to the scriptures better without the status.

Then Simon answered, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me. And when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

The angel of the Lord told Philip, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went, and behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge of all her treasure and had come to Jerusalem to worship. People say this proves Philip went to the heathen Ethiopians, but this eunuch was a Jew, part of the remnant of Israel scattered in Ethiopia, in Kush, during the Babylonian and Persian captivity. That is why Christians confuse the Ethiopian eunuch; they do not understand Bible prophecy or Bible history. Candace was a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe, and the queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.

The eunuch was returning, sitting in his chariot, reading Esaias the prophet, and the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join thyself to this chariot. Philip ran and heard him read Isaiah and asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? The eunuch answered, How can I, except some man should guide me, and desired Philip to come up and sit with him. Notice the humility of the brother. Rather than making his own assumptions, he admitted he did not understand. Some brothers and sisters lack that humility, claiming, I always knew I was Israel, or, the Most High spoke to me while I was in my sins, rather than saying, This is the first time I heard this, teach me. You had to be taught this Bible to know this Bible; the Most High is not just going to hand it to you out of nowhere. Expressing that you do not know keeps you in a low state and away from the spirit of preeminence and vainglory.

The place of the scripture he read was Isaiah: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth; in his humiliation his judgment was taken away, and who shall declare his generation, for his life is taken from the earth. The eunuch asked Philip, Of whom speaketh the prophet this, of himself or of some other man? He did not know, so rather than assume or give his own interpretation, he asked. That is how you should handle what you do not know: write it down and ask, rather than making an assumption and teaching others, which is how heresies come into the body. Then Philip opened his mouth, began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus, because Philip had the Holy Ghost, wisdom, and understanding, having learned under the feet of the apostles.

As they went on their way they came to a certain water, and the eunuch said, See, here is water, what doth hinder me to be baptized? Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. He answered, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and he commanded the chariot to stand still, and they went down both into the water, and Philip baptized him. This seems to contradict everything taught earlier about Christ's baptism not being water. Philip baptized the eunuch in water because, like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism; John understood his own place and told his disciples to follow Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more, and he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through he preached in all the cities till he came to Caesarea. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,
And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.
And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.
And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.
For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.
Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
(For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

cases.name: The scribes and Pharisees
cases.charge: Shutting up the kingdom against men; devouring widows' houses; tithing mint and omitting judgment, mercy and faith; whited sepulchres
cases.summary: They sat in Moses' seat and were to be heard; their works were not to be followed. Eight woes in Matthew 23 name the crimes, and the sentence at the end gathers all the righteous blood from Abel to Zacharias on that generation: your house is left unto you desolate.
cases.offense: They bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers. Ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men. Ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer. Ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith. Ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones. Ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
cases.judgment: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell? Behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. Forty years later the house was.

entries.commentary: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works, for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and lay them on men's shoulders, but will not move them with one of their fingers.

All their works they do for to be seen of men. They love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the markets. He that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Woe unto you: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. They devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer, and shall receive the greater damnation. There is a lesson in what they would not do. Where leadership provokes a man to works and he finds himself falling behind, he should take it to heart, because telling people who they are without putting in the labour yields no fruit.

They compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Their rules about swearing by the gold rather than the temple, and by the gift rather than the altar, are called out as blindness: the temple sanctifies the gold and the altar sanctifies the gift.

They pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin and have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

They make clean the outside of the cup and platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Cleanse first that which is within. They are likened unto whited sepulchres, beautiful outward but within full of dead men's bones. Outwardly they appear righteous unto men, but within are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

They build the tombs of the prophets and say they would not have shed their blood, and by saying it they witness against themselves that they are the children of them which killed the prophets. Upon them comes all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias. This is the plainest speaking in the gospel. Christ was no soft man with these teachers of the law who did not believe it.
O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples. He gives them the words: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

The friend at midnight will not rise because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth. Importunity is persistence to the point of annoyance. The man kept knocking, and the man inside gave him enough that he would not come back.

Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. The parable before it is the point: prayer is not said once and left. There is persistence in it, and there is action behind it, because the man in the parable was standing at the door. If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
He casts out a devil, and it was dumb, and when the devil was gone out the dumb spake, and the people wondered. Others said he cast out devils through Beelzebub.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges. But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace; but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, he taketh from him all his armour and divideth his spoils. He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

The unclean spirit returns and finds the house swept and garnished, and takes seven other spirits more wicked than himself. The house was clean and empty. There was no stronger one dwelling in it, and that is why what came back could enter, and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
A woman blesses the womb that bare him, and he answers, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it. He turned honour away from the mother and onto the keeping of the word.

This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet. The queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and a greater than Solomon is here. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and a greater than Jonas is here. Men came a long way for less than what these would not cross the room for.

The light of the body is the eye: when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness. One lamp lights a whole room, and put out, the whole room is dark. An eye fixed on the word fills the man with light; an eye that goes looking in dark places fills the whole man, thoughts and judgments together, with darkness.

Ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness. Ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and ye are as graves which appear not.

One of the lawyers says, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also, and is answered with a woe of his own. Ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers. Ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them, so ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers. The blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, shall be required of this generation. Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
The scribes and Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him. From that point they were done with him.

Woe to Ariel, the city where David dwelt; Ariel means lion of God, and this is spoken to Israel, to Jerusalem. Year to year they add and kill sacrifices, yet He will distress Ariel with heaviness and sorrow. He will encamp against her round about and lay siege, bringing the nations around because of Israel's sins, and she shall be brought down to speak low out of the ground, her voice like one that hath a familiar spirit whispering out of the dust.

The multitude of her strangers shall be like small dust and the terrible ones as chaff that passes away suddenly; she shall be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire, for Israel is contending against the Most High as well as the nations He brings. The multitude of nations that fight against Ariel shall be as a dream of a night vision: like a hungry man who dreams he eats but awakes empty, or a thirsty man who dreams he drinks but awakes faint. The nations dream of destroying Israel, but it shall not come to pass, though it will still be like a nightmare to His people. -

They are drunken but not with wine; their spiritual eyes are closed in a deep sleep of blindness, unable to see the things of the Bible. Before coming to the truth many thought Esau was actually white, until the scriptures showed by his description that he is red, showing how deep the spiritual sleep runs. The vision is become as the words of a book that is sealed: delivered to the learned who says he cannot read it because it is sealed, and to the unlearned who says he is not learned. Today's pastors say Revelation is still sealed, but it is sealed only to them, not to the righteous; many learn only how to mimic and perform from the television.

This people draw near with their mouth and honour Him with their lips but have removed their heart far from Him; they praise God but when [Deuteronomy 22:5](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v5) comes out they will not do it, for their fear toward Him is taught by the precepts of men, by the oppressors. Therefore He will do a marvellous work, and the wisdom of their wise men, the oppressors and mainly Esau, shall perish. Woe to them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Most High and work in the dark saying, Who seeth us? Their turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay, for the Most High is setting His people back in order, turning right side up what Esau turned upside down. -

Yet a little while and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field; in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and the deaf are Israel, in a spiritual deep sleep now beginning to wake and hear the word of God rightly. The eyes of the blind shall see out of their obscurity, and the blind are Israel, like the obscurity of thinking Esau is white when he is red; the meek shall increase their joy in the Most High. -

The poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel, the poor in spirit, which is us; the terrible one and the scorner, Esau, is brought to naught and consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off, including Israelites who love the oppressor with all their heart. Concerning the house of Jacob, the Most High who redeemed Abraham says Jacob shall not be ashamed nor his face wax pale; when he sees his children they shall sanctify His name and fear the God of Israel, and they that erred in spirit shall come to understanding and they that murmured shall learn doctrine. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

verses.text: Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples,
Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:
All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.
For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.
Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,
And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?

Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:
That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
And the Lord said unto him, Now do ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.
Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without make that which is within also?
But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.
But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them are not aware of them.
Then answered one of the lawyers, and said unto him, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also.
And he said, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
Woe unto you! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and ye build their sepulchres.
Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:
That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.
Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.

Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:

Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.

cases.name: The traders in the temple
cases.charge: Making the house of prayer a den of thieves
cases.summary: Twice Christ found the temple court full of those that sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting. He made a scourge of small cords, drove them out, poured out the changers' money, overthrew the tables, and would not suffer any man to carry a vessel through the temple.
cases.offense: Isaiah had called it a house of prayer for all people; Jeremiah had asked, is this house become a den of robbers in your eyes? The trade occupied the court of the Gentiles, the only place the nations could pray, and did it, on the gospel's account, for profit under the priests' patronage.
cases.judgment: Driven out with a whip. The chief priests sought how they might destroy him for it. Zechariah's last verse hangs over the scene: in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite, the trafficker, in the house of the Lord of hosts.

entries.commentary: At the marriage in Cana his mother tells him they have no wine, and though he answers, Mine hour is not yet come, she tells the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. She knew what he could do. The governor of the feast says every man sets forth good wine first, and the worse afterward, but thou hast kept the good wine until now. What was made was better than what had been served. This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

He made a scourge of small cords and drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and the oxen, poured out the changers' money and overthrew the tables. He drove grown men out with a whip. Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise. No man had business trading in there at the passover. His disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up. He was fulfilling what David had written.

They ask what sign he shews. Asking after signs was their habit, and the epistle names it. Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. It went over their heads, and they answered with the forty and six years of building. He spake of the temple of his body. The Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, and the body itself is called a temple in the scriptures. The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.
Many believed when they saw the miracles, but he did not commit himself unto them, for he knew all men, and needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.

He rides into Jerusalem on an ass and a colt, and the multitudes spread their garments and branches in the way, crying Hosanna to the son of David. All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet.

He casts out them that sold and bought in the temple and overthrows the tables of the moneychangers, saying, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.
The chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did and were sore displeased. The works themselves angered them.

The fig tree with leaves and no fruit withers away at his word, and the disciples marvel at how soon it withered. If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and it shall be done.

Asked by what authority he does these things, he asks them first whether the baptism of John was from heaven or of men. They reason among themselves and will not answer, because either answer condemns them, so he does not answer them either.

Of the two sons, the one who said I will not and afterward repented and went is the one that did the will of his father. The publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you. These were teachers of the law who were not doers of it. John came in the way of righteousness and they believed him not, and when they had seen it they repented not afterward that they might believe him.

The householder sends servants for the fruits of his vineyard and they are beaten, killed and stoned; last of all he sends his son, and the husbandmen kill him to seize the inheritance. The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner. This is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes. Therefore the kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof. The chief priests and Pharisees perceived that he spake of them. --- Topics: [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
Two disciples are sent for the colt whereon never man sat, and the multitude spread their garments and branches in the way, crying Hosanna.
Seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he finds nothing but leaves, and says, No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever.

He casts out them that sold and bought in the temple, overthrows the tables of the moneychangers and the seats of them that sold doves, and will not suffer that any man carry a vessel through the temple. Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves. He did not lead those men out gently. This is not the soft figure preached in the churches; where the law was concerned he acted, and the scribes and chief priests sought how they might destroy him, for they feared him.

The fig tree is dried up from the roots, and the word given is, Have faith in God. Whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and shall not doubt in his heart, he shall have whatsoever he saith. When ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any, that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.

Asked by what authority he does these things, he answers with a question about the baptism of John, and they will not answer it, so neither does he answer them. They came at him again and again, and there was no way to trap him. He was ready in season and out of season.

Keep judgment and do justice, for His salvation is near to come and His righteousness to be revealed. Blessed is the man that does this and lays hold on it, that keeps the Sabbath from polluting it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.

The son of the stranger that has joined himself to the Most High is not to say the Lord has utterly separated him from His people, and the eunuch is not to say he is a dry tree. These strangers spoken of are Israel; the whole passage is the Most High speaking to Israel. To the eunuchs that keep His Sabbaths and take hold of His covenant, He gives a place and a name in His house better than of sons and daughters, an everlasting name that will not be cut off. The sons of the stranger that join themselves to Him, keep the Sabbath, and take hold of His covenant, He will bring to His holy mountain and make joyful in His house of prayer; their offerings will be accepted, for His house will be called a house of prayer for all people. The Lord God who gathers the outcasts of Israel says He will yet gather others to Him besides those already gathered.

All the beasts of the field and forest are called to devour. Judgment is turned on the failed leadership. The watchmen are blind and ignorant, dumb dogs that cannot bark, sleeping and loving to slumber. They are greedy dogs that never have enough, shepherds that cannot understand. They all look to their own way, every one for his gain, saying they will fetch wine and fill themselves with strong drink, and tomorrow will be as this day and much more abundant.

The word came to Jeremiah to stand in the gate of the Lord's house and proclaim to all Judah that enter in to worship. Amend your ways and your doings and He will cause you to dwell in this place, which ties back to how our iniquities turn away the good things, for as long as we keep the law He will bless us.

Trust not in lying words, saying, The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, as though the building itself would save them. If they truly amend their ways, execute judgment between a man and his neighbor, oppress not the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, shed not innocent blood, and walk not after other gods, then He will let them dwell in the land He gave their fathers.

They trust in lying words that cannot profit while they steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal. They walk after other gods and then come and stand before Him in the house called by His name, saying they are delivered to do all these abominations; has this house become a den of robbers in their eyes.

Go now to Shiloh where He first set His name and see what He did to it for the wickedness of His people Israel; we cannot always blame the other nations, for we did these things while still in our own land. Because they did all these works and He spoke to them rising up early, but they heard not, and He called but they answered not.

Therefore He will do to this house, called by His name and trusted in, as He did to Shiloh. He will cast them out of His sight as He cast out their brethren, the whole seed of Ephraim, the northern kingdom.

Pray not for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer nor make intercession, for He will not hear. The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough to make cakes to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke Him to anger.

Do they provoke Him to anger, or do they not rather provoke themselves to the confusion of their own faces. His anger and fury shall be poured out upon this place, upon man and beast, the trees and the fruit, and it shall burn and not be quenched.

Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices and eat flesh, for He spoke not to their fathers concerning burnt offerings when He brought them out of Egypt. This one thing He commanded them: obey My voice, and I will be your God and ye shall be My people, and walk in all the ways He commanded, that it may be well with them.

They hearkened not nor inclined their ear but walked in the counsels and imagination of their evil heart and went backward, not forward. He sent all His servants the prophets daily, rising up early, yet they hearkened not, hardened their neck, and did worse than their fathers.

The Most High tells Jeremiah he shall speak all these words to them, but they will not hearken, and call to them, but they will not answer. This is a nation that obeyeth not His voice nor receiveth correction; truth is perished and cut off from their mouth.

Cut off thine hair, O Jerusalem, and take up a lamentation, for the Most High has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath. The children of Judah set their abominations in the house called by His name and built the high places of Tophet to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, which points to the abortions of today, a thing He never commanded.

The days come when it shall be called the valley of slaughter, for they shall bury in Tophet till there is no more room. The carcasses shall be meat for the fowls and beasts with none to fray them away, and He will cause to cease the voice of mirth, gladness, the bridegroom, and the bride, for the land shall be desolate. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee. I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled, and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city. Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle. His feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley. Ye shall flee to the valley of the mountains, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with thee.

It shall come to pass in that day, that the light shall not be clear, nor dark: but it shall be one day which shall be known to the Lord, not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light. Living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be. The Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one. All the land shall be turned as a plain; and it shall be lifted up, and inhabited in her place; and men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.

This shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth. A great tumult from the Lord shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbour. Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the heathen round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance.

Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles. Whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain. This shall be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles. In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD; and every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the Lord of hosts. In that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

Save me, O God, for the waters are come in unto my soul; I sink in deep mire where there is no standing, come into deep waters where the floods overflow me. I am weary of my crying, my throat is dry, my eyes fail while I wait for my God. They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head.
O God, Thou knowest my foolishness, and my sins are not hid from Thee. Nothing is hid from God. Whether it be good or evil, He brings every secret thing into judgment. -

Let not them that wait on Thee be ashamed for my sake, nor those that seek Thee be confounded, O God of Israel. For Thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face. I am become a stranger unto my brethren and an alien unto my mother's children, for the zeal of Thine house hath eaten me up. The scripture says blessed are you when they hate you, mistreat you, and speak evil of you. We should look at going through these conditions and know that according to the scriptures we are blessed. It may not look like it, but this is one of the ways you know you are on the right track, because the world hates what we teach because they love their evil deeds.

When I wept and chastened my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach; I made sackcloth my garment and became a proverb to them. Just like it says in [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), this is how it feels to be under the curses, to be a proverb and an astonishment and a byword. David was like, Lord, I am a king, this is not supposed to be happening. They that sit in the gate speak against me, and I was the song of the drunkards.

But my prayer is unto Thee, O Lord, in an acceptable time; in the multitude of Thy mercy hear me, in the truth of Thy salvation. We may think the Lord does not hear us. That is why in the fullness of time God sent His son. In the Christian church they say He may not come when you want Him, but He is always on time; the Lord comes in an acceptable time. Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink; let me be delivered from them that hate me and out of the deep waters. Deliver me from the haters, and let not the deep swallow me up.

Hear me, O Lord, for Thy lovingkindness is good; turn unto me according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies, and hide not Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble. When we call on God we want Him to hear us. It is not pleasant to call on God and have Him tell you, as in [Hosea 5:15](/bible/hosea/5#v15), that He will return to His place till you acknowledge your offense. Hear me speedily; draw nigh unto my soul and redeem it; deliver me because of mine enemies. -

Thou hast known my reproach, my shame, and my dishonour; mine adversaries are all before Thee. Reproach hath broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness. Do not give yourself to heaviness, because heaviness and sorrow have killed many people. Through faith and comfort of the scriptures you will have hope, because in this walk you look to this person and that person for comfort and find none. We have to deliver our own soul by our own righteousness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none. They gave me gall for my meat, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. This goes into Christ.

Let their table become a snare before them, and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap. You can read about this in Isaiah 28: the word became precept upon precept and became a snare and a trap unto them, and they went backwards, because we bring out the understanding of the Bible but people do not want to hear it. You think you are a Christian and good with God going to church every Sunday, but it does not work like that. Let their eyes be darkened that they see not.

Pour out Thine indignation upon them, and let Thy wrathful anger take hold of them; let their habitation be desolate. This is why blindness happened to the southern Kingdom leadership that forsook Christ; their eyes were darkened and their table became a snare. You read about all this in [Romans 11](/bible/romans/11). Add iniquity unto their iniquity, and let them not come into Thy righteousness; let them be blotted out of the book of the living and not be written with the righteous. That is a heavy statement. -

But I am poor and sorrowful; let Thy salvation, O God, set me up on high. I will praise the name of God with a song and magnify Him with thanksgiving. This shall please the Lord better than an ox or bullock, because He loves obedience more than sacrifice. The humble shall see this and be glad, for the Lord heareth the poor and despiseth not His prisoners.

Let the heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moveth therein. When you read the Three Holy Children, all the creation praises God. For God will save Zion and will build the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and have it in possession. Only the oppressed need to be saved, and that is us. The seed of His servants shall inherit it, and they that love His name shall dwell therein. Those that keep the commandments are going to dwell there. -
