Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. The word is to speak comfortably to Jerusalem and cry that her warfare is accomplished and her iniquity pardoned, for she has received of the Lord's hand double for all her sins. The voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord goes into the prophecy of John, the spirit of Elijah, with every valley exalted, every mountain and hill made low, and the crooked made straight so the glory of the Lord shall be revealed and all flesh shall see it together. All flesh is grass and its goodliness as the flower of the field; the grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever. It compares our lives to the flowers of the field: we are born, we grow, we die, and go back into the ground, but the word of the Most High is forever. -

Zion is told to get up to the high mountain and lift up her voice with strength, not afraid, to say to the cities of Judah, Behold your God. The Lord God will come with a strong hand, his arm ruling for him, his reward with him and his work before him. He shall feed his flock like a shepherd, gather the lambs with his arm and carry them in his bosom, and gently lead those that are with young.

The Most High measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, meted out heaven with a span, and weighed the mountains in scales. No one directed his Spirit or taught him counsel, judgment, knowledge, or the way of understanding. All nations are as a drop of a bucket and counted as the small dust of the balance. Lebanon is not sufficient to burn nor its beasts sufficient for the offering; all nations before him are as nothing, counted less than nothing and vanity. -

To whom then will you liken God, or what likeness compare to him? The workman melts a graven image, the goldsmith spreads it with gold and casts silver chains. He that is too poor for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot and seeks a skilled workman to prepare a graven image that will not be moved. Seeking a tree is the spirit of Nimrod that our people worshipped back then; instead of the tree itself, he made a graven image of the tree.

Have you not known, have you not heard from the beginning? It is he that sits upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants are as grasshoppers; he stretches out the heavens as a curtain and spreads them as a tent to dwell in. The circle of the earth is the two-dimensional shape of a sphere. He brings the princes to nothing and makes the judges of the earth as vanity; they are not planted or sown before he blows upon them and the whirlwind takes them away as stubble. Lift up your eyes on high and behold who created these things, bringing out their host by number and calling them all by name; by the greatness of his might, not one fails.

Why does Jacob say his way is hid from the Lord and his judgment passed over from his God? The everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth, faints not, is not weary, and there is no searching of his understanding. He gives power to the faint and increases strength to them that have no might. Even the youths faint and the young men utterly fall, but they that wait upon the Lord renew their strength. This goes into Israel receiving the kingdom and the power of the Lord. Everybody may get weary and faint, but the Lord does not, and those that trust in him mount up with wings as eagles, run and are not weary, walk and do not faint.

And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law,

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:

Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people;

And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him.

John's disciples ask, Art thou he that should come? and in that same hour he cured many, and answered by the works: the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

verses.text: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.
The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.
Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.

Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:
Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.
For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant;

Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.

cases.name: The Samaritan leper who returned
cases.charge: One of ten: turning back to glorify God with a loud voice, and giving thanks at his feet
cases.summary: Ten lepers stood afar off and cried for mercy, and were sent to shew themselves to the priests as the law commands. As they went they were cleansed. Nine kept going. One, a Samaritan, turned back, fell on his face at his feet and gave thanks. He alone was told, thy faith hath made thee whole.
cases.offense: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. The other nine had obeyed the letter, going to the priests; this one came back to the one who had sent them.
cases.judgment: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole. Ten were cleansed of leprosy; one went home whole.

entries.commentary: This is the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing. The leper stays outside the camp; the priest goes forth out of the camp to him and looks whether the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper. The priest does not heal the plague; he examines the man after the healing and carries out the cleansing the Most High commanded.

For him that is to be cleansed the priest commands two birds alive and clean, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop. One bird is killed in an earthen vessel over running water. The living bird, with the cedar wood, the scarlet, and the hyssop, is dipped in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water; the priest sprinkles him that is to be cleansed seven times, pronounces him clean, and lets the living bird loose into the open field.

He that is to be cleansed washes his clothes, shaves off all his hair, and washes himself in water, and comes into the camp; but he tarries abroad out of his tent seven days. On the seventh day he shaves all his hair off his head, his beard, and his eyebrows, washes his clothes and his flesh in water, and is clean.

On the eighth day he brings two he lambs without blemish, one ewe lamb of the first year without blemish, three tenth deals of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering, and one log of oil. The priest that makes him clean presents him with these things before the Most High at the door of the tabernacle. One he lamb is offered for a trespass offering with the log of oil, waved for a wave offering, and slain in the holy place: as the sin offering is the priest's, so is the trespass offering; it is most holy.

The priest takes of the blood of the trespass offering and puts it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot. Of the log of oil the priest pours into his own left hand, sprinkles of it with his finger seven times before the Lord, and puts oil upon the ear, the thumb, and the toe, upon the blood of the trespass offering; the remnant of the oil he pours upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make an atonement for him before the Lord.

The priest then offers the sin offering to make an atonement for him that is to be cleansed from his uncleanness, kills the burnt offering, and offers the burnt offering and the meat offering upon the altar; the priest makes an atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

If he be poor and cannot get so much, the law makes provision: one lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, one tenth deal of fine flour mingled with oil, a log of oil, and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, such as he is able to get, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. The same order is kept for the poor man: the blood of the trespass offering upon the right ear, the right thumb, and the right great toe, the oil sprinkled seven times and put upon the same places, and the rest of the oil upon his head. This is the law of him in whom is the plague of leprosy, whose hand is not able to get that which pertaineth to his cleansing.

The Most High tells Moses and Aaron that when Israel comes into the land of Canaan, and he puts the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of their possession, the owner shall come and tell the priest, saying, It seemeth to me there is as it were a plague in the house. The priest commands that the house be emptied before he goes in, that all that is in it be not made unclean; then he looks on the plague, and if it be in the walls with hollow strakes, greenish or reddish, in sight lower than the wall, he shuts up the house seven days. If at the seventh day the plague be spread in the walls, the stones in which the plague is are taken away and cast into an unclean place without the city; the house is scraped within round about, the dust poured out without the city into an unclean place, and other stones and other mortar are put in their place.

If the plague come again and break out in the house after the stones were taken away and the house scraped and plastered, the priest looks, and if the plague be spread, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean. He breaks down the house, the stones of it, the timber, and all the mortar, and carries them forth out of the city into an unclean place. He that goes into the house while it is shut up is unclean until the even, and he that lies or eats in the house washes his clothes.

If the priest comes in and looks, and the plague hath not spread in the house after it was plastered, the priest pronounces the house clean, because the plague is healed. The house is cleansed the same way as the leper: two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop; one bird killed in an earthen vessel over running water, the house sprinkled seven times, and the living bird let go out of the city into the open fields; so he makes an atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.

The chapter closes the summary: this is the law for all manner of plague of leprosy and scall, for the leprosy of a garment and of a house, for a rising, a scab, and a bright spot, to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law of leprosy.

David charges his own soul and all that is within him to bless the holy name of the Most High and to forget not His benefits. Those benefits are named: He forgives all iniquities, heals diseases, redeems life from destruction, crowns with lovingkindness and tender mercies, and renews the youth like the eagle's. The Most High executes righteousness and judgment for all that are oppressed. Hear that clearly: it does not say for all people, it says for all that are oppressed.

He made known His ways unto Moses, His acts unto the children of Israel. Look at that: His acts unto the children of Israel, not to every nation. When Israel fled Egypt there were oppressed nations who came out with us; the Bible calls them strangers. But the ways of the Most High were made known to Moses and Israel. -

The Most High is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, plenteous in mercy. He has not dealt with us after our sins nor rewarded us according to our iniquities. This is heavy because Christ came to forgive Israel of their sins. That mercy and grace is to Israel, and it is not so that we could continue in sin. As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust. -

Man's days are as grass and as a flower of the field; the wind passes over it and it is gone. But the mercy of the Most High is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear Him, and His righteousness unto children's children. This is why we must teach our children in every generation, so they receive that same mercy. The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word. -

The Most High has prepared His throne in the heavens and His kingdom rules over all. The angels that excel in strength bless Him by doing His commandments and hearkening to the voice of His word. All His hosts and works in every place of His dominion bless Him; and David returns to charge his own soul: bless the Lord.

cases.name: The widow and her two mites
cases.charge: Casting in all that she had, even all her living
cases.summary: He sat over against the treasury and watched the rich cast in much. A poor widow threw in two mites, which make a farthing. He called his disciples to see it, and weighed it against everything else in the box: she had cast in more than they all.
cases.offense: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing. The rich cast in of their abundance; she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. No one had asked her for it.
cases.judgment: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: for all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. Her gift is the standard by which every other gift in the temple that day was found smaller, and it is read in every generation since.

entries.commentary: The vineyard is let out to husbandmen who beat and kill the servants sent for the fruit, and at last kill the son to seize the inheritance. The vineyard is the nation; the servants are the prophets, who were beaten, stoned and killed, and who all came with the same message. Then the son came with that message and they killed him too. The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner. They knew he had spoken the parable against them.

The Pharisees and Herodians come with flattery first: we know that thou art true, and carest for no man. Then comes the trap about tribute to Caesar. That is still how men come to this word. They will say they like what is being said and then set the thing they disagree with beside it. Knowing their hypocrisy, he calls for the penny and answers by the image on it: Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. They were careful of Caesar's law while mishandling the priesthood.

The Sadducees bring the seven brethren and one wife, and are answered, Ye therefore do greatly err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God. The law they built the question on was for inheritance, so that a dead man's name and portion would not be put out of Israel. When they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage. A woman is bound by that law while her husband lives, and in the resurrection there is no more dying. He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living.

The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. The second is, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these. Loving him is keeping his commandments, and loving your neighbour as yourself means holding him to them as you hold yourself, because the wages of sin is death and you do not want to see your brother die. The scribe answered discreetly, and was told, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God, and no man after that durst ask him any question.

How say the scribes that Christ is the son of David? David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand. Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces, and the chief seats in the synagogues. What they wanted was the recognition of men.
The rich cast in much, but the poor widow threw in two mites, and he says she cast in more than they all, for they cast in of their abundance, but she of her want did cast in all that she had.

Observe the month of Abib and keep the passover unto the Most High, for in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night. Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, even the bread of affliction, because thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste, that thou mayest remember the day all the days of thy life. Nothing of the flesh sacrificed the first day at even, the lamb, may remain all night until the morning. The passover may not be sacrificed within any of thy gates, but only at the place which the Lord thy God shall choose to place his name there, at even, at the going down of the sun. Six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a solemn assembly and no work: the first day of the passover is a sabbath, and the seventh day of the passover is a sabbath.

Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee: begin to number the seven weeks from such time as thou beginnest to put the sickle to the corn, and keep the feast of weeks unto the Most High with a tribute of a freewill offering according as the Lord thy God hath blessed thee. Another name for the feast of weeks is the feast of firstfruits: you count seven weeks and then a day, fifty days, which is Pentecost. Rejoice before the Most High, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow; and remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt.

Thou shalt observe the feast of tabernacles seven days, after that thou hast gathered in thy corn and thy wine. Rejoice in thy feast, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates. Seven days shalt thou keep a solemn feast in the place which the Lord shall choose, because the Most High shall bless thee in all thine increase and in all the works of thine hands; therefore thou shalt surely rejoice.

Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Most High in the place which he shall choose: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. They shall not appear before the Lord empty, meaning they have to come with their sacrifices: every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee.

Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, throughout thy tribes, and they shall judge the people with just judgment. There is nothing new under the sun: when you see judges and officers among us today, know that we are following the things that are written within this book. Thou shalt not wrest judgment, thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift, for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise and pervert the words of the righteous. That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live and inherit the land.

Thou shalt not plant thee a grove of any trees near unto the altar of the Lord thy God; yet these pastors set up Christmas trees inside the church, directly against this law. Neither shalt thou set thee up any image, which the Lord thy God hateth.

cases.name: The woman with the issue of blood
cases.charge: Believing that if she might but touch his clothes she should be whole
cases.summary: Twelve years unclean under the law, spent to her last penny on physicians and worse for it, she came behind him in the press and touched the border of his garment. The flow dried up in the same hour. He turned and made her say it before everyone, and gave her the verdict in front of them: thy faith hath made thee whole.
cases.offense: A certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, and had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse, when she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. When she saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared unto him before all the people for what cause she had touched him.
cases.judgment: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague. Under the law her touch should have made him unclean; instead his made her clean, and she went home with the word that did it.

entries.commentary: He went throughout every city and village preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God, and with him the twelve, and certain women which had been healed, who ministered unto him of their substance.
A sower went out to sow his seed: some fell by the way side, some upon a rock, some among thorns, and other fell on good ground and bare fruit an hundredfold.

The seed is the word of God. Those by the way side hear, then the devil taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved. They on the rock receive the word with joy and have no root, and in time of temptation fall away. That among thorns is choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life. That on the good ground are they which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.

No man lighteth a candle and covereth it. Nothing is secret that shall not be made manifest. Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.
My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.

The storm fills the ship and they wake him, and he rebukes the wind and the raging of the water, and there was a calm. Where is your faith? They wondered, saying, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him.

The man of the Gadarenes had devils a long time, wore no clothes, and abode in the tombs, and could not be held by chains. What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many devils were entered into him. They enter the swine and the herd runs violently down a steep place into the lake. The man is found sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind, and is sent home to shew how great things God had done unto him.

The woman with an issue of blood twelve years, who had spent all her living upon physicians, touches the border of his garment and immediately is healed. Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me. Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.

Word comes that Jairus' daughter is dead, and he answers, Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole. He puts them all out, takes her by the hand, and calls, Maid, arise. Her spirit came again, and he commanded to give her meat. These chapters are one work of power after another, and every one of them turns on faith. It is by faith and by works that healing comes to a man, and not by touching him with the hand.

When any man hath a running issue out of his flesh, because of his issue he is unclean, whether his flesh run with his issue or be stopped from his issue. Every bed whereon he lies and every thing whereon he sits is unclean. Whoever touches his bed, sits where he sat, touches his flesh, or is touched by him before he has rinsed his hands, washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even; the same goes for his spittle and his saddle. The vessel of earth that he touches shall be broken, and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water.

When he that hath an issue is cleansed of his issue, he numbers to himself seven days for his cleansing, washes his clothes, and bathes his flesh in running water, and shall be clean. On the eighth day he takes two turtledoves or two young pigeons and comes before the Lord unto the door of the tabernacle, and gives them unto the priest; the priest offers the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and makes an atonement for him before the Lord for his issue.

If any man's seed of copulation go out from him, he washes all his flesh in water and is unclean until the even; every garment and every skin whereon is the seed is washed with water and unclean until the even. The woman also with whom a man lies with seed of copulation: they both bathe themselves in water and are unclean until the even.

When a woman has an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she is put apart seven days for her separation, and whosoever toucheth her is unclean until the even. Every thing that she lies upon or sits upon in her separation is unclean; whoever touches her bed or any thing she sat upon washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even. If any man lie with her at all, and her flowers be upon him, he is unclean seven days, and all the bed whereon he lies is unclean.

If a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation, or if it run beyond the time of her separation, all the days of the issue of her uncleanness are as the days of her separation: she is unclean. Every bed she lies on and every thing she sits upon in those days is as the uncleanness of her separation, and whosoever touches those things washes his clothes, bathes in water, and is unclean until the even.

When she is cleansed of her issue, she numbers to herself seven days, and after that she shall be clean. On the eighth day she takes two turtles or two young pigeons and brings them unto the priest to the door of the tabernacle; the priest offers the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and makes an atonement for her before the Lord for the issue of her uncleanness.

The purpose of the whole chapter is stated plainly: thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not in their uncleanness when they defile the tabernacle of the Most High that is among them. This is the law of him that hath an issue, of him whose seed goeth from him, of her that is sick of her flowers, of him and her that have issues, and of him that lieth with her that is unclean. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

verses.text: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.
And it came to pass, that while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course,
According to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord.
And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the time of incense.
And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
And when Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.
For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother’s womb.
And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God.

And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months, saying,
Thus hath the Lord dealt with me in the days wherein he looked on me, to take away my reproach among men.
Now Elisabeth’s full time came that she should be delivered; and she brought forth a son.
And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her.
And it came to pass, that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child; and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John.
And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name.
And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called.
And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.
And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, and praised God.
And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judea.
And all they that heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying, What manner of child shall this be! And the hand of the Lord was with him.
And his father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Ghost, and prophesied, saying,
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people,
And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David;
As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began:
That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us;
To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant;
The oath which he sware to our father Abraham,
That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear,
In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.
And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways;
To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins,
Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us,
To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his shewing unto Israel.
Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.

cases.name: Alexander the coppersmith
cases.charge: Doing Paul much evil; greatly withstanding his words
cases.summary: Named in Paul's last letter as a man to beware of. Whether he is the Alexander delivered to Satan with Hymenaeus for blasphemy, or the Alexander the Jews put forward in the Ephesian theatre, the sentence Paul leaves is the law's own: the Lord reward him according to his works.
cases.offense: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words. In the first letter to Timothy, Hymenaeus and Alexander had put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck, and were delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme.
cases.judgment: The Lord reward him according to his works. Paul does not curse him in his own name; he cites the judgment already written for every man, and leaves Alexander under it. Timothy was told to beware of him, which is the church's share of the sentence: a man marked and avoided.

entries.commentary: Truly David's soul waits upon God, from whom comes his salvation; He only is his rock and salvation and defense, so he shall not be greatly moved. He rebukes those who imagine mischief against a man, who shall be slain like a bowing wall and a tottering fence; they consult to cast him down from his excellency, delight in lies, and bless with their mouth but curse inwardly.

David tells his own soul to wait only upon God, for his expectation is from Him; He only is his rock, salvation, defense, glory, and refuge. A lot of us expect things from men and expect people not to let us down. "I expected more of you," "I expected you to be this way," and that is your problem. Let your expectations be of God, as David's expectations were of God. You cannot change anybody, but God can. Trust in Him at all times, pour out your heart before Him, for God is a refuge for us.

Men of low degree are vanity and men of high degree are a lie; laid in the balance they are altogether lighter than vanity. Trust not in oppression, become not vain in robbery, and if riches increase, set not your heart upon them. God has spoken once, twice have we heard this: that power belongs to God, and to Him belongs mercy, for He renders to every man according to his work. Expect great things from the Most High and you do great things yourself. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom)

cases.name: Ananias and Sapphira
cases.charge: Lying to the Holy Spirit about a gift
cases.summary: A couple sold property and gave part of the proceeds to the apostles while claiming it was the whole. The gift was never required; the lie was the offense. Each fell dead as it was exposed.
cases.offense: They agreed together to keep back part of the price and present the rest as the full amount, a staged generosity meant to buy standing. Peter named it: not a lie to men but to God.
cases.judgment: Ananias fell dead at Peter's word; Sapphira, questioned three hours later and holding to the same story, fell dead as well. Great fear came on the whole church.

entries.commentary: Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession and kept back part of the price, his wife being privy to it, and brought only a portion and laid it at the apostles' feet. This continues from Acts 4: none among the believers lacked, because those who possessed lands or houses sold them, laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man as he had need. The church was the epicenter of the community, where counsel was given and economic and community problems were resolved, the way the black Wall Street towns like Rosewood and Tulsa once kept the dollar circulating among our own people for months before it left. A community is a people with all things in common: common government, common heritage, common interest, and common culture, and the word community itself comes from the root "common." So-called black people today are not yet a community, divided by religion, politics, and color, until they come into the fullness of Christ. Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry; use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation. -

Peter asks why Satan has filled Ananias' heart to lie to the Holy Ghost and keep back part of the price; while it remained it was his own, so he has not lied unto men but unto the Most High. The spirit upon them was covetousness as well as lying; they saw the full value and coveted it, and did not put away lying as the renewed mind requires. To be renewed in the spirit of the mind is to be born again, to reboot the mind and clear out the programming of this world's philosophy, and to speak every man truth with his neighbour, for we are members one of another. Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform. -

Hearing these words, Ananias fell down and gave up the ghost, and the young men wound him up, carried him out, and buried him. This is after the death of Christ, under grace, yet he was put to death for lying and breaking his vow. Grace was never a licence to sin; the wages of sin is death, even now. The christian church hands out a licence to sin by teaching the law is done away and all is covered by grace, and is answerable for the blood in the community when men sin presumptuously believing there are no consequences. Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure. -

About three hours later Sapphira came in, not knowing what was done, and agreed to the same lie; Peter told her the feet of those who buried her husband were at the door, and she fell down and yielded up the ghost and was buried by him, and great fear came upon all the church. She shared his fate because they agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Most High. A wife is meant to be a tower against death and a help meet; had she refused the evil or brought it to the leadership, she could have saved his life, as Abigail did. A wife submits to her husband as unto the Most High, in righteousness, not in wickedness; if he tells her to break the law, she is not to agree with him. Not everyone has the same measure of grace; one man is put to death for a smaller sin while David was spared far greater ones, for grace is given by the measure of the gift of Christ. The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him. -

By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were wrought; they were together in Solomon's porch, believers were the more added, and multitudes brought the sick into the streets on beds and couches that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow them, and they were healed every one. This is the power poured out after they waited in Jerusalem for the Holy Ghost, fulfilling that these signs would follow them that believe. These gifts of healing and tongues were for that time, to introduce the Son of God and prove the power of the Most High on earth; they are not the gifts of today, which is why our people still die of disease no matter what the pastors claim. In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established. -

The high priest and the sect of the Sadducees, filled with indignation, laid hands on the apostles and put them in the common prison, but the angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night and sent them to stand and speak in the temple all the words of this life. Read the lives of the apostles and prophets as a pattern for today: what the forefathers suffered will come again under America, the last kingdom, and worse; if you teach this gospel, prison and loss will come, so you cannot be joined to this world. Prepare for it: set aside a nest so your wife and family are provided for if you are locked up, for they will freeze accounts and take houses; the Most High will help, but you must still prepare. Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat. -

At dawn the apostles entered the temple and taught; when the council sent to the prison the officers found it shut with all safety and the keepers standing, but no man within, and word came that the men they had imprisoned were standing in the temple teaching the people. This is boldness: freed from prison, they did not hide but went straight back to teach. If they lock you up, go right back out, the way those who truly love their people keep returning no matter how many times they are jailed.

The captain and officers brought them without violence, fearing the people would stone them, and the high priest charged them, saying, did we not straitly command you not to teach in this name, yet you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine and intend to bring this man's blood upon us. It is the same charge leveled today: that teaching the truth fills the cities with this doctrine and tries to lay guilt on the accusers, the way they say teaching history is only meant to make them feel guilty.

Peter and the apostles answer that we ought to obey the Most High rather than men; the God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom they slew and hanged on a tree, and exalted him to be a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. Christ came through the loins of David, from Judah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; the law was given to Israel, so repentance from breaking the law is given to Israel. The apostles are his witnesses of these things because their lineage experienced his ministry, death, and miracles; popes and denominations are not witnesses. The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it. -

Cut to the heart, the council took counsel to slay them, no different from religious leaders today who take counsel against the truth, publish books against it, and would sooner hire accusers than correct themselves. Then Gamaliel, a Pharisee and a doctor of the law held in reputation among all the people, stood up and commanded the apostles to be put outside a little space. When men believe the law is done away they hold no morals to restrain them, and will put the teachers to death thinking they do the will of the Most High. -

Gamaliel warns the council to take heed what they do: before these days Theudas rose up boasting himself to be somebody, and about four hundred joined him, but he was slain and his followers scattered to nothing; after him Judas of Galilee drew people in the days of the taxing and also perished, and his followers were dispersed. The record of Josephus tells the same of Theudas, a magician who persuaded a great part of the people that he was a prophet who could divide the river Jordan, until horsemen fell on them, killed many, and beheaded him; examine such men and see what their work comes to. Therefore refrain from these men and let them alone: if this counsel or work be of men it will come to nought, but if it be of the Most High it cannot be overthrown, lest they be found to fight against God. Examine our works the same way: if the teaching reforms the brothers off the streets and restores our people's identity worldwide, it is of the Most High; the more they persecute, lock up, and kill, the faster prophecy is filled toward the number to be sealed, so every move is checkmate.

The council agreed with Gamaliel, and when they had called the apostles and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus and let them go. The apostles departed rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name; that is the level to reach, to rejoice in the beatings, jail, and loss that come with the gospel. Daily in the temple and in every house they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ; this is the pattern, to teach every day on every platform, not once a week. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.

verses.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,
And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.
And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.
And the young men arose, wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him.
And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.
And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much.
Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out.
Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and the young men came in, and found her dead, and, carrying her forth, buried her by her husband.
Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.

cases.name: Ananias the high priest
cases.charge: Commanding Paul to be smitten on the mouth, contrary to the law, while sitting to judge him by the law
cases.summary: Paul had said one sentence to the council when the high priest ordered him struck. Paul answered as a prophet answers: God shall smite thee, thou whited wall; for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law? Then he withdrew the words toward the office, not the man.
cases.offense: Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day. And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth. The law forbids condemning a man before he is heard, and forbids the judge to strike the accused; Ananias did both from the judgment seat.
cases.judgment: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall. Told it was the high priest, he answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people. Scripture records the word spoken and not its performance; the office was honoured, the man was named, and the sentence was left with God.

entries.commentary: If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God. Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day.

If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

The word of the Lord came telling Ezekiel to prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy out of their own hearts. Woe unto the foolish prophets that follow their own spirit and have seen nothing, just like the pastors today who follow the spirit of the white man, the spirit of Esau, Christmas, and all these things, changing our people and giving them a false sense of security that they will get the kingdom of heaven. The prophets are like the foxes in the desert, using craftiness in a ruined and wasted area of Israel to make gain among the people, the same as a well-groomed church in a run-down area of the hood where the pastor makes gain off the people. They have not gone up into the gaps nor made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the Lord, meaning they did not protect Israel from the Lord's wrath the way Moses stood in the gap when we went into idolatry. They have seen vanity and lying divination, saying the Lord sent them when He had not, making Israel hope their lies would be confirmed.

Because they speak vanity and see lies, the Most High is against them; His hand will be upon the prophets that see vanity and divine lies. They shall not be in the assembly of His people, nor written in the writing of the house of Israel, nor enter the land of Israel, meaning they will die in captivity. They have seduced His people with another spirit, saying peace when there is no peace, the way pastors today seduce our people with the spirit of white jesus and not the spirit of the Most High of this Bible. One built a wall and others daubed it with untempered mortar, patchwork upon the wall of Jerusalem, the prophets saying peace and safety while telling the people to build the walls up.

The Most High will rend the wall with a stormy wind in His fury, with an overflowing shower in His anger and great hailstones in His fury to consume it. He will break down the wall daubed with untempered mortar and bring it to the ground so its foundation is discovered, and they shall be consumed in the midst of it and know He is the Lord. He will accomplish His wrath upon the wall and upon them that daubed it, the prophets of Israel which prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her when there was no peace, because of our sins.

Ezekiel is to set his face against the daughters of his people which prophesy out of their own heart, just like the female pastors today who want to prophesy and teach our people and teach the men. Woe to the women that sew pillows to all armholes and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls; the pillows are the wide robe-like openings down the arm and the kerchief is the covering placed on the head. They hunt the souls of the Most High's people and pollute His word among the people, saying God loves everybody and praise white jesus, doing it back then for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread and today for money.

The Most High is against their pillows, wherewith they hunt the souls to make them fly, meaning to fly into sin and wickedness; He will tear them from their arms and let the hunted souls go free. He will use men who keep His commandments to go out and teach the people the proper way and tear them from the arms of these wicked women. He will tear their kerchiefs and deliver His people out of their hand, so they shall be no more in their hand to be hunted, and they shall know He is the Lord.

With lies they made the heart of the righteous sad whom the Most High had not made sad, and strengthened the hands of the wicked that he should not return from his wicked way by promising him life. That is what happens today: the righteous are made sad by these women carrying on with no Bible in hand, just talking lies, while they strengthen the hands of the wicked and the people that put them in power. Therefore they shall see no more vanity nor divine divinations, for the Most High will deliver His people out of their hand, and they shall know He is the Lord.

cases.name: Demas
cases.charge: Forsaking Paul, having loved this present world
cases.summary: Three times Demas appears in Paul's letters: a fellowlabourer sending greetings from Rome, then a name without a word, then a name with a verdict. Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica. Scripture says nothing more of him.
cases.offense: He had stood with Paul in the first imprisonment, named with Luke among the fellowlabourers. In the second, with Paul's death near, he loved this present world and went to Thessalonica. The love of the world is named by John as the thing that cannot share a heart with the love of the Father.
cases.judgment: No sentence is written; the departure is the record. The law's word on the man who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the apostle's on the friendship of the world, stand over the empty place where his name had been. Whether he came back is not told.

entries.commentary: He gave the twelve power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases, and sent them to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick. Take nothing for your journey. Where they are not received, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
Herod is perplexed, hearing that John was risen from the dead, or that Elias had appeared, and says, John have I beheaded: but who is this?
Five loaves and two fishes feed about five thousand men, sat down by fifties in a company, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up.

Whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God. The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day. That word stood alongside all the power they had just seen, and they still could not hold the two together.

If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. What is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away? Whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed.

As he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias, who spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem. Out of the cloud came a voice, This is my beloved Son: hear him. And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone.

A father brings his only child, whom the disciples could not deliver, and Christ answers, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? He rebukes the unclean spirit, heals the child, and delivers him again to his father, and they were all amazed at the mighty power of God.

Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men. The saying comes straight after a devil the disciples could not cast out. He had power to give power, and would still be delivered into the hands of men. They understood it not, and feared to ask him.
There arose a reasoning among them which of them should be greatest, and he set a child by him and said, He that is least among you all, the same shall be great.

John reports one casting out devils in his name whom they forbade, because he followed not with them. Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us. Men who are not speaking against Christ and are teaching the same identity of the people are not to be forbidden merely because they do not stand with us.

The Samaritan village would not receive him, and James and John ask to command fire to come down from heaven. Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them.

Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head. Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God. This is not a bar on burying your own father. It is leaving the affairs of those who are not keeping the commandments to be handled by them, while the work goes on.
