verses.text: And cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man’s feet, whose name was Saul.

And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him.
As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison.
And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,
And desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.
And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:
And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.
And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.
But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel:
For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.

And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.
And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:
And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry;
Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
And the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
Howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might shew forth all longsuffering, for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting.

cases.name: Simon Magus
cases.charge: Offering money for the gift of the Holy Ghost
cases.summary: A sorcerer of Samaria who had long bewitched the people and given out that he was some great one, Simon believed and was baptized under Philip. When he saw that the Spirit was given through the apostles' hands he offered them money for the same power.
cases.offense: Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Peter names the state behind the offer: thy heart is not right in the sight of God; thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. A sorcerer's instinct, to buy power.
cases.judgment: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. Simon asked Peter to pray for him that none of these things come upon him, and the record ends there. His name became the word for buying office in the church.

entries.commentary: Saul was consenting unto Stephen's death. This is Saul who becomes Paul, part of the same people persecuting the church, killing disciples and women, thinking he was doing it for the right reasons. That is why the scripture says judge no one before their time; a man as evil as Saul was doing back there became Paul the apostle. At that time there was a great persecution against the church at Jerusalem, and they were all scattered abroad throughout Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Notice that unlike the other epistles, the book of Acts never closes with Amen, showing there is a continuation: the apostles come back on the scene and redo the Acts all over again, so the things that happened back then are the things that happen today. There will be a great persecution today. This gospel is a witness against the whole world. When you pray thy kingdom come, thy will be done, you are saying the Most High's will overpowers America's will, Russia's, China's, every nation racing for world domination. To preach a black Christ in the streets is to speak against the system that was designed to keep our people debased, a Christ with many crowns upon his head who takes the crowns of all the nations. They are not going to let a people they despise rise up and preach a gospel that overthrows the world superpowers and do nothing; it is going to be a great persecution. Gird your mind, study, pray, and apply, because wisdom and knowledge will be the stability of our time.
Devout men carried Stephen to his burial and made great lamentation over him. A devout man is a man according to the laws of the Most High who has a good report.

As for Saul, he made havoc of the church, entering into every house, haling men and women and committing them to prison. This is the same spirit that will rise up in the religious leaders again; they will seek after us and put us through hell, thinking they do the Most High a service. Because of this you have to be as a pilgrim, one that is ready to get up at any moment and abandon everything. They may come to your house to arrest you, and you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence, and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime, the way our fathers were fugitives. Christ warned the disciples this would happen from city to city, and it came to pass, and it is coming again.

Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ unto them. Philip was preaching to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles; the Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

The people with one accord gave heed to the things Philip spoke, hearing and seeing the miracles he did. Unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, came out of many that were possessed, and many taken with palsies and that were lame were healed, and there was great joy in that city.

Before this there was a certain man called Simon who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, and they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. History outside the Bible says Simon Magus followed Peter performing tricks, became known as the father of heretics, taught salvation by grace alone without works, and finally fell to his death when Peter commanded the demons carrying him to release him; the validity of that account is uncertain, but it shows Simon was a sorcerer deceiving the people. Christianity works the same way, a binding spell over our people that covers the eyes from seeing the truth. You can read the plain scripture that Christ is black and that he came first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and they walk away not believing, or say they do not want to hear the Bible, only your opinion, and then reject that too. It is an enchantment to the highest level, where a man can read something in front of them and they see something else.

But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of the Most High and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Then Simon himself believed also, and was baptized, and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs. Some of our brothers recover themselves, though the outside history says Simon never truly recovered and went back to what he was doing.

When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands he may receive the Holy Ghost. Simon had the spirits of covetousness, envy, preeminence, and vainglory; he had held status as the great power of God, and when he lost it those spirits rose up in him and he wanted to buy back what he had, thinking, I have the money, I will pay you for what you have.

Peter said, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of the Most High may be purchased with money; thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter, for thy heart is not right. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness and pray, for I perceive thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. The gall of bitterness is resentment and bitterness of spirit. Simon became jealous because the signs the Most High worked through the apostles overshadowed what the people had known him for. That thing did not come overnight; he fed envy, preeminence, vainglory, and covetousness day by day until the roots of bitterness took hold and bound him, and he became a prisoner of his own mind, trapped and sinning. This is why, when people come into the truth, some who had status, fame, or money as celebrities, pastors, or deacons have to come up as a member and clean themselves. Some get jealous, hold on to the envy, and try to bring different doctrines to sway members away, the same spirit of bitterness that moved the Pharisees to kill Christ because the disciples came from nowhere, spoke more eloquently, and went to the scriptures better without the status.

Then Simon answered, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me. And when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

The angel of the Lord told Philip, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went, and behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge of all her treasure and had come to Jerusalem to worship. People say this proves Philip went to the heathen Ethiopians, but this eunuch was a Jew, part of the remnant of Israel scattered in Ethiopia, in Kush, during the Babylonian and Persian captivity. That is why Christians confuse the Ethiopian eunuch; they do not understand Bible prophecy or Bible history. Candace was a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe, and the queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.

The eunuch was returning, sitting in his chariot, reading Esaias the prophet, and the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join thyself to this chariot. Philip ran and heard him read Isaiah and asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? The eunuch answered, How can I, except some man should guide me, and desired Philip to come up and sit with him. Notice the humility of the brother. Rather than making his own assumptions, he admitted he did not understand. Some brothers and sisters lack that humility, claiming, I always knew I was Israel, or, the Most High spoke to me while I was in my sins, rather than saying, This is the first time I heard this, teach me. You had to be taught this Bible to know this Bible; the Most High is not just going to hand it to you out of nowhere. Expressing that you do not know keeps you in a low state and away from the spirit of preeminence and vainglory.

The place of the scripture he read was Isaiah: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth; in his humiliation his judgment was taken away, and who shall declare his generation, for his life is taken from the earth. The eunuch asked Philip, Of whom speaketh the prophet this, of himself or of some other man? He did not know, so rather than assume or give his own interpretation, he asked. That is how you should handle what you do not know: write it down and ask, rather than making an assumption and teaching others, which is how heresies come into the body. Then Philip opened his mouth, began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus, because Philip had the Holy Ghost, wisdom, and understanding, having learned under the feet of the apostles.

As they went on their way they came to a certain water, and the eunuch said, See, here is water, what doth hinder me to be baptized? Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. He answered, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and he commanded the chariot to stand still, and they went down both into the water, and Philip baptized him. This seems to contradict everything taught earlier about Christ's baptism not being water. Philip baptized the eunuch in water because, like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism; John understood his own place and told his disciples to follow Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more, and he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through he preached in all the cities till he came to Caesarea. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the Lord is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

This shall be the priest's due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw. The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him. For the Most High hath chosen him out of all thy tribes to stand to minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.

If a Levite come from any of thy gates out of all Israel, and come with all the desire of his mind unto the place which the Lord shall choose, then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do which stand there before the Lord. They shall have like portions to eat, beside that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony.

When thou art come into the land, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations: there shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. These things actually existed and they are all real: wizards, necromancers, divination, observers of times, people that consult with familiar spirits. If they were not real, they would not be in the Bible with the Most High telling us not to do them. All that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord, and because of these abominations the Most High driveth those nations out from before thee. Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God, meaning upright; the nations hearken unto observers of times and unto diviners, but as for thee, the Most High hath not suffered thee so to do.

The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken. This is talking about Christ, Yeshua. This answers what Israel desired of the Most High in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not; and the Lord said, They have well spoken that which they have spoken. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him; and whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. If we do not follow Christ and do what Christ says, that judgment falls on us.

The prophet which shall presume to speak a word in the name of the Most High which he hath not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. By this law a lot of these pastors stand condemned: they say things and claim Christ said them, when the Most High never commanded Christ to say it and Christ is not telling them to say it. How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken; the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously, and thou shalt not be afraid of him. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Everyone that thirsts is called to the waters, and he that has no money is told to come, buy, and eat wine and milk without money and without price. The invitation is free. He asks why they spend money for that which is not bread and their labour for that which does not satisfy. They are told to hearken and eat that which is good, and let the soul delight itself in fatness. If they incline their ear and come, their soul will live, and He will make an everlasting covenant with them, even the sure mercies of David. David is given for a witness to the people, a leader and a commander. A nation not known will be called, and nations that did not know her will run to her because of the Most High, who has glorified her.

Seek the Most High while He may be found, call upon Him while He is near. The wicked is to forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts, and return to the Most High, who will have mercy and abundantly pardon. His thoughts are not our thoughts, and His ways are not our ways. As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are His ways and His thoughts higher than ours.

As the rain and snow come down from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, causing it to bring forth seed and bread, so His word does not return to Him void but accomplishes what He pleases. His people will go out with joy and be led forth with peace; the mountains and hills will break forth into singing and the trees of the field will clap their hands. Instead of the thorn will come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier the myrtle tree, and this will be to the Most High for a name and an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.

Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, is a great man with his master and honorable, because by him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria. He is a mighty man of valor, but he is a leper. The Syrians had gone out by companies and brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid, and she waits on Naaman's wife. This maid is an Israelite sister serving in a foreign house. She tells her mistress that if only her lord were with the prophet in Samaria, he would recover him of his leprosy. Naaman goes and tells his lord what the maid of Israel said.

The king of Syria sends Naaman with a letter to the king of Israel, and Naaman takes ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment. The letter asks the king of Israel to recover Naaman of his leprosy. When the king of Israel reads the letter, he rends his clothes and asks, am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to recover a man of his leprosy. He thinks the king of Syria is seeking a quarrel against him, knowing he has no such power.

When Elisha the man of God hears that the king of Israel has rent his clothes, he sends to the king asking why, and says let the man come to him, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel. Naaman comes with his horses and chariot and stands at the door of Elisha's house. Elisha sends a messenger out to him, saying go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

Naaman is wroth and goes away, saying he thought the prophet would surely come out to him, stand, call on the name of the Lord his God, strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper. He complains in his pride that this was not the process he expected. He asks whether Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, are not better than all the waters of Israel, and turns away in a rage, thinking of a physical cleansing rather than a spiritual one. His mind is carnal, not thinking as the prophet thinks. His servants come near and reason with him, that if the prophet had bidden him do some great thing he would have done it; how much rather then when he says only wash and be clean. Taking heed, Naaman goes down and dips himself seven times in Jordan according to the saying of the man of God, and his flesh comes again like the flesh of a little child, and he is clean.

Naaman returns to the man of God with all his company and stands before him, saying, behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. He asks Elisha to take a blessing of his servant. Elisha says, as the Lord liveth before whom I stand, I will receive none, and though Naaman urges him, he refuses. Naaman asks that he be given two mules' burden of earth, for from now on he will offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods but to the Lord. He asks that the Lord pardon him in one thing, that when his master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship and leans on his hand, and he bows there, the Lord pardon his servant. Elisha says, go in peace, and Naaman departs a little way.

Gehazi, the servant of Elisha, reasons that his master has spared Naaman the Syrian by not receiving what he brought, and swears, as the Lord liveth, he will run after him and take somewhat of him. When Naaman sees him running, he lights down from the chariot to meet him and asks whether all is well. Gehazi lies, saying his master has sent him, that two young men of the sons of the prophets have come from mount Ephraim, and asks for a talent of silver and two changes of garments. Naaman urges him to take two talents, binds them in two bags with two changes of garments, and lays them on two of his servants to carry before Gehazi. When Gehazi comes to the tower, he takes the goods from their hand, bestows them in the house, and sends the men away, hiding what he took like a thief.

Gehazi goes in and stands before his master, and Elisha asks where he has come from, and Gehazi says his servant went nowhere. Elisha says, went not my heart with thee when the man turned from his chariot to meet thee; is it a time to receive money, garments, oliveyards, vineyards, sheep, oxen, menservants, and maidservants. Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to him and to his seed forever, and he goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow. This shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks now, hasty to grasp things by unjust means. -

Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel; Is it not for you to know judgment? Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; who also eat the flesh of my people. Then shall they cry unto the Lord, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings.

Thus saith the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him. Night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine. Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded, for there is no answer of God. But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the Lord, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin.

Ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert all equity; they build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.

cases.name: The church in Pergamos
cases.charge: Holding among them the doctrine of Balaam and the doctrine of the Nicolaitans
cases.summary: Pergamos held fast his name and had not denied his faith, even where Satan's seat is, and in the days when Antipas was slain among them. The commendation stands; so does the charge. They kept the name and kept the teachers with it, and the sentence is suspended on one word: repent.
cases.offense: I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith. But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication. So hast thou also them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which thing I hate. The fault is not that they taught it, but that they had them there.
cases.judgment: Repent; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will fight against them with the sword of my mouth. The sentence is pronounced and held: he which hath the sharp sword with two edges names the weapon he will use, and stays it on their repentance. To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.

entries.commentary: Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.

The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25); go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.

A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25).

They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them.

Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25). Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to [Numbers 5:2](/bible/numbers/5#v2), putting the defiled outside the camp. Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in [Numbers 19](/bible/numbers/19). Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.

Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other. A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle.

Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

cases.name: The churches of Ephesus, Sardis, and Laodicea
cases.charge: Leaving the first love; a name to live while dead; lukewarm, and saying, I am rich
cases.summary: Three of the seven letters in the Revelation carry a sentence with a condition. Ephesus, sound in doctrine and patient, had left her first love and would lose her candlestick. Sardis had a name that it lived and was dead. Laodicea was neither cold nor hot, and was about to be spued out. Each was told what to do, and given time.
cases.offense: Ephesus: I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Sardis: thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead; I have not found thy works perfect before God. Laodicea: thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot; thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked.
cases.judgment: Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief. I will spue thee out of my mouth. As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door, and knock. The sentence is written in full and stayed on the condition.

entries.commentary: The word comes to cry aloud in the ears of Jerusalem: the Most High remembers the kindness of Israel's youth and her love in the wilderness. Israel was holiness unto the Most High and the firstfruits of His increase, and all that devour him shall offend; the nations have devoured us because of our sins.

This is the question the Most High is asking the so-called blacks and Hispanics today: what iniquity have your fathers found in Me, that they are gone far from Me, walked after vanity, and become vain. They did not ask where is the Most High that brought them up out of Egypt and led them through the wilderness; our people keep doing these same things.

He brought them into a plentiful country to eat its fruit and goodness, but when they entered they defiled the land and made His heritage an abomination. That is Israel: we had it good, and we messed it up.

The priests did not ask where is the Most High, they that handle the law knew Him not, and the pastors transgressed against Him. The prophets prophesied by Baal and walked after things that do not profit; that is the Christian pastor today, breaking the laws and worshipping Satan.

The Most High will yet plead with Israel and with their children's children; pass over to the isles of Chittim and see whether a nation has changed its gods, which are yet no gods. But My people have changed their glory for that which does not profit; the glory is the kingdom rulership, traded away for things that do not profit.

The heavens are called to be astonished, for My people have committed two evils. They have forsaken the Most High, the fountain of living waters, and hewed themselves broken cisterns that can hold no water, meaning they hold no truth.

Is Israel a servant, is he a homeborn slave, why is he spoiled? That is the question for the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans today. The young lions roared upon him and made his land waste, and the children of Noph and Tahapanes, the Egyptians, have broken the crown of his head.

Israel procured this unto himself by forsaking the Most High; what has he to do in the way of Egypt to drink the waters of Sihor, or in the way of Assyria to drink the waters of the river. Drinking the waters means learning the philosophies and ways of Egypt; thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee.

Of old the Most High broke Israel's yoke and burst his bands, yet upon every high hill and under every green tree he wandered, playing the harlot in spiritual idolatry. He was planted a noble vine, a right seed, but turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine: worshipping the white man Jesus and the cobblestone.

Though washed with nitre and much soap, the iniquity is marked before the Most High; how can Israel say I am not polluted, being a swift dromedary and a wild ass used to the wilderness that snuffs up the wind in her time. Israel said there is no hope, for I have loved strangers, and after them will I go; the strangers and the white man, mainly Esau, cannot save us.

As a thief is ashamed when found, so is the house of Israel ashamed, their kings, princes, priests, and prophets, saying to a stock thou art my father and to a stone thou hast brought me forth: the wooden cross and the cobblestone. They turned their backs and not their faces, but in the time of trouble they say arise and save us; where are the gods they have made, let them arise if they can save.

The Most High has smitten their children, but they received no correction, and their own sword devoured their prophets like a destroying lion. He asks whether He has been a wilderness to Israel; a maid does not forget her ornaments nor a bride her attire, yet My people have forgotten Me days without number.

Why do you trim your way to seek love from the nations that hate us, and thereby teach even the wicked ones your ways? In thy skirts is found the blood of the souls of the poor innocents, yet thou sayest I am innocent; the Most High will plead against that claim.

Israel gads about so much to change his way, leaning on one nation after another; he shall be ashamed of Egypt as he was ashamed of Assyria. Egypt today is spiritual, the white man Esau, and Israel will be ashamed of leaning on the nations, for the Most High has rejected his confidences and he shall not prosper in them.

verses.text: Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write; These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks;
I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars:
And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name’s sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.
Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love.
Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.
But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.

And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars; I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead.
Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God.

Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.
Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy.
He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.
And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write; These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God;
I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot.
So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.
Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked:

I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see.
As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.
Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.
He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.

Go and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, Thus saith the Lord; I remember thee, the kindness of thy youth, the love of thine espousals, when thou wentest after me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.
Israel was holiness unto the Lord, and the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend; evil shall come upon them, saith the Lord.
Hear ye the word of the Lord, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel:
Thus saith the Lord, What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?
And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.
Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.

cases.name: The Corinthian who had his father's wife
cases.charge: Fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles: a man with his father's wife
cases.summary: Paul heard that a member of the Corinthian church was living with his father's wife and that the church, instead of mourning, was puffed up. He judged the case in absence: deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
cases.offense: Leviticus 18 and 20 and Deuteronomy 27 all name it, the last with a curse and the middle with death. Paul's rule follows the statute's shape: put away from among yourselves that wicked person. The church's tolerance was a second offense: a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
cases.judgment: Excommunicated by the assembly. The second letter shows the outcome: the punishment inflicted of many was sufficient, the man was overwhelmed with sorrow, and Paul urged them to forgive and comfort him and confirm their love toward him, lest Satan get an advantage. Banishment, then restoration on repentance.

entries.commentary: In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians, and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt. The same word stands for us: when the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom. The land of Canaan was full of idols. If Israel obeyed His voice the Most High would be an enemy to their enemies, bless their bread and water, and take sickness away; the charge in Canaan was not to bow to their gods nor do after their works, but to utterly overthrow them and break down their images. Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

Keep the statutes and judgments of the Most High, which if a man do, he shall live in them. The Ten Commandments are not the whole of the law but a summary. Under the Sabbath commandment sit sub-statutes such as no buying, no selling, no working; likewise under the law of adultery sit all the laws of this chapter, the ordinances of marriage and the forbidden beds. None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to uncover their nakedness; these laws name who a man may not lay down with.

The nakedness of thy father's wife is thy father's nakedness; that is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked. This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did.

The sister, whether born at home or born abroad, and the son's daughter and the daughter's daughter are all forbidden; the grandchildren's nakedness is thine own nakedness. There are sick spirits out there, and some of them are grandfathers, uncles, and fathers. Be careful and mindful who you leave your children around; do not hand your children to just anybody for the sake of your own pleasure.

The father's sister, the mother's sister, and the wife of the father's brother, thine aunt, are all near kinswomen and off limits. Incest is still practiced among the nations of this land, and children born of incestuous unions often carry defects and disabilities; the law guards the seed.

The daughter in law, the brother's wife, and a woman with her daughter or her granddaughter are all forbidden; it is wickedness. Neither take a wife to her sister to vex her, to uncover her nakedness beside the other in her lifetime; that also shuts down what the world today calls threesomes.

A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15) details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class.
To lie carnally with thy neighbour's wife is adultery. This world even sings songs celebrating adultery; the law forbids defiling thyself with her.

Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them, as Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem slaying the children of the Most High. The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

Abomination means a thing that causes disgust or hatred. When a man lies with mankind as with womankind, the Most High calls it disgusting and hateful. What a man hates and finds disgusting he removes far from himself; so we must teach our people to repent and come out of the things the Most High hates.
Lying with any beast is confusion, for man and for woman alike. The nations have set up places where these strange lusts are fulfilled, and the sin is found among every people; it is all wickedness.

In all these things the nations were defiled which the Most High cast out; the Egyptians and the Canaanites were doing these very abominations, and the land itself was defiled by them. The land spews out the defiled. That is why Israel was put out of Jerusalem: we could not abide in the land with our sins, sacrificing to idol gods and working all manner of evil, so the Most High raised up an enemy to carry us into bondage and remove us out of the land. Whosoever commits any of these abominations, the souls that commit them shall be cut off from among their people, meaning put to death.

Whosoever of Israel or of the strangers in the land gave of his seed unto Molech was surely put to death; the people of the land stoned him with stones. This is the child sacrifice shown in [Ezekiel 16](/bible/ezekiel/16), slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to pass through the fire. If the people of the land hid their eyes from the man and killed him not, the Most High set His face against that man and against his family. When you see wickedness you must utter it and expose it; a witness that holds his peace bears iniquity. Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

The soul that turns after such as have familiar spirits and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, is cut off from among his people. Sanctify yourselves and be ye holy; keep the statutes of the Most High, for He is the Lord which sanctifieth you. Every one that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; his blood shall be upon him. Disrespecting your mother and your father carried the death penalty.

The man that committeth adultery with another man's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress, shall surely be put to death. This world openly defends adultery and men even boast of committing it with another man's wife; the scriptures call for death upon both.

The man that lies with his father's wife, and the man that lies with his daughter in law, shall surely be put to death; they have wrought confusion. If a man lie with mankind as he lieth with a woman, both have committed an abomination and shall surely be put to death; abomination means hateful and disgusting unto the Most High. The man that takes a wife and her mother is burnt with fire, both he and they, that there be no wickedness among you. The man or woman that lies with a beast is put to death, and the beast is slain also. All of these judgments fall under the laws of adultery, the sub-statutes of that commandment.

The man that takes his sister and sees her nakedness, it is a wicked thing; they are cut off in the sight of their people, and he bears his iniquity. The man that lies with a woman having her sickness, her menstrual cycle, has discovered her fountain, and both are cut off from among their people; this goes with the laws of [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15). The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless.

Keep all my statutes and all my judgments, that the land whither I bring you spew you not out. Walk not in the manners of the nation cast out before you, for they committed all these things and therefore the Most High abhorred them. I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people. The Most High separated Israel from the other people, so Israel is to walk differently; these laws are the separation.

Put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean; this goes back to [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11), the dietary laws. No shrimp, crab, lobster, pork, catfish, and the like; everything is not clean, whatever the church teaches. If you eat whatever you please, you are not separating yourself from the other nations. Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.

A man or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, was surely put to death by stoning. The tarot card readings, the fortune telling, and the horoscopes of today are that same dealing with familiar spirits; do not touch any of it.

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

verses.text: It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.
And ye are puffed up, and have not rather mourned, that he that hath done this deed might be taken away from among you.
For I verily, as absent in body, but present in spirit, have judged already, as though I were present, concerning him that hath so done this deed,
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
Your glorying is not good. Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?
Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us:
Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.
For what have I to do to judge them also that are without? do not ye judge them that are within?
But them that are without God judgeth. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.
The nakedness of thy father’s wife shalt thou not uncover: it is thy father’s nakedness.
And the man that lieth with his father’s wife hath uncovered his father’s nakedness: both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife; because he uncovereth his father’s skirt. And all the people shall say, Amen.
But if any have caused grief, he hath not grieved me, but in part: that I may not overcharge you all.
Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.
So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.
Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.
For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.
To whom ye forgive any thing, I forgive also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave it, for your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ;
Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.
For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not repent, though I did repent: for I perceive that the same epistle hath made you sorry, though it were but for a season.
Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.
For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.
Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you.

cases.name: The Corinthians at the Lord's supper
cases.charge: Eating and drinking unworthily; shaming them that have not
cases.summary: When the Corinthians came together it was not to eat the Lord's supper: every one took his own supper before another, one was hungry and another drunken, and the poor were shamed in the assembly of the church. Paul: what, have ye not houses to eat and to drink in?
cases.offense: Contempt for the assembly and for the brethren who had nothing, in the very meal that proclaimed the Lord's death. Whosoever shall eat this bread and drink this cup unworthily shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
cases.judgment: For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. Paul frames it as chastening: when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world. The remedy: let a man examine himself, and tarry one for another.

entries.commentary: My son, forget not my law, and let thine heart keep my commandments, for length of days, long life, and peace shall they add to thee. Let not mercy and truth forsake thee; bind them about thy neck and write them upon the table of thine heart, so shalt thou find favor and good understanding in the sight of the Most High and man.

Trust in the Most High with all thine heart and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge Him and He shall direct thy paths. Be not wise in thine own eyes; fear the Most High and depart from evil. It shall be health to thy navel and marrow to thy bones.

Honor the Most High with thy substance and with the firstfruits of all thine increase, so shall thy barns be filled with plenty and thy presses shall burst out with new wine. My son, despise not the chastening of the Most High, neither be weary of His correction, for whom the Most High loveth He correcteth, even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.

Happy is the man that findeth wisdom and the man that getteth understanding, for the merchandise of it is better than the merchandise of silver and the gain thereof than fine gold. Wisdom far, far exceeds riches, because we read in verse 1 of chapter 1 about those that are greedy of gain; the only gain you should be greedy of is keeping the commandments and growing in your spirit. She is more precious than rubies, and all the things thou canst desire are not to be compared unto her. Nothing can be compared to the wisdom of the Most High. Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and honor. Her ways are ways of pleasantness and all her paths are peace. She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her, and happy is everyone that retaineth her.

The Most High by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding He hath established the heavens; by His knowledge the depths are broken up and the clouds drop down the dew. My son, let not them depart from thine eyes; keep sound wisdom and discretion, so shall they be life unto thy soul and grace to thy neck. Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely and thy foot shall not stumble; when thou liest down thou shalt not be afraid, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked when it cometh, for the Most High shall be thy confidence and shall keep thy foot from being taken. Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it. Say not unto thy neighbor go and come again and tomorrow I will give, when thou hast it by thee. Devise not evil against thy neighbor, seeing he dwelleth securely by thee, and strive not with a man without cause if he have done thee no harm.

Envy thou not the oppressor and choose none of his ways, for the forward is abomination to the Most High, but His secret is with the righteous. The curse of the Most High is in the house of the wicked, but He blesseth the habitation of the just. Surely He scorneth the scorners, but He giveth grace unto the lowly. The wise shall inherit glory, but shame shall be the promotion of fools.

verses.text: Now in this that I declare unto you I praise you not, that ye come together not for the better, but for the worse.
For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it.
For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.
When ye come together therefore into one place, this is not to eat the Lord’s supper.
For in eating every one taketh before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken.
What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not.
Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.
