cases.name: The false witnesses against Stephen
cases.charge: Suborning witnesses and stirring up the council against a man they could not answer
cases.summary: They disputed with Stephen and were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake. So they suborned men to say he had spoken blasphemous words against Moses and against God, stirred up the people and the elders, and set up false witnesses before the council. Losing an argument, they bought a charge.
cases.offense: There arose certain of the synagogue of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of them of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing with Stephen. And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake. Then they suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God. They stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, caught him, brought him to the council, and set up false witnesses. The law they claimed to defend requires the false witness to bear the penalty he sought for his brother.
cases.judgment: No sentence is recorded on them. They got what they came for: the council gnashed on Stephen with their teeth, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city and stoned him, and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul. The last word spoken over them is the dying man's: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. The young man who kept their clothes was afterward made the apostle to the Gentiles.

entries.commentary: People who do not know the history hear Grecians and assume the Most High began dealing with the heathen nations under Christ. But the Grecians here are Israelites scattered into the Greek provinces during the Greek captivity, the same way our people dropped off in England, the Caribbean, and the Americas take the name of the land that enslaved them and are called African American. The old substantiates the new. The gospel of Christ fulfills the prophecies written in the old testament, and the apostles taught those Israelites scattered through the Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek, and Roman captivities. This is why the churches Paul wrote to sit in Greek provinces like Ephesus and Philippi. Those who argue the Most High deals with the Greeks too are themselves so-called African American, West Indian, Haitian, and Jamaican, and they do not fit the title. To claim the grafting you must prove by your records which Gentile nation you are, and each Gentile nation had judgments that are not yet fulfilled.

The twelve said it is not reason that they should leave the word of the Most High and serve tables. This sets the rank and order: the bishop and the deacons are focused on the diaspora globally, not on one city's disputes, so men are put in place to handle matters and free the leadership to pray, fast, and reach the whole nation. Much of what people bring to the leadership is self-generated and could be solved by themselves; going outside the order to burden the leadership shows a lack of respect and is often nothing but a want of attention.

Look out seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom. Just as the daily ministration had a criterion, rank and order has a criterion. You cannot put a man over a matter who has not conquered his own demons, cannot counsel himself, and cannot get his own wife and children in order. To be full of the Holy Ghost is first and foremost to be keeping the laws. The office is desired by your works, your dedication, and your natural love for your people, not by gunning for a title. Moses was made a leader because he defended his people, and David showed the attributes of a leader wrestling lions and bears and facing Goliath before he was ever called.

The saying pleased the multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, with Philip and the others, and set them before the apostles, who prayed and laid hands on them. Men are not picked because they ask to be officers or captains; they must fit the criteria and have served for a time, with a pattern of good works, full of the Holy Ghost and full of wisdom.
The word of the Most High increased, the disciples multiplied greatly in Jerusalem, and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.

Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people. He was doing the same work being done today, reasoning out of the scriptures with the Israelites scattered through the diaspora.

The synagogue of the Libertines, along with the Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and those of Cilicia and of Asia, rose up disputing with Stephen. The Libertines were Jews and proselytes who had been Roman slaves and obtained their freedom, or were their descendants; Pompey enslaved Jews who kept the sabbath and the kosher law so strictly they were useless as slaves, so he released them. Every group named is Hellenist, Greek-speaking Jews. Only our people are described with the language of freedmen, liberty, and slaves; you never hear the nations of the holocaust call themselves slaves. The Cyrenians are from Cyrene in modern Libya, the Alexandrians from Alexandria in Egypt where the Septuagint was written, Cilicia is the province of Tarsus where Paul came from, and Asia here means the province of Asia Minor with Ephesus, Colosse, and the churches of Revelation, not the eastern continent. All these synagogues, from Cyrene to Alexandria to Asia Minor, held large populations of Greek-speaking Jews. When Paul writes to the churches at Ephesus, Colosse, Rome, or Philippi, he is speaking to the Jews scattered in those places.

They were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which Stephen spoke. When we go to these churches today many cannot refute the wisdom; the spirit of envy drives them to try, and though they leave, many keep coming back because they have never heard it taught this way.

Unable to beat him with the scriptures, they suborned men, bribing and inducing them to give false testimony that Stephen spoke blasphemous words against Moses and against the Most High. Stephen was not teaching them to break the laws; he was teaching them to accept Christ as the sacrifice, and they could not tell the difference between mercy and keeping the law. The same thing was done to Paul in [Acts 21](/bible/acts/21), when they charged that he taught the people not to keep the customs of Moses.

They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, came upon Stephen, caught him, and brought him to the council. The church-going people did back then exactly what they do now, raising false witnesses and false accusations to bring us before judges and the courts, claiming we disrupt traffic or their services when we come peacefully.

They set up false witnesses who said Stephen ceased not to speak against the holy place and the law, though he had not. This is why we teach only the words of the bible: when they bring an accusation, we can answer that we spoke nothing but what is written in the same bible they swear on in court and read in their churches. It will come to a point where the words of the scripture themselves, harlot, sodomite, the law that a man should not lie with mankind, are treated as hate crimes, so a teacher must stay in the scriptures and not use his own words.

The false witnesses said Jesus of Nazareth would destroy the temple and change the customs Moses delivered. But Christ said He came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill. The only thing set aside was the sacrifice and offerings, and even that is written throughout the old testament. Christ did only what the Most High intended, to make His soul an offering for sin. The scripture always shows that sacrifice was temporary and that obedience and mercy were desired above it.

All who sat in the council looked steadfastly on Stephen and saw his face as the face of an angel. This means they saw the power, the boldness, the authority, and the wisdom coming from him that they could not refuse. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

This is Stephen at the council, addressing the audience just before he is put to death. He answers the high priest by going all the way back to the beginning: the God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran. Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, dwelt in Charran, and after his father died the Most High removed him into this land wherein they now dwell, and gave him no inheritance in it, not so much as to set his foot on, yet promised to give it to him and his seed after him when as yet he had no child. Notice how Stephen recites this history off the top of his head. Our forefathers read more than their four chapters a day. When you read, you put these things to memory, so you can recite it. A lot of us cannot recite our own history, but we can recite LeBron James and the NBA stats, football stats. These men were studious; they constantly gave attendance to studying. They called Paul mad for reading so many letters. Our forefathers were addicted to this gospel.

The Most High spoke that Abraham's seed should sojourn in a strange land and be brought into bondage and treated evil four hundred years, and the nation to whom they were in bondage he would judge, and after that they would come forth and serve him in this place. Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt, but the Most High was with him and delivered him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, who made him governor over Egypt and all his house. When the famine came over Egypt and Canaan, Jacob heard there was corn in Egypt and sent out our fathers first; the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren, and Joseph's kindred was made known to Pharaoh. Jacob went down into Egypt with threescore and fifteen souls, and he and our fathers died and were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money.

As the time of the promise drew near which the Most High had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who knew not Joseph. The same dealt subtly with our kindred and evil-treated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children to the end they might not live.

In that time Moses was born, exceeding fair, nourished up in his father's house three months, and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son. Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was mighty in words and in deeds. That corrects the doctrine that certain Christian pastors preach, that Moses stuttered and could not speak. You cannot be a stupid man and be a prince over Egypt. He was raised under Pharaoh, so he had to learn everything of Egypt, their gods, their laws, the language. He was not a stupid man, and he did not stutter.

When Moses was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel. Contrary to the movie The Ten Commandments, Moses always knew who he was; his own mother raised and nursed him, so he knew his brothers, he was only raised under the household of the Egyptians. Seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him and smote the Egyptian, supposing his brethren would understand that the Most High by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not. The next day, striving to make peace, he was thrust away with, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? Only the Most High could set a man to judge. This is the crabs in a barrel spirit: even after you help somebody, they say, Who are you to be over us? Everybody wants to be the head, the chief, a leader, but nobody wants to be a follower, and nobody wants to give credit when credit is due. The Most High was using the status Moses had in Egypt to help his brother, and they used it against him: Wilt thou kill me as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday? Certain of us will be put in different positions in this society, in politics, in education, and the Most High will use those accolades to your advantage, the same way he used Moses to go to Pharaoh and not be put to death right off the bat. Then Moses fled and was a stranger in the land of Midian, understanding that if he stayed among his own people they would get him killed, and there he begat two sons. People use the excuse that Moses married an Ethiopian to justify interracial marriage, saying maybe the Lord would forgive them the same way. But the Most High says, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy. You are not Moses. Ask Aaron and Miriam, whom the Most High plagued in the skin and put out of the camp seven days for speaking against a matter that did not concern them. Do not point fingers and compare yourself to the person next to you, wondering why one brother is judged for a matter and another is treated differently. Different judgments belong to the Most High. You are not David; do not weigh Saul's sins against David's and assume you know how the Most High will judge, the way men questioned why Uzza was struck for touching the ark. Work out your own soul salvation with fear and trembling, study to be quiet, and mind your own business.

Forty years later, Moses now eighty years old, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush at Mount Sinai. Brothers and sisters say they are too old to repent; you are never too old. The Most High used Moses at eighty to deliver the whole nation, and retained his strength. The voice of the Lord said, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses trembled and durst not behold. He was told to put off his shoes, for the place was holy ground, and the Most High said, I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, I have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them; now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

This Moses, whom they refused saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge, the same did the Most High send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared in the bush. Be careful with one another; the same person you reject is the same person the Most High raises up over you. This is the spirit of preeminence, not wanting another brother to rule over you because you believe you should be in that position. The Most High sees the heart and knows the spirits he is setting up. Moses was the meekest, most humble man. For a prince to go down to people counted as slaves and servants, defend them, and risk himself for a stiffnecked and rebellious people, shows he loved his people even in his position of authority. This is that Moses who said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren like unto me; him shall ye hear. Stephen rehearsed all the history to bring them up to Christ, because the whole ministry throughout Acts is Christ's name preached in the place of animal sacrifice. Even as Pharisees, they knew this prophecy, so he made it plain: the prophet Moses spoke about is that Christ.

This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him in Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received the lively oracles to give unto us. The one in the church in the wilderness is that Christ, the prophet of verse 37. Our fathers would not obey him but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt, telling Aaron, Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses we know not what is become of him. They did not obey Christ in the wilderness, just as they did not obey Christ in his day. They made a calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands, so the Most High gave them up to worship the host of heaven; they took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Remphan, figures they made to worship, and he carried them away beyond Babylon.

Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, made according to the fashion Moses had seen, which our fathers brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom the Most High drove out before their face. That Jesus is Joshua, and the Most High drove out the nations before the fathers. This continued unto the days of David, who found favor before the Most High and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, but Solomon built him a house. Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool; what house will ye build me, saith the Lord, or what is the place of my rest? Hath not my hand made all these things?

Stephen turns it on them: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost; as your fathers did, so do ye. The Holy Ghost the fathers resisted in the wilderness is the same Holy Ghost resisted in Christ's day, and that Holy Ghost is first and foremost the laws. There are three forms of the Holy Ghost taught in this series: first the laws, when you keep the laws of the Most High; then wisdom and understanding, which comes after you keep the laws; and then power, as the apostles received power to speak in tongues and perform miracles. Which of the prophets did their fathers not persecute? They slew them that showed before of the coming of the Just One, of whom they had now been the betrayers and murderers, who received the law by the disposition of angels and kept it not.

When they heard these things they were cut to the heart and gnashed on him with their teeth. But Stephen, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of the Most High and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city, and stoned him; the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen, calling on the Most High, said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, and kneeling down he cried, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge, and fell asleep. This is the same spirit Christ had when he said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

When the Most High cut off the nations of the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and Israel succeeded them and dwelt in their cities and houses, Israel was to separate three cities in the midst of the land and prepare the way to them. This law goes into accidental death, what the Bible sometimes calls manslaughter. An Israelite who accidentally killed another could flee to one of these three cities of refuge, where the avenger of blood could not seek him out and kill him there to revenge the blood of his nearest of kin.

Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past, means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident. The example given is two men hewing wood, and the axe head slips from the helve and strikes the neighbour that he die: he shall flee to one of those cities and live. The avenger of blood is the nearest of kin, and while his heart is hot he may pursue and overtake the slayer because the way is long. But the slayer was not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time past; there was no premeditation, no intention to kill. Accidents happen, and the Most High put laws in place for when these things happened. If it was for sure an accident, the man is not worthy of death, as the scripture says.

If the Lord enlarge thy coast as he sware unto the fathers, then three more cities were to be added. As Israel grew and possessed more of the land of Canaan, more cities of refuge were established where a slayer could flee from the avenger of blood. The purpose is stated plainly: that innocent blood be not shed in the land which the Lord giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.

This gives the distinction between an accident and intentional killing; this is describing murder. He hated his neighbour and lay in wait for him: he devised a scheme, waited for the right opportunity and the right time, rose up against him, and smote him mortally that he died. The murderer cannot then run to a city of refuge to lay low. Those cities were not established for him; they were established so retaliation did not come on those who accidentally brought harm to somebody. The elders of his own city shall fetch him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him: putting away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel is what makes it go well with the nation.

What is a landmark? It pays to use tools outside the scriptures, because what good is reading the Bible without understanding of the words written in it. The Zondervan Bible Dictionary defines a landmark as an object, stone, or post used to mark the boundary of a field, and notes that removal of landmarks was prohibited by the Mosaic law. The landmark establishes the boundaries of a man's property, where it begins and where it ends. A man who keeps nudging his neighbour's landmark over little by little until he has taken an acre is stealing land; the dictionary notes it was considered equal to theft.

One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin. One man alone saying he saw a theft is not proof; anybody can come and lie and get people put to death, imprisoned, or beaten. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. It has to be clear-cut; two or three solid witnesses, not one solid witness and a shaky witness. We deal with facts.

When a false witness rises up, both men in the controversy stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges of those days. False accusation is real: people will lie on a man to cover themselves, and false witnesses arise among your own people as well, which is part of why the nation fell into captivity. The judges shall make diligent inquisition: they get to the bottom of the matter and find out exactly who is telling the truth, who is lying, and what the facts are. A judge cannot judge a matter off what one person says; each side tells the story in his own favour, so you must examine the whole matter, question both sides against each other, and decipher the truth. Diligent inquisition is what separates a good judge from a bad judge; a lazy or partial judge makes false judgment. If the witness is found false, then shall ye do unto him as he had thought to have done unto his brother. Accuse a man falsely of stealing, and the judgment for stealing comes on you; accuse him falsely of adultery or another sin punishable by death, and you are put to death, because that is what you intended for your neighbour. So is evil put away from Israel.
The judgment is public and it teaches: those which remain shall hear and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil among you.

Thine eye shall not pity: in this time under Moses it was life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law. Christ spoke on this saying, because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge. Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
If a false witness rise up against any man to testify against him that which is wrong;
Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother: so shalt thou put the evil away from among you.
Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

cases.name: The magistrates of Philippi
cases.charge: Beating and imprisoning uncondemned Romans on the word of a mob
cases.summary: The masters of the damsel lost their gains and brought Paul and Silas to the magistrates on a charge about customs. The magistrates rent off their clothes, commanded to beat them, laid many stripes on them and cast them into prison — no trial, no condemnation, and two Roman citizens. In the morning they tried to send them away privily.
cases.offense: When her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city, and teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans. The multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them. And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison. They heard no defence and passed no sentence; the mob was the trial.
cases.judgment: They were made to undo it in person. When it was day the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go; but Paul said, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out. And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans. And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.

entries.commentary: If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God. Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day.

Observe the month of Abib and keep the passover unto the Most High, for in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night. Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, even the bread of affliction, because thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste, that thou mayest remember the day all the days of thy life. Nothing of the flesh sacrificed the first day at even, the lamb, may remain all night until the morning. The passover may not be sacrificed within any of thy gates, but only at the place which the Lord thy God shall choose to place his name there, at even, at the going down of the sun. Six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a solemn assembly and no work: the first day of the passover is a sabbath, and the seventh day of the passover is a sabbath.

Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee: begin to number the seven weeks from such time as thou beginnest to put the sickle to the corn, and keep the feast of weeks unto the Most High with a tribute of a freewill offering according as the Lord thy God hath blessed thee. Another name for the feast of weeks is the feast of firstfruits: you count seven weeks and then a day, fifty days, which is Pentecost. Rejoice before the Most High, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow; and remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt.

Thou shalt observe the feast of tabernacles seven days, after that thou hast gathered in thy corn and thy wine. Rejoice in thy feast, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates. Seven days shalt thou keep a solemn feast in the place which the Lord shall choose, because the Most High shall bless thee in all thine increase and in all the works of thine hands; therefore thou shalt surely rejoice.

Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Most High in the place which he shall choose: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. They shall not appear before the Lord empty, meaning they have to come with their sacrifices: every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee.

Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, throughout thy tribes, and they shall judge the people with just judgment. There is nothing new under the sun: when you see judges and officers among us today, know that we are following the things that are written within this book. Thou shalt not wrest judgment, thou shalt not respect persons, neither take a gift, for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise and pervert the words of the righteous. That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live and inherit the land.

Thou shalt not plant thee a grove of any trees near unto the altar of the Lord thy God; yet these pastors set up Christmas trees inside the church, directly against this law. Neither shalt thou set thee up any image, which the Lord thy God hateth.

cases.name: The seven sons of Sceva
cases.charge: Exorcising in the name of Jesus whom Paul preacheth
cases.summary: Vagabond Jewish exorcists at Ephesus, seven sons of a chief priest, took up the name of the Lord Jesus as a formula over those that had evil spirits. The spirit answered, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
cases.offense: The Name used as a spell by men who did not belong to it, in a city given to curious arts. Taking the name in vain in its most literal form.
cases.judgment: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded. Fear fell on the city, the name was magnified, and the practitioners of curious arts burned their books, fifty thousand pieces of silver worth.

entries.commentary: An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the Lord is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

This shall be the priest's due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw. The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him. For the Most High hath chosen him out of all thy tribes to stand to minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.

If a Levite come from any of thy gates out of all Israel, and come with all the desire of his mind unto the place which the Lord shall choose, then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do which stand there before the Lord. They shall have like portions to eat, beside that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony.

When thou art come into the land, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations: there shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. These things actually existed and they are all real: wizards, necromancers, divination, observers of times, people that consult with familiar spirits. If they were not real, they would not be in the Bible with the Most High telling us not to do them. All that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord, and because of these abominations the Most High driveth those nations out from before thee. Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God, meaning upright; the nations hearken unto observers of times and unto diviners, but as for thee, the Most High hath not suffered thee so to do.

The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken. This is talking about Christ, Yeshua. This answers what Israel desired of the Most High in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not; and the Lord said, They have well spoken that which they have spoken. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him; and whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. If we do not follow Christ and do what Christ says, that judgment falls on us.

The prophet which shall presume to speak a word in the name of the Most High which he hath not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. By this law a lot of these pastors stand condemned: they say things and claim Christ said them, when the Most High never commanded Christ to say it and Christ is not telling them to say it. How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken; the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously, and thou shalt not be afraid of him. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.

cases.name: They that troubled the churches with circumcision
cases.charge: Preaching another gospel, subverting souls with a commandment the apostles never gave
cases.summary: Certain men came down from Judea teaching that except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved. The council at Jerusalem disowned them by name — to whom we gave no such commandment — and Paul, writing to Galatia, put them under a curse twice over in two verses.
cases.offense: Certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved; and there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses. verses.text: And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.

When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.
But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.

Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia:

Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment:
I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:
Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.
But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.
As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
Ye did run well; who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?
This persuasion cometh not of him that calleth you.
A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.
I have confidence in you through the Lord, that ye will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be.
And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? then is the offence of the cross ceased.
I would they were even cut off which trouble you.

cases.name: Antipas, Smyrna, and Philadelphia
cases.charge: Faithful unto death; keeping the word of his patience; not denying his name in the place where Satan's seat is
cases.summary: Of the seven churches, two are given no rebuke at all, and one man in a third is named by the Lord himself. Smyrna, poor and slandered, is promised a crown of life. Philadelphia, with a little strength, has an open door no man can shut and will be kept from the hour of temptation. Antipas of Pergamos is called my faithful martyr, slain among them where Satan dwelleth.
cases.offense: I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich). Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried. Be thou faithful unto death. Thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth. Thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Because thou hast kept the word of my patience.
cases.judgment: Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death. Behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it. I will make them of the synagogue of Satan to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world. Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God. Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.

entries.commentary: Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.
