cases.name: Barnabas
cases.charge: Selling his land and laying the money at the apostles' feet; a good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith
cases.summary: A Levite of Cyprus sold his land and brought the whole price to the apostles, in the same chapter and by the same rule that Ananias and Sapphira broke with theirs. He took Saul in when the disciples were afraid of him, went to find him in Tarsus when Antioch needed a teacher, and was the man Antioch's Gentiles first believed under. The apostles named him: the son of consolation.
cases.offense: Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Barnabas took Saul, and brought him to the apostles. When he came to Antioch, and had seen the grace of God, he was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord. For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.
cases.judgment: And much people was added unto the Lord. The Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them. The Spirit's own naming of him for the first mission to the Gentiles is the blessing; the church's naming of him is the other: son of consolation. His gift and Ananias' lie stand a few verses apart so no one can miss the difference.

entries.commentary: As they spake unto the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them, grieved that they taught the people and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead. The Sadducees, Pharisees, elders, and chief priests were the religious leaders of that day, and they are the same religious leaders today: your Creflo Dollars, your TD Jakes, your Joel Osteens, your Gino Jennings, speaking the same things they spoke back then. The Sadducees were the upper class, the wealthy priestly and merchant families, moved by political and economic position. They came under the influence of Hellenism the same way today's pastors come under the influence of Americanism, preaching a prosperity and a political gospel and adopting their own man-made traditions. They were grieved because the teaching pulled the people, the money, and the control away from them. It is jealousy, envy, and the inability to guide the people, the same reason these pastors avoid a real sit-down with someone who actually knows the scriptures. The Sadducees did not even believe in the resurrection, yet they used scriptures they did not believe to try to confound Christ, the same way Christians and five-percenters take our scriptures they reject and use them to try to confound us. -

They laid hands on them and put them in hold unto the next day. The spirit that was on the Pharisees is being activated again, and everyone plays their role again in this lifetime; just as the disciples are back in the truth, the chief priests, Sadducees, and Pharisees are back too, saying the same things they said before. They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched. -

Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed, and the number of the men was about five thousand. Many still hear and believe today, and it is mainly black men leaving the dead churches, because the church gives them no purpose, no structure, no discipline, and no position to lead, teaching them to be docile and subservient. This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law. -

On the morrow the rulers, elders, and scribes, with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, and Alexander, and the kindred of the high priest, gathered together at Jerusalem. Annas had been high priest around 6 to 15 AD and kept the title even after the Romans ejected him, while Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was the official high priest the year Christ was killed. These were the very persons who procured the death of Christ. Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in [Isaiah 53](/bible/isaiah/53) and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim. -

When they had set them in the midst, they asked by what power or by what name have ye done this, and Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, ye rulers of the people and elders of Israel. The conversation is still to Israel, always the Israelites. Being filled with the Holy Ghost did not mean Peter was shaking, sweating, or speaking in tongues; it means he was filled with the wisdom to speak with poise before the rulers. When you are brought before the synagogues, magistrates, and powers, the Holy Ghost teaches you in that same hour what to say, the way brother Abiel spoke eloquently in court and was released. You must be wise as a serpent and harmless as a dove, and the wisdom of God will speak through you. Peter, Paul, John, and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque, or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged, and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors. -

If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole; be it known that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, this man stands here before you whole. Examine our good deeds the same way: taking brothers off the streets from drug dealing, gang banging, killing, and stealing; taking sisters out of prostitution; putting black households back together; keeping children from being aborted; keeping men out of prison. What did the disciples do wrong but heal the impotent man? Any time there is a good deed the Pharisees still attack, which shows the hardness of our people's hearts. It was never about the nation or the people; it was about their own vainglory, position, power, and authority.

This is the stone which was set at naught of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. It was the builders' job to build and bind the nation, to raise up the tabernacle of David, to bind the brokenhearted, and to feed the flock, but when the stone, Christ, came, jealousy and vainglory arose and they rejected him. The kingdom is therefore taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits. Christ is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, because men stumble at his location, his upbringing, his appearance, and his low social class. He came from the same hoods we came from, from your Philadelphias, your Detroits, the south side of Chicago, so the Most High confounds the wise by the foolish and chooses the base and the underdog, the way he chose David, not the Creflo Dollars, the TD Jakes, the Cornel Wests, or the Umar Johnsons who already have a following and would take the glory for themselves. This is how you know God is working with us, taking men called nobody and setting them before princes. Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests. -

Neither is there salvation in any other, for there is none other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved. Christians reduce this to saying the words "in the name of Jesus," but "none other name" means no other power or authority was given to any man; that authority was given to Christ alone, so there is no salvation in Moses or Elias, only through Christ. You cannot sneak into the kingdom through Islam, the Nation of Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormonism, Pentecostalism, Seventh-day Adventism, the Baptists, or Buddhism. Whoever climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber trying to sneak in without laboring; you must enter by the door, which is Christ. -

When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus. The rulers saw these men were not slick, cunning, and crafty like themselves; they were bold, coming as if straight off a plantation and a field, not the regular church men. That boldness is the natural animation of the Holy Spirit, not something you force or make up. Brothers who teach weak, like the Christian pastors, with no power and no conviction, are lacking the Holy Spirit. You cannot push the spirit out; when you keep the Most High's laws and stay in the scriptures, the spirit animates your teaching with boldness, the way Christ taught with authority and not as the scribes. People who call us hostile have simply never seen a man of God speak with the Holy Spirit. Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ. -
Beholding the man which was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it. The living proof of the miracle was standing right there, and the rulers had no answer.

They commanded them to go aside out of the council and conferred, saying what shall we do to these men, for a notable miracle has been done by them and we cannot deny it; but that it spread no further among the people, let us straitly threaten them and command them not to speak in the name of Jesus. It was never about the miracle but about losing their power and their seat of authority, and you have to be that wicked to witness the great works and still plot against the men who did them. Satan cannot cast out Satan, so they knew the miracle was of the Most High; yet the same way they consulted to put Lazarus back to death after Christ raised him, they chose to threaten the disciples rather than glorify God. That level of hatred, envy, and emulation is what the religious leaders had for the people. The Pharisees were divided over Christ, some saying he is not of God because he healed on the Sabbath, others asking how a man that is a sinner could do such miracles. That same division will bring people out of the Christian church to examine the matter and repent based on our works. -

Peter and John answered, whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye, for we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. Having further threatened them, the council let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them because of the people, for all men glorified God for the man who was healed, who was above forty years old.

Being let go, they went to their own company and reported all, and they lifted up their voice to God with one accord: Lord, thou art God who made heaven and earth; why did the heathen rage and the people imagine vain things; the kings of the earth stood up and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. Against the holy child Jesus, Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel were gathered together, and this same thing is going to happen all over again. Their prayer was for boldness to speak the word and that signs and wonders be done, so if you lack the Holy Spirit, your prayer should be that the Most High put it in you, for he gives it freely. When they had prayed, the place was shaken, they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness. -

The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul, and neither said any of them that ought he possessed was his own, but they had all things common. They did not cleave to materialistic things; when you come into the truth those things lose their importance and your objective becomes how you can support the truth. This is the establishment of a community, for community comes from common. With great power the apostles gave witness of the resurrection, and great grace was upon them all; neither was there any that lacked, for as many as owned lands or houses sold them and laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man according as he had need. This was not a prosperity doctrine where you give to get rich; you give so that when one lacks, all supply his need, whether food, an eviction, or a proper burial. The church was the epicenter and hub of the community, and the arms, not tithes, circled through it and were distributed according to each man's need. Joseph, surnamed Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, sold his land and laid the money at the apostles' feet; this is the same Barnabas who later traveled with Paul, and even as an apostle he gave arms. Every ranked man should give arms as a testament of his faith and leadership, even while spending his own money to travel and teach. --- Topics: [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Saul is still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples, going to the high priest for letters to Damascus so he can bind any of "this way," whether men or women, and drag them bound to Jerusalem. This is why we tell brothers and sisters both to gird up their minds and build their faith by studying, because when they notice you by your last name or your fringes you will be persecuted. Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in [Acts 11](/bible/acts/11), they were called "this way," meaning the way of Christ. Some people, when the persecution comes, will change their name back, stop wearing fringes, stop keeping the Sabbath, and hide, saying "that's not me." -

As Saul journeys near Damascus a light from heaven, a chariot of the Most High, shines round about him, he falls to the earth, and hears a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Christ was already dead at this time, yet he says "why persecutest thou me," because what you do to one of his little ones you do to him also. Saul did not realize he was in error. He thought the disciples were bringing heresy, but it was not heresy, it was the New Covenant being introduced. Trembling and astonished, he immediately humbles himself and says, "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do."

The men journeying with Saul stood speechless, hearing a voice but seeing no man. People read this against [Acts 22](/bible/acts/22) and claim a contradiction, but there is none. It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. There is no contradiction in the Bible. -
Saul arose from the earth, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus. He was struck blind by what he witnessed. -

Saul is three days without sight, neither eating nor drinking. The Most High speaks in a vision to a disciple at Damascus named Ananias and sends him to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas, to lay hands on Saul. Saul himself is given a vision of Ananias coming to restore his sight. People are still given dreams and visions this way, some seeing a man show them truth before they understood it was about Israel.

Ananias objects: he has heard by many how much evil this man has done to the saints at Jerusalem, and that he holds authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on the Most High's name. Saul had consented to Stephen's death and chased disciples from city to city with zeal. Was Saul doing it in ignorance? Yes. That is why the scripture says judge nothing before the time. The things we all did in the world were worthy of death, so who are we to say a man is beyond repentance? The killer, even a pastor putting us to death in the future, may come to the truth later and say he did it in ignorance, as Christ and Stephen both prayed "Father, forgive them." Even a sister who cursed the teacher out on the streets for months came around and began to listen, because anyone can repent. This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent. -

The Most High tells Ananias to go his way, for Saul is a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel. People discredit Paul's writings, but the book of Acts credits and justifies them, so to throw out Paul you would have to throw out Acts too. The Most High will show Saul how great things he must suffer for his name's sake. The teaching on the Gentiles is held for later, when Paul actually begins his ministry.

Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly. -

Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from. -

All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level. -

After many days the Jews take counsel to kill Saul, watching the gates day and night, so the disciples take him by night and let him down the wall in a basket. This is what you are in: your front door may be occupied and you may have to go down the window on a rope. Properly prepare your mind, because anything can happen at any moment and you must be ready to drop everything and leave. In the world men drove drunk and gang-banged unafraid of death, so do not now be a coward for the truth; the Most High controls death, and it is better to die for this truth than to die for nothing. -

When Saul comes to Jerusalem he tries to join the disciples, but they are afraid of him until Barnabas brings him to the apostles and declares how he had seen the Lord and preached boldly at Damascus. Notice Acts does not tell us he went to Arabia first; Paul fills in that detail himself in Galatians. He goes to Peter and James specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness would be established with the leadership. -

Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus. -
Then the churches have rest throughout all Judaea, Galilee, and Samaria, are edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Holy Ghost, are multiplied. -

As Peter passes through all quarters he comes to the saints at Lydda and finds Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years sick of the palsy. Peter says, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole; arise and make thy bed," and he arises immediately. All that dwelt at Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

At Joppa a disciple named Tabitha, called Dorcas, full of good works and almsdeeds, falls sick and dies, and they wash her and lay her in an upper chamber. Women were disciples too, students and followers of Christ, and washing the dead shows our own customs of purifying the body. The disciples send for Peter, who puts them all out, kneels, prays, and says, "Tabitha, arise." She opens her eyes and sits up, and he presents her alive to the saints and widows, so that many in Joppa believed. Peter then tarries many days in Joppa with Simon a tanner. Dorcas made coats and garments and gave almsdeeds, so she had a good name and no covetous spirit; what she took in she gave back. This is unlike the opportunists who see thousands at Passover and only think of what they can get from the people, coveting to live off of them. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The apostles and brethren in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God, and now Peter is rehearsing what happened in [Acts 10](/bible/acts/10). The "Gentiles" is a reference to Cornelius, who was not Italian by nation; he was an Israelite who served as a general over a hundred men in the Roman army, just as today there are black generals and black soldiers in the American army, and America is an extension of ancient Rome. -

When Peter came up to Jerusalem, they of the circumcision contended with him, saying he went in to men uncircumcised and did eat with them. The complaint was about Peter dealing with the Gentiles, meaning the northern kingdom, and there had been contention between the northern and southern kingdom ever since the split under Solomon. To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations. -

Peter rehearses the vision from the beginning: he was in Joppa praying, and in a trance saw a vessel descend like a great sheet. That vessel is Israel, swallowed up and consumed among the Gentiles, made a vessel of no honour by learning their works and serving their idols. -

The voice said, "Arise, Peter; slay and eat," but Peter refused because nothing common or unclean had ever entered his mouth. The voice answered, "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common," because it was never about food but about people. -

Peter continues the account: immediately three men came to the house from Caesarea, and the Spirit bade him go with them, nothing doubting. Six brethren went with him into the man's house, and Cornelius told how an angel had stood in his house and directed him to send to Joppa for Simon Peter, who would tell him words whereby he and all his house would be saved.

As Peter began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them as it did on the apostles at the beginning, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how that John baptized with water but they would be baptized with the Holy Ghost. Since the Most High gave these Israelites the same gift he gave the apostles who believed on Christ, Peter asks what he was that he could withstand God.

When they heard this they held their peace and glorified God, saying the Most High had also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life. These Gentiles are the Israelites who took on Gentile customs, whether the northern kingdom broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks. -

Those scattered by the persecution over Stephen traveled as far as Phenice, Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but the Jews only, going where the Israelites were scattered. Phenice was the coastal region north of Israel, modern Lebanon; Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean; and Antioch was a major Roman city in ancient Syria, now Antakya, Turkey. The reason they preached to the Jews only is the prophecy that the Most High saves the tents of Judah first. -

The hand of the Lord was with them and a great number believed and turned to the Lord. The church at Jerusalem sent Barnabas, a good man full of the Holy Ghost and faith, who exhorted them to cleave to the Lord, then went to Tarsus to seek Saul and brought him to Antioch, where for a whole year they taught much people. The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one. -

In those days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch, and one named Agabus signified by the Spirit that there would be a great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. This famine is historically documented; Elliott's commentary notes the frequent famines of Claudius's reign, and Josephus records a famine affecting Judea and Syria under the procurator Cuspius Fadus around AD 45, when Queen Helena of Adiabene sent supplies of corn and figs, again giving validity to the Bible as an accurate history book. The disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief to the brethren in Judea, which they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul. That is the end of [Acts 11](/bible/acts/11). --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath) ← [Acts 10](/study/acts/10) · [Acts Study](/study/acts)

At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release: every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it, and shall not exact it of his neighbour or of his brother, because it is called the Lord's release. Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again, but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release. The seven year release stands on the sabbath of the land already given in [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25).

If thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Most High to observe all these commandments, thou shalt lend unto many nations but thou shalt not borrow, and thou shalt reign over many nations but they shall not reign over thee. This is the blessing that was to come upon us. Since we broke the commandments of the Most High, the other nations lend to us and we borrow from them; we go to them for loans and everything else.

If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren, thou shalt not harden thine heart nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother. It is a commandment to us to help our brothers: open thine hand wide unto him and lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand, and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother and thou givest him nought; if he cry unto the Lord against thee, it is sin unto thee. Give him surely, and let not thine heart be grieved when thou givest, for because of this thing the Most High shall bless thee in all thy works. Notice that Esau had this Bible, these commandments and these laws, yet worked us to death for over four hundred years, and when they released us we did not go out with anything. They had these laws written before them and did not do them. The poor shall never cease out of the land; Christ said the same, that the poor are always going to be among us. That is why no campaign can fight poverty out of existence: Christ said it will always be among us.

If thy brother, an Hebrew man or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee and serve thee six years, then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free, and thou shalt not let him go away empty. When people say slavery was taking place in Africa among us, it was not slavery like we suffered: it was people among us that fell poor and sold themselves to their brothers, the very case this law and [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) govern. Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress; he must leave blessed, with some of the flock, the corn, and the wine. He cannot go out poor the way he came in; that shows you the Most High is a good God. The reason given is memory: remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee.

If the servant say, I will not go away from thee, because he loveth thee and thine house and is well with thee, then thou shalt take an aul and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever; likewise unto thy maidservant. It shall not seem hard unto thee when thou sendest him away free, for he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee in serving thee six years. A double hired servant: reading this makes you think about slavery and how many years they had us. We were double hired servants unto them, and we still serve them even to this day.

All the firstling males of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto the Most High: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock, nor shear the firstling of thy sheep. The firstlings were to do no work at all; they were to be sacrificed to the Most High, and thou shalt eat it before the Lord thy God year by year in the place which the Lord shall choose. If there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame or blind, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God; thou shalt eat it within thy gates, the unclean and the clean person alike, as the roebuck and as the hart. Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it upon the ground as water.

cases.name: Cornelius
cases.charge: A devout man, one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway
cases.summary: A centurion of the Italian band at Caesarea, a Gentile, was praying at the ninth hour when an angel told him his prayers and alms were come up for a memorial before God, and to send for Peter. Peter came, learned on the way that God is no respecter of persons, preached, and the Holy Ghost fell on the whole house before he had finished. They were the first Gentiles baptized.
cases.offense: A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house. When Peter came, Cornelius met him and fell down at his feet; Peter took him up: I myself also am a man. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God.
cases.judgment: Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God. Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

entries.commentary: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian band. When our people read "Italian band" they automatically picture a Caucasian, but Caesarea Maritima sat on a seacoast in the land of Israel, and Cornelius was an Israelite officer in the Roman army, not a man of another nation. Jews of the diaspora were fully enmeshed in Roman culture, took Greek and Latin names, and built careers in the Roman military, so a black man, an Israelite, serving under the Italian band is nothing strange. It is the same as so-called black people and Latinos serving in the American military today, from the Buffalo Soldiers to a general like Colin Powell. Because the Israelites were scattered through every province and took the names of their captivities, scholars cannot tell a Roman Jewish soldier from a Roman by his name alone, and the New Testament was written in Greek because Israel spoke Greek under the Greeks. Correcting a misheard reference to [Luke 3](/bible/luke/3), the centurions of scripture were often Israelite servants in the army. -

Cornelius was a devout man, one that feared the Most High with all his house, gave much alms, and prayed always. To be devout is to be devout according to the law, a man who keeps the commandments, and to fear the Most High is to keep his commandments. The law, the statutes, and the judgments were shown to Jacob and to Israel only, never to any other nation, so a man keeping the commandments and called devout is being marked as an Israelite. Israel followed the nations into idolatry; the nations never turned around and started keeping the law of the Most High. Scholars themselves suppose from this language that Cornelius was a Jew or a proselyte instructed in the Jewish religion, because the pagan Romans worshipped the sun, the moon, and gods like Mars, Venus, Jupiter, and Hermes, not the commandments. -

Cornelius saw in a vision about the ninth hour an angel of the Most High who told him his prayers and his alms were come up for a memorial before God. The Most High only regards the prayer of Zion, the destitute, the prisoner, so this hearing of Cornelius marks him as Israel. Israel were the prisoners of Rome, the oppressed, and the Most High hears the prayer of the oppressed, not the prayer of the oppressor. Salvation coming up as a memorial belongs to Zion and to Jerusalem, not to the captor. -

The angel sends Cornelius to Joppa for Simon called Peter, lodging with Simon a tanner by the seaside, who will tell him what he ought to do. When the angel departed, Cornelius called two household servants and a devout soldier who waited on him. That soldier is called devout, meaning he kept the commandments, showing again that Israelites, Jews, were serving as soldiers and officers in the Roman army while still keeping the law.
On the next day, as the men drew near the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray about the sixth hour. He became very hungry, and while they made ready he fell into a trance.

Peter saw heaven opened and a vessel descending like a great sheet knit at the four corners, let down to the earth, full of all manner of fourfooted beasts, wild beasts, creeping things, and fowls of the air. Christians use this to justify eating unclean food, but the vision is symbolic and points back to the northern kingdom. The vessel is Israel, swallowed up among the nations. The sheet knit and let down from the four corners is the Israelite diaspora, the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah gathered from the four corners of the earth, which is why the Most High used a sheet from four corners. The beasts, creeping things, and fowls are men, because scripture testifies that men in their estate are as beasts, so the whole allegory is about the state of the northern kingdom, not about food. -

A voice said, "Rise, Peter; kill, and eat," but Peter answered, "Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean." Peter refuses because he knows the dietary law, that there is a beast that may be eaten and a beast that may not. The Most High did not change the duty of a pig, a hawk, or a vulture; the unclean animals are the scavengers, the garbage disposal of the earth, made to filter the filth, while the clean animals have a filtration system so their meat is safe. Nothing in the vision changed the nature of any animal. -

The voice speaks a second time, "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common." Praying over pork does not change the toxicity of the animal or its eating habits, so what the Most High cleansed is man, not the swine, and the vision is about people the Most High cleansed from idolatry. The northern kingdom was planted a holy and righteous seed, so it can be cleansed again, unlike the unclean animals that were made unclean from the beginning. The Most High promised to save Israel out of all their dwelling places where they had sinned and to cleanse them. -

This was done thrice, and the vessel was received up again into heaven. While Peter doubted in himself what the vision meant, the men sent from Cornelius had already found Simon's house and stood before the gate, asking whether Simon called Peter lodged there.

While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit told him three men were seeking him and to go with them, doubting nothing, for the Most High had sent them. The men reported that Cornelius the centurion, a just man that feareth God and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned by a holy angel to send for Peter. Cornelius is now called a just man, adding to devout from verse 2, and to be just is to keep the law that is holy, just, and good. Even the southern kingdom, which had no dealings with the north, understood that this particular man of the northern tribes kept the commandments and had a good reputation, like Tobit before him, so they vouched for him by his pattern of good works and alms. -

The next day they entered Caesarea, and Cornelius, who had gathered his kinsmen and near friends, met Peter, fell down at his feet, and worshipped him. Peter took him up, saying, "Stand up; I myself also am a man," refusing the worship, and went in to find many come together.

Peter tells them it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company with one of another nation, then says the Most High has shewed him not to call any man common or unclean. "One of another nation" is not other races; it is the northern kingdom, and this whole verse rests on the split between Judah and Ephraim. The division began when Rehoboam refused the people and Jeroboam led the ten tribes away, so the southern kingdom (Judah, Benjamin, Levi) and the northern kingdom went their separate ways, and the Levites and a remnant that set their hearts to seek the Most High left the north and came to Judah. This is the same enmity you keep seeing as Jew and Gentile in the New Testament. -

Cornelius rehearses the events: four days ago at the ninth hour he was praying and fasting when a man stood before him in bright clothing, an angel, and told him his prayer was heard and his alms had in remembrance in the sight of the Most High. This shows our alms and prayers are regarded and counted as a memorial before the Most High. Because of his good works, his alms, his being a just and devout man who feared the Most High and prayed often, the Most High counted him worthy that through him the whole northern kingdom could receive the salvation already promised through Abraham. Cornelius says they are all present before the Most High to hear all things commanded of God.

Peter opens his mouth and says the Most High is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted, and the word was sent unto the children of Israel. "No respecter of persons" does not mean nations are equal, because the Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people; it means he does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law, so whether a man sins outside the law or inside it he is judged. -

Peter rehearses the ministry of Christ, published throughout Judea from Galilee, how the Most High anointed Jesus of Nazareth, who went about doing good and healing all oppressed of the devil, whom they slew and hanged on a tree, and whom the Most High raised the third day and shewed openly to chosen witnesses. To him all the prophets witness that through his name whosoever believeth receiveth remission of sins. The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed. -

While Peter yet spake, the Holy Ghost fell on all who heard, and they of the circumcision were astonished that on the "Gentiles" also the gift was poured out, for they spake with tongues and magnified the Most High. The Spirit is poured only on the house of Israel, so the Gentiles receiving it are the children of Israel, the northern kingdom. -

The apostles and brethren in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God, and now Peter is rehearsing what happened in [Acts 10](/bible/acts/10). The "Gentiles" is a reference to Cornelius, who was not Italian by nation; he was an Israelite who served as a general over a hundred men in the Roman army, just as today there are black generals and black soldiers in the American army, and America is an extension of ancient Rome. -

When Peter came up to Jerusalem, they of the circumcision contended with him, saying he went in to men uncircumcised and did eat with them. The complaint was about Peter dealing with the Gentiles, meaning the northern kingdom, and there had been contention between the northern and southern kingdom ever since the split under Solomon. To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations. -

Peter rehearses the vision from the beginning: he was in Joppa praying, and in a trance saw a vessel descend like a great sheet. That vessel is Israel, swallowed up and consumed among the Gentiles, made a vessel of no honour by learning their works and serving their idols. -

The voice said, "Arise, Peter; slay and eat," but Peter refused because nothing common or unclean had ever entered his mouth. The voice answered, "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common," because it was never about food but about people. -

Peter continues the account: immediately three men came to the house from Caesarea, and the Spirit bade him go with them, nothing doubting. Six brethren went with him into the man's house, and Cornelius told how an angel had stood in his house and directed him to send to Joppa for Simon Peter, who would tell him words whereby he and all his house would be saved.

As Peter began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them as it did on the apostles at the beginning, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how that John baptized with water but they would be baptized with the Holy Ghost. Since the Most High gave these Israelites the same gift he gave the apostles who believed on Christ, Peter asks what he was that he could withstand God.

When they heard this they held their peace and glorified God, saying the Most High had also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life. These Gentiles are the Israelites who took on Gentile customs, whether the northern kingdom broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks. -

Those scattered by the persecution over Stephen traveled as far as Phenice, Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but the Jews only, going where the Israelites were scattered. Phenice was the coastal region north of Israel, modern Lebanon; Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean; and Antioch was a major Roman city in ancient Syria, now Antakya, Turkey. The reason they preached to the Jews only is the prophecy that the Most High saves the tents of Judah first. -

The hand of the Lord was with them and a great number believed and turned to the Lord. The church at Jerusalem sent Barnabas, a good man full of the Holy Ghost and faith, who exhorted them to cleave to the Lord, then went to Tarsus to seek Saul and brought him to Antioch, where for a whole year they taught much people. The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one. -

In those days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch, and one named Agabus signified by the Spirit that there would be a great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. This famine is historically documented; Elliott's commentary notes the frequent famines of Claudius's reign, and Josephus records a famine affecting Judea and Syria under the procurator Cuspius Fadus around AD 45, when Queen Helena of Adiabene sent supplies of corn and figs, again giving validity to the Bible as an accurate history book. The disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief to the brethren in Judea, which they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul. That is the end of [Acts 11](/bible/acts/11). --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath) ← [Acts 10](/study/acts/10) · [Acts Study](/study/acts)
David cries to the Lord to make haste to him and to hear his voice, asking that his prayer be set before the Lord as incense and the lifting up of his hands as the evening sacrifice.

Set a watch before my mouth, keep the door of my lips: this is asking the Lord to help him control his mouth, the same as James telling us to bridle the tongue. Incline not my heart to any evil thing means do not let my mind and my spirit go after things that are evil; help me walk in the spirit. He asks the Lord not to let his heart be inclined to practice wicked works with men that work iniquity, and not to let him eat of their dainties, meaning not to partake or follow the wicked to do evil. -

Now David says the opposite. Instead of being inclined to work evil, he asks that the righteous correct him, and that correction is counted as kindness and love. Correction may be uncomely and it will not be very comely, but it is for good; it shall not break his head, meaning it is not going to hurt him. When you get corrected, that is kindness. A danger he names is envying the wicked, because a lot of times we envy those in the world when nothing seems to be happening to them.

David trusts the Lord and asks that his soul not be left destitute, that he be kept from the snares and gins the workers of iniquity have laid, and that the wicked fall into their own nets while he escapes. This is the prayer he gives to the Lord: to hear his voice, to keep him from his enemies, and to keep him from wickedness himself. These are the things we keep an eye on in our prayers, thoughts, and studies as we walk through this truth.

verses.text: There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,
A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.
He saw in a vision evidently about the ninth hour of the day an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.
And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.
And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter:
He lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side: he shall tell thee what thou oughtest to do.
And when the angel which spake unto Cornelius was departed, he called two of his household servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;
And when he had declared all these things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.
And the morrow after they entered into Cesarea. And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.
And as Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him.
But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.
And as he talked with him, he went in, and found many that were come together.

And he said unto them, Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
Therefore came I unto you without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for: I ask therefore for what intent ye have sent for me?
And Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
And said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.
Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter; he is lodged in the house of one Simon a tanner by the sea side: who, when he cometh, shall speak unto thee.
Immediately therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God.
Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.
While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.
And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost.
For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,
Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?
And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.
And he shewed us how he had seen an angel in his house, which stood and said unto him, Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter;
Who shall tell thee words, whereby thou and all thy house shall be saved.
And as I began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them, as on us at the beginning.
Then remembered I the word of the Lord, how that he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost.
Forasmuch then as God gave them the like gift as he did unto us, who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ; what was I, that I could withstand God?
When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.
Now therefore, when thou didst pray, and Sara thy daughter in law, I did bring the remembrance of your prayers before the Holy One: and when thou didst bury the dead, I was with thee likewise.
Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.

When he came, the widows stood by him weeping and showing the coats and garments she had made. He put them out, kneeled, prayed, and said, Tabitha, arise. She opened her eyes, and he presented her alive.

entries.commentary: Saul is still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples, going to the high priest for letters to Damascus so he can bind any of "this way," whether men or women, and drag them bound to Jerusalem. This is why we tell brothers and sisters both to gird up their minds and build their faith by studying, because when they notice you by your last name or your fringes you will be persecuted. Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in [Acts 11](/bible/acts/11), they were called "this way," meaning the way of Christ. Some people, when the persecution comes, will change their name back, stop wearing fringes, stop keeping the Sabbath, and hide, saying "that's not me." -

As Saul journeys near Damascus a light from heaven, a chariot of the Most High, shines round about him, he falls to the earth, and hears a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Christ was already dead at this time, yet he says "why persecutest thou me," because what you do to one of his little ones you do to him also. Saul did not realize he was in error. He thought the disciples were bringing heresy, but it was not heresy, it was the New Covenant being introduced. Trembling and astonished, he immediately humbles himself and says, "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do."

The men journeying with Saul stood speechless, hearing a voice but seeing no man. People read this against [Acts 22](/bible/acts/22) and claim a contradiction, but there is none. It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. There is no contradiction in the Bible. -
Saul arose from the earth, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus. He was struck blind by what he witnessed. -

Saul is three days without sight, neither eating nor drinking. The Most High speaks in a vision to a disciple at Damascus named Ananias and sends him to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas, to lay hands on Saul. Saul himself is given a vision of Ananias coming to restore his sight. People are still given dreams and visions this way, some seeing a man show them truth before they understood it was about Israel.

Ananias objects: he has heard by many how much evil this man has done to the saints at Jerusalem, and that he holds authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on the Most High's name. Saul had consented to Stephen's death and chased disciples from city to city with zeal. Was Saul doing it in ignorance? Yes. That is why the scripture says judge nothing before the time. The things we all did in the world were worthy of death, so who are we to say a man is beyond repentance? The killer, even a pastor putting us to death in the future, may come to the truth later and say he did it in ignorance, as Christ and Stephen both prayed "Father, forgive them." Even a sister who cursed the teacher out on the streets for months came around and began to listen, because anyone can repent. This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent. -

The Most High tells Ananias to go his way, for Saul is a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel. People discredit Paul's writings, but the book of Acts credits and justifies them, so to throw out Paul you would have to throw out Acts too. The Most High will show Saul how great things he must suffer for his name's sake. The teaching on the Gentiles is held for later, when Paul actually begins his ministry.

Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly. -

Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from. -

All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level. -

After many days the Jews take counsel to kill Saul, watching the gates day and night, so the disciples take him by night and let him down the wall in a basket. This is what you are in: your front door may be occupied and you may have to go down the window on a rope. Properly prepare your mind, because anything can happen at any moment and you must be ready to drop everything and leave. In the world men drove drunk and gang-banged unafraid of death, so do not now be a coward for the truth; the Most High controls death, and it is better to die for this truth than to die for nothing. -

When Saul comes to Jerusalem he tries to join the disciples, but they are afraid of him until Barnabas brings him to the apostles and declares how he had seen the Lord and preached boldly at Damascus. Notice Acts does not tell us he went to Arabia first; Paul fills in that detail himself in Galatians. He goes to Peter and James specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness would be established with the leadership. -

Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus. -
Then the churches have rest throughout all Judaea, Galilee, and Samaria, are edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Holy Ghost, are multiplied. -

As Peter passes through all quarters he comes to the saints at Lydda and finds Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years sick of the palsy. Peter says, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole; arise and make thy bed," and he arises immediately. All that dwelt at Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

At Joppa a disciple named Tabitha, called Dorcas, full of good works and almsdeeds, falls sick and dies, and they wash her and lay her in an upper chamber. Women were disciples too, students and followers of Christ, and washing the dead shows our own customs of purifying the body. The disciples send for Peter, who puts them all out, kneels, prays, and says, "Tabitha, arise." She opens her eyes and sits up, and he presents her alive to the saints and widows, so that many in Joppa believed. Peter then tarries many days in Joppa with Simon a tanner. Dorcas made coats and garments and gave almsdeeds, so she had a good name and no covetous spirit; what she took in she gave back. This is unlike the opportunists who see thousands at Passover and only think of what they can get from the people, coveting to live off of them. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

When a man hath taken a wife and she find no favour in his eyes because he hath found some uncleanness in her, then let him write her a bill of divorcement, give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. Christ magnified this law: when the Pharisees asked why Moses then commanded to give a writing of divorcement, he said, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery; and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

If the latter husband hate her and write her a bill of divorcement, or if the latter husband die, her former husband which sent her away may not take her again to be his wife after that she is defiled, for that is abomination before the Lord. The question is whether a woman who leaves her husband and becomes another man's wife can be joined to the first again; the prophet asks the same thing: shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?

When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business; he shall be free at home one year and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken. Make it plain: the first year, stay at home and make a baby. Husband and wife render due benevolence to one another; benevolence means good, it is a good thing. The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge, for he taketh a man's life to pledge. The millstone is a tool for grinding meal: the manna was gathered and ground in mills or beaten in a mortar and baked into cakes. Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money.

Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married, and Miriam was not supposed to be speaking against Moses. The anger of the Lord was kindled against them, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow. The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding.

When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge; stand abroad, and let the man bring the pledge out unto thee. If the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge; deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment and bless thee, and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God. The law was already given: if thou at all take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, deliver it by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only, and when he crieth unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious. The history shows how wicked we were to each other: Israel laid themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, stacking up people's raiment like pallets and drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their god, instead of returning the pledge before the sun went down as righteousness. That is why the Lord was judging us.

The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin. The example: as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in Amaziah's hand, he slew his servants which had slain the king his father, but the children of the murderers he slew not, according unto that which is written in the book of the law of Moses. The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.

The Most High tells the prophet to cry aloud and spare not, to lift up his voice like a trumpet and show the people their transgression and the house of Jacob their sins. The people seek him daily and delight to know his ways as a nation that did righteousness, and they ask why they have fasted and afflicted their soul and he has taken no knowledge of it.

Their fasting is for strife and debate and to smite with the fist of wickedness, and such a fast will not make their voice to be heard on high. The Most High is not looking for a man to bow his head like a bulrush and spread sackcloth and ashes. The fast he has chosen is to loose the bands of wickedness, undo the heavy burdens, let the oppressed go free, break every yoke, deal thy bread to the hungry, bring the poor that are cast out to thy house, and cover the naked. The reward is that thy light breaks forth as the morning, thy health springs forth speedily, thy righteousness goes before thee, and the glory of the Lord is thy reward; then thou shalt call and the Lord shall answer. "The putting forth of the finger" is when you blame other people. Somebody comes and says a brother did this or that, and instead of taking it, the brother says, "no, but what about her, look what she did." You have to take accountability for your own actions; this is about taking accountability.

If thou draw out thy soul to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, thy light shall rise in obscurity and thy darkness be as the noonday, and the Lord shall guide thee continually and make fat thy bones. Thou shalt be like a watered garden and a spring of water whose waters fail not, and they that come of thee shall build the old waste places and be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy own pleasure on his holy day, and call the sabbath a delight and honor him, then thou shalt delight thyself in the Lord. He will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken it.

verses.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom when they had washed, they laid her in an upper chamber.
And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent unto him two men, desiring him that he would not delay to come to them.

Then Peter arose and went with them. When he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.
But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up, and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive.
And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord.

When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.
When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it afterward: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?
Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the Lord shall be thy rereward.
Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold:
For alms doth deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:

cases.name: Gaius, the wellbeloved
cases.charge: Walking in the truth; doing faithfully to the brethren and to strangers; bringing them forward on their journey after a godly sort
cases.summary: The third epistle of John is written to him. He kept the travelling brethren, strangers to him, and sent them on their way supplied, and they testified of his charity before the church. In the same short letter Diotrephes is cast out of the church for the opposite. John has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth.
cases.offense: Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers; which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well: because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles. entries.commentary: Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.
